_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-09-24-diagnostics-plane · **Version:** viola-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-09-24T10:20:00Z
- **Take-up HEAD:** `4d8be5287b00a00c772e9d0a4264f08d6942f512` (CI green, 9/9 check-runs)

Turn the walking skeleton's hand-rolled role logging into the diagnostics plane obs-plan §3 describes. That means a closed
`ObsEvent` / `ObsProcess` vocabulary and the one sanctioned `obs_event!` macro in `viola-core`, a root-bin `viola::obs`
that owns the per-role JSON sink, and a `config.json` `diagnostics_level` read (the only level knob, never
`RUST_LOG`). It also means owner-only per-instance detail files that finally receive the panic payload and backtrace,
plus two committed line schemas (`diag-line.v1.json`, `diag-detail.v1.json`). The harness `logs` merge gains the
detail source (per obs-plan §3 Logging stack / Log format / Snapshot integration, §6, §7, §8; test-plan §3 Log format
and `logs`; security-plan §Bootstrap `logging-redaction-wire`; architecture §Cross-cutting Patterns → Config management).

Research found most of the builder chain already in place. `src/run/mod.rs:65-80` already sets every mandatory
builder setting, and `viola_core::{SERVICE_NAME, VERSION}` exist at `crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs:3-4`. What is missing is
the vocabulary, the macro, the detail sink and the level read. The chunk is therefore mostly a move plus a migration:
the six raw `tracing::info!/error!` sites in `src/run/mod.rs:83-148` become `obs_event!` calls whose `process` /
`instance` come from a process-global context, and `process-exit{subject:"self"}` gains `duration_ms` (CARRY).

The chunk also closes two pieces of carried work. First, the Rust gate deferral from
2026-09-24-supply-chain-and-workflow-gates is closed by running the unit suite on a real `.rs` delta (PREREQ).
Second, the operator-relayed repair of the `.claude/settings.json` PreToolUse write guard is folded in. P3 measured
that the guard blocks nothing under Git Bash and verified the fix. A repo-local regression probe proves the fix,
chosen by the operator at P4.

1. **`viola_core::obs` vocabulary** — new `crates/viola-core/src/obs.rs`, declared `pub mod obs;` in
   `crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs`.
   - `ObsEvent`: a closed enum with exactly the 19 values of obs-plan §3 Log format (`obs-plan.md:650-656`): `channel-request`,
     `channel-response`, `dialog-raised`, `dialog-answered`, `hook-invoked`, `hook-decision`, `send-issued`,
     `send-confirmed`, `send-refused`, `release-from-driver`, `process-start`, `process-exit`, `http-request`,
     `panic`, `liveness-changed`, `state-recovered`, `sse-opened`, `sse-closed`, `parse-rejected`. Its `Display` and
     `as_str()` are kebab-case. There is no `a11y-violation` variant.
   - `ObsProcess`: `run|hook|mcp|ui|cli` with a kebab `Display`/`as_str()`.
   - `ProcessCtx { process: ObsProcess, instance: Option<ViolaName> }`, held in a private `OnceLock` with a setter
     (`set_ctx`, first call wins, returns whether it took) and a getter (`ctx() -> Option<&ProcessCtx>`).
   - No new dependency in `crates/viola-core/Cargo.toml`.

2. **`obs_event!`** — a `#[macro_export] macro_rules!` in the same module.
   - It takes a level, an `ObsEvent` path, an optional `corr` and additive `key = value` fields. It expands to a block
     whose inner `::tracing::event!` statement carries `#[allow(clippy::disallowed_macros)]`.
   - It attaches `event = <ObsEvent>.as_str()`, `process` and `instance` from `ctx()`, and `corr` as a typed value,
     never `?`/`%`. An absent `instance`/`corr` is an `Option::None` field, so the key is absent.
   - The message is the event's static literal.
   - The `::tracing` path resolves in the calling crate; `viola-core` does not name tracing in its manifest.

3. **`MAX_FRAME`** — add `pub const MAX_FRAME: u64 = 16 * 1024 * 1024;` to `crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs` (the 16 MiB
   cap, per security-plan §Input Validation, CLAUDE.md module map). Its first consumer is step 5's config read.

4. **Root-bin `viola::obs`** — new `src/obs.rs` (`mod obs;` in `src/main.rs`). Move into it from `src/run/mod.rs`:
   `ensure_private_dir` (:19-30), the private append-open of `open_role_file` (:33-50), `timestamp` (:52-54),
   `MillisUtc` (:56-62) and the builder of `init_role_logger` (:65-80). Re-point the callers
   `viola_panic_hook @ src/main.rs:50` and the test at `src/run/mod.rs:168`, moving that test with the function.
   - `role_file_name(process, instance, port)` maps each `ObsProcess` to its basename: `run-<name>`, `hook-<name>`, `mcp`,
     `ui-<port>`, `cli-<name>`, each `.ndjson`.
   - `viola_obs_init(home, process, instance, level)` does the following, in this order:
     - sets `ProcessCtx`;
     - opens the role file 0600 in a 0700 `<home>/diagnostics/`;
     - installs the JSON layer (the existing builder chain, unchanged) behind a `filter::Targets` from step 5: the
       viola targets `viola`, `viola_core`, `viola_pty`, `viola_channel`, `viola_state`, `viola_agent_claude`,
       `viola_mcp`, `viola_ui` at the level, everything else OFF;
     - hands the role file to the panic sink.
   - The error path of an open failure returns the `io::Error` to the caller. It never falls back to stdout/stderr
     (`io::sink` only for `mcp`, which is not built yet).

5. **`diagnostics_level` read** — `read_diagnostics_level(home) -> (Level, Option<Rejection>)` in `src/obs.rs`.
   - It reads `<home>/config.json` through `Read::take(MAX_FRAME)` as a tolerant `serde_json::Value`.
   - Absent file → INFO, no rejection.
   - Unreadable file, or not a JSON object, or `v` not equal to `1` → INFO plus `malformed`/`unreadable`.
   - `diagnostics_level` absent → INFO. `"info"` → INFO. `"debug"` → DEBUG. Any other value → INFO plus `malformed`.
   - Keys outside `{v, diagnostics_level}` → `unknown-keys` with `count`.
   - It never reads an env var.
   - The `Rejection` is emitted as `parse-rejected{parser:"config-json", detail, count}` at WARN, right after
     `process-start` (obs init step 6, D-28).

6. **Detail writer** — `write_detail(home, instance, process, fields)` in `src/obs.rs`.
   - It creates `<home>/instances/<name>/diagnostics/` 0700 (all levels via `ensure_private_dir`).
   - It opens `detail-<process>.ndjson` 0600 append, lazily, on first write.
   - It hand-formats one line with `timestamp`/`level`/`target`/`message`/`event`/`process`/`instance` plus the given
     fields, and writes it with one `write_all`.
   - Every failure is swallowed: the line is dropped and nothing goes to stderr.
   - The path is built only from a `ViolaName`.

7. **Panic hook → detail** (`src/main.rs:41-57`). `PanicSink` also carries the home. When an instance resolves, the
   hook writes the unchanged home-level line (`panic_line`, :59-82) and then one `detail-<process>.ndjson` line through
   step 6.
   - That detail line has `event:"panic"`, the same `panic_location` and `thread`, `panic_payload` (the `&str`/`String`
     downcast, else the fixed text `non-string payload`) and `backtrace`.
   - `backtrace` is an array of the non-empty trimmed lines of `std::backtrace::Backtrace::force_capture()`, never
     gated by `RUST_BACKTRACE`.
   - The hook still never calls the default hook and never writes stderr.
   - `set_panic_sink` callers are `init_role_logger @ src/run/mod.rs:66`, which becomes `viola_obs_init`, and the test
     `@ src/main.rs:181`.

8. **Run catch-site exit line** (`src/main.rs:32-36`). When `catch_unwind` returns `Err` and `ctx()` reports
   `process == run`, `main` emits `obs_event!(ERROR, ProcessExit, subject = "self", exit_code = 1u8, detail =
   "internal-error", duration_ms = …)` before `ExitCode::from(1)`.
   - The duration is measured from a process-start `Instant` held in `viola::obs`.
   - Factor this into `panic_exit_line()` in `src/obs.rs` so a unit test can drive it under a scoped subscriber.

9. **Migrate the run lines** — `src/run/mod.rs:82-149` and `src/cmd/run.rs:22-45`.
   - `run()` calls `read_diagnostics_level(home)` and then `viola_obs_init(home, ObsProcess::Run, Some(name), level)`.
     This replaces `open_role_file` @ :24 and `init_role_logger` @ :25.
   - It emits `process-start{subject:"self", service_name, version, os, pid}` and then the optional `parse-rejected`.
   - The four `log_*` helpers become `obs_event!` calls with the same `subject`, `child_pid`, `child_exit_status`,
     `exit_source`, `exit_code` and `detail` keys and values, at the same levels (self-exit with `detail` at ERROR).
   - `process-exit{subject:"self"}` adds `duration_ms` on both exits (:37, :41).
   - After this step, no raw `tracing::{info,error,warn,debug,trace}!` remains in the workspace.

10. **Schemas** — new `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` and `schemas/diag-detail.v1.json`, both JSON Schema 2020-12.
    - **Home-level lines** (`diag-line`):
      - The required keys are `timestamp` (the `…\.\d{3}Z` pattern), `level` (`DEBUG|INFO|WARN|ERROR`), `target`,
        `message`, `event` (the 19-value enum), and `process` (the 5 values).
      - `instance` is an optional string and `corr` is an optional number|string. A literal `null` for either is
        rejected.
      - `message` must equal `event`.
      - Per `event`, `additionalProperties: false` over the obs-plan §6 Additive field catalog (`obs-plan.md:1043-1058`).
      - `parse-rejected.detail` is limited to the §6 closed list (`obs-plan.md:1065`), and `process-exit.detail` to its
        exit-1/20/21 codes (`obs-plan.md:1061-1063`).
    - **Detail lines** (`diag-detail`): the same required keys plus `corr`/`conn`. On `panic` lines,
      `panic_location` and `thread` are also allowed. The only content fields are `panic_payload`, `backtrace`, `chain`
      and `drift_report` (`obs-plan.md:1202-1205`), with `additionalProperties: false`.

11. **Harness `logs` detail source** — `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/logs.rs`. After the home-level files, walk
    `<home>/instances/*/diagnostics/detail-*.ndjson`.
    - Instance dir names parse through `ViolaName::try_new`, and a failure is skipped.
    - Entries are checked with `symlink_metadata`, and symlinks are skipped.
    - Files are read with the existing `take(MAX_FILE)`, sorted by instance then file name.
    - Each line is wrapped by `wrap_lines` with an added `instance` key, giving `{"src":"diag","file","instance","record"}`
      or `{"src":"diag","file","instance","torn":true,"offset":n}`.
    - `--instance`/`--process` filter as today. `--kind`/`--after` stay clap usage errors (research: exit 2 `reason:"usage"`).
    - Update the module doc (:1-3): only the events source remains to arrive with its producer.

12. **Write-guard repair** — `.claude/settings.json:14`. Replace the substring `path=${path//\\\\//};` with
    `path=$(printf \"%s\" \"$path\" | tr \"\\\\\\\\\" \"/\");` so that the decoded command carries
    `path=$(printf "%s" "$path" | tr "\\\\" "/");`, the form measured at P3.
    - It is written JSON-escaped in the file.
    - No other byte of the file changes. Read the file back and diff it: one line changed.

13. **Guard regression probe** — new `scripts/guard-probe.py` (python, stdlib only, `-X utf8`).
    - It loads `.claude/settings.json`, takes the `command` of the `PreToolUse` entry whose `matcher` is
      `Edit|MultiEdit|Write|NotebookEdit`, and runs it AS RENDERED (no substitution).
    - The resolved Git Bash path is taken from `shutil.which("bash")`, falling back to
      `C:/Program Files/Git/bin/bash.exe` on Windows.
    - It runs `bash -c <command>` with the stdin payload `{"tool_name":"Write","tool_input":{"file_path":P,"content":"x"}}`
      for the six paths, in this order: `<repo>\target\x.rs`, `<repo>/target/x.rs`, `target\x.rs`, `target/x.rs`,
      `src\x.rs`, `src/x.rs`. `<repo>` is the absolute repo root.
    - It prints one line per path and then a last line of the six exit codes comma-joined.
    - It exits 0 when it ran, and 1 if it cannot find the entry.

14. **Tests** (names are the filter tokens in `## Test Commands`):
    - **`crates/viola-core/src/obs.rs` `mod tests`:**
      - `obs_event_display_matches_the_log_format_literals`: a literal 19-string array in the test, compared both
        ways with every variant's `Display`, and `a11y-violation` absent.
      - `obs_process_display_is_the_five_roles`.
      - `obs_ctx_first_set_wins`.
    - **`src/obs.rs` `mod tests`:**
      - `role_file_name_maps_every_process`, with rstest cases for all five roles.
      - `read_diagnostics_level_*` rstest cases: absent file, `{}`, `{"v":1}`, `"info"`, `"debug"`, `"trace"` →
        INFO+malformed, `v:2` → malformed, a non-object → malformed, extra keys → `unknown-keys` with count 2.
      - `write_detail_creates_owner_only_dirs_and_one_line` (Unix mode asserts under `#[cfg(unix)]`).
      - `panic_exit_line_writes_run_internal_error` (scoped subscriber writing to a buffer).
    - **`src/main.rs` `mod tests`:** `panic_hook_writes_detail_line_with_payload_and_backtrace`. It extends the
      :172-197 pattern with a temp home and instance. The role file keeps exactly one line with no payload. The detail
      file has one line with `panic_payload` equal to the canary and a non-empty `backtrace` array, and that line
      validates against `schemas/diag-detail.v1.json` (jsonschema dev-dep).
    - **`crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/logs.rs` `mod tests`:**
      - `detail_lines_carry_instance_and_skip_invalid_names`: `Builder/` and `..`-free invalid names are skipped, and a
        valid instance's lines carry `instance`.
      - `detail_lines_mark_torn_lines`.
    - **`tests/run_cli.rs`** (new cases; existing assertions stay):
      - `run_self_exit_carries_duration_ms`.
      - `run_config_debug_level_keeps_the_key_set`: same four lines, same key sets as `"info"`.
      - `run_config_malformed_emits_parse_rejected`: a `{"v":1,"diagnostics_level":"loud","x":1}` config gives line 2
        `parse-rejected{parser:"config-json"}` at WARN, and the run still exits 0.
      - `run_rust_log_changes_nothing`: `Command::env("RUST_LOG","trace")` gives the same four lines.
      - `run_is_silent_on_stdout_and_stderr`: default fake agent plus the missing-program path, with captured stdout and
        stderr both empty.
    - **New `tests/contract_diag_schema.rs`** (`[[test]]` in root `Cargo.toml`, `required-features = ["fake-agent"]`):
      - `diag_line_schema_event_enum_equals_the_log_format_literals`: the literal 19-string array, not `ObsEvent`.
      - `diag_line_schema_rejects_literal_null_corr_and_instance`.
      - `diag_lines_from_real_runs_validate`: the fake-agent run, the missing-program run and the malformed-config run.
        Every role line validates, and failures print file, line and keyword, never content.
- `crates/viola-core/src/obs.rs` — `ObsEvent`, `ObsProcess`, `ProcessCtx` + `OnceLock`, `obs_event!`, tests.

- `src/obs.rs` — `viola::obs`: timestamps, private dir/file helpers, role-file naming, `viola_obs_init`, the
  `diagnostics_level` read, the detail writer, `panic_exit_line`, tests.
- `schemas/diag-line.v1.json`, `schemas/diag-detail.v1.json` — the two line schemas.
- `tests/contract_diag_schema.rs` — schema enum/null/real-line conformance.
- `scripts/guard-probe.py` — the rendered-guard regression probe.
- `crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs` — `pub mod obs;`, `MAX_FRAME`.

- `src/main.rs` — `mod obs;`; `PanicSink` gains the home; the hook writes the detail line; the catch site calls
  `panic_exit_line`; the `timestamp` call is re-pointed (:50).

- `src/run/mod.rs` — the moved helpers leave; the six `log_*` sites become `obs_event!` (+ `duration_ms`); `spawn_child`
  stays.
- `src/cmd/run.rs` — level read and `viola_obs_init` replace :24-25; `duration_ms` threading to :37/:41.
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/logs.rs` — the detail walk + tests + module doc.
- `tests/run_cli.rs` — five new cases.
- Root `Cargo.toml` — `[[test]] contract_diag_schema`.
- `.claude/settings.json` — the one-line guard rewrite (:14).
These are local gates, plus the operator's push and CI read.
- No external process is driven and there is no live leg this chunk, so no `probe` liveness precondition exists.

- The boot smoke re-runs the previous chunks' lifecycle. Interim readiness keys on the migrated `process-start` lines,
  so it must still reach `ready`. It then reads `logs` for the booted session.

- The filtered entries pin this chunk's tests by name. nextest fails an unmatched filter (exit 4 → harness red), so
  they cannot pass vacuously.
- `run --unit` on this `.rs` delta is the PREREQ close.
- The mutation entry runs the whole chunk diff against the take-up HEAD.
- The last two entries witness CI on the operator's push.

  source. These run once, with both readings recorded in `chunks/2026-09-24-epoch-1-cleanup/evidence/`:

  authoring; a split re-tests them against today's tests, so survivors are possible but not expected.]

- **Orphans probe** (a scratch crate, cargo-modules 0.27.0): `lib.rs` with `#[cfg(test)] mod t;` plus `src/t.rs` → `Found 1 orphans`, rc 1.
  **An out-of-line `#[cfg(test)]` module file is an orphan to the gate as the script runs it.** Tests that move must stay inline in the
  file they test (`mod tests { … }` inside each new submodule file). A new `#[cfg(test)] mod x;` file is not an option unless the gate
  itself changes, which is out of this chunk.

- **`--in-diff` scope mechanism:**
  - `chunk_diff` (run.rs:510) is `git diff <merge-base>` plus untracked files as `/dev/null` diffs, with git 2.53 rename detection on by default.
  - Code moved into NEW files (`run/<concern>.rs`) appears as wholly added lines, so every moved production line is mutated.
  - Code left in `run.rs` is mutated only where its lines changed. Lines deleted from `run.rs` are never mutated.
  - Hence the split's mutant scope ≈ the moved production functions plus the reshaped `run_with`, up to the 154.

- **`--browser` at HEAD:** unbuilt. `cli.rs:60` asserts `run --browser` → exit 2 `reason:"usage"`. The a11y extract's
  `browser-linux-only` / `browser-missing` outcomes are target state with no code at HEAD. The only obligation here is that
  `run --browser` stays a usage error.

- **logs / status:** `harness/logs.rs` and `harness/status.rs` are not in this chunk's modify set, so their output cannot change.

- **Runner seam** (run.rs:29 `Runner`, :110 `run_with`): every tool invocation goes through an injected `FnMut(&mut Command)`. The harness's
  own tests drive `run_with` with a recording stand-in (run.rs:1241 `Calls`, :1268 `run_coverage`), so a submodule function stays testable
  without nesting cargo.

- **Mini-workspace tests** (run.rs:966 `GOOD_LIB`, :971 `mini`): a throwaway `viola`-named Cargo project runs real nextest/doctest/mutants
  for the `run_*` integration-style unit tests. This is the slow viola-e2e class (the 20.6 s test).

- **Document assembly order:** `json!({"v":1,"cmd":"run","ok":ok})`, then `reason`/`detail`, `suites`, `mutants` (run.rs:162–172). Key
  order is serde_json `preserve_order`, so an extracted document builder must insert in exactly this order.

- **Binary-level harness tests** (cli.rs:12 `harness`, :20 `document`): one document, no SGR, leading keys `v, cmd, ok`. This is the killing
  surface for any extracted `viola-harness` handler whose return is an `ExitCode`.

- **Marker:** 2026-09-24-fake-agent-and-test-data-fixtures · **Version:** viola-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-09-24T08:21:16Z

Grow `viola-fake-agent` from the `--version`/Ctrl-C slice into the test double the later chunks drive: a JSON turn
script gated line by line on a control file read by byte offset, an ndjson receipt of everything it received (prompts,
keystrokes, env NAMES, Unix fds, hook invocations), bracketed paste + Enter as one prompt, hook invocation from the
plugin folder `run` passes with `--plugin-dir`, and the prompt-submit modes (`--suppress-prompt-submit`,
`--local-command-mode`, `--inject-harness-turn`) plus `--exit-no-eof` and `--report-version` (per test-plan §7 Fake
agent, architecture §Established Decisions [Hook Transport] / [Delivery Confirmation] / [Human Takeover / Wheel]).
Alongside it: the sync root fixture chain `home → fake_agent_path → stamped_home → booted_wrapper` in `tests/support/`
(homes under `target/e2e-home/`, keep semantics for the CI gates — test-plan §3 `run` step 2, obs-plan §9), the
fixture scrub-and-schema walk proven non-vacuous (test-plan §7 Fixture hygiene, security-plan §Data Protection), and
a `ViolaName` property test with committed regressions persistence (test-plan §7 Seed strategies).

The operator's P4 word fixes the chunk's edges consumer-first: no shape is invented before a recorded fixture exists,
and each deferral is pinned as a CARRY on its consumer at wrap. Deferred: `--vt100-panic-bytes`, `statusline-echo`
(with the `settings.json` read), the `agents --json` modes, the `viola_e2e::fixtures` copy of the chain, and the
`fixtures/claude/*/*.json` walk.

The CI fold (scope item 7): the mutation gate stops failing on a Rust-free diff. It classifies `chunk.diff` itself,
reports an explicit `no-rust-delta` verdict that names the diff, and never reads an `outcomes.json` the current
invocation did not produce. Research (research.md §Mechanism equalities) found this second, host-only face of the
defect by reproducing it.

1. **Workspace dependencies.** In root `Cargo.toml` `[workspace.dependencies]`, pin `rstest = "=0.27.0"`
   (`default-features = false`), `proptest = "=1.11.0"` (`default-features = false, features = ["std"]`) and
   `jsonschema = "=0.57.0"` (`default-features = false`). The last one matters: its defaults pull reqwest and
   `aws-lc-rs`, a C-building crate (research.md §Open questions). Root `[dev-dependencies]` gain `rstest` and
   `jsonschema`. `crates/viola-core/Cargo.toml` gains `[dev-dependencies] proptest`. The root package gains NO
   `viola-e2e` dependency (test-plan.md:542).

2. **Fake agent: argument surface** (`src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs`). Parse, in any order:
   - `--version`
   - `--cli-version <v>` (default `2.1.0`, existing `cli_version` @ `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs:19`)
   - `--report-version <v>`: overrides ONLY the `--version` answer, so replay still follows `--cli-version`
   - `--script <path>`, `--control <path>`, `--receipt <path>`, `--fixtures <dir>`, `--plugin-dir <dir>`
   - the mode flags `--suppress-prompt-submit`, `--local-command-mode`, `--inject-harness-turn`, `--exit-no-eof`

   Every other argument is ignored, as today (`run_cli.rs` passes `--argv-sentinel-q1`). Paths are used exactly as
   given: resolving a relative `--script`/`--fixtures` against the workspace root is the caller's job (the root chain,
   step 9), never the fake agent's.

4. **Fake agent: input.** Read stdin byte by byte:
   - `\x03` ends the process with exit 0, as today.
   - `ESC[200~ … ESC[201~` collects paste content; the next CR submits it as ONE prompt (`origin:"human"`).
   - Bytes typed outside a paste each produce a `key` line; a CR after typed bytes submits those bytes as one prompt.
   - `bare_esc` is true when the prompt's bytes contain `0x1b`.
   - Text is decoded lossily; `hex` is always the exact bytes.

5. **Fake agent: hook invocation.** For event E:
   - Read `<plugin-dir>/hooks/hooks.json` (architecture.md:345/364) as the documented Claude Code hooks shape
     `{"hooks":{E:[{"hooks":[{"type":"command","command":…,"args":[…]}]}]}}`. Run every `type:"command"` entry
     registered for E; matchers are NOT evaluated this chunk (see Constraints).
   - The payload is the bytes of `<fixtures>/<cli-version>/<E>.<variant>.json`. For `UserPromptSubmit` only, the
     top-level `prompt` key is set to the prompt text (the documented input field). No other payload is built.
   - An absolute `command` is spawned directly with its `args`: never through a shell, never via PATH lookup. Its
     stdin is the payload; exit code, stderr length and stdout bytes are captured into a `hook` receipt.
   - A non-absolute `command` is not run: `hook` {`command_absolute:false`, `ran:false`}.
   - With no `--plugin-dir` or no `hooks.json`: `no-hooks`. With no fixture file: `no-fixture`. In both cases no
     process is spawned.

6. **Fake agent: prompt-submit modes.**
   - A submitted prompt fires `UserPromptSubmit` with variant `default`.
   - `--suppress-prompt-submit` never fires it (`submit:"suppressed"`).
   - `--local-command-mode` does not fire it for a prompt whose text starts with `/` (`submit:"local-command"`); any
     other prompt fires normally.
   - `--inject-harness-turn` adds one gated step before the script's first step. When released, it fires
     `UserPromptSubmit` whose `prompt` starts with the harness-turn prefix `<task-notification>` (architecture
     §Established Decisions [Human Takeover / Wheel]) and writes a `prompt` receipt with `origin:"harness"`.

7. **Fake agent: script + control.**
   - `--script <file>` is JSON `{"v":1,"steps":[{"event":E,"variant":V,"gate":bool},…]}`, where E is one of the nine
     registered hook events (architecture.md:344). The steps run in order on their own thread, and stdin keeps being
     read.
   - A `gate:true` step blocks until one more complete line (`\n`-terminated) exists in the `--control` file past the
     agent's last byte offset. A missing control file reads as empty. The agent polls; the TESTS never sleep.
   - Each executed step writes a `step` receipt, then fires E (step 5).

8. **Fake agent: `--exit-no-eof`.** At `\x03` the agent first spawns a copy of itself (its own exe, hidden internal
   argument) that inherits stdout and holds it for a bounded 10 s, then exits 0. The process exit can therefore be
   observed while stdout has not reached EOF. The grandchild never outlives 10 s.

9. **Root fixture chain** (`tests/support/mod.rs`, `tests/support/home.rs`, `tests/support/fake.rs`; sync, no tokio):
   - `home`: a `tempfile::Builder` dir with prefix `viola-test-` under `<CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR>/target/e2e-home/`, with
     the home at `<dir>/home`. The home is NOT created; viola creates it. On drop it keeps the dir
     (`TempDir::keep()`) when `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES=1`, or when `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_FAILED=1` and the thread is
     panicking; otherwise it removes the dir. The decision is a pure function with a unit test over all four inputs.
   - `fake_agent_path`: `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_viola-fake-agent")`.
   - `stamped_home`: the interim seam. It returns the home with a documented "not stamped until `viola verify`
     exists" marker and never writes `ledger/stamps.json` (test-plan §7, §12 Stamps conflict).
   - `booted_wrapper`: spawns `viola --home <home> run <name> -- <fake agent> --control <home>/fake/<name>.control
     --receipt <home>/fake/<name>.receipt.ndjson [--script <workspace-root-resolved path>] <args>` with piped stdin,
     and env set per child only (`Command::env`). It waits (bounded 20 s, file-state probe, no sleep-as-sync) for the
     interim readiness lines `process-start` self + `claude-child` in `diagnostics/run-<name>.ndjson`.
     It exposes: write stdin bytes, append a control line, read receipt lines, and `stop()` (`\x03`, then wait).
     `Drop` is only a best-effort fallback.

10. **Migrate `tests/run_cli.rs`.** Replace `scratch()` (`run_cli.rs:31-39`; 6 sites via graph `scratch` callers
    `run_cli.rs:64,122,133,144,161,237`) with the root `home` fixture; behaviour and assertions stay unchanged.

11. **Fake-agent integration tests** (new `tests/cli_fake_agent.rs`, `[[test]]` with `required-features =
    ["fake-agent"]`). Each mode and receipt kind from steps 2-8 gets a test that observes its effect through the
    receipt, stdout or exit. Tests use the chain where a wrapper is needed and spawn the fake agent directly
    otherwise. Ordering is only by control appends; there is no sleep anywhere in a test.

12. **Fixture hygiene** (new `tests/support/hygiene.rs` + `tests/contract_fixture_hygiene.rs`, `[[test]]` with
    `required-features = ["fake-agent"]`). One checker returns a violation CLASS, never the offending content, for:
    - absolute paths (`^[A-Za-z]:[\\/]`, `/home/`, `/Users/`, `\Users\`)
    - the host's own username (from `USER`/`USERNAME`, whole word, case-insensitive) other than the placeholder `<user>`
    - a jsonschema failure against `schemas/fake-script.v1.json`. That schema is tolerant: unknown fields are
      allowed, `v` is const 1, and `event` is a closed enum of the nine registered events.

    An rstest `#[files("fixtures/fake-scripts/*.json")]` test applies the checker to every committed script. Planted
    in-memory inputs prove each class red.

13. **Committed scenario script.** Add `fixtures/fake-scripts/gated-turn.json` (synthetic text only; two gated steps,
    `PreToolUse` then `Stop`). The step-11 gating test and the step-12 walk both consume it.

14. **ViolaName property test** (`crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs` `#[cfg(test)]`). A proptest at `cases: 512` with
    explicit `FileFailurePersistence::SourceParallel("proptest-regressions")` asserts, for arbitrary strings, that
    `try_new` accepts exactly the inputs matching a literal oracle `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$`. It also asserts that a
    valid-name strategy and path-hostile neighbours (`..`, separators, uppercase, controls, 33 chars) are decided
    correctly. Commit `crates/viola-core/proptest-regressions/lib.txt` with proptest's standard header and no
    invented seeds.

15. **Mutation gate verdict** (`crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run.rs::mutants`, sole caller `run()` @ `run.rs:82`):
    - After writing `chunk.diff`, classify it: a Rust delta is any changed path (from the `diff --git a/… b/…`
      headers) ending in `.rs`.
    - **No Rust delta:** do NOT run cargo-mutants or the prebuild. Return a green `mutants` suite
      (`artifact:"target/agent-run/chunk.diff"`), and the document's `mutants` object becomes
      `{"tested":0,"verdict":"no-rust-delta","diff":"target/agent-run/chunk.diff","files":N}`, where N is the
      changed-path count.
    - **Rust delta:** before invoking cargo-mutants, remove any `mutants.out/outcomes.json` an earlier run left, so the
      file read afterwards can only be this invocation's. The existing count verdict then applies, with
      `"verdict":"counted"`. A missing `outcomes.json` stays `failures:["outcomes-missing"]`, `ok:false`.
    - The `diff.trim().is_empty()` arm (`run.rs:409`) is replaced by the classifier (an empty diff has no Rust delta).
      `base-missing` handling is untouched.
    - Unit tests: (a) the classifier over Rust / Rust-free / empty / rename diffs; (b) a Rust-free change in the
      throwaway `mini()` workspace (`run.rs:622`) with a planted stale `mutants.out/outcomes.json` reporting
      survivors yields `ok:true`, `verdict:"no-rust-delta"` and `tested:0`, and the planted counts appear nowhere;
      (c) a Rust delta whose outcomes are absent yields `outcomes-missing`, `ok:false`, even with a stale file
      planted before the call.
- `tests/support/mod.rs`, `tests/support/home.rs`, `tests/support/fake.rs`, `tests/support/hygiene.rs`: the root chain, fake-agent helpers, hygiene checker
- `tests/cli_fake_agent.rs`: fake-agent mode/receipt/script/hook tests
- `tests/contract_fixture_hygiene.rs`: the `#[files]` walk + planted-input tests
- `fixtures/fake-scripts/gated-turn.json`: the first committed scenario script
- `schemas/fake-script.v1.json`: tolerant schema for scenario scripts
- `crates/viola-core/proptest-regressions/lib.txt`: persistence file (standard header)
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs`: steps 2-8
- `tests/run_cli.rs`: `scratch()` → `home` fixture (6 sites)
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run.rs`: step 15 (+ its tests)
- `crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs`: step 14; `crates/viola-core/Cargo.toml`: proptest dev-dep
- `Cargo.toml` (root): workspace deps, root dev-deps, `[[test]]` entries; `Cargo.lock`

These are the local gates /implement runs. No external process is driven and there is no live leg this chunk, so no
`probe` precondition exists. The boot lifecycle smoke re-runs the previous chunk's form: the fake agent that `boot`
copies changes, so the smoke must still reach `ready`. The filtered entries pin the chunk's key tests by name;
nextest fails an unmatched filter (exit 4 → harness red), so they cannot pass vacuously. The mutation entry runs the
whole chunk diff against this chunk's take-up HEAD `dc01bd9`. The last two entries witness CI on the operator's push.
Given the fold, that means `mutants` concludes success on the push.

- (tests) `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --unit` and `run --integration` print `"cmd":"run","ok":true` on this host,
  and CI's three `test` legs conclude success on the pushed sha (per test-plan §3 `run` step 1).

- (tests) The fake agent's gated script steps are released only by control-file appends, and their order is read
  from `step` receipt lines. No test sleeps. Covered by `run --integration --filter 'binary(cli_fake_agent)'`
  (per test-plan §7 Fake agent; §11 E2E).

- (tests) A bracketed paste + CR yields exactly one `prompt` receipt whose `hex` equals the pasted bytes, and each
  byte typed outside a paste yields one `key` line, including focus-in/out `ESC[I`/`ESC[O` (per test-plan §7; a11y-plan §4 P4).

- (tests) `--suppress-prompt-submit` → `submit:"suppressed"` and no `hook` line. `--local-command-mode` → a `/`-prefixed
  prompt gets `submit:"local-command"` and a plain prompt fires. `--inject-harness-turn` → one `prompt` with
  `origin:"harness"` whose text starts `<task-notification>` (per test-plan §7 Modes; architecture §Established Decisions [Delivery Confirmation]).

- (arch) A `hooks.json` naming an absolute command runs it with its `args`, and the payload's `prompt` key carries the
  prompt text. A non-absolute command whose same-named decoy is first on the per-child PATH never runs (the decoy's
  marker file is absent; receipt `command_absolute:false, ran:false`) (per architecture §Established Decisions [Hook
  Transport], [Deployment / Distribution]).

- (security) With `CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN=<sentinel>` set per child, the receipt's `env` line holds that NAME and
  no receipt byte holds the sentinel value (per security-plan §Bootstrap phases `logging-redaction-wire`).

- (tests) `--report-version 9.0.0 --cli-version 2.1.0 --version` prints `9.0.0 (Claude Code)`, and fixture replay in
  the same run reads `<fixtures>/2.1.0/` (per test-plan §7 Modes).

- (arch) Under `viola run`, a `--exit-no-eof` child's exit is recorded (`process-exit` claude-child,
  `exit_source:"handle-wait"`) while its stdout is still held open (per architecture §Established Decisions [PTY]).

- (obs) Every chain home resolves under `<workspace>/target/e2e-home/`; the keep decision keeps under
  `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES=1` and on a panicking test under `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_FAILED=1`, and removes otherwise (unit-tested
  over all four inputs); `ledger/stamps.json` is absent after `stamped_home` (per obs-plan §9 step 1; test-plan §12 Stamps conflict).

- (security) The hygiene checker returns `absolute-path` for each of the four patterns, `username` for the planted
  host username and `schema` for a script violating `schemas/fake-script.v1.json`; every committed
  `fixtures/fake-scripts/*.json` passes; the walk covers ≥ 1 file by construction (per security-plan §Data Protection
  "Repository fixtures"; test-plan §7 Fixture hygiene).

- (tests) `ViolaName::try_new` agrees with the literal oracle over 512 generated cases, and
  `crates/viola-core/proptest-regressions/lib.txt` exists with the persistence header (per test-plan §7 Seed strategies).

- (tests) Mutation verdict: a Rust-free change yields `ok:true`, `"verdict":"no-rust-delta"`, the diff path and
  `files`, and a planted stale `outcomes.json` is never counted. A Rust delta with no fresh `outcomes.json` yields
  `outcomes-missing`, `ok:false`. Both are unit-tested (operator constraint, scope item 7; per test-plan §3 `run` step 4).

- (tests) `AGENT_RUN_CHUNK_BASE=dc01bd9cd426ab3659ad41a5656dff619dee0fd9 bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --mutants`
  exits 0 with `"survived":0` and `"verdict":"counted"` over this chunk's diff, and after the operator's push the CI

- Leaned `default-features = false` for jsonschema per the arch no-C-building-crates invariant (research.md §Open questions).
- Leaned the existing `viola-test-` home prefix (`run_cli.rs:35`): obs gates read `target/e2e-home/**`, any prefix.

  tokio-based `viola-e2e`". The arch extract's contrary line leaned on withdrawn scope wording (research.md §Extract overrides).

- Inventing payload or output shapes before a recorded fixture is rejected (operator, P4). Hook payloads come only
  from fixture files; the one documented field touched is `prompt`.

- Evaluating hook `matcher`s is deferred. Every `command` for the event runs, and matcher semantics land with the
  drift contract, where recorded `tool_name`s exist.

- Running cargo-mutants on a Rust-free diff and trusting its silent exit 0 is rejected. The harness classifies the
  diff itself, and a stale `mutants.out/` can never feed a verdict.

- A sleep in any test is rejected: order comes from control appends and receipt lines. The fake agent's own
  control-file poll and the `--exit-no-eof` grandchild's bounded hold are inside the double, not in tests.

- Reading `instances/<name>/settings.json` is deferred with `statusline-echo`: the settings-override mechanism is an
  unrecorded ledger row (architecture.md:346).

- Zero-missed gate: the root package's tests must kill every mutant in `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs`
  (test-plan.md:557). Each receipt field and mode needs an asserting test (testing.md Session Additions 2026-09-24).
  Tests that block on the control file must finish inside `[profile.mutants]` 15 s × 2.

- The `--exit-no-eof` test must bound its observation with a deadline loop (the `run_cli.rs:231-238` pattern), never a sleep.
  The test gives `viola run` a PIPED stdout. `viola run` spawns the child with inherited stdio
  (`src/run/mod.rs:152-153`) and records the exit from the process handle (`src/run/mod.rs:115`, `:123`). So viola's
  own exit and the `process-exit` claude-child line arrive while the grandchild still holds that pipe, and a reader
  thread has not yet seen EOF. With `Stdio::null()` (as `run_viola` uses today) nothing is held and the criterion is vacuous.

- Windows: the agent spawns a hook `command` by absolute path; a `.cmd` target is not a concern here (security rules
  cover PTY children). Write the receipt with one `write_all` per line; the stdin thread and the script thread share it.

**Working entry (verbatim):** Fake agent and test-data fixtures — scripted modes and control file, receipts,
temp-home fixture chain under target/e2e-home, fixture scrub-and-schema walk, committed property seeds
**Annotations:** none stand on the entry (`route.py pins`: 5 freight blocks on the markerless tail, none on line 13).

**CI fold (operator-ratified, Setup 5a):** run `35973118026` on sha `dc01bd9cd426ab3659ad41a5656dff619dee0fd9`,
job `mutants` ("Mutation gate (chunk diff)") — completed `failure`; `test (ubuntu-latest)` success;
`test (windows-2025)` / `test (macos-latest)` were in progress at take-up and completed `success` at P3 (re-read via
`gh api …/commits/dc01bd9…/check-runs`). Folded as item 7 below by the operator's word ("Fold into this chunk"),
with the operator's constraint recorded verbatim there.

_P3 premise closure applied 2026-09-24: of 9 `[inferred]` bullets, 8 verified (tag dropped) and 1 corrected (the
Boundaries boot-wiring bullet); 2 further `[premise-corrected]` bullets fix an untagged statement (item 4's chain
location) and add a finding (item 7's stale-outcomes face); evidence in `research.md`._

1. **Fake agent — scripted turns and the control file.** `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs` (root-package `[[bin]]`,
   `required-features = ["fake-agent"]`) grows from the `--version`/Ctrl-C slice to the §7 contract: a JSON turn
   script (`--script <path>`, resolved relative to the workspace root like `--fixtures`) whose gated steps each wait
   for the next line appended to `--control <path>`, read by byte offset (deterministic ordering, no sleeps).
   Checked-in scenario scripts live in `fixtures/fake-scripts/<scenario>.json`, synthetic text only.

2. **Fake agent — receipts.** `--receipt <path>` receives one line per observation: received prompts (text, raw hex,
   `bare_esc`), keystrokes, env names, Unix fds, and hook invocations (exit code, stderr length, stdout bytes). The
   receipt line format is this chunk's to fix (a harness-owned test format, not a product format).
   - Receipt lines are ndjson carrying `v` (project rule: every viola format carries `v`; readers skip unknown
     kinds/fields; architecture §Conventions "Protocol versioning").

3. **Fake agent — modes.** Bracketed paste + Enter accepted as one prompt; `--suppress-prompt-submit`,
   `--local-command-mode`, `--inject-harness-turn`, `--exit-no-eof`, `--vt100-panic-bytes`, `--report-version <ver>`
   (changes only the `--version` answer), `statusline-echo`, `agents --json` with
   `FAKE_CLAUDE_AGENTS_MODE=recorded|oversize|malformed`. Exits on `\x03`.
   - Hook invocation reads the hook commands from the `plugin/` + `settings.json` files `run` wrote, never PATH — but
     no product surface writes those files at HEAD (the plugin folder is Epoch 2 "Instance state and start order";
     hooks are Epoch 2 "Hooks to normalised events"). This chunk builds the reader and the invocation path against
     test-written plugin/settings inputs; the end-to-end hook replay lands with those chunks.
   - Fixture replay of `fixtures/claude/<cli-version>/` has no recorded fixtures to replay at HEAD (`viola verify`
     recording is Epoch 2 "Capability ledger and viola verify"; the drift contract is Epoch 2 "Fake-agent drift
     contract"). This chunk builds the `--fixtures`/`--cli-version` loading seam and exercises it on synthetic test
     inputs only.

4. **Temp-home fixture chain.** rstest `#[fixture]` chain `home → fake_agent_path → stamped_home → booted_wrapper`:
   a not-yet-existing `home` path inside a `tempfile` dir under `<workspace>/target/e2e-home/`; `TempDir::keep()`
   when `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_FAILED=1` on a failing test and always under `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES=1`; env per child via
   `Command::env`, never `std::env::set_var`.
   - [premise-corrected: test-plan §3 `run` step 2 (test-plan.md:542) — "the root package must not dev-depend on the
     tokio-based `viola-e2e`, so the chain exists twice (the sync root copy and the `viola-e2e` copy) against one
     contract"] The chain is built TWICE against one contract: a sync root copy in `tests/support/` (root tests find
     the fake agent via `CARGO_BIN_EXE_viola-fake-agent`) and a copy in `viola_e2e::fixtures` (fake agent from the

- **Tests inline + rstest tables** (`src/obs.rs:389-423`), `<subject>_<condition>_<expected>` naming, real temp files, never mocks.

- **One test per process-global `OnceLock`** (testing.md Session Addition): `PANIC_SINK` and `ProcessCtx` are already set by one test each (`src/main.rs:238`, `src/obs.rs:547`). A catch-site test that sets either needs nextest's process-per-test isolation and must not add a second setter of the same global.

title: Measured facts (the equalities the plan leans on)

data.head: ## Measured facts (the equalities the plan leans on)

body:
- **Open semantics, measured this session.**
  - **Linux 6.6 (WSL2, busybox `cat`):** opening a directory SUCCEEDS and the failure comes at read (`cat: read error: Is a directory`). Opening `<regular file>/config.json` FAILS at open (`can't open …: Not a directory`, ENOTDIR).
  - **Windows 11 (python `open`):** a directory → `PermissionError` errno 13, and a file-as-parent → `FileNotFoundError` errno 2.
  - Rust maps ENOTDIR → `io::ErrorKind::NotADirectory` (≠ `NotFound`) and Windows `ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND` → `NotFound`.

- **The missed-mutant mechanism, re-derived.**
  - **On Linux,** the existing directory test reaches `Err(_)` at `src/obs.rs:197` (a read error), never the open-error arm at :194. The mutant `guard → true` at :193 is therefore unobserved there.
  - **On Windows,** the same test fails at open with `PermissionDenied`, which is :194, so the mutant is caught locally. This is the observed split: 0 survived locally, 1 missed on ubuntu.

- **The kill equality.** `read_diagnostics_level(home)` with `home` = a regular file yields `(INFO, Some(Unreadable))` on Linux and macOS through :194, because ENOTDIR ≠ `NotFound`. Under the mutant, every open error matches :193 and the call yields `(INFO, None)`, so a Unix-cfg case asserting `Unreadable` kills it. The same input on Windows yields `(INFO, None)` legitimately (`NotFound`), and the existing directory case keeps covering :194 there.

- **The mutation gate is diff-scoped** (harness `run.rs:426-440`, `--in-diff`). A chunk diff that adds only a test never re-generates the `:193` mutant, so a green `mutants` job on this chunk's push would be vacuous for it. The ubuntu `test` job running the new case green is the direct witness of the equality above.

title: Scope — Log redaction and never-log floor

data.head: # Scope — Log redaction and never-log floor

body: **Marker:** `2026-09-24-log-redaction-and-never-log-floor` · **Version:** viola-0.1.0 · **Epoch:** Epoch 1 — Foundation

Log redaction and never-log floor — skip-all span fields, redacted payload types, fixed error displays, content-bearing records only in instance detail files  CARRY: chunk 2026-09-24-diagnostics-plane shipped the detail sink. `viola::obs::write_detail` / `detail_line` write owner-only `instances/<name>/diagnostics/detail-<process>.ndjson`, and `schemas/diag-detail.v1.json` already admits `chain` and `drift_report`. Anyhow chains and serde drift reports route through that sink; today only the panic hook uses it.

The merged obs `pii-scrubbing-wire` + security `logging-redaction-wire` phase (obs-plan §3 "Merged phase position"; security-plan §Bootstrap phases). It sits after the diagnostics plane (sinks, `obs_event!`, detail routing target exist) and before "Observability gates" (G1, secret-scan canary and the print/raw-log bans verify it).

- **Skip-all span fields** — every `#[instrument]` in product code takes the `#[instrument(skip_all, name = "<area>.<operation>", fields(..))]` form; no bare `#[instrument]`, no `err`/`ret` on anything that can carry a serde source or user content. The mechanical G1 gate itself belongs to "Observability gates", not here.

- **Redacted payload types** — veil 0.3.0 `#[derive(Redact)]` is the type-level second layer (obs-plan §6, security Data Protection § Logs): a stray `?value` capture of a payload type prints `[REDACTED]`. The `toggle` feature stays banned (already in `deny.toml`).

- **Fixed error displays** — thiserror `Display` impls on `<Crate>Error` enums use fixed messages (no paths, no upstream text, no payloads); anyhow chains stop at the root bin; a serde_json / serde_path_to_error source is mapped to a fixed message before it joins a chain (security-plan §error-sanitization-wire).

- **Content-bearing records only in instance detail files** — the anyhow chain and serde drift reports route through the shipped detail sink (`viola::obs::write_detail` / `detail_line`) into `instances/<name>/diagnostics/detail-<process>.ndjson` (0600) when an instance resolves; never to a role file, stderr error line, `--json` error, or `error.data`.

- **The NEVER-log floor** — the consolidated list in security-plan §logging-redaction-wire (GUI token, launch URL/`.url`, `Cookie`, `CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN`/`_SOCKET`, every R8-stripped `CLAUDE*` value; user content and tool `input` only in instance detail files) is honoured by every sink that exists at HEAD, and no env var, flag or `config.json` key can widen or disable redaction.

**Closure at HEAD (P3):** of the five bullets above, only the anyhow-chain routing and the NEVER-log floor have a live subject at HEAD. Skip-all spans, veil-redacted payload types, fixed `<Crate>Error` displays and drift-report routing have zero sites today (research.md §Subjects at HEAD). For those four the chunk verifies the floor's invariants hold at HEAD and hands the mechanism to the chunk that mints its first subject. [premise-corrected: the entry presumes subjects that research measured absent]

- IN: the root `viola` bin (`src/main.rs` catch site, `src/cmd/*`, `src/run/*`, `src/obs.rs`) and `viola-core` — the only product crates at HEAD (verified: `crates/` holds `viola-core` + the test-only `viola-e2e`).
- IN: the catch site in `main` today discards `Err(_)` → exit 1 with nothing recorded; routing that chain to the detail sink is this chunk's CARRY (verified: `src/main.rs:46`).

- OUT: surfaces whose crates do not exist yet — channel frames/`error.data` (viola-channel), MCP `isError` (viola-mcp), Problem Details + tower-http `make_span_with` + cookie/`?t=` handling (viola-ui), hook payloads (viola-agent-claude). They land with their own route entries. [premise-corrected: "this chunk leaves the mechanism (types, derive, …) they will reuse" — research.md §Subjects at HEAD measured 0 `#[instrument`, 0 product `<Crate>Error` enums, 0 payload types, 0 drift-report producers and no `veil` dependency; under testing.md's observable-effect rule a mechanism with no consumer is an unkillable mutant, so the veil derive, a drift-report writer and fixed-`Display` enums land with their first consumer's chunk, not here]
- OUT: the CI gates that verify this floor (G1 bare-instrument, secret-scan canary, `disallowed-macros`, print bans) — route entry "Observability gates".
- OUT: the R8 `CLAUDE*` strip itself — route entry "PTY wrapper on Windows"; this chunk only guarantees no sink at HEAD can carry those values.

- **Marker:** 2026-09-24-observability-gates · **Version:** viola-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-09-24T12:12:39Z
Turn the obs contract into mechanical gates (obs-plan §3 `obs-ci-gate-wire`, §9, §11 Logs/CI):
- the print/`dbg!` and raw-`tracing` lint bans, with their both-ways proofs;
- a member-list assertion and a panic-hook-first witness;
- in CI, the fmt and clippy steps that do not run today (research.md: the `lint` job runs only the Tokio-free check);
- a checksum-verified PCRE2 ripgrep plus G1 and G3 on all three OSes;
- G2, G4 and the secret scan in the `test` job, with the §9 scan-gated upload order replacing today's unscanned `agent-run-<os>` upload.
The G4 and secret-scan check bodies are tests-owned Rust (test-plan §6) and live as two internal `viola-harness` subcommands (operator decision, P4).

The chunk also owns the mutants failure on `2834e4d` (run `35995290314`), folded on the overseer's direction and fixed at its cause. The root fixture chain's `Wrapper::wait_ready` never looks at the child it spawned, so a wrapper that exits without writing a role line spins to the 20 s readiness deadline. That deadline sits at cargo-mutants' 20 s floor, so both mutants were graded Timeout instead of caught (research.md §Measured facts). The fix has two parts, per the operator's P4 decision "fix by cause and by value":
- **By cause:** readiness fails fast on an observed exit.
- **By value:** every in-test deadline a root-package mutant can reach drops to ≤ 10 s, and so does the nextest mutants kill.

1. **Workspace lint table.** In `Cargo.toml`, add `[workspace.lints.clippy]` with `print_stdout = "deny"`, `print_stderr = "deny"` and `dbg_macro = "deny"`, beside the existing `[workspace.lints.rust]`. The root `[lints] workspace = true` (`Cargo.toml:55-56`) and `crates/viola-core/Cargo.toml` `[lints] workspace = true` stay as they are.

2. **Raw-tracing ban.** Create `clippy.toml` at the workspace root. Its `disallowed-macros` lists `tracing::event`, `tracing::info`, `tracing::warn`, `tracing::error`, `tracing::debug` and `tracing::trace`, each with a reason naming `viola_core::obs_event!`. `obs_event!` already carries `#[allow(clippy::disallowed_macros)]` on its inner `::tracing::event!` (`crates/viola-core/src/obs.rs:155`), so no source change is needed there.

3. **Test-only crate's own table.** `crates/viola-e2e/Cargo.toml` keeps omitting `workspace = true`. Next to its `[lints.rust]` it gains a `[lints.clippy]` table with `dbg_macro = "deny"` and without `print_stdout` / `print_stderr`: the harness prints one JSON document by design (obs-plan §3 `obs-ci-gate-wire`, B5).

4. **Fake-agent exemption (CARRY).** `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs` gains the crate-level `#![allow(clippy::print_stdout, clippy::print_stderr)]` as its first inner attribute (obs-plan §3 `obs-ci-gate-wire` as amended 2026-09-24). Its stdout/stderr bytes are unchanged.

5. **Clean clippy under the bans.** `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features fake-agent -- -D warnings` must pass. Product code has zero print sites (research.md, grep over `src crates/viola-core`: 0 hits). Any hit clippy reports in root `tests/` gets a local `#[allow]` on that test helper, with a one-line reason; a product site never does. The expected count is 0, and the actual count is recorded in the report.

6. **Contract test `tests/contract_lints.rs`** (a new root test file with a `[[test]]` entry in `Cargo.toml` carrying `required-features = ["fake-agent"]`, like its siblings):
   - `workspace_members_inherit_the_lint_table_except_the_harness_crate`: reads the root `Cargo.toml` and every `crates/*/Cargo.toml`. It asserts that each one except `crates/viola-e2e` carries a `[lints]` table whose body is `workspace = true`, and that `crates/viola-e2e` carries none but does carry a `[lints.clippy]` table. It also asserts the checked list is non-empty and contains `viola-core`, so it fails closed.
   - `panic_hook_is_the_first_statement_of_main`: reads `src/main.rs`, finds `fn main() -> ExitCode {`, and asserts that the first non-empty line after it, trimmed, starts with `std::panic::set_hook(`.

7. **Both-ways lint proofs, `scripts/lint-probes.sh`** (new, modelled on `scripts/deny-probes.sh:1-40`). Throwaway Cargo projects go under `target/lint-probes/run-<UTC stamp>-<pid>/`, each with an empty `[workspace]` table.
   - Each probe copies the repo's `clippy.toml` byte-for-byte and takes the repo's `[workspace.lints.clippy]` table text extracted from `Cargo.toml`, so the table is never hand-copied. It sets `[lints] workspace = true` and depends on `viola-core` by path and on `tracing = "=0.1.44"`.
   - Four negative probes must each fail `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` with that lint's own name in the output: `println!` → `print_stdout`, `eprintln!` → `print_stderr`, `dbg!` → `dbg_macro`, and `tracing::info!` → `disallowed_macros`.
   - Two controls must pass: a module under `#[allow(clippy::print_stdout, clippy::print_stderr)]` that prints, and a call to the real `viola_core::obs_event!`.
   - A missing `cargo clippy` prints `tool-missing: clippy` and exits 1.
   - The last line is `lint-probes: 4 bans fired, 2 controls clean`.

8. **Exit-aware readiness, the mutants cause fix** (`tests/support/home.rs`):
   - `Wrapper::wait_ready` (`:151-172`, reached only through `Wrapper::boot` @ `tests/support/home.rs:145`) checks `self.child.try_wait()` on every poll. On an exit it panics at once with `wrapper {name} exited before ready: {status}`, which is distinct from the deadline message `wrapper {name} not ready`.
   - `wait_ready` takes `&mut self`, and `boot`'s local binding at `tests/support/home.rs:139` becomes `let mut wrapper`, a change inside `boot` only. `boot`'s callers (`chain_boots_…` @ `tests/cli_fake_agent.rs:591`, `booted_wrapper` @ `tests/support/home.rs:213`) do not change, because `boot` still returns the `Wrapper` by value.
   - `READY_WITHIN` goes from 20 s to 10 s (`:16`).

9. **Same shape in `tests/run_cli.rs:202-209`.** `run_self_exit_carries_duration_ms` checks `child.try_wait()` on each poll and panics with `wrapper exited before the child started: {status}`. Its deadline goes from 20 s to 10 s.

10. **The witness test for step 8**, in `tests/cli_fake_agent.rs`: `wrapper_boot_exiting_before_ready_fails_as_exited` (`#[rstest]`, `#[should_panic(expected = "exited before ready")]`). It builds a `StampedHome` whose `fake` is a non-existent path under the test's scratch dir, then calls `Wrapper::boot`. `viola run` cannot spawn the child and exits 1 before any `claude-child` start line. That frame is `run_with_a_missing_program_exits_1_with_internal_error` (`tests/run_cli.rs:131-144`): exit 1, exactly 2 role lines (`process-start{self}` and `process-exit{self}`, `internal-error`), and no `claude-child` line. With step 8 the exit branch panics. Without it the loop reaches the deadline message, which does not match `expected`.

11. **Mutants profile below the floor.** In `.config/nextest.toml`, set `[profile.mutants]` `slow-timeout` to `{ period = "5s", terminate-after = 2 }`, a 10 s kill. Rewrite its comment to state the invariant: every in-test wait and the profile kill sit below cargo-mutants' 20 s auto-timeout floor, so a hang is graded caught, never Timeout. `tests/support/fake.rs:12` (10 s) and `tests/cli_fake_agent.rs:575` (5 s) already comply and are unchanged.

12. **`viola-harness schema-check`** (internal subcommand; new module `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/schema_check.rs`; `jsonschema.workspace = true` added to `crates/viola-e2e/Cargo.toml` `[dependencies]`, already in `Cargo.lock` through the root dev-dependency):
   - Walks `target/e2e-home/**`. Every home-level `diagnostics/*.ndjson` that is not a `detail-*` file is validated against `schemas/diag-line.v1.json`. Every `instances/*/diagnostics/detail-*.ndjson` is validated against `schemas/diag-detail.v1.json`.
   - A non-JSON line is skipped and counted as `torn`.
   - It prints one JSON document: `{"v":1,"cmd":"schema-check","ok":…,"files":N,"lines":N,"torn":N,"failures":[{"file","line","keyword"}]}`. `file` is relative to `target/e2e-home`, and no line content is ever included.
   - Exit 0 only when there are no failures and the scope is non-empty. An empty scope gives `ok:false`, `reason:"empty-scope"`, exit 1.
   - Registered in `COMMANDS` (`crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-harness.rs:67`) beside `supervise`. It is not an agent command, so the five-command surface is unchanged.
   - Only regular files are read. A `*.ndjson` path that is a directory is skipped and counted in the document as `skipped_non_file`. Some root tests create a directory at the role-file path to force an I/O error; P5 measured such directories at `target/e2e-home/viola-test-*/home/diagnostics/run-builder.ndjson` in a kept-homes pass, and G2's `awk` warns and skips them too.
   - **Shim forwarding.** `scripts/agent-run.sh` (the `supervise|ui-restart|gate)` arm) and `scripts/agent-run.ps1` (the `switch` arms) both forward `schema-check` and `secret-scan` to the harness unchanged, as internal subcommands, and their header comments list them beside `supervise`. P5 measured that both shims answer any other verb with `{"v":1,"cmd":null,"ok":false,"reason":"usage"}`, exit 2 (`b17.log`). The two shims stay identical in semantics.

13. **`viola-harness secret-scan`** (internal; new module `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/secret_scan.rs`). Scope: `target/e2e-home/**/diagnostics/*.ndjson` (incl. `instances/*/diagnostics/detail-*`), every file under `target/agent-run/` when present, and `target/nextest/ci/junit.xml` when present.
   - **Critical classes** fail anywhere in scope:
     - `claude-stripped`: the literal values `canary-token-value-7f3a`, `canary-socket-value-2b9d` and `canary-entrypoint-value-8e41`;
     - `cookie`: `Cookie:` case-insensitively, or `viola_<digits>=`;
     - `token-query`: `?t=`;
     - `gui-token`: for each home holding `ui/*.url`, the token read from that file.
   - **High class** `content-canary` (`canary-chain-value-5c1e`) fails only in a home-level role file. It may appear in `detail-*` files and `target/agent-run/*` (obs-plan §8 item 6).
   - **Unix mode:** a `diagnostics/` file whose mode is not `0600` is a `mode` hit. On Windows this class is skipped, and the skip is recorded in the document as `"mode_check":"skipped-windows"`.
   - Each hit is `{file, line, offset, class}` and never carries the matched bytes. Hits are written to `target/secret-scan/hits.json`, which is created only when there is a hit. The same document goes to stdout with `ok`, `files` and `hits`.
   - Exit 1 on any hit. An empty `target/e2e-home` scope gives `reason:"empty-scope"`, exit 1.
   - Only regular files are read. A directory at a `*.ndjson` path is skipped and counted, as in step 12.

14. **The canary list stays single-sourced**, via a contract in `crates/viola-e2e/tests/scan_patterns.rs`: `scan_covers_every_canary_the_root_tests_plant`. It greps root `tests/**/*.rs` and `src/**/*.rs` for literals matching `canary-[a-z]+-value-[0-9a-f]{4}`, and asserts each one is in `secret_scan`'s pattern table under a class. The set found must be non-empty.

16. **`scripts/install-ripgrep.sh`** (new): installs the official ripgrep 15.2.0 release binary, whose release builds include PCRE2, into `target/tools/ripgrep/bin/`.
    - It picks the asset for the host triple (`x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`, `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`).
    - It verifies the asset against a sha256 pinned in the script. The value is taken from the release's own `.sha256` asset at implement time.
    - It extracts with `tar` or `unzip` after checking the tool is present, and prints the installed path.
    - `tool-missing: <tool>` → exit 1. A checksum mismatch → exit 1.
    - No new Action is added, so security-plan §Dependency Security's pinned set is unchanged.

Every added `uses:` is `actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1`. `permissions: {}` and per-job `contents: read` are unchanged. The pinned install-action has no ripgrep manifest at `7623a79…` (`gh api …/manifests/ripgrep.json` → 404), so the install is a checksum-verified release download. body: - `log/baseline.log`: `Starting 125 tests across 6 binaries`, `Summary [1.346s] 125 tests run: 125 passed`. The binaries are root-package only: `bin/viola` 84 lines, `bin/viola-fake-agent` 18, `cli_fake_agent` 64, `contract_diag_schema` 18, `contract_fixture_hygiene` 30, `run_cli` 36 (grep of the `) <binary>` prefix). The mutation gate's step log shows `Auto-set test timeout to 20s` and `Unmutated baseline in 44s build + 1s test`: the 1 s baseline puts cargo-mutants at its 20 s floor.

- `log/src__main.rs_line_43_col_5.log:591-620` and `log/src__cmd__mod.rs_line_39_col_5.log:368-397`: in both mutants, only **2 of 125 tests started**, both `wait_ready` consumers:
  - `booted_wrapper_fixture_is_ready_and_receipting`
  - `chain_boots_the_fake_agent_under_viola_with_a_gated_script`

  Each went `SLOW [> 15.000s]` and was killed by `SIGTERM [19.82s]` when cargo-mutants hit its 20 s timeout (`*** result: Timeout`). Two tests running at once means the runner gave nextest 2 test threads.

- **Mechanism, re-derived.** The overseer's claim was marked as a hypothesis and is verified here:
  - Both mutants make `viola` exit 0 at once and write no role line. `main → Default::default()` never runs `dispatch`. `dispatch → Ok(Default::default())` returns before `run` opens a sink.
  - `Wrapper::wait_ready` never looks at the child, so it cannot tell "exited" from "not ready yet". It spins to `READY_WITHIN = 20 s`.
  - 20 s ≥ cargo-mutants' 20 s timeout, so the run is graded Timeout before either test can fail.
  - `[profile.mutants]`'s 30 s nextest kill (15 s × 2) is also ≥ 20 s, so nextest's own termination can never pre-empt cargo-mutants on a hang. The profile comment "a hung test is killed at 30 s" never takes effect under the 20 s floor.

- **Why Windows caught the same mutants** (local `mutants.out/`, `outcomes.json`): the same 20 s auto timeout applied (`debug.log`: `Auto-set test timeout to 20s`), and each mutant was caught in 0.66 s / 0.91 s. The first FAIL was `fake_agent_exit_no_eof_exits_while_stdout_is_held` (`tests/cli_fake_agent.rs:558`, `stdout reached EOF`), which the Windows host scheduled alongside the waiters (more threads). The kill depends on scheduling: on a 2-thread runner that happens to start the two waiters first, no fast-failing test ever starts.

- **In-test deadlines a root-package mutant can reach** (grep `Duration::from_(secs|millis)\([0-9]+\)|READY_WITHIN|deadline` over `tests src crates`; the viola-e2e rows are outside the root mutants run):

  | Site | Deadline | Reachable? |
  |---|---|---|
  | `tests/support/home.rs:16` | 20 s | yes, it hangs both mutants |
  | `tests/run_cli.rs:202` | 20 s | yes, same shape |
  | `tests/support/fake.rs:12` | 10 s | only after a successful boot |
  | `tests/cli_fake_agent.rs:575` | 5 s | yes |
  | `.config/nextest.toml` `[profile.mutants]` | 30 s | on any hang |
- **Readiness in practice:** `booted_wrapper_fixture_is_ready_and_receipting` passes in 0.010 s on ubuntu (ci run log, `(1/86)`), so a readiness deadline far below 20 s keeps a large margin.

- **Exit-aware readiness (harness)** (`crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/boot.rs:229-231`, `:264-266`): readiness returns `Exited(code)` → `run-exited` as soon as the wrapper's exit is observable. The root chain lacks the equivalent. It holds the `Child`, so `try_wait()` is the direct probe (test-plan §3 Readiness: a `process-exit` for `self` arriving first means `run-exited`).

- **Throwaway-project probes** (`scripts/deny-probes.sh:12-40`): prove each ban both ways with a clean control, fail closed on a missing tool (`tool-missing`), and keep scratch under `target/<probes>/run-*`.
- **Canary reporting without bytes** (`tests/run_cli.rs:376-409`): hits are reported as `<where> <variable>`.
- **Job-level env, SHA pins, `persist-credentials: false`, per-job `contents: read`** (`ci.yml` throughout).
- **Waits are bounded file-state or pid probes, never `sleep`** (testing.md Determinism; `tests/support/fake.rs:2`).
- **Tests named `<subject>_<condition>_<expected>`**, with root sync suites at `tests/{cli,hook,…,contract}_<topic>.rs` (testing.md Naming).
- **Tool versions: one source each.** Cargo tools come from taiki-e/install-action `@7623a79…` or `cargo install --locked` (test-plan `:1412`). Actions are SHA-pinned (`ci.yml:22,27,28,76`).

A clean `bash --noprofile --norc` finds no `rg` (measured), so gate-shell commands must not rely on it. The official ripgrep release is 15.2.0 (`gh release view -R BurntSushi/ripgrep`, 2026-07-15). `jq` is on the host through scoop; `jaq` is absent.

Provenance: test-plan §3/§9/§10; architecture §Infrastructure Patterns → CI/CD approach and §Module Boundaries; security-plan §Dependency Security and §Secret Management; obs-plan §9 step order and §10; a11y-plan §10 (the `playwright` breach semantics `gate` must already honour).

1. **`file_mode` as one body, first** (scope item 9, PREREQ). In `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/secret_scan.rs:222-231`, replace the two cfg-split `file_mode` functions with ONE `fn file_mode(path: &Path) -> Option<u32>`:
   - its body holds a `#[cfg(unix)]` block (the existing minimal `PermissionsExt` reader) and a `#[cfg(not(unix))]` block that consumes `path` and yields `None`;
   - the signature is unchanged, and its only production caller is `harness/secret_scan/scan()` @ `secret_scan.rs:64`.

   cargo-mutants then lists exactly 3 `file_mode` mutants (`-> None`, `Some(0)`, `Some(1)`), all in a body Linux compiles:
   - `secret_scan_flags_a_diagnostics_file_that_is_not_owner_only` (`:463`) kills `None`;
   - `secret_scan_passes_a_clean_tree` (`:287`) kills `Some(0)` and `Some(1)` (research M1).

   No new test is needed for the kill. `mode_hit` / `owner_only` keep the decision logic (testing.md SA #7).

2. **`run` selectors** (`crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run.rs`, `Selection` at `:19-36`; its caller `main()` @ `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-harness.rs:134`, plus the two `selection_*` tests):
   - add `coverage` and `fuzz_replay`;
   - `--all` / no selector keep today's meaning (unit + integration + mutants). Neither new selector joins the default, because `--coverage` replaces the nextest calls and `--fuzz-replay` is Linux-only.
   - The `Run` clap struct gains `--coverage`, `--fuzz-replay` and `--leg <name>`. `--leg` is valid only with `--mutants`, and its value must pass `valid_session_id` (`harness/mod.rs:99`), else usage `detail:"invalid-leg"`.

4. **`--fuzz-replay` suite** (test-plan §3 `--fuzz-replay`):
   - off Linux: exit 2 `reason:"fuzz-linux-only"` (the `browser-linux-only` precedent).
   - `cargo fuzz --version` fails → exit 1 `reason:"tool-missing"`, `detail:"cargo-fuzz"`.
   - Otherwise, for every `fuzz/fuzz_targets/<t>.rs`:
     - an absent or empty `fuzz/corpus/<t>/` fails that target (`corpus-empty` in `failures[]`), never a vacuous pass;
     - else run `cargo +<channel> fuzz run --fuzz-dir fuzz <t> fuzz/corpus/<t> -- -runs=0` from the workspace root, where `<channel>` is read from `fuzz/rust-toolchain.toml`, the single source of the fuzz toolchain.
   - No targets at all → exit 1 `reason:"corpus-empty"`.
   - Suite `fuzz-replay`: `passed` = targets exiting 0, `failed` = the rest, `failures[]` names each.
   - The tool invocation is a seam (the program name passed in), so tests drive the `tool-missing` / `corpus-empty` / pass / fail arms against a temp tree with a stub program. There is never a nested fuzz build of this workspace (testing.md SA #1).

5. **`--mutants --leg <name>`** (the P4 union decision). On the `counted` arm, after `outcomes.json` is read, write `target/agent-run/artifacts/mutants-verdict-<name>.json`:
   - `{"v":1,"leg":<name>,"verdict":"counted","mutants":[{"name":<scenario.Mutant.name>,"outcome":"caught"|"missed"|"timeout"|"unviable"}]}`, built from each outcome's mutant name and `summary` ONLY: no `argv`, `log_path` or test output (research M8);
   - on the `no-rust-delta` arm it writes `{"v":1,"leg":<name>,"verdict":"no-rust-delta","mutants":[]}`.

   With `--leg`, the run's `ok` and exit follow the tool arms only (`reason` absent). Survivors are still counted in the suite and in `failures[]`, but the verdict is deferred to `gate` (step 6). Without `--leg`, today's strict behaviour is unchanged.

8. **Zero retries as a checked property** (scope item 5). Add `crates/viola-e2e/tests/zero_retries.rs`, modeled on `scan_patterns.rs`:
   - a plain checker over nextest-config TEXT (line-based: a `retries` key under any `[profile.*]` must be `0`, and `[profile.ci]` must state `retries = 0`) asserts the repo's `.config/nextest.toml` is clean;
   - the same checker flags planted negatives: `retries = 1`, `retries = { backoff = "fixed", count = 2 }`, and a `[profile.ci]` with the line removed.

   It runs in every OS `test` job. Playwright's `retries: 0` has no subject until Epoch 8 and is not touched.

11. **`ci.yml` mutation: two legs plus a union verdict** (P4 decision):
    - The `mutants` job becomes a matrix `os: [ubuntu-latest, windows-2025]` with `fail-fast: false`; its name keeps the os. It runs `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --mutants --leg "$LEG"`, with `LEG` and `AGENT_RUN_CHUNK_BASE` through `env:` only.
    - Each leg uploads ONLY `target/agent-run/artifacts/mutants-verdict-<os>.json` (upload-artifact v7.0.1, 7 days) as artifact `mutants-verdict-<os>`. **The `mutants.out/` upload is removed** (CARRY: M8, outcomes.json holds absolute argv paths and `log/` holds test output).
    - A new ubuntu job `mutants-verdict` (`needs: mutants`, `if: always()`, `contents: read`) runs checkout, toolchain and rust-cache, then `actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1` (`pattern: mutants-verdict-*`, `merge-multiple: true`, `path: target/agent-run/artifacts`), then `bash scripts/agent-run.sh gate --require mutants --mutants-legs ubuntu-latest,windows-2025`.
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/gate.rs`: the `gate` verb and its unit tests (planted-artifact cases for every breach).
- `crates/viola-e2e/tests/zero_retries.rs`: the zero-retries contract test, with a negative probe and a clean control.
- `fuzz/Cargo.toml`, `fuzz/Cargo.lock`, `fuzz/rust-toolchain.toml`, `fuzz/fuzz_targets/viola_name.rs`, `fuzz/corpus/viola_name/*`: the fuzz workspace and its first target.
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/secret_scan.rs`: step 1 (`file_mode` one body; callers: `scan()` @ `:64` only).

- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run.rs`: steps 2–5. `Selection` gains fields, and the `nextest` call sites at `:71`/`:74` gain the coverage sibling. It also gets the fuzz-replay suite, the `--leg` verdict file and its tests.
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/mod.rs`: `pub mod gate;`.
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-harness.rs`: the `Run` flags, `Cmd::Gate` and `COMMANDS` (steps 2, 6).
- `crates/viola-e2e/tests/cli.rs`: step 7 (the `:61` case swap plus new cases).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: steps 10–12.
- `.github/workflows/nightly.yml`: step 13.
- `Cargo.toml`: `exclude = ["fuzz"]` (step 9).
- `.gitignore`: the fuzz output dirs (step 9).
- `scripts/agent-run.sh` / `scripts/agent-run.ps1`: **no change**. `gate` is already forwarded (sh `supervise|ui-restart|gate|schema-check|secret-scan`; ps1 `'gate'` at `:70`), read at P3.
The gates run on this Windows host during /implement. There is no live leg; the standing smoke is the harness cleanup → boot → status → logs → cleanup.
Linux-only halves have their witness in CI on the pushed sha:
- the fuzz replay;
- the ubuntu kill of `file_mode`'s mutants;
- the Linux/macOS coverage floors.
The operator entries at the end read that witness.

Every output path the entries write is gitignored (`git check-ignore -q`, run bare at P5): `target/…`, `mutants.out`. The exception is `fuzz/target/`, which step 9 adds to `.gitignore` before the fuzz build entry first runs.

The local mutation entry uses `--leg`. By construction, its single-leg union cannot kill a mutant that is equivalent or compiled out on Windows: `file_mode -> None` is equivalent here, because Windows has no mode. So its `gate` read is report-only, with a stated forecast. The CI two-leg union is the verdict.
