body: - **Depth:** moderate. The harness crate is mature; the CI workflows, the harness dispatch, `run.rs`, `secret_scan.rs` and the shims were read in full or by section. There are eight host measurements (M1–M8).
- **Reads:** 14 · **Globs/Greps:** 12 · **graph queries:** 1 (45 rows, `db_state` fresh)

- **Harness rules consulted:**
  - `.claude/rules/verification-harness.md`, read in full: 1 Session Addition applied (`--in-diff` mutates only lines the chunk diff touches).
  - `.claude/rules/testing.md`, read in full: 7 Session Additions. Applied: #1 (every function needs an observable effect), #5 (process-global `OnceLock`), #6 (a mutant-reachable wait stays under 20 s) and #7 (keep `#[cfg(unix)]` to a minimal reader).
  - `.claude/rules/host-win32.md`, always loaded: 5 Session Additions, including the separate-`CARGO_TARGET_DIR` rule for a running `.exe`.

- **Platform issues consulted:**
  - Query: cargo-mutants `#[cfg]` platform code reported missed.
  - Fetched source: https://mutants.rs/limitations.html, verbatim: *"cargo-mutants does not yet understand conditional compilation, such as `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]`. It will report functions for other platforms as missed, when it should know to skip them."*
  - This explains the folded CI red (M1). The runner is not at fault.

- **M1: which `file_mode` mutants were missed.** Command: `cargo mutants --list --file crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/secret_scan.rs --workspace` (cargo-mutants 27.1.0).
  - `224:5` is the `#[cfg(unix)]` reader (`secret_scan.rs:222-226`), with `None`, `Some(0)` and `Some(1)`.
  - `230:5` is the `#[cfg(not(unix))]` stub body `None` (`secret_scan.rs:228-231`), with `Some(0)` and `Some(1)` only, because the body already is `None`.
  - The CI run `36005608858` MISSED pair (the overseer's reading: `230:5 -> Some(0)`, `-> Some(1)`) is therefore the **non-unix stub**. Linux never compiles that body, so no Linux test can observe it.
  - The 3 survivors of the prior chunk's local Windows gate were `224:5`, the unix reader, which Windows does not compile. **Each OS misses the other OS's cfg-gated body.**
  - The existing unix tests already observe the mode value: `secret_scan_flags_a_diagnostics_file_that_is_not_owner_only` (`secret_scan.rs:463`, 0644 → `["mode"]`) kills `224:5 → None`, and `secret_scan_passes_a_clean_tree` (`:287`, planted 0600 → exit 0) kills `224:5 → Some(0)/Some(1)`. The CI caught count (70) is consistent with that.

- **M2: the cfg-split census at HEAD.** Command: `grep -rn -A1 -E '#\[cfg\((windows|not\(unix\)|unix|not\(windows\))\)\]' --include=*.rs src crates tests | grep -E 'fn '` gives 2 hits, both `file_mode` (`secret_scan.rs:223`, `:229`). No other cfg-gated function body exists at HEAD, so the blind spot's only live instance is this pair. Epoch 2 (the Windows slice: ConPTY, SQOS pipes, DACL) will add `#[cfg(windows)]` bodies, which the ubuntu-only `mutants` job cannot kill (the fetched limitation above).

- **M3: MSRV build.**
  - `rustup toolchain install 1.96 --profile minimal` resolves to `rustc 1.96.1 (31fca3adb 2026-06-26)`.
  - Build: `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target/msrv-probe cargo +1.96 check --workspace --all-targets --features viola/fake-agent` exits 0, with 0 `warning`/`error` lines (`grep -cE '^(warning|error)'` on the log = 0).

- **M4: MSRV unit leg.** `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.96 CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target/msrv-probe cargo nextest run --workspace --features viola/fake-agent --profile ci -E 'kind(lib) | kind(bin)'` ran 158 tests: 158 passed, 0 skipped, exit 0. `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.96 rustc --version` prints `1.96.1`, so the env override outranks `rust-toolchain.toml`'s `1.98.1` pin. That is the mechanism the MSRV job needs to select 1.96 without editing the pin.

- **M5: coverage, Windows leg.** Command: `cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --features fake-agent --profile ci --ignore-filename-regex '(viola-fake-agent|crates/viola-e2e|tests/support|fuzz/)' --json --summary-only` (cargo-llvm-cov 0.9.1, the CI pin, installed on the host for this probe; cargo-nextest 0.9.133 on the host vs the 0.9.146 CI pin). Result: 248 tests run, 248 passed, exit 0.
  - **The ignore regex does not match on Windows.** The report lists `crates\viola-e2e\...` files, because llvm-cov gives Windows paths with `\`, and `python -c "re.search(r'(…crates/viola-e2e…)', r'D:\…\crates\viola-e2e\src\x.rs')"` returns `False`. `tests/support` is subject to the same defect, and `fuzz/` will be once it exists. Only `viola-fake-agent` (no separator) matches.
  - Totals as reported (e2e wrongly included): lines 97.85 %, functions 97.22 %, regions 97.66 %.
  - **Product-only totals** (the 7 files outside `viola-e2e`: `crates/viola-core/src/{lib,obs}.rs`, `src/{main,obs}.rs`, `src/cmd/{mod,run}.rs`, `src/run/mod.rs`): lines 98.21 % (879/895), **functions 96.55 % (112/116)**, regions 98.34 % (1540/1566). This is above 85 / 95 / 80. Functions has the thinnest margin: 4 uncovered functions, one each in `src/cmd/mod.rs`, `src/cmd/run.rs`, `src/main.rs` and `src/obs.rs`. Losing 2 more drops the Windows leg under 95.
  - The Linux and macOS legs are unmeasured here. Their witness is the CI `test` job's `--coverage` step on this chunk's push.

- **M6: JUnit location under llvm-cov.** `stat` before and after M5: `target/nextest/ci/junit.xml` was rewritten (mtime 15:24 → 15:53), and `target/llvm-cov-target/nextest/ci/junit.xml` does not exist. So test-plan §3 `gate` Inputs' "for coverage it is `target/llvm-cov-target/nextest/ci/junit.xml`" is falsified at nextest 0.9.133 + llvm-cov 0.9.1. nextest's store stays workspace-root-relative under llvm-cov too, the same fact test-plan §3 step 1 already records for `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`. Consequence: the secret-scan root (`secret_scan.rs:43`) and the `junit-<os>` upload path (`ci.yml:124`) remain correct under `--coverage`, with no scan-scope change.

- **M7: zizmor pedantic.** `zizmor --persona pedantic --format plain .github/workflows/` reports 2 findings, both `help[concurrency-limits]` "workflow is missing concurrency setting" (one per workflow): 0 informational, 2 low, 0 medium, 0 high. The default persona reports none.
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/secret_scan.rs` (full). The scan, the `Roots` (the JUnit root at `:43`), `mode_hit`/`owner_only`/`file_mode` (`:213-231`) and the 15 tests.
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/mod.rs` (full): `Workspace::{artifacts, cargo_target, e2e_home}`, `Outcome::{new, usage}`, `write_json`, `read_json`.
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-harness.rs` (full): the `Cmd` enum (no `Gate`, no `--coverage` / `--fuzz-replay`) and `COMMANDS` (`:73-82`, 8 entries).
- `crates/viola-e2e/tests/cli.rs` (55–79): `unbuilt_selectors_and_unknown_commands_are_usage` pins `run --coverage` as usage at `:61`.
- `scripts/agent-run.sh` (40–80) and `agent-run.ps1` (grep): `gate` is already forwarded by both (sh `supervise|ui-restart|gate|schema-check|secret-scan`; ps1 `'gate'` at `:70`).
- `.github/workflows/nightly.yml` (full): one `advisories` job, with no cache and no toolchain action.
- `Cargo.toml` (full): `members = ["crates/*"]`, `rust-version = "1.96"`, proptest `=1.11.0` pinned, `[profile.*] panic = "unwind"`.

     `rustup toolchain install`, taiki-e `cargo-deny@0.20.2`, `cargo deny --version`, then `cargo deny check
     advisories`.
   - No cache of any kind (test-plan §9 Cache column / §11 CI), and no event-payload value in any `run:`.
   - The repo's default branch is `build/viola-0.1.0`, so both triggers are live on push (research.md §Platform issues).

9. **Run zizmor over every workflow and fix every finding at its cause**, keeping the least-privilege shape. Findings on
   HEAD's `ci.yml` are unmeasured (research.md Open questions). A finding is never silenced with a zizmor config,
   ignore comment or persona change. If a finding cannot be fixed within this chunk's boundaries, surface it to the
   operator.

10. **Run the local gates below.** Then hand the tree to the operator for the commit + push and the `nightly.yml`
    dispatch that the CI-witness entries read.
- `deny.toml`: the workspace cargo-deny policy (step 2).
- `deny-sync.toml`: the tokio-only ban config, used for the sync crates as sole roots (step 3).
- `scripts/sync-crates.txt`: the single sync-crate list (step 4).
- `scripts/deny-probes.sh`: the permanent negative ban probes + control (step 5).
- `.github/workflows/nightly.yml`: the weekly advisory run (step 8).

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: add jobs `lint` and `supply-chain` (steps 6-7). The existing `test` and `mutants` jobs
  stay byte-identical except for any zizmor finding fixed at its cause (step 9).

These are the local gates /implement runs. No external process is driven and there is no live leg, so no `probe`
precondition exists. There is no boot smoke: the chunk changes no Rust source and no harness path. The workspace unit
suite is `defer`red on zero `.rs` delta. The mutation entry still runs, because the harness's own `no-rust-delta`
verdict is the assertion. The per-OS `cargo check` runs here on the Windows host; its macOS/Linux legs are witnessed
by CI. The last four entries are operator-driven: the commit+push, the CI read pinned to the pushed sha, the
`nightly.yml` dispatch, and that dispatched run's read pinned to the same sha. The deny/zizmor JSON artifacts
(`target/supply-chain/`, gitignored) have no local producer by design. They are produced by the CI `supply-chain`
job on the operator's push, and that job's `success` is read by the check-runs entry. Every local output path
(`target/deny-probes/`, `mutants.out/`) is gitignored (`git check-ignore -q` exit 0 on each).

  `unmaintained = "all"`, `unsound = "all"`, `yanked = "deny"`, `unknown-registry = "deny"`, `unknown-git = "deny"`
  and exactly one advisory ignore, RUSTSEC-2017-0008 with a `reason` (per security-plan §Dependency Security). The
  evidence is the `cargo deny check` entry.

- (arch) The tokio ban holds per sync crate as sole root for the three triples. Every crate in
  `scripts/sync-crates.txt` passes `cargo deny --config deny-sync.toml … check bans`, and a probe project pulling tokio fails it with
  `error[banned]` (per architecture §Infrastructure Patterns → Build system; §Established Decisions [Concurrency]).
  The evidence is the sole-root loop entry + the `deny-probes.sh` tokio probe.

- (arch) CI job 3: `cargo check` of the listed sync crates, without features, passes on windows-2025, macos-latest and
  ubuntu-latest. An empty or absent-package list fails the step (per architecture §CI/CD approach, job 3; test-plan §9
  Lint row). The evidence is the local `cargo check` entry + the CI read showing all `lint` legs `success`.

- (obs/security) Each of the 13 bans is proven live: `bash scripts/deny-probes.sh` prints
  `deny-probes: 13/13 banned, control clean`, and it runs in CI on every push (per obs-plan §3 otel-sdk-install, §8
  D-19, §9; security-plan §Dependency Security `[[bans.features]]`; arch C-crate ban).

- (tests/security) `zizmor .github/workflows/` exits 0 over `ci.yml` and `nightly.yml` with no silencing config. CI runs
  `zizmor --format=json` on ubuntu and uploads the JSON beside the deny JSON (per test-plan §9 paragraph after the
  Pipeline table and §9 Test report format; security-plan §Dependency Security, CI integration).

- (security) Every workflow has `permissions: {}` at the top, `contents: read` per job, full-SHA `uses:` with a
  version comment, and `persist-credentials: false` on checkout. No `${{ github.event… }}` appears inside a `run:` (per
  security-plan §Dependency Security, CI integration; §Security Anti-Patterns › Code Patterns). The evidence is the
  zizmor entry + the grep probe entry.

- (security/tests) `nightly.yml` runs `cargo deny check advisories` on a weekly `schedule` without code changes, and
  one `workflow_dispatch` run on the pushed sha concludes `success` (per security-plan §Dependency Security, CI
  integration; test-plan §9 Platform). The evidence is the dispatch read entry.

- (tests) The CI run on the pushed sha concludes `success` on every check-run: test ×3, lint ×3, supply-chain, mutants.
  The mutation verdict for this diff is `no-rust-delta` (per test-plan §10 Mutation gate). The evidence is the
  check-runs read entry + the mutants entry.

- Spec anchors: architecture §Established Decisions [Concurrency / Backend Framework], [Module Boundaries];
  §Infrastructure Patterns → Build system, CI/CD approach, directory tree · security-plan §Dependency Security (Audit
  tool, deny.toml additions, Pinning, CI integration, CVE SLA), §Security Anti-Patterns › Code Patterns / API ·
  obs-plan §3 otel-sdk-install, logger-stack-install, §8 PII Scrubbing (D-19), §9 Pipeline integration / Gate
  commands, §10, §11 Logs (D-15) · test-plan §1 supply-chain trigger, §3 ci-tool-install / Closed enums, §9 Pipeline
  structure / Platform / Test report format, §10 Mutation gate, §11 CI · a11y-plan §9 (ci.yml stays the single PR
  workflow).

- Research files inspected: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `Cargo.toml`, `crates/viola-core/Cargo.toml`,
  `crates/viola-e2e/Cargo.toml`, `.claude/docs/commands.md`, `scripts/agent-run.sh`,
  `.claude/rules/verification-harness.md`, `.claude/rules/testing.md`; scratch probes in research.md §Measured facts.

- Decisions: weekly home = `nightly.yml`; ban probes = permanent in CI (operator, P4 AskUserQuestion). Harness
  exposure: leaned NO new `run` suite, per test-plan §3 Closed enums (a new suite value needs a Decisions Log entry).
  The gates are direct CI steps and local commands.

- `cargo deny --exclude viola-mcp …` or `[graph] exclude` for the tokio ban: rejected. Measured false-fail: workspace
  feature unification keeps a shared crate's optional tokio feature on after the enabler is excluded (research.md).

- A cargo-deny `wrappers` allowlist for tokio (test-plan L1617 "added to the cargo-deny tokio wrappers list"):
  rejected. It is a direct-parent allowlist, which architecture §Build system rejects. Under sole roots `viola-e2e` is
  simply not a root.
- A tokio entry in the workspace `deny.toml`: rejected. `viola-mcp`/`viola-ui` will legitimately use tokio.
- A one-time local ban proof: rejected by the operator. A ban no gate sees failing is vacuous.
- A `schedule:` trigger on `ci.yml`: rejected by the operator. Every job would need a schedule guard.

- A cache in `nightly.yml`, a toolchain action, a new third-party action (`cargo-deny-action`, `zizmor-action`), a
  mutable `uses:` ref: forbidden (test-plan §9/§11 CI; security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns).

- Silencing a zizmor finding, or adding any `[bans] skip`/`allow` exception or a second advisory ignore to reach
  green: forbidden (test-plan §11 Quality; obs-plan §11 "a skip counts as admitting it").

- The probe projects live under the gitignored `target/`, but cargo walks up to the viola root `Cargo.toml`. Each probe
  manifest therefore carries its own empty `[workspace]` table (research.md scratch probes used a separate root).

- The probe projects resolve real crates from crates.io, so the script needs the network. An offline host fails the
  probes loudly, which is correct; it never skips them.

- The licence allow-list at HEAD, from the draft run (research.md, cargo-deny 0.19.4): `MIT`, `Apache-2.0`, `Zlib`,
  `Unicode-3.0`. `MIT-0` was unmatched (`warning[license-not-encountered]`). Re-derive it under 0.20.2 and keep the
  list minimal.

- `warning[advisory-not-detected]` for RUSTSEC-2017-0008 and `warning[duplicate]` for `syn` are warnings at HEAD
  (draft exit 0). Neither may be promoted to `deny` in a way that turns the gate red today.

- The deny JSON goes to stderr in cargo-deny's JSON mode. The redirect must keep the step's exit code as the verdict:
  no `|| true`, and no pipe without `pipefail`.

- Channel-root limit (research.md): once `viola-channel` exists and `viola-mcp` enables its `tokio` feature,
  `viola-channel` as its own sole root false-fails, because `cargo metadata` unifies its features. It is then covered

- print / raw-log lint bans, `disallowed-macros`, canary secret scan → *Observability gates*.

- Adding any product dependency (portable-pty, rmcp, axum, veil, interprocess, notify…) — those land with their

- A release workflow, cargo-auditable, cargo-audit (deferred to v1.x).
- New: `deny.toml` (arch §Infrastructure Patterns tree lists it at the root).
- Modified: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`; possibly a new scheduled workflow file.

- Possibly: `scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1}` if the dependency-policy gate is exposed through the harness, and the

- Specs read: architecture §Build system / §CI/CD approach; security-plan §Dependencies (deny.toml additions, CI
  integration, pinning, CVE SLA); obs-plan otel-sdk-install / pii-scrubbing-wire (veil toggle ban) / §9; test-plan

- Only `viola-core` (sync) and `viola-e2e` (test-only) exist today; `viola-pty`, `viola-channel`,

- [premise-corrected: scratch-workspace probe — `--exclude` false-fails under workspace feature unification; the

title: Plan — 2026-09-24-three-os-ci-headless-harness-skeleton: "Three-OS CI and headless harness skeleton"

data.head: # Plan — 2026-09-24-three-os-ci-headless-harness-skeleton: "Three-OS CI and headless harness skeleton"

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-09-24-three-os-ci-headless-harness-skeleton · **Version:** viola-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-09-24T06:05:00Z

Give viola its first build: a Cargo workspace on one pinned toolchain, the headless five-command harness
(`boot · run · status · cleanup · logs`) driving a real product process pair on Windows, macOS and Linux, a
per-chunk mutation gate that runs locally and in CI, and a 3-OS GitHub Actions workflow with SHA-pinned,
least-privilege actions (per test-plan §3 Test Harness Contract, §9 CI Integration, §10 Mutation gate;
security-plan §Dependency Security; architecture §Infrastructure Patterns).

The skeleton is a **walking skeleton** (operator decision, P4 fork 1). Its product side is the **first slice of the
real `viola run`**, in the root bin and on the spawn seam that Epoch 2 extends, not a throwaway stub. No abstraction
is built over code that does not exist yet. It resolves the home, writes the role's JSON lines
(`process-start` / `process-exit` / `panic`) to `<home>/diagnostics/run-<name>.ndjson` (per test-plan §3 Log format,
obs-plan §3, §7), spawns the named child directly, and detects the child's exit on the process handle. The harness
drives that process pair with a detached supervisor and a minimal fake agent. It proves the lifecycle end to end:
readiness, liveness, graceful stop and verified teardown.

Codebase reality (research.md): cold start. No `Cargo.toml`, `src/` or `crates/` exists yet. The setup-seeded
`scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1}` shims already match the contract and are consumed unchanged. The host runs rustc
1.95.0, below the floor. No `main` branch exists on the remote, so the mutation base comes from
`AGENT_RUN_CHUNK_BASE` or the push's `before` sha (operator decision, P4 fork 2).

1. **Toolchain pin.** Create `rust-toolchain.toml` with `channel = "1.98.1"` (current stable, measured with
   `rustup check` on 2026-09-24; ≥ 1.96 floor) and `components = ["rustfmt", "clippy"]`. Run `rustup toolchain
   install` on the host so every cargo call in the repo resolves to 1.98.1 (per test-plan §9 Language version;
   F-19).

2. **Workspace manifest.** Create the root `Cargo.toml`. It is the `viola` bin package plus `[workspace]` with
   `members = ["crates/*"]` and `resolver = "3"`. `[workspace.package]` sets `version`, `edition = "2024"`,
   `rust-version = "1.96"` and `publish = false`, and every member inherits them. `[workspace.dependencies]` pins each
   third-party version exactly, crates.io only. Every profile, including `release` and any custom one, sets
   `panic = "unwind"`. `[workspace.lints]` exists and product members (`viola`, `viola-core`) opt in with
   `[lints] workspace = true`. The root package declares feature `fake-agent` and a `[[bin]] name =
   "viola-fake-agent"` with `required-features = ["fake-agent"]`. Commit `Cargo.lock`. (per architecture
   §Infrastructure Patterns "Build system"; security-plan §Dependency Security Pinning; obs-plan §7 Unwinding)

3. **`crates/viola-core` (born here, with this chunk's consumer).**
   - `ViolaName`: a nutype 0.8.0 newtype over ASCII `[a-z0-9-]`, 1–32 characters, starting with a letter (per
     architecture §Conventions line 174). `ViolaName::try_new` is the only constructor.
   - The service-identity constants `SERVICE_NAME = "viola"` and `VERSION = env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")` (per obs-plan
     §3 Service identity, line 520).
   - One thiserror `CoreError` enum with fixed `Display` strings.
   - Nothing else. `RefusalReason`, `Percent`, `validate_paste_text` and `MAX_FRAME` arrive with their first consumers.
   - Unit tests cover the name grammar at every boundary: empty, 32 vs 33 characters, a leading digit or hyphen,
     upper case, `/`, `..`, and non-ASCII.

4. **Root bin `viola`, the process shell (`src/main.rs`).**
   - The first statement of `main` installs `viola_panic_hook` with `std::panic::set_hook`.
   - Everything after it runs inside one `std::panic::catch_unwind`, and the exit code is decided at that catch site:
     1 for a caught panic.
   - The hook never calls the default hook and never writes stderr. It writes one JSON line with one `write_all` to a
     pre-opened `OnceLock<Arc<File>>` role file. The key set is `timestamp`, `level:"ERROR"`, `target:"viola::panic"`,
     `message:"panic"`, `event:"panic"`, `process` and `instance`. It never includes the panic payload or `corr`, and
     `panic_location` is workspace-relative. Before the role file is open, the hook writes nothing. (per obs-plan §7
     Panic hooks, §3 Init order; design-system §Surface: cli Platform-Specific Notes)
   - Dispatch uses clap 4.6.7. The global option is `--home <dir>`. Home resolution is `--home`, else
     `<user home>/.viola/`. The `VIOLA_DIR` step arrives with `hook`. (per architecture §Cross-cutting Patterns
     "Config management")
   - anyhow is allowed here only (per architecture §Established Decisions [Error Handling]).
   - Clap usage errors exit 2, per architecture §Conventions CLI exit codes.

5. **`viola run <name> -- <program> [args…]`, first slice (`src/cmd/run.rs` + `src/run/`).** Steps, in order:
   1. Parse `<name>` through `ViolaName::try_new` before any path join. An invalid name is a usage error (exit 2).
   2. Create the home and `diagnostics/`. On Unix, directories are created 0700 via `DirBuilderExt::mode` and files
      0600 via `OpenOptionsExt::mode`, never through the umask. On Windows, the protected DACL is the home-integrity
      chunk's (see Constraints).
   3. Open `diagnostics/run-<name>.ndjson` in append mode. Initialize tracing-subscriber 0.3.23 with the obs-mandated
      builder:
      - `default-features = false`, features `fmt,json,registry,std`;
      - an explicit writer;
      - `.log_internal_errors(false)`, `.with_ansi(false)`, `.with_span_list(false)`, `.with_current_span(false)`,
        `.flatten_event(true)`;
      - a `MillisUtc` timer on chrono 0.4.45;
      - a `filter::Targets` level filter only (no env-filter, no `RUST_LOG`).

      Every event is one line and one `write`. If the file cannot be opened, the writer falls back to `io::sink`.
   4. Emit `process-start` with `process:"run"`, `instance:<name>`, `service_name`, `version`, `os` and `pid`
      (message == event; `corr` absent).
   5. Spawn `<program>` directly with std `Command`: no shell, stdio inherited, `VIOLA_DIR` set per child through
      `Command::env`. Emit `process-start` for the child with its pid.
   6. Wait on the child's process handle. Emit `process-exit` with the child's exit code, using fields from the
      obs-plan §6 additive catalog only.
   7. Exit 0. A spawn failure emits `process-exit` with a detail code and exits 1.

   The spawn lives in one function in `src/run/`. The PTY chunk replaces its body with the `viola-pty` seam: no trait,
   no alternative backend (operator note). Upstream text, env values and argv never reach a line (per security-plan
   §Bootstrap phases `logging-redaction-wire`).

6. **Minimal fake agent (`src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs`, feature `fake-agent`).**
   - `--version` prints the real CLI's version line for `--cli-version <ver>` (default a fixed fixture version) and
     exits 0 (per test-plan §7).
   - Any other invocation reads stdin until a `\x03` byte or EOF, then exits 0.
   - It prints no ANSI and only ASCII text (per design-system §Anti-Patterns cli).
   - Scripted modes, the control file, receipts and fixture replay are left out (next chunk).
   - It carries its own `[lints.clippy]` without the print bans (per obs-plan §3 obs-ci-gate-wire, B5).

7. **`crates/viola-e2e` harness: the library.**
   - `publish = false`. Normal deps: serde, serde_json, clap, thiserror, tempfile, sysinfo 0.39.6. No tokio and no
     anyhow in this chunk: no HTTP or MCP client exists yet, and anyhow is root-only (leaned per architecture
     §Conventions "Rust error types"; test-plan §3's tokio dev-dep arrives with the first Tokio client).
   - It has its own `[lints.clippy]` without print bans, one `HarnessError` enum, and modules `harness::{boot, run,
     status, cleanup, logs, supervise}`.
   - `boot` takes a binary-dir parameter. The CLI passes `target/debug`, and tests pass the test executable's own
     target dir (per test-plan §3 `run` step 2). Children are spawned directly and get env through `Command::env`,
     never `set_var`.
   - Readiness and teardown probes are bounded 100 ms file-state or pid probes against deadlines, never
     sleep-as-synchronization. Kill and liveness targets are checked by pid + start time via sysinfo (per test-plan §3
     PID file).

8. **`boot` (`viola-harness boot [--session <id>] [--instance <name>[:<fake-args>]]… [--cli-version <ver>]`).**
   - With no `--instance`, the instances are `overseer` and `builder`. `--ui`, `--unstamped`, `--agents-mode` and
     `--statusline-echo` are not in this chunk's grammar (Constraints).
   - The steps, per test-plan §3 `boot`:
     1. `cargo build --workspace --features fake-agent`. On failure, `reason:"build-failed"`.
     2. A fresh `tempfile::Builder::new().prefix("viola-session-").tempdir_in("<root>/target/e2e-home")?.keep()`
        parent, passing `<parent>/home`, which does not exist yet, so `viola run` creates it.
     3. Copy the fake agent to `target/agent-run/<session>/bin/claude[.exe]`, with that dir first on a per-child
        `PATH`.
     4. (Step 4, `viola verify`, is absent this chunk.)
     5. Write `supervise.json` and spawn the detached `viola-harness supervise --session <id>`. It uses
        `process_group(0)` on Unix and `CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP | DETACHED_PROCESS` on Windows (std `CommandExt`).
        The supervisor spawns, per instance, `<bin>/viola run <name> --home <home> -- <bin>/claude[.exe]
        --cli-version <ver> <fake-args>` with stdin piped and stdout/stderr drained.
   - **Interim readiness**, polled per instance within 20 s:
     - `diagnostics/run-<name>.ndjson` holds a parseable `process-start` line for `process:"run"`, `instance:<name>`;
     - the wrapper pid is alive with a matching start time;
     - the child `process-start` line is present.
   - `session.json` = `{home, instances:[{name, wrapper_pid, started_at, fake_args}], ui:null, supervisor_pid,
     cookie_file:null}`, written once readiness passes.
   - Output: `{"v":1,"cmd":"boot","ok":true,"session":…,"instances":[…]}`.
   - On failure: `ok:false` with `reason` from the closed §3 list (`build-failed | run-exited | readiness-timeout`),
     `instance`, `exit_code` and `missing` naming the unmet checks.

9. **`supervise` (internal).**
   - Owns the wrapper processes and polls for `stop.request` every 100 ms.
   - On stop, it writes `\x03` to each wrapper's stdin and closes it. That is the pipe analogue of test-plan §3
     cleanup step 1; the outer PTY arrives with `viola-pty`.
   - It waits up to 10 s per handle, then calls `kill()` on survivors.
   - It writes `supervisor-exit.json` = `{"v":1,"cmd":"supervise","ok":…,"exits":[{name, exit_code, killed}]}`.
   - Exit 0 when nothing was killed, 1 otherwise.

10. **`status` (`viola-harness status [--session <id>]`).**
    - No `session.json` → exit 2, `{"v":1,"cmd":"status","ok":false,"reason":"unknown-session"}`.
    - Otherwise it prints the §3 Status endpoint shape. `list`, `ui`, `pid` and `uptime_ms` are `null` (no
      `viola list` / `viola ui` yet), `api_sessions_equal_list` is `null`, and an added `instances:[{name,
      wrapper_pid, alive}]` member holds pid+start-time liveness.
    - `state` is `ready` when every wrapper is alive and `degraded` when any is not. `ok` is true only for `ready`.
      Exit 0 for ready, 1 otherwise.

11. **`cleanup` (`viola-harness cleanup [--session <id>|--all]`).**
    - It creates `stop.request`, waits for the supervisor pid (+ start time) to be gone, reads
      `supervisor-exit.json`, and verifies every wrapper and child pid is gone.
    - It then removes the `viola-session-*` parent, the session dir's `session.json` and `supervise.json`. Under
      `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES=1` it keeps the home and reports `home_removed:"kept"`.
    - Report: `{"cleaned":[…],"processes_gone":true,"endpoint_gone":null,"port_free":null,"url_file_removed":null,
      "home_removed":true|"kept","killed":[…]}`. `null` means that no endpoint or UI exists this chunk. Any `false`
      field means exit 1. A force-kill is reported and does not by itself fail cleanup.
    - With no `session.json` it prints `{"v":1,"cmd":"cleanup","ok":true,"cleaned":[]}` and exits 0 (idempotent).

12. **`logs` (`viola-harness logs [--session <id>] [--instance <name>] [--process <role>]`).**
    - It streams ndjson on stdout. Each `<home>/diagnostics/*.ndjson` line becomes
      `{"src":"diag","file":<basename>,"record":<line>}`.
    - A torn or unparseable line becomes `{"src":"diag","file":…,"torn":true,"offset":n}` and is never dropped.
    - `--instance` and `--process` filter on `record.instance` / `record.process`. An absent key equals null.
    - The `events` and `detail-*` sources and the `--kind` / `--after` filters arrive with their producers
      (Constraints).
    - Unknown session → exit 2 with one JSON document.

13. **`run` (`viola-harness run [--unit|--integration|--mutants|--all] [--filter <set>]`).** (operator decision, P4
    fork 3: the grammar grows per chunk)
    - Selectors whose suites are not built yet (`--e2e`, `--browser`, `--coverage`, `--perf`, `--fuzz-replay`,
      `--local-live`) are usage errors: exit 2, one document, `reason:"usage"`.
    - `--all` = unit → integration → doctest → mutants.
    - unit: `cargo nextest run --workspace --features fake-agent --profile ci -E 'kind(lib) | kind(bin)'`.
    - integration: `-E 'kind(test) & !binary(/^(path|tui|mcp|http|sse|cross|chaos|contract)_/)'`.
    - Both are followed by `cargo test --workspace --doc` as suite `doctest`. The doctest counts come from the
      `test result:` lines, with `ignored` as `skipped`.
    - Before each nextest invocation `run` deletes `target/nextest/ci/junit.xml`, and afterwards copies it to
      `target/agent-run/artifacts/junit-<suite>.xml`. If the file is missing after the run, that suite fails with
      artifact missing.
    - Output: `{"v":1,"cmd":"run","ok":…,"suites":[{suite,passed,failed,skipped,survived,artifact,failures[]}]}`.
      The same document is merged by `suite` into `target/agent-run/artifacts/run-summary.json`.
    - Suite names come from the closed nine.

14. **Mutation step (`run --mutants`).**
    1. First delete any existing `target/agent-run/chunk.diff`, so a stale diff can never stand in for this run's.
       Base = `AGENT_RUN_CHUNK_BASE`, else `git merge-base HEAD origin/main`. If neither resolves, or
       `git cat-file -e <base>^{commit}` fails (the all-zero sha included), exit 1 with `reason:"base-missing"` and
       write no `chunk.diff`.
    2. The diff is `git diff <merge-base(base, HEAD)>` against the WORKING TREE, plus a new-file diff for every
       untracked, non-ignored file (`git ls-files --others --exclude-standard`). It is written to
       `target/agent-run/chunk.diff`. On a committed tree this equals test-plan §3's `<base>...HEAD` whenever the base
       is an ancestor. On /implement's uncommitted tree it is the only form that sees the chunk (Constraints).
    3. Run `cargo mutants --workspace --features fake-agent --in-diff target/agent-run/chunk.diff --test-tool=nextest`
       with `NEXTEST_PROFILE=mutants` set per child. `--test-workspace` is not used.
    4. Verdict from `mutants.out/outcomes.json`: `missed == 0 && timeout == 0`. The exit code is checked too: only 0,
       2 or 3 can pass, and 1/4/5/6/70 map to `reason:"mutants-exit-<code>"`.
    5. The suite `mutants` reports `passed` = caught, `survived` = `failed` = missed + timeout, and `artifact` =
       `mutants.out/outcomes.json`. A diff touching no mutable code reports `"mutants":{"tested":0}`.

15. **nextest config (`.config/nextest.toml`).**
    - `[profile.ci]`: `junit.path = "junit.xml"`, `retries = 0`, `slow-timeout = { period = "30s", terminate-after = 4 }`,
      `fail-fast = false`.
    - `[profile.mutants]`: `fail-fast = true`.
    - `[test-groups] fixed-port = { max-threads = 1 }`, plus `[[profile.default.overrides]] filter =
      'test(/default_port/)'`, `test-group = 'fixed-port'`.

    (per test-plan §3 Bootstrap phases test-runner-install)

16. **Tests (each package kills its own mutants; names `<subject>_<condition>_<expected>`).**
    - **`viola-core`:** inline unit tests for `ViolaName`.
    - **Root `viola`:**
      - Inline tests for the timer format (RFC 3339 UTC, ms, `Z`) and for the panic hook. The panic-hook test installs
        the hook in-process, points the `OnceLock` at a temp file, and asserts that one `catch_unwind(|| panic!(…))`
        leaves exactly one `event:"panic"` line, with no payload text and no `corr`.
      - `tests/run_cli.rs` (assert_cmd + tempfile), covering:
        - the `process-start` → `process-exit` line pair and its field set;
        - absent `corr`;
        - a bad name → exit 2 with no file created;
        - Unix modes 0700/0600;
        - a missing program → exit 1 with a `process-exit` detail;
        - no CLAUDE* env values in any line.
    - **`viola-e2e`:**
      - Inline unit tests for argument grammar and usage exits, the `run` summary merge, the outcomes.json verdict
        (missed/timeout/unviable fixtures), the mutants exit-code mapping, the base-missing branch, the torn-line
        envelope and the absent-equals-null filter.
      - `crates/viola-e2e/tests/harness_lifecycle.rs`, which drives `harness::{boot, status, logs, cleanup}` as library
        calls against the real built bins (boot step 1 skipped): ready, then alive, then a diag line streamed, then
        cleanup with `processes_gone`, then a second cleanup with `cleaned:[]`, then a killed-wrapper path giving
        `degraded`.
      - No test shells out to `agent-run` / `viola-harness` (no nested `cargo run`).

17. **CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`).** Triggers are `push` and `pull_request`. The workflow sets `permissions: {}`
    and each job `permissions: contents: read`. Every `uses:` is `owner/repo@<40-hex> # <tag>`:
    - `actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1`, with `persist-credentials: false`
    - `Swatinem/rust-cache@6323deb102c322ba6fcbdcafc7e3dddab59af2b6 # v2.9.2`
    - `taiki-e/install-action@7623a79cdfecb99d681017af368ca353d9f49bb5 # v2.87.19`, with `tool: cargo-nextest@0.9.146`
      (plus `cargo-mutants@27.1.0` in the mutation job)
    - `actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1`, with `retention-days: 7`

    The toolchain comes from `rust-toolchain.toml` through a `rustup toolchain install` step: one version source, no
    toolchain action.

    Jobs:
    - **`test`**: matrix `[windows-2025, macos-latest, ubuntu-latest]`, `fail-fast: false`,
      `env: AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES: "1"`. Steps:
      1. `agent-run run --unit`, then `run --integration`. The shim is `.ps1` on windows (`shell: pwsh`) and `.sh`
         elsewhere.
      2. The lifecycle leg: `boot` → `status` → `logs` → `cleanup` → `cleanup`.
      3. Upload `target/agent-run/artifacts/` as `agent-run-${{ matrix.os }}` with `if: always()`. The path is never
         `diagnostics/`, homes or merged `logs` output.
    - **`mutants`**: ubuntu, `actions/checkout` `fetch-depth: 0`. `AGENT_RUN_CHUNK_BASE` is passed through `env:` as
      `${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha || github.event.before }}`, never interpolated into `run:`.
      1. Run `agent-run run --mutants`.
      2. Upload `mutants.out/` with `if: always()`.

      (operator decision, P4 fork 2)
- `rust-toolchain.toml` — the exact toolchain pin (1.98.1)
- `Cargo.toml` — workspace root + `viola` bin package, `fake-agent` feature, profiles, workspace deps/lints
- `Cargo.lock` — committed lockfile
- `.config/nextest.toml` — `ci` / `mutants` profiles, `fixed-port` group
- `crates/viola-core/Cargo.toml`, `crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs` — `ViolaName`, `SERVICE_NAME`, `VERSION`, `CoreError`
- `src/main.rs` — panic hook first, catch_unwind, clap dispatch, `--home`
- `src/cmd/mod.rs`, `src/cmd/run.rs` — the `run` verb's first slice
- `src/run/mod.rs` — home/diagnostics setup, role logger + `MillisUtc`, the direct-spawn function (Epoch 2's PTY seam point)
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs` — minimal fake agent
- `tests/run_cli.rs` — root integration tests for `viola run`

- `crates/viola-e2e/Cargo.toml`, `crates/viola-e2e/src/lib.rs`, `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/{mod,boot,run,status,cleanup,logs,supervise}.rs`, `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-harness.rs` — the harness

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — the 3-OS workflow + mutation job

- A trait or alternate "backend" around the child spawn — rejected: no abstraction over emptiness. The PTY chunk
  swaps the one function's body for the `viola-pty` seam.

- Pre-creating the home in the harness — rejected: test-plan §3 boot step 2 says a pre-created home inherits the
  workspace ACL. `viola run` creates it.

- The Windows protected DACL on a `--home` outside `%USERPROFILE%` — deferred to the home-integrity chunk (F-45).
  This chunk sets the Unix modes only. No strict-modes check exists to trip yet.

- `--ui`, `--unstamped`, `--agents-mode`, `--statusline-echo` (boot), `--e2e`, `--browser`, `--coverage`, `--perf`,
  `--fuzz-replay`, `--local-live` (run), and `--kind` / `--after` / events / detail sources (logs) — not in the grammar
  until their producers land. They are usage errors now, never a vacuous pass.

- test-plan §3's literal `git diff <base>...HEAD` — replaced by the working-tree + untracked diff from
  `merge-base(base, HEAD)`. /implement never commits, so the committed-only form would mutate nothing and report a
  vacuous `tested:0`. On a committed tree with an ancestor base both forms are equal.

- `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` and `--test-workspace` — rejected: the toolchain file is the one version source, and each
  package's own tests must kill its mutants.

- fmt/clippy as fatal CI steps, cargo-deny, zizmor, the weekly run, the MSRV job, coverage, the release build and the
  `gate` verdict — the later Epoch 1 chunks own these. Locally, fmt and clippy are gates of this plan.

- **Mutation runtime is the chunk's main cost risk.** cargo-mutants rebuilds per mutant, and the whole new tree is in
  the diff. Keep product code small and each branch tested. The local gate has `timeout = 14400` and runs in the
  background. If the CI mutants job threatens the 6 h job limit, use `--jobs` on the ubuntu runner and record it;
  never add an `exclude_re` to dodge a mutant.

- The detached supervisor must outlive `boot`: `process_group(0)` on Unix and `DETACHED_PROCESS |
  CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP` on Windows, both std `CommandExt`, so no new dependency. Stdin is a pipe, so no console is
  needed.
- Windows exit detection is on the process handle (`Child::wait`), never on pipe EOF (per obs-plan §3 line 177).

- The lifecycle test and the gate use the host's `-gnu` default triple, while CI windows uses `-msvc`. Only pure-Rust
  deps are allowed, so both link. Do not add a C-building crate (security-plan §Dependency Security).

- `jq` is on the host (research) and is used only by the local logs gate. CI's lifecycle leg asserts with the shim's
  exit codes plus a `python -X utf8` one-liner, never an unpinned jq.

   is present; if not, print `tool-missing: jq` and exit 1 (the `deny-probes.sh:10-13` precedent).
   - **One judging function** reads cargo `--message-format=json` lines on stdin. It selects
     `reason == "compiler-artifact"` records whose `executable` is non-null and collects each record's
     `target.name`.
     - It fails with `release-check: FAILED — no executable in the build output` when the set is empty. This is the
       non-vacuity guard (obs-plan §9 Gate commands, G2's `test -n` precedent).
     - It fails with `release-check: FAILED — test-only binary <name>` for any name other than `viola`.
     - Otherwise it prints `release-check: viola only`.
   - **Default mode** runs `cargo build --release --locked --bin viola --message-format=json`. Its stdout goes into
     the judging function, and cargo's stderr passes through. A cargo failure fails the script, under pipefail. The
     script honours an inherited `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`: cargo reads it natively, and the script never sets it.
   - **`--probe` mode** feeds synthetic lines to the same judging function. Three records must be refused, each
     matched against its own fixed diagnostic: `viola` + `viola-harness`, `viola` + `viola-fake-agent`, and an empty
     stream. A control record set, `viola` alone, must pass. It prints `release-check probes: 3/3 refused, control

  - (1) The R8 strip removes every `CLAUDE*` name except those defined in the persistent environment. On Windows that is the HKCU/HKLM `Environment` keys; on Unix it is an explicit pass-list in `config.json`. Each stripped and kept name is named in the log.

  - (3) No `VIOLA_*` is set here. It becomes a route-sequencing CARRY on "Instance state and start order".

- **Standing directions:** every guard test gets its remove-the-guard run (0 missed, 0 timeout; the unviable-swamp and test-only verdicts apply) · fold, do not carry · headless agent verification first (fake agent + harness).

`viola run <name> -- <program>` hosts its child in a real pseudo-terminal: ConPTY on Windows (the live target) and openpty on Unix. It does this through a new `viola-pty` seam over portable-pty `=0.8.1` (per architecture §Established Decisions [PTY], §Infrastructure Patterns → Crate dependency direction).

The human's keystrokes reach the child byte-exact and at once, Ctrl-C included, and the child's screen reaches the terminal. viola adds no byte of its own, and child exit is read on the process handle, never on EOF (per layout-templates §Surface: cli / Output structure — `viola run`; design-system §Brand Identity 0.0 row; obs-plan §3 Sink; a11y-plan §1 tui). Research measured what that takes on Windows (research.md §Measured facts 1-4):
- the wrapper switches its own console into raw VT input and VT output while it runs, and restores it afterwards;
- the fake agent does the same, as the real CLI does;
- the child's cwd is set explicitly;
- the program is resolved by viola, never by portable-pty's own search.
A new `viola-agent-claude` crate holds the two Claude-specific decisions (per architecture §Established Decisions [Agent Coverage]; security-plan §Input Validation row "Child executable resolution"):
- **npm-shim resolution:** a `claude.cmd` resolves to its sibling `claude.exe`, and any other `.cmd`/`.bat` child is refused with exit 1 and design's fixed line + hint.

- **The R8 strip, per the operator's ruling:** every `CLAUDE*` name leaves the child's environment except names defined in the persistent environment. A compile-time identity floor is stripped whatever the persistent environment says.

The run logs `process-start{claude-child, pty_backend, env_stripped_count, env_stripped_known, env_kept}` and `process-exit{exit_source}` codes-only (per obs-plan §4 Scenario 1, §6 PTY seam, D-14 as amended).
The harness `supervise`, the root `Wrapper` and the `run_cli` tests leave the stdin-pipe interim for outer PTYs on all three OSes (per test-plan §3 `boot` step 5, `cleanup` 1-2).
Folded in here are:
- the cfg-aware orphans gate (the CARRY's verified hypothesis);
- the ripgrep install's resilience to the Schannel revocation-offline transient, with the sha256 check intact (CI run 36141312209);
- the portable-pty line record (verification-matrix.json#v1-25).

1. **Workspace pins** (`Cargo.toml` `[workspace.dependencies]`).
   - Add `portable-pty = "=0.8.1"` with a rationale comment. The comment is the v1-25 record: 0.9.0 is excluded for wezterm#6783 (Windows `pty.read` garbage, open as of 2026-09-25, 0.9.0 still crates.io's newest); 0.8.1 spawns with `bInheritHandles = 0`; exit is read on the handle.
   - Add `mockall = "=0.15.0"` (testing.md Framework) and `libc = "=0.2.189"` (the version already locked through portable-pty, research fact 10).
   - Extend `windows-sys` features with `Win32_System_Console` and `Win32_System_Registry`.
   - Append `viola-pty` and `viola-agent-claude` to `scripts/sync-crates.txt`.

2. **`crates/viola-pty`** (new; sync; deps portable-pty, `cfg(windows)` windows-sys, `cfg(unix)` libc; `[lints] workspace = true`).
   - **The seam:** a `Pty` trait with spawn · read · write · resize · wait · kill, behind `#[cfg_attr(test, mockall::automock)]`.
   - **Spawn input:** a `SpawnSpec` with an absolute program path, args, cwd, the names to remove and the size.
   - **Spawn behaviour:** spawning always sets `cwd` (research fact 5: portable-pty's default is `%USERPROFILE%`) and applies `env_remove` per name.
   - **Child handle:** a child handle with `wait`/`try_wait`/`kill`. `kill` falls back to `TerminateProcess` on the pid via windows-sys when portable-pty's kill errs, inside an **inline** `#[cfg(windows)]` block (research fact 8). `ExitSource::{HandleWait, KillFallback}` carries which path produced the exit.
   - **`HostTerminal`:** an RAII guard that switches a terminal stdin to raw input and a terminal stdout to VT output, and restores the saved modes on `Drop`. On Windows it clears `ECHO|LINE|PROCESSED` and sets `ENABLE_VIRTUAL_TERMINAL_INPUT`, and sets `ENABLE_VIRTUAL_TERMINAL_PROCESSING|DISABLE_NEWLINE_AUTO_RETURN` on stdout (research fact 2 measured `0x1f7 → 0x3f0`). On Unix it applies `cfmakeraw` via `tcgetattr`/`tcsetattr`. It is a no-op returning `None` when the handle is not a terminal (a pipe).
   - **`host_size()`:** reads the terminal's cols/rows (`GetConsoleScreenBufferInfo` / `TIOCGWINSZ`), `None` off a terminal.
   - **`PTY_BACKEND`:** a `const` `"conpty"`/`"openpty"` chosen by an inline cfg block. It is a const, not a `cfg!()`-valued fn, per the deferred learning in the handoff.
   - **`PtyError`:** thiserror with fixed-message `Display`. The portable-pty `anyhow` error is kept only as a boxed `#[source]` for the detail file, never in `Display` (research fact 5: its message embeds the command line and cwd).
   - **Crate doc:** records the portable-pty line, why, exit-on-handle and non-inheritance (v1-25).

3. **`crates/viola-agent-claude`** (new; sync; deps `viola-core`, thiserror; `[lints] workspace = true`).
   - (a) **`plan_strip(inherited names, persistent names) -> StripPlan { remove, kept, count }`.**
     - A name is stripped when it starts with `CLAUDE` (ASCII case-insensitive on Windows, where env names are case-insensitive; exact on Unix) unless it is in the persistent set **and** not on `IDENTITY_FLOOR`.
     - `IDENTITY_FLOOR` holds the 11 names measured in research fact 7: `CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_CODE_BRIDGE_SESSION_ID, CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION, CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT, CLAUDE_CODE_EXECPATH, CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET, CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN, CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED, CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, CLAUDE_EFFORT, CLAUDE_PID`.
     - Values are never touched: the function sees names only.
   - (b) **`resolve_program(program, PATH, PATHEXT, is_file) -> Result<PathBuf, Refusal>`.**
     - A program containing a path separator is taken as given.
     - Otherwise the PATH is searched: on Windows over the PATHEXT extensions only, never the bare name (fact 5: the extensionless sh shim); on Unix the bare name.
     - A hit or given path whose file name is `claude.cmd`/`claude.bat` (case-insensitive) resolves to `<dir>/node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-code/bin/claude.exe` when `is_file` says it exists (fact 6). The shim is never read or parsed.
     - Every other `.cmd`/`.bat`, a `claude.cmd` without that sibling included, is `Refusal::BatchScriptChild` (arch §Established Decisions [CI/CD]: resolution applies only to the `claude` npm shim).
     - A `.exe`/`.com` or Unix hit is used as is.
   - `AgentError`/`Refusal` are thiserror enums with fixed messages.

4. **Persistent-environment names** (root, `src/run/env.rs`, a minimal OS reader; its decision lives in step 3a).
   - On Windows, enumerate value **names** (never data) under `HKCU\Environment` and `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Environment` via windows-sys Registry. The root gains `windows-sys` as a `cfg(windows)` normal dependency.
   - On Unix, read `config.json` `claude_env_keep`, an array of names each matching `^CLAUDE[A-Z0-9_]*$`, at most 32. Read it with `Read::take(MAX_FRAME)` like `read_diagnostics_level` (`src/obs.rs:190-200`), and add `claude_env_keep` to `CONFIG_KEYS` (`src/obs.rs:33`) so the key is not an `unknown-keys` rejection.
   - A bad value is rejected whole through the existing `ConfigRejection`/`log_config_rejection` path. A floor name in the list is simply ineffective (step 3a), never an error.

5. **The run path** (`src/run/mod.rs`, `src/cmd/run.rs::run()`, the only caller of `spawn_child` @ `src/cmd/run.rs:36`, research §Graph impact).
   - The order is: obs init → `resolve_program` → strip plan → PTY spawn (cwd = `std::env::current_dir()`, size = `host_size()` or 80×24) → `log_child_start` → `HostTerminal` guard → pump.
   - **Pump:** three threads, each body in `std::panic::catch_unwind` with an `Err` routed to `run()`'s exit path:
     - stdin → PTY writer;
     - PTY reader → stdout, flushed per read;
     - a resize poller that compares `host_size()` every 250 ms and calls `resize` on change.
   - **Exit:** `run()` blocks on the child's `wait()`, logs `process-exit{claude-child, child_exit_status, exit_source}`, drops the guard (modes restored), drains the reader for a bounded time after closing the PTY, and logs `process-exit{self}`.
   - **Exit code:** it keeps today's contract: 0 when the child ran (its status is logged), 1 on refusal or internal error.
   - **`log_child_start` fields:** `pty_backend = PTY_BACKEND`, `env_stripped_count`, `env_stripped_known` (the stripped names, comma-joined) and `env_kept` (the kept names, comma-joined). `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` `process-start` gains `env_kept` (string).
   - **`.cmd`/`.bat` refusal:** exit 1 with no child spawned and no `process-start{claude-child}`. It writes `process-exit{self, exit_code:1, detail:"batch-script-child"}` and exactly two stderr lines, `unable: <name>'s command is a .cmd or .bat script` then `hint: pass the real executable, not a .cmd or .bat shim` (design-system.md:772). This is the root bin's first human output site, in one small fn with a local `#[allow(clippy::print_stderr)]` (Cargo.toml lints comment).
   - **Other spawn/resolution failures:** unchanged (`internal-error`, chain to the detail file only).

6. **Fake agent** (`src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs`).
   - At start, before reading stdin, it takes a `viola_pty::HostTerminal` guard on its own stdin/stdout, as the real CLI does (research facts 1-2). A pipe stays a pipe.

   - `env` receipt, `\x03` exit and `--exit-no-eof` are unchanged.

7. **Outer-PTY test driver** (`tests/support/outer_pty.rs`, new; over `viola-pty`).
   - `OuterPty::spawn(program, args, env, cwd)` has a drain thread that appends master bytes to a shared buffer, plus `write`, `resize`, `try_wait` and a bounded `wait_exit`.

The wrapper exits 0 with `process-exit{subject:"claude-child", exit_source:"handle-wait"}`, and the master stream carries none of `unable:`, `hint:`, `error:` or `"event":` (per a11y-plan §3 Keyboard test harness → Tooling, as corrected by research fact 4; layouts §Surface: cli / Output structure — `viola run`).
- (tests) On the Unix legs the outer-PTY stream of a wrapped fake-agent run equals the stream of an unwrapped one byte for byte (per a11y-plan §3 Keyboard test harness → Tooling).

- (tests / arch) `viola-pty` detects exit on the handle: the `--exit-no-eof` fake child's exit is reported by `wait()` while its grandchild holds the output open (real PTY), and a mockall seam test with a never-EOF reader returns on `wait()` (per test-plan §4 viola-pty, §5 Module ↔ PTY; architecture §Established Decisions [PTY]).

- (tests) A PTY `resize` and a host resize under `viola run` each reach the child as a `size` receipt with the new cols/rows, and the child's cwd equals the spawner's (per test-plan §5 Module ↔ PTY; research fact 5).

- (security / obs / tests) With canary values set for the 11 `IDENTITY_FLOOR` names and an unknown `CLAUDE_VIOLA_TEST_NEW_X`, none of those names is in the child's `env` receipt.
  - The start line carries `env_stripped_count` ≥ 12, `env_stripped_known` naming them and `env_kept` naming the kept ones.
  - `secret-scan` finds 0 canary values in any `diagnostics/` file.
  - On Unix a `claude_env_keep`-listed name survives.
  - In `plan_strip` unit tables, a persistent-set name survives, a floor name in the persistent set is still stripped, and a Windows lower-case `claude_x` is stripped.

  (per security-plan §Secret Management → Storage; obs-plan §8, D-14 as amended by ruling 1; test-plan §6 E2 strip half.)

- (arch / tests) `crates/viola-pty` depends on exactly portable-pty `=0.8.1`, windows-sys (`cfg(windows)`) and libc (`cfg(unix)`), and on no viola crate. Both new crates are in `scripts/sync-crates.txt` and pass the sole-root tokio ban, and `cargo deny check` stays four-green with RUSTSEC-2017-0008 the only ignore (per architecture §Infrastructure Patterns → Crate dependency direction; security-plan §Dependency Security).

- (arch / tests) `orphans-check.sh --probe` passes with the `cfg(windows)`/`cfg(unix)` pair clean and the stray firing, and `orphans-check.sh` ends `N/N targets clean` on all three `lint` legs (per architecture §Build system, Boundary review; the CARRY's verified hypothesis).

The real install still verifies 15.2.0, and zizmor stays green on the edited `ci.yml` (per security-plan §Dependency Security → CI integration; obs-plan §9 G1; CI run 36141312209 `lint (windows-2025)`).

The per-OS coverage floors of 85/95/80 hold, witnessed by the three CI `test` jobs inside the operator all-green check-runs entry. Every step 12 guard has its recorded red/green pair in `evidence/`, as one-shot runs (per test-plan §10 Mutation gate, Coverage thresholds; standing direction).

- Parsing `claude.cmd` to find its target is rejected: upstream text is content, never a command (Critical Warnings). Resolution is the fixed sibling path only.
- Byte identity or "no cursor control the child did not emit" as the Windows oracle is rejected: ConPTY emits its own preamble, an OSC 0 title and a nested re-render (research fact 4).

- Setting `VIOLA_NAME`/`VIOLA_DIR`/`VIOLA_BIN` here is rejected (ruling 3): they point at an instance dir and a pinned copy the next entry creates.

- Building the `viola_e2e::fixtures` copy here is rejected: E2 lands only its strip half, in a sync root suite on the root chain (test-plan §2 root `tests/tui_*`). A copy with no consumer is an unobservable body (testing.md 2026-09-24).
- Reading any env **value** in the strip, the registry reader or a log is rejected: names only (security-plan NEVER-log floor).
- A `sleep` in a test is rejected. Tests wait on receipt/role-file lines, bounded below 20 s and exit-aware (testing.md). The product's 250 ms resize poll is product timing, not test sync.

- **Mutants and cfg:** the Windows-only bodies are the console modes, the registry reader, `TerminateProcess` and the `.cmd` refusal test. They are killed only on the windows leg, and the Unix termios / `claude_env_keep` bodies only on ubuntu (testing.md 2026-09-24). Keep each OS body a minimal reader and the decisions in the plain fns of step 3.

- **Supervisor leak hazard:** a mutated `stop`/`cleanup` that leaks a PTY-owning supervisor locks `viola-harness.exe` and swamps the leg with unviable mutants (verification-harness.md). Every booted-session test keeps its `Drop` guard.

- **ConPTY close ordering:** after `wait()` returns, closing the PTY may be needed before the reader sees EOF, and a grandchild (`--exit-no-eof`) may hold the console. `run()` must exit within its bound regardless. Measure the drain on this host and record the reading in `evidence/`.
- **Windows env names are case-insensitive:** `plan_strip` compares ASCII-uppercased names on Windows only, via an inline cfg in one shared fn.
- **`env_stripped_known` and `env_kept`** are comma-joined strings: the schema types `env_stripped_known` as a string (`schemas/diag-line.v1.json` allOf[25]).

1. **ConPTY + the unmodified fake agent.** The fake agent was spawned through portable-pty 0.8.1 `openpty` + `spawn_command`, then sent `ab\r` and `\x03`.
   - It received `61 62 0d` followed by `0a`. ConPTY's cooked console turned CR into CR LF, delivered it only after Enter and echoed `ab\r\n` onto the master.
   - `\x03` never arrived and the child did **not** exit within 5 s (killed).
   - **So the fake agent as it stands cannot be driven through a PTY on Windows.**

2. **ConPTY + a child that sets raw VT input.** The child called `SetConsoleMode(stdin, mode & ~(ECHO|LINE|PROCESSED) | ENABLE_VIRTUAL_TERMINAL_INPUT)`, going from `0x1f7` to `0x3f0`.
   - It received exactly `61 62 0d 03`, with no echo, and exited 0 on `0x03` (`EXIT success=true code=0`).
   - The cooked control repeated fact 1.
   - This is what a TUI like `claude` does itself (brief §4.1 S1: it switches bracketed paste on by itself).

3. **Nested: outer ConPTY → relay → inner ConPTY → raw child.** The relay is shaped like viola: it puts its own console into raw VT input plus VT output processing, pumps both ways, and exits on the child's `wait()`.
   - With the relay's raw mode on, the child got `61 62 0d 03` and the relay exited 0 via the handle.
   - With the relay's raw mode **off** (control), the relay's console line-buffered (`61 62 0d 0a`), `\x03` never reached the child, and nothing exited in 5 s.
   - **So on Windows the wrapper must put its own console stdin into raw VT input (and stdout into VT processing) when stdin/stdout are consoles, and restore the original modes on exit.** Otherwise a human keystroke is delayed until Enter and Ctrl-C is swallowed, a Critical Warning ("never … delay a human keystroke").

4. **ConPTY writes bytes the child never wrote.** On every spawn the master stream began `ESC[?9001h ESC[?1004h ESC[?25l ESC[2J ESC[m ESC[H` and carried `ESC]0;<child command line>BEL` and `ESC[?25h`.
   - The OSC 0 title holds the spawned exe path, and through two layers both titles appear.
   - Nested, the outer stream is the outer ConPTY's **re-render** of the inner output (`ESC[K\r\n` rows, cursor moves).
   - **So on Windows neither byte identity nor "no cursor control the child did not emit" is achievable.** The only sound zero-own-bytes oracle there is the absence of viola's own literals, as a11y-plan §3 already states for ConPTY. On Unix openpty does not re-render, so a byte comparison is possible there (not measurable on this host).

5. **portable-pty 0.8.1 spawn facts (source):**
   - `CreateProcessW(..., bInheritHandles = 0, EXTENDED_STARTUPINFO_PRESENT | CREATE_UNICODE_ENVIRONMENT, ...)`, with stdio set to `INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE` under `STARTF_USESTDHANDLES` (`psuedocon.rs:119-142`). Non-inheritable is satisfied.
   - With no `cwd` set, the child's cwd defaults to `%USERPROFILE%` (`cmdbuilder.rs:560-567`). **viola must pass `cwd` = its own current dir** (a bare `claude` without the wrapper starts in the caller's dir).
   - The Windows PATH search tries the **exact name first**, then PATHEXT (`cmdbuilder.rs:532-556`). On this host `<npm prefix>/claude` (an extensionless sh shim) exists beside `claude.cmd`, so `CommandBuilder::new("claude")` resolves to the sh script, which `CreateProcessW` cannot run. **viola resolves the program itself and hands portable-pty an absolute path.**
   - A spawn failure is an `anyhow` error whose message embeds the command line and cwd (`psuedocon.rs:152-157`), which is content. It also goes to `log::error!`, which reaches no sink because viola installs no `log` bridge.
   - `kill()` is `TerminateProcess(handle, 1)` (`win/mod.rs:72`), `wait()` is `WaitForSingleObject(INFINITE)` and `try_wait()` exists.
   - `CommandBuilder` starts from the parent's full env, and `env_remove` removes names (measured: `CLAUDECODE` and `CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN` set then removed were absent from the child's `env` receipt).

6. **npm shim layout (this host, CLI 2.x).** `<npm prefix>/` holds `claude` (sh: `exec "$basedir/node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-code/bin/claude.exe"`), `claude.cmd` (`"%dp0%\node_modules\@anthropic-ai\claude-code\bin\claude.exe" %*`) and `claude.ps1`. The real binary is `<npm prefix>/node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-code/bin/claude.exe`, which exists. This matches brief §4.1 "Windows details". A resolution that **never parses the shim** (upstream text is content): the resolved `claude.cmd`'s sibling `node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-code/bin/claude.exe`, when it is a file.

7. **Inherited `CLAUDE*` names on this host.** The shell this session runs in holds 11 names (read as names only, values never read): `CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_CODE_BRIDGE_SESSION_ID, CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION, CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT, CLAUDE_CODE_EXECPATH, CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET, CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN, CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED, CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, CLAUDE_EFFORT, CLAUDE_PID`. The spike child additionally saw `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MOUSE_CLICKS`. S6 says the spike's parent held **14** and names only five, and the brief says "the wrapper removed them", i.e. all 14. **No artifact enumerates the 14.** The test-plan's "literal 14-name S6 list" cannot be copied from S6 as written.

8. **cargo-modules 0.27.0 and cfg-gated files** (scratch crates, Windows host):
   - `#[cfg(unix)] mod gated;` + `src/gated.rs` gives exit 1, `orphaned module 'gated' at src/gated.rs`.
   - `#[cfg(windows)]` gives exit 0.
   - The same `cfg(unix)` crate with `--target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` gives exit 0.
   - An inline `#[cfg(unix)] mod gated { … }` gives exit 0.
   - **The CARRY's hypothesis is verified, and `--target <own triple>` per leg does not fix it.** A `cfg(windows)` file is an orphan on the Linux/macOS legs, and only analysis for a triple that compiles it clears it.

9. **curl exit 35 and retries.** Git-for-Windows curl 8.18.0 (Schannel) is the curl the runner's `shell: bash` step resolves (`C:\Program Files\Git\mingw64\bin\curl.exe`). It was pointed at a local TCP server that answers with non-TLS bytes, which gives handshake failure exit 35, the class of `CRYPT_E_REVOCATION_OFFLINE`.
   - `--retry 3 --retry-delay 1`: exit 35 after **1** connection. The existing flag does not retry this class, which is why attempt 1 failed at once.
   - Adding `--retry-all-errors`: **4** connections.
   - `--ssl-revoke-best-effort --retry 2 --retry-all-errors`: 3 connections, and the flag is accepted.
   - `--ssl-revoke-best-effort` turned out to work on this host's real HTTPS fetch of crates.io (exit 0).

**Marker:** `2026-09-25-pty-wrapper-on-windows` · **Version:** viola-0.1.0 · **Epoch:** Epoch 2 — Windows slice I: wrapper, events, ledger
**Working entry (verbatim title + hint):** PTY wrapper on Windows — viola run passthrough with zero own bytes, npm-shim resolution, .cmd refusal, CLAUDE* strip, process-handle exit, portable-pty line recorded

- **`viola run` over a real PTY on Windows (ConPTY).** The wrapper spawns its child inside a pseudo-terminal and pumps it both ways: the child's screen bytes reach the wrapper's stdout, and the human's keystrokes reach the child. Passthrough carries **zero own bytes**: viola adds nothing to the child's output stream and nothing to its input stream that the human did not type.

- **The `viola-pty` crate** (the PTY seam: spawn · read · write · resize · wait · kill over portable-pty `=0.8.1`; it knows no agent). `src/run/mod.rs::spawn_child` is the one spawn function, and its body becomes this seam (CARRY, three-os-ci chunk).

- **npm-shim → `claude.exe` resolution.** A `claude` found on PATH as an npm shim (`claude.cmd` / `claude.ps1` / an extensionless sh shim) resolves to the real `.exe` it launches, which is then spawned directly.
- **`.cmd` / `.bat` refusal.** A child that resolves to a `.cmd` or `.bat` is refused, never spawned (portable-pty bypasses BatBadBut escaping; security rule "never spawn a `.cmd`/`.bat` PTY child").

- **R8 `CLAUDE*` strip.** Per the founder ruling of 2026-09-25 (P4; intent-incomplete, amended at P5 validation-1), every `CLAUDE*` name is removed from the child's environment except names defined in the persistent environment. On Windows that is the HKCU/HKLM `Environment` keys; on Unix it is an explicit pass-list in `config.json`. Each stripped and kept name is named in the start line.
  - The plan adds a compile-time identity floor that is always stripped, which keeps the "no config key disables a control" invariant: the 11 identity names measured on this host (research fact 7).
  - The tests check that a session-identity name is stripped, a persistent-config name survives, and an unknown new `CLAUDE*` name is stripped.
  - The S6 "14 names" are enumerated nowhere (research fact 7). Today `spawn_child` passes the full inherited environment, so the strip is this entry's (CARRY). The stripped values are secrets that must never reach a log, event, snapshot, fixture or error body.

- **Process-handle exit.** The child's exit is read from its process handle (`wait`), never inferred from EOF on the PTY. The logged `process-exit{claude-child}` carries it (`exit_source = "handle-wait"`, or `"kill-fallback"`). The wrapper's own exit-code contract stays as it is at HEAD: 0 once the child ran, 1 on refusal or internal error (`src/cmd/run.rs:36-47`).

- **The portable-pty line recorded** (requirement v1-25 / intent F-25): the chunk that writes the PTY seam records which portable-pty line it uses and why, with the Windows defect re-checked, keeping the seam's contract, exit-on-handle detection and non-inheritable handles. Research re-checked it: wezterm#6783 is still open against 0.9.0, 0.9.0 is still crates.io's newest, and 0.8.1 passes `bInheritHandles = 0`. The record lives beside the pin (the `[workspace.dependencies]` comment) and in the `viola-pty` crate doc. The `TerminateProcess` kill fallback via windows-sys is part of the seam (arch §Established Decisions [PTY]).

- **Host terminal in raw mode.** [premise-corrected: research facts 1-3 — through ConPTY a cooked console line-buffers keystrokes until Enter, echoes them and swallows `\x03`, both in the child and in the wrapper's own console] "Passthrough with zero own bytes" requires two things. First, the wrapper puts its own console/tty stdin into raw VT input (and stdout into VT processing) when they are terminals, and restores the modes on exit. Second, the fake agent sets its own terminal raw, as the real CLI does. Without both, a human keystroke is delayed and Ctrl-C never arrives. The child's cwd is set to the wrapper's cwd (portable-pty otherwise defaults to `%USERPROFILE%`, research fact 5). Host-size changes are forwarded to the child PTY (resize).

- **Zero own bytes, Windows oracle.** [premise-corrected: research fact 4 — ConPTY itself emits `ESC[?9001h ESC[?1004h ESC[?25l ESC[2J ESC[m ESC[H`, an OSC 0 title with the command line, and a re-render when nested] On Windows the witness is the absence of viola-authored bytes (its literals, refusal/hint/error text, diagnostic lines), not byte identity and not "no cursor control the child did not emit". A byte comparison applies on the Unix legs.

- **Marker:** 2026-09-25-security-prerequisites · **Version:** viola-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-09-25T12:40:00Z

Close the two security-plan Decisions Log open questions before the chunks they block, with evidence that lives in the
repo and runs in CI (per security-plan §Security Decisions Log → Open questions; §Bootstrap phases
`auth-scaffolding-baseline`):

- **The SQOS spike.** Can interprocess 2.4.4's `local_socket::Stream::try_from(OwnedHandle)` adopt a handle that windows-sys
  `CreateFileW` opened with `SECURITY_SQOS_PRESENT | SECURITY_IDENTIFICATION | FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED`? It blocks the
  Wrapper-channel client chunk.

- **The SHA-256 pick.** Which pure-Rust crate computes the truncated `<hash>`? It blocks the Instance-state chunk that
  writes `bin/`.
P3 measured both premises in a scratch probe (research.md §Measured facts):
- The spec's own path **passes**: the server reads `SecurityIdentification`.
- A no-SQOS open reads `SecurityImpersonation`, so the check discriminates.
- `FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED` is load-bearing, since non-overlapped adoption hangs.
- `sha2 =0.11.0` (no default features) passes the C-build ban and the licences, and builds on the 1.96 floor.
This chunk turns those measurements into durable witnesses:

- a `#[cfg(windows)]` integration test that pins the exact open the channel client will reuse, with its discriminating
  control;
- a known-answer test that makes the hash crate part of the resolved graph `cargo deny` checks.

No product crate is created: `viola-channel` and `viola-state` belong to their first consumers, per architecture
§Established Decisions [Module Boundaries].

The chunk also carries the founder's licence ruling of 2026-09-25 (relayed by the overseer). The now-public repo is licensed
**MIT OR Apache-2.0**: root `LICENSE-MIT` + `LICENSE-APACHE`, the `license` key in every manifest, and a README line.

It records the operator's P4 ruling that interprocess's two `0BSD` transitive crates enter through **per-crate licence
exceptions**, the narrowest widening. The allowlist itself is untouched. The wrap records this as a security-plan /
architecture Build-system amendment.

2. **Root dev-dependencies** (`Cargo.toml` root package).
   - Add `sha2.workspace = true` to the existing `[dev-dependencies]`.
   - Add a new `[target.'cfg(windows)'.dev-dependencies]` table with `interprocess.workspace = true` and
     `windows-sys.workspace = true`.
   - Declare no `[[test]]` entry: the two new test files need no `fake-agent`, and auto-discovery picks them up.

3. **SQOS witness.** Create `tests/channel_sqos_open.rs`, a file-level `#![cfg(windows)]` integration test.
   - **The client-open recipe:** a named helper that opens the pipe path with `CreateFileW(GENERIC_READ | GENERIC_WRITE, 0,
     null, OPEN_EXISTING, SECURITY_SQOS_PRESENT | SECURITY_IDENTIFICATION | FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED, null)`, wraps the
     handle as an `OwnedHandle`, and adopts it with `interprocess::os::windows::named_pipe::local_socket::Stream::try_from`.
     The SQOS and overlapped flags are the recipe's own constant, so the remove-the-guard run edits one line.
   - **The test-owned server:**
     - a same-user pipe instance created BEFORE the client opens, which is the ordering that replaces any wait;
     - it accepts one client, reads 4 bytes, calls `ImpersonateNamedPipeClient`, reads `TokenImpersonationLevel` through
       `OpenThreadToken(TOKEN_QUERY, OpenAsSelf = TRUE)` + `GetTokenInformation`, calls `RevertToSelf`, writes 4 bytes
       back, and reports the level plus the bytes it read.
     - Research's probe used windows-sys `CreateNamedPipeW` + `ConnectNamedPipe`. test-plan §8 prefers the interprocess
       server API; /implement may use it only if it exposes the accepted handle for `ImpersonateNamedPipeClient`.
   - **Pipe name:** unique per test, `\\.\pipe\viola-test-sqos-<pid>-<label>`. That is outside the `viola-<h12>` endpoint
     namespace (the `viola-test-` prefix can never be 12 lowercase hex characters) and never reused. `try_overwrite` is
     never used.
   - **Test `sqos_identification_open_adopted_reads_identification`:**
     - the recipe → `Stream` writes 4 bytes and reads the server's 4 bytes back;
     - the server-observed level equals the literal `SecurityIdentification` (1);
     - the bytes match both ways.
   - **Test `sqos_flags_absent_open_reads_impersonation`:**
     - the discriminating control: the same exchange with a handle opened with only `FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED` (no SQOS
       flags);
     - it asserts the server reads `SecurityImpersonation` (2), which proves the measurement can go red;
     - it opens through the same helper shape with the flags passed in, never through interprocess's default connect.
   - **Hygiene:**
     - The server thread is joined; no `sleep` anywhere.
     - No print or `dbg!`: the root package's print bans apply to tests.
     - Levels are compared as integer literals, never `Debug` strings.
     - Every `unsafe` FFI call is confined to a small helper, with a `// SAFETY:` line.

4. **Hash known-answer test.** Create `tests/contract_content_hash.rs`, an rstest `#[case::…]` table over `sha2::Sha256`
   with published FIPS 180-2 / NIST vectors as literal lowercase-hex digests:
   - `""` →
     `e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855`;
   - `"abc"` →
     `ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad`;
   - the 448-bit two-block message `"abcdbcdecdefdefgefghfghighijhijkijkljklmmnopnopq"` →
     `248d6a61d20638b8e5c026930c3e6039a33ce45964ff2167f6ecedd419db06c1`.

   A second test asserts the `<hash>` truncation rule (security-plan §Data Protection, Code-bearing artefacts): the first
   16 hex characters of the digest, i.e. the first 8 bytes. `"abc"` gives the literal `ba7816bf8f01cfea`, `""` gives
   `e3b0c44298fc1c14`, and each truncation is exactly 16 lowercase hex characters. The oracle digests are literals; the test
   never derives an expected value from a second hashing path.

5. **Licence exceptions** (`deny.toml` `[licenses]`, per the operator's P4 ruling):
   - Add two `[[licenses.exceptions]]` entries, `crate = "doctest-file"` and `crate = "recvmsg"`, each
     `allow = ["0BSD"]`, with a comment naming why: interprocess 2.4.4's transitive crates, and 0BSD, OSI-approved and
     more permissive than MIT.
   - The `allow` list stays exactly `["MIT", "Apache-2.0", "Zlib", "Unicode-3.0"]`.
   - Add no `ignore`, `skip` or `[bans]` change.

6. **Licence files and keys:**
   - Create `LICENSE-MIT`: the standard MIT text with `Copyright (c) 2026 Turbolet85` (the founder's ruling at P4).
   - Create `LICENSE-APACHE`: the standard Apache License 2.0 text, unmodified.
   - `Cargo.toml` `[workspace.package]` gains `license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"`, and the root `[package]` gains
     `license.workspace = true`.
   - `crates/viola-core/Cargo.toml` and `crates/viola-e2e/Cargo.toml` each gain `license.workspace = true` beside their
     other `.workspace = true` keys.
   - `fuzz/Cargo.toml` gains `license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"` as a literal. It is its own workspace and cannot inherit.
   - `publish = false` stays everywhere.

8. **Lockfile.** Let cargo regenerate `Cargo.lock` from steps 1–2 (any build does it). `fuzz/Cargo.lock` must stay
   byte-unchanged, because the fuzz package gains no dependency.

9. **Remove-the-guard runs** (one-shot at /implement, never gate entries). Record each reading in
   `chunks/2026-09-25-security-prerequisites/evidence/remove-the-guard.md`:
   - (a) Drop `SECURITY_SQOS_PRESENT | SECURITY_IDENTIFICATION` from step 3's recipe constant (keep `FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED`).
     `sqos_identification_open_adopted_reads_identification` must go red, reading level 2. Restore it and show it green.
   - (b) Drop `FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED` from the recipe. Record what the test does:
     - research measured a hang (research.md case B);
     - the ci profile's slow-timeout terminates it; under `run --integration`, record the reading;
     - restore the flag.

     This reading makes the load-bearing flag's evidence durable. If it hangs past the harness bound, record the
     termination as the reading.
   - (c) Alter one KAT digest literal by one hex digit. The KAT test must go red; restore it.

10. **Mutation.** Run the windows leg of the in-diff mutation gate (base 874420d).
    - Prediction, to be measured: 0 mutants are generated, because every `.rs` delta is in `tests/` targets, which
      cargo-mutants does not mutate (research.md §Scope premise closure, hypothesis).
    - Whatever the count, the verdict must read `counted` with 0 missed, 0 timeout and unviable <= caught (test-plan §10
      Mutation gate).
    - Any survivor gets a killing test in this chunk (fold, do not carry).
- `tests/channel_sqos_open.rs` — `#![cfg(windows)]` SQOS open witness plus its discriminating no-SQOS control (steps 3, 9a, 9b).
- `tests/contract_content_hash.rs` — `sha2` SHA-256 KAT table and the 16-hex truncation (steps 4, 9c).
- `LICENSE-MIT` — MIT text, `Copyright (c) 2026 Turbolet85`.
- `LICENSE-APACHE` — Apache License 2.0 text.
- `README.md` — title, one-paragraph description, `## License` section.
- `chunks/2026-09-25-security-prerequisites/evidence/remove-the-guard.md` — the three one-shot readings (written by /implement).
- `crates/viola-core/Cargo.toml` — `license.workspace = true`.
- `crates/viola-e2e/Cargo.toml` — `license.workspace = true`.
- `fuzz/Cargo.toml` — `license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"`.
- `deny.toml` — two `[[licenses.exceptions]]` (0BSD: `doctest-file`, `recvmsg`).
- `Cargo.lock` — regenerated by cargo (new dev-dependency graph).
The gates run on this Windows host during /implement.
- **Rust delta:** the delta is test-target-only plus manifests. The workspace lint and test gates run, and none defers.

- **No smoke leg:** no product binary behaviour, boot path or harness path changes. `src/` and `crates/viola-e2e/src/`
  are untouched (research.md §Files to modify).

- **Separate target dir:** the msrv entry uses its own `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` so the pinned toolchain's artifacts are not
  churned (host-win32 §Session Additions 2026-09-24).

- **One-shot mutating controls:** step 9's remove-the-guard runs are never entries, because the light gate re-runs entries
  verbatim. The non-mutating guard probes below re-check their subjects on every re-run.
