- `deny-sync.toml` (full): `exclude-dev = true`, tokio ban. `scripts/sync-crates.txt` = `viola-core` only.

- `scripts/deny-probes.sh`: 13 probes (`sed -n 19,33p scripts/deny-probes.sh | grep -c '|deny'` = 13). It prints
  `deny-probes: 13/13 banned, control clean` on success (line 83).

- `.config/nextest.toml` (full): `ci` profile `retries = 0`, slow-timeout 30 s × 4. The `mutants` profile kills at
  5 s × 2.

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:
  - `test` runs `agent-run run --coverage` on `[windows-2025, macos-latest, ubuntu-latest]`.
  - `mutants` runs `run --mutants --leg` on `[ubuntu-latest, windows-2025]`, then `gate --mutants-legs`.

- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run/coverage.rs:11`: `COVERAGE_IGNORE` = `(viola-fake-agent|crates[/\\]viola-e2e|tests[/\\]support|fuzz[/\\])`.
  Root `tests/*.rs` files are NOT ignored, so a new test file's own functions count toward the per-OS function floor
  (95) on the OS that compiles them.

- interprocess 2.4.4 source (`D:/dev/rust/cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-*/interprocess-2.4.4/src/os/windows/`):
  - `named_pipe/local_socket/stream.rs:21`: `type StreamImpl = DuplexPipeStream<Bytes>`.
  - `stream.rs:111` `impl TryFrom<OwnedHandle> for Stream` delegates to
    `named_pipe/stream/impl/handle.rs:68` `impl TryFrom<OwnedHandle> for PipeStream<Rm, Sm>`. That impl:
    - checks `get_flags`;
    - **re-opens the handle through `np_wrappers::reopen_overlapped`** (`named_pipe/c_wrappers.rs:176-182`:
      `ReOpenFile(h, access, share, FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED)`, which passes **no SQOS flags**);
    - keeps the original handle if the re-open fails.
  - interprocess's own client open is `named_pipe/c_wrappers.rs:152-170` `connect_without_waiting`, a `CreateFileW` with
    only `FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED`: no SQOS, which confirms the spec's warning.

title: Measured facts (scratch probe, not repo code)

data.head: ## Measured facts (scratch probe, not repo code)

body:
Probe: `{scratchpad}/p3probe/`, a standalone Cargo project with an empty `[workspace]` and its own target dirs. Each case
creates a unique `\\.\pipe\p3probe-<pid>-<case>` server (`CreateNamedPipeW`, byte mode, 1 instance). The server:
1. `ConnectNamedPipe`, then `ReadFile` 4 bytes;

2. `ImpersonateNamedPipeClient` → `OpenThreadToken(TOKEN_QUERY, OpenAsSelf=TRUE)` →
   `GetTokenInformation(TokenImpersonationLevel)` → `RevertToSelf`;
3. writes `pong`.
The client writes `ping` and reads `pong`. Each case runs in its own process under `timeout 20`.

The probe ran on toolchains `1.98.1-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` (the repo pin, CI's target) and stable-gnu, with identical
results. Case A ran 3× with identical results.
| case | client open | adopted via `Stream::try_from` | server level | bytes both ways |
| A | windows-sys `CreateFileW(SECURITY_SQOS_PRESENT \| SECURITY_IDENTIFICATION \| FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED)` | yes | **1 = SecurityIdentification** | yes |
| B | same, **without** `FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED` | yes | — (**hangs**, killed at 20 s) | — |
| C | std `OpenOptions::security_qos_flags(SECURITY_IDENTIFICATION)`, no overlapped | yes | — (**hangs**, 20 s) | — |
| D | std `OpenOptions` + `custom_flags(FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED)` + `security_qos_flags(SECURITY_IDENTIFICATION)` | yes | **1** | yes |
| E | case A's flags minus overlapped, used as a plain `std::fs::File` (no adoption) | no | 1 | yes |
| F | `CreateFileW(FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED)` only, no SQOS | yes | **2 = SecurityImpersonation** | yes |
| G | interprocess default `LocalSocketStream::connect` | n/a | **2** | yes |

- **The spec's spike passes:** case A yields `SecurityIdentification` after adoption. The `ReOpenFile` inside `try_from`
  does not lose the level: the level is fixed by the client's connect-time QoS, and the re-open keeps the same
  connection.

- **`FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED` is load-bearing:** a non-overlapped handle adopted by `try_from` hangs the exchange (cases B
  and C). The measured fact is the hang. Its cause is unmeasured (hypothesis: the re-open and the sync-over-overlapped
  I/O interplay).

- **The measurement discriminates:** F and G read level 2. A test asserting `== SecurityIdentification` goes red when the
  SQOS flags are removed, which is exactly the remove-the-guard reading.

- **A safe-Rust equivalent exists** (case D, no `unsafe` on the client side). The spec names the windows-sys path, and it
  passes, so D is recorded as a fact for the channel chunk, not as a replacement.

- **windows-msvc:**
  - interprocess 2.4.4 → doctest-file 1.1.1 (proc-macro), recvmsg 1.0.0, widestring 1.2.1, windows-sys 0.61.2 →
    windows-link 0.2.1.
  - sha2 0.11.0 → cfg-if 1.0.5, cpufeatures 0.3.1, digest 0.11.3 → block-buffer 0.12.1, crypto-common 0.2.2,
    hybrid-array 0.4.15, typenum 1.20.1.
- **linux-gnu:** sha2's tree as above.
- **aarch64-apple-darwin:** sha2's tree plus `cpufeatures → libc 0.2.189`.
- **No `cc` on any triple.** windows-sys 0.61.2 links through `windows-link`, not `windows-targets` import libs.

  - with the SQOS flags removed, the level reads 2 and the test goes red;
  - with a KAT digest altered, the test goes red.

1. How should the root graph accept 0BSD (`doctest-file`, `recvmsg`, via interprocess)? As a per-crate
   `[[licenses.exceptions]]` (measured green), as `"0BSD"` added to `allow`, or with interprocess deferred? → blocks:
   plan-decision.

2. The MIT copyright holder line in `LICENSE-MIT` (git author and GitHub owner = `Turbolet85`). → blocks:
   plan-decision.
**Working entry (verbatim):** Security prerequisites — SQOS pipe-handle spike and pure-Rust SHA-256 pick, both recorded ahead of the channel client and bin/ writes; no unprotected-connect fallback
**Epoch:** Epoch 2 — Windows slice I: wrapper, events, ledger · **Version:** viola-0.1.0

It settles the two **open questions** in the security-plan Decisions Log (`security-plan.md` §Decisions Log → Open questions,
the SQOS spike and the SHA-256 crate). Each blocks a later chunk under the Bootstrap `auth-scaffolding-baseline` rules
(`security-plan.md` ~:365-375): the `viola-channel` client needs the SQOS answer, and the `viola-state` `bin/` writer needs
the hash crate. Settling a question means measuring it at HEAD, leaving evidence in the repo, and having the Decisions Log
entry turned from an open question into a decision. Phase and implement never amend the spec; the chunk's wrap records it
from the evidence.

- The question as the plan states it (`security-plan.md` ~:609): does interprocess 2.4.4's
  `interprocess::os::windows::named_pipe::local_socket::Stream::try_from(OwnedHandle)` accept a handle that windows-sys
  0.61.2 `CreateFileW` opened with `SECURITY_SQOS_PRESENT | SECURITY_IDENTIFICATION | FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED`?

- The answer is a **measurement**, not a reading. Open the handle that way against a test-owned, same-user pipe server,
  adopt it, and exchange bytes in both directions. The server side calls `ImpersonateNamedPipeClient` and reads the thread
  token's `TokenImpersonationLevel`: it must be `SecurityIdentification`, never `SecurityImpersonation` or higher. This is
  the shape of test-plan's "Windows client SQOS" negative (`test-plan.md` ~:1282), used here as the spike's pass
  criterion.

- **Fail path:** if the adoption refuses the handle, or the level is wrong, the chunk records a working replacement SQOS
  open instead, measured the same way. The Windows client chunk stays blocked until a working open is recorded.

- **No unprotected-connect fallback:** interprocess's default connect (`connect_without_waiting`, which opens without SQOS)
  is never an accepted outcome, a fallback or a test double for the client open. The evidence must show the protected open
  itself.
- Windows-only (`#[cfg(windows)]`). Unix has no SQOS; its server verification (`peer_creds`) belongs to the channel chunk.

- Pick the crate that computes the truncated SHA-256 `<hash>` (first 16 hex characters of the digest) of the exe bytes for
  `bin/<version>-<hash>/` and `plugin/<version>-<hash>/` (`security-plan.md` ~:265, :599, :611).
- The pick is shown to compute SHA-256 correctly: a published known-answer vector and the 16-hex truncation.
- **Never FNV-1a or `DefaultHasher`** (`security-plan.md` ~:519).

- Not the `viola-channel` crate, its listener (SDDL, `accept_remote(false)`), its client verb path, or the pid +
  start-time server verification (that is the Wrapper channel entry).
- Not the `bin/` / `plugin/` writer, the re-hash-before-reuse check, or strict-modes (the Instance state entry).
- The spike and the pick are evidence and a pinned dependency. They are not the production API.

title: Plan — 2026-09-26-ci-chunk-base-and-union-verdict: "CI chunk base and union verdict"

data.head: # Plan — 2026-09-26-ci-chunk-base-and-union-verdict: "CI chunk base and union verdict"

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-09-26-ci-chunk-base-and-union-verdict · **Version:** viola-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-09-26T19:50:00Z

After this chunk, every CI run of an operator pass mutates the WHOLE chunk, so a fix push re-reads everything (founder
ruling 2026-09-25; V15 instance half; V17 fix commits live). The mutation base stops coming from the push event
(`ci.yml:166`) and is derived by the harness from the repository's own history. It is the last master-flip commit
reachable from the parent of the oldest operator pre-CI commit, a bound no mid-pass commit can move (measured at this
phase: the unbounded pickaxe moves to a fix commit that edits a `· complete ·` line; the bounded one holds). The rule
lives in `resolve_base` only, so a local run and CI read the same base (per test-plan §3 `run` step 4 Base; architecture
§Infrastructure Patterns → CI/CD approach).

The `gate --mutants-legs` union judges each mutant only on the legs that COMPILE its line. A mutant unviable on the leg
that compiles its code is not a survivor, whatever the other leg reads. A mutant missed on a compiling leg stays one.
This closes run 36165685381's breach (`HostTerminal::enter -> Some(Default::default())` at `crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs:395`
/ `:420`) without a product change. Outcomes alone cannot carry this rule: "compiled out" and "missed on a compiling
leg" both read `missed` (research.md §Measured). So the gate evaluates the `#[cfg]` attributes around each mutant's line
in the checked-out source. The leg verdict file keeps its ratified names-and-outcomes content (per test-plan §3
`gate`, §10 Mutation gate; obs-plan §8 integration point 6).

`secret-scan` stops reading the mutation leg's `target/agent-run/chunk.diff`. That file is repository source text by
construction, so it hits on the scan's own `?t=` pattern whether fresh or stale. The `harness-<os>` upload stops
shipping it too, so the scan still covers every file that upload ships. The planted-secret red tests stay (per
test-plan §3 `secret-scan` Scope, §6 Canary; obs-plan §9 step 3; security-plan §Secret Management).

1. **The derived base** — `resolve_base` (`crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run/mutants.rs:34`; its one production
   caller `mutants()` @ mutants.rs:239, re-exported @ run.rs:26). Resolution order:
   a. `AGENT_RUN_CHUNK_BASE`, trimmed and non-empty, stays an explicit override, unchanged. CI stops setting it
      (step 6), and the harness's own tests keep pinning bases through it.
   b. Otherwise read `.andromeda/master-route.md` from HEAD's tree and take every `pending` record's marker (a line
      starting `{marker} · pending · `). Find the OLDEST commit in HEAD's history whose subject carries
      `chore({marker}): operator pre-CI commit` for any of those markers. The bound is that commit's parent. With no
      pending record, or no such commit (a local run before the pass, a 0-pending push), the bound is HEAD.
   c. The base is `git log -1 --format=%H -G ' · complete · ' {bound} -- .andromeda/master-route.md`. When that commit
      IS HEAD (the wrap push, whose own commit flips the record), the base is `HEAD^`. That push then reads its own
      delta, as it does today, never an empty diff.
   d. With no flip in history, fall back to today's `merge-base HEAD origin/main`. Otherwise `None` →
      `base-missing`, unchanged, and no `chunk.diff` is written (mutants.rs:238–242).
   Restate the doc comments at mutants.rs:33 and run.rs:80.

2. **The base in the run document** — the `run --mutants` document (the `counted` doc at mutants.rs:304 and
   `unmutated` at :168) gains `"base": "<full sha>"`. It is a commit id, never a path. The operator reads it in each leg's
   log to see that every run of the pass read the same base. The leg verdict file does not change.

3. **Base tests** (inline `mod tests` in mutants.rs, names prefixed `chunk_base_`, temp repos built like `git_repo()`
   @ run.rs:274, oracles are literal shas the test captured):
   - `chunk_base_holds_the_flip_across_a_pass`: the phase probe as a test. Flip → `chore(m): operator pre-CI commit` →
     a code-only `fix(m): …` → a `fix(m): …` that edits a `· complete ·` line. Every commit resolves to the flip's sha.
   - `chunk_base_is_the_last_flip_before_any_pre_ci_commit`: a pending record with no pre-CI commit, and no pending
     record at all, both resolve to the last flip.
   - `chunk_base_of_the_wrap_push_is_its_parent`: the wrap commit that flips the record resolves to its parent.
   - `chunk_base_bound_is_the_oldest_pre_ci_commit`: two commits carry the pre-CI subject, and the bound is the older
     one's parent.
   - `chunk_base_override_wins`: an explicit value beats the derivation.
   - The existing `resolve_base_needs_a_real_commit` (mutants.rs:384) stays green unchanged. It covers a repo with no
     master route and no `origin/main` → `None`.

4. **Which legs compile a line** — a new harness module `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/cfg_legs.rs`, declared in
   `harness/mod.rs`. Given the workspace root, a mutant name (`{path}:{line}:{col}: {description}`, as the leg files
   carry it) and the named legs, it returns the legs whose target compiles that line.
   - It parses the file with `syn` and collects every `#[cfg(…)]` on a syntax node whose span covers the line: items,
     impl and trait items, inline modules, fields, statements, expressions, match arms, and inner `#![cfg]`. At HEAD
     that means fn-level (viola-pty lib.rs:393/417) and statement-level (lib.rs:435/442) attributes.
   - It evaluates them per leg with three values: true, false, unknown. The leg family comes from the leg name's
     prefix: `windows-` → windows; `ubuntu-` → unix + linux; `macos-` → unix + macos.
   - Known predicates: `unix`, `windows`, `target_os = "linux"|"macos"|"windows"`, `target_family = "unix"|"windows"`,
     `not`, `all`, `any`. Everything else, `test` and `feature` included, is unknown.
   - A leg is dropped ONLY when some covering cfg is PROVEN false for it. An unknown leg family, an unparsable name, an
     unreadable or unparsable file, a line outside every cfg, and an unknown predicate all keep the leg. Uncertainty
     never exempts a mutant.
   - `cfg_attr` is not evaluated. Its one site gates no code (lib.rs:113).

5. **The union by compiling legs** — `union` (`crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/gate.rs:117`; its one caller `gate()` @
   gate.rs:63):
   - For each mutant name, its judged legs are the named legs that compile its line (step 4). When that set is empty
     (a body no named leg compiles, e.g. macOS-only), every named leg judges it, as today, so it is never silently green.
   - A mutant is red iff no judged leg reads `caught` and some judged leg reads `missed` or `timeout`. Readings of the
     other legs are ignored.
   - A missing leg file stays `artifact-missing` with no mutant judged.
   - `gate()` gains the source root as a parameter. `gate_cmd` passes `ws.root` (viola-harness.rs:194), and the 15
     test call sites in gate.rs pass a temp dir.
   - The existing `gate_union_is_red_only_where_no_leg_caught_the_mutant` (gate.rs:411) stays green as written: its
     names are not paths, so every leg judges them.
   - Restate the doc comment at gate.rs:115–116.

6. **CI wiring** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`):
   - Remove the `AGENT_RUN_CHUNK_BASE` line (:166), keep `LEG`, and add a comment that the harness derives the base.
   - Update the `mutants` comment (:140–141) to the compiling-leg union.
   - The `harness-<os>` upload (:110–117) ships `target/agent-run/` minus `!target/agent-run/chunk.diff`.
   - The `mutants-verdict` job already checks out the same sha, and the gate reads its source there. Nothing else
     changes: no `concurrency:`, no new action, and `permissions` untouched.

7. **secret-scan scope** — `scan` (`crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/secret_scan.rs:62`; caller `secret_scan()` :59) skips
   exactly one file, the mutation leg's `<agent_run>/chunk.diff`. A `chunk.diff` anywhere else under the capture is still
   scanned. The doc comment names why: repo source by construction, not runtime capture, and never uploaded (step 6).
   Every class, the report shape and `empty-scope` stay as they are. Tests, names containing `skips_the_mutation_diff`:
   - `secret_scan_skips_the_mutation_diff`: a `?t=` line in `agent_run/chunk.diff` → `ok:true`.
   - `secret_scan_skips_the_mutation_diff_only_at_its_path`: the same bytes in `agent_run/logs.ndjson` and in
     `agent_run/x/chunk.diff` → two `token-query` hits.
   The existing planted-secret tests (:308, :353, :422) stay green unchanged.

8. **Union tests** (inline `mod tests` in gate.rs and cfg_legs.rs, names containing `compiled_legs_`; source trees
   written into a temp dir; oracle names are the literal recorded strings):
   - `union_by_compiled_legs_clears_the_recorded_breach` (the witness): the two records of run 36165685381 verbatim.
     `lib.rs:395:9 … Some(Default::default())` is windows unviable / ubuntu-latest missed; `:420:9` is the reverse. The
     tree puts a `#[cfg(windows)]` fn over line 395 and a `#[cfg(unix)]` fn over line 420 → `ok:true`.
   - `union_by_compiled_legs_control_without_cfg_keeps_both`: the same records over the same tree without the cfg
     attributes → exactly the two breaches, in today's words.
   - `union_by_compiled_legs_missed_on_the_compiling_leg_stays_red` (the negative): a windows-only fn missed on windows
     → red, even when the ubuntu leg reads `caught`.
   - `union_by_compiled_legs_shared_code_unviable_and_missed_stays_red` (the negative for shared code): windows
     unviable and ubuntu missed on an uncfg'd fn → red.
   - `union_by_compiled_legs_body_no_leg_compiles_is_judged_by_all`: a `#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]` fn missed on both
     legs → red.
   - `compiled_legs_*` tables in cfg_legs.rs cover each of the five shapes at HEAD plus the `target_os` and
     `target_family` forms, fn-level against statement-level placement, nesting (a cfg'd impl around a cfg'd fn), and
     every conservative arm: unknown predicate, unknown leg name, unparsable name, missing file, line outside any cfg.

9. **Dependencies** — root `Cargo.toml` `[workspace.dependencies]` pins `syn = "=2.0.119"` (default features off;
   `full`, `parsing`, `visit`) and `proc-macro2 = "=1.0.107"` (`span-locations`, for line numbers), both at the
   lockfile's resolved versions (research.md §Measured). `crates/viola-e2e/Cargo.toml` consumes them as
   `.workspace = true`. No product crate takes them.

11. **Operator pass** (overseer direction 1, V17): the operator's pre-CI commit
    `chore(2026-09-26-ci-chunk-base-and-union-verdict): operator pre-CI commit, for the run this chunk's verdict reads`
    comes first, then the push entry below. A red CI read is fixed by
    `fix(2026-09-26-ci-chunk-base-and-union-verdict): operator fix after CI run {id}, {what it changes}`, pushed
    fast-forward, never an amend, rebase or force-push.
    - With step 1 landed, the pre-CI commit's own CI run already uses the derived base: bound = the pre-CI commit's
      parent (e486544), base = fcca1ce.
    - Every later fix run reads the same whole chunk. Record each leg's `"base"` field (step 2) and each run's verdict in
      `evidence/operator-pass.md`.
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/cfg_legs.rs` — which named legs compile a mutant's line (step 4), with its inline tests.
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run/mutants.rs` — `resolve_base` rule, `base` in the run document, `chunk_base_` tests.
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run.rs` — the doc comment at :80.

- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/gate.rs` — `union` by compiling legs, `gate` gains the source root, 15 test call sites,
  `union_by_compiled_legs_` tests.
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/mod.rs` — declare `cfg_legs`.
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-harness.rs` — `gate_cmd` passes `ws.root` (:194).
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/secret_scan.rs` — skip the mutation diff at its exact path, tests.
- `crates/viola-e2e/Cargo.toml` and root `Cargo.toml` (`[workspace.dependencies]`) — the `syn` / `proc-macro2` pins.
- `Cargo.lock` — the feature change only, no new crate.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — :140–141 comment, :166 removal, :115 upload exclusion.

The gates run on this Windows host during /implement. The Rust delta is harness-only (`viola-e2e`) plus manifests and
`ci.yml`; no product crate changes and no gate defers. There is no boot smoke: this chunk changes no boot path and no
harness lifecycle verb, so the harness lifecycle is not re-driven here (the CI `test` jobs drive it on every push).
Order matters twice:
- `run --integration` keeps the homes that `secret-scan` needs, or the scan reads `empty-scope`.

- `run --mutants` precedes `secret-scan`, so the scan runs over a live `target/agent-run/chunk.diff`. This chunk's diff
  touches `secret_scan.rs`, which holds `?t=`; the probe between them proves the residue is there.

The remove-the-guard runs (step 10) mutate source and revert, so they are ONE-SHOT runs at implement, never entries. Both
readings of each go to `evidence/guards/`, and the `run --unit` entries guard every property on re-run.

The witness replay (`gate … --artifacts …run-36165685381/artifacts`) reads run 36165685381's two recorded leg files
against HEAD's tree. `crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs` is byte-identical to the 17ea8c7 tree those files were cut from
(`git diff --stat 17ea8c7 HEAD -- crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs`: empty). CI's ubuntu leg and the union are read by the
operator entries at the end.

body:
- (tests / arch) Across a simulated pass, the derived base holds the last flip on every commit: flip → pre-CI commit →
  code fix → a fix editing a `· complete ·` master line. Before any pre-CI commit it is the last flip, and on the wrap
  push it is HEAD's parent. An explicit `AGENT_RUN_CHUNK_BASE` still wins. A repo with no flip and no `origin/main`
  still exits `base-missing` with no `chunk.diff` (`chunk_base_*` + `resolve_base_needs_a_real_commit` in the
  `run --unit` entries; per test-plan §3 `run` step 4 Base; architecture §Infrastructure Patterns → CI/CD approach).

- (tests) The local windows leg run WITHOUT `AGENT_RUN_CHUNK_BASE` prints `"base":"fcca1ce…"` and `counted`, with 0
  missed, 0 timeout and unviable ≤ caught (the `run --mutants` entry). In CI both legs and the union read success on
  the final HEAD, and every run of the pass records the same `base` (operator entries; per test-plan §10 Mutation gate).

- (tests / obs) Over run 36165685381's recorded leg files and HEAD's tree, the compiling-leg union reads `ok:true`.
  Today's gate printed exactly the two `lib.rs:395:9` / `:420:9` breaches over the same files (the replay entry;
  research.md §Measured).
  - In unit tests the recorded shape clears, and the same records without cfg attributes breach.
  - A mutant missed on its compiling leg stays red, even when the non-compiling leg reads caught. Shared code
    unviable-and-missed stays red, and a body no named leg compiles is judged by every leg.
  - Each is a `union_by_compiled_legs_*` test (per test-plan §3 `gate` union bullet; obs-plan §10 Build / deploy failure
    conditions; a11y-plan §10 Standard+ invariants).

- (security / obs / tests) `secret-scan` reads `ok:true` over kept homes plus a live `target/agent-run/chunk.diff` holding
  `?t=` (the probe → scan entries). The same bytes in a capture file or in a nested `chunk.diff` still hit `token-query`,
  and the existing planted-secret tests stay green. The `harness-<os>` upload excludes exactly that file (the grep
  entry; per security-plan §Secret Management, "Secret scanning in CI"; obs-plan §9 step 3, §8 integration point 6).

- (security / arch) `ci.yml` has 0 `github.event` references, no `concurrency:` key and only the five pinned actions, and
  zizmor stays clean (the grep and zizmor entries; per security-plan §Dependency Security, CI integration; architecture
  §Infrastructure Patterns → CI/CD approach, Least privilege).

- (arch / security) Only `crates/viola-e2e/**`, the two manifests, `Cargo.lock` and `ci.yml` change. No product crate
  changes. `cargo deny check` stays four-green and the MSRV check passes with `syn` / `proc-macro2` pinned in
  `[workspace.dependencies]` (per architecture §Established Decisions [Module Boundaries]; security-plan §Dependency
  Security).

- (tests) Every guard g1–g7 has its recorded red/green pair in `evidence/guards/` (standing direction; testing.md
  2026-09-25).

- Spec anchors: test-plan §3 `run` step 4 (Base, Diff, Verdict, Output format), §3 `gate` (union bullet, Output), §3
  Internal harness subcommands `secret-scan`, §3 Closed enums, §6 Error sanitization and secret scan, §9 Mutation row /
  Test report format, §10 Mutation gate, §11, §12 · architecture §Established Decisions [Module Boundaries],
  §Conventions (Environment variables), §Infrastructure Patterns → CI/CD approach, Build system, §Occupied Resources →
  Environment variables / Repository · security-plan §Dependency Security (CI integration), §Secret Management,
  §Bootstrap phases `secret-scanning-ci-gate`, Decisions Log 2026-09-24 · obs-plan §8 integration point 6, §9 Step order
  step 3 / Mutation row, §10, §11 · a11y-plan §10 Standard+ invariants.

- Research files inspected: `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/{gate.rs,secret_scan.rs,run/mutants.rs,run.rs}`,
  `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-harness.rs`, `crates/viola-e2e/Cargo.toml`, `crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs`,
  `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `deny.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, the pty chunk's `evidence/operator-pass.md`, run 36165685381's
  downloaded leg files.

- Graph impact (research.md §Graph impact): `resolve_base` @ mutants.rs:239 · `union` @ gate.rs:63 · `gate` @
  viola-harness.rs:194 + 15 gate.rs tests · `scan` @ secret_scan.rs:59 + 13 tests.

- Leans (decisive, not asked):
  - The gate learns compiling legs from the source with `syn`, gate-side. Per research.md §Measured, statement-level
    cfg (lib.rs:435/442) defeats a line scan. Per the security and obs extracts, a leg-side annotation would widen the
    ratified content class of the unscanned leg upload.
  - `AGENT_RUN_CHUNK_BASE` stays as the override, because the harness's own tests pin bases through it
    (mutants.rs:384).
  - The wrap push reads `HEAD^`, per the tests extract's "a base equal to HEAD" anti-pattern.
  - The scan skips by exact path, not by file name, per obs-plan §8 integration point 6: exclusion is admissible only
    for a file never uploaded.

- An outcome-only union ("unviable on any leg exempts") is rejected. It cannot tell a compiled-out `missed` from a
  compiling-leg `missed`, so shared code unviable on one OS and missed on the other would go green (overseer direction
  3's negative).

- Leg-side annotation (each leg records whether it compiles a mutant) is rejected. It changes the leg file's ratified
  content class (security-plan Decisions Log 2026-09-24; obs-plan §8 item 6) and the closed §3 shape, for the same
  information the gate reads from the source.
- A text scan for `#[cfg]` lines above a mutant is rejected: statement-level cfg (lib.rs:435/442) and nesting defeat it.

- Keeping the event-derived base anywhere in `ci.yml`, even as a fallback, is rejected. It is the value that made fix
  pushes read only their own delta.
- The unbounded pickaxe from HEAD is rejected as the rule: measured moving mid-pass (research.md §Measured).

- Removing the `?t=` pattern, or skipping every file named `chunk.diff`, is rejected. The first weakens the floor and
  the second opens a blind spot (security extract; obs-plan §8).
- A macOS mutants leg, the local Linux pre-push gate, and any product-crate change are out of scope (scope §Boundaries).
- No `concurrency:` block, no new action, no `sleep` in tests.

- **cargo-mutants on the new module:** `cfg_legs.rs` is harness lib code, so the legs mutate it. Every arm of the
  three-valued evaluator needs a literal-oracle case, including one per operand position of `all` / `any` (testing.md
  2026-09-24, operator swaps).

- **One body per OS:** no new `#[cfg(unix)]` / `#[cfg(windows)]` body in harness code (secret_scan.rs:231–244 pattern),
  so the plain `run --mutants` form fits this Windows host (verification-harness.md 2026-09-25).

- **Line numbers:** `proc-macro2` `span-locations` makes `Span::start().line` 1-based outside a proc macro. Without the
  feature it reads 0, and every mutant would fall to the conservative arm. That would pass nothing wrongly, but the
  witness would stay red, which is how the replay entry catches it.

- **Mutant-name parsing:** the name is `{path}:{line}:{col}: {description}`. Split at the first `": "`, then take
  `line` and `col` from the right; repo-relative paths contain no `": "`.

- **`gate()` signature change:** 16 call sites (research.md §Graph impact: gate_cmd + 15 tests). A non-mutant suite
  never reads the root.

- **Expected amendments (wrap):**
  - test-plan §3 `run` step 4 Base, and §9 Mutation row: the derived base, the override, the wrap-push `HEAD^`, and
    the `base` field in the run document.
  - test-plan §3 `gate` union bullet and §10 Mutation gate: judged by compiling legs, with the empty-set fallback.
  - test-plan §3 `secret-scan` Scope and §6 Canary bullet: minus the mutation leg's `chunk.diff`.

- **The pickaxe over this repo** (`git log --format='%h %ad %s' -G ' · complete · ' -- .andromeda/master-route.md`): 11 hits, exactly the 11 chunk wrap commits (b0236ca … fcca1ce); neither 0-pending adaptation commit (9df9e45, e486544) nor any pre-CI commit matches.

- **Parser availability** (`Cargo.lock`): `syn` 2.0.119 and 3.0.6, `proc-macro2` 1.0.107, `quote` 1.0.47 already resolved (proc-macro deps); none is a `[workspace.dependencies]` entry (`grep syn|proc-macro2 Cargo.toml`: 0). Licences MIT OR Apache-2.0 (in `deny.toml` `allow`); no ban names them (`deny.toml` `[bans] deny`: cc, libsqlite3-sys, openssl-sys, opentelemetry-*, sentry, tracing-appender).
- **Local residue** (`ls target/agent-run/`): `artifacts/` plus dozens of `cli-drive-*` session dirs; the scan walks all of it.

title: (a) A CI chunk base that survives the operator pass

data.head: ### (a) A CI chunk base that survives the operator pass

body:
- The mutation leg's chunk base is derived from the repository's own history, not from the push event.
  Today `.github/workflows/ci.yml:166` sets `AGENT_RUN_CHUNK_BASE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha ||
  github.event.before }}`, so a fix push's leg reads only that push's delta. (CARRY, operator adaptation 2026-09-25.)

- The base is the last master-flip commit, the pickaxe /andromeda-phase Setup 5a uses (`git log -1 --format=%H -G
  ' · complete · ' -- .andromeda/master-route.md`; it read fcca1ce at the adaptation). The CI checkout already
  fetches full history (`fetch-depth: 0`, ci.yml:155). (CARRY.)

- The CARRY's hypothesis ("`-G` selects any commit whose diff adds or removes a `· complete ·` line, so a mid-pass edit
  of a complete master record would move the base") is measured true at this phase (research.md §Measured, scratch
  probe `base_probe.sh`: the HEAD pickaxe moved to the fix commit that edited a complete line).

- The chosen rule cannot move mid-pass: the last master-flip commit reachable from the OLDEST operator pre-CI commit's
  parent (overseer direction 2). The same probe measured it holding the flip through every commit of the pass. Before
  any pre-CI commit exists (no pending record, or a pending chunk not yet pushed), the rule reads the pickaxe from HEAD.
  On the wrap push, whose own commit is the flip, the base is that commit's parent, so the push reads its own delta
  and never an empty diff (val-1 fold from plan step 1c; test-plan §3 Base forbids a vacuous pass).

- The `run --mutants` document names the base it read (`"base"`, a commit id), so every run of a pass can be shown to
  read the same whole chunk (val-1 fold from plan step 2; overseer direction 1).

- A probe proves it: a simulated pass (flip commit → pre-CI commit → a fix commit, including one that edits a
  `· complete ·` master line) resolves to the same base on every commit of the pass.
- test-plan states the rule (a wrap amendment, listed in the plan's Expected amendments). (CARRY.)

- The union rule (CARRY, chunk 2026-09-25-pty-wrapper-on-windows, overseer direction 2): a mutant unviable on the leg
  that compiles its code is not a survivor, whatever the other leg reads (`gate --mutants-legs`). The per-leg union
  is the project harness's to define (overseer1).

- It closes run 36165685381's breach: `HostTerminal::enter -> Some(Default::default())`, reported at
  `crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs:395` / `:420` (the two cfg variants; `fn enter` at :394 / :418 on HEAD fcca1ce),
  ratified with no product change at that wrap. (CARRY.)

- A witness on the recorded 36165685381 breach shape (overseer direction 3). The shape is measured from that run's own
  leg files: `lib.rs:395:9` windows unviable / ubuntu missed; `lib.rs:420:9` ubuntu unviable / windows missed
  (research.md §Measured).
- A negative (overseer direction 3): a mutant MISSED on a leg that compiles its line stays a survivor.

- [premise-corrected: outcomes alone cannot separate "compiled out" from "missed on a compiling leg" — research.md
  §Measured] The gate needs to know which legs COMPILE each mutant's line; the leg files carry names and outcomes only.
  The `mutants-verdict` job checks out the same sha, so the source is at hand where the union runs. The workspace's
  lib/bin code uses five cfg predicates (`test`, `unix`, `windows`, `not(unix)`, `not(windows)`), at fn, field and
  statement level, with no cfg-gated `mod` declaration. The mechanism is P4's decision.

- CARRY, chunk 2026-09-25-pty-wrapper-on-windows: `secret-scan` (`scripts/agent-run.sh secret-scan`, ci.yml:100) read
  `target/agent-run/chunk.diff` residue left by a prior `run --mutants`, where it hit its own `?t=` pattern line (that
  chunk's report.md:124). It had no owner; this chunk sets the scan's scope.

- [premise-corrected: the hit is not staleness — `chunk.diff` is repo source text by construction, so a fresh diff that
  touches `secret_scan.rs` hits too; and the `harness-<os>` upload ships the whole `target/agent-run/` (ci.yml:115) —
  research.md §Files inspected] The scan stops reading the mutation leg's `chunk.diff` (overseer direction 4), and the
  `harness-<os>` upload stops shipping it, so the scan still covers every file that upload ships. The planted-secret
  red tests stay. Today `scan` collects every file under `target/agent-run` (`secret_scan.rs:78`).

- Planned from the start under V17 (overseer direction 1; the pty chunk's pass ran this shape — its evidence/operator-pass.md): the pre-CI commit, then any fixes as `fix({marker}): operator fix after
  CI run {id}, …`, fast-forward only; with (a) landed, each run of the pass reads the whole chunk.

- Every guard gets a remove-the-guard run; the mutation leg ends 0 missed / 0 timeout; the swamp and test-only
  verdicts hold. Fold, do not carry.
- NOT this chunk: the local Linux pre-push gate (the next entry, "Local Linux pre-push gate").
- No product-crate behaviour change; the subject is CI, the harness (`viola-e2e`) and test-plan.
- The macOS mutants leg stays out (the "Unix endpoint and home hardening" CARRY owns adding one).

- Base fcca1ce (the last flip), shas fcca1ce and e486544: both green, 15/15 checks (runs 36171941029, 36172787056).
  Nothing to disposition.

_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-09-26-local-linux-pre-push-gate · **Version:** viola-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-09-26T21:55:00Z

The goal is to catch Unix reds before the push (founder ruling, overseer direction 1). This is a new internal
`viola-harness` subcommand, `pre-push`, run from this Windows host, and it does four things:

- It syncs a history-carrying clone in WSL2 `Ubuntu`'s Linux filesystem from the Windows working tree,
  uncommitted and untracked files included.
- It runs the ubuntu test job's own suites there (`run --coverage` + `gate --require coverage,doctest`).
- It runs the `ubuntu-latest` mutation leg there, and the `windows-2025` leg on the host.
- It judges both legs with CI's own union (`gate --require mutants --mutants-legs ubuntu-latest,windows-2025`).

The result is one JSON document with a typed exit, and a red stops the push. A provisioning script installs the
toolchain inside Ubuntu at CI's pins. The harness verifies those pins on every run, and they never float.

One base-rule fix makes the local legs print CI's `base`. Before the pre-CI commit, HEAD is the last wrap flip, so
the derived base stepped back to HEAD^ (scope item 4, `premise-corrected`). The rule now skips that step while a
promoted chunk is uncommitted, and the fix also corrects /implement's local Windows leg.
- fix the base rule;
- the union of both legs;
- CI test-job suites;

- project-side wiring, with the Andromeda `plan-template.md` change recorded as a proposal in evidence for the
  overseer to relay. A project chunk never edits Andromeda.

1. **Base rule: an uncommitted promotion keeps the flip** (`crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run/mutants.rs`).
   - Add `uncommitted_promotion(repo) -> bool`. It is true when the working tree's `.andromeda/master-route.md`
     (read from disk, `repo.join(MASTER_ROUTE)`) carries a `{marker} · pending · ` record whose marker HEAD's copy
     (`git show HEAD:…`, as `pre_ci_parent` reads it at :89) lacks. Use `pending_marker` (:108) on both sides.
   - In `chunk_flip`, the `flip == HEAD → HEAD^` step (:80-82) applies only when `!uncommitted_promotion(repo)`.
   - Nothing else in `resolve_base` changes: the override, the pre-CI bound, the merge-base fallback and
     `base-missing` behave as before.
   - Equality this step must make true, at THIS repo's state (HEAD a69c5ef = the flip, working tree holding this
     chunk's pending record): `resolve_base(root, None)` = a69c5ef (today: acd08c7, re-derived at P4 — scope item 4).
   - Tests (inline, in the existing `mod tests` scratch-repo style):
     - `chunk_base_of_an_uncommitted_promotion_is_the_flip_at_head`: flip committed at HEAD plus an uncommitted
       pending record → base = HEAD.
     - The existing `chunk_base_of_the_wrap_push_is_its_parent` (flip at HEAD, no pending record) stays green unchanged.
     - The existing `chunk_base_holds_the_flip_across_a_pass` stays green unchanged.

2. **Provisioning script** `scripts/wsl-provision.sh` (new; runs INSIDE Ubuntu, from the repo dir). It follows
   `scripts/install-ripgrep.sh`'s shape: `set -euo pipefail`, `need`, typed `tool-missing: <tool>` lines, sha256
   `verify`, curl retry flags, and a `--probe`.
   - **Precondition.** `cc` absent → print `tool-missing: cc` plus the one-line install command
     (`wsl.exe -d Ubuntu -u root --exec /usr/bin/apt-get install -y build-essential`, the plan's build entry) and exit
     1. The script never runs sudo and never installs system packages itself.
   - **rustup.** rustup-init 1.29.1 (the host's rustup version) for `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` from
     `https://static.rust-lang.org/rustup/archive/1.29.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/rustup-init`, checked against a
     sha256 LITERAL embedded in the script. /implement reads the literal from the published `.sha256` and records it in
     `evidence/provision.md`. Then run `rustup-init -y --no-modify-path --profile minimal --default-toolchain none`.
   - **Toolchain.** `rustup toolchain install` in the repo dir (reads `rust-toolchain.toml`: 1.98.1 + rustfmt +
     clippy), then `rustup component add llvm-tools-preview`.
   - **Cargo tools.** `cargo install --locked` of exactly the versions on the `test` job's `tool:` line of
     `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (today `cargo-nextest@0.9.146,cargo-mutants@27.1.0,cargo-llvm-cov@0.9.1`, :33). The
     versions are parsed from that line, never restated. A tool already at its pin is not reinstalled.
   - **Last line.** `wsl-provision: pins ok rustc <v> cargo-nextest <v> cargo-mutants <v> cargo-llvm-cov <v>`, where
     each value is read from the installed tool's own `--version`, then compared with the pin. A mismatch prints
     `pin-mismatch: <tool>` and exits 1.
   - **`--check`** prints the same last line without installing anything.
   - **`--probe`** proves two refusals: a tampered sha256 is refused, and a pin read from a planted ci.yml line that
     differs from the installed tool is refused. It also proves the clean control (`--check` against the real pins),
     and ends `wsl-provision --probe: 2/2 refused, control clean`.

3. **`pre-push` module** `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/pre_push.rs` (new; declared in `harness/mod.rs`).
   - **Plain code, no `#[cfg]` bodies.** Every external call goes through the `Runner` seam (`run.rs:31`). The host
     gate is a const, `PRE_PUSH_HOST_SUPPORTED: bool = cfg!(windows)`, mirroring `FUZZ_HOST_SUPPORTED`
     (`run/fuzz.rs:11`), and the entry point takes the flag as a parameter so tests reach both arms. Result: both
     mutation legs compile and judge every line.
   - **Stages, fail-fast, in order.** Each stage's failure ends the run with `ok:false` and names the `stage`:
     1. `host`. Off Windows → exit 2, `reason:"pre-push-windows-only"`.
     2. `tools`. `wsl.exe -d Ubuntu --exec /usr/bin/printenv HOME` (the distro probe; its value is kept in memory,
        never printed) → non-zero = `reason:"tool-missing", detail:"wsl-distro-ubuntu"`. Then `cc`, `rustc`,
        `cargo nextest`, `cargo mutants` and `cargo llvm-cov` `--version` inside the clean env below. Absent →
        `tool-missing` + `detail` naming the tool. A version other than the pin → `reason:"tool-pin-mismatch"` +
        `detail` naming the tool. Pins come from `rust-toolchain.toml`'s `channel` and ci.yml's `test`-job `tool:`
        line, via pure parsers `toolchain_channel` / `ci_pins` tested against the repo's own files.
     3. `sync`: the measured form (research M8).
        - Windows side: with `GIT_INDEX_FILE=target/pre-push/index`, run `git read-tree HEAD` → `git add -A` →
          `git write-tree` (the tree id) → `git diff --cached --binary --no-color --no-ext-diff HEAD` into
          `target/pre-push/tree.patch`. Run git with `-c core.safecrlf=false` and no stderr on stdout. The real index
          is never touched.
        - Clone `<home>/viola-pre-push`: `git clone --no-hardlinks <src>` when absent, where `<src>` is
          `wsl_path(ws.root)` (a pure `D:\a\b` → `/mnt/d/a/b` mapper; non-drive → `sync-failed` / `source-path`).
          Then `fetch --no-tags <src> HEAD` → `rev-parse FETCH_HEAD` must equal the Windows HEAD sha →
          `reset --hard <sha>` → `clean -fdq` (no `-x`: the build cache survives, stale untracked files go) →
          `apply --binary <patch>` (skipped on an empty patch).
        - Verify: `add -A` + `write-tree` in the clone must equal the Windows tree id, else
          `reason:"sync-mismatch"`. That equality is the per-run proof that every dirty, untracked and deleted file
          reached Linux. A failing git step is `reason:"sync-failed"`, with `detail` = the step (`patch`, `clone`,
          `fetch`, `reset`, `clean`, `apply`).
     4. `cache`. `du -sb <clone>/target` (0 when absent). Above `CACHE_CAP_BYTES` (40 GiB, leaned below), run
        `rm -rf <clone>/target` before the run. Report `{"bytes":…, "cap":…, "cleaned":…}` plus `bytes_after`, read
        again after the last Linux stage.
     5. `linux-tests`. `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --coverage`, then `bash scripts/agent-run.sh gate --require
        coverage,doctest`, both in the clone. Each stdout's last non-empty line is parsed as the harness document.
        A non-JSON line is `reason:"linux-document-unreadable"`, and `ok:false` of either document stops here.
     6. `linux-leg`. `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --mutants --leg ubuntu-latest` in the clone, then
        `cat <clone>/target/agent-run/artifacts/mutants-verdict-ubuntu-latest.json`. The file must parse with
        `"leg":"ubuntu-latest"`; it is written to the host's `leg_verdict_path(ws.artifacts(), "ubuntu-latest")`.
        Absent or unparsable → `reason:"verdict-missing"`. The leg's own `ok:false` (a refusal,
        `outcomes-missing`, `unviable-exceeds-caught`) stops here.
     7. `windows-leg`. In-process `run_with(ws, Selection { mutants: true, .. }, None, None,
        Some("windows-2025"), runner)`. Its `ok:false` stops here.
     8. `union`. Both documents' `mutants.base` must be equal, else `reason:"base-mismatch"`. Then
        `gate(&ws.artifacts(), &ws.root, &["mutants"], Some(&["ubuntu-latest", "windows-2025"]))`, whose document is
        the stage's verdict.
   - **Every WSL call** is `wsl.exe -d Ubuntu [--cd <dir>] --exec /usr/bin/env -i HOME=<home>
     PATH=<home>/.cargo/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin <argv…>`.
     - Never the `--` form: it re-parses argv through the distro shell (research M2).
     - Never the inherited environment: `env -i` drops the Windows PATH leak (M4) and any `CLAUDE*` value a
       future `WSLENV` might forward (M5).
     - No `Command::env` carries a `CLAUDE*` name.
     - Output streams to stderr, and stdout keeps the one document (`run_forwarding`, `run.rs:216`).
   - **The document.** Key order `v, cmd, ok, reason?, detail?, stage`, then
     `sync {head, tree, files, ms}`, `cache {bytes, cap, cleaned, bytes_after}`, `linux {run, gate}` (the two parsed
     documents' `ok` and `suites` / `breaches`), `legs {"ubuntu-latest": {ok, base, verdict, tested},
     "windows-2025": {…}}` and `gate` (the union document). Rules:
     - It holds no absolute path: neither `<home>`, the clone path nor `ws.root`.
     - Exit 0 when every stage is green, 1 on a red stage or failure reason, 2 on `pre-push-windows-only` or usage.

4. **Dispatch.** `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-harness.rs`: a `PrePush` variant (no flags), a `pre_push_cmd`
   calling the module with `PRE_PUSH_HOST_SUPPORTED` and `run_forwarding`, and `COMMANDS` gains `pre-push`.
   `scripts/agent-run.sh` (:74) and `scripts/agent-run.ps1` (the internal-subcommand arm) gain `pre-push`, with
   their header comments naming it among the internal subcommands. The 5-command agent surface is unchanged.

5. **Tests** (inline `mod tests` in `pre_push.rs`, names prefixed `pre_push_`; stand-in runners, never WSL itself).
   - **Pure parsers:**
     - `pre_push_ci_pins_parse_the_test_job_tool_line`: over the repo's own `.github/workflows/ci.yml` →
       nextest 0.9.146, mutants 27.1.0, llvm-cov 0.9.1, plus a missing-line case → `None`.
     - `pre_push_toolchain_channel_reads_the_pin` (`rust-toolchain.toml` → `1.98.1`).
     - `pre_push_wsl_path_maps_drive_paths` (drive-letter cases, lower-casing, a UNC / relative path → `None`).
   - **Refusals and stages:**
     - `pre_push_refuses_off_windows_host` (exit 2, no runner call).
     - `pre_push_distro_missing_is_tool_missing`.
     - `pre_push_cc_missing_is_tool_missing_cc`.
     - `pre_push_pin_mismatch_names_the_tool` (the runner answers `cargo-mutants 27.0.9`).
     - `pre_push_sync_mismatch_is_red`.
     - `pre_push_cache_over_cap_is_cleaned_and_reported` and its under-cap control (no `rm`).
     - `pre_push_linux_test_red_stops_before_the_legs` (no mutants call recorded).
     - `pre_push_verdict_missing_is_red`.
     - `pre_push_base_mismatch_is_red`.
   - **Argv:** `pre_push_every_wsl_call_uses_exec_and_a_clean_env` checks every recorded WSL `Command`:
     - `-d Ubuntu`, then `--exec /usr/bin/env -i`;
     - no bare `--` separator;
     - no `CLAUDE` in `get_envs()`.
   - **Real sync, native:** `pre_push_sync_reproduces_a_dirty_tree`.
     - Setup: two scratch git repos (source and clone), with an identity path mapper and a runner that strips the
       `wsl.exe … --exec /usr/bin/env -i K=V…` prefix, applies `--cd` as the cwd, and runs the rest natively.
     - The source holds a commit plus a modified tracked file, an untracked file, a deleted tracked file and an
       ignored file.
     - After sync, the clone's tree id equals the source's temp-index tree id. The modified content and the
       untracked file are present, the deleted file is absent, and the ignored file is absent.
     - The source's real index is unchanged (`git diff --cached --quiet` before and after).
     - A second sync, after deleting the untracked file and editing another, is still equal: `clean` dropped the stale
       file.
   - **Union through the real gate:** `pre_push_union_reads_both_legs` uses run.rs's `mini()` workspace and the
     stand-in `outcomes.json` pattern of the existing `run_mutants_leg_*` tests (mutants.rs :934-1040). With the
     Linux verdict text answered by the runner and the Windows leg run in-process:
     - a mutant missed on both legs → `ok:false` with the union breach;
     - one caught on either leg → `ok:true`.
   - **No absolute path:** `pre_push_document_carries_no_absolute_path` (the doc text lacks the stand-in home and
     `ws.root`).

6. **Remove-the-guard runs** (standing; one-shot at implement, both readings in `evidence/guards/`, never entries).
   Neutralise each guard, run its named test red, restore it, run it green. Re-Read the site before each edit
   (testing.md 2026-09-25).
   - (g1) the tree-id comparison → `pre_push_sync_mismatch_is_red`
   - (g2) the base comparison → `pre_push_base_mismatch_is_red`
   - (g3) the uncommitted-promotion skip → `chunk_base_of_an_uncommitted_promotion_is_the_flip_at_head`
   - (g4) the cache cap → `pre_push_cache_over_cap_is_cleaned_and_reported`
   - (g5) the pin comparison → `pre_push_pin_mismatch_names_the_tool`
   - (g6) `env -i` → `pre_push_every_wsl_call_uses_exec_and_a_clean_env`
   - (g7) fail-fast after `linux-tests` → `pre_push_linux_test_red_stops_before_the_legs`
   - (g8) `clean -fdq` → `pre_push_sync_reproduces_a_dirty_tree`

7. **Unix-only witness** (overseer direction 6; one-shot, recorded in `evidence/witness-unix-red.md`).
   - Plant, in `pre_push.rs`'s test module, `#[cfg(unix)] #[test] fn pre_push_planted_unix_red() { panic!("planted
     unix red") }`.
   - On Windows, `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --unit --filter 'test(=pre_push_planted_unix_red)'` must be RED with
     `nextest-exit-4` (compiled out, nothing selected). That is the proof this host alone cannot see it.
   - `bash scripts/agent-run.sh pre-push` must be `ok:false`, `stage:"linux-tests"`, with `pre_push_planted_unix_red`
     in the Linux run's `coverage` suite `failures`, and no leg run.
   - Remove the plant. The standing `pre-push` entry below is then the green reading.
   - Also record the dirty-file proof: the `sync.files` / `sync.tree` fields of that red run. The run ran over an
     uncommitted tree whose only home for the plant was the Windows working copy.

8. **Evidence** (`chunks/2026-09-26-local-linux-pre-push-gate/evidence/`):
   - `provision.md`: the root apt entry's result, `build-essential` version, the rustup-init sha256 and its
     source, the `--check` last line, and `du` of `~/.rustup` + `~/.cargo`.
   - `sync-measurement.md`: the implemented form's first and repeat sync `ms`, the tree-id equality and the
     `files` count, set beside research M8.
   - `plan-template-proposal.md`: the operator ruling's relay text. Proposed plan-template.md wording: on a project
     whose harness exposes a pre-push gate, the operator pass lists it as an `operator` entry BEFORE the pre-CI
     commit and the push entry, and a red there stops the pass. It carries this plan's entries as the worked
     example, for the overseer to relay to overseer1.
   - `guards/` (step 6), `witness-unix-red.md` (step 7), `operator-pass.md` (step 9).

9. **Operator pass** (the standing wiring, dogfooded).
   - The order is: stop rust-analyzer by exact `ExecutablePath` (host-win32.md 2026-09-26) → the operator
     `pre-push` entry on the uncommitted tree → the operator's pre-CI commit
     `chore(2026-09-26-local-linux-pre-push-gate): operator pre-CI commit, for the run this chunk's verdict reads`
     → the push entry → the CI reads.
   - A red `pre-push` stops the pass before any commit.
   - A red CI read is fixed by
     `fix(2026-09-26-local-linux-pre-push-gate): operator fix after CI run {id}, {what it changes}`, pushed
     fast-forward and never amended, rebased or force-pushed. Each fix commit takes `pre-push` again first.
   - Record in `evidence/operator-pass.md`: the local `legs.*.base` and the CI legs' base, which must all read
     a69c5ef, and each run's verdict.

10. **Instrument the Linux red, before any fix** (operator ruling at implement, scope item 6; one-shot).
    - Permanent, `tests/tui_passthrough.rs` (`tui_host_resize_reaches_the_child`): record the wall-clock time (unix
      µs) the resize is sent and the time each child `size` receipt is first observed; on the deadline the panic
      message carries both, plus the content of `<home>/pump-probe.ndjson` when that file exists.
    - Temporary, `src/cmd/run.rs`: append to `<home>/pump-probe.ndjson` one line per event — `spawn` (the :63 read),
      `baseline` (the closure's first call from `pump`), `poll` (each later call whose value differs from the one
      before) — each `{t_us, what, cols, rows}`. Nothing else reads the file; it never ships.
    - Run `bash scripts/agent-run.sh pre-push` with the instrument in the tree. The prediction to check on a red:
      `spawn.t_us < resize.t_us < baseline.t_us` and `baseline` = 100×30.
    - Record the dump verbatim in `evidence/linux-red-investigation.md`. Confirmed → step 11. Not confirmed →
      STOP: report what the dump shows, apply no fix.

11. **The fix, only on a confirmed window.** Remove the temporary instrument from `src/cmd/run.rs` whole. `pump`
    gains a `spawned: Size` parameter, the size the PTY was spawned with, and starts `last` from it instead of a
    second `host_size()` read (`crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs:293`). `run` passes `spec.size`. The 10 test call sites
    pass their spawn size (graph: research §Scope widening).

12. **Deterministic window test** (`crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs`, `mod tests`): `pump_forwards_a_resize_that_lands_before_its_first_look`
    — spawned at 80×24, a size closure answering 100×30 from its FIRST call (the resize already happened when the
    pump looks), a `MockPty` expecting exactly one `resize(100×30)`. On the old code the baseline is 100×30 and the
    resize count is 0: the test fails without any timing. Its remove-the-guard run: restore the second read →
    red → restore → green (`evidence/guards/`).
    - Added by the operator's ruling (experiment A, "force the window"): a test-only seam in `src/cmd/run.rs`,
      compiled only with the test-only `fake-agent` feature (absent from any release build), where
      `FAKE_AGENT_PUMP_DELAY_MS` holds the pump back after the child starts; and the integration test
      `tui_host_resize_in_the_pump_start_window_reaches_the_child` (`tests/tui_passthrough.rs`) that sends its
      resize inside a 1 s hold. It was red 6/6 with the exact signature before the fix (control green 6/6), and it is
      the deterministic end-to-end regression test after it. The resize test's deadline is 8 s (`RESIZE_WITHIN`),
      below nextest's 10 s `mutants` kill, and it appends each observation to `viola-resize-<pid>.ndjson` in the temp
      dir as it goes (experiment B), removed on success.

13. **Three consecutive green `pre-push` runs** after steps 11–12, each document recorded in
    `evidence/linux-red-investigation.md`; the unit/integration entries green alongside.
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/pre_push.rs` — the `pre-push` stages, parsers, document and `pre_push_` tests (steps 3, 5).
- `scripts/wsl-provision.sh` — in-Ubuntu provisioning at ci.yml's pins, `--check`, `--probe` (step 2).

- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run/mutants.rs` — `uncommitted_promotion`, the `chunk_flip` condition (:80-82), one new
  `chunk_base_` test (step 1). `resolve_base`'s callers (`mutants` @ mutants.rs:316, tests; research §Graph impact)
  are unchanged: no signature moves.
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/mod.rs` — `pub mod pre_push;`.

- `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-harness.rs` — `PrePush` variant, `pre_push_cmd`, `COMMANDS` (step 4); reuses `run_with`
  (callers `run_cmd` @ :146, `run` @ run.rs:88) and `gate` (caller `gate_cmd` @ :194) unchanged.
- `scripts/agent-run.sh`, `scripts/agent-run.ps1` — the internal-subcommand arm and header comment gain `pre-push`.
- `src/cmd/run.rs` — the temporary instrument (step 10, removed at step 11); passes `spec.size` to `pump` (step 11).

- `crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs` — `pump(…, spawned: Size, host_size)` and its 10 test call sites; the window test
  (steps 11–12). Callers: `run` @ `src/cmd/run.rs:69` + 10 tests (research §Scope widening).
- `tests/tui_passthrough.rs` — the resize test's failure dump (step 10).

The gates run on this Windows host during /implement. The Rust delta is harness-only (`viola-e2e`) plus two scripts. No
product crate changes, no manifest changes and no dependency is added, so `cargo deny` is not re-run: no graph change.
There is no boot smoke: this chunk changes no boot path or lifecycle verb, and CI's `test` jobs drive the lifecycle on
every push.

The provisioning entries come before the gate that needs them. The `build-essential` install runs as root through
`wsl.exe -u root` (uid 0, no sudo, no password — overseer measurement, re-read at P5), so it is an ordinary `build`
entry. Every WSL entry carries `MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL='*'`, because Git Bash rewrites a leading-`/` argument (research
M2).

The `pre-push` entry is this chunk's mutation gate. It runs both legs and CI's union, so no separate `run --mutants`
entry exists. Stop rust-analyzer by exact `ExecutablePath` before it (host-win32.md 2026-09-26).
Steps 6 and 7 are one-shot source edits (guards, the Unix witness): evidence, never entries.

body:
- (tests / arch) With HEAD at a wrap flip and a promoted, uncommitted chunk, the derived base is the flip, not HEAD^.
  With no pending record it is still HEAD^ (the wrap push), and the pass and override rules are unchanged. These are
  the `chunk_base_` tests in the `run --unit` entries, and the `pre-push` entry's `"base":"a69c5ef` where the
  pre-change rule derives acd08c7 (per test-plan §3 `run` step 4 Base; architecture §Infrastructure Patterns → CI/CD
  approach).

- (tests) A planted `#[cfg(unix)]` failing test is compiled out on this host (the filtered `run --unit` reads
  `nextest-exit-4`) and turns `pre-push` red at `stage:"linux-tests"`, naming the test, before any leg runs. Removing
  it returns green (step 7, `evidence/witness-unix-red.md`; per test-plan §3 `run` Exit code semantics / Output
  format; §10 Zero-flakiness budget — no retry).

- (tests / security) Every run proves the sync: the clone's `write-tree` equals the Windows temp-index tree id, over a
  tree carrying modified, untracked and deleted files. Ignored files never reach the clone, and the Windows index is
  never touched (`pre_push_sync_reproduces_a_dirty_tree`, `pre_push_sync_mismatch_is_red`, the witness run's `sync`
  fields; per test-plan §3 `run` step 4 Diff; security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Secrets).

- (security / arch) The toolchain inside Ubuntu is `rust-toolchain.toml`'s 1.98.1 via a sha256-pinned rustup-init, and
  the cargo tools are ci.yml's exact pins via `cargo install --locked`. `pre-push` refuses a missing or mismatched tool
  with `tool-missing` / `tool-pin-mismatch` + `detail` (the provisioning, `--probe` and `pre_push_pin_mismatch_…`
  entries/tests; per security-plan §Dependency Security, Pinning; architecture §Stack and Technologies; test-plan §3
  Bootstrap `ci-tool-install`).

- (security / obs) No `CLAUDE*` value crosses into Ubuntu, from WSLENV or from the gate. Every WSL call is
  `--exec /usr/bin/env -i …`. The document and the copied-back verdict hold no absolute path (`/home/`, `/mnt/`, a
  drive letter) (the canary, verdict-grep and argv / no-absolute-path tests; per security-plan §Bootstrap phases
  `logging-redaction-wire` / `secret-scanning-ci-gate`; obs-plan §8 item 6, §11 PII Scrubbing).

- (arch) Only `crates/viola-e2e/**` and `scripts/` change. No product crate, no manifest and no workflow changes. The
  5-command agent surface is unchanged, and `pre-push` is an internal subcommand both shims forward (the ps1 grep; per
  architecture §Established Decisions [Module Boundaries]; test-plan §3 Internal harness subcommands).

- (tests) Every guard g1–g8 has its recorded red/green pair in `evidence/guards/` (standing direction; testing.md
  2026-09-25). This chunk's own new Rust passes the local union and CI's: 0 missed, 0 timeout, unviable ≤ caught on each
  leg (the `pre-push` and CI mutants entries).

- (tests / arch) The Linux red's cause is MEASURED before any fix: the instrument's dump shows, on a red,
  `spawn < resize < baseline` with `baseline` = 100×30 (`evidence/linux-red-investigation.md`). Only then does the
  pump start from the spawn size, `pump_forwards_a_resize_that_lands_before_its_first_look` forces the window with no
  timing (its guard pair in `evidence/guards/`), and `pre-push` reads green three runs in a row (step 13). A dump that
  does not confirm the window ends the chunk's implement as surfaced, with no fix (per test-plan §5 Module ↔ PTY "a
  resize is propagated"; architecture §Established Decisions [PTY]).

- (process) In the operator pass, `pre-push` runs before the pre-CI commit, and the CI legs' `base` equals the local
  legs' a69c5ef (`evidence/operator-pass.md`). The plan-template proposal is recorded for the overseer
  (`evidence/plan-template-proposal.md`; operator ruling at P4).

- Spec anchors:
  - test-plan §3 Internal harness subcommands, `run` step 4 (Base, Diff, Verdict), Exit code semantics, Output
    format, Bootstrap `ci-tool-install`, Closed enums; §9 tool-install paragraph / Mutation row; §10 Mutation gate,
    Zero-flakiness budget; §11; §12.
  - architecture §Established Decisions [Module Boundaries]; §Conventions (Environment variables); §Stack and
    Technologies; §Infrastructure Patterns → Build system / CI/CD approach; §Occupied Resources → Repository /
    Environment variables; §Cross-cutting Patterns → Cross-platform discipline.
  - security-plan §Dependency Security (Pinning, CI integration); §Secret Management; §Security Anti-Patterns →
    Secrets / Universal; §Bootstrap phases `logging-redaction-wire`, `secret-scanning-ci-gate`; §Authentication &
    Authorization (IPC access control (Unix)).
  - obs-plan §3 obs-ci-gate-wire; §8 item 6; §9 Mutation row / Step order; §10; §11.
  - a11y-plan §3 Keyboard test harness → Tooling (the Unix byte-for-byte oracle now runs pre-push); §10 Standard+
    invariants.

- Research files inspected: `crates/viola-e2e/src/{bin/viola-harness.rs,harness/mod.rs,harness/run.rs,harness/run/mutants.rs,harness/gate.rs,harness/cfg_legs.rs}`,
  `scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1}`, `scripts/install-ripgrep.sh`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, test-plan §3 :611-666, the
  pty chunk's and the previous chunk's evidence; host measurements research M1–M9.

- Leans (decisive, not asked):
  - An internal subcommand, not a sixth agent command, per test-plan §3 Internal harness subcommands (the shape of
    `gate` / `secret-scan`) and verification-harness.md §Shims ("A 6th agent command needs a test-plan amendment").
  - The sync form, per research M8: clone + temp-index patch is ≈0.9 s repeat against 2.74 s for rsync, and rsync
    carries every ignored file not excluded by hand.
  - Fail-fast stages: a red test stage already stops the push, and the witness becomes cheap (the obs/tests "no
    retry" anti-patterns hold either way).
  - `env -i` into WSL, per research M4/M5 and the security extract's WSLENV anti-pattern.
  - `target/pre-push/` for the patch and temp index, outside `target/agent-run/`: the patch is repository source, and
    `secret-scan` scans every other `target/agent-run/` file (test-plan §3 `secret-scan` Scope).
  - `CACHE_CAP_BYTES` = 40 GiB. Its basis: `C:` 199.1 GB free and the vhdx never shrinks (research M6). A mutation run
    copies `target/` once (`--copy-target=true`, 2.9 GB measured, test-plan §3). The Windows `target/` is 25 GB with
    msrv/llvm-cov/harness dirs (new-session disk read), so 40 GiB leaves one cold rebuild of headroom for the
    peak ≈ 2 × cap. **Confirmed at P5 by the overseer** (C: 199 GB free, measured 23:48; the overseer's disk check
    watches C: every 2 h).

- rsync from `/mnt/d`: rejected. It is slower (9.85 s / 2.74 s against 4.47 s / ≈0.9 s) and carries every git-ignored
  file (local homes, `.url` token files) unless excluded by hand (research M8; security extract).

- A checkout on `/mnt/d` (drvfs): rejected. Unix modes and the per-user 0700 checks need a real Linux filesystem
  (security extract; scope item 2).

- The `wsl -d Ubuntu -- …` form: rejected. It re-parses argv through the distro shell (research M2). Every call is
  `--exec`.

- Inheriting the WSL environment: rejected. It carries the Windows PATH, and a future `WSLENV` could carry `CLAUDE*`
  (research M4/M5).

- Setting `AGENT_RUN_CHUNK_BASE` from the gate, or deriving the base outside `resolve_base`: rejected. It would split
  the local legs from CI (arch extract).

- Judging the Linux leg alone: rejected (operator ruling). A `--leg` run defers survivors (run.rs:122), and a single
  named leg judges `#[cfg(windows)]` bodies (gate.rs:144-149).
- A sync over a listener (git daemon, rsync daemon, sshd): rejected (security extract, listener ban in spirit).
- Any retry of a red stage or leg: rejected (obs-plan §11 SLO; test-plan §11).
- Editing Andromeda's `plan-template.md` or any pipeline file: rejected (operator ruling). It is a proposal in evidence.

- Applying the pump fix without the instrument's confirmation, or reading "it went green" as the cause: rejected
  (operator ruling at implement). A timing-based window test (a sleep, a race to win): rejected; the window is
  forced by the size closure.

- Shipping the instrument: rejected. A product file written outside the declared sinks breaks the obs contract
  (observability.md §Sinks); it is removed whole at step 11.

- `#[cfg(unix)]` / `#[cfg(windows)]` bodies in `pre_push.rs`: rejected. One body per OS keeps both legs judging every
  line (verification-harness.md 2026-09-25; the carried 0.8 learning — the host gate is a const).

- **Leg name.** The Linux leg is exactly `ubuntu-latest`, the unix+linux family (cfg_legs.rs:24). A bare `ubuntu`
  would fall to "unknown family keeps the leg".

- **Empty patch.** `git apply` refuses empty input ("No valid patches in input"), so skip the apply when the Windows
  diff has 0 files. The tree-id check still runs.

- **CRLF warnings.** `git add -A` under the temp index warns per `w/crlf` checkout-artifact file (research M8: those
  files normalise to their HEAD blobs). Run with `-c core.safecrlf=false` and keep stderr off the document.

- **Linux documents.** `cargo run -q` keeps stdout to the one document. Parse the LAST non-empty stdout line and treat
  anything else as `linux-document-unreadable`, never a pass.

- **Clean env.** `env -i` also drops `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `TERM` and `NO_COLOR`. Today no product code reads
  `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` (research M7: `grep -rn XDG_RUNTIME_DIR crates src tests` → 0), and a TERM-less env matches a
  non-TTY CI runner (a11y extract §6 note). Record the env the Linux run saw (names only) in `evidence/sync-measurement.md`.

- **Ubuntu 26.04 locally vs `ubuntu-latest` in CI** (research M1). A green local gate is a filter, never CI's twin.
  Record any local-only red that CI does not reproduce in `evidence/operator-pass.md` rather than "fixing" it blind.

- **Timing.** The first `pre-push` is cold: rustup components, an instrumented build and two mutation runs. Later runs
  reuse the clone's `target/`. Record both durations in `evidence/sync-measurement.md`.

- **Expected amendments (wrap):**
  - test-plan §3 Internal harness subcommands: the `pre-push` entry (stages, document, exits).
  - test-plan §3 Closed enums: the values above.
  - test-plan §3 `run` step 4 Base: the uncommitted-promotion rule.
  - test-plan §9 tool-install paragraph: WSL provisioning reads ci.yml's pins.
  - test-plan §10 Mutation gate: the local union before the push.
  - test-plan §12: one Decisions Log entry.
  - architecture §Project directory structure: `scripts/wsl-provision.sh`, `harness/pre_push.rs`.
  - architecture §Occupied Resources → Repository: `target/pre-push/`.
  - architecture §Infrastructure Patterns → CI/CD approach: the local pre-push gate precedes the operator push.
  - security-plan §Dependency Security: the pinned rustup-init + `cargo install --locked` inside WSL.
  - security-plan §Secret Management: `env -i` into WSL, no `CLAUDE*` crossing.
  - obs-plan §9 Mutation row: the local union is the same verdict.
  - obs-plan §8 item 6: Linux clone paths never in a document.
  - test-plan §5 Module ↔ PTY row (the resize bullet): a resize landing before the pump's first look is still
    forwarded — the pump's baseline is the spawn size (only if steps 10–11 confirm and land it).
  - test-plan §12: the Decisions Log entry also names the folded red and its measured cause.
  - architecture §Occupied Resources → Environment variables: `FAKE_AGENT_PUMP_DELAY_MS`, read only by a `viola`
    built with the test-only `fake-agent` feature (a test seam, never a configuration channel; absent from release).
  - security-plan §Bootstrap phases / Anti-Patterns (the env-var rule): the seam's carve-out — compiled out of every
    release build, it disables no control and widens no redaction.

- **Not amendments (other channels, for the wrap):**
  - The wrap cascade re-derives these leaves from the amended masters above; they are not touchpoints:
    `.claude/docs/commands.md`, `.claude/docs/workflow.md` (the operator-pass order pre-push → pre-CI commit → push),
    `.claude/rules/verification-harness.md`, `.claude/rules/testing.md`.
  - Curation candidates for `host-win32.md` Session Additions: `wsl -d Ubuntu --exec`, never `--`;
    `MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL` for a `/mnt/…` argument; the distro PATH carries the Windows PATH.

- **Matrix.** No capability is claimed. v1-53 (Linux/macOS parity) needs the Unix end-to-end suite and a live Linux
  run, which this chunk does not build; the local Linux host is its future runner. v1-14 is unrelated.

title: Scope widening at implement (operator ruling, 2026-09-26 — scope item 6)

data.head: ## Scope widening at implement (operator ruling, 2026-09-26 — scope item 6)

body:
The gate's first real run found a Linux red (`evidence/linux-red-investigation.md`); the overseer folded it into
this chunk, instrument first. Files read for it:

- `src/cmd/run.rs` (full) — `SpawnSpec.size = viola_pty::host_size()` at :63 (the spawn read); `pump(&mut pty,
  stdin, stdout, &mut viola_pty::host_size)` at :69-74, so pump's FIRST call of that closure is its baseline read.
  `run(home, args)` holds the `--home` path, so a closure wrapped here can stamp both reads into the home.

- `crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs` (:114-124 `Pty` trait; :270-322 `pump`; :450-478 `host_size`; :480-620 tests) —
  `let mut last = host_size();` at :293 is the baseline; a change is forwarded only when a poll differs from it
  (:316). `RESIZE_EVERY` 250 ms (:23), `TICK` 20 ms (:22). The tests drive `pump` with a `MockPty` and a size
  closure (`pump_forwards_a_host_size_change_once` :580).

- `tests/tui_passthrough.rs` (1-121) — the failing test (:93-121): spawn 80×24, wait for the child's `start`
  receipt, resize to 100×30, then press keys until a `size` receipt equals 100×30, asserting within `EXIT_WITHIN`
  (10 s, `tests/support/outer_pty.rs:15`). Receipts carry no timestamp (`src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs:105-116`), and
  the test compares whole receipt objects, so a timestamp field cannot be added to them.

- **Graph impact** — `pump`: 11 call sites — `run` @ `src/cmd/run.rs:69` and 10 tests in
  `crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs` (trace `.andromeda/runs/2026-09-26T21-57-01-implement/tree-query-…json`,
  `callee_name = 'pump'`; the query regenerated the stale rust DB first). A signature change threads through all 11.

- `src/cmd/run.rs` — the temporary instrument (one-shot, removed before the fix lands); then passes the spawn size
  to `pump`.

- `crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs` — `pump` takes the size the PTY was spawned with as its baseline; the 10 test call
  sites; a deterministic test forcing the resize into the window.

- `tests/tui_passthrough.rs` — the resize test's failure message dumps the child's `size` receipts with the times
  the resize was sent and each receipt observed (permanent), plus the instrument's file while it exists.

- Does the local verdict union BOTH legs (Linux leg in WSL + a Windows leg on the host, then CI's `gate --mutants-legs ubuntu-latest,windows-2025`), or judge the Linux leg alone? A Linux leg alone under `--leg` defers every survivor (`run.rs:122`), and `gate --mutants-legs ubuntu-latest` alone judges a `#[cfg(windows)]` body by the ubuntu leg (no named leg compiles it → every named leg judges, `gate.rs:144-149`) — so a Linux-only verdict needs new judging code or goes red on this very chunk's Windows-only WSL-spawning code → blocks: plan-decision.

- Do the local Unix tests take CI's instrumented form (`run --coverage` + `gate --require coverage,doctest`, floors included, needs `llvm-tools-preview` + `cargo-llvm-cov@0.9.1`) or the plain `run --unit --integration` (+ doctest) → blocks: plan-decision.

- Where the operator-pass wiring lives: the project's leaves + test-plan (wrap) and this plan's own operator pass, vs also editing the Andromeda skill's `plan-template.md` (outside this repo) → blocks: plan-decision.
