title: Aim (founder ruling, relayed by the overseer 2026-09-26)

data.head: ## Aim (founder ruling, relayed by the overseer 2026-09-26)

body:
Catch Unix reds BEFORE the push. The last two chunks lost CI round-trips to Unix-only reds this Windows host
could not run: the PTY SIGHUP holder (chunk 2026-09-25-pty-wrapper-on-windows, `fix` commits c05e6e2 / 7681c73)
and the Windows/Linux mutation asymmetry (chunk 2026-09-26-ci-chunk-base-and-union-verdict). CI round-trips cost
more than the code (CARRY 1, operator route adaptation 2026-09-25).

1. **A provisioned Linux toolchain inside WSL2 `Ubuntu`, at CI's pins, never floating.**
   - Every call is `wsl -d Ubuntu -- …`; the DEFAULT distro is `docker-desktop` (CARRY 1; overseer direction 2).
   - rustup + the `rust-toolchain.toml` channel `1.98.1` (components `rustfmt`, `clippy`); cargo-nextest `0.9.146`
     and cargo-mutants `27.1.0`, the CI pins (`ci.yml:166`, `tool: cargo-nextest@0.9.146,cargo-mutants@27.1.0`; the
     CARRY cites `ci.yml:162`, re-verified at promotion to line 166). Installing them inside Ubuntu is in scope
     (overseer direction 3).
   - The pins are read FROM `ci.yml` / `rust-toolchain.toml` (or asserted equal to them) by the provisioning
     step, so a CI pin bump cannot leave the local leg on a stale tool silently (verified feasible: the pins sit
     at `ci.yml:33`, `:166`, `rust-toolchain.toml:2`; research §Files inspected).
   - [premise-corrected: CI's `test` job runs `run --coverage` then `gate --require coverage,doctest`
     (ci.yml:36-44, :137-140), and the harness has both forms] Whether the local Unix tests take CI's
     instrumented form or plain `run --unit --integration` is a P4 fork (research §Open questions 2).
   - [premise-corrected: `cc`/`gcc`/`make`/`pkg-config`/`jq` are absent (research M3); `sudo` needs a password, but
     `wsl.exe -d Ubuntu -u root` is uid 0 with no password (overseer measurement 2026-09-26 23:58, re-read at P5)]
     The C linker (`build-essential`) is installed as root through `wsl -u root --exec /usr/bin/apt-get`, an
     ordinary agent-run build step recorded with its version; so are rustup, the toolchain and the cargo tools.
     `git 2.53.0` is already present.
   - The Rust side of provisioning uses a pinned rustup-init with its published sha256 (host rustup is 1.29.1)
     and `cargo install --locked` for the ci.yml tool pins (arch/security extracts; research M3).

2. **A Linux-filesystem clone of the repo, synced from the Windows working tree.**
   - Lives in the Linux filesystem (e.g. under `~` in Ubuntu), never `/mnt/d` (CARRY 1; direction 4).
   - Carries the repo's git HISTORY, not only the working tree's files: `resolve_base`
     (`crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run/mutants.rs`) derives the mutation base from the master-route
     `· complete ·` pickaxe bounded at the oldest `chore({marker}): operator pre-CI commit`'s parent; without the
     flip in history the base falls to `merge-base HEAD origin/main` and then `base-missing` (the path
     `resolve_base_needs_a_real_commit` tests) (CARRY 2).
   - Synced INCLUDING uncommitted changes — the gate runs before the operator pre-CI commit (direction 4).
   - The sync form is CHOSEN BY MEASUREMENT (speed + correctness) across candidate forms, and the plan records the
     measurement (direction 4).
   - Proven: a dirty file in the Windows tree reaches the Linux run (direction 4).
   - The sync never carries Windows `target/`, `mutants.out*`, or any other git-ignored file into the clone,
     and deletions / renames in the Windows tree propagate (a stale Linux file must not mask a Windows delete)
     — verified by measurement for the clone + fetch + temp-index-patch form: `git add -A` honours
     `.gitignore`, the patch carries deletions, `git clean -fd` (no `-x`) drops stale untracked files while
     keeping the ignored build cache (research M8).
   - Line endings: the synced bytes are the LF bytes — verified (0 CRLF files in the clone's `crates/` and
     `src/`; the patch form normalises through git by construction; research M8).
   - Measured choice (research M8): clone once (4.47 s), then per gate a Windows-built binary patch through a
     temporary index + `fetch` + `reset --hard` + `apply` ≈ 0.9 s, vs rsync 9.85 s / 2.74 s that also carries
     every ignored file not excluded by hand. No listener in either form.
   - Every WSL call is `wsl -d Ubuntu --exec …` with an explicit PATH: the `--` form re-parses argv through the
     distro shell, and the distro PATH carries the Windows PATH incl. the Windows cargo (research M2, M4).
   - The session's `CLAUDE*` values (10 present, incl. `CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN`) do not reach WSL
     (`WSLENV` forwards only `WT_*`; measured 0 inside), and the gate must not add them (research M5).

3. **A bounded Linux build cache.** The WSL vhdx lives on C: (199.1 GB free and a 1.48 GB vhdx, re-measured
   2026-09-26, research M6); the Linux `target/` stays bounded and its size is REPORTED by the gate (direction 2).
   - [inferred] "Bounded" is a stated cap the gate enforces (a cold clean of the clone's `target/` when above
     it), not only a printed size; a vhdx never shrinks on delete, so the cap bounds the PEAK (research M6).
     The cap's value is P4's.

4. **An agent-run gate entry** that, from Windows, syncs the clone and runs inside Ubuntu: the Unix tests + the
   ubuntu mutation leg (`run --mutants --leg ubuntu` or its harness equivalent) against the DERIVED base
   (direction 5; CARRY 1).
   - The leg's printed `base` should equal the Windows and CI legs' base (CARRY 2).
   - The leg is judged by its VERDICT — 0 missed, 0 timeout, unviable ≤ caught — never by caught/unviable counts,
     which differ run to run and from CI's (local 73/6 and 71/8 on one tree, CI 74/5) (CARRY 2).
   - A red there STOPS the push (direction 5).
   - The entry surfaces a missing/unprovisioned distro or tool as a typed, named failure (not a silent skip and
     not a green) — verified pattern: `Refusal { reason, detail }` / `tool-missing` (run.rs:93-105).
   - Where it lives: an INTERNAL `viola-harness` subcommand (`pre-push`, like `gate` / `secret-scan`), forwarded
     by one shim arm each — verified shape (bin/viola-harness.rs:56-69, agent-run.sh:74); the 5-command agent
     surface is untouched; test-plan §3 Internal harness subcommands + Closed enums gain it at wrap.
   - [premise-corrected: under `--leg` a run defers every survivor (run.rs:122), and `gate --mutants-legs
     ubuntu-latest` alone judges a `#[cfg(windows)]` body by the ubuntu leg (gate.rs:144-149)] "Judged by its
     verdict" needs a union reading, not the leg's own exit: either the local union of both legs or new
     Linux-only judging code — a P4 fork (research §Open questions 1). The leg must be NAMED `ubuntu-latest`
     for the unix+linux family (cfg_legs.rs:24).
   - The printed `base` equals the Windows-local derivation by construction: the clone's HEAD is the Windows HEAD
     (fetched sha), its history holds the flip (`a69c5ef` at promotion) and its tree holds the pending record
     (research M8).
   - [premise-corrected: re-derived at P4 — HEAD a69c5ef IS the last flip (`git log -1 -G ' · complete · ' HEAD
     -- .andromeda/master-route.md` → a69c5ef) and HEAD's tree holds 0 pending records, so before the pre-CI
     commit `pre_ci_parent` finds none, the bound is HEAD, and `chunk_flip` takes its "flip is HEAD → HEAD^"
     step (mutants.rs:80-82) → base acd08c7; after the pre-CI commit CI derives a69c5ef] CARRY 2's "the leg's
     printed base should equal the Windows and CI legs' base" does NOT hold for a gate run before the pre-CI
     commit while HEAD is the wrap flip (the normal state at an operator pass): the local base is HEAD^ and the
     local diff adds the previous wrap commit's delta. /implement's local Windows leg has the same skew. How
     the local base reaches CI's (a base-rule change, or the gate after the commit) is a P4 fork.

5. **Wired into the operator pass BEFORE the push entry** (direction 5): every chunk's operator pass runs this gate
   ahead of the `git push` operator entry, and a red there stops the push.
   - [inferred] The wiring's home: the project's own operator-pass contract (test-plan §3 / §10, `.claude/docs/
     workflow.md`, `rules/verification-harness.md`) — the Andromeda skill's `plan-template.md` lives outside this
     repo; whether the "plan template" in direction 5 means the project's docs or the pipeline skill is a P4 fork
     (research §Open questions 3; unverifiable at HEAD — the operator's word decides it).

6. **The Linux red the gate found, folded in** (operator ruling at implement, 2026-09-26, relayed by the overseer:
   "fold, don't split — a red found now goes into this chunk"; `evidence/linux-red-investigation.md`).
   `pre-push` went red 3/3 at `linux-tests` on `tui_host_resize_reaches_the_child` while 68 isolated reproductions
   stayed green. The order is binding, so the cause is MEASURED, not inferred from a green:
   - [inferred] HYPOTHESIS (read from code, unmeasured): the resize lands between the spawn sizing
     (`src/cmd/run.rs:63`) and the pump's second size read (`crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs:293`), so the pump's
     baseline already equals the new size and nothing is ever forwarded.
   - First, instrument: a one-shot, temporary stamp of the spawn read, the pump's baseline read and each changed
     poll (time and value), and a permanent failure dump in the test of the child's `size` receipts with the times
     the test sent the resize and observed each receipt. Run `pre-push` with it before any fix.
   - Only if the dump confirms the window: the pump starts from the spawn size instead of a second read, a test
     forces the resize into that window deterministically (not a timing bet), and `pre-push` reads green three
     times running. If the dump does not confirm it: stop and report what it shows; no fix applied blind.
   - This is a product defect a real user can hit (a terminal resized while `viola run` starts), whatever the
     gate's environment adds.

7. **Entry 6 carries `apt-get update`** (operator ruling, same relay): measured at implement, exit 100 on three 404s
   under stale package lists (`evidence/provision.md`).

- A PLANTED Unix-only failure (e.g. a `#[cfg(unix)]` test that fails) goes RED locally through the gate, before
  any push; removing the plant returns it green.

- The gate's own guard takes its remove-the-guard runs as usual, including a mutation witness (CARRY 1: "that
  gate's own guard takes a mutation witness as usual").
- The dirty-file sync proof (item 2).
- Standing: tests with mutations; fold, do not carry (direction 6).

- [premise-corrected: operator ruling at implement, item 6] Product code changes in exactly one place, the
  `viola-pty` pump's resize baseline (and its caller in `src/cmd/run.rs`), and only if the instrument confirms the
  window; everything else stays test-side / harness / scripts / docs (`viola-e2e`, `scripts/`, the tui test,
  spec amendments at wrap).
- CI stays the verdict of record; the local gate is a pre-push filter, not a replacement for the CI legs.

- [premise-corrected: item 4's base bullet; operator ruling at P4 "Fix the base rule"] The derived-base
  algorithm changes in ONE place only: `chunk_flip`'s "flip is HEAD → HEAD^" step is skipped while the working
  tree's master-route carries a pending record that HEAD's tree lacks (a promoted, uncommitted chunk). Every
  other base rule (override, pre-CI bound, merge-base fallback, `base-missing`) stays as it is.

- Operator rulings at P4 (2026-09-26): the local verdict is the UNION of both legs (ubuntu-latest in WSL +
  windows-2025 on the host, CI's own `gate --mutants-legs`); the Unix tests take the CI test-job form
  (`run --coverage` + `gate --require coverage,doctest`); the wiring is project-side, and the Andromeda
  `plan-template.md` change is a PROPOSAL recorded in this chunk's evidence for the overseer to relay (a project
  chunk never edits Andromeda).
- macOS reds are out of scope (no local macOS).
- `scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1}` + `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/` (the gate entry, its JSON output and typed exit).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` + `rust-toolchain.toml` as pin SOURCES (read, not changed).

- test-plan §3 (harness commands) / §10 (quality gates) / §12, `.claude/docs/{workflow,commands}.md`,
  `rules/verification-harness.md`, `rules/host-win32.md` (WSL recipes) — amended at wrap.

- a69c5ef (the last wrap's flip = HEAD): 13/15 completed success; `lint (windows-2025)` and `test (macos-latest)`
  in progress — **verdict not yet available**; no completed red to disposition.
- Update at P5 (relayed by the overseer): a69c5ef finished success, run 36272899441, all 15.

- **Marker:** 2026-09-27-browser-verdict-reachability · **Version:** viola-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-09-27T18:40:00Z

Prove the browser test pipe end to end before any feature needs it (founder ruling W125; scope.md). A stub Playwright spec opens
a `file://` stub page and asserts one trivially true thing, on:
- all three CI OSes, inside the existing `test` job;
- the WSL pre-push Linux leg.

Its outcome travels through `viola-harness run --browser` into a recorded `playwright` suite, and `gate --require playwright`
reads that suite green. The real assertions, axe and the a11y verdict stay in Epoch 8 and build on this pipe (per test-plan §3
`run` step 3 and `gate`; a11y-plan §9 Pipeline integration).
One set of pins serves every leg:

- **Node** v24.21.0 comes from the official per-OS builds, sha256-checked. The pin lines sit in `ci.yml`, which is the single
  source `scripts/wsl-provision.sh` parses. There is no toolchain action (operator fork 1; security-plan §Dependency Security, CI
  integration).
- **`@playwright/test`** is pinned at 1.63.0 through a committed npm lockfile.

- **The lockfile** gets its own advisory and sources audit in `supply-chain`, plus a weekly advisory twin in `nightly.yml` (operator
  fork 3; the `fuzz/Cargo.lock` template, security-plan §Dependency Security).
Folded work, not about the browser:

- **The overseer direction.** The 8 root-package test waits with a 10 s bound (equal to the nextest `mutants` 10 s kill) drop
  to 7 s and stream a codes-and-counts report to a known file. This is a recorder, not a fix; it copies the viola-pty recorder
  (`2026-09-27-epoch-2-cleanup/evidence/pty-watch-recorder.md`).
- **CARRY 2.** The pty watch stays open. Its expiry now reads 2 of 3 (research.md, Measured facts).

1. **Node pin lines in `ci.yml`.** Add a workflow-level `env:` block holding exactly four keys:
   - `NODE_PIN_VERSION: "24.21.0"`
   - `NODE_PIN_SHA256_LINUX_X64: "fd8e59d5a511510f6a298afb548f18c7d2b1be404d8b4a27d94fbe49f56cb2d6"`
   - `NODE_PIN_SHA256_DARWIN_ARM64: "bed7eea5325e1108f32ce5228ddd6a5f0f08a499ee42aa7442aea583702f6057"`
   - `NODE_PIN_SHA256_WIN_X64: "158f7685b44de51f6c0df1d153526cbcd3e1bc739a8dfc607721cef75de9e541"`

   The values are the official `SHASUMS256.txt` of v24.21.0, read over HTTPS at P4 (see Implementation notes). Implement re-reads
   that file before committing the lines and stops on any difference. No other file restates these values.

2. **`scripts/install-node.sh` (new).** One bash script that CI (on all three OSes, under the runner's bash) and
   `wsl-provision.sh` both call.
   - **Arguments:** `install-node.sh <os-key> <dest-dir>`, where `<os-key>` ∈ `linux-x64 · darwin-arm64 · win-x64`.
   - **Reading the pins:** it reads `NODE_PIN_VERSION` and `NODE_PIN_SHA256_<KEY>` by parsing `.github/workflows/ci.yml` text,
     never the environment. It never restates a value.
   - **Install:** downloads `https://nodejs.org/dist/v<ver>/node-v<ver>-<os-key>.<ext>` with the same curl retry flags as
     rustup-init. It verifies the file with `sha256sum`, falling back to `shasum -a 256`. It extracts to `<dest-dir>`
     (`tar -xJf` / `tar -xzf` / `unzip -q`).
   - **Output:** prints exactly one line, `install-node: <bin dir>`, where the bin dir is `<dest-dir>/bin` on unix and `<dest-dir>`
     on win-x64.
   - **Refusals:**
     - a checksum mismatch → `install-node: checksum mismatch for <file>`, exit 1, nothing extracted;
     - an unreadable pin → `install-node: pin-unreadable`, exit 1;
     - usage → exit 2.
   - **`--probe`:** proves the checksum refusal on a tampered file and the pin parse against the real `ci.yml`. It prints
     `install-node --probe: 1/1 refused, pins ok v<ver>`, never downloading (the `wsl-provision.sh` probe shape, lines 112–133).

3. **`ci.yml` `test` job, the browser steps** (per OS, after `Harness lifecycle` and before `Gate tools present`):
   1. `Node (pinned)`: `bash scripts/install-node.sh <key> "$RUNNER_TEMP/node"`, with the key picked per `runner.os`. The printed
      bin dir is appended to `$GITHUB_PATH`, then `node --version` must equal `v$NODE_PIN_VERSION`.
   2. `npm ci --prefix e2e-web`.
   3. The Chromium install: `npx --no --prefix e2e-web playwright install --with-deps chromium` on ubuntu, and
      `npx --no --prefix e2e-web playwright install chromium` on windows and macOS.
   4. `run --browser` through the pwsh shim on Windows and the sh shim elsewhere (the shape at ci.yml:36–45).

   Then:
   - `Gate verdict` becomes `gate --require coverage,doctest,playwright`.
   - `Upload JUnit` adds `target/agent-run/artifacts/junit-playwright.xml` to its `path`. The artifact name, the scan gate and the
     retention are unchanged.
   - No new job, no new action, no npm or browser cache, no `setup-node`.
   - The step order still ends G2 → G4 → capture → scan → uploads → gate (obs-plan §9 Step order).

4. **`ci.yml` `supply-chain` job, the npm lockfile audit** (after the fuzz lockfile audit):
   - `Node (pinned)` (linux-x64, as in step 3).
   - Then `bash scripts/npm-audit.sh`.
   - Its JSON goes to `target/npm-audit/`, which is **not** the uploaded `target/supply-chain/`, so the unscanned supply-chain
     artifact gains no member. On a failure the step `cat`s it to the log.

5. **`scripts/npm-audit.sh` (new).**
   - `npm audit --prefix e2e-web --package-lock-only --audit-level=low --json > target/npm-audit/audit.json`.
   - Then the sources check: every lockfile `packages.*.resolved` URL starts with `https://registry.npmjs.org/`. It uses `jq -e`;
     jq is a runner tool presence-checked by the job.
   - It prints `npm-audit: advisories 0, sources registry.npmjs.org only`, or names the failing half, and exits 1 on either.
   - `--probe` proves that the sources check refuses a minted lockfile with a foreign `resolved` URL. It prints
     `npm-audit --probe: 1/1 refused, control clean`.

6. **`nightly.yml`:** a weekly job, on the same `schedule` + `workflow_dispatch`, that runs `Node (pinned)` + `npm-audit.sh`
   advisories only, with no cache.

9. **The harness arm, `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run/browser.rs` (new).** `pub(super) fn browser(ws, runner) -> (Suite, Option<Refusal>)`
   runs, in order, each spawn through the `Runner` seam:
   1. It deletes `e2e-web/pw.json` and `e2e-web/pw-junit.xml` (fresh-file-only, the nextest.rs:50 rule).
   2. It runs `NPM ci` in `e2e-web/`. `const NPM: &str` is `"npm.cmd"` on Windows and `"npm"` elsewhere; it is a const, never a fn
      (the fuzz.rs:9–11 rule).
   3. It probes Chromium with `node -e` in `e2e-web/`: exit 0 iff `require('playwright-core').chromium.executablePath()` exists.
   4. It runs `node node_modules/@playwright/test/cli.js test` in `e2e-web/`.
   5. It reads `pw.json` `stats`: `passed = expected`, `failed = unexpected + flaky`, `skipped = skipped`. The failure names come
      from `parse_junit(pw-junit.xml)`. It copies `pw-junit.xml` to `artifacts/junit-playwright.xml`, and the suite's `artifact`
      is the `e2e-web/pw.json` path.
   6. It applies `exit_must_agree(code, "playwright")`.

   Failure arms:
   - If step 2 or step 3 fails, the suite is `failed: 1` with `failures: ["npm-ci-exit-<n>"]` / `["chromium-missing"]`, step 4
     never runs, and the refusal is `browser-missing` (no `detail`).
   - A `pw.json` absent after step 4 is `failed: 1, failures: ["artifact-missing"]`.

10. **`run.rs` threading.**
    - `Selection` gains `pub browser: bool`. `from_flags` is unchanged: `--all` and the default do not select it (operator fork 2).
    - `test_suites` calls `browser::browser` when `sel.browser`, and pushes the suite. The refusal reaches `run_with`'s document as
      `reason: "browser-missing"`, whose `ok` is false.
    - `archive_sources`' filter lists `"playwright"`, so `junit-playwright.xml` is archived.
    - The one full `Selection` literal, `viola-harness.rs:147`, takes the new field from `args.browser`. Every other
      construction spreads a base (`..Selection::default()` / `..flags(…)` / `..named`) and needs no edit. Re-derived at P5:
      `grep -rnE 'Selection \{'`, each literal read to its closing brace for a `..` line.
    - `RunArgs` gains `#[arg(long)] browser: bool`.

11. **Pre-push Linux leg.**
    - `wsl-provision.sh`:
      1. installs Node through `install-node.sh linux-x64 "$HOME/.local/viola-node"`, after moving the extracted
         `node-v<ver>-linux-x64/*` up so the bin dir is `$HOME/.local/viola-node/bin`, and checks `node --version`;
      2. copies the checkout's `e2e-web/package.json` and `package-lock.json` into its own distro scratch
         `$HOME/.cache/viola-provision/e2e-web/`, runs `npm ci` there, then `npx --no playwright install chromium` there.
         It never runs `npm ci` in a checkout: the harness arm does that in the clone, and a run from `/mnt/d` would write Linux
         `node_modules` into the Windows tree.

      `--check` adds `node v<ver>` to the pins-ok line, and `--probe` adds the install-node checksum refusal to its count (3/3).

      A new mode, `--install-deps <user home>`, installs Chromium's system libraries (overseer review direction, 2026-09-27).
      - It refuses with exit 2 unless it runs as uid 0.
      - It first prints the apt command that
        `<user home>/.local/viola-node/bin/node <user home>/.cache/viola-provision/e2e-web/node_modules/@playwright/test/cli.js install-deps --dry-run chromium`
        reports, then runs the same command without `--dry-run`, under `PATH=<user home>/.local/viola-node/bin:` + the system
        dirs.
      - Its last line is `wsl-provision: install-deps ok`.
      - It is launched through `wsl.exe -d Ubuntu -u root`, which is uid 0 with no password (measured 2026-09-26, the form of the
        `build-essential` line). No sudo is ever run.
    - Evidence: `evidence/wsl-chromium-deps.md` records the printed apt package list and a `dpkg-query -W` reading of those
      packages after the install.
    - `pre_push/linux.rs`:
      - `Linux::cmd_env`'s PATH gains the constant, distro-home-derived component `<home>/.local/viola-node/bin`, between
        `.cargo/bin` and `/usr/local/bin`.
      - `tools()` checks `node --version` against `v` + the `NODE_PIN_VERSION` a new `node_pin(ci_yml)` reads. A mismatch stops
        with `tool-pin-mismatch` detail `node`; absence stops with `tool-missing` detail `node`.
      - `linux_tests` runs `run --coverage` (doc key `run`), then `run --browser` (doc key `browser`), then
        `gate --require coverage,doctest,playwright` (doc key `gate`). The stage stays `linux-tests`, so there is no new stage value.

12. **The root-watch recorder (overseer direction; a recorder, not a fix).** New `tests/support/watch.rs`, `pub mod watch;` in
    `tests/support/mod.rs`:
    - `pub const WITHIN: Duration = Duration::from_secs(7)`.
    - `Watch::start(label)`: the report is `<std::env::temp_dir()>/viola-root-watch/<thread name, :: → .>.<label>.report`, created
      and truncated.
    - `note(&self, line)`: appends one line only when it differs from the last one noted (streamed as the state changes).
    - `deadline_check(&self, deadline, what)`: panics after the deadline with `what` plus every report line so far.
    - `Drop`: removes the report unless the thread is panicking.

    Report lines carry codes, counts and booleans only, never file or screen content. The 8 sites:
    - `fake.rs` `WAIT_WITHIN` → `watch::WITHIN`. `wait_for` notes `receipt lines <n> kinds <kinds>`.
    - `home.rs` `READY_WITHIN` → `watch::WITHIN`. `wait_ready` notes `starts w<a> c<b> r<c> snapshot <bool> beat <bool>`.
    - `outer_pty.rs` `EXIT_WITHIN` → `watch::WITHIN`. `wait_exit` notes `exit none` / `exit <code>`, plus `output bytes <n>`.
    - `run_cli.rs` `READY_WITHIN` → `watch::WITHIN`. `wait_raw` notes `start receipt <bool> exited <bool>`.
    - `run_cli.rs:262` notes `claude-child line <bool> role bytes <n>`.
    - `cli_instance_state.rs:220` notes `stat <first char>`.
    - `contract_diag_schema.rs:244` notes `start receipt <bool> exited <bool>`, and `:264` notes `exited <bool>`.

    Each loop's assertion text and its predicate are unchanged.

13. **The recorder's remove-the-guard pair** (testing.md 2026-09-25; the pty precedent). A temporary `zz_root_watch_control` test
    in one root test binary waits on a never-true predicate through `Watch`. Run it with
    `cargo nextest run --features viola/fake-agent --profile mutants -E 'test(=zz_root_watch_control)'`:
    - at `WITHIN` 7 s: `FAIL [~7 s]`, with the report dumped in the message and the file kept;
    - at 12 s: `TIMEOUT [~10 s]`, the output lost, the file kept.

    Confirm each edit on disk (`grep -n`) before its run. Restore 7 s, remove the control (`grep -c zz_root_watch_control` = 0), and
    record both readings in `evidence/root-watch-recorder.md`.
- `scripts/install-node.sh` — the pinned Node install + `--probe` (step 2)
- `scripts/npm-audit.sh` — the lockfile advisory + sources audit + `--probe` (step 5)
- `e2e-web/package.json`, `e2e-web/package-lock.json`, `e2e-web/playwright.config.ts`, `e2e-web/tsconfig.json` (step 7)
- `e2e-web/stub/pipe.html`, `e2e-web/tests/pipe-reachability.spec.ts` (step 8)
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run/browser.rs` — the arm + its runner-seam unit tests (step 9)
- `tests/support/watch.rs` — the recorder (step 12)
- `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-09-27-browser-verdict-reachability/evidence/{root-watch-recorder,code-graph-planes,wsl-chromium-deps}.md` (steps 11, 13–14)

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — the env pin block, the `test` job browser steps + gate + upload path, and the `supply-chain`
  npm audit (steps 1, 3, 4)
- `.github/workflows/nightly.yml` — the weekly npm advisories (step 6)

- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run.rs` — `Selection.browser`, `test_suites`, `archive_sources`, `mod browser;` (step 10).
  Graph: `run_with` @ run.rs:90, viola-harness.rs:154, pre_push.rs:155/184/251. `test_suites` has one caller, run.rs:126.
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-harness.rs` — `RunArgs.browser`, the literal at :147 (step 10)

- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/pre_push/linux.rs` — PATH, `node_pin`, `tools()`, `linux_tests` (step 11). `linux_tests` has one
  caller, `pre_push::stages`.
- `scripts/wsl-provision.sh` — Node, npm ci, Chromium, the deps line, `--check`/`--probe` (step 11)

- `tests/support/mod.rs`, `tests/support/{fake,home,outer_pty}.rs`, `tests/run_cli.rs`, `tests/cli_instance_state.rs`,
  `tests/contract_diag_schema.rs` (step 12)
The live smoke is the harness lifecycle (boot/status/cleanup), because the recorder touches `home.rs`'s readiness.

- **Browser leg:** runs locally on the host's Node (v24.13.1, which satisfies `engines >=20`), after a host Chromium install
  entry.

- **WSL leg:** proven by the pre-push entry. Two plan entries run before it (overseer review direction, 2026-09-27; no operator
  step): the re-provision, as the distro user under `env -i`, then the root `--install-deps` through `wsl.exe -d Ubuntu -u root`.
  The installed package list is recorded in `evidence/wsl-chromium-deps.md`.
- **Pinned Node download:** proven by CI's own run on each OS, because the host keeps its own Node.

- **No headful self-verify gate:** none exists yet, because `viola ui` and its page arrive in Epoch 8, and the stub is a test
  fixture, not a UI surface.

- **One-shot control:** the recorder's remove-the-guard pair (step 13) MUTATES source and reverts, so it runs once at implement,
  with both readings in `evidence/root-watch-recorder.md`. The non-mutating entries that guard it on every re-run are the
  `from_secs(10)` census and the `zz_root_watch_control` census.

- **`npx --no`:** every `npx` form carries `--no`, so a missing local package fails instead of fetching the registry's newest
  Playwright.

  `webServer`, no `bypassCSP`, and the `pw.json` + `pw-junit.xml` reporters. The stub spec carries no tag, `skip`, `fixme` or
  `waitForTimeout`, and no `route` interception (per test-plan §3 Bootstrap phases `test-runner-install`; a11y-plan §10, §11 SLO).

- (tests / obs) In CI, the `test` job on windows-2025, macos-latest and ubuntu-latest runs `run --browser`. Its `Gate verdict`
  requires `coverage,doctest,playwright`, and the operator's `ci.py conclusion` read is `verdict: green` on the pushed HEAD, with
  its run id recorded. G2, G4 and `secret-scan` still run `if: always()` after the browser step, and `junit-playwright.xml` uploads
  only behind `steps.secret-scan.outcome == 'success'` (per test-plan §9 Pipeline structure; obs-plan §9 Step order and
  conditions).

- (security) `zizmor .github/workflows/` passes. No new `uses:` is added: every one stays a 40-hex SHA, and Node comes from a
  sha256-verified download with no toolchain action. `install-node.sh --probe` shows the checksum refusal. The four pin lines exist
  once, in `ci.yml` (per security-plan §Dependency Security, CI integration; §Security Anti-Patterns → Code Patterns).

- (security) The npm lockfile is committed and audited. `npm-audit.sh` reports 0 advisories and registry.npmjs.org-only sources in
  `supply-chain`, `--probe` refuses a foreign source, the weekly nightly twin exists, and `target/supply-chain/` gains no member
  (per security-plan §Dependency Security, the `fuzz/` exemption precedent).

- (security) The WSL leg installs only CI's pins: `install-node.sh linux-x64` parses `ci.yml`, and `tools()` refuses
  `tool-pin-mismatch` `node` on any other version. The only new `env -i` content is the constant PATH component
  `<home>/.local/viola-node/bin`, which carries no host value. No gate or harness step runs through `wsl-exec.sh` (per security-plan
  §Dependency Security, Pinning (WSL2); §Secret Management, Development).

- (tests) The pre-push document's `linux` object carries `browser` with `playwright` passed ≥ 1, and `gate` requiring
  `coverage,doctest,playwright`, at `"stage":"union"` ok (per test-plan §3 Internal harness subcommands `pre-push`).

- (arch) `e2e-web/tsconfig.json` is present with `noEmit` and `strict`, and no `tsconfig*.json` or `package.json` exists under
  `crates/`. No Cargo workspace member is added, and `release-check.sh` prints `release-check: viola only` (per architecture
  §Infrastructure Patterns → Code-graph planes; §Established Decisions [Module Boundaries]).

- (design) `e2e-web/stub/pipe.html` has no inline script or style, no `@font-face`, no web font or CDN asset, no hex colour, and no
  `viola-*` element (per design-system §Anti-Patterns → Per-Surface Bans (web-spa); §Surface: web-spa (Toolkit)).

- (tests, overseer direction) `grep -rnE 'from_secs\(10\)' tests` prints nothing, and each of the 8 sites waits on
  `watch::WITHIN` (7 s). The remove-the-guard pair is recorded:
  - 7 s → `FAIL` with the report in its message and the file kept;
  - 12 s → `TIMEOUT`, the output lost, the file kept.

  No report resolves under `target/e2e-home/**/diagnostics/`, and `schema-check` is green (per test-plan §3 Bootstrap phases
  `[profile.mutants]`; obs-plan §9 G4).

- (tests) The chunk's mutation verdict is green on the CI union: `missed == 0`, `timeout == 0`, `unviable <= caught` (per test-plan
  §10 Mutation gate).
- Research files inspected: see research.md §Files inspected.

- Operator forks (P4, overseer): Node = pinned download (the sha256 per OS sits in ci.yml as the single source wsl-provision
  parses); reach = `--browser` only, with the host-stage mirror a route note with an owner; npm audit wired now, no exemption.

- `actions/setup-node` or any toolchain action — rejected at fork 1. It reverses "no toolchain action" and would be a boundary
  widening.
- Runner-image Node — rejected. The images disagree (22.23.2 / 22.23.2 / 24.20.0), and WSL would have no CI pin to copy.

- A Playwright `route` fulfilment or a fixture server for the stub — rejected. test-plan §3 Browser-side controls ban
  `route.fulfill`/`route.abort`, and §8 bans HTTP fake servers; a server would also be a new listener (security-plan
  §Anti-Patterns → Universal).

- `--all` selecting browser, and the pre-push host `windows-tests` stage running it — rejected at fork 2 for this chunk. The host
  mirror is a route note (Implementation notes).

- Uploading `pw.json` or `e2e-web/test-results/` — not this chunk. `pw.json` embeds absolute paths, and the `test-results/` upload
  is a11y-ci-gate-wire's (a11y-plan §9 Artifact retention).
- The npm audit JSON in `target/supply-chain/` — rejected. It would join the unscanned upload, which needs a live ratification.

- Pinning `@axe-core/playwright` now, or `typescript` / `@types/node` — rejected. axe is Epoch 8, and no typecheck gate lands in
  this chunk (the tsconfig marks the ts code-graph plane).

- Spawning `npx`/`npm` through a shell, or an `.cmd` as a PTY child — never (security.md). `npm.cmd` goes through
  `std::process::Command` with fixed literal args only, and Playwright runs as `node <cli.js>`.
- Raising any wait bound — never (overseer direction; testing.md 2026-09-24 extended 2026-09-27).
- An `npm`/Playwright cache in CI — never (test-plan §12 Browser caching; security-plan cache-poisoning class).

  - that `unzip` exists in the windows-2025 runner's bash: measured by CI's own `Node (pinned)` step on that leg. Fall back to
    `pwsh Expand-Archive` in a pwsh step if red;

    `run --browser` gate.

- **The `browser-missing` reason is new to the run document's closed reasons.** Together with the `tool-pin-mismatch` / `tool-missing`

    - §3 `run` step 3: browser on every OS; the `browser-linux-only` arm retired; the harness spawns npm and the Playwright CLI

    - §3 `run` step 2: the `booted_wrapper` bound 10 s → 7 s.

    - the npm lockfile audit and its nightly twin;

  - architecture:

      `supply-chain` npm audit, `nightly.yml`, and pre-push `linux-tests` carrying browser;

      - `target/npm-audit/`;
      - the CI `$RUNNER_TEMP/node`;
      - the distro's `~/.local/viola-node/` and `~/.cache/ms-playwright/`;
    - §Infrastructure Patterns → Project directory structure: the `e2e-web/` entries this chunk creates.
  - obs-plan §9 Step order and Test report format: the browser step in the `test` job, and `junit-playwright.xml` in `junit-<os>`.

**Chunk:** Browser verdict reachability. An e2e-web/ stub spec runs under pinned Playwright on three CI OSes and the WSL pre-push,
piped through `run --browser` to a gated green playwright suite. The 8 root 10 s waits are lowered to 7 s with streamed reports.
**Date:** 2026-09-27T19:55Z
**Commits:** `5f0a809 chore(2026-09-27-browser-verdict-reachability): operator pre-CI commit, for the run this chunk's verdict reads`
(the only commit since `last_wrap` 2026-09-27T17:41:38Z besides that wrap's own `49f6444`; `git log 49f6444..HEAD`)

- **Symbols / APIs:**
  - **`viola-harness run --browser`** (a new `RunArgs.browser` flag; `Selection.browser: bool`). `Selection::from_flags` is
    unchanged: `--all` and the no-selector default do NOT select browser (operator fork 2). The one full `Selection` literal,
    `viola-harness.rs` `run_cmd`, takes `browser: args.browser`. Every other literal spreads a base.
  - **`run/browser.rs` `browser(ws, runner) -> (Suite, Option<Refusal>)`**, which runs each step through the `Runner` seam:
    1. It deletes `e2e-web/pw.json`, `e2e-web/pw-junit.xml` and `artifacts/junit-playwright.xml`.
    2. It spawns `NPM ci` in `e2e-web/`, where `const NPM` is `npm.cmd` on Windows and `npm` elsewhere, with fixed literal args
       through `std::process::Command`.
    3. It runs `node -e <CHROMIUM_PROBE>`: exit 0 iff `require('playwright-core').chromium.executablePath()` exists.
    4. It runs `node node_modules/@playwright/test/cli.js test`. No shell and no npx.
    5. The suite `playwright` is built from `pw.json` `stats`: passed = `expected`, failed = `unexpected + flaky`, skipped =
       `skipped`. Its `failures` names come from `parse_junit(pw-junit.xml)`, which is copied to `artifacts/junit-playwright.xml`.
       Its `artifact` is the absolute `e2e-web/pw.json`. Then `exit_must_agree(code, "playwright")`.

    Failure arms: `npm ci` red → `failed:1, failures:["npm-ci-exit-<n>|signal"]`. Chromium absent →
    `failures:["chromium-missing"]`. Either one gives the refusal `browser-missing` (no `detail`), and Playwright never runs. A
    `pw.json` absent or without `stats` → `failures:["artifact-missing"]`.
  - **`run.rs`:**
    - `test_suites` now returns `(Vec<Suite>, Option<Refusal>)`, and pushes the browser suite after the doctests when
      `sel.browser`. Its caller, `run_with` (the sole caller, per the graph at P3), takes `browser_refusal.or(tool_refusal)`.
    - `archive_sources` adds `playwright`: its archived `junit-playwright.xml` is sourced from the sibling of the suite's
      artifact, `pw-junit.xml`.
    - `run_with`'s other callers (`run()`, `run_cmd`, `pre_push::stages`, `windows_tests`) keep their selections; none sets
      `browser`.
  - **`pre_push/linux.rs`:**
    - A new `pub fn node_pin(ci_yml) -> Option<String>` reads the workflow-level `  NODE_PIN_VERSION:` line.
    - A new `const NODE_BIN = ".local/viola-node/bin"`. `Linux::cmd_env`'s `env -i` PATH is now
      `<home>/.cargo/bin:<home>/.local/viola-node/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin` (a constant, distro-home-derived
      component; no host value).
    - `tools()` checks `node --version` == `v<pin>` after the cargo pins. Absent → `tool-missing` detail **`node`**; off-pin →
      `tool-pin-mismatch` detail **`node`**; the pin line unreadable → `tool-pin-mismatch` `pins-unreadable`.
    - `linux_tests` runs `run --coverage` (doc key `run`), then **`run --browser` (a new doc key `linux.browser`)**, then
      `gate --require coverage,doctest,playwright` (doc key `gate`). A browser red stops before the gate, and the stage stays
      `linux-tests`. An unreadable `run --browser` document stops `linux-document-unreadable` with the existing detail `run`.
    - `linux_tests` has one caller, `pre_push::stages`. The host `windows-tests` stage is unchanged: no browser (fork 2).

body: sit ~44 of 50 chunks after base CI, the shape that cost another project ~588 runner-minutes in 11 days.

- `viola-pty tests::spawn_runs_a_raw_child_that_sees_its_size_a_resize_and_its_own_exit_code` stays OPEN. It recurred once
  (2026-09-27 16:02:58Z, the operator pre-push windows leg's cargo-mutants unmutated baseline, `TIMEOUT [10.107s]`), with no
  capture. The recorder is in place (`CHILD_WITHIN` 7 s; report at `<temp dir>/viola-pty-watch/<test name>.report`). Match any
  recurrence to this name; a red with a captured report re-opens the cause. A green re-run never closes it.
- `viola-e2e::harness_lifecycle harness_session_boots_reports_logs_and_tears_down`: no recurrence.

- Expiry: both watches retire after 3 consecutive green CI runs with no recurrence of either name. The count is 1 of 3 so far
  (ci#36333711860 on `f0e6dbc`). This chunk records each CI run it reads against the count.
- H2 (a key lost within ~50 ms of a ConPTY resize, rstudio/rstudio#18884) is owed to the operator. It is not this chunk's work.

title: Overseer direction at P1: the 8 root-package tests with a 10 s child wait (NOT a CARRY)

data.head: ### Overseer direction at P1: the 8 root-package tests with a 10 s child wait (NOT a CARRY)

body:
Each waits on a child with a 10 s bound, equal to the nextest `mutants` profile's kill (`slow-timeout` period 5 s × terminate-after
2 = 10 s). The pty-watch remove-the-guard pair measured the race (`2026-09-27-epoch-2-cleanup/evidence/pty-watch-recorder.md`):
7 s = the test fails itself and its dump survives; 10 s = a race; 12 s = killed, report lost. **Direction, as corrected by the
overseer:** LOWER each bound below the kill (7 s, as the viola-pty recorder did) and stream the child report to a known file.
Never raise a bound. (The session-start dashboard said "raise"; that wording was wrong and is corrected here.)
Coordinates, re-verified on disk at P1 (all read `from_secs(10)`):
- `tests/support/fake.rs:12` `WAIT_WITHIN`
- `tests/support/home.rs:19` `READY_WITHIN`
- `tests/support/outer_pty.rs:15` `EXIT_WITHIN` (pub; also used by `home.rs:270` and `run_cli.rs:70`)
- `tests/run_cli.rs:19` `READY_WITHIN`
- `tests/run_cli.rs:262` (an inline `Duration::from_secs(10)`)
- `tests/cli_instance_state.rs:220` (an inline `Duration::from_secs(10)`, the `-STOP` wait)
- `tests/contract_diag_schema.rs:244` and `:264` (inline, the raw-terminal wait and the exit wait)

"Stream the child report" per test means the evidence at the moment of a stuck wait: what the test was polling. It survives a
runner kill in a known file under `<temp dir>/viola-root-watch/<test name>.report` (or the pty recorder's dir; P4 picks), is kept
on failure or kill, and is removed by a passing test. It is also dumped in the test's own panic message at the 7 s bound.
Behaviour and assertions are unchanged. This is a recorder, not a fix.

Verified at P3. The count of 8 was re-derived by `grep -rnE 'from_secs\((1[0-9]|[2-9][0-9])\)'` over `tests`: 9 hits, one an
mtime back-date. What each loop polls:
- the fake-agent receipt (`fake.rs` `wait_for`);
- `Starts` + snapshot + heartbeat + `try_wait` (`home.rs` `wait_ready`);
- `try_wait` (`outer_pty.rs` `wait_exit`, also `finish` and `Drop`);
- the receipt `start` (`run_cli.rs` `wait_raw`);
- `run-builder.ndjson` `claude-child` (`run_cli.rs:262`);
- `ps -o stat=` (`cli_instance_state.rs:220`);
- the raw receipt and `try_wait` (`contract_diag_schema.rs:244`/`:264`).
Reports stay outside `target/e2e-home/**/diagnostics/` (G4, obs extract).

title: CI verdict read at Setup 5a (the second fold source)

data.head: ## CI verdict read at Setup 5a (the second fold source)

body: - Base: the last master flip `49f644472a11` (the epoch-2-cleanup wrap commit). Shas read: `49f644472a11` only.

- `49f644472a11`: **CI 49f644472a11: verdict not yet available.** ci#36340086338 was `in_progress` at 18:21Z (checks 15/15 listed,
  the oldest running `lint (windows-2025)` at 233 s). Wall-clock was not yet measurable, so it was neither folded nor read as
  green. The operator's CI read for this chunk uses the `ci.py conclusion` tool form (overseer directive 4).

- Re-read at P3 (the runner-only witness, the same run): `49f644472a11 verdict: green · checks 15/15 · wall 235 s · runs
  ci#36340086338 completed/success`. Nothing is owed to fold. CARRY 2's expiry count is now **2 of 3** (ci#36333711860 on
  `f0e6dbc`, then ci#36340086338 on `49f6444`), with no recurrence of either watched name.

_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-09-27-epoch-2-cleanup · **Version:** viola-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-09-27T14:40:00Z

Clean the Epoch 2 problem spots before Epoch 2b builds on them, without changing product behaviour. Four files drop under 800
tokei code lines by moving whole concerns, with their inline tests, into submodules beside a kept parent file. The three named
clone pairs are replaced by one feature-gated test-support module in `viola-channel`. The harness stops leaving ~30 GB on C: and
stops fighting rust-analyzer: on a Windows host, `run --mutants` puts cargo-mutants' temp copies and output in one guarded scratch
dir outside the repo. Four fix-loop aids land: a scoped inner loop, a failed test's home kept, per-run archives, a WSL wrapper.
The machete false positive is annotated. The viola-pty recurrence watch gets its forced-window reproduction.

The audit's 11 "survivors" need no killing tests: recorded CI verdicts judged all 11 caught or unviable on their compiling leg
(scope item 3, premise-corrected; research.md fact 5). This chunk's own union re-judges every mutant its diff regenerates.

Provenance: architecture §Infrastructure Patterns (Crate dependency direction, Build system, CI/CD approach) · test-plan §3
(`run`, `pre-push`, Closed enums), §9 Lint, §10 Mutation gate · security-plan §Bootstrap phases (secret-scanning-ci-gate),
§Dependency Security, §Secret Management (Development) · obs-plan §8 item 6, §9 G1/G4 · a11y-plan §1 (tui), §3 Keyboard test
harness · design-system §Surface: cli (Streams, `viola run` passthrough).

1. **Metrics tool and before-controls.** Copy `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-09-24-epoch-1-cleanup/metrics.py` to this chunk's folder,
   keeping its population rule (`git ls-files -co --exclude-standard '*.rs'` minus `scripts/ docs/ refs/ fuzz/ .andromeda/ .claude/`)
   and its fresh-tempdir output. Keep two subcommands, each printing detail lines then the verdict count as its LAST line:
   - `size`: tokei `code` for the four split files, their new submodules, and every file over 800; last line = the count over 800.
   - `clones`: the audit's jscpd command (`.andromeda/code-metrics.ndjson` last record `commands.duplication`). It prints each pair
     that is IN SCOPE or NEW, then their count:
     - in scope: an end in `tests/channel_endpoint.rs` with the other in `crates/viola-channel/src/server.rs` or its `server/`
       dir; or one end in `crates/viola-channel/src/lib.rs` or `test_capture` and the other in `src/cmd/run.rs`;
     - new: a file-pair absent from the ALLOWED list, which is the file-pairs the control run prints outside the in-scope set,
       written into the script from that run.
   Run both on the UNTOUCHED tree first and record the readings in `evidence/metrics-before.md`: predicted `size` 4, `clones` 3.

2. **Forced-window reproduction of the viola-pty watch (first, per the route CARRY).** In `crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs` tests:
   - Add a `CHILD_MODE` value `hold` to `pty_child_entry` (:982). After reporting the first byte, it holds for a fixed test-only
     interval before its second `read_exact`. The hold widens the window; it is not synchronisation (testing.md 2026-09-27).
   - Add a test that runs `spawn_runs_a_raw_child_that_sees_its_size_a_resize_and_its_own_exit_code`'s sequence (:1123) under
     `hold`: the key, then `resize(120x40)` and the second key while the child is still holding.
   - Hypothesis H1 under test: the red of run 36296402785 lost the key because the resize and the key reached ConPTY before the
     child re-entered its read.
   - Hypothesis H2, from the platform record (research.md Platform issues consulted): rstudio/rstudio#18884 measured "a keystroke
     typed within ~50ms of a process_set_size RPC was lost on Windows CI (ConPTY + MSYS bash)", below the app. The existing test
     already writes its key within that window and was 60/60 green on this host, so H2 is not forced by this step. If it is real,
     it is a product question, because viola forwards resizes and keys. The report records H2 as an owed item for the operator
     whatever step 2 reads; this chunk builds no fix for it.
   - Run it 20 times in isolation on this host (the gate entry below).
   - **Green 20/20:** the hypothesis is falsified here. Record it, keep the test as a standing witness, and keep the watch with its
     expiry.
   - **Any red:** STOP the chunk's fix-loop on this item and report the reading to the operator. A key dropped after a resize would
     break "the human always wins", and the fix's scope is the operator's decision. Do not raise `CHILD_WITHIN` and do not retry.
   - Record every reading in `evidence/pty-forced-window.md`.

3. **viola-pty split.** Move the pump machinery from `crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs` into `crates/viola-pty/src/pump.rs` with its
   inline tests:
   - `Worker`, `spawn_worker`, `copy`, `pump`, `drain`, `kill_and_reap`, the pump-only consts;
   - the pump tests (:524–929).
   `lib.rs` re-exports `pump` and `PumpEnd` so every graph row stays at `viola_pty::<name>` (research.md Graph impact: `pump` 1
   site, `PumpEnd` 3). `PtyError`'s hand-written `Display` and the dependency set stay unchanged. Target: `lib.rs` ≤ 700 code lines.

4. **viola-channel test-support module (the two clone classes).** Operator decision at P4:
   - Add `crates/viola-channel/src/test_support.rs`, compiled under `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))]`. It holds:
     - a `JsonFields` `tracing::field::Visit` into a `serde_json` map (debug · str · u64 · i64 · bool);
     - on Windows: `canonical_sddl`, `dacl_of(endpoint)`, and an independent `user_sid` read from the process token, apart from
       `server::win::user_sid`.
   - `test_capture` (lib.rs:103) and `src/cmd/run.rs`'s test module use `JsonFields`.
   - `server.rs`'s DACL read-back test (:896) uses `dacl_of`, `canonical_sddl` and the independent `user_sid`.
   - `tests/channel_endpoint.rs` drops its `mod win` copies of those three for the shared ones.
   - Add `test-support = []` to `crates/viola-channel/Cargo.toml` `[features]`. Enable it only from the root `Cargo.toml`
     `[dev-dependencies]` (`viola-channel` with `features = ["test-support"]`). No other manifest names it.
   - Kill every mutant the module adds with `viola-channel` unit tests: one JSON value per `record_*` type, and the existing
     alias case for `canonical_sddl`.

5. **viola-channel split.** Move `mod win` (server.rs:456–554) and its DACL/SDDL tests into `crates/viola-channel/src/server/win.rs`.
   `server.rs` stays the module root and keeps `bind`/`serve`/`Dispatch`/`Serving` at their paths (graph rows: `Server` 13 sites,
   `bind` 9). The listener controls stay at their call sites: `security_descriptor`, `accept_remote(false)`, first-instance,
   `inheritable(false)`, and no `ListenerOptionsExt::mode` or `try_overwrite`. Target: `server.rs` ≤ 700 code lines.

6. **run/mutants split.** Move the base resolution from `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run/mutants.rs` into
   `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run/mutants/base.rs` with its tests:
   - `git`, `commit_sha`, `MASTER_ROUTE`, `resolve_base`, `chunk_flip`, `uncommitted_promotion`, `pre_ci_parent`, `pending_marker`,
     `chunk_diff`;
   - `resolve_base_needs_a_real_commit`, the `chunk_base_*` tests, `chunk_diff_holds_tracked_edits_and_untracked_files`.
   `mutants.rs` keeps `mutants()` and the suite/verdict code. Callers keep their paths through `pub use`. Target: `mutants.rs` ≤ 700.

7. **Host mutation scratch, with its guard.** New `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run/mutants/scratch.rs` (operator decision at P4).
   - A const `HOST_SCRATCH: bool = cfg!(windows)`. It is a const, never a fn, so its mutant is killable (testing.md 2026-09-24).
   - The scratch path is `<repo root parent>/viola-mutants-scratch`. It is never printed, and no document carries it.
   - **Guard** (overseer condition): a pure fn refuses unless the resolved path's final component is exactly
     `viola-mutants-scratch`, the path is neither the repo root nor any ancestor of it, and the path is not a drive or filesystem
     root. A refusal is `reason:"scratch-refused"`, never a fallback to `%TEMP%` or the repo. rstest cases cover each refusal and
     the accepted path. Give the guard its own remove-the-guard pair: neutralise it, show the refusal tests red, restore it; record
     both readings in `evidence/scratch-guard.md`.
   - Before cargo-mutants, `mutants()` measures the scratch's bytes, removes it and recreates it. A removal that fails (a leaked
     process holding a file) is `reason:"scratch-wipe-failed"`, never ignored.
   - The `cargo mutants` command gets `TMP`/`TEMP` set to the scratch and `--output <scratch>`.
   - The stale-outcomes delete, `outcomes.json`, `missed.txt` and `timeout.txt` are all read from `<scratch>/mutants.out`.
   - The `mutants` section of the document gains `scratch_bytes`, the bytes found before the wipe.
   - Off Windows (`HOST_SCRATCH` false) nothing changes: `ws.root/mutants.out`, the inherited temp dir, no `scratch_bytes`.
   - The leftover `mutants.out/` at the repo root (gitignored residue of runs before this change) is removed once, by hand, at
     implement, with its size recorded in evidence. After that, the `test ! -e mutants.out` entry proves no run recreates it.

8. **pre-push split and its scratch report.** Move the distro side of `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/pre_push.rs` into
   `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/pre_push/linux.rs`: `Linux`, `distro_home`, `tools`, `sync`, `dir_bytes`, `target_bytes`, `cache`,
   `linux_harness`, `linux_tests`, `linux_leg`, the pure helpers `wsl_path`, `ci_pins`, `last_document`, `summary`, `leg`, and their
   tests. The `Fake` runner scaffolding stays in the parent's inline test module as `pub(super)` items, never an out-of-line
   `#[cfg(test)]` file (testing.md 2026-09-25). `viola-harness` keeps its `harness::pre_push::` paths through `pub use`.
   `cache` gains two path-free fields:
   - `windows_scratch_bytes`: the host scratch's bytes at the cache stage, 0 when absent;
   - `windows_scratch_bytes_after`: the same, read after the windows leg.
   Extend `pre_push_document_carries_no_absolute_path` (:1145) to the new fields. Target: `pre_push.rs` ≤ 700 code lines.

9. **Scoped inner loop (evolve P3).**
   - `run --mutants --file <path>` (repeatable) passes each `--file` to cargo-mutants beside `--in-diff`.
   - The document says `verdict:"scoped"` with `files`. It never writes a `mutants-verdict-<leg>.json`, so no union can read it.
   - `--file` together with `--leg` is a usage refusal (exit 2, `reason:"usage"`, `detail:"scoped-leg"`).
   - Survivors make it red like a counted run. It is a filter, never the verdict (test-plan §10).
   - Parse in `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-harness.rs` and `harness/run.rs` (`Selection`), with unit tests for each branch.

10. **A failed lifecycle test keeps its home (evolve P3).** `crates/viola-e2e/tests/harness_lifecycle.rs`'s booted tests call
    `cleanup` keeping the home, then remove it in a `Drop` guard. The guard keeps the home when the thread is panicking and
    `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_FAILED=1`, mirroring `tests/support/home.rs` `keep_decision` (:21–23). A passing run removes the home as today.
    `run --mutants` still sets `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_FAILED=0` (mutants.rs:375, its test :1058 unchanged).

11. **Per-run archive (evolve P7).** At the end of every `run`, copy the JUnit files this run wrote under
    `target/agent-run/artifacts/`, and the `outcomes.json` it read, into `target/run-archive/<n>/`. `<n>` is one more than the
    highest existing. Keep the newest 10 and remove older ones. The archive sits outside `target/agent-run/`, so no CI upload
    reaches it (ci.yml:114–118) and no absolute argv path leaves the host. A missing source is skipped and named. The document
    gains `archived`, the repo-relative dir. Unit-test the numbering, the pruning and the skip.

12. **`scripts/wsl-exec.sh` (evolve P11).** A fail-closed bash wrapper:
    - it resolves the distro user's HOME with `wsl.exe -d Ubuntu --exec /usr/bin/printenv HOME`;
    - it runs `MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL='*' wsl.exe -d Ubuntu [--cd DIR] --exec /usr/bin/env -i HOME=<home>
      PATH=<home>/.cargo/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin "$@"`, the same env discipline as `pre_push.rs` `cmd_env` (:79–94);
    - `--probe` runs `/usr/bin/printenv` through itself and passes only when exactly HOME and PATH are set, no `CLAUDE*` name is
      present and the argv `/usr/bin/printenv` arrived unconverted.
    It is an operator aid. `pre-push` keeps its own `Command`s.

13. **cargo-machete annotation.** Add `[package.metadata.cargo-machete] ignored = ["proc-macro2"]` to `crates/viola-e2e/Cargo.toml`,
    with a one-line comment: the pin only enables syn's `span-locations` for `harness::cfg_legs`.

14. **release-check proves the feature absent (overseer condition).** In `scripts/release-check.sh`, `judge` also refuses a
    compiler-artifact record whose `features` contain `test-support` or `fake-agent`
    with a `release-check: FAILED — test-only feature` line that names the feature and the target. `--probe` adds a synthetic record for each, so the probe
    reads `5/5 refused, control clean`. The release build's own verdict stays `release-check: viola only`.

15. **Evidence and the sizing reading.** Write `evidence/audit-survivors-union.md` with research.md fact 5's three CI readings (run
    ids, legs, outcomes per mutant). After the green pre-push, record `legs.*.tested`, the per-leg `mutants tested in` lines and the
    pre-push wall-clock against the prediction below.
- `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-09-27-epoch-2-cleanup/metrics.py` — the size/clones instrument (step 1).
- `crates/viola-pty/src/pump.rs` — the pump machinery + tests (step 3).
- `crates/viola-channel/src/test_support.rs` — `JsonFields` + the Windows DACL helpers (step 4).
- `crates/viola-channel/src/server/win.rs` — `mod win` + its tests (step 5).
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run/mutants/base.rs` — base resolution + tests (step 6).
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run/mutants/scratch.rs` — the host scratch, its guard and wipe (step 7).
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/pre_push/linux.rs` — the distro side of `pre-push` + tests (step 8).
- `scripts/wsl-exec.sh` — the WSL wrapper (step 12).
- `crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs` — the `hold` child mode + forced-window test; the pump moved out and re-exported (steps 2–3).
- `crates/viola-channel/src/lib.rs` — `mod test_support` declaration; `test_capture` uses `JsonFields` (step 4).
- `crates/viola-channel/src/server.rs` — `mod win;` declaration; DACL test on the shared helpers (steps 4–5).
- `crates/viola-channel/Cargo.toml` — `test-support = []` (step 4).
- `Cargo.toml` (root) — `[dev-dependencies]` enables `viola-channel/test-support` (step 4).
- `src/cmd/run.rs` — its test module's `Fields` replaced by `JsonFields` (step 4).
- `tests/channel_endpoint.rs` — `mod win` reduced to the shared helpers (step 4).
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run/mutants.rs` — the split, the scratch wiring, the scoped mode (steps 6, 7, 9).
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run.rs` — `Selection` / scoped files; the archive at the end of `run_with` (steps 9, 11).
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/pre_push.rs` — the split; the `cache` scratch fields (step 8).
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-harness.rs` — `--file` parse (step 9).
- `crates/viola-e2e/tests/harness_lifecycle.rs` — the keep-on-failure guard (step 10).
- `crates/viola-e2e/Cargo.toml` — the machete metadata (step 13).
- `scripts/release-check.sh` — the feature refusal + probes (step 14).
The gates run on this Windows host during /implement.

- **Supply-chain and release:** the manifests change (a feature on `viola-channel`, a root dev-dependency entry), so the
  supply-chain gates run and `release-check` proves the feature stays out of the release build.
- **Integration:** runs with `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES=1` so `schema-check` and `secret-scan` read the homes.
- **Boot smoke:** a mint-then-read session `p-cleanup-smoke`, because `viola-harness` changes.

- **pre-push:** the mutation and coverage gate. Stop rust-analyzer by exact `ExecutablePath` before it until step 7 lands
  (host-win32.md 2026-09-26); after that, the scratch keeps `mutants.out` outside the repo. Its windows leg now runs in the scratch.
- **CI read:** `ci.py conclusion --wait`. A check that completes failed ends the read red; a green read waits for the whole run.

  unit/integration entries are green, with test names and assertions unchanged (per test-plan §3; research.md Graph impact).

- (tests) The scratch guard refuses each bad path with `scratch-refused` and accepts the exact sibling. Its remove-the-guard pair
  is recorded in `evidence/scratch-guard.md` (per test-plan §10; overseer condition at P4).

- (tests) On this host `run --mutants` takes the scratch path: the scoped entry's document carries `scratch_bytes`, and
  `test ! -e mutants.out` passes after it, so no output lands under the repo root. The green pre-push's windows leg runs the same

- (tests) `run --mutants --file …` prints `verdict:"scoped"` and writes no leg verdict. `--file` with `--leg` exits 2 with
  `detail:"scoped-leg"` (per test-plan §3 Closed enums, §10).

- (tests) A deliberately failing lifecycle test under `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_FAILED=1` leaves its session home, and a passing one removes
  it. Both readings are recorded in `evidence/keep-failed-home.md` (per test-plan §3 Test data bootstrap).

  reading goes in `evidence/pty-forced-window.md` (per test-plan §10 zero-flakiness; testing.md 2026-09-27).

- (tests) `pre-push` ends `ok:true` at `stage:"union"`. Its `cache` carries `windows_scratch_bytes` / `windows_scratch_bytes_after`,
  and the document carries no absolute path (per test-plan §3 `pre-push`; obs-plan §8 item 6).

- (security) `release-check --probe` reads `5/5 refused, control clean` and `release-check` reads `viola only`: `test-support` and
  `fake-agent` are absent from the release build (per security-plan Decisions Log 2026-09-27 → Conditions; overseer condition at P4).

- (security) `target/run-archive/` is gitignored (the `git check-ignore` entry), and the scratch sits outside the repo. No CI upload
  reaches either, since the ci.yml upload paths are unchanged. `wsl-exec.sh --probe` passes (per security-plan §Bootstrap phases →

- (security) `viola-channel` still constructs exactly one listener with `security_descriptor`, and has zero `try_overwrite` /

  `harness_lifecycle.rs`, `tests/support/home.rs`, `ci.yml`, the channel/core manifests, the CI evidence).

- Operator decisions (P4, overseer on the founder's delegation): the `viola-channel` `test-support` feature, with release-check
  proving it absent; one host scratch dir for temp copies and `--output`, with the path guard and its remove-the-guard pair.
- Killing tests for the audit's 11 survivors — not owed. Recorded CI verdicts judged all 11 on their compiling leg (scope item 3).

- rust-analyzer stopped by the harness — rejected at P4. It would kill rust-analyzer serving other workspaces; the scratch
  removes the cause instead.

- The `Fields` visitor in `viola-core` — rejected at P4. Core has no tracing/serde_json/windows-sys, so the helpers would split
  across two crates.

- Deleting either DACL test — rejected. The in-crate test is the one cargo-mutants runs (testing.md 2026-09-27); the root test
  holds the independent SID oracle.

- An archive under `target/agent-run/` — rejected. `harness-<os>` uploads that tree, and `outcomes.json` carries absolute argv
  paths (the `mutants.out/` upload precedent).
- A `cfg!(windows)`-valued fn for the scratch condition — rejected. It is an unkillable mutant on one leg; use a const.
- A scratch wipe that falls back to `%TEMP%` or the repo on refusal or failure — rejected: overseer condition.
- `mod.rs` renames for the splits — rejected. The kept-parent shape keeps unmoved lines out of `--in-diff`.
- Raising `CHILD_WITHIN`, retries or `#[ignore]` for either watch — banned (test-plan §10 zero-flakiness).
- A new product env seam for the forced window — not needed. The hold is a `CHILD_MODE` value inside viola-pty's own test binary.
- `apt-get update` in `wsl-provision.sh` (evolve P10's second half) — out of this chunk (scope Boundaries).

- **Sizing (overseer direction, CARRY 3).** The mutants in the four files are 325 (cargo-mutants 27.1.0 `--list --json
  --file <f>`, research.md fact 2).
  - This split design moves about 107 of them: pre_push Linux side + helpers ≈ 46, run/mutants base 32, pty pump 17, server `win`
    12 (the same listing's per-function counts).
  - The new code adds about 50: test_support ≈ 10, scratch + guard ≈ 15, archive ≈ 12, scoped mode ≈ 6, pre-push fields ≈ 6.
  - Edits inside kept functions add about 10.
  - **Predicted diff: ≈ 165 mutants per leg.** At the green `3efed41` pre-push's rates (ubuntu 190 in 6 m, windows 190 in 17 m,
    research.md fact 4), about 8.4 s per mutant across both legs: **predicted ≈ 23 min of legs + ≈ 2 min of other stages ≈ 25 min
    per pre-push.**
  - Upper bound, if every production line of the four files moved: ≈ 385 mutants, ≈ 56 min. Both are under the ~60 min line, so
    no split is deferred.
  - These are predictions: step 15 records what the run measures (`legs.*.tested`, the `mutants tested in` lines, the wall-clock).
    Fix-loop re-runs multiply the pre-push cost; the scoped mode (step 9) is the cheaper inner loop.
