widening, owner `:82` or the founder's ruling); no `--vt100-panic-bytes` fake-agent mode and no run-level forced-panic
E2E (owner `:74`'s send chaos case, which also owns the G2 question); no verdict consumer (`send` is `:74`'s).

1. **viola-core: `Clock` and `SPINE_DEADLINE`** (`crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs`). Add a `Clock` trait (`Send + Sync`,
   one method returning `std::time::Instant`) and a `SystemClock` unit struct implementing it with `Instant::now()` —
   std only, no new dependency (architecture §Infrastructure Patterns → Crate dependency direction: viola-core's
   third-party deps are nutype only). Add `pub const SPINE_DEADLINE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(1)` with a doc line:
   the bound every spine hook process meets, read by the perf gate (test-plan §10 Spine deadline). Unit tests pin the
   literal (`SPINE_DEADLINE.as_millis() == 1000`) and that two `SystemClock` readings never go backwards.

2. **The hook's connect deadline stays below it** (`src/cmd/hook.rs:40-43`). Rename the crate-private
   `SPINE_DEADLINE` (750 ms) to `CONNECT_DEADLINE` — same value, same use in `spine_deadline` — so the product constant
   has one name; add a unit test asserting `CONNECT_DEADLINE < viola_core::SPINE_DEADLINE` (the ordering test-plan :1220
   states: "below the gate").

3. **The perf gate reads the named value** (`crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/gate.rs:36`, readers :155 and :159 —
   `grep -rn 'SPINE_DEADLINE_S' crates src tests` → these 3 lines only). Replace the `1.0` literal so the bound is
   `viola_core::SPINE_DEADLINE` (as seconds); the failure message keeps its `max {max} >= {bound}` shape. viola-e2e
   already depends on viola-core (`crates/viola-e2e/Cargo.toml`).

4. **vt100 0.16.2 into `viola-agent-claude` only** (`Cargo.toml` `[workspace.dependencies]`:
   `vt100 = "=0.16.2"`, default features; `crates/viola-agent-claude/Cargo.toml`; `Cargo.lock`). No other manifest names
   it (`fuzz/` reaches it through its path dep on viola-agent-claude). 0.16.x, never 0.15.x: 0.15 wrote unhandled
   escapes to STDERR, which is `run`'s terminal (vt100 CHANGELOG 0.16.0, research.md M1).

5. **The screen model** (new `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/screen.rs`, exported from `lib.rs`). Pure, no I/O, no
   clock read — every instant is a parameter:
   - `Screen`: owns an optional `vt100::Parser` (scrollback 0), the current size and the instant of the last fed byte.
     `new(rows, cols, now)`; `feed(bytes, now)` processes bytes and records `now` (a no-op while poisoned);
     `resize(rows, cols, now)` builds a FRESH parser at the new size (clearing poison) and records `now`; `poison()`
     drops the parser; `is_poisoned()`.
   - Constants (one home each, doc line: provisional built-ins, not measured; per-version ledger values land with the
     held rows): `QUIET_PERIOD` = 300 ms, `GATE_MAX_WAIT` = 5 s, `CONFIRM_WINDOW_FALLBACK` = 10 s (architecture
     [Delivery Confirmation]: "a built-in fallback window compiled into `viola-agent-claude`").
   - `Signatures`: two `&'static [&'static str]` lists — `input_box` (a screen row must contain at least one) and
     `modals` (no screen row may contain any). Compiled data only, never built from screen or upstream text
     (security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Code Patterns). No per-version table is added (rows held).
   - `Readiness` closed enum `Ready | InputNotReady` with kebab `as_str` (`ready`, `input-not-ready` — the obs
     `run.readiness_gate.outcome` values and the design word, design-system §Color Palette → Semantic Colors), and a
     `GateStep` `Wait | Done(Readiness)`.
   - `verdict(&self, sigs, waiting_since, now) -> GateStep`, in this order: poisoned → `Done(InputNotReady)`; not quiet
     (`now - last_fed < QUIET_PERIOD`) and `now - waiting_since >= GATE_MAX_WAIT` → `Done(InputNotReady)`; not quiet →
     `Wait`; quiet → `Done(Ready)` only when some row contains an `input_box` literal and no row contains a `modals`
     literal, else `Done(InputNotReady)`. Rows are read as plain text (`Screen::rows`) inside this function only; no row
     text is returned, stored or logged (obs-plan §11 "NEVER derive telemetry from screen content").

6. **The tee and the feed thread** (new `src/run/gate.rs`, `mod gate` in `src/run/mod.rs`):
   - A `Tee` implementing `Write` over the real output and a `Sender` of feed messages: `write` writes to the output
     first and only then sends a copy of exactly the bytes written; a send failure is ignored; `flush` flushes the
     output. The human's bytes are never delayed by the model and never altered (architecture §Design Philosophy "The
     human always wins the wheel").
   - Feed messages: bytes, or a host size. `start(clock, size)` spawns the feed thread owning a `Screen` and returns the
     sender. Bytes → `feed` under `std::panic::catch_unwind(AssertUnwindSafe(..))`; an `Err` → `poison()` and ONE
     `obs_event!(WARN, ObsEvent::ParseRejected, parser = "vt100-feed", detail = "panicked", count = 1)` (the
     `log_config_rejection` shape, `src/obs.rs:208-216`; no `corr` key). While poisoned, bytes are dropped unread (no
     second panic, no second line, no per-chunk work — obs-plan §11 no hot-path telemetry). A size different from the
     current one → `resize` under the same catch (an `Err` poisons and logs the same way). The thread ends when every
     sender is dropped.
   - Wiring (`src/cmd/run.rs:409-439` `pump_child`, the pump's one production caller — research.md §Graph impact): start
     the gate with `Launched.size` and a `SystemClock`, hand `pump` a `Tee` over `io::stdout()` instead of the bare
     stdout, and a `host_size` closure that reads `viola_pty::host_size()` and also sends each reading to the feed.
     `viola_pty::pump`'s signature and viola-pty are unchanged.
   - No `#[instrument]` on the feed (no per-chunk span); the `run.readiness_gate` span opens where a verdict is taken,
     which is `:74`'s.

7. **The property** (`screen.rs` `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`, `cases: 512`, `FileFailurePersistence::SourceParallel
   ("proptest-regressions")` as `crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs:80-88`): over sizes rows 1–30 × cols 1–120, chunks of
   arbitrary bytes and interleaved resizes, each `feed`/`resize` inside `catch_unwind`: an `Err` is followed by
   `poison()`, after which `verdict` is `Done(InputNotReady)` for any instants and `feed` is a no-op; nothing escapes the
   catch. Build strings outside format macros (testing.md 2026-09-24).

8. **The unit cases** (`screen.rs` tests, `<subject>_<condition>_<expected>`, rstest `#[case::label]` tables, literal
   oracles):
   - the measured bytes: a `Screen` at 24×1 fed `e4 b8 ad` panics inside `feed` (asserted through `catch_unwind`); the
     same bytes at 24×80 do not (research.md M2 — the oracle pins vt100 0.16.2's behaviour; a vt100 bump that fixes it
     reads red here, deliberately);
   - each boundary exactly (instants built from one base `Instant` plus literal durations): quiet at exactly 300 ms →
     `Ready` (with matching signatures), at 299 ms → `Wait`; waited exactly 5 s while not quiet → `InputNotReady`,
     4.999 s → `Wait`; input box absent → `InputNotReady`; a modal literal present → `InputNotReady`; poisoned →
     `InputNotReady`; `resize` after `poison` clears it; the three constants' literal values pinned (300 ms, 5 s, 10 s).

9. **The feed-thread witness** (`src/run/gate.rs` `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`): with a hand-written fake `Clock` and an
   in-memory output:
   - the tee's output equals the input byte for byte, including the panicking bytes;
   - the real 24×1 + `e4 b8 ad` input yields exactly one `parse-rejected` line (`parser` `vt100-feed`, `detail`
     `panicked`, `count` 1, level WARN, no `corr`), captured through a process-global subscriber (testing.md
     2026-09-27: a line emitted off the test thread); a further 8 KiB of bytes adds no line; a size message followed by
     the same bytes adds exactly one more (recovery proven by a second panic).
   One process-global per test (testing.md 2026-09-24).

10. **The fuzz target** (new `fuzz/fuzz_targets/vt100_feed.rs`, a `[[bin]]` in `fuzz/Cargo.toml` like `hook_stdin`;
    `fuzz/Cargo.lock` updated by the fuzz toolchain build). The first two input bytes pick the size (rows `1 + b0 % 64`,
    cols `1 + b1 % 200`); the rest is fed in a few chunks through `catch_unwind`, poisoning on `Err` and asserting
    `verdict` is then `Done(InputNotReady)`. Its findings are hangs, OOMs and an escape of the catch — not vt100's caught
    panic, which is the documented degrade. libfuzzer-sys is held to abort on any panic through its own panic hook
    (premise, not measured here: its source is not on this host); the target therefore installs a silent panic hook once
    before its first feed, and implement records the remove-the-guard pair: the 24×1 wide-char seed replays green with
    the override and crashes without it (evidence/fuzz-override.md). Seed `fuzz/corpus/vt100_feed/` with ≥ 6 synthetic
    files: the three measured panic cases (24×1 + U+4E2D, 1×1 + `?u`, 1×2 + `abc`), a 24×80 SGR/CUP line, an OSC title
    with BEL, and a wide-char line at 24×80. Synthetic bytes only (security-plan §Dependency Security `fuzz/` paragraph;
    the nightly `fuzz/artifacts/` upload is unscanned).

11. **CARRY 4 — the fixture repos' detached maintenance** (`crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run.rs` `init_repo` :516-531,
    `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run/mutants/base.rs` `Pass::commit` :248-268). Add `-c maintenance.auto=false` beside
    the existing `-c user.name=t -c user.email=…` args in both git arg lists, so no `git commit` in a throwaway repo
    spawns `git maintenance run --auto --detach`. No `GIT_*` env assignment (pre-push's `env -i` rule) and no harness
    wipe of the NOCOW `TMPDIR` (security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Code Patterns).

12. **CARRY 4's two-sided witness** (operator pass, evidence only — no `[[gate]]` entry: testing.md 2026-10-04, a
    scoring run is a one-off witness). Two full `TMPDIR=<fresh short dir under viola-mutants-scratch> bash
    scripts/agent-run.sh run --mutants --package viola-e2e` runs (≈ 78 min each, test-plan history), each in its own
    fresh short NOCOW dir (path ≤ ~60 B, verification-harness.md 2026-10-04): the CONTROL on the tree with step 11
    reverted, the FIX on this chunk's tree. Count, in each dir after its run, the `.tmp*` dirs holding `a.rs` +
    `.git` without `.git/HEAD` (the leak.md:76-81 signature). Record both counts, both run documents' verdicts and the
    dirs in `evidence/carry4.md`. Economy (overseer at P5, 2026-10-04): if a smaller witness — e.g. the fixture
    git-repo tests (`init_repo` / `Pass`) looped N times in a fresh short NOCOW `TMPDIR` — shows ≥ 1 half-removed repo
    on the CONTROL side, use it instead of the two 78-min mutation runs, run the same witness on the FIX side, and
    record in `evidence/carry4.md` why it stands in; the two-sided shape (control ≥ 1, fix 0, same witness both sides)
    holds either way. Pass: fix 0, control ≥ 1. A control reading 0 does NOT pass: the hypothesis stays
    unproven, the fix stays in (it removes a detached process either way), and the item returns to the route as an open
    `[inferred]` owned by the Epoch 3 boundary audit.
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/screen.rs` — the pure screen model, signatures, verdict, gate constants
- `src/run/gate.rs` — the tee, the feed thread, the catch and the degrade line
- `fuzz/fuzz_targets/vt100_feed.rs` — the vt100 feed fuzz target
- `fuzz/corpus/vt100_feed/` — its synthetic seed corpus (≥ 6 files)
- `Cargo.toml` — `vt100 = "=0.16.2"` in `[workspace.dependencies]`
- `Cargo.lock` — vt100, vte, unicode-width 0.2, arrayvec
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/Cargo.toml` — the vt100 dependency
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/lib.rs` — `mod screen` and its exports
- `crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs` — `Clock`, `SystemClock`, `SPINE_DEADLINE`
- `src/cmd/run.rs` — `pump_child` hands `pump` the tee and the reporting `host_size`
- `src/run/mod.rs` — `mod gate`
- `src/cmd/hook.rs` — `SPINE_DEADLINE` → `CONNECT_DEADLINE`, the ordering test
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/gate.rs` — the bound from `viola_core::SPINE_DEADLINE`
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run.rs` — `-c maintenance.auto=false` in `init_repo`
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run/mutants/base.rs` — `-c maintenance.auto=false` in `Pass::commit`
- `fuzz/Cargo.toml` — the `vt100_feed` `[[bin]]`
- `fuzz/Cargo.lock` — vt100's graph in the fuzz workspace

No live leg runs in this chunk (the live recording is held), so there is no liveness probe. `src/cmd/run.rs` is on the
boot path (no declared boot-smoke list in test-plan; by shape), so the block boots one harness session through the tee
(`p-rg-smoke`: pre-clean, boot, status, cleanup — the form of the 2026-09-28 ledger chunk's smoke). The fuzz override's
remove-the-guard pair (step 10) MUTATES source and reverts, so it is a ONE-SHOT run at implement with both readings in
`evidence/fuzz-override.md`; the listed `run --fuzz-replay` entry guards the property on re-run. The run-level
passthrough witness is the existing `tests/tui_passthrough.rs` set
(`tui_child_output_passes_through_without_viola_bytes` :261, `tui_hooks_firing_add_no_viola_bytes` :209, the two resize
cases :176/:184), which runs with the feed active once step 6 lands, on all three CI OSes — Windows is witnessed only by
the `windows-2025` CI runner (the host is Linux). CARRY 4's mutation runs are evidence, not entries (step 12). The base
sha for every preservation read is `5bcb0a0cc584` (HEAD at P4).

body:
- (arch) `vt100` is named only in `Cargo.toml` `[workspace.dependencies]` and `crates/viola-agent-claude/Cargo.toml`;
  `viola-agent-claude` gains no I/O; `cargo deny check`, the per-sync-crate tokio ban, `scripts/deny-probes.sh` and the
  fuzz lockfile audit pass with no new allow, skip, ignore or exception (per architecture §Infrastructure Patterns →
  Crate dependency direction; security-plan §Dependency Security).

- (arch/security) The quiet period (300 ms), maximum wait (5 s) and confirmation-window fallback (10 s) each have exactly
  one named home in `viola-agent-claude`, with no `config.json` key; the signature lists are compiled data with no path
  from screen or upstream text (per architecture §Established Decisions [Screen Model], [Delivery Confirmation];
  security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Code Patterns).

- (arch/tests) `viola_core::SPINE_DEADLINE` is the one spine bound: the perf gate reads it (no `1.0` literal left in
  `gate.rs`) and the hook's `CONNECT_DEADLINE` is asserted below it (per architecture §Established Decisions [Hook
  Transport]; test-plan §10 Spine deadline).

- (tests) The verdict is asserted only as `ready` / `input-not-ready` / wait over fed bytes; each named deadline expires
  exactly at its boundary and not 1 ms before, from injected instants; the vt100 feed property runs 512 cases (per
  test-plan §4 viola-agent-claude; §6 Property suite; §8 Time).

- (security/obs) A vt100 panic in the feed is caught at the feed's own `catch_unwind`: the gate poisons
  (`input-not-ready` until the next resize), exactly one `parse-rejected{parser:"vt100-feed", detail:"panicked",
  count:1}` WARN line is written with no `corr`, no further line for further bytes, and the process does not exit (per
  security-plan §Input Validation, PTY output row; obs-plan §7 Error classes captured, §6 detail catalog).

- (design/layouts/a11y) The tee's output is byte-identical to the child's output, the panicking bytes included, and the
  `tui_passthrough` cases stay green with the feed active on all three CI OSes (Windows on the `windows-2025` runner):
  viola writes no byte of its own to the human terminal (per design-system §Surface: cli → Colour decision order rule 2;
  layout-templates §Output structure — `viola run`; a11y-plan §1 `viola run` TUI passthrough).

- (tests) `run --fuzz-replay` replays four targets, `vt100_feed` among them, each corpus non-empty and synthetic; the
  fuzz override's remove-the-guard pair is recorded (per test-plan §6 cargo-fuzz paragraph).

- (tests) CARRY 4: the fix run leaves 0 half-removed `Pass`/`init_repo` repos and the control run ≥ 1, both in fresh
  short NOCOW `TMPDIR`s, recorded in `evidence/carry4.md` (per test-plan §10 Mutation gate — evidence, not a gate).

- (obs) No line, span field or detail record carries screen bytes, row text or signature text; the feed has no per-chunk
  span or event (per obs-plan §11 Telemetry Strategy).

- (tests) The operator pass's CI read on the final HEAD reads `verdict: green` (the `ci.py conclusion` entry); its run id
  is named in the report.

title: Held widening — FOR DISCUSSION (founder, morning of 2026-10-05)

data.head: ## Held widening — FOR DISCUSSION (founder, morning of 2026-10-05)

body:
Not built in this chunk. Shown here with its exact shape, as the overseer directed ("show the PTY probe + live 2.1.287
recording at P4 as a HELD widening with its exact shape; the founder rules it in the morning"). Playbook pattern:
**Boundary widening** — a subprocess boundary gains a new crossing; it is ratified only by a live founder answer.

- **What it is:** a second `viola verify` probe drive — the typed-input probe CARRY 1 names — which spawns the resolved
  `claude` executable under a `viola-pty` PTY (verify's first PTY child; today verify spawns only through
  `run_bounded`, `src/cmd/verify.rs:78`), interactive (no `-p`), `--model haiku --no-session-persistence --plugin-dir
  <ledger/probes/<pid>>/plugin`, cwd the probe dir, at a fixed 80×24 with no resize (the H2 discipline), on the inbox
  ConPTY on Windows (not the sideloaded companions, so it borrows no `run`-only interim gap), under the existing 120 s
  probe deadline and a `MAX_FRAME`-capped output reader.

- **What it does:** waits for the SessionStart capture, then for the screen to go quiet (`QUIET_PERIOD`), records the
  screen's row text; types `PROBE_PROMPT` as one bracketed paste + Enter; waits for the UserPromptSubmit and Stop
  captures and quiet again; records again; ends the child (Ctrl-C twice, then the deadline kill). The rows it would add:
  `input-box-signature` (a recorded row literal present after quiet), `modal-absent` (no known modal literal), and
  `measured` keys for the observed quiet period — so `LedgerRow::ALL` grows and every stamped home re-stamps.

- **Crossings it adds (each the founder's to rule):** (1) a PTY child of `verify` — does the R8 strip apply to it as it
  does to `run`'s child?; (2) the hidden `hook --capture` arm, today called only by the print-mode probe's plugin,
  called from an interactive session; (3) a new obs `subject` (or `verify-probe` redefined — D-35 template, a
  `diag-line.v1.json` change); (4) `--record` writing screen row text as fixtures (scrubbed for paths and the
  username, refused whole if either survives) — the first fixture class that is screen content.

- **The live leg it needs:** `run --local-live` on the operator's Linux host against the installed `claude` 2.1.287 (a
  subscription use, on the operator's word; refused under `CI`), recording a 2.1.287 set beside the 2.1.283 hook
  fixtures; the fake agent would then replay the recorded screen so CI stamps the new rows.

- **Owner:** `:82` First live test and self-drive, or the founder's ruling moves it elsewhere. Until it lands every CLI
  build reads "screen unverified", and per architecture [Screen Model] the gate falls back to delivery confirmation
  only.

- Spec anchors: architecture §Established Decisions [Screen Model], [Delivery Confirmation], [Hook Transport], [CLI
  Version Compatibility], [Agent Coverage]; §Infrastructure Patterns → Crate dependency direction, Build system;
  §Design Philosophy "The human always wins the wheel" · security-plan §Input Validation (PTY output row, Parser
  surfaces), §Security Anti-Patterns → Code Patterns / Universal, §Dependency Security · test-plan §4
  viola-agent-claude, §6 Property suite / cargo-fuzz, §8 Time, §10 Spine deadline / Zero-flakiness / Mutation gate ·
  obs-plan §4 Scenario Confirmed `send`, §6 detail catalog, §7 Error classes captured / Panic hooks, §11 · design-system
  §Surface: cli, §Color Palette → Semantic Colors · layout-templates §Output structure — `viola run` / `viola verify` ·
  a11y-plan §1, §11.

- History the plan rests on: architecture-amendments `2026-09-27-hooks-to-normalised-events` (SPINE_DEADLINE handed to
  this chunk), `2026-09-28-capability-ledger-and-viola-verify` (the six rows; verify's one writer), `2026-09-29-h2-
  conpty-resize-probe` (why typed probes wait); obs-plan-amendments `2026-09-28-hook-perf-gate` (G2's one exemption);
  test-plan-amendments `2026-09-24-fake-agent-and-test-data-fixtures` (`--vt100-panic-bytes` consumer-first),

- Research: `research.md` (M1 vt100 graph, M2 measured panics, M3 the panic hook, M4 signature rows vs stamped homes,

title: 1. Screen model and readiness gate (the working entry's head)

data.head: ### 1. Screen model and readiness gate (the working entry's head)

body:
- vt100 0.16.2 (architecture Stack row "Screen model") is added and fed every PTY output byte on `run`'s pump thread;
  byte passthrough to the human terminal is never delayed or altered by the feed. VERIFIED (research.md M1): vt100 and
  vte are absent from `Cargo.lock`; the graph is vt100 (MIT) · vte 0.15 (Apache-2.0 OR MIT) · itoa · unicode-width 0.2 ·
  arrayvec · memchr (MIT OR Apache-2.0), no build script, no env read, every MSRV under 1.96; the `cargo deny` verdict
  itself is implement's to read. 0.16.x is required: 0.15.x logged unhandled escapes to STDERR, `run`'s terminal. The
  pump's one production caller hands it `io::stdout()` (`src/cmd/run.rs:419`), so a tee there feeds the model without a
  viola-pty change.

- The gate's verdict is a closed outcome `ready | input-not-ready` (obs-plan `run.readiness_gate` span: `outcome`,
  `vt100_panicked`). Screen content is read ONLY as that verdict — never logged, never an event field, never asserted in
  a test (test-plan R7, obs-plan §11 "never derive telemetry from screen content").

- Quiet period: the screen must show no change for the quiet period before the signature checks; the gate gives up at
  its maximum wait. Both are open items architecture holds "as ledger rows beside the signatures".

- On an unverified CLI build the gate falls back to delivery confirmation only (architecture [Screen Model], last
  sentence). VERIFIED as an open design point: that sentence is the only source (no code reads a verdict yet), so what
  "falls back" means for the verdict is P4's to pin.

- The gate's first in-repo consumer. VERIFIED: no `send` verb, channel `send` method or MCP `send` exists at
  take-up (`src/cmd/` holds `hook`, `run`, `verify` only; the channel `Methods::dispatch` serves only `hook.event`,
  `src/cmd/run.rs:100-110`); no `RefusalReason` or refusal-detail type exists anywhere yet; the next entry (`:74 Confirmed send`) owns `send`. The
  consumer this chunk can wire is CARRY 1's typed-input probe in `viola verify` and the run pump itself; whether the
  channel exposes the gate here or at :74 is a P4 question under the consumer-first rule (testing.md: no code without a

- **Chunk base:** `eb37914c0c59` (HEAD at P4; every `git diff` guard below names it)

The wrapper learns that a turn is running. Any `prompt-submitted` marks it, whether the driver's own confirmed
prompt, a human's or a harness turn's. `turn-ended`, `session-start` or `session-end` ends it. A `viola release` that
returns the wheel clears it, because a user interrupt ends a turn with no `turn-ended`. While a turn runs, an automated
`send` is refused `not-delivered` / `turn-running` at the existing rung. It is never queued, and nothing is typed for it
(per architecture §Established Decisions [Human Takeover / Wheel]; §Conventions Error handling schema, the `send` order).

As built, `turn-running` covers only a second `send` in flight (`src/run/send.rs:239-243`). The folded CARRY's
hypothesis is measured true at HEAD: `path5_harness_turns_never_take_the_wheel` (`tests/tui_wheel.rs:240-258`) shows a
driver `send` accepted, so pasted, into an unended harness turn (research.md §Mechanism claims). This chunk closes that
gap. It adds no event kind, refusal detail, snapshot field, channel method, param or test seam: the state lives in memory
only, and the refusal reuses the one existing emitter (per architecture §Standard Contracts; obs-plan §6, §8 Default-deny;
security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Universal).

It also folds the wheel wrap's renumber CARRY: `tests/tui_wheel.rs:267` and `tests/cli_answer.rs:9` cite First live
test as `:84`. The `.profraw` WATCH rides as an observation only (scope.md).

title: Rulings and leans this plan rests on

data.head: ## Rulings and leans this plan rests on

body:
- **Leaned: only a wheel-returning `release` clears the turn.** Per `architecture.md:70`: "the `viola release` that
  returns the wheel is to clear the running-turn state", and "a `release` on a wheel the driver already holds changes
  nothing and appends nothing". `release {budget:true}` (leaves the wheel), a `release` on a driver-held wheel and a
  rejected `release-from-driver` therefore clear nothing. A turn stuck under a driver-held wheel is recovered without a
  keystroke by `viola pause` then `viola release` (step 7 witnesses it). The alternative, any non-budget `release`
  clears, contradicts that sentence and would need an architecture reversal.

- **Leaned: the rung decides at the send's arrival.** Per `architecture.md:70`: "A `send` while a turn is running (after
  `prompt-submitted`, before `turn-ended`) is not queued. It is refused". The turn is read once, at the existing
  `turn-running` rung. A turn that starts during the readiness gate's wait (≤ `GATE_MAX_WAIT`) is not refused by this
  chunk. That window is recorded as a residual (Expected amendments), not closed. A second check after the gate has no
  observable effect a test could force without a new seam, so it would be an unkillable mutant
  (`.claude/rules/testing.md:52`).

- **Leaned: the state is marked and cleared before the hook line is appended.** Per the precedent at
  `src/run/send.rs:152-156` (an unsent human prompt moves the wheel "before the line can be read"). A driver that read
  `turn-ended` through `wait` is never refused by that turn, and one that read a `prompt-submitted` is.

- **Leaned: the state sits in `WheelSlot`'s `Held`, beside holder and cause.** `release` lives on `WheelSlot`, and `send`
  already holds an `Arc<WheelSlot>` (`src/run/send.rs:52`). A wheel-returning move and its clear are therefore one lock
  hold, with no instant at which the wheel is the driver's while a stale turn still refuses. No signature changes.

- **Not a widening:** no playbook `verdict: escalate` pattern applies (`.andromeda/playbook.md:37`, `:49`, the
  "Boundary widening" class). The chunk narrows what automation may do and adds no crossing, input class or method.

1. **The running-turn state** (`src/run/wheel.rs`). Add a closed two-state type, idle or running, never a bool parsed
   from text and never a `String` (security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Input, the closed-types rule). It goes in
   `Held` (`:73-76` region), starting idle. `WheelSlot` gains three crate-private methods: one marks the turn running,
   one marks it idle, and one reads whether it is running. None of them records anything: no event, no snapshot, no
   span, no obs line (obs-plan §11 Logs, "never log at `info` inside hot loops"; §6, no new field).

2. **`release` clears it** (`src/run/wheel.rs`, `apply` `:123-143`). When the `Input::Release` move is made (the
   `next()` arm at `:44`, a human-held wheel), the same `held` hold sets the turn idle. Every path where `next()` returns
   `None` for `Release` (`:45`), the `budget:true` path (`release` `:177-179`) and the `release-from-driver` / invalid
   params returns (`:170-176`, before `apply`) leave the turn as it was. `pause` and `Input::Human` never touch it.

3. **Turn start and end at the one hook entry** (`src/run/send.rs`, `append_hook_event` `:139-161`). Before
   `feed.appending`, beside the existing human-wheel move:
   - a `prompt-submitted` of any origin marks the turn running, the claimed driver prompt included;
   - a `turn-ended`, `session-start` or `session-end` marks it idle;
   - `activity` changes nothing.

   It keys on `line.kind` only, never on prompt text (security-plan §Input Validation, `hook.event` re-validation). The
   existing claim, relabel and settle order is unchanged.

4. **The rung** (`src/run/send.rs`, `send` `:236-243`). Under the flight lock hold, the rung returns
   `ctx.not_delivered(None, NotDelivered::TurnRunning)` when another send is in flight or a turn is running. The flight
   is not reserved, nothing is pasted, and `send-issued` is not written. Lock order is flight, then held. Nothing in
   `WheelSlot` takes the flight lock (`WheelSlot` holds no `SendSlot`), so no inversion exists. The rung keeps its place:
   after `control-character` and `human-typing`, before the readiness gate and confirmation.

6. **The hypothesis witness** (`tests/tui_wheel.rs`, `path5_harness_turns_never_take_the_wheel` `:240-258`; keep its
   name, since matrix `v1-32`'s `ref` cites it). Boot with `--inject-harness-turn` and the committed
   `fixtures/fake-scripts/path3.json` (gated `PostToolUse`, then gated `Stop`). The local `boot` (`:27`) gains the
   script argument the shared `Wrapper::boot` already takes. The steps:
   1. Release the control once and wait for the harness `prompt-submitted`.
   2. `viola send builder --json` exits 13 with stdout `{"v":1,"refusal":"not-delivered","detail":"turn-running"}`.
      The receipt still holds exactly one `prompt` (the harness one), and the records after the pre-send offset are one
      `send-refused` without `cursor` and no `send-issued`.
   3. Release twice more, wait for `turn-ended`, and `send` again: it exits 0.
   4. The existing `origin:"harness"` and no-`wheel`-record assertions stay.

   Fix the `:267` comment to cite `:84`.

7. **The release witnesses** (`tests/cli_wheel.rs`). Add a new test. Boot with `--inject-harness-turn` and no Stop,
   release the control once, and wait for the harness `prompt-submitted`. Then:
   - `send --json` exits 13 `turn-running`;
   - a bare `viola release builder --json` (a driver-held wheel) exits 0 with `{wheel:"driver",budget_paused:false}`,
     and the next `send` still exits 13 `turn-running`;
   - `viola pause builder` then `viola release builder` make the next `send` exit 0.

   `path5_human_takes_the_wheel_and_release_returns_it` (`tests/tui_wheel.rs:158-237`) is unchanged. Its post-release
   `send` exit 0 (`:199`) after the unended human prompt `hello` is now the wheel-move witness: it reads 13 if the clear
   is missing.

8. **The driver's own turn** (`tests/cli_send.rs`).
   - `path2_send_confirms_with_cl1_events` (`:151`) ends the first send's turn before its second `send` (`:216`):
     boot over `fixtures/fake-scripts/path3.json`, release its two gated steps, and wait for `turn-ended`. Every
     existing assertion stays.
   - A new test `send_after_a_confirmed_send_is_turn_running_until_turn_ended`, over `path3.json`: a confirmed `send`
     exits 0, and a second `send` exits 13. Human mode prints exactly `[/ ] unable         builder  not-delivered
     turn-running` then `hint: a turn is running; viola wait builder first` (the literal pinned by
     `send_window_second_concurrent_send_is_refused_turn_running`, `:264-305`). Release both steps and wait for
     `turn-ended`; the same `send` then exits 0.

9. **The controls row** (`tests/cli_controls_not_disableable.rs`). Beside `setting_does_not_disable_the_send_human_wheel_control`
   (`:263`), add a turn-running row: the wrapper booted with `--fixtures` and `--inject-harness-turn`, its control
   released once, and its harness `prompt-submitted` awaited. `viola send --json` then exits 13 with stdout exactly
   `{"v":1,"refusal":"not-delivered","detail":"turn-running"}` under every setting in the same list. This follows the
   wheel row's form.

- (arch) **The turn's life**, in `src/run/send.rs` / `src/run/wheel.rs` literal-oracle unit tables run by the first unit
  entry:
  - a `prompt-submitted` of origin `harness` or the claimed driver prompt makes the next `send` refuse
    `turn-running` with zero pastes; one of origin `human` marks the turn too, but it also moves the wheel to the
    human first, so the next `send` reads `human-typing` (with zero pastes) — the earlier rung — and only the
    `release` that returns the wheel, which clears the turn, makes it pass [amended at the wrap, 2026-10-04, on the
    operator's directive (2), as measured: `send_a_prompt_of_any_origin_starts_a_turn::case_2_human`];
  - `turn-ended`, `session-start` and `session-end` each make it pass the rung, and `activity` does not;
  - a wheel-returning `release` clears the turn;
  - `release` on a driver-held wheel, `release {budget:true}`, a `release` carrying a string `from` and `pause` each
    leave it running.
  - (per architecture §Established Decisions [Human Takeover / Wheel]; test-plan §4 root bin)

- (arch) `send` still refuses in the order `control-character` → `human-typing` → `turn-running` → `input-not-ready` →
  `no-prompt-submitted` with a turn running. `answer` is never refused `turn-running` (`tests/cli_answer.rs` green
  unchanged) (per architecture §Conventions Error handling schema; test-plan §4 root bin "Refusal ordering").

- (security) During a running turn, a `release` carrying a string `from` returns `-32602` with
  `data: {"reason":"release-from-driver"}`, and the turn is not cleared: the step 5 unit case. Human keys still reach the
  child: `path5_human_takes_the_wheel_and_release_returns_it` is green unchanged (per security-plan §Authentication &
  Authorization, "Driver-originated `release`"; §Security Anti-Patterns → Universal).

- (security) No event kind, refusal detail, snapshot field, method, param, test seam, env read, `#[ignore]` or deny
  exception is added (the three `git diff eb37914c0c59` probe entries).

- (tests) **Release and recovery**, in `tests/cli_wheel.rs` on all three CI OSes: a turn left running under a
  driver-held wheel refuses `send` 13 `turn-running`. A bare `viola release` changes nothing, and the next `send` is
  still 13. `viola pause` then `viola release` make the next `send` exit 0. In `tests/tui_wheel.rs`, the `send` after a
  human prompt and `viola release` exits 0 (per architecture [Human Takeover / Wheel]; test-plan §6 Path 5 steps 4–5).

- (tests) **The driver's own turn**, in `tests/cli_send.rs`: after a confirmed `send`, a second `send` exits 13 with
  exactly `[/ ] unable         builder  not-delivered  turn-running` then `hint: a turn is running; viola wait builder
  first` on stderr, until `turn-ended`, after which it exits 0. `path2_send_confirms_with_cl1_events` passes with its
  first turn ended (per test-plan §6 Path 2; §11 E2E).

- (tests) `tests/cli_controls_not_disableable.rs`'s turn-running row holds under every setting (per test-plan §5 CLI;
  CLAUDE.md "No `config.json` key, `VIOLA_*` env var or CLI flag may disable a control").

- (tests) The renumber CARRY: both probe entries hold (`last line 0` for `` `:82` `` under `tests` / `src`, `last line 2`
  for `` `:84` `` in the two files).

- (obs) The refusal's wrapper `send-refused` line carries `detail:"turn-running"`, `side:"wrapper"`, `wheel:"driver"`,
  `corr`, `conn` and `rpc_id`, with no `send-issued` for that `rpc_id`. The existing emitter is reused, and CI's per-OS
  "G4 schema conformance" step passes, read by the operator pass's CI entry (per obs-plan §4 Scenario: Confirmed `send`;
  §3 Log format JSON schema; §9 G4).

- (obs) No harness or human prompt text reaches a home-level process-log line. CI's per-OS "Secret scan" step stays
  green (per obs-plan §8).

- (a11y) The refusal is text (`unable`, `not-delivered`, `turn-running`) ending in one `hint:` line, with no SGR under a
  non-TTY (per a11y-plan §8 Error recovery).

- (tests) `scripts/agent-run.sh pre-push` reads `"ok":true` at `linux-tests`, and the operator pass's CI read is
  `verdict: green` on the final HEAD (per test-plan §9; §10).

- Research files inspected: research.md §Files inspected (19 reads); trace
  `.andromeda/runs/2026-10-04T21-38-24-phase/tree-query-2026-10-04-running-turn-refusal.json` (1 query, fresh, 96 rows).

- Queueing a refused `send`, or retrying it inside the wrapper — rejected (architecture [Human Takeover / Wheel]: "not
  queued").

- Deriving "turn running" from the vt100 screen or the readiness gate — rejected. Turn state keys on hook lines only
  (obs-plan §10 Deterministic emission; a11y-plan §11 R7).

- A new event kind (turn-started / turn-cleared), a snapshot field or a second `turn-running` detail to tell the causes
  apart — rejected. No consumer exists, and each is a contract amendment (architecture §Standard Contracts; obs-plan §6).
- Clearing the turn on every `release` — rejected per the lean above (`architecture.md:70`).

- A second turn check after the readiness gate — rejected per the lean above (an unobservable guard,
  `.claude/rules/testing.md:52`).

- A new fake-agent mode or test seam to end a turn — not added. The committed `path3.json` gated `Stop` ends it, and a
  new seam is a widening needing a Decisions Log ruling (security.md).
- `release` emptying the in-flight send slot — rejected (architecture: the slot belongs to a live send).
- Gating `answer` or `hook.dialog` on the turn — rejected (architecture §Conventions `answer` order).
- A new fixture script — not added. `path3.json` already holds a gated turn end (research.md, the fixtures read).

- **Order sensitivity.**
  - The mark and clear in `append_hook_event` happen before `feed.appending`. A `wait` that returns `turn-ended` (it
    re-scans only after the append, `src/run/wait.rs:71-84`) is therefore never followed by a `turn-running` refusal
    from that turn.
  - The claimed driver prompt marks the turn too. Its own `send` is already past the rung, so it confirms as before.

- **The boot `session-start`** (start records line 3) finds the turn idle and changes nothing. The wrapper starts idle,
  so a restarted wrapper never inherits a turn.

- **SessionEnd fallback** (`src/cmd/hook.rs:174-175`): a SessionEnd the channel missed is appended directly, and the
  wrapper's turn stays running. Its child is ending, so no driver send depends on it. Recorded as a residual.

- **Fake-agent turns:** an interactive submit fires no Stop (`src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs:288-307`), so every test that
  sends twice ends the first turn with a scripted gated `Stop`. Research's sweep found exactly two existing sites that
  needed it (`tests/cli_send.rs:216`, `tests/tui_wheel.rs:254`; research.md §Companion sweep).

- **`--inject-harness-turn` with `--script`:** the harness step comes first, then the script's steps, each gated in
  control-line order (`src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs:466-485`). With `path3.json` the releases are: 1 the harness prompt,
  2 `PostToolUse`, 3 `Stop`.

- **Expected amendments (wrap):**
  - architecture §Established Decisions [Human Takeover / Wheel] — retire "as built, no running-turn state exists beyond
    the in-flight `send` slot … so `release` returns the wheel alone". Now: the running-turn state lives in `WheelSlot`
    beside holder and cause, in memory only. A `prompt-submitted` of any origin marks it, and `turn-ended` /
    `session-start` / `session-end` clear it, before the line is appended. A wheel-returning `release` clears it in the
    same hold, and a driver-held `release` changes nothing (recovery: `pause` then `release`). The rung decides at
    arrival. Residuals: a turn starting during the readiness gate's wait (up to `GATE_MAX_WAIT`, 5 s provisional) is
    not refused (lean 2, accepted at P5 by the overseer, 2026-10-04, to be recorded at the wrap as this residual), and
    a SessionEnd the hook appends directly leaves the turn marked.
  - test-plan §6 Path 5 — the harness-turn verification gains the `turn-running` refusal and acceptance after
    `turn-ended`. As landed, `tests/cli_wheel.rs` adds the `pause` / `release` recovery. §6 Path 2 — its two sends span
    a scripted turn end. §5 CLI — the controls table's turn-running row.
  - obs-plan §4 Scenario: Confirmed `send` — `turn-running` now also covers a running turn, the same closed detail, with
    no new field.
  - `matrix#v1-32 notes` — `path5_harness_turns_never_take_the_wheel` now also asserts the `turn-running` refusal, and
    `viola release`'s `send` exit 0 rests on the running-turn clear (status, ref and acceptance untouched).

- **Matrix notes owed at P5** (pooled caps this chunk advances but cannot verify):
  - `v1-29` — its `turn-running` detail now covers a running turn, not only a second send in flight. "Only when the input
    box is ready", `unconfirmable` and `/clear` remain owed (`:84`).

- **Test-authoring hazard:** a fake-agent `prompt` receipt is written only after its UserPromptSubmit hook returns. A
  count taken right after the send's reply, or right after the `prompt-submitted` line, races it. Wait for the
  receipt first (`prompts_at_least` / `fake::wait_for`).

- **Sweep hazard (gate authoring):** a zero-is-healthy count probe written as `git grep … | wc -l` with an `exit 0` atom can never pass on its green state under a pipefail shell (`git grep` exits 1 on no match). The gate tool runs `bash -c` with pipefail, so `last line 0` alone, or `{ git grep … || true; } | wc -l`, is the green-reachable form. The P5 baseline read only the red side, so nothing exercised the green.

- **Test-authoring lesson:** a remove-the-guard control can turn a unit test whose guard is a refusal into a hang. A wrongly accepted send under a fixed test clock parks on its confirmation window forever. Give the refused call a clock that can expire, so the control reads FAIL, not TIMEOUT.

- **Diagnosis technique:** a truncated LLVM raw profile whose cut falls in its trailing names section keeps every counter. Match the record name hashes (MD5 lower 64 bits of the mangled names, taken from a complete sibling of the same binary signature) to read which functions the dead process ran, and so name the process with no surviving home or log.

- **Fake-agent fact:** `--script` / `--inject-harness-turn` steps fire on a detached thread, and the agent is its PTY's session leader. Any test that stops the wrapper right after a scripted hook's event line lands could, before this fix, SIGHUP that hook mid-exit. A hook killed before its profile dump left no profile at all, a silent coverage loss.

- **release** (`WheelSlot::release`) — production caller `dispatch_call` @ `src/cmd/run.rs:131`. The same name also covers the CLI verb `cmd::dispatch` @ `src/cmd/mod.rs:109` and the test-support `Wrapper::release` (the fake agent's control-line writer, `tests/support/home.rs:397`) with its many test callers. Those are name collisions, not callers of the wheel method.
- **send** (`send::send`) — production caller `dispatch_call` @ `src/cmd/run.rs:125`; 11 unit callers in `src/run/send.rs`. The CLI-side `send` hits are other functions sharing the name.

- **human_input** — production callers `append_hook_event` @ `src/run/send.rs:155` and `Observed::read` @ `src/run/wheel.rs:282`. This is the precedent: a state move made before the hook line is appended.
- **try_append_event** — `append_session_end` @ `src/cmd/hook.rs:422`, the only product writer that bypasses the wrapper.

- **State moved before the line is readable** (`src/run/send.rs:152-156`): an unsent human prompt moves the wheel before `feed.appending`, so anyone who sees the line on disk already sees the move. The running-turn mark and clear follow the same rule. A driver that read `turn-ended` through `wait` is then never refused by that turn, and one that read a `prompt-submitted` is.

- **One lock per related state; records off the hot path** (`src/run/wheel.rs:73-76`, `:123-143`): holder and cause under one `Mutex`, the record queued under the same hold. The running-turn state carries no record (scope, the obs extract), so it is a plain in-memory flag on a std lock.

- **Gated fake-agent steps as the turn driver** (`src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs:328-342`): a turn's end in a test is a scripted `Stop` released through the control file, never a timer.

data.head: ## Rulings and leans this plan rests on

body: - **F-W1 — the founder's live ruling, 2026-10-04, relayed by the overseer through the operator's P4 answer (the pause-swallow residual shown):** CLI `viola pause` / `viola release` write their frames after the same liveness-only pre-check as `send` / `wait` / `last` / `answer` (`src/cmd/client.rs:95-102`). This is a **seventh dated gap** until Epoch 6 `:109` / `:111`, and it borrows none of the six earlier gaps. Pattern: playbook "Boundary widening — what ratifies it".

- **Leaned per architecture [Human Takeover / Wheel] ("after which automated `send` is refused `human-typing` with detail `manual-pause`"):** `pause` always leaves the wheel `human` / `manual-pause`. A later human key while `manual-pause` holds changes nothing and appends nothing. `pause` on a `human-input` wheel turns the cause to `manual-pause` and appends one `wheel` line.

- **Leaned per architecture [Budget Governor] ("`release --budget` leaves the wheel where it is"):** the channel `release` parses `budget` (absent or a bool, else `-32602`), and `budget:true` leaves the wheel unchanged. The CLI `--budget` flag and lifting a pause are `:91`'s, so no CLI flag lands here.
- **Leaned per research.md §Mechanisms:** `release` clears no running-turn state. None exists beyond the in-flight `send` slot, which belongs to a live send.

- **Leaned per test-plan §11 Test Strategy (a lower-layer case belongs in unit tests):** Path 5's `<agent-message from=` prefix stays proven by `viola-agent-claude`'s unit cases (`hook.rs:445-460`). The e2e harness turn uses the existing `--inject-harness-turn` (`<task-notification>`), so the fake agent is not changed.
- **Leaned per test-plan precedent (Path 2 / Path 3 "as landed … owed to"):** Path 5's MCP `send` step is owed to `:102` and its Playwright WHEEL-cell step to `:139`.

- **Leaned, obs vocabulary:** `run.wheel_transition.cause` uses `human-input` (architecture §Standard Contracts `wheel` causes; test-plan §6 Path 5). Spans are not serialized (`with_current_span(false)`), so obs-plan §4's `human-key` is aligned at wrap.

   - Add the closed `human-typing` detail type with one variant `manual-pause` (kebab serde, `as_str`). The `human-typing` details are then the closed set `null` · `manual-pause` (architecture §Conventions Error handling schema).
   - Add the closed wheel cause `start` · `human-input` · `manual-pause` · `release` (kebab, `as_str`).
   - The holder stays `viola_state::snapshot::Wheel` (`driver` / `human`); add an `as_str` to it if none exists, with no free strings anywhere (security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Input).
   - Pin each with a literal-oracle unit case.

3. **viola-channel — `release-from-driver` on the wire** (`crates/viola-channel/src/lib.rs`, `crates/viola-channel/src/server.rs`).
   - Add a `ProtocolError` variant whose `code()` is `-32602`, `message()` is "invalid params" and `body()` `data` is exactly `{"reason":"release-from-driver"}`.
   - The doc comment on `body` changes from "no other `data` is ever built" to name both data-bearing variants.
   - Add the variant to the server's `-32602` classification (`server.rs:509`), so `channel-response` logs `error_code:-32602` at the level obs-plan §6 Log levels mapping gives `-32602`.
   - Unit: the frame body literal.

4. **The wrapper's one snapshot holder** (new `src/run/snapshot.rs`; `src/run/mod.rs`).
   - Make one in-process owner of the instance snapshot: the current `InstanceSnapshot` under one `Mutex`, and an update function that applies a change and writes it through `viola_state::snapshot::write_snapshot` (which goes through `replace_private`) while still holding the lock.
   - `start_state` (`src/cmd/run.rs:376-412`) builds it.
   - `spawn_child`'s child-pid write (`:435-436`), `DialogSlot::write_pending` (`src/run/dialog.rs:283-288`) and every wheel change go through it, so a wheel write is never lost behind a pending-dialog write (research.md §Conventions).
   - Unit: two threads updating `wheel` and `pending_dialog` concurrently both land on disk.

5. **The wheel and its stdin observer** (new `src/run/wheel.rs`; `src/run/mod.rs`).
   1. **State.** Holder + cause under one `Mutex`, starting `driver` / `start`.
      - Each CHANGE of (holder, cause) appends one `wheel` event `{holder, cause}`, `source: wrapper`, through `viola_state::events::append_event`. It never goes through the wait feed: `wheel` is log-only and never wakes `wait`.
      - Each change also updates the snapshot's `wheel` through step 4's holder, and opens one point-in-time `run.wheel_transition` span (`#[instrument(skip_all, name = "run.wheel_transition", fields(wheel_from, wheel_to, cause))]`, static name, closed codes only; obs-plan §4 Scenario "Human takes the wheel…").
      - A move to `human` also hands the pending dialog back (step 7).
   2. **Transitions.**
      - human editing key → `human` / `human-input` (no change while already `human`, whatever the cause);
      - an unsent `prompt-submitted` with `origin:"human"`, while `driver` → `human` / `human-input` ("an unsent `prompt-submitted` confirms and logs the take"). An `origin:"harness"` prompt, and the in-flight send's own prompt relabelled `driver` (`src/run/send.rs:132-150`), never move it;
      - `pause` → `human` / `manual-pause`;
      - `release` → `driver` / `release`;
      - `release` with `budget:true` → no change.
   3. **The byte classifier** (F-W2). A bounded state machine over the stdin byte stream that carries an unfinished sequence across reads.
      - Ground bytes are editing.
      - `ESC` starts a sequence. A sequence that completes as one of F-W2's non-editing forms is not editing; any other completed sequence is editing.
      - A sequence past its bound (64 bytes of parameters or payload) is editing and resets the machine.
      - A read that ends on a lone `ESC` counts it at once as the Esc key, an editing key, since the human's Esc must take the wheel without waiting for a next read. A sequence already past `ESC [` / `ESC ]` / `ESC P` / `CSI M` carries over.
   4. **The observer.** A `Read` wrapper around the host stdin, mirroring the output `Tee` (`src/run/gate.rs:130-140`).
      - Each `read` returns the inner bytes unchanged and in full. Before returning, if the chunk held an editing key and the holder is `driver`, the wrapper flips the holder in memory (so a `send` that checks after this read is refused).
      - The disk work (event, snapshot, dialog hand-back) runs on a wheel worker thread fed by a channel, so no human byte waits on disk I/O.
      - No per-byte span or line (observability.md "No per-byte or per-line logging in hot loops"), and the keystroke bytes reach no log, span, event or detail line (obs-plan §8).
   5. **Wiring.** `pump_child` (`src/cmd/run.rs:447-491`) passes the observer, wrapping step 9's host stdin, as `pump_with_paste`'s `input` (`:470-472`). No viola-pty pump change.

6. **`send`'s wheel step** (`src/run/send.rs`).
   - `send` (`:200-244`) takes the wheel. After `validate_paste_text` and before the in-flight `turn-running` check, a `human` holder refuses `human-typing` with detail `null`, or `manual-pause` when that is the cause.
   - No cursor, and `corr` = the end offset at refusal (obs-plan D-28, as `Ctx::refuse` already does).
   - The order is `control-character` → `human-typing` → `turn-running` → `input-not-ready` → `no-prompt-submitted` (`budget-paused` is `:91`'s slot).
   - `Ctx::refuse` (`:319-344`) takes a reason and an optional detail string. EVERY wrapper `send-refused` obs line gains `wheel = <holder>` (obs-plan §4 Scenario CL-1, the `Kept` clause of the 2026-10-04-confirmed-send-with-cl-1-records obs amendment). The `send-refused` event data stays `{refusal, detail, cursor?}`.
   - `append_hook_event` reports an unclaimed human-origin `prompt-submitted` to the wheel (step 5's prompt transition).
   - Callers: `run::send::send @ src/cmd/run.rs:121`; `SendSlot::new @ src/cmd/run.rs:204` and the file's tests (research.md §Graph impact).
   - Unit: the literal refusal-order table gains the `human-typing` rows (detail null and `manual-pause`), ahead of an in-flight send.

7. **Dialogs under the wheel** (`src/run/dialog.rs`).
   - `DialogSlot` reads the holder.
   - `hook_dialog` (`:168-199`) holds a dialog only while the holder is `driver`. Under `human` it still registers the dialog (the event appended with its own `dialog_id`, `:208-245`) and replies `{dialog_id, response:null}` at once.
   - A new hand-back, called by the wheel on a move to `human`, makes a held `await_answer` (`:254-279`) end at once with `null`. The pending dialog clears, `pending_dialog` leaves the snapshot (through step 4's holder), `WaitFeed::dialog_settled` fires, and the PreToolUse arm is marked unanswered.
   - `answer` (`:292-338`) gains the `human-typing` slot after the free-text `control-character` check and before `unverified-cli`, with detail `null` or `manual-pause`.
   - The `refusal()` helper (`:128-130`) takes a reason and an optional detail string.
   - Callers: `hook_dialog @ src/cmd/run.rs:124`, `answer @ src/cmd/run.rs:125`, `DialogSlot::new @ src/cmd/run.rs:209` and the file's tests.
   - Unit, on the injected clock:
     - a held dialog handed back at the wheel move replies `null` at once (before `DIALOG_DEADLINE`) and clears `pending_dialog`;
     - a `hook.dialog` under a `human` wheel is logged once and `null` at once;
     - the literal `answer` refusal-order table with the `human-typing` rows (`control-character` first; `human-typing` beats a stamped CLI and beats an unknown id).

8. **The `pause` / `release` methods** (`src/cmd/run.rs`).
   - `Methods` holds the wheel. `dispatch_call` (`:119-128`) routes `pause` and `release`:
     - `pause` params `{from?}` (other fields ignored, `from` through `parse_from`) → `{ok:{wheel:"human"}}`.
     - `release` params `{budget?, from?}`: a string `from` → the step-3 `release-from-driver` error, plus one `release-from-driver` obs line `{corr:<JSON-RPC id>, conn, from, from_trust:"self-reported"}` (obs-plan §6 catalog; the schema already admits it, `schemas/diag-line.v1.json:66-68`, `:105-107`). A non-bool `budget` → `-32602`. Otherwise → `{ok:{wheel:<holder>, budget_paused:false}}`.
   - The wheel, the snapshot holder and the stdin observer are built in `start` (`:168-254`) and handed to `Methods`, `SendSlot` / `send`, `DialogSlot` and `pump_child`.
   - Retarget `methods_answer_method_not_found_for_every_other_method` (`:611-620`) to `["link", "unlink", "anything"]`.
   - Unit: `pause` / `release` replies, `release-from-driver` with its obs line, the bad `budget`, `budget:true` leaving the wheel.

9. **The Windows console stdin** (CARRY §8; `crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs`).
   - A host-stdin constructor for the wrapper. On Windows, when the standard input handle is a console, it returns a reader that calls `ReadConsoleW` itself, without std's `0x1A` strip (`std/src/sys/stdio/windows.rs:353-392` at 1.98.1).
     - It converts UTF-16 to UTF-8, carrying a split surrogate pair to the next read.
     - It keeps every `0x1A`.
     - It treats a successful zero-character read as no data and reads again, never as end of input.
   - Everywhere else, including a redirected Windows stdin, it returns `std::io::stdin()` unchanged.
   - It stays in `lib.rs`, which `windows-mutants.yml` already lists. A new Windows-gated file would need that list and `tests/contract_windows_mutation_scope.rs` to move.
   - Unit: the zero-read and surrogate-split rules on a stand-in console source, compiled on every OS. Per testing.md 2026-09-24, the decision logic sits in a plain function and the `cfg(windows)` reader stays minimal.

10. **The CLI verbs** (new `src/cmd/pause.rs`, `src/cmd/release.rs`; `src/cmd/mod.rs`).
    - `viola pause <name> [--json]` and `viola release <name> [--json]`, with names through `send::parse_name`.
    - Each runs `client::start`, then the F-W1 liveness-only pre-check (`live_endpoint`, else exit 21 via `client::unreachable`), then one request carrying `from` from `own_name()` (so `VIOLA_NAME` set makes a CLI `release` a driver's), under a `pause.client` / `release.client` span.
    - Replies:
      - `Ok` → exit 0, printing `<name>  wheel human  manual-pause  I have control` (pause) or `<name>  wheel <holder>  you have control` (release) on stdout, or `{"v":1,"ok":{…}}` under `--json` (design-system §Surface: cli → Component Patterns 4; layout-templates §Output structure — wheel verbs);
      - `Fault` → exit 20 via `client::fault`;
      - unreachable → exit 21.
    - A reply of no known shape is the internal-error path (exit 1).
    - `role_of` needs no edit (`src/main.rs:90-104`).
    - The `release` `about` text names it the human's verb returning the wheel, and no other help text, hint or doc names it. `--help` grouping is `:100`'s.

11. **Hints and lines** (`src/human.rs`, `src/cmd/send.rs`, `src/cmd/answer.rs`).
    - The `human-typing` hint, for both details, is the design string `the human has the wheel; send again after the human hands it back` (design-system §Surface: cli → Component Patterns 2). `send`'s `Out::unable` (`src/cmd/send.rs:127-141`) asks for it on reason `human-typing`, and `answer_hint` (`src/human.rs:172-183`) returns it.
    - The `answer_hint_is_the_fixed_table` case at `:515` turns from `None` to that string.
    - Add the two wheel-verb result writers (one `write_all` each).
    - No hint string in `src/human.rs` contains `release`. A unit case iterates every hint the two tables return and asserts it. The integration and outer-PTY tests assert each human-mode refusal's last stderr line.
- `src/run/wheel.rs` — the wheel state, transitions, classifier, stdin observer, worker
- `src/run/snapshot.rs` — the wrapper's one in-process snapshot holder
- `src/cmd/pause.rs` — `viola pause`
- `src/cmd/release.rs` — `viola release`
- `tests/cli_wheel.rs` — CLI and channel wheel behaviour on a booted wrapper
- `tests/tui_wheel.rs` — Path 5, a11y case (3), the `^Z` and focus-report measurements
- `src/run/mod.rs` — declare `wheel`, `snapshot`
- `src/cmd/mod.rs` — `Pause` / `Release` subcommands and dispatch
- `src/cmd/run.rs` — the two methods, construction and wiring in `start` / `pump_child`, snapshot writes through the holder, the retargeted pin
- `src/run/send.rs` — the `human-typing` step, `wheel` on every wrapper `send-refused` line, the unclaimed-human-prompt report
- `src/run/dialog.rs` — null under a human wheel, the hand-back, `answer`'s slot, `write_pending` through the holder
- `src/cmd/send.rs` — the `human-typing` hint
- `src/cmd/answer.rs` — the `human-typing` hint
- `src/human.rs` — the hint rows, the two verb result writers, their tests
- `crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs` — the closed detail and cause types
- `crates/viola-channel/src/lib.rs` — the `release-from-driver` `-32602` variant
- `crates/viola-channel/src/server.rs` — the variant in the `-32602` classification
- `crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs` — the Windows console stdin reader
- `tests/channel_endpoint.rs` — `pause` → `unlink`
- `tests/cli_controls_not_disableable.rs` — the human-wheel row, its header
- `tests/contract_fixture_hygiene.rs` — the U40 mark
- `tests/contract_ledger_probes.rs` — the U40 mark
- `tests/contract_fake_agent_drift.rs` — the U40 mark

The boot smoke runs as a minted session (cleanup, boot, status, cleanup). No live leg against a real CLI. Every leg drives the fake agent through the harness, so there is no `round` probe. The Windows-only measurements (CARRY §8 `^Z`, CARRY §9 focus reports) cannot run on this Linux host. Their witness is the operator pass's CI read on `windows-2025` (`tests/tui_wheel.rs` runs on all three legs), and their red-before half rests on the source read named in research.md. Mutation is the epoch-boundary audit's (testing.md 2026-10-04). The walk-class witness is the header that every `gate.py run` of this block prints. The probe entry below counts the marks independently.

- (security) A channel `release` whose `from` is a string gets `{"code":-32602,"message":"invalid params","data":{"reason":"release-from-driver"}}`. CLI `viola release` with `VIOLA_NAME` set exits 20 with that detail, and a `pause` carrying `from` is accepted (per security-plan §Authentication & Authorization, "Driver-originated `release`").

- (security) CLI `pause` / `release` write their frame only after the liveness-only pre-check (snapshot pid + start time alive, heartbeat live, endpoint present; else exit 21). This is the seventh dated gap, the founder's live ruling F-W1, recorded as an Expected amendment below (per security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Authentication).
- (security) No `#[ignore]`, retry, skip, new env read, test seam or G2 exemption is added, and no deny allow, skip, ignore or exception is added (the three `git diff eb53a582c8dc` probe entries).

A `release` with `from` logs one `release-from-driver` line with `corr`, `conn`, `from` and `from_trust:"self-reported"`. CI's per-OS `test` job step "G4 schema conformance" (`agent-run.sh schema-check` over the kept homes) passes, read by the operator pass's `ci.py conclusion` entry (per obs-plan §4 Scenario "Human takes the wheel…"; §3 Log format JSON schema).

- A classifier inside viola-pty's pump — rejected. `pump_with_paste` already takes any `Read` (research.md), and viola-pty must not learn the wheel.

- Holding or buffering human bytes until a sequence is classified — rejected. The human is never delayed past the current paste (CLAUDE.md invariant 1). Classification only observes, and a trailing lone `ESC` counts at once.
- Writing the `wheel` event and snapshot on the stdin thread — rejected. Disk I/O would delay the human's next byte, so the in-memory flip is synchronous and the disk work is the worker's.
- Appending `wheel` through the wait feed — rejected. It is log-only and must not wake `wait` (architecture §Standard Contracts).
- A fake-agent mode emitting `<agent-message from=` — rejected. The wheel reads `origin`, and the prefix set is unit-proven at the hook layer.
- An MCP `pause` / `release` tool, a `--budget` CLI flag, `--help` grouping, a GUI brake route — out of scope (architecture [MCP]; `:91`; `:100`; v1.x).

- A new fake-agent or wrapper test seam (for example, to stall a paste) — not added. A third seam is a boundary widening needing a Decisions Log ruling (security.md); the existing receipts and the outer PTY suffice.
- `release` emptying the in-flight send slot — rejected. That slot belongs to a live `send` (research.md §Mechanisms).
- `#[ignore]`-parking the Windows focus or `^Z` cases — forbidden (test-plan §10). A Windows red folds into this chunk.

- **Order sensitivity.**
  - The snapshot holder (step 4) lands before the wheel (step 5) and the hand-back (step 7).
  - The wheel's in-memory flip happens inside the observer's `read`, before the bytes are returned to the pump's copy thread. A `send` racing the key therefore either sees `human` or was already past its wheel check, and its paste then holds the human chunk behind it (`pump.rs:96-101`), exactly the "atomic send window".

- **The DA1 reply on Windows x64** reaches the child through the same stdin. It must be non-editing (F-W2) or every `windows-2025` boot reads `human` from the start. `tests/tui_passthrough.rs` and `chaos_feed_panic.rs` would then go red on Windows, and the boot readiness `start_records` would still pass.
- **`chaos_feed_panic.rs`** sends before its typed `k` (`:71-104`), so its `input-not-ready` verdict is unchanged on Linux/macOS (research.md sweep: 25 outer-PTY writers, 0 changed).
- **Windows outer-PTY backend:** `OuterPty` runs on the inbox ConPTY and the child on the sideloaded one (2026-09-29-sideloaded-conpty). The CARRY §9 reading names the inbox outer backend.

- **Surfaced, not folded:** the `prompt-submitted` → `turn-ended` running-turn state of architecture [Human Takeover / Wheel] has no owner on the route (`grep -n 'turn.running' viola-0.1.0/working-route.md` → `:80` only). The mask (`dwCtrlWakeupMask`) matters only under line input, which `HostTerminal` clears, but the strip at `:389-391` runs in every mode. The carried hypothesis ("may treat a leading `^Z` as end of input") holds by the source and is wider than stated: any read ending in `^Z` loses that byte. To measure: a `windows-2025` outer-PTY case writing `\x1a` then `k`.

title: 1. A human editing key takes the wheel (working entry)

data.head: ### 1. A human editing key takes the wheel (working entry)

body: - `viola run` owns the real stdin, so it knows byte provenance exactly. Any human editing key since the last turn boundary moves the wheel to `human` (`architecture.md:70`).

- The move appends one `wheel` event `{holder:"human", cause:"human-input"}` (`source: wrapper`, log-only, never wakes `wait`) and rewrites the snapshot's `wheel` (`architecture.md:255`, `:299`, `:305`). Only a CHANGE appends — a second key while `human` adds no line.
- An automated `send` while the wheel is `human` is refused `human-typing` (exit 10, `src/cmd/send.rs:87`).
- A human interrupt is human input: it moves the wheel to the human (`architecture.md:70`).
- The human always wins: no human byte is blocked, refused or delayed past the current atomic paste (CLAUDE.md universal invariant 1).

- What an "editing key" is is a classifier over the stdin byte stream, agent-neutral (verified, research.md §Patterns: `pump_with_paste` takes any `Box<dyn Read + Send>` at `src/cmd/run.rs:470-472`, so a `Read` wrapper in the root bin's `src/run/` sees every human byte before the child, mirroring the output `Tee` at `src/run/gate.rs:130-140`; viola-pty is not changed for it).

- [premise-corrected: the stdin stream carries terminal replies as well as keys — on Windows x64 the outer terminal's DA1 answer to the sideloaded ConPTY's spawn-time `ESC[c` travels through `viola run`'s stdin (`tests/tui_passthrough.rs:101-104`; chunk 2026-09-29-sideloaded-conpty `evidence/da1-stall.md`, measured). The architecture names only focus, mouse and resize as non-editing, so whether DA/CPR/DECRPM/OSC/DCS replies count is a P4 ruling, not a code detail.]

title: 2. Focus, mouse and resize never take it (working entry)

data.head: ### 2. Focus, mouse and resize never take it (working entry)

body: - Focus reports (`ESC[I` / `ESC[O`), mouse reports and resize events do not count as editing keys and never move the wheel (`architecture.md:70`; a11y-plan §3 tui clause, `a11y-plan.md:321`, and its three outer-PTY nextest cases, `a11y-plan.md:573`).
- These bytes still pass through to the child unchanged — "never move the wheel" is not "swallowed".

title: 3. Held bytes during the paste (working entry)

data.head: ### 3. Held bytes during the paste (working entry)

body: - A bridge send is ONE `ESC[200~…ESC[201~` + CR write. Human bytes arriving during that write are held in the pump and passed on straight after it (`architecture.md:70`; `viola-pty`'s `PasteHandle` is the shared child input, CLAUDE.md Modules).

What this chunk owes is that those held bytes still move the wheel.

title: 4. Harness turns never take it (working entry)

data.head: ### 4. Harness turns never take it (working entry)

body: - An unsent `prompt-submitted` (one no `send` issued) confirms and logs a human take. A prompt whose raw start (no trim) is one of `viola-agent-claude`'s four `HARNESS_PREFIXES` is a harness turn, never a human take (`architecture.md:70`; `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/hook.rs:105`, `:177`).
- The founder-accepted side effect stands: a human who types the cross-session tag at a prompt's start is filed `harness` (2026-09-29 15:21:44).

- The fake agent's `--inject-harness-turn` submits one `<task-notification>` prompt filed `origin:"harness"` (verified, `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs:22`, `:466-485`). The wheel reads only the normalised `origin`; each of the four prefixes is pinned at the unit layer (`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/hook.rs:445-460`), so the existing mode witnesses "harness turn ignored" end-to-end without a fake-agent change.

- CLI `viola pause` moves the wheel to `human` without a keystroke, cause `manual-pause`; channel `pause` `{}` → `{wheel:"human"}` (`architecture.md:282`). After it, automated `send` is refused `human-typing` with detail `manual-pause`. It is the CLI twin of the reserved v1.x GUI brake route (no GUI route lands here).
- The wheel returns ONLY through CLI `viola release`: channel `release` `{budget?:bool}` → `{wheel:<holder>, budget_paused:bool}` (`architecture.md:283`); cause `release`.

No code tracks `prompt-submitted` → `turn-ended`, and no route entry owns that half of the architecture's `turn-running` (research.md §Mechanisms). Surfaced at P5, not folded.]

data.head: ### 12. CARRY — `answer` and `hook.dialog` under a human wheel (chunk 2026-10-04-dialog-answers-by-dialog-id)
