A panic or a dispatch error then prints it exactly once (obs-plan §7 Per-role behaviour). CLI `wait` / `last` write their frame after `send`'s liveness-only pre-check under a **fifth dated interim gap**, ratified live by the founder at this P4 (F1 below), owned by Epoch 6 `:109` / `:111`.

1. **`viola-core` dialog kinds** (`crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs`). `EventKind` gains `Question`, `Permission`, `Plan` (`as_str` `question` / `permission` / `plan`), and the `event_kind_as_str_is_kebab_case` table gains their rows. No producer is added: dialog events are `working-route.md:78`'s (research E3, E9).

2. **A capped event-log reader** (`crates/viola-state/src/events.rs`). One function reads the complete lines of `events.ndjson` whose start offset is ≥ a given byte offset. Each line comes back with its start offset, its end offset (the byte after its `\n`) and its parsed JSON value.
   - Each line is read through `Read::take(MAX_FRAME + 1)`. An over-long line is skipped and counted.
   - A line that is not a JSON object is skipped and counted.
   - A last line with no `\n` is not returned and is not rewritten. Healing it is `:85`'s (research E8).
   - An offset inside a line skips that line, which is the contract's "line STARTS at or after".
   - An absent log reads as no lines.
   - Unit tests in the same file cover every case above.

4. **Wiring in `run`** (`src/cmd/run.rs`, `src/run/send.rs`).
   - `Methods` gains the step-3 struct (`Arc`).
   - `start` builds it and rebuilds it from the log BEFORE `server.serve` (`src/cmd/run.rs:196-201`), so the first `last` already sees the replayed turn.
   - `dispatch_call` routes `wait` and `last` beside `send`.
   - `append_hook_event` (`src/run/send.rs:130-147`) takes the struct and signals it after every successful append.
   - Its callers follow: `Methods::dispatch` @ `src/cmd/run.rs:109` and the 6 unit tests @ `src/run/send.rs:538`, `:576`, `:591`, `:608`, `:635`, `:655` (graph, research §Graph impact).
   - The unit test at `src/cmd/run.rs:579-582` keeps `-32601` for `hook.dialog` and an unknown method, with `answer` in place of `wait`.
   - The wrapper's own `send-*` records are not signalled. They never wake `wait`, so a signal there would be unobservable (testing.md 2026-09-24).

5. **Shared client plumbing** (new `src/cmd/client.rs`; `src/cmd/send.rs` uses it). Move `Reply`, `reply_of`, `fault_detail`, `fault_document`, `live_endpoint` and `own_name` out of `send.rs` unchanged (`src/cmd/send.rs:87-130`, `:292-305`), with their unit tests.
   - Add one exit-21 helper that prints the human or `--json` form and logs `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:21, detail:"instance-dead", during}` at **WARN**. That level is obs-plan §6 Log levels mapping (`.andromeda/obs-plan.md:844`: "`process-exit` exit 21" in the `warn` row). It fixes `send`'s ERROR line at `src/cmd/send.rs:325` (research E6).
   - `send`'s human exit-21 form stays its bracketed mirror.

6. **`viola wait`** (new `src/cmd/wait.rs`) and **`viola last`** (new `src/cmd/last.rs`); subcommands in `src/cmd/mod.rs`.
   - Arguments: `<name>` through `ViolaName::try_new`, `--after <u64>` and `--timeout-ms <u64>` (`wait` only), and `--json`. A non-integer value is a clap usage error, exit 2.
   - Each verb, like `send`: obs init as `ObsProcess::Cli` with the instance, then `log_self_start`.
   - Each connects through `client::live_endpoint`; none → exit 21 `during:"connect"`.
   - One request under `#[instrument(skip_all, name = "wait.block", fields(after, timeout_ms))]` / `name = "last.client"`, adding `from` from `VIOLA_NAME`.
   - `ChannelError::Connect` → exit 21 `connect`. `Closed | Io` → exit 21 `call` (research E1). A JSON-RPC `error` → exit 20 with the wrapper-fault document or `error: wrapper fault  <code>`. An `ok` → exit 0.
   - `log_self_exit` on every path.
   - **Human forms** (design-system cli Component Patterns 3; layout-templates §Output structure — `viola wait` / `viola last`):
     - `wait`: `waiting: <name>` once on stderr, only when stderr is a terminal and not `--json` (a11y-plan §4 P6). Then one stdout line:
       - `turn-ended  <name>  <HH:MM:SS.mmmZ>  cursor <n>`;
       - `<kind>  <name>  dialog <id>  cursor <n>` for a dialog kind;
       - `session-end  <name>  <HH:MM:SS.mmmZ>  cursor <n>`;
       - `timed out  <name>  <ms> ms`.
     - `last`: `last  <name>  turn-ended <HH:MM:SS.mmmZ>` on stderr (terminal, not `--json`), then the escaped message on stdout. A `null` message → `no message` on stderr and nothing on stdout.
     - Exit 21: `unable  <name>  instance-unreachable` then `hint: <name> is not running; viola list shows the live instances` (`send_hint`'s `not-running`, `src/human.rs:99`) as the last stderr line.
     - `--json`: exactly one document on stdout (`{"v":1,"ok":…}`, the exit-21 or the wrapper-fault document) and nothing on stderr.

7. **`src/human.rs`**.
   - The message-mode escaper: over decoded `char`s every `char::is_control` except `\n` and `\t` becomes `\xHH` text, two uppercase hex digits of the code point (ESC → `\x1B`, CR → `\x0D`, DEL → `\x7F`, U+009B → `\x9B`); everything else passes through. It never strips (CARRY 1; design-system cli Component Patterns 3).
   - The step-6 writers, each one `write_all`, no print macro, no `#[allow]`.
   - Unit tests: the escaper table, plus one write per writer with literal output.

8. **The `cli`-role panic line** (`src/main.rs`, `src/cmd/mod.rs`; CARRY 2).
   - `role_of` returns `Hook` for `hook`, `Other` for `run`, and `Cli` for every other first word, per obs-plan §7 Main-thread catch site: "`run|hook|mcp|ui` are named roles; any other verb is `cli`" (the obs extract, obs-plan §7). The `--home` skipping is unchanged.
   - The `Send` arm stops calling `crate::human::internal_error()` (`src/cmd/mod.rs:73`), so the catch site at `src/main.rs:72-74` is the one printer. The `Wait` and `Last` arms build their `DetailSink` like `Send`'s.
   - The rstest tables at `src/main.rs:309-361` gain literal rows: `send`, `wait`, `last` (and after `--home`) → `Cli`; `run` → `Other`; `hook` → `Hook`. `exit_code(Cli, Panicked)` → 1 and `prints_internal_error(Cli, Panicked | Failed)` → true already exist and stay.

9. **Channel logs for `wait`** (`crates/viola-channel/src/server.rs`, `crates/viola-channel/src/client.rs`; obs-plan §4 Scenario `wait` / `last`).
   - Both sides' `channel-request` carry `after` and `timeout_ms` when `method` is `wait` and the params hold them as `u64` (schema admits both, research E5).
   - Both sides' `channel-response` carry `outcome`, derived only for `method:"wait"` from the reply: `timed-out` for `ok.timed_out:true`, the event's `kind` when it is one of the five wake kinds, `instance-unreachable` on the client when the reply never arrived (`Closed | Io`).
   - No result body or event content is logged.
   - Unit tests sit beside the existing `client_and_server_log_the_call_under_one_conn_and_corr` (`crates/viola-channel/src/client.rs:302-327`).

10. **Path 3 fixtures** (new `fixtures/fake-scripts/path3.json`, schema `schemas/fake-script.v1.json`): a gated `PostToolUse` `default` step, then a gated `Stop` `default` step. Tests pass a scratch `--fixtures` root holding synthetic `SessionStart` / `PostToolUse` / `Stop` bodies, the `Stop` one carrying the canary and the control characters (the `tests/hook_events.rs:31-37` precedent, research E7).

11. **Integration tests** (new `tests/cli_wait_last.rs`):
    - `path3_wait_parks_until_turn_ended_then_last_reads_it`: boot with `path3.json`; take `C` = the log's end offset after `session-start`; spawn `viola wait builder --after C --json`; release the activity step and wait for its `activity` line; the spawned `wait` is still `try_wait() == None`; release `Stop`; it exits 0 with `event.kind == "turn-ended"` and `cursor` equal to the end offset of that line on disk; the same `--after C` again returns the same document at once; `--after <file end> --timeout-ms 500 --json` exits 0 with `{"v":1,"ok":{"timed_out":true}}`; `viola last builder --json` before the Stop is `{"v":1,"ok":{"last_assistant_message":null,"ts":null}}` and after it is the canary message and the line's `ts`.
    - `wait_after_a_send_cursor_returns_the_turn`: `send` `--json` → its `ok.cursor` → `viola wait builder --after <cursor> --json` returns the `turn-ended` that follows.
    - `last_survives_a_wrapper_restart`: `stop_keep`, boot the same name again, and `last --json` equals the value before the restart (the rebuild).
    - `last_human_escapes_controls`: a `Stop` message with ESC, BEL, CR, DEL, U+009B, `\n`, `\t` → human `last` stdout holds each control only as `\xHH` text, `\n` / `\t` raw, no raw C0/C1 byte; `--json` stays serde-escaped.
    - `wait_human_lines_are_linear`: under `tests/support/outer_pty.rs`, `viola wait builder --timeout-ms 200` shows the literal `waiting: builder` exactly once and `timed out  builder  200 ms`. Piped, there is no `waiting:` line and no ESC byte.
    - `wait_last_unreachable_exit_21`: no wrapper. Both verbs give the human pair and the `--json` document. `cli-builder.ndjson` holds `process-exit{exit_code:21, detail:"instance-dead", during:"connect"}` at `level:"WARN"`.
    - `cli_verbs_print_internal_error_once`: for each of `send` (stdin given), `wait`, `last` with `--home <a regular file>`, exit 1 and stderr exactly `error: internal error\n` (one line, counted), stdout empty (research E4).
    - `channel_wait_last_invalid_params`: through a raw `Client` on a booted wrapper, `wait` with `after:-1` / `after:"x"` / `timeout_ms:"x"` / `from:"Bad Name"` and `last` with `from:7` → `error.code == -32602`, `data == null`.
    - Every `--json` line is checked against the product's own reply shapes. No home-level `diagnostics/*.ndjson` line carries the canary.

12. **Chaos** (new `tests/chaos_wait_vanish.rs`): `chaos_wait_parked_wrapper_killed_exits_21`. Boot, spawn `viola wait builder --json` with no timeout, and wait for the wrapper's `channel-request{method:"wait"}` line (it is parked). Kill the wrapper by its snapshot `pid`: `TerminateProcess` on Windows, `Command::new("kill")` with `-KILL` on Unix (research E10). Within `WITHIN`, the `wait` exits 21 with exactly `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":null}`, never 20. `cli-builder.ndjson` holds one `process-exit{exit_code:21, detail:"instance-dead", during:"call"}`. The test stays inside `target/e2e-home`: no panic is forced.

13. **`tests/channel_endpoint.rs`**: `channel_wrapper_logs_each_call_with_corr_and_conn` (`:211`) uses `answer` in place of `last` and `pause` in place of `wait` for its two `-32601` calls, with the same assertions.
- `src/run/wait.rs` — the wrapper's append signal, `wait` scan + timeout, in-memory `last` + rebuild, unit tests
- `src/cmd/wait.rs` — `viola wait`
- `src/cmd/last.rs` — `viola last`
- `src/cmd/client.rs` — client plumbing shared by `send` / `wait` / `last`
- `tests/cli_wait_last.rs` — Path 3's cli + channel half and the CLI cases
- `tests/chaos_wait_vanish.rs` — the wrapper killed under a parked `wait`
- `fixtures/fake-scripts/path3.json` — the gated activity + Stop turn
- `crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs` — `EventKind::{Question, Permission, Plan}`
- `crates/viola-state/src/events.rs` — the capped reader from an offset
- `src/run/mod.rs` — `mod wait`
- `src/run/send.rs` — `append_hook_event` signals the wait struct; its 6 test callers
- `src/cmd/run.rs` — `Methods` routes `wait` / `last`; rebuild before serve; the `:579` test
- `src/cmd/mod.rs` — `Wait` / `Last`; the `Send` arm no longer prints
- `src/cmd/send.rs` — uses `client.rs`; exit 21 at WARN
- `src/human.rs` — escaper + writers
- `src/main.rs` — `role_of` and its table rows
- `crates/viola-channel/src/server.rs` — `after` / `timeout_ms` / `outcome` for `wait`
- `crates/viola-channel/src/client.rs` — the same on the client side
- `tests/channel_endpoint.rs` — no `wait` / `last` as unserved methods

No live leg runs: `claude` is never driven, and the held typed probe stays held. `src/cmd/run.rs` is on the boot path, so the block boots one harness session (`p-wait-smoke`: pre-clean, boot, status, cleanup), as the prior chunks did. Path 3's run-level witness is the root integration tests, on all three CI OSes. Windows is witnessed only by `windows-2025`.

body: - (tests) **The wake set and the deadline, clock-driven**: the `run::wait::tests::` unit entry shows each of `turn-ended`, `question`, `permission`, `plan`, `session-end` waking. Every other kind, an unknown one included, never wakes. A logged match returns at once. `timed_out` comes only after the injected clock passes `timeout_ms` (per test-plan §4 root bin channel `wait` handler; §8 Time).

- (tests / chaos) **Vanished wrapper**: `chaos_wait_parked_wrapper_killed_exits_21` gives exit 21 with exactly `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":null}`, never 20, and one `process-exit{exit_code:21, detail:"instance-dead", during:"call"}`. Same integration gate (per test-plan §6 Chaos suite; obs-plan §4 Scenario `wait` / `last` Cleanup).

- (obs / design / layouts) **CARRY 2, the `cli`-role line, its own item**. The real-binary witness `cli_verbs_print_internal_error_once`: `send`, `wait` and `last` each exit 1 with stderr exactly one `error: internal error` line and no hint. A double print reads two lines and an unfiled verb reads zero, so this cannot pass vacuously (research E4). The panic half is the literal rstest rows: `role_of` → `Cli` for all three, `exit_code(Cli, Panicked)` → 1, `prints_internal_error(Cli, Panicked)` → true. The `grep -c 'crate::human::internal_error' src/cmd/mod.rs` entry reads 0. Gates: the integration entry, the `tests::role_of|…` unit entry, the count entry (per obs-plan §7 Panic hooks → Per-role behaviour; architecture §Conventions exit `1`; layout-templates §Component — Primary content block 2).

- (security / a11y / design) **Human escaping**: `last_human_escapes_controls` shows ESC, BEL, CR, DEL and U+009B only as `\xHH` text with `\n` / `\t` raw and no raw C0/C1 byte on stdout, while `--json` stays serde-escaped. The escaper table pins `\x1B` · `\x0D` · `\x7F` · `\x9B` (per security-plan §Input Validation `:425`; design-system cli Component Patterns 3; a11y-plan §4 P6).

- (a11y / layouts) **Linear output**: `wait_human_lines_are_linear` shows `waiting: builder` exactly once under the outer PTY and absent when piped, `timed out  builder  200 ms` on stdout, and no ESC byte when piped. `--json` is exactly one document with an empty stderr in every case (per a11y-plan §4 P6; layout-templates §Output structure — `viola wait` / `viola last`).

- (security) **Bounded params, wrapper-side**: `channel_wait_last_invalid_params` gives `-32602` with `data: null` for each bad `after` / `timeout_ms` / `from`, and an extra field stays no fault (per security-plan §Input Validation, row "Channel frames").

- (obs) A woken `wait` leaves `channel-request{method:"wait", after}` and `channel-response{method:"wait", outcome:"turn-ended"}` on both sides, joined by `corr` + `conn` (the `server::tests::` / `client::tests::` unit entry). Exit 21 logs at WARN. No home-level line carries the canary, and G4 reads green in CI (per obs-plan §4 Scenario `wait` / `last`; §6 Log levels mapping; §9 G4).

- (arch) The held boundary is untouched (the `git diff --quiet bcff692e4249` entry). No `tokio` enters a sync crate (the per-crate ban entry) (per architecture §Cross-cutting Patterns "Tokio containment").
- (tests) `bash scripts/agent-run.sh pre-push` reads `"ok":true`, and the operator's CI read of the final HEAD reads `verdict: green` (per test-plan §10).

- **F1 — the fifth dated interim gap (Boundary widening, playbook escalate; the founder's ruling, live, 2026-10-04, relayed by the Viola overseer through a live AskUserQuestion at this P4).** CLI `viola wait` and `viola last` write their frame after `send`'s liveness-only pre-check: the snapshot's pid + start time alive, the heartbeat live, an `endpoint` present, else exit 21. There is no server identity and no strict-modes check, until Epoch 6 `:109` / `:111`. They do not borrow `hook.event`'s exception.
- **F2 — the CARRY 2 witness (overseer, founder-delegated, 2026-10-04).** Unit rows for the panic half, plus the counted real-binary Err-path line for all three verbs. No new seam, no G2 change.

- Spec anchors: architecture §Established Decisions [Message Broker / IPC], §Standard Contracts (Channel methods, Event `data` per kind, CLI `--json` output), §Conventions (CLI, exit codes), §Cross-cutting Patterns (Tokio containment); security-plan §Authentication & Authorization (IPC client-side server verification), §Input Validation (Channel frames; `:425`), §Error Handling; obs-plan §4 Scenario `wait` / `last`, §6 (Log levels mapping), §7 (Per-role behaviour, Main-thread catch site), §9 G2/G4; test-plan §4 root bin, §6 Path 3 / Chaos, §7, §10; design-system cli Component Patterns 1–3, Exit-code phraseology; layout-templates §Output structure — `viola wait` / `viola last`, §Component — Primary content block 2; a11y-plan §4 P6, §8.

- Research files inspected: `src/main.rs`, `src/cmd/mod.rs`, `src/cmd/send.rs`, `src/cmd/run.rs`, `src/run/send.rs`, `src/cmd/hook.rs`, `src/human.rs`, `src/obs.rs`, `src/run/mod.rs`, `crates/viola-channel/src/{client,frame,server}.rs`, `crates/viola-state/src/events.rs`, `crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs`, `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/hook.rs`, `schemas/diag-line.v1.json`, `tests/{hook_events,cli_send,channel_endpoint,run_cli,cli_instance_state}.rs`, `tests/support/home.rs`.
- A timed re-read of `events.ndjson` as the wake — rejected: "nothing polls" (architecture [Message Broker / IPC]). The step timeout only re-reads the clock.
- `notify` / file tailing in `viola-state` for the wake — rejected: every wake-bearing append is in-process (research E2). A tail adds a dependency and a second wake source for no observable case.
- Healing the torn last line or logging `state-recovered` from the new reader — rejected: `working-route.md:85` owns torn-line healing (research E8).

- The without-`after` pending-dialog return, a dialog wake end to end, and `dialog_id` — rejected here: no dialog event can be produced at HEAD (research E3). They are `:78`'s (Implementation notes, route pin).
- Reusing the `list` escaper rule (escaping `\n` / `\t`) for `last` — rejected: `wait` / `last` keep them (design-system cli Component Patterns 1, T5; layouts extract).
- A third panic seam or a G2 exemption — rejected (F2).
- A `timeout_ms` maximum or an `after`-past-EOF refusal — rejected as decisive leans below. Neither is stated by any master, and both inputs are type-bounded (`u64`).
- Logging any event content, the message or a result body in a codes-only line — banned (obs-plan §8; security-plan §Error Handling).

- **Leaned decisions** (each a decisive material lean, stated for the P5 review):
  - leaned literal `after` past EOF per architecture `:52` ("returns the first driver-relevant event whose line starts at or after it"): no refusal, no clamp. It parks until such a line exists.
  - leaned `timeout_ms` bounded by its `u64` type with a `checked_add` deadline (an overflow = no deadline), per architecture `:52` (no cap stated). A huge timeout behaves as none.
  - leaned `role_of` "every other verb is `cli`" per obs-plan §7 Main-thread catch site.
  - leaned `outcome` derived in `viola-channel` per obs-plan §4 Scenario `wait` / `last` (`channel-response{… outcome}`).
  - leaned the exit-21 human form `unable  <name>  instance-unreachable` per layout-templates §Component — Primary content block 2 (`unable  <name>  <reason>  <detail>`) over the design line that omits the name.
  - leaned exit 21 at WARN for all three verbs per obs-plan §6 Log levels mapping (`.andromeda/obs-plan.md:844`).
  - leaned unknown params fields ignored per `tests/channel_endpoint.rs:113`.

- **Order sensitivity**: rebuild before `server.serve` (step 4). Signal after the append succeeds, never before (a scan then sees the line). Read the generation BEFORE each scan, so a line appended during the scan is never missed.

- **A parked handler holds its connection's worker thread** (`crates/viola-channel/src/server.rs:67-74`) until the next wake, its deadline, or the wrapper's exit. An abandoned no-timeout `wait` is released by the next wake event, whose reply write then fails.

- **Expected amendments (wrap):**

The served-as line for `wait` / `last` under the IPC controls. `MAX_FRAME` consumers gain the `events.ndjson` reader.

  - design-system cli Component Patterns 3 — the `session-end` result line.

- **Route pin owed (wrap route-resolve) on `working-route.md:78`, a CONDITION of the v1-30 claim (the operator, at the P5 approval, 2026-10-04):** the pin names `:78` as OWNER of the end-to-end `question` / `permission` / `plan` wait witness for `verification-matrix.json#v1-30`. A dialog event's append must signal the wait struct (`src/run/wait.rs`). The without-`after` pending-dialog return and the `<kind>  <name>  dialog <id>` line's end-to-end witness land there too.

- **Symbols / APIs:**
  - **Channel method `wait`** (served by `run`, `src/cmd/run.rs` `Methods::dispatch_call`): `params` `{after?, timeout_ms?, from?}` + `v` / `sender` → `{"ok":{"event":<the line's JSON object>,"cursor":<its line's end offset>}}` or `{"ok":{"timed_out":true}}`. `after` / `timeout_ms` must be a non-negative integer fitting `u64` — `null`, a negative, a fraction or a string is `-32602` `invalid params`, `data: null`; `from` absent, `null` or a valid `ViolaName`, else `-32602`; unknown fields ignored. Start offset = `after`, else `events::end_offset` read at the call. Deadline = `now + timeout_ms` through `Instant::checked_add` (an unrepresentable instant = no deadline). Wake set = `EventKind::WAIT_WAKE` (`turn-ended` · `question` · `permission` · `plan` · `session-end`); every other kind, an unknown one included, never wakes. A line `after` falls inside is skipped (the line must START at or after it).

  - **The wake mechanism** (`src/run/wait.rs` `WaitFeed`): one `Mutex` (generation counter + the newest turn) + one `Condvar`. `WaitFeed::appending(line, append)` runs the hook line's append INSIDE the lock hold, then bumps the generation, keeps a `turn-ended` as the newest turn and `notify_all`s — so anyone who has seen the line on disk gets that turn from `last` (fixed at the operator pass, `3de125f`; `db15b2b` had updated the feed in a second step after the append). A parked `wait` reads the generation BEFORE each scan, scans outside the lock, and re-scans only when the generation moves; its `wait_timeout(STEP = 20 ms)` re-reads the injected `Clock` against the deadline and never re-scans the file. Each scan resumes at the end of the last line it read. `WaitFeed::rebuild(instance_dir)` reads the whole log once at start, BEFORE `server.serve` (`src/cmd/run.rs` `start`), for the newest `turn-ended`. Only hook lines signal (`append_hook_event`); the wrapper's own `send-*` / start records do not (they never wake). A parked handler holds its connection's worker thread until a wake, its deadline or the wrapper's exit.

data.head: ## Graph impact (from the code-graph query; rust plane, `tree-query-2026-10-04-wait-and-last.json`, 42 rows; lines below are editor lines = SCIP + 1)

body: - **role_of** — 2 callers: `main` @ `src/main.rs:53` and the rstest @ `:323`. The change is internal to `main.rs`.
- **prints_internal_error** — `main` @ `src/main.rs:72` and the rstest @ `:361`.
- **internal_error** (human) — `cmd::dispatch` @ `src/cmd/mod.rs:74` (the `Send` arm) and `main` @ `src/main.rs:73`. These two sites are the double print the fix removes.
- **append_hook_event** — `Methods::dispatch` @ `src/cmd/run.rs:109` plus 6 unit tests in `src/run/send.rs` (`:538`, `:576`, `:591`, `:608`, `:635`, `:655`). A signature change threads through all 7.

- **live_endpoint · own_name · reply_of · send_hint · write_send_unable** — callers only in `src/cmd/send.rs` and `src/human.rs`'s own tests. Extracting the shared client pieces touches only these two files plus the new verbs.
- **end_offset** — `src/run/send.rs:320`, viola-state's own tests, and `tests/cli_send.rs` (test-side reader, unaffected).

- **Condvar wake with injected-clock deadline** (`src/run/send.rs:101-124`): a `Mutex` state plus `Condvar::wait_timeout(STEP)` that re-reads `Clock::now()` against a deadline each step. Tests drive it with a `JumpClock` (`src/run/send.rs:363-371`). This is the precedent for `wait`'s parked handler and its §4 clock-driven unit case.

- **The wrapper's in-process append path** (`src/run/send.rs:130-147`, `src/run/send.rs:248-284`): every line the wrapper appends (hook events, send records) is written by the `run` process itself. The one out-of-process writer is the hook's direct SessionEnd (`src/cmd/hook.rs:227-236`), and it runs only when the channel did not take the event.

- **Client verb shape** (`src/cmd/send.rs:223-310`): obs init as `ObsProcess::Cli` with the instance, a liveness-only endpoint, one `Client::connect(…, "cli")?.request(method, params)` under a `<verb>.client` span, and the reply mapped to a document or human lines plus a typed exit and `log_self_exit`.
- **Per-test synthetic fixtures** (`tests/hook_events.rs:31-37`): a `Stop` body written per test into a scratch fixtures root, passed to `Wrapper::boot` via `--fixtures`.
- **One `write_all` per human message** (`src/human.rs:10-12`, `:67-78`): `src/human.rs` stays print-macro-free and `#[allow]`-free.
- **Fixed-message thiserror / codes only** (`crates/viola-channel/src/lib.rs:30-46`): a new client error is a variant of the crate's one enum.
- **`#[instrument(skip_all, name = "<area>.<op>")]` only** (`src/cmd/send.rs:307`): the obs spans `wait.block`, `last.client` and `run.wait_dispatch` follow.
- **Unit tables with literal oracles** (`src/main.rs:309-361`): `#[case::label]` rows with integer exits.

- **E1 — mid-call close maps to exit 21.** The equality: a wrapper process that exits while a client is blocked in `Client::request` yields `ChannelError::Closed` (EOF, `frame.rs:31-32`) or `ChannelError::Io` (reset, `frame.rs:26`), and `send` already maps both to exit 21 `during:"call"` (`src/cmd/send.rs:267`). The client-side `channel-response` for that case reads `error`/`-32603` at ERROR (`client.rs:81`), not `outcome:"instance-unreachable"`.

- **E2 — the wake has one in-process source.** Every append that can make a parked `wait` return while its wrapper is alive is made in the `run` process: `hook.event` through `append_hook_event` (`src/cmd/run.rs:108-110` → `src/run/send.rs:142`). The hook's direct SessionEnd (`src/cmd/hook.rs:227-236`) happens only after `deliver` failed, so that wrapper is unreachable and its parked clients see E1. A `wait` called afterwards still finds the line by scanning from `after`.

- **E3 — no dialog event can be produced at HEAD.** `Methods::dispatch` answers `hook.dialog` `-32601` (`src/cmd/run.rs:104-105`), and `HOOK_KINDS` holds no dialog kind (`src/cmd/run.rs:70-76`). The pending-dialog state (`pending_dialog` in the snapshot) is `Dialog answers by dialog_id`'s (`working-route.md:78`).

- **E4 — the Err-path stderr line is witnessable on the real binary without a seam.** `target/harness/debug/viola` (built 2026-10-04 09:00Z, from the `bcff692` tree): `echo hi | viola --home <a regular file> send builder` → exit 1, stderr exactly `error: internal error\n`, stdout empty. The same holds for `verify`. Today `send`'s line comes from its dispatch arm, because `role_of` files it `Other`. So after the fix the same probe gives one line only if the arm no longer prints and `role_of` files `send`, `wait` and `last` as `Cli`. A double print reads as two lines and an unfiled verb as zero, so the witness cannot pass vacuously. Scratch: `<scratchpad>/home-is-a-file`.

- **E5 — the log schema already admits the obs fields.** `after` and `timeout_ms` on `channel-request`, and `outcome` (string) on `channel-response` (`schemas/diag-line.v1.json` `allOf[19]`, `allOf[20]`). No schema change is needed for them. `woken_kind` is absent (0 hits).

- **E6 — exit 21's level.** obs-plan §6 Log levels mapping (`.andromeda/obs-plan.md:844`) puts `process-exit` exit 21 at `warn`. `send`'s `unreachable` logs it at ERROR (`src/cmd/send.rs:325`). This is a pre-existing deviation in the code `wait`/`last` will share.

- **E7 — a Stop payload's control characters reach `turn-ended` intact** (`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/hook.rs:143`). So a scratch `Stop` fixture carrying ESC / CR / DEL / U+009B plus the canary drives `last`'s human-mode escaping end to end, on the `hook_events.rs` precedent, with no recorded fixture invented (the fixture is per-test synthetic, outside `fixtures/claude/`).

- **E9 — `EventKind` lacks the dialog kinds.** `viola-core`'s `EventKind` (`crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs:44-55`) holds 10 variants with no `question` / `permission` / `plan`, and its `as_str` table test is at `:276-286`. events.md says "Normalised kinds live only in `viola-core`", so the wake set's three dialog kinds are added there and named from there.

- **E10 — killing a wrapper from outside, per OS.** Windows: `OpenProcess` + `TerminateProcess` on the snapshot `pid` (`tests/run_cli.rs:606-623`; the child ends with its wrapper there). Unix: `Command::new("kill")` with a signal on the snapshot pid (`tests/cli_instance_state.rs:208-214`). Either way the wrapper dies without a SessionEnd, so a parked `wait` meets E1 rather than a `session-end` wake.
- **E8 — torn-line healing belongs to `working-route.md:85`** (Epoch 4 `Self-healing state`). This chunk's reader skips a last line with no `\n` without healing it or logging `state-recovered`.

- `src/run/wait.rs` — the wrapper's `wait` and `last`: the append feed (generation counter + Condvar, signalled after every wrapper append), the scan from `after` for the first wake kind, the injected-clock timeout, the in-memory newest turn and its start-up rebuild, plus unit tests

title: 1. `wait` — cursor-based wake on driver-relevant events (working entry)

data.head: ### 1. `wait` — cursor-based wake on driver-relevant events (working entry)

body:
- Surfaces:
  - the CLI verb `viola wait <target> [--after <cursor>] [--timeout-ms <n>]` (architecture §Conventions CLI, `architecture.md:176`);
  - the channel method `wait` `{after?, timeout_ms?}` → `{event:<ndjson event line>, cursor}` or `{timed_out:true}` (`architecture.md:276`), served by `run` beside `hook.event` and `send`. Every `params` also carries `v` and `sender`, plus `from` when `VIOLA_NAME` is set.
  - Re-verified at P1: `METHODS` lists `"wait"` (`crates/viola-channel/src/server.rs:356`), and `run`'s `Methods::dispatch` answers it `-32601` today (`src/cmd/run.rs:103-105`), pinned by the unit test at `src/cmd/run.rs:579-582`, which changes here.

- The wake set is the driver-relevant kinds: `turn-ended`, `question`, `permission`, `plan`, `session-end` (`architecture.md:52`). `activity` never wakes `wait` (`architecture.md:172`). Neither do the wrapper's `wheel`, `budget-gate`, `send-issued`, `send-confirmed`, `send-refused` lines (`architecture.md:305`), nor `session-start` / `prompt-submitted` (absent from the set).

- `cursor` is the end offset of the returned event's line. It is the next `after`. `send`'s `ok` cursor is a valid `after` (architecture: "Every `send` `ok` payload and every `wait` event result carries `cursor`").

- **Already-logged events returned at once** (working entry): with `after`, `wait` returns the first driver-relevant event whose line STARTS at or after that byte offset, at once if it is already logged. So a turn that ends before the driver calls `wait` is never missed. Without `after`, it returns the next such event appended after the call.

- VERIFIED (research.md; architecture `:52`): `after` is a byte offset into `events.ndjson`. A mid-line `after` needs no reading of its own: the contract's "first driver-relevant event whose line STARTS at or after it" already skips the line it falls inside. An `after` past the file's end is still unpinned (no refusal detail, no clamp). That one is P4's, and a new detail is a §Conventions amendment at wrap.

- VERIFIED (research E3: `src/cmd/run.rs:104-105` answers `hook.dialog` `-32601`, and `HOOK_KINDS` holds no dialog kind): The dialog-pending rule ("a dialog already pending when `wait` is called without `after`, or with an `after` at or before that dialog's event line, is returned at once"; `architecture.md:52`) needs dialog events, which no code emits until `Dialog answers by dialog_id` (`working-route.md:78`). This chunk puts the dialog kinds in the wake filter. Whether the without-`after` pending-dialog return lands here (witnessable only with a hand-appended dialog line) or with `:78` is P4's call.

- Blocking: std threads and blocking I/O only — CLI `wait` is a blocking read on `viola-channel`'s sync client (architecture Tokio containment, `architecture.md:457`). VERIFIED (research E2): `viola-state` has no reader, tailing or notify. Every append that can wake a parked `wait` while its wrapper lives is made in the `run` process (`append_hook_event`, `src/run/send.rs:130-147`). The only out-of-process writer is the hook's direct SessionEnd (`src/cmd/hook.rs:227-236`), taken only when the channel did not take the event, so its wrapper is unreachable. The wake is therefore a signal on the wrapper's own append path, on the `SendSlot` Condvar + injected-clock precedent (`src/run/send.rs:44-124`). A timed re-read of the file is never the wake.
- The human always wins: a parked `wait` never blocks, refuses or delays a human keystroke (CLAUDE.md Critical Warnings).

title: 2. Typed timeout and unreachable on a vanished wrapper (working entry)

data.head: ### 2. Typed timeout and unreachable on a vanished wrapper (working entry)

body: - **Typed timeout:** with `timeout_ms`, `wait` returns `ok` with `{"timed_out":true}` when no driver-relevant event arrives in time (`architecture.md:52`). With no `timeout_ms` it blocks until one arrives. VERIFIED as open (no spec states a cap; research): Whether `timeout_ms` is bounded (a maximum, a zero) is open. The MCP default is an open item that must stay below the MCP client's tool-call timeout (`architecture.md:61`). MCP is not built here (§Boundaries).

- **Unreachable on a vanished wrapper:** if the endpoint vanishes while a caller is parked, the caller gets `instance-unreachable` — exit `21`, CLI `--json` `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":null}` (`architecture.md:147`, `:310`). VERIFIED (research E1): a wrapper that exits while a client is blocked in `Client::request` yields `ChannelError::Closed` (EOF, `crates/viola-channel/src/frame.rs:31-32`) or `Io` (reset). `send` already maps both to exit 21 `during:"call"` (`src/cmd/send.rs:267`), so no client change is needed for the exit. The client's own `channel-response` for that case reads `error` / `-32603` at ERROR (`client.rs:81`), which is not obs-plan §4's `outcome:"instance-unreachable"`.

- VERIFIED as a founder fork (security extract C1; security-plan-amendments `2026-10-04-confirmed-send-with-cl-1-records`, the fourth gap's no-borrow clause): The pre-connect liveness check reuses `send`'s founder-ratified fourth dated gap: a liveness-only pre-check (the snapshot's pid + start time alive, the heartbeat live, an `endpoint` present; else exit 21), with no server identity and no strict-modes, until Epoch 6 `:109` / `:111` (security.md, the fourth exception). That exception names CLI `viola send` only. Whether `wait` / `last` may ride it, or need their own Decisions Log entry, is a fork the wrap would halt on. P4 asks it against `.andromeda/playbook.md`'s escalate patterns.

title: 3. `last` — the newest turn's text (working entry + CARRY 1)

data.head: ### 3. `last` — the newest turn's text (working entry + CARRY 1)

body: - Surfaces: the CLI verb `viola last <target>` and the channel method `last` `{}` → `{last_assistant_message:<string|null>, ts:<string|null>}` (`architecture.md:277`).

- The value is the newest `turn-ended` event's `last_assistant_message` (`architecture.md:292`). The wrapper holds it in memory and rebuilds it from `events.ndjson` on start (`architecture.md:52`). Before any turn has ended, both fields are `null`.

- CARRY 1, verbatim: "chunk 2026-09-28-cli-output-tokens (P4 operator ruling: no code without a live consumer) left the message-mode escaper to this entry: over decoded `char`s every Unicode `Cc` (C0, DEL, C1 — `char::is_control`) prints as `\xHH` text, `\n` and `\t` kept, CR and DEL escaped; never a strip (security-plan §Input Validation; design-system Component Patterns 3); in `src/human.rs`".
  - Re-verified at P1: `src/human.rs` (302 lines) holds no escaper (its functions are the refusal, internal-error, result and send-mirror writers). security-plan `:425` names it: "Human-mode CLI output of `wait`/`last` … escapes C0/C1 controls (keeping `\n` and `\t`)". design-system has two `### Component Patterns` headings (`:530`, `:731`). Which one numbers the message-mode pattern as 3 is the design extract's to confirm.
  - Its live consumers are `last`'s human-mode message and `wait`'s human-mode event rendering. `--json` output stays serde-escaped JSON (the escaper is human mode only).

- Upstream text (`last_assistant_message`) is content, never a command or config (CLAUDE.md Critical Warnings). It reaches no codes-only log. User content goes only to `instances/<name>/diagnostics/detail-*.ndjson`.

title: 4. The `cli`-role panic line (CARRY 2; its own acceptance item, operator directive)

data.head: ### 4. The `cli`-role panic line (CARRY 2; its own acceptance item, operator directive)

body: - CARRY 2, verbatim: "chunk 2026-10-04-confirmed-send-with-cl-1-records (the overseer's wrap pre-direction: \"route the main.rs panic-line gap in send to the first chunk allowed to touch src/main.rs, as a named [inferred] item\"; this entry is the first after that chunk's held-boundary probe on `src/main.rs`): [inferred] the `cli` role's panic line — `src/main.rs` `role_of` files only `verify` as `Role::Cli`, so a panic inside `viola send` exits 1 with no `error: internal error` on stderr (obs-plan §7 Per-role behaviour; arch §Conventions exit `1`); the `Send` dispatch arm prints the line for an ordinary `Err` only. `wait` and `last` are `cli`-role verbs too".

- VERIFIED (graph: the two `internal_error` call sites above): Filing `send` / `wait` / `last` as `Role::Cli` alone would print `error: internal error` TWICE on an ordinary `send` `Err` (the arm's line, then the catch site's). So the fix moves the line to the one catch site. obs-plan §7: `cli` → `process-exit{detail:"internal-error"}` when an instance resolves, then exit 1 with exactly `error: internal error` (observability.md §Panics and errors).

- Acceptance (operator directive): a named acceptance criterion with a witness that cannot pass vacuously. A panic inside each of `send` / `wait` / `last` exits 1 with exactly one `error: internal error` line on stderr, and an ordinary dispatch `Err` prints it exactly once. [premise-corrected: the dispatch-`Err` half needs no seam — research E4 measured `viola --home <a regular file> send builder` → exit 1 with exactly one `error: internal error` on the 09:00Z harness build, so the same probe on `wait` / `last` / `send` is a real-binary once-only witness that cannot pass vacuously; only the PANIC half needs a forced panic] A real-binary PANIC witness needs a forced panic in a `cli` verb. The only panic seam is `FAKE_AGENT_HOOK_PANIC` (hook-only, `src/cmd/hook/seam.rs`), and "another seam … needs a Decisions Log entry" (security.md §Dependencies and CI). So the witness is either unit-level (the `role_of` / `exit_code` / `prints_internal_error` rstest tables at `src/main.rs:309-348`, extended to `send` / `wait` / `last`, plus a once-only assertion) or a new seam needing that entry. P4 decides, and asks if the lean is contestable.

body:
- (tests) The workflow drives only the harness verb `scripts/agent-run.ps1 run --mutants --package <member> --file …`,
  never a bare `cargo mutants` step (per test-plan §3 `run` step 4; architecture §CI/CD approach).

- (tests) The leak (`evidence/leak.md`). `.config/nextest.toml`'s only non-comment change is
  `terminate = "wait"`. One full Linux-host `run --mutants --package viola-e2e` in a fresh NOCOW `TMPDIR`
  then leaves 0 `.tmp*` dirs and 0 nested `cargo-mutants-*` copies. Its verdict reads `missed == 0`,
  `timeout == 0` and `unviable <= caught` over the measurable set (the two owed `scratch.rs` mutants are the
  only misses). The mechanism is fixed, with no sweep or cleanup step added anywhere (per test-plan §3 Test data
  bootstrap Cleanup; security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Code Patterns).

- (tests) Survivors outside the 34 from the first dispatch are listed by coordinate as Epoch 3 boundary-audit items,
  not killed in this chunk (per the C2 ruling: "its survivors become corrective-chunk items like any boundary survivor").

- (obs, security) In each of the six jobs' harness documents, the absolute-path probe (`D:\`, `C:\`, `/home/`)
  reads 0, and no step uploads anything (per obs-plan §8 item 6; security-plan §Bootstrap phases
  `secret-scanning-ci-gate`).

- (tests) `pre-push` reads `"ok":true` at `linux-tests`, and the final HEAD's CI run reads `verdict: green` on all
  three OSes. No `#[ignore]`, retry or skip is added (per test-plan §10 Zero-flakiness budget).
- (tests) `.claude/docs/commands.md` carries the dispatch and read recipe.

- No verification-matrix capability is linked: no `v1-*` acceptance is advanced by a dispatch-only mutation workflow
  (`matrix.py show --unclaimed`: v1-01 is the per-push pipeline, v1-07 the coverage/perf/fuzz gates).

- Graph impact:
  - `prepare` ← `mutate @ crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run/mutants.rs:207` and its test
    `@ crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run/mutants/scratch.rs:162`;
  - the graph is built for the Linux cfg, so `cfg(windows)` items have no `symbol` rows (research.md §Graph impact).

- P4 forks (AskUserQuestion round 1, answered by the overseer, founder-delegated):
  - selection: gated files per package ("a third of the cost, and the root contract guard covers 'later ones'
    mechanically");
  - job shape: per-package matrix, `fail-fast: false` ("'one long job' was my cost estimate, not part of the
    ruling").

- Leaned `terminate = "wait"` per the CARRY's acceptance ("the mechanism fixed rather than a cleanup step bolted on")
  and P3's two-sided witness (A 170 / B 0).

- Leaned not-a-widening per playbook.md:36 (the "Boundary widening" definition): the workflow adds no permission,
  secret, action pin, input class or upload. The C2 founder ruling is what created the dispatch-only mutation
  workflow. Showing it to the founder again is the wrap's locked-decision step (§Implementation notes).
- Leaned "links no capability" per `matrix.py show --id v1-01` / `--id v1-07`.

- Whole-package scoring (1 626 mutants, ≈ 2.3–5.7 h) — rejected at P4: three times the cost, plus host-excluded noise
  from shared bodies whose killing tests are `cfg(unix)`.

- One sequential job — rejected at P4: a red package must not hide the others, and each package's document gets its
  own log.

- Any artifact upload (`mutants.out/`, `outcomes.json`, the run archive, even a scanned summary) — rejected:
  - an unscanned mutation upload is a disclosure widening (security-plan §Bootstrap phases
    `secret-scanning-ci-gate`; obs-plan §8 item 6), which this autonomous night may only HOLD;
  - the job log already carries the repo-relative document.

- A `workflow_dispatch` `inputs:` selector (package, files) — rejected: a new event-payload input class on a CI
  boundary; the matrix covers every package on every dispatch.

- Keeping `terminate = "immediate"` on Windows only (where the scratch wipe bounds the leak) — rejected: one
  profile for every host; the slow-timeout kill already bounds the tail on both.

- `rust-cache` in the new workflow — rejected: `ci.yml` only (architecture §CI/CD approach); zizmor's cache-poisoning
  audit.

- A mutation entry in this chunk's `[[gate]]` block, or a pre-push mutation stage — rejected (the 2026-09-28 ruling;
  testing.md 2026-10-04).

- Reshaping any `cfg(windows)` body so a Linux test reaches its mutant, or out of cargo-mutants' generated set —
  rejected (testing.md 2026-09-28).

- A file list maintained by hand with no guard, or a per-file grep without the `mod`-line rule — rejected: either
  silently drops "later ones". The per-file grep alone misses `sideload.rs`, `server/win.rs` and `conpty.rs`, the
  ruling's named targets.

- **Forecasts, to be measured (step 8 records what the dispatch reads):**
  - mutants per job: viola-pty 79 · viola-channel 125 · viola-state 65 · viola-agent-claude 40 · viola 131 ·
    viola-e2e 68 = 508 (`cargo mutants --list --package <package> --file …`, research.md §Open questions);
  - job wall time ≤ ~35 min each: 131 × 12.6 s ≈ 28 min, plus the build; per-mutant cost 5.1–12.6 s from the
    retired windows-2025 leg's job logs 109057229416 / 109017403827 / 108660420086.
  - Step 1 lengthens every mutation run: each caught mutant now waits for its running tests (+5 s per mutant in P3's
    viola-e2e witness: 59 s → 106 s for 10 mutants). Predicted: step 5's full viola-e2e run takes longer than run 4's
    22 m 49 s. Record what it measures.

- **Equality step 1 rests on, re-derived at P3:** with `terminate = "wait"`, a caught mutant's run ends at
  max(remaining running tests) ≤ the kill line (10 s; viola-e2e 30 s), and that sits below cargo-mutants' test
  timeout (the 20 s floor; viola-e2e auto-set 105 s in run B's `Auto-set test timeout to 105s`). So no caught
  mutant is graded Timeout.
- **The graph cannot see Windows code.** Callers inside `cfg(windows)` items are read from source.

- **Expected amendments (wrap):**
  - architecture §Infrastructure Patterns → CI/CD approach (keyed `registries/contracts/architecture/ci-cd-approach.md`)
    — "two workflows" and "CI runs no mutation job" → name the dispatch-only, non-blocking `windows-mutants.yml`
    (founder C2), its matrix, its no-upload / no-cache form, and the CI check count it does not change;
  - architecture §Infrastructure Patterns → Project directory structure (`…/project-directory-structure.md`) — add
    `.github/workflows/windows-mutants.yml` and `tests/contract_windows_mutation_scope.rs`;
  - architecture §Occupied Resources — the `viola-mutants-scratch` row gains the runner's checkout parent; the
    `AGENT_RUN_CHUNK_BASE` row ("CI runs no mutation job and never sets it") is reworded so it stays true;
  - test-plan §9 Mutation row and §10 Mutation gate — the boundary audit's Windows leg is a manual dispatch of
    `windows-mutants.yml`, never a gate; the §9 tool-pin paragraph gains the new workflow's line, single-sourced by
    `contract_windows_mutation_scope`;
  - test-plan §3 `run` step 2 / Test data bootstrap Cleanup (`registries/contracts/test-plan/test-data-bootstrap.md`,
    `…/bootstrap-phases-derive-for-route-setup-project.md`) — `terminate = "immediate"` → `"wait"`, with the measured
    reason. This REVERSES the 2026-09-24 locked choice (the Timeout misgrade it answered is now bounded by the
    slow-timeout kill). Per playbook.md:30 it is not routine: the wrap escalates it once, naming the pattern ("a
    REVERSAL of a locked decision"). The owner the overseer named for the CARRY asked for this mechanism fix.
  - security-plan §Dependency Security (CI integration) — the workflow list gains the third file. The
    concurrency/least-privilege note ("CI runs no mutation job") is reworded. The unscanned-upload list stays exactly
    the nightly `fuzz/artifacts/`;
  - obs-plan §9 Mutation row and §9 Platform — name the dispatch workflow as the boundary run's Windows form.

**Chunk:** Windows boundary mutation workflow — cfg(windows) mutants scored on the windows-2025 runner by a dispatch-only, non-blocking workflow; the 34 owed coordinates graded; the mutation-run temp-dir leak
**Date:** 2026-10-04
**Commits:** `60c569b chore(2026-10-04-windows-boundary-mutation-workflow): operator pre-CI commit, for the run this chunk's verdict reads` (the only commit since `last_wrap` 2026-10-04T01:25:50Z besides the prior wrap `7aca558`)

- **Symbols / APIs:** no product symbol, IPC method, endpoint, port, socket or env var added or changed. Two new
  test-side and CI surfaces:
  - **The new GitHub Actions workflow `windows-mutants`** (`.github/workflows/windows-mutants.yml`).
    - Trigger: `on: workflow_dispatch` with no `inputs:` (the only trigger).
    - Permissions: workflow `permissions: {}`; job `mutants` with display name `mutants (${{ matrix.package }})`,
      `runs-on: windows-2025`, job `permissions: contents: read`, `timeout-minutes: 120`.
    - Strategy: `fail-fast: false`, six `matrix.include` items (`package` + one-line space-separated `files`):
      - viola-pty: `lib.rs`, `sideload.rs`;
      - viola-channel: `client.rs`, `endpoint.rs`, `server.rs`, `server/win.rs`, `test_support.rs`;
      - viola-state: `pin.rs`, `fs.rs`;
      - viola-agent-claude: `lib.rs`;
      - viola: `src/cmd/run.rs`, `src/run/env.rs`, `src/panic_frames.rs`, `src/main.rs`, `src/conpty.rs`;
      - viola-e2e: `harness/run/mutants/scratch.rs`, `harness/cleanup.rs`, `harness/run/browser.rs`.
    - Steps: checkout `3d3c42e5…` (v7.0.1, `persist-credentials: false`) → `rustup toolchain install` →
      install-action `7623a79c…` (v2.87.19) with `tool: cargo-nextest@0.9.146,cargo-mutants@27.1.0` → one
      `shell: pwsh` step reading `PACKAGE` / `FILES` from step `env:` (set from `matrix.*`) that runs
      `./scripts/agent-run.ps1 run --mutants --package $env:PACKAGE` with one `--file` per entry, then
      `if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }`.
    - Absent: no cache, `concurrency:`, `secrets.`, upload or `needs:`.
    - Its checks appear on the dispatched sha as `mutants (<package>)` × 6.
  - **The new root integration test binary `contract_windows_mutation_scope`** (sync, no new dependency,
    auto-discovered: no `[[test]]` entry, no `required-features`). Three tests:
    - `windows_gated_sources_equal_the_workflow_scope_both_ways`:
      - walks every `*.rs` under `src/` and `crates/*/src/`;
      - a file is gated by a product line (before the first column-0 `#[cfg(test)]`) carrying
        `cfg(windows` / `cfg(all(windows` / `cfg(any(windows` / `cfg!(windows)` / `target_os = "windows"`;
      - or by a gated `mod x;` line (resolved to `x.rs` / `x/mod.rs` beside `lib.rs` / `main.rs` / `mod.rs`, else
        under the declarer's stem dir), transitively through modules such a module declares;
      - asserts set equality with the workflow's matrix both ways, plus own-package membership.
    - `workflow_tool_pins_equal_the_ci_test_job_line`: the workflow's `tool:` pins (cargo-nextest, cargo-mutants)
      equal ci.yml's test-job line, the one `ci_pins` in `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/pre_push/linux.rs` also reads.
    - `workflow_trigger_is_dispatch_only_without_inputs`.
    - Each test runs synthetic known positives first.
- **Crates / modules:** none added, removed or changed.

- **Dependencies:** none — no `Cargo.toml` or `Cargo.lock` change (`git diff --quiet 7aca558 -- Cargo.toml Cargo.lock`:
  exit 0). The workflow installs cargo-nextest 0.9.146 and cargo-mutants 27.1.0, the existing ci.yml pins.

- **Schema / config:** `.config/nextest.toml` `[profile.mutants]`:
  - `fail-fast = { max-fail = 1, terminate = "immediate" }` → `{ max-fail = 1, terminate = "wait" }`, and the comment
    above it rewritten to the new reason;
  - `slow-timeout` 5 s × 2, the `package(viola-e2e)` override 15 s × 2 and `[profile.ci]` byte-unchanged (gate entry
    `git diff -U0 7aca558 -- .config/nextest.toml | … | grep -vc …`: last line 0).
- **Spec-master edits:** none (implement and the operator pass edit no master).

- **Counts / qualifiers moved:**
  - GitHub workflows: 2 → **3** (`ci.yml`, `nightly.yml`, `windows-mutants.yml`; `ls .github/workflows`). Stated as
    two at `registries/contracts/architecture/ci-cd-approach.md:2` ("two workflows"), test-plan.md:1153 ("Every

title: 3. The mutation-run temp-dir leak (CARRY 3 — [inferred] at the previous chunk, owner named at its wrap)

data.head: ### 3. The mutation-run temp-dir leak (CARRY 3 — [inferred] at the previous chunk, owner named at its wrap)

body:
- Mechanism, verbatim from the CARRY: "the mutants nextest profile terminates every running test at once on the first
  failure, so `TempDir` drops and the `Booted` guard never run — one viola-e2e boundary run left ~25k test temp dirs
  plus 62 nested `cargo-mutants-ws-*` copies in `TMPDIR` (pre-existing)." VERIFIED for the temp-dir half by a two-sided
  local witness (research.md §Measured facts): the same 10-mutant viola-e2e run left 170 `.tmp*` dirs under the
  committed `terminate = "immediate"` and 0 under `--max-fail=1:wait`, 10/10 caught on both sides, +5 s per caught
  mutant. Counts re-derived: 25 275 `.tmp*` + 62 `cargo-mutants-ws-*` in the scratch, all in the runs' time window.
  The nested-copy half: its producer is the two real-cargo-mutants self-tests (`mutants.rs:389-430`); not reproduced in
  the 10-mutant witness (0 on both sides), so the full-run witness below is what proves it.

- Acceptance (from the CARRY): a before/after count of `TMPDIR` across one boundary run reads no leftover test temp dir
  and no nested copy, with the mechanism fixed rather than a cleanup step bolted on.

- The boundary run that witnesses it is a Linux-host `run --mutants --package viola-e2e` run with a fresh NOCOW
  `TMPDIR`. VERIFIED as the right host: the leak was measured there; on Windows the harness's own scratch wipe before
  every run already bounds it to one run on an ephemeral runner.
- No change to `ci.yml`'s blocking jobs (the zizmor gate already covers a new workflow file).

- No mutation entry in this chunk's `[[gate]]` block and no `pre-push` leg (the 2026-09-28 ruling). The workflow's
  own dispatch is an operator act (it needs a push and a dispatch), not a gate.
- No reshaping of `cfg(windows)` code to let a Linux test reach a mutant (testing.md 2026-09-28).
- No Claude credential and no secret on any runner.
- No artifact upload from the new workflow (an unscanned mutation upload would be a disclosure widening).

- **Marker:** 2026-10-05-dialog-rows-and-re-probe · **Version:** viola-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-05T11:41Z
- **Base:** HEAD `75198e53b918` (every base-sha guard below reads against it)

- **Authority:** the founder's live rulings at this P4 (inputs#I3): M7 path A, the hook answers; live cap 16, both
  versions stamped; W3d + W6 split off to "Permission end to end". The playbook pattern "Boundary widening — what

The capability ledger gains its dialog tier. It adds four rows, each with a `viola verify` post-condition measured
live on the installed `claude`:
- `question-answer` (S3);
- `plan-approve-revise` (S7);
- `question-notes` (S8);
- `dialog-concurrency`.

They are measured by two new interactive runs beside Run A and Run B: Run C for dialogs and Run D for plan mode. In
both, the probe's own hook answers each dialog with a body the product's `dialog::decision_body` builds. viola never
types a key into a dialog (the founder's ruling, inputs#I3). The decision taking effect is read at the hook layer:
- a PermissionRequest that never comes;
- a PostToolUse that does come;
- a re-plan after a revise.

The prototype measured exactly this on 2.1.287 (inputs#I2, research M7), and 2.1.288's binary carries the path
(research M6). This chunk measures it with viola's own bodies.

The grown ledger closes the founder's R2 dated gap without a new contract. architecture [CLI Version Compatibility]
already says a version is verified only when every landed row passes, and that an unverified version withholds
dialog answers. So a non-`null` decision now needs the dialog rows. Run C and Run D record the first real dialog
fixtures for 2.1.288 and 2.1.287, which supersede the relayed set as measured truth. A new fake-agent argv mode
replays them, so CI stamps all fourteen rows without a credential. The `permission` end-to-end case and the
`tests/cli_answer.rs:9` reword go to "Permission end to end" (founder, P4).

Provenance: architecture [CLI Version Compatibility], [Hook Contract], [Plugin Scope]; security-plan §Data Protection
(interactive probe dirs, repository fixtures) and §Security Anti-Patterns → Universal (the stamp gate, R2);
test-plan §1, §5 `contract_ledger_probes.rs`, §7 Fixture hygiene and Fake agent, §11; obs-plan §4 Capability ledger,
§6, §10 exemption 5; design-system §Surface: cli Component Patterns 5; layout-templates §Output structure —
`viola verify`; a11y-plan §4 P6.

1. **The rows and the probe's compiled inputs** (`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs`).
   - `LedgerRow` gains `QuestionAnswer` / `question-answer` ("a question answered through PreToolUse takes effect"),
     `PlanApproveRevise` / `plan-approve-revise` ("a plan revise and approve each take effect"), `QuestionNotes` /
     `question-notes` ("free text and notes reach the question") and `DialogConcurrency` / `dialog-concurrency`
     ("two parallel questions each raise a dialog").
   - `ALL` becomes `[Self; 14]`, in that order after `ConfirmWindow`.
   - Compiled ASCII prompts with no tag characters:
     - `DIALOG_PROMPT_QUESTIONS`: one AskUserQuestion call carrying two questions, each with two named options;
     - `DIALOG_PROMPT_PARALLEL`: two AskUserQuestion calls in one message;
     - `DIALOG_PROMPT_PERMISSION`: run exactly `touch viola-probe-permission`;
     - `PLAN_PROMPT`: plan only, present the plan with ExitPlanMode, and on a send-back revise once and present again.
   - Two more compiled values:
     - the `--settings` JSON literal of step 0;
     - a closed `ProbeAnswer` enum: `QuestionsFirstAndFreeText`, `QuestionFirstOption`, `PlanRevise`,
       `PlanApprove`, `PermitAllow`. Each has a kebab id, the compiled free text, the compiled note text and the
       compiled revise message.
   - A compiled answer table maps (run, event, ordinal of that event in the run) to a `ProbeAnswer`:
     - Run C: PreToolUse 1 → `QuestionsFirstAndFreeText`, PreToolUse 2 and 3 → `QuestionFirstOption`,
       PermissionRequest 1 → `PermitAllow`;
     - Run D: PreToolUse 1 → none, PermissionRequest 1 → `PlanRevise`, PreToolUse 2 → `PlanApprove`.
   - A pure `probe_body(event, payload: &[u8], answer) -> Option<String>`:
     - it reads the payload's `tool_input`;
     - it builds the `dialog::Response` the answer names, keyed by the payload's own question texts;
     - it returns `dialog::decision_body(event, input, &response)`, the product's mapping, never a second one.
   - `capture_plugin_files` takes the plugin's kind:
     - spine only (print probe, Run B: today's four events);
     - dialog (Run C, Run D): the four spine events, PreToolUse with the matcher `AskUserQuestion|ExitPlanMode`,
       PermissionRequest, and PostToolUse, each in exec form. The two dialog events carry `--answers <answers dir>`
       after `--capture <dir>`.

2. **The checks** (`ledger.rs`).
   - `Probes` gains `dialogs: DialogRuns { questions: Vec<Capture>, plan: Vec<Capture> }`, the Run C and Run D
     captures in claim order.
   - `check` gains four arms, written against step 0's recorded shapes (`evidence/step0-dialog-shapes.md`):
     - `question-answer`: Run C's PreToolUse 1 has a PostToolUse with its `tool_use_id`. That PostToolUse carries the
       first question's first option label. Run C holds no PermissionRequest whose `tool_name` is AskUserQuestion.
     - `question-notes`: that PostToolUse carries the compiled free text and the compiled note text.
     - `plan-approve-revise`: Run D's captures read, in claim order:
       - PreToolUse(ExitPlanMode) 1;
       - PermissionRequest(ExitPlanMode) 1;
       - PreToolUse(ExitPlanMode) 2;
       - then a PostToolUse(ExitPlanMode) with PreToolUse 2's `tool_use_id`, and no PermissionRequest(ExitPlanMode)
         after PreToolUse 2.
     - `dialog-concurrency`: Run C holds two PreToolUse(AskUserQuestion) captures from the parallel prompt with
       distinct `tool_use_id`s, each followed by its own PostToolUse.
   - A run that raised no dialog fails its rows. Absence is never a pass.
   - `merge_stamp` adds `measured.dialog_probe.parallel_both_before_first_post` (a bool, or null when not measured):
     whether both parallel PreToolUse captures were claimed before either PostToolUse. `run` reads no field of it.

3. **Exclusive capture naming** (`crates/viola-state/src/fs.rs`, `src/cmd/hook.rs`).
   - Add a viola-state helper that creates a file exclusively at `FILE_MODE` and fails on an existing name.
   - `capture` claims `<Event>.<k>.json` through it, taking the next `k` on a lost race, then writes the bytes with
     `replace_private` over its own claim.
   - Two concurrent captures can no longer share a `k`. Claim order is the order the checks read.
   - **Red-before-green control** (the operator's direction at P5). The claim becomes its own function taking a
     starting `k`. The unit test `capture_two_claims_racing_for_one_k_keep_both_payloads` forces the race open
     deterministically: both captures compute the same `k` before either claims. It never samples timing
     (testing.md 2026-09-27).
     - Run it first against HEAD's naming (`free_k` then `replace_private`). It must read RED: the second payload
       replaces the first under one name.
     - Then run it against the exclusive claim. It must read GREEN: both payloads are kept, under `k` and `k + 1`.
     - Record both readings in `evidence/capture-race.md`. The test then rides entry 3's `cmd::hook::tests::`
       filter.

5. **Run C and Run D** (`src/cmd/verify/typed.rs`, `src/cmd/verify.rs`).
   - `ProbeDir` builds two more roots, each with a dialog-kind `plugin/`, `captures/` and an `answers/` dir:
     - `questions/`: Run C's answer files;
     - `plan/`: Run D's answer files.
     The answer files are written from the compiled table before the spawn.
   - `typed::measure` gains Run C and Run D after Run B, each a direct spawn under the same R8 strip at 80×24 with the
     same `MAX_FRAME`-capped `Screen` feed.
   - Run C runs in `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>-dialogs/`. It passes `--model haiku`, the `--settings` literal and the
     dialog plugin. It pastes `DIALOG_PROMPT_QUESTIONS`, waits for its Stop capture, pastes `DIALOG_PROMPT_PARALLEL`,
     waits for its Stop, pastes `DIALOG_PROMPT_PERMISSION`, and waits for its Stop.
   - Run D runs in `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>-plan/` with `--model haiku --permission-mode plan`. It pastes
     `PLAN_PROMPT` and waits for the ExitPlanMode PostToolUse capture.
   - Both dirs are 0700 with a drop guard, and both are under the existing `/.viola-verify-*/` ignore.
   - Each wait is bounded by `PROBE_DEADLINE`. A start that shows a modal is killed with no key, as in Run B.
   - Both runs are ended by a kill, never Ctrl-C. A key must never reach a dialog that may be up.
   - Each spawn is logged as a `verify-pty-probe` pair, the existing subject, so there is no schema change: verify now
     logs six spawn pairs.

6. **`--record` for the dialog tier** (`src/cmd/verify.rs`). Only when 0 rows fail:
   - each Run C / Run D capture is scrubbed through `ledger::scrub` and `unclean`, and written as
     `<Event>.<variant>.json`. The variant comes from the compiled table: `questions-1`, `parallel-1`, `parallel-2`,
     `permission-1`, `plan-1` (the PreToolUse and its PermissionRequest), `plan-2`. A PostToolUse takes its
     PreToolUse's variant.
   - A dirty payload refuses the whole recording, naming the file and the closed code, never the content.
   - The relayed 2.1.287 files and every other existing file keep their bytes (the preservation guard).

7. **The fake agent's dialog replay** (`src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs`; an argv flag, never an env seam).
   - Add `--dialogs`. In a trusted interactive run it acts on the pasted prompts:
     - `DIALOG_PROMPT_QUESTIONS`, `_PARALLEL` and `_PERMISSION` fire UserPromptSubmit, then each recorded variant of
       that prompt in claim order, then Stop;
     - `PLAN_PROMPT` fires the `plan-*` variants.
   - For each PreToolUse / PermissionRequest it reads the hook's stdout:
     - a body → it fires the PostToolUse of that variant;
     - none → it fires that variant's PermissionRequest (Run D's `plan-1`);
     - none, with no PermissionRequest fixture → it fires nothing more for the call.
   - It reuses the compiled prompts and variant table from `viola_agent_claude::ledger`.
   - The receipt's `hook` lines keep `stdin_hex` and `stdout_hex` (the drift contract).

8. **Test-side homes and literals.** These are row literals, never `LedgerRow::ALL`. The 37 hits come from
   `grep -c -E '/10\]|10 pass|"/10"|LEDGER_ROWS'` (research M11).
   - `tests/support/` passes `--dialogs` beside `--screens --turn-stop --trusted-root` in `stamped_home`.
   - The harness `boot` step 4 does the same (`crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/boot.rs`). `supervise.rs`'s wrapped
     sessions do not take it, because only verify needs the replay.
   - `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run.rs:333` `LEDGER_ROWS` grows to `[&str; 14]`.
   - `tests/cli_verify.rs` and `tests/contract_ledger_probes.rs` move to `/14` and `14 pass  0 fail`.
   - `src/cmd/verify.rs`'s `step_line` test moves its `/10` cases.

9. **The R2 closure's witnesses** (`tests/cli_answer.rs`, `tests/cli_verify.rs`, `src/run/version_gate.rs` tests).
   - A home stamped by `viola verify` against the fake agent WITHOUT `--dialogs` stamps `10 pass  4 fail`.
   - On that home, `run` records `cli_verified:false`, a `hook.dialog` is answered `null`, and `viola answer` exits
     12 `{"refusal":"unverified-cli"}` with empty hook stdout.
   - The same flow on a `--dialogs` home emits the body.
   - `version_gate`'s unit tests cover a ten-row stamp, one with all fourteen rows passing and one with a failing
     dialog row.

10. **Fixtures and their contracts.**
    - `tests/contract_fixture_hygiene.rs` walks the new dialog variants, including a planted red: an absolute path
      inside a nested `tool_input` string.
    - `tests/contract_fake_agent_drift.rs` compares the replayed dialog receipts byte for byte with the recorded
      files.
    - `fixtures/claude/2.1.287/RELAYED.md` gains a dated "Superseded" section naming each relayed file's recorded
      counterpart, or naming none: a hook-answered AskUserQuestion raises no PermissionRequest. The relayed files stay
      for Path 4's existing cases.

11. **The live record runs (10 sessions, rows 3-12 of the session ledger).** Run the two `build`/`live` entries
    below:
    - 2.1.288: print, Run A, Run B, Run C, Run D;
    - then 2.1.287: the same five.
    Copy each set's new dialog files into `fixtures/claude/<ver>/`. A red STOPs the round with the spare count stated.
    The STOP quotes every `[NN/14] <row-id> … fail` step line of the run, so the failed row is named (one verdict
    unverifies the whole version — the operator's P5 direction). There is no retry without the operator's word (the
    cap is 16: 12 planned, 4 spare).
- derived `fixtures/claude/2.1.288/*.json` by `viola verify --record` — the dialog variants of step 6
- derived `fixtures/claude/2.1.287/*.json` by `viola verify --record` — the same at 2.1.287

- `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-05-dialog-rows-and-re-probe/evidence/` — `live-sessions.md`, `step0-dialog-shapes.md`,
  `capture-race.md`
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs` — rows, prompts, `ProbeAnswer`, `probe_body`, dialog plugin, checks
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/dialog.rs` — only a body step 0 or the record run forces (else untouched)
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/snapshots/` — only with a body change
- `crates/viola-state/src/fs.rs` — the exclusive create helper
- `src/cmd/hook.rs` — exclusive claim, `--answers`
- `src/cmd/verify.rs` — the dialog roots, record of the dialog tier, `step_line` tests
- `src/cmd/verify/typed.rs` — Run C, Run D
- `src/run/version_gate.rs` — tests only (the verdict code already reads every row, research M4)
- `src/cmd/run.rs` — none expected (research M4); listed for an `#[instrument]` field change if one is forced
- `src/run/dialog.rs` — none expected; listed as the gate's consumer
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs` — `--dialogs`
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run.rs` — `LEDGER_ROWS`
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/boot.rs` — step 4's `--dialogs`

- `tests/cli_verify.rs`, `tests/contract_ledger_probes.rs`, `tests/cli_answer.rs`, `tests/contract_fixture_hygiene.rs`,
  `tests/contract_fake_agent_drift.rs`, `tests/support/`
- `fixtures/claude/2.1.287/RELAYED.md` — the superseded section

`/implement` runs the entries below in order. The `leg = 'live'` entries spend founder-capped sessions: 5 each,
written into `evidence/live-sessions.md` before they start. Their non-priming probe is `claude --version` (no API
call). Step 0 is not a gate entry. It is a scratch measurement whose evidence the plan's checks are written against,
2 sessions. `evidence/live-sessions.md` has no producing entry by construction: it is the session ledger
`/implement` writes by hand, one row before each live session starts (the previous chunk's form). The two `live`
entries' sessions are its rows 3-12.
