title: M7 — what the gate does with a quiet screen that holds no literal

data.head: ### M7 — what the gate does with a quiet screen that holds no literal

body:
- `Screen::verdict` (`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/screen.rs:122-152`): while the screen is not quiet it waits,
  up to `GATE_MAX_WAIT` from the start of the wait (`:131-135`). Once the screen has been quiet for `QUIET_PERIOD`
  (300 ms) it decides at once: no signature set, `Ready` (`:137-139`); a modal literal, `InputNotReady` (`:142-144`);
  an input-box literal, `Ready`; neither, `InputNotReady` (`:147-151`).

- The equality the W2 hypothesis needs — a verified gate, a quiet screen, no `for agents` row, no modal row, gives
  `InputNotReady` — is pinned at unit level already: `wait_ready_verified_over_the_input_box_is_ready`
  (`src/run/gate.rs:557-568`) asserts it for a screen holding only `thinking`, 300 ms after its last byte.
- `send` types nothing on that verdict and records `send-refused` with no cursor (`src/run/send.rs:264-267`).

- So on a verified CLI a `send` issued while the paste hint stands is refused about 300 ms after the screen goes
  quiet. The 5 s maximum is not reached and plays no part. Raising it alone changes nothing for this case.

- verify's own settle differs by design: `settled` waits out `GATE_MAX_WAIT` on a quiet literal-less screen
  (`src/cmd/verify/typed.rs:477-487`), and `box_wait` keeps waiting past it (`:502-505`).

- The driver-facing side: the hint printed for `input-not-ready` is "`<name>` was not ready for input; viola wait
  `<name>`, then send again" (`src/human.rs:208-210`). In the hint window the turn has already ended, so a `wait`
  has no later event to wake on.

title: M8 — the paste-hint hold reaches a `send` test as it stands

data.head: ### M8 — the paste-hint hold reaches a `send` test as it stands

body:
- `--paste-hint-ms` acts inside the agent's `submit`: for the compiled long text under `--framing`, with
  `--turn-stop`, the agent fires the recorded UserPromptSubmit and the Stop, clears the screen, sleeps the hold, then
  draws the `turn` screen (`src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs:460-475`). It does not matter who pasted the text.

- `tests/cli_send.rs` already sends that text under `--framing`: `send_long_text_wrapped_by_the_cli_is_confirmed`
  takes it from the recorded `paste-1` variant (`:493-510`).

- On a `stamped_home` wrapper with `--framing --turn-stop --paste-hint-ms <n>`: the first send is confirmed, the
  Stop ends the turn, and a second send issued inside the hold meets a quiet cleared screen. No new option is needed.

- The agent sleeps on its stdin thread, so it reads no key during the hold and `Wrapper::stop` returns only after
  it. A test's length is the stamp, the boot and the hold.

- Bounds a new case lives under: `binary(cli_send)` is killed at 10 s × 2 in `[profile.ci]`
  (`.config/nextest.toml:29-31`); the `send_window_` prefix buys 15 s × 2 under `[profile.mutants]` only (`:48-50`).

body:
- **`SendSlot::new`** (`src/run/send.rs`) — 17 call sites: `start` @ `src/cmd/run.rs:216`, `methods` @

  `new` defined in that file also hold the test helper `Pastes::new`; every row is in those two files. A new
  parameter stays inside them.

- **`append_hook_event`** — 16 rows: `Methods::dispatch` @ `src/cmd/run.rs:117`, the other 15 unit tests in
  `src/run/send.rs`. Its signature need not change: the slot it already takes carries the new state.

- **`send`** (`src/run/send.rs`) — 15 rows: `Methods::dispatch_call` @ `src/cmd/run.rs:125`, the other 14 unit
  tests in the same file. Its signature need not change.

- **`read_back`** — 1 caller, `deliver` @ `src/cmd/send.rs:200`. **`write_read_back`** — `Out::read_back` @

  send claimed before the line is appended and settles it with the appended line's `ts`, so the confirming line
  always precedes the outcome record. A post-condition confirmation is the same three steps on another kind.

new-session post-condition.

title: Plan — 2026-10-07-a-send-ending-in-a-newline-is-confirmed: "A send ending in a newline is confirmed"

data.head: # Plan — 2026-10-07-a-send-ending-in-a-newline-is-confirmed: "A send ending in a newline is confirmed"

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-10-07-a-send-ending-in-a-newline-is-confirmed · **Version:** viola-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-07T14:03Z · **Revised:** 2026-10-07T14:43Z

- **Revision:** `/andromeda-implement` stopped on the take-up plan with nothing pushed (`inputs#I7`). Step 7 is
  now the step as built, the census counts one whole profile a run, and steps 6 to 8 and the census entry read
  what was measured. Nothing else moved. Implement re-enters at step 6's remaining part. At the review the
  operator added a planted control for the revised rule's failing side (`inputs#I8`, steps 6 and 8).

A `send` whose text ends in a newline is typed, delivered and runs a turn today, and is still reported
`not-delivered` / `no-prompt-submitted` after the 10 s window, with its own prompt filed `human` and the wheel
moved to the human. The cause is measured: the `claude` CLI drops a pasted text's last newline before
UserPromptSubmit, so the prompt is one byte short of the text the wrapper compares it with (scope items 8 and 10).

This chunk builds the remedy chosen on the P4 card (`inputs#I2`): `send` validates the text as received and then
types it without its trailing newlines. Classification, the paste and the claim all read that one typed text, and
the claim stays an exact match (per architecture §Established Decisions → [Delivery Confirmation]; security-plan
§Input Validation, Paste text row). The answer is the overseer's, PROVISIONAL for the founder, who is away: it is
his contract, and it is listed for him below with every option.

The chunk also closes the CI red on `9f2bebe` (ci#37627485806 attempt 1), folded on the operator's word
(`inputs#I1`). Its mechanism is measured at HEAD: a root-bin unit test killed its own instrumented child while
that child could be writing its coverage profile. The test's child becomes a host program that writes no
profile (`inputs#I5`), and a counted witness is added. The closure has one stated limit: the mechanism is
measured, and pid 10799's identity is not provable from the run.
No live `claude` session is started and no capability is claimed (`inputs#I1`).

Steps 1 to 5 are the send. Steps 6 to 9 are the red. Steps 1 to 5, 7 and 9 are done and their evidence is
named; step 6 is done but for its rule; step 8 is not done. **Implement re-enters at step 6's remaining part.**
The line coordinates in steps 1 to 5 are the take-up's.

1. **The rule, in the agent crate.** In `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/hook.rs`, beside `prompt_text`, one public
   function, `typed_text`, takes a sent text and returns it without its trailing LF characters. It removes
   nothing else: not a CR, a TAB or a space, and no newline that is not at the very end. Its doc comment says why
   it exists, that the width is every trailing LF by the P4 card, and that the answer is provisional.
   - Unit cases beside it: one rstest table of exactly nine cases with literal oracles, in one test function
     whose name carries `trailing_newline`. Nine tests by the filter's count.
   - **Done.** `hook.rs:203`; the table at `:667`. The test module already held a strategy named `typed_text`,
     so the table calls `super::typed_text` (`evidence/newline-red-green.md`).

2. **`send` takes the typed text once.** In `src/run/send.rs`, `send`: `validate_paste_text` runs first, on the
   text as received; directly after it the typed text is taken through `typed_text`, and from there on it is the
   only text `send` uses: `classify`, the in-flight text the claim compares, the length handed to `ctx.issue` and
   the paste. `SendSlot::claim` is not changed. The module doc says the text is typed without its trailing
   newlines.
   - **Done.** `send.rs:321`.

3. **Unit cases in `src/run/send.rs`**: exactly seven tests, every test function's name carrying
   `trailing_newline`, and no other test in the workspace carrying it. With step 1's nine that is sixteen tests
   by the filter's count: two confirmed cases (one LF, two); a refused control character before a newline;
   `/clear` and a newline on a verified slot, confirmed by its new session; the second listed command and a
   newline, `unconfirmable` at once; the one existing pin that turned (`/clear` and a newline on the unverified
   slot is the listed command, typed as `/clear` and answered `unconfirmable`); and the negative control (a
   prompt that still carries the newline claims nothing).
   - **Done.** `send.rs:924`, `:930`, `:948`, `:1525`, `:1548`, `:1568`. The confirmed harness runs on a clock
     that jumps once the hook's line is on disk, so an unconfirmed send expires and no case parks. Six cases
     read red before step 2, each on the pasted value; the control-character case cannot be read red that way
     and is recorded so (`evidence/newline-red-green.md`).

4. **The cross-process case** in `tests/cli_send.rs`, named `send_text_ending_in_newlines_is_typed_without_them_and_confirmed`,
   booted over `PATH3`, one rstest case for one trailing LF and one for two: exactly two tests by the filter's
   count. It reads the `--json` document, the records after the pre-send offset, the fake agent's receipt (the
   one `prompt` line's `text` is the typed text and its `hex` does not end in `0a`), the role file's
   `text_bytes`, the canary's absence, and a second send in human mode that is not refused `human-typing`.
   - **Done.** `cli_send.rs:286`. Both cases read red before step 2 at the receipt's bytes. The second send
     also ends in the same newlines, so the `[RB] read back` criterion is true as written
     (`evidence/newline-red-green.md`).

5. **The pins that stay.** `long_ending_newline` and `short_ending_newline` in `hook.rs` are not edited.
   - **Done** (nothing to do): the guard entry reads them unchanged with the rest of the file's existing cases.

6. **The witness script.** `scripts/profraw-census.sh <runs> <workers>`:
   - it finds the newest executable `target/llvm-cov-target/debug/deps/viola-*` whose `--list` names
     `cmd::run::tests::start_opens_the_scenario_one_spans_under_run_start`; with none it prints
     `profraw-census: no instrumented binary` and exits 2;
   - it runs that one test `<runs>` times over `<workers>` concurrent loops, each run with its own
     `LLVM_PROFILE_FILE` prefix under a directory it makes, `target/profraw-census/<UTC stamp>-<pid>/`;
   - after each run it counts that run's profiles and their sizes, then removes that run's profiles;
   - a profile is short when it is smaller than the largest profile the census saw;
   - its first line of output names the runs and the workers; its last line is `profraw-census: runs N · passed
     N · profiles P · third K · short S`.
   - Before every census run, write the operator one line: that it starts, with how many workers, and for how
     long (about 2.5 minutes for `4800 48`). A notice, not a question.
   - **Done:** the script (84 lines), under the take-up's rule: two whole profiles a run, a `third` when a run
     left more than two, exit 0 only when P is twice N. Its reading on the untouched test is the census's red
     side and stands as recorded (`inputs#I7`): `bash scripts/profraw-census.sh 4800 48` on the instrumented
     binary of `9f2bebe` → exit 1, wall 136.6 s, `runs 4800 · passed 4800 · profiles 9603 · third 3 · short 3`;
     the three third profiles are 0 B, 73 728 B and 124 288 B against a whole 128 264 B
     (`evidence/profraw-red-green.md`). The untouched test is not rebuilt for a second red reading.
   - **Remaining — the re-entry point.** The rule becomes one whole profile a run, which is what the fixed test
     leaves (step 7). In `scripts/profraw-census.sh`: a run counts under `third` when it left more than one
     profile (`:73`); the script exits 0 only when every run passed, P equals N, and K and S are 0 (`:80`); any
     other count is exit 1; the header comment says a clean run leaves one profile, the test process's own,
     because neither the wrapper's child nor the version probe's child is instrumented. The line keeps its
     words: `third` now names a profile beyond the one a clean run leaves (`inputs#I8`).
   - **Remaining — one more word, for the planted control of step 8** (`inputs#I8`). The script takes an
     optional third word, a name: `profraw-census.sh <runs> <workers> [<name>]`. With it the census directory
     is `target/profraw-census/<name>/` and may already exist; without it the directory is the stamped one as
     today. A name that is not one path segment of letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-` is a usage error, exit 2.
     Nothing else in the script changes. Why the word is needed: the script counts a run's profiles in its own
     worker directory straight after the run (`:51`) and removes them (`:53`), and today only the script knows
     that directory's name (`:21`), so nothing can be planted in it.

7. **The test's child writes no coverage profile.** In `src/cmd/run.rs`,
   `start_opens_the_scenario_one_spans_under_run_start`, the program is the host program `whoami`, not the test
   binary with `--list`. It refuses the wrapper's plugin flag and exits by itself, as the old child did, but it
   is not instrumented, so no kill can land in a profile write. Every span assertion stays as it is.
   - **Done** (`run.rs:926-935`), on the step 7 card (`inputs#I5`); the deviation from the take-up's step is in
     `scope-record.md` with the overseer's word. Why the take-up's design could not be built: the wrapper puts
     `--plugin-dir <dir>` first in a child's arguments (`src/run/mod.rs:124-128`), and the test binary refuses
     it, `error: Unrecognized option: 'plugin-dir'`, exit 101, before any test body runs. The old child
     therefore never listed anything: it exited 101 at once, which is why a kill could land in its exit-time
     write. `grep -c '"--list"' src/cmd/run.rs` reads 0 (`evidence/profraw-red-green.md`).

8. **The census after the fix.** Not done. After step 6's remaining part, on the instrumented binary `pre-push`
   has built from the final tree:
   - the must-pass control first, `bash scripts/profraw-census.sh 48 1`, which must end `runs 48 · passed 48 ·
     profiles 48 · third 0 · short 0` with exit 0. Measured under the old rule at implement: that same line,
     every run one profile of 129 512 B, exit 1 only because the script expected two a run;
   - then the planted control, the revised rule's own failing side, two one-run censuses with no rebuild
     (`inputs#I8`). For each, make a census directory under a name not used before and plant one file in its
     first worker's directory, `target/profraw-census/<name>/w0/r0-plant.profraw`, then run `bash
     scripts/profraw-census.sh 1 1 <name>`. The script reads sizes only, so a plant is a file of zeros of a chosen
     size (`truncate -s`):
     - the extra plant is exactly a whole profile's size, the size the must-pass control's tally shows. It must
       read exit 1 with the last line `profraw-census: runs 1 · passed 1 · profiles 2 · third 1 · short 0`;
     - the short plant is 1 000 bytes. It must read exit 1 with the last line `profraw-census: runs 1 · passed
       1 · profiles 2 · third 1 · short 1`. A short plant is also one file too many, so `third` reads 1 here as
       well; the size rule's own reading is `short 1` against the extra plant's `short 0`;
     - the script removes a run's profiles after counting them, the plant with them. Check the removal: no
       `.profraw` file is left under either planted directory. The two directories keep their tallies and stay
       with the other census directories under `target/`;
   - then the census entry. Predicted: `runs 4800 · passed 4800 · profiles 4800 · third 0 · short 0` — record
     what the run measures. One profile a run is measured at 48 runs one at a time, and at 4 800 loaded runs by
     the revision's baseline read of the entry (the entry's `baseline`).
   - Record every reading in `evidence/profraw-red-green.md` under the readings it holds, each with its wall
     time. The notice of step 6 goes before each run, the one-run ones included.

9. **The record of attempt 1.** `evidence/ci-attempt-1.md`, from the run itself while its artifacts stand (they
   expire 2026-10-14), each figure with the command that read it, and the limit of the closure in one sentence.
   - **Done.** The reader is kept as `evidence/guards/read-attempt1.py`.
- `scripts/profraw-census.sh` — the counted witness of step 6 (written; its rule changes at the re-entry)

- `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-a-send-ending-in-a-newline-is-confirmed/evidence/` — `newline-red-green.md`, `profraw-red-green.md`, `ci-attempt-1.md`, `guards/read-attempt1.py` (written; step 8 adds to the second)
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/hook.rs` — `typed_text` and its table (step 1, done)

- `src/run/send.rs` — the typed text taken once after validation; the module doc; the unit cases (steps 2, 3,
  done). `SendSlot::claim` has one caller, `append_hook_event @ src/run/send.rs:219` (take-up coordinate), and
  is not changed
- `tests/cli_send.rs` — the cross-process case (step 4, done)
- `src/cmd/run.rs` — the changed test (step 7, done)

The gates are the standing lint, unit and default-selection entries, two filter entries that select only this
chunk's new cases, two census reads, the preservation guard, the harness smoke with G2 and G4 over its home, the
native `pre-push`, the profile census, and the operator's push and CI reads.

No live leg: the chunk starts no `claude` process (`inputs#I1`). What stays unmeasured on a live CLI is in the
Implementation notes and is carried to "First live test and self-drive".

Three red-first readings were one-shot runs at implement and not entries, because each needs the tree in a state
the finished chunk no longer has: step 3's cases before step 2, step 4's case before step 2, and step 6's census
on the untouched test. Their records are in `evidence/`. No mutation entry is listed (the mutation run is the
epoch boundary's).

The census script is an instrument this chunk builds, so its two known-verdict controls are one-shot runs at
implement, read into `evidence/profraw-red-green.md` before its graded use. The must-fail reading is step 6's
census on the untouched test, read through the script under the two-a-run rule it then held. The must-pass
reading is `bash scripts/profraw-census.sh 48 1` after step 6's remaining part, on the instrumented binary
`pre-push` has built, 48 runs one at a time, which must end `runs 48 · passed 48 · profiles 48 · third 0 ·
short 0`. The untouched test is not rebuilt (`inputs#I7`), so the revised rule gets its own failing side as a
planted control (`inputs#I8`, step 8): one census run given one extra profile file and one given a short file,
each of which must read exit 1, with `third 1 · short 0` and with `third 1 · short 1`. The plants are gone
after the runs and their removal is checked. All of these are one-shot runs and not entries: the planted
control writes files into a census directory before the script runs, and an entry is one statement the wrap's
light gate re-runs verbatim.

The census loads the host. `4800 48` runs 48 workers at once on a 32-core host that four other builders share
(the operator's word at the review, `inputs#I3`), for about 2.5 minutes: 4 800 runs at 48 workers took 136.6 s
(measured at implement, `evidence/profraw-red-green.md`).
Before each census run, at any size and by whoever fires it (implement, the operator pass, the wrap's light
gate), one line is written to the operator saying that it starts and for how long. It is a notice, not a
question: the run follows it without waiting for an answer. The script's own first line of output names the runs
and the workers.

The census entry stands after `pre-push`, whose coverage run rebuilds the instrumented binary it reads. Its
profile path is an assignment inside its own script, not in the `pre-push` launcher. Implement fires the block
up to and including `pre-push`, then the must-pass control, then the planted control, then the census entry, so
the controls are read before the graded use. A census red that is not of the `third` or `short` shape (a run that failed, a profile
count that is not one a run) is a finding and is recorded as read; it is never re-run for a green.
The preservation guard names the base commit, because the operator pass's pre-CI commit moves HEAD onto the chunk.
No push goes out while an entry of this block is red by its own letter (`inputs#I6`).

body:
- (arch) For a sent text whose last byte is a newline, `events.ndjson` holds `send-issued`, then that send's
  `prompt-submitted` with `origin:"driver"`, then `send-confirmed`, in that order, and the result is `ok`
  `{submitted_at, cursor}` with `submitted_at` equal to that prompt line's `ts`: steps 3 and 4 (per architecture
  §Established Decisions → [Delivery Confirmation]; §Standard Contracts → Channel methods).

- (arch, a11y) That send appends no `wheel` record, the holder stays `driver`, and a following `send` is not
  refused `human-typing`; a prompt that is not the in-flight send's typed text is appended as the hook filed it,
  and `send_an_unsent_human_prompt_takes_the_wheel_before_its_line_and_a_harness_one_does_not` passes unchanged
  (per architecture §Established Decisions → [Human Takeover / Wheel]; a11y-plan §4 ARIA Patterns & Roles, P4).

- (arch) The rule for a sent text's trailing newlines is defined in `viola-agent-claude` and only read by
  `src/run/send.rs`; no crate gains a dependency edge; the ledger stays the closed seventeen-row set and no stamp
  is written: the guard entry `git diff --quiet 9f2bebe5102b -- …` (per architecture §Infrastructure Patterns →
  Crate dependency direction; §Cross-cutting Patterns → Capability ledger as the single gate).

- (security) A text that ends in a newline and holds a refused control character is still refused
  `not-delivered` / `control-character` with nothing typed, first in the wrapper's order: step 3 (per
  security-plan §Input Validation, Paste text row).

- (security) A `prompt-submitted` text that differs from the typed text is filed by its hook `origin`, not
  `driver`, and the send is not confirmed: step 3's negative control (per security-plan §Threat Model Summary,
  Attack surface, CLI input vector).

- (security, arch) The chunk adds no environment read in a product crate, no CLI flag, no `config.json` key, no
  event kind, no channel method and no write to `ledger/stamps.json`: the guard entry, and the CI read (per
  security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Universal; architecture §Cross-cutting Patterns → Config management).

- (obs) For that send the wrapper's role file holds one `send-issued` and one `send-confirmed` on one cursor, no
  `send-refused`, and `text_bytes` is the typed text's length; the schemas are unchanged, `bash
  scripts/agent-run.sh schema-check` and `bash scripts/g2-zero-panics.sh` pass, and the canary is in no
  home-level diagnostics file (per obs-plan §4 Scenario: Confirmed `send` (CL-1) from driver to readback; §9 CI
  Integration, Gate commands G2 / G4; §8 PII Scrubbing, integration point 6).

- (design, layouts, a11y) A delivered send of a text ending in a newline prints `[RB] read back  <name>  <time>
  cursor <n>` on stdout with exit 0 and nothing on stderr, and under `--json` one `ok` document; the diff adds no
  refusal word, detail, hint or column: step 4 (per design-system §Surface: cli → Component Patterns, "2. `viola
  send`: the readback mirror"; layout-templates §Output structure — `viola send`; a11y-plan §4 ARIA Patterns &
  Roles, P2).

- (tests) `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --unit --filter 'test(/trailing_newline/)'` is green with sixteen
  passed and none failed, and `evidence/newline-red-green.md` holds the same cases red before step 2 (per
  test-plan §4 What unit tests cover → root bin; §3 `run`).

- (tests) `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --integration --filter 'test(/ending_in_newlines/)'` is green with two
  passed and none failed, and the evidence file holds its red reading before step 2, at the receipt's bytes. The exit code and the records are a
  floor under the fake agent, which echoes what it is typed; the receipt and the `text` are what prove the
  remedy (per test-plan §6 Scenario: Path 2).

- (tests) `bash scripts/agent-run.sh pre-push` is green on the uncommitted tree, with no breach and the coverage
  floors held (per test-plan §3 `pre-push`; §10 Coverage thresholds).

- (tests) The folded red is closed by its named cause. `grep -c '"--list"' src/cmd/run.rs` reads 0; `bash
  scripts/profraw-census.sh 4800 48` ends `runs 4800 · passed 4800 · profiles 4800 · third 0 · short 0`;
  `evidence/profraw-red-green.md` holds the census on the untouched test, read under the two-a-run rule: 3 runs
  of 4 800 with a third profile, all 3 short, and the revised rule's two planted readings, each exit 1, with
  the check that no planted file is left; nextest's `retries`, the coverage ignore regex and the gate's
  required suites are unchanged, by the guard entry (per test-plan §10 Zero-flakiness budget; §11 Test Strategy,
  CI; §3 `gate`).

- (security, obs) No workflow file changes and no artifact gains a member: `.github` is in the guard entry (per
  security-plan §Bootstrap phases, `secret-scanning-ci-gate`; obs-plan §9 CI Integration, Step order and
  conditions).

- (arch) The pre-CI commit's CI run reads `verdict: green` through the `ci.py conclusion` entry, and the
  `run_attempt` entry reads 1; the report names the run id (per architecture §Infrastructure Patterns → CI/CD
  approach).

- The report states the red's limit in these terms: the mechanism is measured at HEAD, and pid 10799's identity
  is not provable from the run (`inputs#I2`).

- Spec anchors: architecture §Established Decisions → [Delivery Confirmation], [Human Takeover / Wheel], [CLI
  Version Compatibility], [Agent Coverage]; §Standard Contracts → Event `data` per kind, Channel methods;

  `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/hook.rs`, `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs`, `tests/cli_send.rs`,
  `src/cmd/run.rs`, `src/run/version_gate.rs`, `src/run/mod.rs`, `crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs`,
  `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `scripts/profraw-census.sh`, the chunk's `evidence/`, and ci#37627485806 attempt 1
  with its three artifacts.

- External inputs: `inputs#I1` (the take-up directive), `inputs#I2` (the P4 card's answers), `inputs#I3` (the
  operator's review: the two count atoms, the census's wall time and its notice), `inputs#I4` (the word with the

  `text_bytes` on `send-issued` and on the `pty.paste_write` span.

- The census line keeps its words and only its count moves (`inputs#I7`, confirmed at the review, `inputs#I8`);
  `third` names a profile beyond the one a clean run leaves.

- Leaned: the planted control reaches the script through an optional third word naming the census directory,
  per `scripts/profraw-census.sh:21`, `:51` and `:53` (the script alone names its directory today, counts a run's
  files straight after the run and removes them).

- A claim that also accepts the prompt less one newline — the playbook's "Boundary widening" pattern (a validated
  surface admits a new input class) and a reliance on an unprobed CLI behaviour; it halts for the founder's live
  answer and was not chosen (`inputs#I2`).

- Refusing a text that ends in a newline — LF is an allowed character, the refusal has no detail or hint in any
  plan, and the entry asks for the send to be confirmed.

- Removing exactly one newline — it leaves `x\n\n` on the CLI's unmeasured handling of two; not chosen
  (`inputs#I2`).
- Removing anything but trailing LF (a CR, a TAB, a space, an inner newline) — outside the card's answer.

- A fake-agent option, fixture or turn script that reproduces the drop — no shape is invented before a recording,
  and with the strip none is needed.
- A new ledger row, probe paste or stamp — no `send` relies on the drop after step 2; a row needs live starts.

- A merge that skips or tolerates a corrupt profile, a retry, a re-run for green, a wider ignore regex — none
  closes the red.

- Keeping or uploading the refused profile, or any new member in a CI upload — a boundary widening, held
  (`inputs#I2`).

- A profile variable set in the `pre-push` launcher or in a harness child's environment — an added assignment
  across the `env -i` boundary. The census sets it inside its own script only.

- The test binary as the wrapper's child at a child-entry test — it cannot be entered: libtest exits 101 on the
  wrapper's plugin flag before any test body runs (measured at implement, `evidence/profraw-red-green.md`).

- Waiting for the test-binary child's own exit before the kill — not chosen on the step 7 card (`inputs#I5`): on
  Unix the kill would then signal a pid already reaped, and a run would leave three profiles. The take-up's
  reason for this line, 38 729 B written to an unread PTY, described the standalone binary, not the wrapper's
  child.

- Rebuilding the untouched test for a second red census reading — the operator's word (`inputs#I7`): the red
  side stands as recorded at step 6.
- A push while a gate entry of this block is red by its own letter — the overseer's word (`inputs#I6`).

- **STOP rules.** A pre-push or census red is read and reported, never re-run for a green. A stalled-start red is
  first a finding about the backing (`test -L target/e2e-home && findmnt -n -o FSTYPE -T target/e2e-home/`). A
  red where no assertion failed on a value is read against the backing and the host record before anything else
  (`inputs#I4`). A step that would need a file outside the two lists of research.md stops and reports.

- **The operator pass** is the implementer's on the operator's word (`inputs#I4`): `pre-push`, the hygiene
  entry, the pre-CI commit, the push entry, the `ci.py conclusion` read and the `run_attempt` read. The chunk
  needs green on the first attempt of the final sha's run.

- **Unmeasured before CI** (`inputs#I5`): `whoami` as the wrapper's child on Windows and macOS. It is resolved by
  the wrapper's own program lookup; on Windows that is `whoami.exe`. A Windows red is read and fixed by cause in
  its own commit, and the green-on-first-attempt rule binds the final sha.

- **Unmeasured, carried to "First live test and self-drive":** a send of a text ending in newlines on a live CLI
  after this build; a text of only newlines, which is typed as an empty text and behaves as an empty send does
  today; a trailing CR. No longer leaned on: what the CLI does with one or several trailing newlines.

- **`/clear` and a newline.** Before this build it was not a listed command, and an existing unit case pinned

  `unconfirmable` at once elsewhere. This follows from the one typed text, turned that one case, and is proved

  implement); the 48-run control took 10.3 s. On the untouched test the census read 3 third profiles in 4 800
  runs; research's scratch batches read 5 in 1 720 (research.md).

- **Symbols / APIs:**
  - New public function `viola_agent_claude::hook::typed_text(&str) -> &str`: the sent text without its trailing
    LF characters (`text.trim_end_matches('\n')`). It removes nothing else: not a CR, a TAB or a space, and no
    newline that is not at the very end. Sole product caller: `send` in `src/run/send.rs`.
  - The wrapper's `send` (`src/run/send.rs`): `validate_paste_text` still runs first, on the text as received.
    Directly after it the typed text is taken once, and from there on it is the only text `send` uses: the
    local-command classification (`classify`), the in-flight text the claim compares, the `text_bytes` on
    `send-issued` and on the `pty.paste_write` span, and the paste itself. `SendSlot::claim` is not changed: the
    match is still exact, now against the typed text. Its sole caller is still `append_hook_event`.
  - What a driver sees. A `send` whose text ends in one or more LF characters is typed without them, its
    `prompt-submitted` is relabelled `driver`, the send ends `ok {submitted_at, cursor}`, no `wheel` record is
    appended and the driver keeps the wheel. Before this chunk that send was delivered, reported `not-delivered`
    / `no-prompt-submitted` after the 10 s window, its prompt filed `human` and the wheel moved to the human.
  - `prompt-submitted.text` for such a send is the text as typed (without the trailing LF), not as sent.
  - A consequence of the one typed text: a listed local command followed by newlines is now that command.
    `/clear` and a newline is classified as `/clear` (confirmed by its new session on a verified CLI,
    `unconfirmable` at once elsewhere). Before, it was typed as an ordinary text, and one unit case pinned that;
    that case turned. The founder was shown this consequence with the options (inputs#I10). Proved at the unit
    layer only.
  - A text that ends in a newline and holds a refused control character is still refused `not-delivered` /
    `control-character` with nothing typed, first in the wrapper's order.
  - A text of only newlines is typed as an empty text. What an empty send does is unchanged and not measured
    here.
  - The CLI's own behaviour is unchanged and its measurement stands: `claude` 2.1.287 drops a pasted text's last
    newline before UserPromptSubmit. After this chunk no `send` relies on it, because `send` never types a text
    that ends in a newline.
  - The test `cmd::run::tests::start_opens_the_scenario_one_spans_under_run_start` (`src/cmd/run.rs`) starts its
    wrapper with the host program `whoami` as the child, not the test binary with `--list`. Every span assertion
    is unchanged. No product code in `src/cmd/run.rs` changed.

    dependency edge, ledger row, stamp, compiled literal, fixture, fake-agent option or turn script. No refusal
    word, detail, hint or column was added. `src/human.rs`, `src/cmd/send.rs`, `src/run/wheel.rs`,
    `src/run/gate.rs` and `crates/viola-core` are untouched (the preservation guard entry, green).

- **Crates / modules:** none added or removed. `viola-agent-claude` gains one public function; the root bin reads

data.head: ## The folded red, read against ci#37627485806 attempt 1

body:
- **Still as recorded.** Job `test (ubuntu-latest)`: step 9 `Coverage and doctest (sh shim)` failure, step 27
  `Gate verdict` failure; steps 10-18 skipped, `Browser suite (sh shim)` among them, which is why the gate also
  lists `suite-missing` and `artifact-missing` for `playwright` (re-derived at the take-up: `gh run view
  37627485806 --attempt 1 --json jobs`; re-derived at implement: `evidence/ci-attempt-1.md`).

- **The profile is not on the run.** `harness-ubuntu-latest` holds 10 members; 0 `.profraw` (re-derived twice:
  `unzip -l` of the artifact, `grep -c profraw` = 0). The upload takes `target/agent-run/` (`ci.yml:163-172`); the
  profile sat in `target/llvm-cov-target/`. The session-learnings method reads the refused file's own counters,
  so it cannot run on this attempt.

- **What the run does hold.** The profile's name carries its writer's pid, 10799.
  - `diag-ubuntu-latest`: 222 lines carry a `pid`, all `process-start` of `run` or `cli` (re-derived:
    `evidence/guards/read-attempt1.py` over its 217 files). The nearest below is 10401 at 13:21:39.511Z, the
    nearest above 11040 at 13:21:41.038Z; no line of any of the 127 test homes falls between 13:21:39.514Z and
    13:21:41.038Z.
  - `junit-ubuntu-latest`: 279 cases overlap that window, 277 of suite `viola::bin/viola` and 2 of
    `viola::tui_wheel`. `cmd::run::tests::start_opens_the_scenario_one_spans_under_run_start` ran
    13:21:39.913Z to 13:21:40.706Z. Its home is a tempdir outside `target/e2e-home`, so it leaves no line in the
    diagnostics artifact.

- **Reproduced at HEAD, at the take-up.** The instrumented unit-test binary of the last pre-push ran that one
  test with `LLVM_PROFILE_FILE` pointed at the scratchpad: 40 runs in sequence each left 2 profiles of 128 264 B;
  of 1 200 runs at 48 workers, 1 198 left 2 and 2 left 3, one third profile being 69 632 B, which `llvm-profdata
  show` refuses with attempt 1's line and `merge` with `error: no profile can be merged`.

- **The cause, as far as it is established.** A test kills an instrumented child that exits by itself, and the
  kill sometimes lands inside the child's exit-time profile write. Corrected at implement in one respect: the
  child never ran its `--list`. It was started as `<test binary> --plugin-dir <dir> --list`, libtest refused the
  flag and it exited 101 at once (below). The mechanism is the one stated.

- **What is not established.** That pid 10799 was that child. The file is gone; the runner's binary signature
  (`3177174534174374433`) is not the local one for the same binary (`978539276648341693`). The second `tui_wheel`
  case was also alive in the window.

- **The class.** Every other test that runs the test binary as a child either waits for its exit before any kill
  (`version_gate.rs:296-315`, `liveness.rs:110-116`, `viola-pty` `lib.rs:1072-1126`) or kills a child that blocks
  and never exits by itself (`viola-pty` `lib.rs:1131-1153`, `:1165-1207`, `:1213`). Those `viola-pty` children
  are spawned through `viola_pty::spawn` directly, with arguments the test gives whole; no wrapper flag precedes
  them. `"--list"` as a child argument: 3 hits at the take-up · 1 changed (`src/cmd/run.rs`, now 0 there:
  `grep -c '"--list"' src/cmd/run.rs`) · 2 no-change (they wait). Sweep: `grep -rn '"--list"' src crates tests
  --include=*.rs`.

- **Two earlier runs with the same message** on the same leg, ci#36529038462 and ci#36481260151, stand in
  `test-plan.md:1207` as "recorded, not established". Whether they had this cause is not measurable now.

title: Plan — 2026-10-07-live-rows-and-paste-shapes-on-the-dev-host: "Live rows and paste shapes on the dev host"

data.head: # Plan — 2026-10-07-live-rows-and-paste-shapes-on-the-dev-host: "Live rows and paste shapes on the dev host"

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-10-07-live-rows-and-paste-shapes-on-the-dev-host · **Version:** viola-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-07T09:47Z

Measure, on the Linux dev host against `claude` 2.1.287 named by path, the behaviours the route entry names, and
record them: three paste shapes, a typed `<task-notification>` at a prompt's start, a real cross-session prompt,
the `CLAUDE*` names that CLI hands a hook, and the paste-hint window with a `send` and a `wait` run inside it.
The chunk ends with the founder's answer to a card that carries the hint numbers (R-L4, inputs#I2).

It is a measuring chunk (inputs#I3, the founder's answer): three live starts under one cap of 10, no ledger row,
no row-count move, no fixture, no fake-agent mode, and no change to the readiness gate. The only product file it
edits is `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/hook.rs`: unit cases whose oracles are the measured prompts, and the
unwrap itself only where a measured shape falsifies it and the fix stays inside that file.

Two measurements cross a ruled boundary, each on the founder's own live answer of 2026-10-07T09:43Z given after
the widening was shown (inputs#I3): one fixed synthetic peer message from this builder session into the scratch
session, and the scratch hook's names-only list of its `CLAUDE*` environment. Neither touches product code, the
R8 strip, `viola verify` or the capture arm (per architecture §Established Decisions → [Hook Contract];
security-plan §Input Validation, Hook stdin row).

Order is load-bearing: every live round (steps 2, 4, 5) runs on the build of the base commit `e7e5bf75db8a`,
before any source edit, so no reading is taken on a tree this chunk changed.

Every product command a live round starts from this session runs with `VIOLA_NAME`, `VIOLA_DIR` and `VIOLA_BIN`
removed from its environment and with `--home` given (research M1): this session is itself wrapped by another
tree's bridge, and the product would otherwise file itself under that instance.

title: Step 0 — the record before anything moves

data.head: ### Step 0 — the record before anything moves

body:
- Open `evidence/live-sessions.ndjson`. Every live start gets one `{"kind":"start", …}` line (its ordinal `n`,
  `session` one of `scratch` · `hint-verified` · `hint-unstamped`, `cli` as the binary's own `--version` answered,
  `ts` from `date -u`) **written before the start**. Start 11 is never made.

- Census, written as a `{"kind":"census","when":"before", …}` line and in words in `evidence/probe-dir-census.md`:
  the root's `.viola-verify-*` dirs by name, the OS temp dir's `viola-verify-*` dirs by count. The ten dirs dated
  2026-10-06T22:12Z and `.viola-verify-2095228/` are the operator's and are not touched (scope W5).

- Read and record: `~/.local/share/mise/installs/claude/2.1.287/claude --version`; the standing stamp home
  `target/e2e-home.disk/viola-record-20261006T211429Z/vhome/ledger/stamps.json` (2.1.287, 17 of 17 `pass`); the
  backing (`test -L target/e2e-home && findmnt -n -o FSTYPE -T target/e2e-home/`). A missing stamp home is STOP 4.

- Re-run research M2's counts-only read of the driver's own log and write the counts (no prompt text) to
  `evidence/harness-prompts-driver-log.md`, with the script's classification rule and the time read from the clock.
- Build the product once on the base commit: `cargo build` (the default features; `target/debug/viola`).

title: Step 1 — the scratch probe, built outside the repository and rehearsed dry

data.head: ### Step 1 — the scratch probe, built outside the repository and rehearsed dry

body:
- In the session scratchpad, in step 0's form of the prior chunk (research, Patterns detected; that chunk's
  `evidence/step0-shapes.md` "How it ran" and `evidence/rehearsal-shapes.md` for the wait rule): a Python PTY
  driver at 80×24; a scratch plugin whose four spine hooks run one scratch script in exec form; the script claims
  `<Event>.<k>.json` exclusively at 0600, prints nothing, exits 0. A copy of the earlier driver may be reused only
  after it is read whole.

- The founder's second answer (inputs#I3): on its first invocation the same script also writes one file holding the
  sorted names of its environment that start with `CLAUDE`. Names only: the script reads no value into any file.

- The child: the 2.1.287 binary by path with `--model haiku --plugin-dir <scratch plugin>`; the inherited `CLAUDE*`
  names and the three `VIOLA_*` names removed, names only; cwd a fresh 0700 `<repo root>/.viola-verify-<pid>/`
  that the driver removes on every one of its own exit paths.

- The wait before every paste: the previous turn's Stop is captured and the screen, read through the tree's own
  `Screen` by a scratch helper built against `crates/viola-agent-claude` by path, has been quiet 300 ms with the
  input-box literal on a row and no modal literal on any; a quiet screen with no literal keeps waiting, 60 s at
  most. The record states for every settle how long it took and what it settled on
  (`.claude/rules/testing.md`, 2026-10-06).

- The driver has one hold point for step 2's peer message: it writes a status file, then waits up to 180 s for one
  more UserPromptSubmit capture, then goes on to its end either way.

- Rehearse once against a stand-in script (no CLI, no session) that draws a hint after a long paste, so the waits,
  the hold and the record are seen before the one live start.

title: Step 2 — live session 1: the scratch session (start 1)

data.head: ### Step 2 — live session 1: the scratch session (start 1)

body:
One session, ended by Ctrl-C twice. Each text is synthetic ASCII opening `viola probe:` and is kept whole in
`evidence/scratch-prompts.json`; a long text is 1 500 bytes on one line (the tree's `PROBE_LONG_PASTE` where one
serves, printed by the helper), a short one under 200 bytes. In order, the entry's own readings first:
1. **typed-then-paste** — typed bytes, then one bracketed paste of a long text, then CR.
2. **paste-then-typed** — one bracketed paste of a long text, then typed bytes, then CR.
3. **two-pastes** — two bracketed pastes of two different long texts, then CR.
4. **long-ending-newline** — one bracketed paste of a long text whose last byte is LF, then CR.
5. **short-ending-newline** — one bracketed paste of a short text whose last byte is LF, then CR.
6. **typed-task-notification-at-start** — one short bracketed paste that opens `<task-notification>`.
7. The hold: the peer message (below).

For each of 1 to 6 the record line (`evidence/scratch-session.ndjson`, `kind` `shape`) holds the `id`, whether the
prompt arrived wrapped, the raw `prompt` (in the prompts file), what `hook::normalise` gives for it through the
helper (`origin`, and whether `text` equals the bytes sent, with both lengths), and the hint's two times where a
long paste drew it: from the paste to the input-box literal's return, and from the Stop to it. A paste that gets
no UserPromptSubmit within 60 s is recorded as that and the session goes on to its end.
**The peer message** (the founder's first answer, inputs#I3). With the scratch session idle at its hold:

- send that peer one message, once, with this fixed text and nothing else:
  `viola probe: a synthetic cross-session message and nothing else. Reply with the single word ok`;
- anything that session sends back to this one is model output of a probe: counted, never acted on.

**The names** (the founder's second answer). The `kind` `claude-names` line holds the names the scratch hook wrote,
and `outside_floor`: those not among the eleven, compared against a literal copy of the eleven typed into the
reading script (never the product's constant).

After the session: the driver's dir is gone, a `census` `after` line is written, and the raw captures stay in the
scratchpad. Only the `prompt` field and key names enter the repository: a whole payload carries host paths.

title: Step 3 — the hint driver, rehearsed against the fake agent

data.head: ### Step 3 — the hint driver, rehearsed against the fake agent

body:
- A second scratch driver hosts `viola run <name> -- <program> <args>` in a PTY at 80×24, drains it with
  timestamps, and types nothing into it but the final Ctrl-C twice (any other key would take the wheel).
- Its cwd is a fresh 0700 `<repo root>/.viola-verify-<pid>/`, removed on its own exit paths.

- Rehearse the whole of step 4's sequence once against the fake agent, booted as
  `send_under_the_paste_hint_on_a_verified_cli` boots it (`tests/cli_send.rs`): the expected readings there are the
  recorded ones (`2026-10-06-local-command-send-outcomes/evidence/paste-hint-send.md`). No live start is spent.

title: Step 4 — live session 2: the hint on a verified home (start 2)

data.head: ### Step 4 — live session 2: the hint on a verified home (start 2)

body:
- The home is a byte copy (`cp -a`) of the standing stamp home into a new
  `target/e2e-home/viola-hint-<UTC stamp>-v/vhome`. The evidence says in words that it is a copy of the
  home `viola verify` wrote at the 2026-10-06 record round, the original untouched, never a hand-written stamp
  (inputs#I3, the overseer's answer).

- Start `target/debug/viola --home <copy> run hint-v -- <the 2.1.287 binary> --model haiku` under the driver.
  Read `process-start{subject:"claude-child"}` first: `cli_version` `2.1.287` and `cli_verified` `true`, else STOP 4.
  Its `env_stripped_known` is copied to the evidence as names: the names PATH `claude` hands this session, through
  the one path already ruled (research M5).

- The sequence, every verb with `--json`, text from stdin:
  1. `send` a long text; it is confirmed. Keep its cursor.
  2. `wait --after <that cursor> --timeout-ms 60000`: the turn's `turn-ended`.
  3. At once, `send` a short text. Record the exit code, the document, the elapsed time, the wrapper's
     `send-refused` fields and whether a `parse-rejected{parser:"vt100-feed"}` line stands before it (research M7:
     the refusal is the hint's only with none).
  4. At once, `wait --timeout-ms 20000` with no `--after`. Record its outcome and elapsed time.
  5. `wait --after <step 1's cursor> --timeout-ms 5000`: it should return the logged `turn-ended` at once.
  6. `send` the short text again. Record the outcome, and how long after the Stop a send first succeeds.
  7. After that turn's `turn-ended` and the input box's return, `send` a long text whose last byte is LF: the
     end-to-end test of the newline hypothesis (research M6). Record the outcome; `no-prompt-submitted` when the
     10 s window expires is what the hypothesis predicts.

- From the drained bytes, through the tree's `Screen`: when the footer lost the input-box literal and when it
  came back, against the paste and the Stop. Each timing is one `kind` `hint-timing` line in
  `evidence/hint-window.ndjson`; steps 3, 4 and 5 are `send-in-window` and `wait-in-window` lines.
- End by Ctrl-C twice; read the exit; write the `census` `after` line.

title: Step 5 — live session 3: the hint on an unstamped home (start 3)

data.head: ### Step 5 — live session 3: the hint on an unstamped home (start 3)

body: - The same driver and sequence on a fresh home that `viola run hint-u` creates itself: `cli_verified` `false`.

- Here the gate is partial (research M7): at the first quiet instant after the Stop the short text is typed while
  the hint stands. Record what the real CLI does with it: confirmed, `no-prompt-submitted` after the window, or
  another outcome; whether a `prompt-submitted` record followed and whether its text equals the text sent; what
  the screen's signature rows read afterwards.

- The evidence says in words (the overseer's review, inputs#I4): this run measures what the product already does
  on an unverified CLI; it is a reading and no new widening.
- A session left in a state Ctrl-C twice does not end is killed, with no key typed into it; that is recorded.

- The live homes of steps 4 and 5 hold real CLI content. Once their readings are in the evidence (codes, counts,
  times, names; no assistant text) they are removed, before any gate of the block below runs.

title: Step 6 — the hint record and the founder's card

data.head: ### Step 6 — the hint record and the founder's card

body:
- `evidence/hint-window.md`: every timing of steps 2, 4 and 5 (at least two long pastes), the first chunk's
  8.0 s and 6.5 s beside them, the verified-home `send` and `wait` readings, the unstamped-home reading.

- `evidence/hint-card.md`, the card. The four options the route names for what `send` does while the hint stands
  (wait on a quiet literal-less screen · a longer bound · type under the hint · stay as it is), each priced from
  the numbers: what it would change in code (the sites of research M7), which masters it amends, whether the
  `input-not-ready` hint text or any `send` human line changes, whether a human keystroke arriving in the window
  is delayed or refused by it, what `send`'s longest blocking time becomes against the MCP tool-call timeout, and
  how the fake agent's 8 000 ms hold cap sits against the measured window. Beside them, the `wait` finding and
  what the hint text's advice then is worth.

- Raise the card through one AskUserQuestion. It reaches the founder through the overseer, who relays it to him
  and returns his words (inputs#I4). Write the answer verbatim to the evidence as the founder's, relayed by the
  overseer, snapshot it (`inputs.py snap --step implement`), and add the `kind` `card` line with `answered` true.
  An answer that is not the founder's own leaves `answered` false.

- **Nothing is built from the answer in this chunk.** The gate, `GATE_MAX_WAIT`, `QUIET_PERIOD` and `send_hint`
  stay as they are; the chosen remedy's build is the route's at the wrap.

title: Step 7 — the measured shapes as unit cases

data.head: ### Step 7 — the measured shapes as unit cases

body:
- In `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/hook.rs`, inline in `mod tests`: one rstest whose name contains `live_shape`
  for the unwrap (a case per shape of step 2, 1 to 5: the measured raw prompt as a literal, the text sent as the
  expected `text`), and one whose name contains `live_shape` for `prompt_origin` (the typed `<task-notification>`
  reading, and the cross-session raw start when one was measured). Ids and attribute values are the measured or
  placeholder ones; no path, no host name.

- The two existing guesses `text_then_framed_pair` and `two_framed_pairs` (`hook.rs:556-563`) are brought to the
  measured shapes where they differ.
- The doc comments that say "not measured" for a reading this chunk took (`hook.rs:171-176`) are brought current.

- A case that fails on HEAD's `unwrap_pastes` is a falsified unwrap. Its fix lands here only when it stays inside
  `unwrap_pastes` / `paste_pair` and removes exactly what the measurement shows, nothing wider (per architecture
  §Established Decisions → [CLI Version Compatibility], the long-paste wrapper); the wrapped-paste property and
  `proptest-regressions/` follow. Each new case is shown red before the fix and green after. A fix that needs any
  other file is STOP 5.
- `HARNESS_PREFIXES` and `IDENTITY_FLOOR` do not change in this chunk, whatever was measured (STOP 6 reports it).

title: Step 8 — what the wrap needs to carry

data.head: ### Step 8 — what the wrap needs to carry

body: Written into the report, not into any master:
- the two rows stay owed with their readings, no entry minted (inputs#I3); `v1-34` unclaimed;
- the founder's choice on the hint card and the build it asks for;

- the kill-leftover finding (research M8): a leftover carries a pid and no start time, so a remover needs an owner
  record first; the ten standing dirs are the operator's;
- the expected amendments listed under Implementation notes.
A STOP ends the live work, keeps every record, and returns to the overseer before another start is made.
1. A start that shows a modal: killed with no key.

2. The same live session failing a second time after its one re-run (a re-run is made only after the failed
   round's record is read).
3. The ledger at 10 starts.
4. The stamp home missing, or the copy not reading `cli_verified` `true`: no verify is spent without a word.
5. A falsified unwrap whose fix leaves `hook.rs`.

6. Not a stop of the live work, a report: a cross-session raw start matching neither compiled form, or a `CLAUDE*`
   name outside the eleven. Recorded, changed nowhere, named first in the implement report.

7. A stalled start: read the backing as step 0 does, stop and report; never a re-run for green
   (`.claude/rules/verification-harness.md`, 2026-10-07).

- `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-live-rows-and-paste-shapes-on-the-dev-host/evidence/` — `live-sessions.ndjson`, `probe-dir-census.md`, `harness-prompts-driver-log.md`, `scratch-session.ndjson`, `scratch-prompts.json`, `hint-window.ndjson`, `hint-window.md`, `hint-card.md`, the card's answer

- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/hook.rs` — the `live_shape` cases, the two guessed cases, the doc comments, and `unwrap_pastes` / `paste_pair` only under step 7's rule; callers per research's graph: `prompt_text @ hook.rs:189` → `data_of @ hook.rs:158` and `pasted @ crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs:678`
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/proptest-regressions/hook.txt` — only if the wrapped-paste property records a failing seed

No `live` or `round` entry: the three live sessions are driven by scratch drivers outside the repository and by one
peer message this session sends itself, so no reader can re-run them. They are one-off witnesses whose records go
to `evidence/`, as a mutation kill run's does (`.claude/rules/testing.md`, 2026-10-04). The fence holds their
readers (`jq -e -s …`), which the wrap re-runs over the records. The drivers' known-verdict controls are step 1's
dry rehearsal and step 3's fake-agent rehearsal. The evidence files are records implement writes, not artifacts an
entry produces, so no entry carries `artifact`.

One control mutates source and reverts, so it is a one-shot run at implement and not an entry: step 7's red before
the fix and green after it for a falsified unwrap, both readings in `evidence/`. On every re-run the `live_shape`
filter entry holds the same property.

The harness smoke boots the fake agent; G2 and G4 are read over its home between `status` and `cleanup`. The
preservation guard names the base commit, because the operator pass's pre-CI commit moves HEAD onto the chunk.
A red whose shape is a stalled start is a finding about the backing (STOP 7).

body:
No capability is claimed: `verification-matrix.json#v1-34` needs both rows as probed ledger rows, and the founder's
answers give each a measurement and no stamp (inputs#I3). Its note is written at P5.

- (tests) Every live start is ledgered before it is made, on `claude` 2.1.287 by path, three to ten in all, with
  the scratch session and both hint sessions present; entry `jq -e -s 'map(select(.kind == "start")) as $s …'`
  over `evidence/live-sessions.ndjson` reads true (per test-plan §1 Test Scope Summary; inputs#I2 R-L3).

- (security) After every live round no probe dir this chunk made stands, and the dirs it did not make are
  untouched; the same entry's `census` clause, with `evidence/probe-dir-census.md` naming each count (per
  security-plan §Data Protection, At rest, Interactive probe dirs).

- (arch) Each of the six shape readings is recorded with its raw prompt and what the compiled normalisation makes
  of it; entry `jq -e -s '[.[] | select(.kind == "shape") | .id] …'` reads true (per architecture §Established
  Decisions → [CLI Version Compatibility]).

- (tests) Each measured shape is a `live_shape` unit case whose oracle is the measured prompt as a literal; entry
  `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --unit --filter 'test(/live_shape/)'` exits 0 with `"ok":true`. A falsified
  unwrap is either fixed inside `hook.rs` with its red and green readings in `evidence/`, or reported under STOP 5
  with the failing case recorded (per test-plan §4 Unit Test Strategy, viola-agent-claude).

- (obs) No `CLAUDE*` value, no assistant text and no host path is in any file the chunk commits; environment data
  is names only (per obs-plan §8 PII Scrubbing; security-plan §Bootstrap phases, `logging-redaction-wire`).

- (arch) The hint is timed at least twice more on 2.1.287; a `send` and a no-cursor `wait` are run inside the
  window on a verified home, a `send` on an unstamped one, and the founder's answer to the card is recorded; entry
  `jq -e -s '([.[] | select(.kind == "hint-timing")] | length) >= 2 …'` reads true (per architecture §Established
  Decisions → [CLI Version Compatibility]; inputs#I2 R-L4).

- (layouts) The card states for each of the four options whether `viola send`'s human lines and the
  `input-not-ready` hint stay as they are; the live refusal's lines are recorded as printed (per layout-templates
  §Surface: cli › Output structure — `viola send`; §Surface: cli › IA notes).

- (a11y) The card states for each option whether a human keystroke arriving in the hint window is delayed or
  refused by it (per a11y-plan §1 A11y Scope Summary → `viola run` TUI passthrough).

- (arch) The readiness gate, `GATE_MAX_WAIT`, `QUIET_PERIOD`, `send_hint`, the identity floor, the ledger rows,
  verify, the capture arm, every fixture and the fake agent are unchanged; entry `git diff --quiet e7e5bf75db8a --
  src …` exits 0, and `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --unit` holds the four harness prefixes' existing cases (per
  architecture §Established Decisions → [Screen Model]; security-plan §Input Validation, Hook stdin row, Capture
  arm).

- (tests) `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run` exits 0 with `"ok":true`, and `bash scripts/agent-run.sh pre-push`
  exits 0 with `"ok":true` (per test-plan §3 `run`, Exit code semantics and Output format).

- (obs) G2 and G4 read clean over the smoke home; entries `bash scripts/g2-zero-panics.sh` and `bash
  scripts/agent-run.sh schema-check` exit 0 (per obs-plan §10 SLO Invariants & Telemetry Budgets, Error budget).

- (tests) CI is green on the operator's pre-CI commit; the entry `… ci.py conclusion --sha HEAD --wait 1800`
  reads `verdict: green`, and the report names the run id (per test-plan §10 Quality Gates & Coverage Targets).

- Spec anchors (from the extracts): architecture §Established Decisions → [CLI Version Compatibility], → [Screen
  Model], → [Delivery Confirmation], → [Hook Contract]; §Occupied Resources → Environment variables, →
  Filesystem; §Cross-cutting Patterns → Capability ledger. security-plan §Threat Model Summary (Child process
  spawning); §Secret Management (Storage); §Input Validation (Hook stdin row, Capture arm; Paste text row); §Data
  Protection (Interactive probe dirs; Repository fixtures); §Security Anti-Patterns → Universal. test-plan §1, §3
  `run`, §4 (viola-agent-claude), §7 (Recorded hook payloads; Fake agent, Modes), §10, §11. obs-plan §4 Edge
  flows, §4 Scenario: Confirmed `send`, §8. design-system §Surface: cli → Component Patterns 2 and 5.
  layout-templates §Surface: cli › Output structure — `viola send`, `viola wait` / `viola last`, `viola verify`.
  a11y-plan §1, §4 P4, §8.
- External inputs: inputs#I1 (the take-up directive), inputs#I2 (R-L2, R-L3, R-L4), inputs#I3 (the P4 answers).

- Research files inspected: `src/cmd/verify/typed.rs`, `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/hook.rs`, `lib.rs`,
  `screen.rs`, `ledger.rs`, `src/run/send.rs`, `src/run/wait.rs`, `src/run/mod.rs`, `src/cmd/hook.rs`,
  `src/cmd/run.rs`, `src/human.rs`, `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run.rs`, and the two prior chunks' evidence.

- Leans stated, each on an artifact:
  - the scratch live sessions run under the entry's own rulings (R-L2, R-L3: unattended, 2.1.287 by path, cap 10)
    in the form the prior chunk's step 0 ran under its cap ruling; leaned per inputs#I2 and that chunk's
    `evidence/step0-shapes.md`;
  - the hint remedy is not built here; leaned per R-L4 ("the choice is made on that card") and because its size is
    unknown until the answer;
  - the kill leftovers stay a recorded finding with a census; leaned per research M8 (a pid-only name cannot back
    the exact-identity removal security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Code Patterns asks for).

- Extract tension, resolved here: the arch extract reads no described mechanism for the floor reading while the
  security extract names the `claude-child` start line as the one ruled path. Both hold: that line is used in
  step 4 for PATH `claude`'s names, and the 2.1.287 reading is the scratch hook's, on the founder's answer.

- Overridden extract content: the security extract and two history files state that nothing can address a verify
  child. Research M4 corrected the premise in scope; the plan rests on the correction.

- A probed ledger row for either measurement — rejected by the founder's answers (inputs#I3); no `LedgerRow`, no
  `Probes` field, no `--record` variant, no fake-agent option, no count literal moves.

- Changing the product's capture arm to list names — the arm is founder-ratified and reads no environment
  (security-plan §Input Validation, Hook stdin row, Capture arm); the scratch hook does the listing.

- Sending the peer message when the new peer is not unambiguous — one wrong recipient is another builder's
  session; none or several new peers means nothing is sent.
- More than one peer message, or any other text — the answer covers one fixed synthetic message.

- Recording a whole hook payload, a `from` value or any environment value — a payload carries host paths and an
  address; only `prompt`, key names and bare `CLAUDE*` names enter the repository.
- A fixture from a scratch capture — a fixture comes only from the recorder (test-plan §7).
- A fake-agent mode for a live reading — no shape before a recorded fixture (test-plan §7, Fake agent, Modes).

- A new `viola verify` or `viola run` flag, environment variable or config key as a probe switch — security-plan
  §Security Anti-Patterns → Universal.

- Typing into the `viola run` PTY during a hint run — any key takes the wheel and turns the reading into a
  `human-typing` one.
- `run --local-live` — it reaches PATH `claude` and is `:98`'s to fire.
- Building anything from the hint card's answer, or moving `GATE_MAX_WAIT` "to see" — R-L4.

- Widening the unwrap past what a measurement shows, or loosening the claim's exact match — architecture
  §Established Decisions → [Delivery Confirmation].
- Removing any probe dir this chunk did not make — the operator's.
- `/remote-control`, any key into a CLI dialog — the standing verify rulings.

- The first timing put 1.5 s of the 8.0 s window before the Stop: a `send` placed before `turn-ended` reads
  `turn-running`, not the gate (research M7). Step 4 waits for the record first.
- A no-cursor `wait` with no `--timeout-ms` has no deadline (research M7). Every `wait` of this plan carries one.

- Two long pastes close together may not arrive as two pairs: the footer reads `paste again to expand` after a
  paste. Shape 3 records what arrives, whatever it is.

- The fake agent's hold is capped at 8 000 ms (`src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs:32`, `:105`), the first reading
  exactly. A longer measured window goes on the card as a fact about what CI can replay.

- The scratchpad copies of the earlier drivers stand under the host temp dir today and may be gone tomorrow; the
  plan does not depend on them.

- The live homes sit under `target/e2e-home`, on tmpfs behind the link: inside the local G2 and G4 walks, gone at
  a reboot. Nothing of them is uploaded: CI never runs this chunk's live work.

- Predicted, to be measured and recorded, not expected: `cli_verified` `true` on the copied home; exit 13
  `not-delivered` / `input-not-ready` for the in-window `send` on it; `timed_out` for the no-cursor `wait`.

- Expected amendments (wrap): architecture §Established Decisions → [CLI Version Compatibility] — the harness
  prefixes' "relayed, not yet measured" and the start-of-prompt "unmeasured" become the measured readings; the
  long-paste wrapper's three "Unmeasured" shapes become measured; the hint paragraph takes the live `send` and
  `wait` readings and the founder's choice; "owed to Live rows and paste shapes on the dev host" becomes the two
  rows still owed with no entry minted.

- Expected amendments (wrap): architecture §Occupied Resources → Environment variables — the floor's origin gains
  the Linux reading (a 2.1.287 hook's names, and PATH `claude`'s through the child-start line).

- Expected amendments (wrap): security-plan §Threat Model Summary — the two scratch-probe measurements recorded as
  the founder's live answers of 2026-10-07T09:43Z, relayed by the overseer: one synthetic peer message into a

- Expected amendments (wrap): test-plan §3 → 5-command implementation — the `--local-live` bullet names all

**Chunk:** Live rows and paste shapes on the dev host — the harness-prefix and identity-floor rows, three paste shapes and the paste-hint window, measured on claude 2.1.287 by path
**Date:** 2026-10-07
**Commits:** `33d2084` chore(2026-10-07-live-rows-and-paste-shapes-on-the-dev-host): operator pre-CI commit, for the run this chunk's verdict reads (the one commit since the last wrap; basis `git log --format='%h %s' e7e5bf7..HEAD`)

A measuring chunk. Three live `claude` 2.1.287 sessions were run by path under one cap of 10 (3 used), each ledgered
before it was made. One product file changed. No ledger row landed, no row count moved, no fixture, no fake-agent
mode, and the readiness gate is where the base commit left it.

- **Files:** `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/hook.rs` (99 insertions, 13 deletions; basis `git diff --stat e7e5bf7 --
  crates`). Beside it only the chunk folder (`evidence/` 12 files, `inputs/` I5 and I6), the run dirs and
  bookkeeping. `crates/viola-agent-claude/proptest-regressions/hook.txt` is unchanged (no failing seed).

- **Symbols / APIs:**
  - `unwrap_pastes` (private, `hook.rs`; sole caller `prompt_text`, whose callers are `data_of` and
    `ledger::pasted`, per research's graph) changed behaviour: after a pair's close tag and its one newline, a
    **second newline is removed too when text follows it that is not the next pair's own two-newline frame**. So
    `prompt-submitted.text` for a paste followed by typed text no longer keeps one newline between them.
  - New private const `NEXT_FRAME` (`"\n\n<pasted_content id=\""`) in `hook.rs`. No public symbol, IPC method,
    endpoint, event kind, socket, port, env var or CLI flag was added or changed.
  - `HARNESS_PREFIXES` and `IDENTITY_FLOOR` are unchanged. `paste_pair` is unchanged.
  - Doc comments brought current: `prompt_origin` (the typed `<task-notification>` at a prompt's start; the
    cross-session form as measured) and `unwrap_pastes` (the frame).
  - Tests (inline, `mod tests`): new `prompt_text_live_shape_normalises_as_measured` (5 cases) and
    `prompt_origin_live_shape_files_as_harness` (2 cases); `two_framed_pairs` now carries one id on both pairs;
    `prompt_text_prop_round_trips_a_wrapped_paste` gained a typed tail after the pair. `hook.rs` holds 51 labelled
    cases (44 at the base; basis `/usr/bin/grep -c 'case::'`).
- **Crates / modules:** none added or removed; `viola-agent-claude` changed (`hook.rs` only).

title: M1 — the versions, and how a live round reaches 2.1.287

data.head: ### M1 — the versions, and how a live round reaches 2.1.287

body:
- `viola verify` and `viola run` both take the program after `--` (`src/cmd/run.rs:35-42`; architecture [CLI Version
  Compatibility]); `run --local-live` passes none (`crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run.rs:379-385`), so it reaches PATH
  `claude` and is not this chunk's channel.

- One stamped set: `tests/contract_ledger_probes.rs:36` (`STAMPED: ["2.1.287"]`), `:39`
  (`DRIFT_ONLY: ["2.1.283", "2.1.288"]`).

- This session's tool environment carries `VIOLA_NAME`, `VIOLA_DIR` and `VIOLA_BIN` (names read with `env | cut
  -d= -f1`), set by the bridge that wraps this builder, which is another tree's build. The product reads
  `VIOLA_NAME` as `from` (`src/cmd/client.rs:106`) and as the instance for its process log (`src/cmd/mod.rs:117`).
  So every product command a live round starts from this session runs with those three names removed and `--home`
  given, or it would file itself under the bridge's instance.
