  by `str.startswith` against seven literals and prints counts and key names only; no prompt text is printed or
  kept.

- Reading: 136 `UserPromptSubmit` records. 75 start with `<agent-message from=`. **28 start with
  `<task-notification>`.** 33 start with none of the seven. 0 start with `<cross-session-message`, 0 with
  `<\cross-session-message`, 0 with the model-layer preface `Another Claude session sent a message`, 0 with
  `[SYSTEM NOTIFICATION`, 0 with `<system-reminder`. 0 hold `<task-notification>` anywhere but the start.

- What it settles: the `<task-notification>` form reaches UserPromptSubmit starting at the tag, unescaped, with no
  preface, as the compiled prefix expects (`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/hook.rs:105-110`, `:178`). The CARRY's
  "unmeasured at the hook layer: the `<task-notification>` form" is closed by this reading for the CLI this session
  runs.

- What it does not settle: the version. The log's records carry no CLI version; this session was started through
  PATH `claude`, whose `latest` link has pointed at 2.1.289 since 2026-10-06 (the link's date). It is not a 2.1.287
  reading. And it is the CLI's own injection, not a typed tag: whether a human who types `<task-notification>` at the
  very start of a prompt gets it escaped is still unmeasured.

- No cross-session message has reached this session through the hook in the log's life: the cross-session form
  stays unmeasured here.

title: M3 — what the CLI does with a cross-session message, read statically from the 2.1.287 binary

data.head: ### M3 — what the CLI does with a cross-session message, read statically from the 2.1.287 binary

body:
- `/usr/bin/grep -a -c 'cross-session-message' <the 2.1.287 binary>` reads 10 lines. The surrounding text states
  that incoming peer messages "arrive as user-role messages wrapped in `<cross-session-message from="...">`", and
  the binary's own readers match `^<cross-session-message\b[^>]*>\n?` and strip a closing
  `\n</cross-session-message>`. Attributes read by those matchers: `from`, `from-name`.

- So at the model and transcript layer the tag is unescaped. What the UserPromptSubmit `prompt` holds (the relayed
  measurement says escaped, `<\cross-session-message`) cannot be read statically: the hook payload is built
  elsewhere. Both compiled forms stay as they are until a live reading.

- The same binary says worker results arrive "containing `<task-notification>` XML ... normally inside a
  `<system-reminder>`": the model-layer frame. M2 shows the hook layer has no such frame.

title: M4 — a wrapped child and the peer listing (the premise behind widening 1)

data.head: ### M4 — a wrapped child and the peer listing (the premise behind widening 1)

body:
- `Run::spawn` passes `env_remove: inputs.strip.remove` (`src/cmd/verify/typed.rs:544-551`), and `viola run` plans
  the same strip (`plan_strip @ src/cmd/run.rs:207`). Both messaging names are floor names
  (`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/lib.rs:14-26`). So a child never sees its parent session's socket or token.
  Verified.

- The CARRY's inference from that, "so it cannot be addressed by another session", is not established by the code:
  the strip removes the parent's identity from the child's environment, and says nothing about whether the child
  registers itself with the CLI's peer listing.

- Observed during this phase (the session's own peer listing, PATH `claude`): nine peer sessions are listed, three of
  them builders that are each a child of the other tree's bridge. That bridge's strip is not this product's and was
  not read. So a wrapped interactive session can be listed and addressed on this host; whether a 2.1.287 child
  started under viola's strip is listed is unmeasured, and the first scratch session can read it at no extra start.

- Consequence for the probe-path card: the cross-session measurement needs no change to the strip, to `viola verify`
  or to any product code. What crosses is one message, sent by a second Claude session, into a probed session.

title: M5 — the identity floor: what can see a child's names today

data.head: ### M5 — the identity floor: what can see a child's names today

body: - The floor is 11 names (`lib.rs:14-26`); its only readers are `plan_strip_with @ lib.rs:102` and the crate's tests.

- The capture arm takes the event, the dir and stdin and nothing else (`src/cmd/hook.rs:94-95`, `:359-372`): it
  reads no environment. Verified.

- One names-only path is already ruled: `log_child_start` writes `env_stripped_known` and `env_kept` on
  `process-start{subject:"claude-child"}` (`src/run/mod.rs:39-60`; the only site, `grep -rn 'env_stripped_known'
  src crates`: 1 file). It lists the `CLAUDE*` names `viola run` removed from **its own** inherited environment. A
  `viola run` this builder starts therefore records the names this session exports (PATH `claude`), names only, at
  no widening. It records a 2.1.287 session's names only when `viola run` is started from inside a 2.1.287 session,
  which no planned step does.

- Read here by count: this session exports 10 `CLAUDE*` names (`env | cut -d= -f1 | grep -c '^CLAUDE'`), the count
  the prior chunk's research M7 read by name on 2.1.289.

- A 2.1.287 reading needs something running inside a 2.1.287 session to list names: a hook's own environment (what
  that CLI hands its hooks) or a tool's (what it hands a command the model runs). The two may differ; the floor's
  Windows origin measured a wrapped host's inherited set.

title: M6 — the three paste shapes against the compiled unwrap

data.head: ### M6 — the three paste shapes against the compiled unwrap

body:
- `unwrap_pastes` (`hook.rs:199-219`) and `paste_pair` (`:222-228`): a pair is `<pasted_content id="X">`, a
  newline, the inner text, a newline, `</pasted_content id="X">`. The two newlines directly before the open tag and
  the one directly after the close go with it.

- The compiled expectation for shape 1 (typed text beside a paste) and shape 2 (two pastes) already stands as unit
  cases written from the one-paste measurement, not from a measurement of those shapes:
  `text_then_framed_pair` (`hook.rs:556-559`: `note:` + the framed pair gives `note:A long paste`) and
  `two_framed_pairs` (`:560-563`). If the CLI frames a second pair or a pair after typed text differently, those
  two cases encode a guess.

- Shape 3, re-derived at HEAD: with a pasted text `T\n`, if the CLI adds no newline before the close tag, the raw
  prompt is `…">\nT\n</pasted_content id="X">…`, `paste_pair` returns `T`, and delivery matching compares `T` with
  the sent `T\n` exactly (architecture [Delivery Confirmation]): no claim, and the send ends `not-delivered` /
  `no-prompt-submitted` when the 10 s window expires (`src/run/send.rs:349-351`). The code half is verified; the
  CLI half ("adds no newline") is the freight's static reading and stays the hypothesis the live paste tests.

- No unit case holds a pasted text that itself ends in a newline (`/usr/bin/grep -c 'case::'
  crates/viola-agent-claude/src/hook.rs`: 44 labelled cases; the five whose label names a newline, `hook.rs:511`,
  `:544`, `:548`, `:552`, `:564`, are about the frame's newlines, read one by one).

- Static read of the 2.1.287 binary for the wrapper: the open form is `<pasted_content id="${t}">` + newline, the
  close `</pasted_content id="${t}">`, the id 4 characters (`wKt=4`). What sits between the text and the close is
  not readable from the matched fragments.

- Callers (graph): `unwrap_pastes` ← `prompt_text @ hook.rs:189` alone; `prompt_text` ← `data_of @ hook.rs:158`,
  `pasted @ crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs:678`, and three tests (`hook.rs:528`, `:569`, `:709`). A change
  to the unwrap reaches production through `normalise` → `prompt-submitted`'s `text` → the claim, and through the
  two paste rows' check.

title: M7 — the hint window: the gate, the hint, and `wait`

data.head: ### M7 — the hint window: the gate, the hint, and `wait`

body:
- The gate (`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/screen.rs:122-152`): not quiet for 300 ms keeps waiting up to 5 s; a
  quiet screen with signatures is `Ready` only when a row holds `for agents` and none holds a modal literal; **with
  no signatures** (`sigs` `None`, an unverified CLI) a quiet screen is `Ready` with no row read. `send` refuses
  `input-not-ready` on anything but `Ready` (`src/run/send.rs:338-341`).

- So the same long-paste sequence has two readings on the real CLI: on a verified home the fake-agent result
  predicts `input-not-ready`; on an unstamped home the partial gate reads `Ready` and the second text **is typed
  while the hint stands**. The footer text during the window is `paste again to expand` (the prior chunk's
  `evidence/rehearsal-shapes.md:99`), so what a second paste does there (a new prompt, or an expansion of the first
  paste) is exactly the fact the card's "type under the hint" option needs, and it is unmeasured.

- A verified home needs a stamp whose seventeen rows pass for 2.1.287. One stands on disk, written by `viola
  verify` at the prior chunk's green record round: `target/e2e-home.disk/viola-record-20261006T211429Z/vhome/
  ledger/stamps.json` reads `2.1.287` 17 of 17 `pass` (read with a one-line python count). That directory is on the
  handoff's operator desk as the operator's to delete. Without it a verified home costs one full by-path verify,
  five `claude` starts.

- The first timing: the hint is a timer from the paste, 8.000 s between two footer draws, with the turn's Stop 1.5 s
  in (`rehearsal-shapes.md:102`, `:112`). A `send` placed before `turn-ended` reads `turn-running`, not the gate
  (`send.rs:324-327`), so the live `send` goes after the `turn-ended` record.

- `input-not-ready` has a second cause, a poisoned screen model (`screen.rs:128-130`), which writes
  `parse-rejected{parser:"vt100-feed"}` first. A live refusal is attributed to the hint only with no such line
  before it.

- `wait`, re-derived at HEAD (`src/run/wait.rs:135-170`; `src/cmd/wait.rs:1-4`): with no `--after` the scan starts
  at a held dialog's line, else **at the log's end at the call**, and only `turn-ended`, `question`, `permission`,
  `plan` and `session-end` wake it. In the hint window the turn's `turn-ended` is already logged, and the refused
  send's `send-refused` is a wrapper line that wakes nothing. So a `viola wait <name>` with no `--after` and no
  `--timeout-ms` parks with no deadline. With `--after` at a cursor before the `turn-ended` it returns that record
  at once, and a driver that then sends again is refused again while the hint stands. The freight's hypothesis is
  re-established by reading; the live run is its test.
- The hint string is `{name} was not ready for input; viola wait {name}, then send again` (`src/human.rs:215-217`).

- `GATE_MAX_WAIT` is referenced at `ledger.rs:16`, `:760`, `:761`, `screen.rs:132`, `:184` and
  `src/cmd/verify/typed.rs:28`, `:487` (graph `refs`): the sites a "longer bound" option would reach, with the
  `quiet-period` row's validation among them.

- The fake agent's hold is capped at 8 000 ms (`src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs:32`, `:105`), equal to the first
  reading: a longer second timing cannot be replayed through the hold unchanged.

title: M8 — what a kill leaves, and what stands at the root now

data.head: ### M8 — what a kill leaves, and what stands at the root now

body:
- `TrustedDir` is a drop guard (`src/cmd/verify/typed.rs:334-351`); `create` first removes a dir of the same pid
  name. No signal handling exists in `src/cmd/verify.rs`, `src/cmd/verify/typed.rs` or `src/main.rs`
  (`grep -n 'signal\|ctrlc\|SIGTERM'`: 0 hits). A kill runs no destructor, so the freight's claim holds: a killed
  verify leaves the dir of the run it was in.

- A leftover's name carries the pid alone, with no start time, so the repository's owner-record sweep (pid + start
  time, `tests/support/home.rs`) cannot be applied to it as it is.

- Standing at 2026-10-07T08:52:43Z: ten dirs dated 2026-10-06T22:12:45Z to 22:12:50Z, four `-dialogs` (empty) and
  six `-plan` (one entry each), beside the operator desk's `.viola-verify-2095228/`. None is a bare
  `.viola-verify-<pid>/`, which fits kills that landed during Run C or Run D. What killed them is not established.

title: Plan — 2026-10-07-send-waits-out-the-paste-hint: "Send waits out the paste hint"

data.head: # Plan — 2026-10-07-send-waits-out-the-paste-hint: "Send waits out the paste hint"

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-10-07-send-waits-out-the-paste-hint · **Version:** viola-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-07T12:12Z
- **Base commit:** `56e67bb33e63` (HEAD at P4)

On a verified CLI the readiness gate stops refusing a `send` at the first quiet instant of a screen that holds no
compiled literal. It keeps waiting for the input box, and refuses `not-delivered` / `input-not-ready` only when its
bound has run out; the bound, `GATE_MAX_WAIT`, moves from 5 s to 8.5 s. A `send` issued while the CLI's paste hint
stands is then delivered once the input box returns. This is the founder's ruling of 2026-10-07T10:29Z (scope
§Authority), built in `viola_agent_claude::screen` as architecture §Established Decisions [Screen Model] places it.

The wait is on the automation side only. Research found that `send` reads the wheel once, before the gate's wait,
so a human who starts typing during a wait of seconds would be pasted over. After the wait `send` now reads the
wheel and the running turn again and refuses with nothing typed (the overseer's answer, inputs#I2; a11y-plan §1
and architecture §Established Decisions [Human Takeover / Wheel]).

The moved bound is what the stamped `quiet-period` row is checked against, so the chunk ends with one by-path
`viola verify` of `claude` 2.1.287: 5 live starts, fired once, never retried (inputs#I1). No ledger row, no
compiled literal, no fixture, no product string and no knob is added.
**STOP list** (each stops the run and is reported; none is worked around):

- STOP 1 — the live round reads red (a failing row, a non-zero exit, a modal start). It is not fired again
  (inputs#I1). Report the round's step lines and summary as printed.

- STOP 2 — any step turns out to need a boundary widening (a new env seam, a new verify guard, a new crossing).
  It is held, not answered (inputs#I1).

- STOP 3 — a red whose shape is a stalled start: read `test -L target/e2e-home && findmnt -n -o FSTYPE -T
  target/e2e-home/`, report it, never re-run for green.
- STOP 4 — the planted-hang control of step 9 is not killed under a moved bound.

- STOP 5 — the keystroke case of step 10 cannot be sequenced on an observed signal on an OS leg. No sleep, no
  retry, no skip is the answer.

- STOP 6 — a product-source fix lands after the live round was fired (a CI red in `screen.rs`, `gate.rs`,
  `send.rs`, `ledger.rs` or `typed.rs`). The round is not re-fired; whether the stamp still stands for the fixed
  tree returns to the founder through the overseer.

0. **Open the records.** Create `evidence/` in the chunk folder. Every reading below is written there when it is
   taken, with its time read from `date -u`.

1. **Red before the fix** (`tests/cli_send.rs`, `send_under_the_paste_hint_on_a_verified_cli`). Turn the `hint`
   case's expectation to delivered: exit 0, `ok.cursor` equal to the end offset read before the second send, two
   prompts in the receipt, the second prompt's text equal to the second send's text, no `send-refused` record.
   Keep its 3 000 ms hold and the `no_hint` case as they are. Run the pair against the untouched product and
   record the `hint` case red (exit 13, `input-not-ready`) in `evidence/hint-red-green.md`.

2. **The verdict and the bound** (`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/screen.rs`).
   - `GATE_MAX_WAIT` becomes `Duration::from_millis(8500)`; its pin at `:184` reads the same literal; its doc
     comment names the measured 8.0 s hint timer it covers.
   - `Screen::verdict`'s last arm (`:147-151`): with signatures, on a quiet screen with no modal row, an
     input-box row is `Done(Ready)` as today; without one the verdict is `Wait` while `now - waiting_since <
     GATE_MAX_WAIT` and `Done(InputNotReady)` from the bound on. The poisoned arm, the not-quiet arm, the
     no-signatures arm and the modal read inside the row loop are not edited.
   - Cases, as labelled rstest tables with literal readings:
     - `verdict_verified_without_a_literal_waits_for_the_input_box`: a quiet verified screen with no literal reads
       `Wait` at 300 ms and at 8 499 ms, and `Done(InputNotReady)` at 8 500 ms and at 9 000 ms;
     - the same function family: the input-box row fed at 6 000 ms reads `Wait` at 6 299 ms and `Done(Ready)` at
       6 300 ms; a modal row reads `Done(InputNotReady)` at 300 ms; a poisoned screen reads it at 0 ms;
     - `verdict_reads_the_signatures` (`:269-286`): its `input_box_absent` and `empty_screen` rows become `Wait`;
       `resize_starts_a_blank_screen` (`:330-339`) reads `Wait`;
     - the two boundary tables (`verdict_at_each_boundary`, cases at `:210-214`, and
       `verdict_without_signatures_at_each_boundary`, cases at `:228-232`) read 8 500 and 8 499 in place of 5 000
       and 4 999, and their `quiet_after_the_maximum` rows read 9 000. Both keep `Ready` on a quiet screen: the
       verified table's screen holds the input-box row.
   - `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs:2012-2014`: the `quiet-period` row's cases read 8 500 and 8 501.

3. **The gate's cases** (`src/run/gate.rs`). `Gate::wait_ready` is not edited.
   - `wait_ready_verified_over_the_input_box_is_ready` (`:556-568`): its literal-less half moves to a new case,
     `wait_ready_verified_waits_for_the_input_box_until_the_bound`, on the stepping clock: it returns
     `(InputNotReady, false)` and the clock's last reading is 9 s past `base`, the first one-second step at or
     past the bound, never an earlier step.
   - `wait_ready_never_quiet_by_the_maximum_wait_is_input_not_ready` (`:578-587`) reads 8 500 ms.

4. **`send` reads its rungs again after the wait** (`src/run/send.rs`, between the gate's verdict at `:338-341`
   and `ctx.issue` at `:342`). When the gate returned `Ready`: a human-held wheel refuses `human-typing` with the
   wheel's own detail, exactly as the rung at `:314-320` does; else a running turn refuses `not-delivered` /
   `turn-running`. Nothing is issued and nothing is pasted for either. The in-flight slot is this send's own and
   is not read again. The doc comment of `send` states the two reads and their order.
   - Cases, clock-driven, with a verified gate where the wait is needed (a gate started with `Some(&SIGNATURES)`
     in the test module, beside `quiet_gate`):
     - `send_a_human_key_after_the_gate_wait_is_human_typing`: the wheel moves to the human while the gate waits;
       the reply is `human-typing`, the only record is `send-refused`, no paste was written;
     - `send_a_turn_started_after_the_gate_wait_is_turn_running`: a turn starts while the gate waits; the reply is
       `not-delivered` / `turn-running`, no `send-issued`, no paste;
     - `send_after_the_gate_wait_human_typing_comes_before_turn_running`: both happened; the reply is
       `human-typing`;
     - `send_on_a_verified_screen_without_a_literal_waits_for_the_input_box_to_the_bound`: the reply is
       `not-delivered` / `input-not-ready` once the clock passes 8 500 ms, the only record is `send-refused` with
       no cursor, no paste.

5. **Remove-the-guard controls** (one-shot, never committed; `.claude/rules/testing.md` 2026-09-25). For each of
   the three guards — the waiting arm in `Screen::verdict`, the wheel read after the wait, the turn read after the
   wait — neutralise the guard inside the function the cases call, show the named cases red, restore it, and
   check the restore (`git diff --quiet` against the step's own saved state is not enough: re-read the site).
   Run each control under the nextest `mutants` profile. Both readings of each go to
   `evidence/guard-controls.md`.

6. **verify's settle cases** (`src/cmd/verify/typed.rs:746-786`). `settled` and `box_wait` are not edited: they
   read the constant by name.
   - `settled_without_a_literal_waits_out_the_maximum` reads 8 499 / 8 500, and its late feed at 8 400 settles at
     8 700, not at 8 600;
   - `box_wait_keeps_waiting_past_the_gate_maximum_without_a_literal` adds 8 500 and 8 800 to its instants and
     reads `settled(.., 8 500)` as its control.

7. **The fake agent's cap** (`src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs:32-33`). `PASTE_HINT_CAP_MS` becomes 10 000 and its doc
   comment says why (verify's hint case holds past the gate's bound). The parse case at `:836-869` feeds a value
   above the new cap and reads 10 000 ms. The option stays argv-only and test-only; no option is added (the count
   stays eight).

8. **verify's hint case** (`tests/cli_verify.rs:1052-1061`). The hold becomes 9 000 ms, past the 8.5 s bound, and
   the doc comment states the new numbers. Its expectation is unchanged: `stamped 2.1.0  17 pass  0 fail`.
   The comments at `tests/cli_verify.rs:827` and `tests/support/verify.rs:444` state 8.5 s and about 35 s.

9. **The `verify_window_` kill lines** (`.config/nextest.toml`; the overseer's answer, inputs#I2).
   - `[profile.ci]` override `test(/verify_window_/)`: `period = "20s", terminate-after = 3` (60 s).
   - `[profile.mutants]` override `test(/verify_window_/)`: `period = "15s", terminate-after = 3` (45 s).
   - Both comments state the floor as four waits of 8.5 s, about 35 s (predicted from 20.5 s measured at 5 s;
     record what the first run measures). No other line of the file changes.
   - **Planted-hang control** (one-shot, never committed; testing.md 2026-09-28, extended 2026-10-05), in the form
     of `2026-10-05-permission-end-to-end/evidence/verify-window-hang-control.md`: a scratch sleep longer than
     the kill planted in `verify_window_without_screens_fails_every_interactive_row`, read under `--profile ci`
     (killed at 60 s), under `--profile mutants` (killed at 45 s) and under the default profile (passes, slow);
     then removed and the removal checked. All three status lines verbatim in
     `evidence/verify-window-kill-control.md`, with the unplanted test's own duration under each profile.

10. **The end-to-end cases** (`tests/cli_send.rs`).
    - The `hint` case turned at step 1 now reads green; record it in `evidence/hint-red-green.md` with its
      duration. Its doc comment (`:544-550`) states the new reading.
    - A new case, `send_under_the_paste_hint_a_human_key_during_the_gate_wait_wins`, on a stamped home with
      `--framing --turn-stop --paste-hint-ms 3000`:
      1. send the long text; wait for its `turn-ended` record and the Stop hook's receipt, as the pair does;
      2. start the second `send --json` without waiting for it (`spawn_send`);
      3. wait until the wrapper's role file holds that send's `channel-request` (the form of
         `tests/cli_answer.rs:203-215`): the send is now inside the gate;
      4. write one editing key into the outer PTY (`wrapper.send`);
      5. wait for the `wheel` record `{holder:"human", cause:"human-input"}`;
      6. the send exits 10 with `{"v":1,"refusal":"human-typing","detail":null}`.
      Asserted from literals: in `events.ndjson` after the long turn, the `wheel` record stands before the
      `send-refused` record and no `send-issued` stands between them; the receipt holds exactly one prompt (the
      long text) and, once the hold has ended, the key's own receipt line.
    - Both cases carry the tests-owned canary in every send text, read no screen, own no timer, and stay under
      the `mutants` profile's 10 s kill (the pair's refused case read 7.4 s with the same hold); record both
      durations.
11. **Local gates.** Run the fence's entries in order up to `pre-push`. A red is fixed at its cause.

12. **The live round** (last of implement's own steps, after `pre-push` reads green; 5 live starts, the whole of
    the cap).
    - Before it: write five `start` lines (`print`, `A`, `B`, `C`, `D`, each `cli` `2.1.287`) to
      `evidence/live-sessions.ndjson`, with the time.
    - Fire it once: `gate.py run --plan <this plan> --live-legs`. It runs the version probe, then the verify entry
      from the repository root (a folder trusted in Claude Code, its external import answered).
    - After it, green or red: append one `round` line (`fired` 1, the exit, the last stdout line) and one
      `census` line (`when` `after`, `own_left` = the count of this round's `.viola-verify-<pid>*` dirs still at
      the root or under the OS temp dir, and of `claude` processes whose cwd is one). Write
      `evidence/reverify-round.md`: the seventeen step lines and the summary as printed; from the round's
      `ledger/stamps.json` the seventeen row ids with their verdicts and `measured.typed_probe`'s
      `ready_settle_ms` and `turn_settle_ms`, each beside the 8 500 ms bound (testing.md 2026-10-06); the round's
      wall time; the home's path; the count of CLI transcripts the round left (the accepted residual).
    - The round's home stays where it is. It is not removed and not moved; its path is named in the report.
    - Red: STOP 1.
13. **Operator pass** (the fence's three `operator` entries): hygiene, the pre-CI commit and push, the CI read.

- `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-send-waits-out-the-paste-hint/evidence/` — the red-before and green-after
  readings, the guard controls, the kill-line control, the live-start ledger and the round's record

- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/screen.rs` — the verdict's last arm, the constant, its pin and the cases
  (`Screen::verdict`'s one product caller is `Gate::wait_ready @ src/run/gate.rs:169`)
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs` — the `quiet-period` row's two boundary cases
- `src/run/gate.rs` — two cases; the product code is untouched

- `src/run/send.rs` — the two reads after the gate's wait, the doc comment, four cases (`Gate::wait_ready`'s one
  product caller is `send @ src/run/send.rs:338`)
- `src/cmd/verify/typed.rs` — two cases' readings
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs` — the cap, its doc comment, its parse case
- `tests/cli_send.rs` — the `hint` case turned, the keystroke case
- `tests/cli_verify.rs` — the hint case's hold and two comments
- `tests/support/verify.rs` — one comment
- `.config/nextest.toml` — the two `verify_window_` overrides and their comments

The gates below are the standing lint, unit and default-selection entries, two filter entries that select only
this chunk's new cases, the harness smoke with G2 and G4 over its home, the native `pre-push`, and the one live
round. The smoke boots the fake agent on a stamped session, so verify's settles and the gate run under the moved
bound there.

The live round is two entries: the non-priming version probe, then `viola verify` by path. They are fired once,
by `gate.py run --live-legs`, and re-verified by the wrap from `evidence/`. The verify entry starts five `claude`
processes and nothing else; its `stop` terminates only a `claude` whose cwd is one of the round's probe dirs. The
product runs with `VIOLA_NAME`, `VIOLA_DIR` and `VIOLA_BIN` removed and `--home` given (testing.md 2026-10-07).
The harness's `run --local-live` is not used: it drives PATH `claude`, and this round names 2.1.287 by path.

Three controls mutate source or plant a hang and revert, so they are one-shot runs at implement and not entries:
step 1's red before the fix, step 5's remove-the-guard runs and step 9's planted hang. No mutation entry is
listed (testing.md 2026-10-04). The evidence files are records implement writes, not artifacts an entry produces.

The preservation guard names the base commit, because the operator pass's pre-CI commit moves HEAD onto the
chunk. A red whose shape is a stalled start is a finding about the backing (STOP 3).

data.head: ## Graph impact (from the code-graph query; plane `rust`, trace `tree-query-2026-10-07-send-waits-out-the-paste-hint.json`)

body:
- **`GATE_MAX_WAIT`** — 7 references outside its definition: `ledger.rs:16` (import), `ledger.rs:760`,
  `ledger.rs:761`, `screen.rs:132`, `screen.rs:184`, `typed.rs:28` (import), `typed.rs:487`. No other crate and no
  test target reads it by name; every other "5 s" is a literal in a case or a comment (the sweep below).

- **`Screen::verdict`** — one product caller, `Gate::wait_ready @ src/run/gate.rs:169`; eleven call sites in ten
  test functions of `screen.rs` (`:224`, `:241`, `:250`, `:263`, `:285`, `:295`, `:299`, `:325`, `:337`, `:393`,
  `:501`).

- **`Gate::wait_ready`** — one product caller, `send @ src/run/send.rs:338`; nine call sites in eight cases of
  `gate.rs`. The
  `wait_ready` rows under `crates/viola-e2e` and `tests/support/home.rs` are another function of the same name
  (the harness's boot readiness), not this one.

- **`settled`** (verify) — one product caller, `Run::settle @ typed.rs:599`; `box_wait` — `framing_turns @
  typed.rs:276`.
- **`PASTE_HINT_CAP_MS`** — one reference, `viola-fake-agent.rs:108`.

- **`send_hint`** — product callers `src/cmd/send.rs:149`, `:157`, `src/cmd/client.rs:154`; five cases in
  `human.rs`.
- **`CONFIRM_WINDOW_FALLBACK`** — unchanged by this chunk; `send.rs:178` and `:254`, `ledger.rs:763`.

- **The equality the remedy needs** (`screen.rs:122-152`): for a verified screen (`sigs` is `Some`), quiet for
  `QUIET_PERIOD`, with no modal row and no input-box row, the verdict must be `Wait` while `now - waiting_since <
  GATE_MAX_WAIT` and `Done(InputNotReady)` from the bound on. Today it is `Done(InputNotReady)` at once. The frame
  that produces the asserted quantity is the last arm; `waiting_since` already reaches it as a parameter, so
  `Gate::wait_ready` keeps its shape and its span.

- **The lock is per read** (`gate.rs:163-179`): the model's guard is dropped before the 20 ms sleep, so a wait of
  seconds stalls neither the feed thread nor the human's passthrough. Nothing here changes.

- **The wheel is read once** (`send.rs:314`, then `:338-345`): a human key during the gate's wait moves the wheel
  at once (architecture.md:70, "a read holding an editing key moves the wheel before it returns"), and the send,
  already past that rung, pastes when the gate reads `Ready`. Architecture records the same shape for a turn that
  starts during the wait as an accepted residual, "up to `GATE_MAX_WAIT`, 5 s". Before this build a verified
  literal-less screen ended the wait 0.63 s in; after it the wait can run to 8.5 s on every send that follows a
  long paste, so the same race has a window an order of magnitude longer.

- **A verified case with a fixed clock loops** (`gate.rs:562-567`): `wait_ready_verified_over_the_input_box_is_ready`
  reads a literal-less verified screen through `FixedClock(base + 300 ms)` and expects `InputNotReady`. Under the
  new arm that verdict is `Wait` forever on a fixed clock: the case must read at or past the bound.

- **Cases that turn by the arm** (verified, quiet, no literal, read at 300 ms): `screen.rs:271-272`
  (`input_box_absent`, `empty_screen`), `screen.rs:330-339` (`resize_starts_a_blank_screen`), `gate.rs:562-567`.
  The proptest at `screen.rs:499-502` reads a poisoned screen and stands.

- **Cases that turn by the constant**: `screen.rs:184` (the pin), `screen.rs:230-232` (5000 / 4999 / 6000),
  `gate.rs:579-587` (`from_secs(5)`), `typed.rs:748-756` (4999 / 5000 / 5100 / 5200), `typed.rs:776-785` (the
  `settled(.., 5000)` control), `ledger.rs:2012-2014` (5000 / 5001).

- **`send`'s unit cases are on the partial gate** (`send.rs:538-553`): `quiet_gate` and `poisoned_gate` start the
  gate with no signatures, whatever `cli_verified` the slot carries, so none of them turns by the arm.

- **The by-path round's firing form** (the 2026-10-06 plan's fence; its record `record-round-green.md`): a
  `role = 'probe'`, `leg = 'round'` entry running the 2.1.287 binary's `--version` by path, then a `leg = 'live'`
  entry `cargo build -q && target/debug/viola --home "$h/vhome" verify -- "$HOME/.local/share/mise/installs/claude/2.1.287/claude"`
  with a `stop` keyed on the probe dirs' cwd. The binary is present and executable at that path (read at P3). The
  2026-10-07 rule adds `VIOLA_NAME`, `VIOLA_DIR` and `VIOLA_BIN` removed. That round took 47.8 s and printed
  `stamped 2.1.287  17 pass  0 fail` as its last line.

- **A failing row still stamps** (arch history, 2026-09-28-capability-ledger-and-viola-verify): a red round writes
  a stamp with a `fail` row and exits 1. The round's home is its own, so a red round degrades no standing home.

- **Boundary cases as labelled literals** (`screen.rs:228-232`, `ledger.rs:2011-2016`): the bound's cases name
  8500 and 8499 as literals; the pin at `screen.rs:184` reads `from_millis(8500)`.

- **Clock-driven waits at the unit layer** (`gate.rs:232-249`, `send.rs:496-530`): `FixedClock`, `SteppingClock`
  and `JumpClock` are in the tree; no unit case sleeps.

- **A key into the outer PTY** (`tests/tui_wheel.rs:167`, `tests/support/home.rs:473`): `wrapper.send(b"h")`, the
  wheel read from the `wheel{holder:"human",cause:"human-input"}` record.

- **One human-stderr writer** (`src/human.rs`): a changed hint string changes at `:216` and its two pins, nowhere
  else.

- **The hint line, the lean P4 brings**: after this build the `input-not-ready` line is no longer printed for the
  paste-hint cause; the previous chunk's card said so under options 1 with 2. No amendment has ever changed a hint
  string of cli pattern 2 (design history), and a split by cause would be a new pattern beyond T4.

5. **The fake agent's hold.** `--paste-hint-ms` is capped at 8 000 ms (`src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs:33`), under an
   8.5 s bound. The cap is raised, as the founder was told.
   `[premise-corrected: the case that needs a hold past the bound is verify's own,
   verify_window_paste_hint_past_the_gate_maximum_still_stamps (tests/cli_verify.rs:1057), whose 6 000 ms hold is
   "past the gate maximum" only against 5 s]`
   The cap becomes 10 000 ms, for that case alone. Item 4's refusal is proved at the unit layer on the injected
   clock: no end-to-end case blocks to the bound, and the cross-process `input-not-ready` path keeps its
   end-to-end proof in the trust-dialog case (the overseer's answer, inputs#I2).

6. **The cases that turn.** `send_under_the_paste_hint_on_a_verified_cli` (`tests/cli_send.rs:551-554`, cases
   `hint` and `no_hint`): the `hint` case turns from refused to delivered. `Screen::verdict`'s own cases and the
   gate's cases (`src/run/gate.rs`) follow items 1, 2 and 4.

7. **The `input-not-ready` hint line.** Its advice is `viola wait <name>, then send again` (design-system `:764`,
   layout-templates `:415`; both re-verified at the take-up; the product string is `src/human.rs:216`). Whether
   that line changes is this entry's to settle (the second CARRY). Settled at P4: the line is left as it is, and
   no product string moves (the overseer's answer, inputs#I2). After this build it is no longer printed for the
   paste-hint cause; it stays for a modal, a screen that never goes quiet, a poisoned screen and a hint past the
   bound. Listed for the founder: the line still advises `viola wait` for those causes, and a rewording is his.

8. **No human keystroke is delayed.** The wait is on the automation side only: a key pressed while the gate waits
   goes to the child as today and takes the wheel. a11y-plan's keystroke clause is re-read at this build (the
   third CARRY; the clause stands at a11y-plan `:99`, `:624` and `:990`, re-verified). The chunk shows it with a
   case, not by argument.
   `[premise-corrected: the key is never held (the pump holds human bytes only across the one paste write, and the
   gate takes the model's lock per read, src/run/gate.rs:163-179), but send reads the wheel once, at its arrival
   (send.rs:314), and not again after the gate's wait: a human who starts typing during the wait is pasted over
   once the input box returns]`
   Settled at P4 (the overseer's answer, inputs#I2, a technical fork): after the gate's wait `send` reads the wheel
   and the running turn again, in the documented order, and refuses `human-typing` or `turn-running` with nothing
   typed. This tightens the residual architecture records for a turn that starts during the wait; it widens
   nothing. Listed for the founder as a fact.

9. **`send`'s longest block becomes 18.5 s** (8.5 s of gate, 10 s of confirmation). No bound in the tree was sized
   against 15 s: `viola send`'s client waits on `Client::request`, which has no deadline
   (`src/cmd/send.rs:227-228`), and the tests' `send` helper waits on the child with no bound of its own
   (`tests/cli_send.rs:139-150`). The MCP tool-call bound is an open architecture item and is not settled here.
   `[premise-corrected: what was sized against the gate's bound is the nextest verify_window_ class, which waits
   the maximum four times: .config/nextest.toml:23-27 and :54-58, 15 s x 3 on CI and 15 s x 2 under mutants,
   against about 21 s today and about 35 s at 8.5 s]`
   Settled at P4 (the overseer's answer, inputs#I2): both overrides move in proportion, 20 s × 3 on CI and
   15 s × 3 under `mutants`, with the planted-hang control read both ways in `evidence/`. No other kill moves, and
   `WITHIN` stays 7 s.

10. **The one by-path re-verify.** `GATE_MAX_WAIT` is the bound the stamped `quiet-period` row's measured settles
    are checked within (`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs:760-761`), and `viola verify`'s first settle uses
    it (`src/cmd/verify/typed.rs:487`); both sites re-verified. A moved bound loosens a stamped row's check, so the
    built binary runs `viola verify` once against `claude` 2.1.287 named by path: 5 live starts, each ledgered
    before it starts. A red round is not retried: stop and report (inputs#I1).
    - The round stamps a fresh home of its own under `target/e2e-home/`, as the 2026-10-06 record round did. It
      reads no standing home and nothing in `target/e2e-home.disk/`; nothing there is deleted by this chunk.
    - The round records no fixture: it is a re-verify, not a `--record` round.
    - A stamp is read by its row ids alone (`ledger.rs:919-927`), so a stamp written under the 5 s bound is still
      read as verified; the round is the founder's price, not a mechanical need of the tree.

11. **`viola verify`'s own settles.** The ordinary settle falls back at the first quiet instant past the bound
    (`typed.rs:478-498`), so it moves to 8.5 s on a screen with no literal; Run B's wait after a long paste
    (`box_wait`, `typed.rs:505-523`) reads `PROBE_DEADLINE` and does not move.

title: Plan — 2026-10-07-test-homes-off-the-contended-volume: "Test homes off the contended volume"

data.head: # Plan — 2026-10-07-test-homes-off-the-contended-volume: "Test homes off the contended volume"

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-10-07-test-homes-off-the-contended-volume · **Version:** viola-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-07T07:32Z
- **Base:** `b329083e0266` (HEAD when P4 wrote the gate entries)

On the Linux dev host, `<workspace>/target/e2e-home` becomes a link to a per-user, owner-only directory on tmpfs,
so the 52 MB pinned copy every test home takes no longer waits on the shared volume's dirty-page budget while
another builder links (per test-plan §5 Setup / teardown lifecycle and architecture §Occupied Resources →
Repository; the mechanism per inputs#I3). The homes' path string does not change, no product crate changes, and
no CI runner has a link, so CI keeps writing its homes to a real disk through the real `sync_all()`.

A small test-side keeper, in the two places that create homes, re-creates the link's target after a reboot clears
it and refuses a target that is not an owner-only real directory. G2's walk is written so that a linked scope is
descended.

The harness then creates and deletes outside the working directory through the link. That is a boundary
widening, ratified by the founder's own live answer of 2026-10-07T07:25Z, relayed by the overseer (inputs#I6).

The chunk's claim is a hypothesis until its last step: that the pinned copy is what stalls a real start. The
proof is one contended reading inside another builder's natural link: the stall measured on the shared volume
and, in the same seconds, the verify-driven tests green on the new backing.

title: Step 0 — the record before anything moves

data.head: ### Step 0 — the record before anything moves

body:
- Read `chunks/2026-10-07-test-homes-off-the-contended-volume/inputs/andromeda-inputs.json` and confirm inputs#I6
  is present: it is the word the link rests on. Absent or altered → stop and report; nothing below runs.

- Write `evidence/backing.md`: the authority line (the founder, 2026-10-07T07:25Z, relayed by the overseer,
  inputs#I6), `findmnt -n -o FSTYPE -T target/e2e-home/` as it reads now (btrfs at P4), and the listing of
  `target/e2e-home` (13 entries, 545 MB at P4: `ls -la`, `du -sh`).

title: Step 1 — the keeper in the root fixture chain

data.head: ### Step 1 — the keeper in the root fixture chain

body:
- Ownership is not read separately: the `tempdir_in` that follows succeeds in an owner-only directory only for
  its owner (`.claude/rules/testing.md`, the 2026-09-27 extension on a guard that repeats what the call already
  guarantees).
- The keeper creates the base's backing only. It never creates a `home`, and it removes nothing.

title: Step 2 — the same keeper in the harness

data.head: ### Step 2 — the same keeper in the harness

body:
- In `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/mod.rs` add `Workspace::ensure_e2e_home`, beside `e2e_home` (lines 84-86),
  with the contract of step 1 and an `io::Result<()>` in place of the panic: a refusal is an `io::Error` whose
  message is fixed and names no path. The harness crate takes no new dependency (research: it has neither
  `viola-state` nor `libc`; std's Unix metadata extensions are already used in `secret_scan.rs:240-241`).

- `start @ crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/boot.rs:128`: call it in place of `fs::create_dir_all(opts.ws.e2e_home())?`.
  A refusal takes the path a failed `create_dir_all` takes today and reads `build-failed` (`boot.rs:112`); no
  failure reason is added.

- `local_live @ crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run.rs:370`: call it after the build arm and before the verify
  start. A refusal fails the suite with the existing code `verify-exit-none`, the verify not started; no code is
  added to the list in the function's doc comment.

- The readers and the remover (`schema_check @ schema_check.rs:82`, `of @ secret_scan.rs:50`,
  `remove_session_home @ cleanup.rs:164`) do not call it and do not change.

- Inline cases in `mod.rs`'s test module, six functions named `e2e_home_backing_…`, the same six as step 1 with
  the refusal read as an `Err`; and in `run.rs`'s test module one case named `e2e_home_backing_local_live_…`,
  through the stand-in runner: a refused base fails the suite with `verify-exit-none` after exactly one runner
  call (the build). Seven functions carry the prefix in all.

- For each keeper, once: re-read the call site, replace the keeper call with the bare `create_dir_all` it
  replaced, confirm the edit landed, run that keeper's case 2 alone and record its red; restore the call, confirm
  it is back, run the case again and record its green (`.claude/rules/testing.md`, 2026-09-25 with its
  extensions). The red expected: `create_dir_all` over a link whose target is gone returns an already-exists
  error (research §A link's failure modes: measured as `mkdir(2)` EEXIST through python; Rust's arm is read by this
  very run).
- Both pairs go to `evidence/keeper-control.md`. No net change.

title: Step 4 — G2 descends a linked scope

data.head: ### Step 4 — G2 descends a linked scope

body:
- `scripts/g2-zero-panics.sh`, `count_panics` (lines 18-28): both `find` calls take their start point as
  `"$scope/"`. On a real directory the walk and its output are the same; a missing scope still reads empty.
  Nothing else in the script changes, `--probe` included.

title: Step 5 — set the backing (the builder, no root)

data.head: ### Step 5 — set the backing (the builder, no root)

body:
- Tell the operator in one line before it is done: what moves and where. It is a notice, not a question: write it
  and go on without waiting for an answer (the overseer, 2026-10-07T07:38Z, at the P5 review).

- With no viola test or harness session running: no process named `viola`, `viola-harness` or `viola-fake-agen`
  (the kernel's 15-character name) is alive, read with `pgrep -x` per name and never `pgrep -f`, which matches the
  asking shell's own command line (inputs#I3 records that trap); and `bash scripts/agent-run.sh cleanup` reads
  `"ok":true`:
  1. `mv target/e2e-home target/e2e-home.disk` (the 13 entries, nothing deleted);
  2. `mkdir -m 700 /tmp/viola-e2e-home-<uid>` with the user's numeric id;
  3. `ln -s /tmp/viola-e2e-home-<uid> target/e2e-home`.

- Append to `evidence/backing.md`: `ls -ld` of the link and of its target (the mode column and the type only, the
  owner as "the user"), `findmnt -n -o FSTYPE -T target/e2e-home/` (tmpfs), and `git status --short` showing
  neither the link nor `target/e2e-home.disk` (both are under the ignored `target/`).

- `/tmp` is the location the operator's directive names (inputs#I1). It is aged at ten days and shared with every
  session's scratch (research §The tmpfs candidates); the keeper does not care where the link points, so a move
  to another tmpfs is a re-link and no code.

title: Step 6 — the suite on the backing, quiet

data.head: ### Step 6 — the suite on the backing, quiet

body:
- Run the gate block below in order, through `bash scripts/agent-run.sh pre-push`. The entry after it, the reader
  of the contended reading (`jq -e -s …`), is red until step 8 has written its record: fire it then.

- A red that is about a path (a test comparing a home with a resolved path, a refused start) is not fixed by
  editing the test to pass: stop and report it with the test's name and its failure. The fallback the P4 answer
  leaves is the founder's mount, and that is a revision of this plan, not a step of it.

title: Step 7 — the boot smoke on the backing (/implement P3)

data.head: ### Step 7 — the boot smoke on the backing (/implement P3)

body:
- The gate block's six smoke entries boot a session on the backing, read G2 and G4 over its home and clean it up.
  /implement P3's own boot adds three one-shot readings, taken with a session booted and before its `cleanup`, and
  recorded in `evidence/smoke-on-backing.md`:
  - the one-off control of step 4: the old start point (`find target/e2e-home -path '*/diagnostics/*.ndjson'
    -print`) prints no file over the link, the new one (`find target/e2e-home/ …`) prints at least one;
  - the modes: the session's `home` 0700, its `diagnostics/*.ndjson` 0600, its pinned `bin/*/viola` 0700 (`stat -c
    '%a'`);
  - `grep -rc 'strict-modes-failed\|symlink-ignored'` over the home's `diagnostics/`: 0 in every file.
- Then `cleanup`, and `ls target/e2e-home/` showing no `viola-session-*` left.

- Never pipe `boot` (`.claude/rules/verification-harness.md`, 2026-09-25): each harness step's output goes to a
  file.

title: Step 8 — the contended reading (one natural window, 60 minutes at most)

data.head: ### Step 8 — the contended reading (one natural window, 60 minutes at most)

body:
- Tell the operator in one line before the watcher starts: it waits up to 60 minutes for another builder's link;
  per window it writes 260 MB to `target/contended-control/` on the shared volume and 260 MB to tmpfs, and runs
  the `cli_verify` binary once; at most three windows, so at most 780 MB on the shared volume in all. A notice,
  not a question, as in step 5: write it and start the watcher.

- The driver is a script in the session scratchpad; its text is copied to `evidence/contended-driver.txt`. It
  uses `start_probe.py` by path from the sibling checkout (inputs#I4) and the trigger of `window_watch.py`
  (inputs#I5): a window opens when `Dirty + Writeback` in `/proc/meminfo` stand at or above 100 MB on two
  consecutive one-second reads while a build process of another project is alive and none of viola's is.

- Before it waits: copy `target/debug/viola` to the scratchpad as the probe's payload, and run the quiet
  `binary(cli_verify)` gate entry once so the harness build is fresh.

- The driver's own control, before its first graded use, recorded in `evidence/driver-control.md`: fire it once on
  the quiet host with its trigger forced open, writing to a scratch file and not to the evidence record. Its line
  must carry a `control_write_med_s` under 7, and the reader's `jq` program run over that scratch file must exit 1
  (a quiet window is not a contended reading). The reader's other side was read at P5 over hand-minted lines (its
  `baseline`): a passing line exits 0, a stalled window with a failed suite exits 1.

- It appends one line to `evidence/contended-reading.ndjson` per window: `kind` (`reading`), `t_open` (UTC),
  `dirty_mb` at the open, `other_builds` (project name → process count), `control_write_med_s`,
  `control_write_max_s`, `backing_total_max_s`, `suite_passed`, `suite_failed`, `suite_wall_s`. Numbers and
  project names only: no path, and never the suite's document itself (its `artifact` field is an absolute path).

- A window whose `control_write_med_s` is under 7 (the 7 s of `tests/support/watch.rs` `WITHIN`, the bound a
  stalled start breaks) is not a contended reading: its line stays in the file, the driver cools down 30 s and
  waits for the next.

- The driver ends at the first window whose control reads 7 s or more, after three windows, or at 60 minutes,
  and then removes `target/contended-control/`.

- Outcomes:
  - a window at 7 s or more with the suite at 29 passed, 0 failed and the backing probe under 1 s: the proof.
    Fire the reader entry (`jq -e -s …`);
  - a window at 7 s or more with the suite red: the hypothesis is falsified in part (a write outside the home
    stalls a real start). Stop and report it with the failing tests' names and their logs; do not re-run for a
    green and do not move a bound;
  - no window at 7 s or more within the cap: stop and ask the overseer before any synthetic writer (inputs#I6).
    The chunk is not complete without the reading.

title: Step 9 — what the wrap needs to carry

data.head: ### Step 9 — what the wrap needs to carry

body:
- `evidence/backing.md` gains a closing section: `target/e2e-home.disk` holds the 13 entries that were in
  `target/e2e-home`, `viola-test-WYNVH7` among them (the handoff's operator desk names it at its old path); the
  one-line recipe after a `cargo clean` (step 5's `ln -s`, the `mkdir` done by the keeper); what a reboot does
  (the target is gone, the next start re-creates it); a home kept for a red reading no longer survives a reboot.

- `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-test-homes-off-the-contended-volume/evidence/` — `backing.md`,
  `keeper-control.md`, `smoke-on-backing.md`, `driver-control.md`, `contended-driver.txt`,
  `contended-reading.ndjson`
- `tests/support/home.rs` — the base keeper and its call in `TestHome::new`; everything else as it is
- `tests/cli_instance_state.rs` — the six `home_base_backing_` cases
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/mod.rs` — `Workspace::ensure_e2e_home` and its six inline cases
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/boot.rs` — the call at the session home's creation
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run.rs` — the call in `local_live` and its one case
- `scripts/g2-zero-panics.sh` — the two `find` start points

No live leg: the chunk drives no real `claude` (inputs#I1), so the block holds no `live` or `round` entry and no
liveness probe. The harness smoke boots the fake agent on the backing, and G2 and G4 are read over its home between
`status` and `cleanup`.

The contended reading's producer is step 8's one-off driver. It waits on another builder's link, so no reader can
re-run it, and it is absent from the fence for that reason: it is a one-off witness whose record goes to
`evidence/`, as a mutation kill run's does (`.claude/rules/testing.md`, 2026-10-04). The fence holds its reader
(`jq -e -s …`), which the wrap re-runs over the record. The driver's known-verdict control is implement's one-shot
run of step 8, in `evidence/driver-control.md`.

One control mutates source and reverts, so it is a one-shot run at implement and not an entry: step 3's
remove-the-guard pair for each keeper (`evidence/keeper-control.md`). On every re-run the two keeper entries hold
the same property. `evidence/backing.md` and `evidence/smoke-on-backing.md` are records implement writes (steps 0,
5, 7 and 9), not artifacts an entry produces, so no entry carries `artifact`; on a re-run the entry
`test -L target/e2e-home && findmnt …` holds the backing and the smoke entries hold G2 and G4 over it.
That entry reads the host: it is green only where the link is in force, which is this dev host.

Five builders share this host. A red whose shape is a stalled start is, from this chunk on, a finding about the
backing and not a reason to re-run: its log is read first, with what the other build dirs wrote in its window
(`.claude/rules/verification-harness.md`, 2026-09-29 and its 2026-10-06 extension).

title: Where a home's path comes from

data.head: ### Where a home's path comes from

body:
- Root chain: `TestHome::new` joins `target/e2e-home` to a compile-time manifest dir and takes
  `tempdir_in(base)` with prefix `viola-test-` (`tests/support/home.rs:117-126`, `:228-230`). No environment read.

- Harness: `Workspace::e2e_home` is `<root>/target/e2e-home` (`crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/mod.rs:84-86`); `boot`
  creates it and takes `tempdir_in` with prefix `viola-session-` (`boot.rs:128-131`); `--local-live` joins
  `viola-live-<pid>/home` and creates nothing itself (`run.rs:370-373`).

- So a backing set at the path `target/e2e-home` is seen by every home class and by `pre-push`'s `env -i`
  children, and a backing chosen through a variable is seen by none of those children.

- Two homes are elsewhere by design and stay there: `TestHome::outside_scan` (`viola-chaos-*` under the system temp
  dir, `tests/support/home.rs:139-150`) and the socket-path dir of `tests/channel_endpoint.rs:45` (`/tmp`).

- Under `env -i` the Unix socket dir is already `/tmp/viola-<uid>/`
  (`crates/viola-channel/src/endpoint.rs:39-45`): test-side viola state lives on that tmpfs today.

- `pin_exe` reads the exe whole and writes it through `replace_private_shared` when the copy is absent
  (`crates/viola-state/src/pin.rs:71-83`); the helper writes a temp file beside the target, sets its mode, writes,
  `sync_all`s (`fs.rs:267`) and renames. Callers: `pin_and_plugin @ src/cmd/run.rs:316` and
  `measure @ src/cmd/verify.rs:133` (graph, below). A stamped home is pinned by the fixture's `viola verify`.
- `target/debug/viola` is 52 118 312 B (`ls -la`). 25 starts at once are 1 302 957 800 B (25 × that size).

title: The product and a linked or mounted home

data.head: ### The product and a linked or mounted home

body:
- No product code canonicalises a home on Unix: `grep -rn canonicalize src crates` (viola-e2e excluded) reads
  `crates/viola-pty/src/sideload.rs:84,114` and `crates/viola-state/src/fs.rs:124,130` (Windows arms) and
  `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs:154` (the fake agent's cwd against its trusted root, neither a home). `pin_exe`
  takes `std::path::absolute`, which resolves no link (`pin.rs:75`).

- The strict-modes reader follows a link as `stat` does (`crates/viola-state/src/strict.rs:118-122`) and is called
  on `ledger/` and `ledger/stamps.json` only (`strict.rs:29-39`): no ancestor of a home is read.

- The three product-crate text hits for `e2e-home` are tests and a comment: `strict.rs:372-384` (inside the
  Windows-only `win` module's tests), `fs.rs:461-473` (`#[cfg(windows)]`), `fs.rs:456` (a literal in a unit test),
  `src/cmd/run.rs:925` (a test comment).

- Tests that compare a home path already canonicalise both sides where they read the kernel's view:
  `tests/tui_channel_fds.rs:43` (the `/proc/<pid>/fd` table) and `tests/cli_verify.rs:740`.
  `tests/cli_fake_agent.rs:789-790` compares the home with `workspace_path("target/e2e-home")` as strings, which a
  link leaves equal. Whether the whole suite passes over a link is not measured here; it is the plan's first
  reading under the link option.

- The owner sweep: `fs::read_dir(base)` then per-entry `file_type().is_dir()` (`tests/support/home.rs:48-75`). A
  `read_dir` of a link to a directory lists the target; the entries are real directories on either backing.

- G4 and the secret scan: `read_dir(root)` then `symlink_metadata` per entry
  (`crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/schema_check.rs:34-53`, `secret_scan.rs:209-221`). A link at the root is followed
  by the first `read_dir`; a link below it would not be.

- Harness `cleanup` removes `<e2e-home>/viola-session-*` after a string compare of the parent's parent with
  `ws.e2e_home()` (`cleanup.rs:155-168`): nothing canonicalises, so the compare holds on a link or a mount.

- Removals through a link (the security extract's question): yes. The sweep lists `base` and removes dead-owner
  dirs under it (`tests/support/home.rs:50-72`), a test home's drop removes its own dir (`:162-179`), and harness
  `cleanup` removes the session dir (`cleanup.rs:166`). With `target/e2e-home` a link, each of these creates and
  deletes in a directory outside the workspace. The harness's one sanctioned wipe outside the workspace is the
  guarded Windows mutation scratch (security extract, per security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Code Patterns);
  the removals here take only dirs the harness itself created (by owner record, by its own `TempDir`, by the
  `viola-session-` name), but the far side of the link is not the workspace. A mount keeps every such path inside
  the workspace as the kernel resolves it. `.andromeda/playbook.md:36-38` ("Boundary widening", verdict
  `escalate`) and `:49-51` (what ratifies it) are the patterns a link option is read against at P4.

- G2: `find "$scope" -path '*/diagnostics/*.ndjson' …` with `scope="$root/target/e2e-home"`
  (`scripts/g2-zero-panics.sh:18-28`, `:35`). Measured in the scratchpad with this host's `find` (bfs 4.1.1): a
  start point that is a link to a directory holding one matching file prints 0 files; the same start point with a
  trailing slash prints 1; with `-H` prints 1. So over a linked `target/e2e-home` a local G2 reads its fail-closed
  `empty scope`. G2 runs in CI's `test` and `perf` jobs (`ci.yml:136`, `:230`) and, locally, only by hand
  (`.claude/docs/commands.md:70-75`); `pre-push` does not run it (`grep -rn 'g2\|schema.check\|secret.scan'
  crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/pre_push.rs crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/pre_push/ crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/gate.rs`:
  0 hits).

  `:160` and `:253` (the `diag-*` upload globs), with `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES: "1"` at `:28` and `:211`. No runner
  has a link or a mount, so nothing CI executes changes under either backing.

- A dangling link: measured in the scratchpad, `makedirs(link, exist_ok=True)` over a link whose target is gone
  raises `FileExistsError` (`mkdir(2)` EEXIST; the path is a link and not a directory). Rust's
  `fs::create_dir_all` takes the same arm (an `mkdir` error on a path that is not a directory is returned), so
  after a reboot clears a tmpfs target, `fs::create_dir_all(&base).expect("e2e-home")` at
  `tests/support/home.rs:119` and `boot.rs:128` fail every start until the target is re-created. This is the
  equality a keeper rests on, and its remove-the-guard reading is the keeper's own red case.

- `cargo clean` removes the link with `target/` (`.claude/docs/commands.md:91` names what it removes today); the
  next start then creates a plain directory on the shared volume and the stall returns with no signal.

- `/tmp` is aged by systemd-tmpfiles (`/usr/lib/tmpfiles.d/tmp.conf:11`: `q /tmp 1777 root root 10d`): a file
  untouched for ten days is removed, which reaches a home kept that long and no live one.

data.head: ## Premises carried by the freight (closed at P3, `research.md`)

body:
- "measured at `af179a9`": a test start copies the running exe into its home, `pin_exe` through the private replace
  that ends in `sync_all()`; the exe is 52 118 312 B; `TestHome::new` puts every home under
  `<workspace>/target/e2e-home`, on the btrfs volume every builder shares; the host's `vm.dirty_bytes` is
  268 435 456. Verified at HEAD `b329083`: `crates/viola-state/src/pin.rs:71-83`,
  `crates/viola-state/src/fs.rs:267`, `tests/support/home.rs:117-126`; `ls -la target/debug/viola` reads
  52 118 312; `sysctl vm.dirty_bytes` reads 268 435 456; `findmnt -T target/e2e-home` reads btrfs
  `/dev/mapper/root[/@home]`. Both `viola run` (`src/cmd/run.rs:316`) and `viola verify` (`src/cmd/verify.rs:133`)
  pin, so a stamped home takes its copy at the fixture's `viola verify`.

- "Relayed, measured by overseer1 on 2026-10-07 inside two natural links of another builder and not re-run in this
  repository" (inputs#I3): one 50 MB write alone waited 13.0 s (0.006 s on a quiet host); 25 at once took 14.7 s
  with no fsync at all; the same 25 on tmpfs in the same seconds took 0.48 s. Verified against the snapshot (a
  pointer at andromedaV3 `1ed4a6ab`: its second-window table reads 13.01 s, 14.69 s and 0.48 s, its quiet-host row
  0.005 to 0.006 s). Still not re-run in this repository.

- "the reds of the 2026-10-06-local-command-and-paste-framing-rows wrap read ~18 s against nextest's 20 s kill".
  Verified: that chunk's `evidence/block-reds-host-contention.md` records a stall of about 18 s to 19 s per start
  and 22 tests at the 20 s kill; `.config/nextest.toml:31-33` gives the twelve verify-driven binaries 10 s × 2.

- **hypothesis:** "backing `target/e2e-home` with tmpfs on the dev host, the path unchanged, ends the stalled-start
  reds, and removing `sync_all()` would not (the no-fsync reading above)". What P3 re-established: the pinned copy
  is one buffered write of the whole exe per home, and inputs#I3 measured such a write stalled by another builder's
  link and unstalled on tmpfs. What P3 did not establish: that the pinned copy is the only write of a real start
  that stalls (the 2026-10-06 evidence says it "was not separated here", and a verify-driven start also writes
  small probe dirs under its cwd, on the shared volume). So it stays this chunk's hypothesis, W2's reading on real
  starts is its test, and a red there is a finding to report, not a result to work around.

- `/tmp` on this host is tmpfs (inputs#I1). Verified with `findmnt`: 31.3 G, 24.3 G available at 06:22Z (25.5 G at
  06:14Z: other sessions write there), options `rw,nosuid,nodev,usrquota` (no `noexec`), aged by systemd-tmpfiles

  Kept homes (`AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES` / `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_FAILED`) stay there until removed: a kept home's owner
  record is deleted (`tests/support/home.rs:173-176`), so no sweep takes it.

  (`e2e_home`), `boot.rs:128-131` (`viola-session-*`), `run.rs:370-373` (`viola-live-<pid>`). Both test-side

- `[premise-corrected: the three text hits are test code and a comment, no product branch reads the path]` Product
  code does not name `e2e-home`: `crates/viola-state/src/strict.rs:372-384` and `fs.rs:461-473` are Windows-only

- The backing is a Linux dev-host matter only: Windows, macOS and CI runners keep the present one. Verified for a

- What is in `target/e2e-home` today survives the change or is dispositioned by the operator. Verified by listing:

**Dialogs that arrive by themselves.** If the builder raises a `permission` dialog during a skill turn, the driver
answers it by its id inside the deadline: `{"behavior": "allow"}` when the tool call is a read, or one of the
skill's own tool scripts under `~/.claude/skills/`; `{"behavior": "deny", "message": "not part of this test"}` for
anything else. Each is a `step` line (`id: "permission-<n>"`). A dialog not answered inside 60 s renders for the
human by contract; with nobody at the desk the turn then holds: record it and end the session (S5 decides the rest).

- `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-08-first-live-test-and-self-drive/evidence/` — to write:
  `classifier-pins-first.md`, `reply-probe-fixed.ndjson`, `live-run.ndjson`, `operator-pass.md`; to bring up to
  the end of the live work: `live-run.md`, `compositor.md`, `live-sessions.ndjson`, `live-readings.ndjson`;
  standing from the earlier runs and revisions: `key-probe.md`, `focus-diag.sh`, `focus-diag.log`,
  `hint-pins-first.md`, `comp-probe.md`, `live-compositor.sh`, `live-compositor.lua`, `live-start.sh`,
  `live-drive.py`, `key-probe-own.sh`, `key-probe-own.md`, `reply-probe.sh`, `reply-probe-child.py`,
  `reply-probe.ndjson`, `terminal-replies.md`, `live-run-start6.ndjson`, `local-live.md`, `round-072838Z.txt`,
  `gap-list.md`

- `src/human.rs` — the `input-not-ready` arm of `send_hint` (`:216`) and its two pins (`:371`, `:406`), changed by
  the first implement run; callers unchanged: `unable @ src/cmd/send.rs:149`, `unreachable @ src/cmd/send.rs:157`,
  `unable_unreachable @ src/cmd/client.rs:154` (research, Graph impact)

- `src/run/wheel.rs` — the seven reply shapes in `is_reply` (`:475-504`), its doc comment (`:473-474`), and the
  classifier's test tables (`REPLIES @ :518`, `classifier_typing_is_editing @ :537-559`, one new rstest); its one
  caller is `step @ src/run/wheel.rs:430`, and `feed`'s is `read @ src/run/wheel.rs:308`: no signature moves
  (research, Graph impact)

The gates are the standing lint, unit and default-selection entries, two census reads of the hint line, the
preservation guard, the harness smoke with G2 and G4, the native `pre-push`, the product build, the live round (its
non-priming probe and the one `run --local-live` firing), three readers of the evidence ledgers, and the operator's
push and CI reads.

The live round is fired once, by /implement, through `gate.py run --live-legs`; the wrap never re-runs it and
re-verifies it from `evidence/`. Step 0's compositor start and key probe, the live sessions of steps 6 to 9 and
the end reading of step 9a are driven by /implement by hand, step by step, and are not entries: each needs a window
on the own compositor, a guard read at the moment of the key, or a reading of the desktop lock at its own moment,
and the compositor is started once. Their verdicts are the three reader entries, which the wrap's light gate re-runs over the committed
ledgers. Each reader is red until its step has written its record. The evidence files the criteria name are written
by /implement from those hand-driven steps and from the live entry's printed document, so no entry carries one as
its `artifact`.

The round was fired once, by the second implement run (`evidence/round-072838Z.txt`, `round: COMPLETE`). It is
NOT fired again: the re-entered run fires no `--live-legs`, and the two round entries stay listed for the wrap,
which re-verifies them from `evidence/`.

The second revision adds two readers of the reply probe. The first reads the committed record of the probe before
the fix, `evidence/reply-probe.ndjson`: exactly the seven shapes read as typing. It is the red half of the
red-green pair, pinned. The second reads `evidence/reply-probe-fixed.ndjson`, which step 5c writes: the same 23
queries on the fixed product build, none read as typing, the seven shapes each answered by the terminal, and the
three typed keys each taking the wheel. Step 5c's windows are driven by /implement by hand, like the live
sessions: they need the standing compositor.

The pin-first readings of step 1 and step 5a are one-shot runs at implement, recorded in `evidence/`, not entries:
each needs the tree with the pins changed and the producer not.

The release-check entry clears the product package's cached build before it builds: with nothing to rebuild, its
`artifact` atom read the binary as older than the run (the second implement run's first firing read red on that
alone, with its exit and its last line holding).

The live entry clears the prototype's `VIOLA_NAME`, `VIOLA_DIR` and `VIOLA_BIN` from the harness's environment, as
the by-path re-verify of chunk 2026-10-07-send-waits-out-the-paste-hint did. `CI` is not set in this session
(research M2); under it the entry would refuse `live-in-ci`.

No mutation entry is listed (the mutation run is the epoch boundary's). The preservation guard names the base
commit, because the operator pass's pre-CI commit moves HEAD onto the chunk. No push goes out while an entry of this
block is red by its own letter.
