title: 1. The typed text holds no CR

data.head: ### 1. The typed text holds no CR

body:
- Source: the entry's title and its CARRY. **The founder's ruling**, 2026-10-09T16:51Z, live in the overseer's
  dialog with both inner readings shown (the other options shown: refuse before typing; leave as measured), relayed
  by the operator at the 2026-10-09-epoch-3-cleanup wrap (that chunk's `inputs/I9-relay-1.md.txt`, re-read at P1)
  and placed as an entry of its own at the head on the operator's answer (that chunk's `inputs/I10-relay-2.md.txt`,
  re-read at P1): `send` types a
  CR or a CRLF inside a text as the LF the CLI submits, so such a send is confirmed.

- Today, re-read at P1 at HEAD `3c5e012` (the file is unchanged since `211da16`, the sha the entry names):
  `viola_agent_claude::hook::typed_text` is `text.trim_end_matches(['\r', '\n'])`
  (`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/hook.rs:207-209`). It returns a slice of the received text, so it can remove an
  ending and nothing else.

- The rule as this chunk reads the ruling: inside the typed text every CR LF pair is one LF and every other CR is
  one LF, and the trailing CR and LF characters still go, every one of them. The typed text then holds no CR
  anywhere. The order of the two steps does not change the result. Closed at P3 (research.md §Scope premise
  closure): the match is an equality on the in-flight typed text (`src/run/send.rs:130`) and the paste is one write
  of that same text (`crates/viola-pty/src/pump.rs:77-88`), so a typed text with LF where the received text held a
  CR is what both read. The exact wording of the rule is shown on the P5 review card.

- `Measured at chunk 2026-10-09-epoch-3-cleanup on live claude 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host
  (evidence/live-run.md, evidence/live-readings.ndjson, after-inner-crlf and after-inner-cr): the CLI submitted a
  pasted text's inner CR LF as one LF, and its lone inner CR as one LF.` Spot-checked at P3: the record file holds
  the two `reading` lines and the two `equality` lines (lines 7 to 10), and `hook.rs` is unchanged since the build
  those readings ran on.

- `hypothesis: every inner CR and every inner CR LF is submitted as one LF wherever it stands (two single
  readings, one text each)`. `Not measured: several inner CRs, an inner LF CR, any CLI version but 2.1.287.` Closed at
  P3 as not leaned on: with the rule no `send` types a CR, so no step rests on what the CLI does with one. It stays
  the entry's hypothesis, unverified here.

- [premise-corrected: research.md §Scope premise closure — no recorded measurement of an LF typed inside a paste
  exists] With the rule `send` never types a CR. What is leaned on instead is that the CLI submits a pasted text's
  inner LF unchanged. That is already leaned on today by every multi-line `send`, and it is **not measured**: the
  two compiled paste literals of `viola verify` hold no newline, the five LFs of the recorded `paste-1` prompt are
  the CLI's own frame, and no reading in the two live record files sent a text with an LF inside it. The two inner
  readings show the CLI turning a typed CR into an LF, never what it does with a typed LF. So no ledger row and no
  recorded reading covers the shape. By the scope's own boundary this goes to the operator as a P4 card, with the
  options priced: a live reading in this chunk's planned start, or an eighteenth ledger row with a fifth Run B
  paste.

- `Today the typed text still holds the CR, so the exact match fails, the prompt is filed human, the wheel goes to
  the human and the send ends not-delivered / no-prompt-submitted, exit 13, though the text was delivered and
  answered.` Verified at P3: the in-flight text is the typed text (`src/run/send.rs:341-345`), `SendSlot::claim`
  compares it for equality (`:130`), and a prompt the hook filed `human` that is not claimed moves the wheel
  (`:242-244`).

- **Answered at P4 (`inputs#I2`; the overseer, 2026-10-09, in the P4 dialog, three options shown with their
  prices).** The live reading, and the row stays owed. The planned start sends a text with one LF inside and no CR
  first, as a control with a prediction, then the CR shapes; the readings are recorded as measured on 2.1.287. No
  ledger row, no fifth Run B paste, no re-stamp: the count stays seventeen. Nothing is widened and nothing is ruled
  about the reach of `v1-34`: the row for this shape stays owed to it, beside its two owed rows. A control that is
  not confirmed ends the live work and is reported.

- Source: the CARRY: "With the ruling the text `send` types is no longer the received text less an ending, so what
  `text_bytes`, the local-command classification and the in-flight match read is settled at take-up."

- Today, re-read at P1 in `src/run/send.rs:320-366`: `validate_paste_text` runs on the text as received, then the
  typed text is taken once, and the empty-text check, `classify`, the in-flight text, `ctx.issue(text.len())`
  (`text_bytes`) and the paste all read that one value. The client (`src/cmd/send.rs:190-197`) reads it only for
  the empty-text check.

- Settled here as the rule the masters already state, kept: the typed text is taken once and is the only text
  `send` uses. So the in-flight match, the paste, `text_bytes`, the local-command classification and both
  empty-text checks read the typed text with its inner CRs already turned to LF. `text_bytes` for a text with CR LF
  pairs is then smaller than the sent byte count by one per pair. Verified at P3: one value feeds all five reads in
  the wrapper (`src/run/send.rs:323`, `:324`, `:334`, `:342`, `:365`, `:366`), and the paste span's own
  `text_bytes` is the length of the text it is handed (`crates/viola-pty/src/pump.rs:75`).

- The local-command classification gains no new member from this: a listed command holds no newline, a text with
  an inner newline is never exactly a listed command, and the trailing case (`/clear` and a CRLF is `/clear`)
  already stands. Verified at P3: the compiled list is two entries, `/clear` and `/remote-control`
  (`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs:151-154`), neither holding a CR or an LF.

- A text of only CR and LF characters stays `empty-text` by the same check; its hint line does not change.
  Verified at P3: every CR becomes an LF and every trailing LF goes, so nothing is left; the hint is the fixed
  string at `src/human.rs:216`, which no step touches.

- Validation is unchanged: `validate_paste_text` runs first, on the text as received, and CR stays an allowed
  character. No refusal detail is added and none changes its rung. If P3 or P4 finds one is needed, it is a P4 card
  (`inputs#I1`).

- **Base:** `396c108ba64c` (HEAD when this plan was written; the preservation guard reads against it)

The wrapper gets a real budget gate. It reads the newest usage reading from `budget.json` at three points
(start, a `send`'s arrival, each `turn-ended`), compares it with two thresholds from `config.json`, refuses an
automated `send` with `budget-paused` while a window is over its threshold, and lifts the pause when that
window's reset passes or when the human runs `viola release <name> --budget` (per architecture §Established
Decisions [Budget Governor]; test-plan §6 Path 6; obs-plan §4 Scenario: Budget governor). It also writes the
`budget-gate` lines and the snapshot fields the log replay already reads.

Two defects in shipped code are fixed, each with its own acceptance and witness (`inputs#I1` note 3). Both were
measured at P3 (research.md, Measured at P3): `viola revive` over a group-writable home narrows the home and
refuses for a later cause, and `viola hook statusline`'s refusal of such a home lasts one invocation. Both arms
then check before they open anything under the home, and a refused check writes no log line (`inputs#I3`,
question 1).

Nothing here starts the real `claude`, adds a ledger row or a `viola verify` child, or re-stamps a home: those
are the founder's (`inputs#I1` note 2). Everything is built and rehearsed under the fake agent, and step 15
holds the operator pass until his word on the review card's items is recorded. The chunk claims no capability
(Implementation notes).

1. **`viola-core`: `Percent` and the window word** (`crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs`). Add `Percent`, a `nutype`
   newtype over a whole number that admits 0 to 100 and nothing else, built only through its `try_new`
   (research.md finding 2: it does not exist). Add a closed enum of the two window words beside `HumanTyping`,
   `BudgetWindowKind` with `FiveHour` and `SevenDay`, whose `as_str` gives `five-hour` and `seven-day`. No new
   dependency: `nutype` and `serde` are `viola-core`'s two.

2. **`viola-state`: the reader and the snapshot field.**
   - `crates/viola-state/src/budget.rs`: add `read_budget(home)`, which returns the stored `BudgetReading` or
     nothing. An absent `budget.json` returns nothing and creates no file. Otherwise it runs
     `strict::check_path` on the home and on `budget.json`, takes a shared lock on `budget.json.lock`, reads
     through `take(MAX_FRAME + 1)`, and returns nothing when a check refuses, when the bytes pass `MAX_FRAME`,
     when they do not parse, or when `v` is not 1. It never writes `budget.json`.
   - `crates/viola-state/src/snapshot.rs`: add `budget_override_until`, an optional string, additive in the
     form `cwd` has (`#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`); the envelope's `v` stays 1.
     Add the field at each of the 12 `InstanceSnapshot` literal sites (research.md, Graph impact: 18 hits of
     `grep -rn -E '^\s*budget_paused: ' --include=*.rs src crates tests`, 6 of them `Replayed` literals).

3. **The thresholds** (`src/run/budget.rs`, new; `src/obs.rs`). A `Thresholds` pair of `Percent`, defaults
   `five_hour` 90 and `seven_day` 85, and `read_thresholds(home)`: its own bounded read of `config.json` in the
   shape of `read_env_keep` (`src/run/env.rs:31-67`). The keys are top-level `five_hour` and `seven_day`. A
   value that is not a whole number from 0 to 100 gives that key's default and one
   `ConfigRejection::Malformed`; the other key stands; an absent, unreadable or malformed document is
   `read_diagnostics_level`'s to report, once. `CONFIG_KEYS` (`src/obs.rs:33`) gains the two names so they are
   not counted as unknown.

5. **The gate** (`src/run/budget.rs`). One `BudgetGate` per wrapper: the last recorded state (paused with its
   window facts, or open, and the override's end) under one `Mutex`, with the instance's name, directory,
   home, thresholds and the shared `Snapshots`. `evaluate(trigger, instant)` reads `budget.json`, decides,
   and, only when the triple (paused, window, override end) differs from the last recorded one, appends one
   `budget-gate` line through the shared append (`paused`; `window` when paused; `override_until` when an
   override stands; no other key) and updates the snapshot's `budget_paused` and `budget_override_until`
   through `Snapshots::update`, inline, before it returns. It is declared
   `#[instrument(skip_all, name = "run.budget_eval", fields(trigger, paused, window))]` with `trigger` one of
   `start`, `send`, `turn-ended`. It starts no thread and holds no timer.

6. **The start** (`src/cmd/run.rs`). `start` reads the thresholds, reports a rejection through
   `obs::log_config_rejection`, and builds the gate. `start_state` takes the gate's first verdict (trigger
   `start`) and uses it for the first snapshot's `budget_paused` and for the second start record, in place of
   the constants at `:519` and `:534`: exactly one `budget-gate` is appended at start, as record two. No prior
   snapshot is read (`inputs#I3`, question 4). `revive` starts through the same `start` and gets the same.

7. **The `send` rung and the `turn-ended` point** (`src/run/send.rs`, `src/cmd/run.rs`).
   - `SendSlot` holds the gate in a `OnceLock`, set by `start` as `io` is. In `send`, directly after the
     first `human-typing` read (`src/run/send.rs:329-335`) and before the running-turn read, the gate is
     evaluated with trigger `send`; a paused verdict returns the refusal `budget-paused` with the window word
     as detail, through the one `send-refused` emitter, with no cursor and no `send-issued`. The process-log
     line carries `window`, `used_percentage`, `resets_at` and `paused: true` beside the fields every wrapper
     refusal carries. The gate is not read when an earlier rung refused, and not read a second time after the
     readiness gate's wait.
   - In `Methods::dispatch` (`src/cmd/run.rs:113-118`), after `append_hook_event` has appended a line of kind
     `turn-ended`, the gate is evaluated with trigger `turn-ended`. `append_hook_event`'s signature stands
     (21 callers, research.md Graph impact).

8. **`release` in the wrapper** (`src/run/wheel.rs`, `src/cmd/run.rs`). `WheelSlot::release` takes the gate.
   The string-`from` refusal and the `budget` type check stay first and unchanged. With `budget: true` the
   gate's `lift` runs and the wheel is not touched: when the last recorded state is paused, it records the
   override (its end is the crossed window's `resets_at`) as a `budget-gate` line and a snapshot update, and
   the method answers only after both landed (`-32603` otherwise) with `wheel`, `budget_paused: false` and
   `override_until`; when no pause stands it records nothing and answers `wheel` and `budget_paused: false`
   (`inputs#I3`, question 3). `lift` does not evaluate. A plain `release` answers the gate's recorded
   `budget_paused` in place of the constant.

9. **The verb, its lines and the hint** (`src/cmd/release.rs`, `src/cmd/pause.rs`, `src/human.rs`,
   `src/cmd/send.rs`).
   - `ReleaseArgs` gains `--budget`; `wheel_call` takes the extra params and hands its line writer the `ok`
     payload (its 2 callers, `pause` and `release`, change with it).
   - `src/human.rs`: the lifted line, `<name>  budget gate lifted until <end>  wheel <holder>`, where `<end>`
     is the override's end as `HH:MM:SS` and `Z` when it falls on the current UTC date; the `budget-paused`
     arm of `send_hint` with the design's text, quoted at `design-system.md:760`: "budget gate is closed; it
     lifts at the window reset, or when the human lifts it"; and `no_hint_names_release` gains the cause.
   - Two lines have no words in any master and are built in a **planning form**, each on the review card for
     the founder's wording (`inputs#I3`, question 3): with no pause standing,
     `<name>  budget gate open  wheel <holder>`; with an end on a later UTC date, `<end>` is the date, a space,
     the time and `Z`.
   - `src/cmd/send.rs` `Out::unable` asks `send_hint` for the `budget-paused` reason too.

10. **`viola revive`: the check before the log** (`src/cmd/revive.rs`, `tests/cli_revive.rs`). The start arm
    resolves the home and the instance directory and runs `check_instance` first. A refusal prints the
    state-files pair through `Refusal::write` and returns exit 1 with no log opened and no line written, as
    `list` does (`:202-208`). Only then `open_wrapper_log` and the rest of the preflight, which loses its
    strict-modes reading (`preflight_order` takes three readings: holder, session, directory). Witness, a
    `cfg(unix)` case over a stopped `builder` with a logged session and a standing recorded directory: the
    home is set to 0770, `viola revive builder` exits 1 with the state-files pair, the home reads 0770
    afterwards, `run-builder.ndjson` has gained no line and the fake agent was not started again. The landed
    case `revive_refuses_state_another_user_could_write` now asserts no added line in place of the
    `process-exit` line.

11. **`viola hook statusline`: nothing after a refused check** (`src/cmd/hook/statusline.rs`,
    `tests/hook_statusline.rs`). When `check_instance` refuses, the arm returns exit 0 at once: it reads no
    `config.json`, opens no role file, logs nothing. `handle` loses its `trusted` argument and the
    `strict-modes-failed` outcome. Witness, a `cfg(unix)` case: over one home set to 0770, two invocations in
    a row each exit 0 with empty stdout and stderr, the marker file and `budget.json` are unchanged after
    each, the home reads 0770 after both, and `hook-builder.ndjson` has gained no line.

12. **The root cases** (`tests/support/statusline.rs` new, `tests/support/mod.rs`, `tests/cli_budget.rs` new,
    `Cargo.toml`, `.config/nextest.toml`). The runner and the payload builders move from
    `tests/hook_statusline.rs` into `tests/support/statusline.rs`; a fed `resets_at` is a fixed literal far
    ahead of any run, or far behind it for the passed-window case. `tests/cli_budget.rs` starts every case
    from `stamped_home` (research.md finding 16), feeds readings only through `viola hook statusline`, and
    holds:
    - `path6_a_reading_over_the_threshold_refuses_the_send`: `five_hour` 91 fed, `send --json` exits 11 with
      the document `{"v":1,"refusal":"budget-paused","detail":"five-hour"}`; one `budget-gate` record with
      `paused: true` and `window: "five-hour"`; one `send-refused` event with no cursor and no `send-issued`;
      the wrapper's `send-refused` line and the client's `process-exit` with `exit_code` 11; the snapshot's
      `budget_paused` true; the outer PTY shows none of `unable`, `hint:` or `budget-paused`; then a human key
      reaches the child (its `key` receipt).
    - `path6_the_boundaries_and_the_window_word`: in one session, `seven_day` 86 → detail `seven-day`;
      `five_hour` 90 → `five-hour`; `five_hour` 89 with `seven_day` 84 → the `send` exits 0.
    - `path6_an_unknown_or_passed_reset_does_not_pause`: a malformed `resets_at` is `"unknown"` in
      `budget.json` and the `send` exits 0; a `resets_at` that has passed, the same.
    - `path6_release_budget_lifts_the_pause`: a plain `release` leaves the `send` refused; `release builder
      --budget --json` answers `budget_paused: false` with `override_until`; the `budget-gate` record's
      `override_until` is later than its `ts` and equals the snapshot's `budget_override_until`; no `wheel`
      record is added; the next `send` exits 0; a second `release --budget` adds no record.
    - `path6_the_refusal_hint_never_names_release`: human mode with `VIOLA_NAME` set: the struck `unable` line
      with `budget-paused  five-hour`, then the hint as the last stderr line, holding no `release`; exit 11.
    - `path6_a_turn_end_closes_the_gate`: a reading fed while a turn runs; after the scripted `turn-ended`
      line, one `budget-gate` with `paused: true` follows it, with no `send`.
    - `path6_a_restart_pauses_again`: a pause, an override, a clean stop, a second start over the same home:
      the second life's second record is `budget-gate` with `paused: true` and no `override_until`.
    - `e5_the_replay_reads_what_the_wrapper_wrote`: after the pause `viola_state::replay::replay` reads
      `budget_paused` true; after the override, false with the `budget_override_until` the wrapper wrote; all
      three skip counts read 0.
    `Cargo.toml` gains the `[[test]]` entry (`required-features = ["fake-agent"]`); `binary(cli_budget)` joins
    the 20 s line at `.config/nextest.toml:32`.

13. **The remaining cases.**
    - Unit, named for the filter entry: `percent_*` (step 1); `budget_read_*` (step 2: a round trip with
      `write_budget`; absent creates nothing; over the cap; unparseable; `v` 2; a 0770 home on Unix;
      `budget.json`'s bytes and mode unchanged by a read); `thresholds_*` (step 3: `101`, `-1`, `"90"`, each
      key alone); `gate_decide_*` (step 4: 89 / 90, 84 / 85, both crossed, each unknown form, no reading, a
      passed reset, a standing and an expired override, after which the verdict is `budget-paused` with
      `five-hour` again); `gate_eval_*` (step 5: a line only on a change, the keys of each line, the snapshot
      after each); `gate_release_*` (step 8: with and without a pause; two gates over one `budget.json`, an
      override on one alone); `send_budget_paused_*` (step 7: after `human-typing`, before `turn-running`, no
      cursor, not read when the wheel is the human's).
    - The landed unit cases that pin `release`'s constant answer, `preflight_order`'s four readings, the
      arm's refused outcome and `send_hint`'s cause list are restated to what steps 8 to 11 land.
    - `tests/cli_controls_not_disableable.rs`: three rows, `five_hour` set to `101`, `-1` and `"90"` in
      `config.json`: after `five_hour` 91 is fed, a `send` exits 11.
    - `crates/viola-state/tests/state_replay.rs` and `state_events.rs`: a `budget-gate` line with `window`,
      and one with `override_until`, replay to their values and read back with zero skip counts.

14. **The red and green readings** (`chunks/2026-10-10-budget-governor/evidence/red-green.md`, written by
    /implement). For step 10's and step 11's witnesses: the case red on the tree before its fix, green after.
    For the `send` rung and for `read_budget`'s check: the guard neutralised inside its own function, the
    case red, the guard restored, the case green. Each reading with its command and its time from the clock.
    On the red tree step 10's witness lets a child start: it is the fake agent, first on that process's
    `PATH`, with a null stdin, so it ends at once (`revive_command`, `tests/support/home.rs:734-746`); the
    case's own `Running` guard ends whatever is left (`tests/support/cli.rs:58-64`).

15. **The founder's four items: landed on the operator's word, the hold lifted** (revised 2026-10-10,
    `inputs#I6`; before the revision this step held the operator pass for the founder's own answer).
    Steps 1 to 14 are done and are not re-entered. Their evidence: the implement run dir's trail
    (`.andromeda/runs/2026-10-10T21-29-10-implement/gate-2026-10-10-budget-governor.json`), whose two `run`
    calls each read `entries 16 · green 13 · red 0` with `not-run 3` (the three operator entries) and whose
    last `scope` call reads `scope: clean — changed 31 · listed 31`; and step 14's four red and green pairs in
    `evidence/red-green.md`. /andromeda-implement re-enters at step 16.
    By the operator's word the operator pass no longer waits for the founder's answer. The four items land in
    their planning forms, as built:
    - the `rate_limits` dependence: the refusal flows with no row. No row, probe, re-stamp or live `claude`
      start is made by this chunk (`inputs#I1` note 2 stands). The row and its probe stay owed: the entry's
      third CARRY placed them here, so the wrap's route step asks the operator for their next owner;
    - the wrapper refusing a driver on `budget.json` lands as step 2 builds it. The wrap records it as NOT
      ratified, the founder's word owed, and never as ratified: the playbook's pattern "Boundary widening —
      what ratifies it" (`.andromeda/playbook.md:48-50`), answered for this chunk by the operator, 2026-10-10
      (`inputs#I6`), which is no ratification;
    - a refused check writes no log line on `revive`'s start arm and leaves no trace on the statusline arm
      (steps 10 and 11);
    - the two human lines stand as step 9 words them.
    None of the four is recorded anywhere as answered by the founder. Each is carried on the handoff for him
    at the wrap; an answer of his that differs comes later as a revision or as a new chunk.
    Where the Goal, the Test Commands prose, an operator entry's `note` or an Implementation note still says
    that this step holds the pass, or that the founder rules or words one of the four at this chunk's wrap,
    this step governs.

16. **The operator pass.** After step 15: the hygiene entry, the pre-CI commit, the push entry, then the CI
    read, which is the `ci.py conclusion` call (`inputs#I1` note 6).
- `src/run/budget.rs` — the thresholds reader, the decision, the gate
- `tests/cli_budget.rs` — Path 6's cli and ipc cases and E5's budget leg
- `tests/support/statusline.rs` — the shared `hook statusline` runner and payload builders
- `crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs` — `Percent`, `BudgetWindowKind`
- `crates/viola-state/src/budget.rs` — `read_budget`
- `crates/viola-state/src/snapshot.rs` — `budget_override_until`, one literal
- `crates/viola-state/src/liveness.rs` — one snapshot literal
- `crates/viola-state/src/strict.rs` — one snapshot literal
- `crates/viola-state/src/replay.rs` — one snapshot literal
- `crates/viola-state/tests/state_replay.rs` — one literal, the two replay cases
- `crates/viola-state/tests/state_events.rs` — the read-back case
- `src/run/mod.rs` — the module
- `src/run/send.rs` — the rung, the emitter's four fields
- `src/run/wheel.rs` — `release` takes the gate; one literal
- `src/run/dialog.rs` — one snapshot literal
- `src/run/snapshot.rs` — one snapshot literal
- `src/cmd/run.rs` — the start, the dispatch, one literal
- `src/cmd/release.rs` — `--budget`, the lines
- `src/cmd/pause.rs` — `wheel_call`
- `src/cmd/send.rs` — the hint lookup
- `src/cmd/revive.rs` — the check before the log; one literal
- `src/cmd/hook.rs` — one snapshot literal
- `src/cmd/hook/statusline.rs` — no log after a refused check; one literal
- `src/human.rs` — two lines, the hint
- `src/obs.rs` — `CONFIG_KEYS`
- `tests/cli_revive.rs` — the witness, one restated case
- `tests/hook_statusline.rs` — the witness; its runner moves out
- `tests/cli_controls_not_disableable.rs` — three rows
- `tests/support/mod.rs` — the module
- `Cargo.toml` — the `[[test]]` entry
- `.config/nextest.toml` — `binary(cli_budget)` on the 20 s line

The gates are the standing lint and unit entries; one unit filter and one integration filter that select what
this chunk adds; a preservation guard; the harness smoke with G2 and G4 over its home; the native `pre-push`;
and the operator's hygiene, push and CI read (`leg = 'operator'`, the `ci.py conclusion` call, `inputs#I1`
note 6).

No mutation entry, no witness run and no workflow dispatch is listed (`inputs#I1` note 1). No entry is a live
leg: nothing starts the real `claude`. Step 14's readings are implement's, in `evidence/red-green.md`, and are
never an entry. The operator entries are held by step 15.

The smoke boots an ordinary `viola run` session, so the start goes through the gate's first evaluation and the
harness's own readiness check reads `budget-gate` as record two. The preservation guard names the base commit,
because the operator pass's pre-CI commit moves HEAD onto the chunk. It is what shows that no ledger row, no
Claude shape, no schema value, no fixture, no fake-agent option and no harness file moved; it lists no file a
step edits. If the review card keeps the harness flag in this chunk, the guard loses `crates/viola-e2e` in the
same revision.

body:
- (arch) The gate, its three evaluation points and the `release --budget` handling live in the root bin's
  `src/run/`, the `budget.json` reader in `viola-state`, `Percent` and the window word in `viola-core`; no
  crate gains a viola-crate edge, a dependency or Tokio, and no Claude shape is read outside
  `viola-agent-claude`. Proven by the preservation guard entry exiting 0 and by the entry `cargo clippy
  --workspace --all-targets --features fake-agent -- -D warnings` (per architecture §Infrastructure Patterns →
  Crate dependency direction)

- (arch) An automated `send` over a threshold is answered as the channel refusal `budget-paused` with detail
  `five-hour` or `seven-day`, client exit 11, after `human-typing` and before `turn-running`; `answer`,
  `wait`, `last` and `pause` are not gated. Proven by the `send_budget_paused_` cases and by
  `path6_a_reading_over_the_threshold_refuses_the_send` and `path6_the_boundaries_and_the_window_word` in
  `binary(cli_budget)` (per architecture §Conventions, Error handling schema and CLI exit codes)

- (arch) `budget-gate` is appended once at start, as record two, and then only on a change taken at a `send`'s
  arrival, at a `turn-ended` or by `release --budget`, with only the keys `paused`, `window` and
  `override_until`; the snapshot's `budget_paused` and `budget_override_until` equal the last such line, and
  the replay recovers both with zero skip counts. Proven by the `gate_eval_` cases,
  `path6_a_turn_end_closes_the_gate`, `path6_a_restart_pauses_again` and
  `e5_the_replay_reads_what_the_wrapper_wrote` (per architecture §Standard Contracts, the event data list and
  Instance snapshot)

- (arch) The thresholds are `Percent` values read from `config.json` with defaults 90 and 85; `five_hour` 89
  is open and 90 pauses, `seven_day` 84 is open and 85 pauses; a value outside 0 to 100, or not a whole
  number, gives the default and one `parse-rejected` line with parser `config-json`. Proven by the
  `thresholds_`, `percent_` and `gate_decide_` cases (per architecture §Cross-cutting Patterns, Config
  management; §Occupied Resources, viola home, `config.json`)

- (arch) `release` keeps its params; a `release` carrying a string `from` and `budget: true` answers `-32602`
  with `data` holding `reason: release-from-driver`, logs one `release-from-driver` line and leaves the
  snapshot's two budget fields unchanged; a `budget` that is not a bool answers `-32602` with `data: null`.
  Proven by the restated `release` unit cases in `src/run/wheel.rs` and `src/cmd/run.rs` under the entry
  `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --unit` (per architecture §Standard Contracts, Channel methods; security-plan
  §Authentication & Authorization, Driver-originated `release`)

- (security) A `viola revive` over a group-writable home is refused `strict-modes-failed`: exit 1, the
  state-files `unable:` and `hint:` pair with no recorded directory, pid or logged id, no child started, the
  home's mode unchanged and no line added to `run-builder.ndjson`. The case fails on the order at
  `396c108ba64c`. Proven by step 10's witness in `binary(cli_revive)` and its red and green readings in
  `evidence/red-green.md` (per security-plan §Authentication & Authorization, `~/.viola/` access control,
  Strict-modes check)

- (security) A `viola hook statusline` over a group-writable home runs no command, prints nothing, leaves
  `budget.json` and the marker file unchanged, writes no stderr and exits 0, on the first invocation and on
  the next one over the same home, whose mode is unchanged after both. The case fails on the arm at
  `396c108ba64c`. Proven by step 11's witness in `binary(hook_statusline)` and its readings in
  `evidence/red-green.md` (per security-plan §Authentication & Authorization, `~/.viola/` access control,
  Strict-modes check)

- (security) The gate's read of `budget.json` goes through the `MAX_FRAME` bound and never writes the file: an
  absent, over-cap, unparseable or newer `budget.json`, and one under a home that fails `check_path`, each
  yield no reading, and the file's bytes and mode are unchanged by a read. Proven by the `budget_read_` cases

- (security) No value of a threshold key switches the gate off: with `five_hour` set to `101`, `-1` or `"90"`,
  a `send` after `five_hour` 91 is fed exits 11. Proven by the three rows in

- (design) `viola release <name> --budget` on a paused instance prints one unstyled stdout line with the name,

title: Revision: P3 as premise closure (the stop its finding)

data.head: ## Revision: P3 as premise closure (the stop its finding)

body:
- **The stop.** /andromeda-implement ended at the plan's step 15, as the plan held it. Nothing the stopped run
  left falsifies a scope bullet; the cause of the revision is the operator's word (`inputs#I6`).

- **What the stopped run left, read where it is.** `evidence/red-green.md`: four red and green pairs, for
  steps 10, 11, 7 and 2. No `scope-record.md` (the chunk folder holds `evidence/`, `inputs/`, `plan.md`,
  `research.md` and `scope.md`). The tree's edits: the implement trail
  (`.andromeda/runs/2026-10-10T21-29-10-implement/gate-2026-10-10-budget-governor.json`) reads `entries 16 ·
  green 13 · red 0` with `not-run 3` on each of its two `run` calls, and `scope: clean — changed 31 · listed
  31 · recorded 0` on its last `scope` call. HEAD is `396c108`, with no pre-CI commit for this marker
  (`git log --oneline --grep='chore(2026-10-10-budget-governor)'` printed no line).

- **The four items' built forms, read in the tree at this revision** (3 reads, 1 grep batch):
  - the rung: `src/run/send.rs:347-350` evaluates the gate with the `send` trigger and returns
    `ctx.budget_paused`; the ledger, the probes and the fixtures stand at the base (`git diff --quiet
    396c108ba64c -- crates/viola-agent-claude src/cmd/verify.rs src/cmd/verify fixtures` exits 0);
  - the read: `read_budget` at `crates/viola-state/src/budget.rs:77-82` runs `check_path` on the home and on
    `budget.json` before the shared lock;
  - the refused check: `revive` reads its check at `src/cmd/revive.rs:104`, ahead of `open_wrapper_log` at
    `:108` (`evidence/red-green.md`, reading (a)); the statusline arm returns at
    `src/cmd/hook/statusline.rs:56-58`, ahead of `viola_obs_init` at `:60` (reading (b));
  - the two lines: `write_budget_open` (`src/human.rs:216-219`) and `override_end` (`src/human.rs:192-203`),
    which puts the date ahead of the time when the end falls on another UTC date.

- **The write set is unchanged.** The two lists below stand as P3 wrote them. No extract is voided: the word
  moves when the operator pass starts, not what a master says, so P2 did not re-run and no distiller was
  re-spawned. The take-up's graph trace stands in the take-up run dir
  (`.andromeda/runs/2026-10-10T20-53-16-phase/tree-query-2026-10-10-budget-governor.json`).

- **Closure.** `scope.md` gained the section "The revision: the operator pass no longer waits", each bullet
  verified against the snapshot or the tree, and one corrected bullet in item 11 (the last clause of
  `inputs#I4`).

title: Measured at P3 (the session scratchpad's rig `m-20261010T210657Z/`, 2026-10-10T21:06:57Z)

data.head: ## Measured at P3 (the session scratchpad's rig `m-20261010T210657Z/`, 2026-10-10T21:06:57Z)

body:
`target/debug/viola` (built 2026-10-10 21:39 local, after the last commit that touches `src/` or `crates/`,
`58f8720`; no product file is newer than it: `find src crates -name '*.rs' -newer target/debug/viola` printed
nothing). Every run under `env -i` with `PATH` one empty directory, so no `VIOLA_*` or `CLAUDE*` value crossed
and no `claude` could be resolved. Scratch homes only; nothing under the repository or the user's home.
| Run | Before | Reading |

| A1. `viola hook statusline`, a payload with `rate_limits` (`five_hour` 91) | home 0770, instance directory 0700 | exit 0, stdout and stderr empty, `budget.json` absent, role lines `hook-invoked` then `hook-decision` WARN `strict-modes-failed` `budget_written:false`; home after: **0700** |
| A2. the same invocation again, nothing touched between | home 0700 (as A1 left it) | exit 0, `budget.json` **present**, `hook-decision` INFO `budget_written:true` |
| B. control: the arm over a home at 0700 | home 0700 | exit 0, `budget.json` present, `budget_written:true` |

| C. `viola --home <home> revive rv`, no logged session | home 0770, instance directory 0700 | exit 1, stderr `unable: rv has no logged session to resume` + its hint, role lines `process-start` then `process-exit` `no-session`; home after: **0700** |

| D. control: the same, home 0700, instance directory 0770 | — | exit 1, stderr `unable: rv's state files can be written by another user` + its hint, `process-exit` `strict-modes-failed`; instance directory after: 0770 |
What the readings show:

- **The statusline arm's one-invocation hypothesis is confirmed** (A1, A2): the refused invocation opens its
  role file, which narrows the home, and the next invocation passes the check and writes the reading.

- **The `revive` defect is measured** (C against D): over a group-writable home the start arm narrows the
  home, passes the check and refuses for the next cause in its order. The check itself refuses a widened
  instance directory (D), and the log's opening does not narrow the instance directory.
- Not measured: Windows and macOS; a home another user owns; a home with an other-writable bit only.

- `src/cmd/revive.rs` (60-230) — `revive` calls `open_wrapper_log` (:101) then `preflight` (:102);
  `preflight`'s first reading is `check_instance` (:145); `Refusal::write` prints through `human::refuse`
  (:91-94), which needs no log; `refused(detail)` (`src/cmd/run.rs:323`) writes the `process-exit` line and
  needs one. `list` (:202-218) is the landed form of a check with no log: the stderr pair and exit 1.

- `src/cmd/run.rs` (140-345, 395-560) — `open_wrapper_log` (:169) reads `config.json` for the level, opens
  the role file, logs the start, reads `claude_env_keep`; `start` (:206) builds the slots and calls
  `start_state` (:500), which writes the first snapshot with `budget_paused: false` (:519) and appends
  `wheel` then `budget-gate{paused:false}` (:529-537); `Methods::dispatch_call` (:124-133) routes `send` and
  `release`; `Methods::dispatch` (:113-118) appends a hook's event through `append_hook_event`.

- `src/obs.rs` (30-232) — `open_role_file` calls `ensure_private_dir(home)` (:77), and `create_private_dir`
  narrows an existing directory to 0700 (:37-40): the mechanism behind A1 and C. `read_diagnostics_level`
  (:170) and `parse_diagnostics_level` (:183) are the landed `config.json` reader: `MAX_FRAME` cap, `v` = 1,
  a bad value → the default plus `ConfigRejection::Malformed`, unknown keys counted against `CONFIG_KEYS`
  (:33, three names: `v`, `diagnostics_level`, `claude_env_keep`).

- `src/run/env.rs` (20-70) — the second `config.json` reader (`claude_env_keep`): its own bounded read, a bad
  value reported `Malformed`, the document's own faults left to `read_diagnostics_level` to report once.

- `src/cmd/hook/statusline.rs` (1-205) — `check_instance` (:53) runs before `viola_obs_init` (:55), which
  runs whatever the check said; `handle` (:110) logs `hook-invoked`, then serves or records
  `strict-modes-failed`; `serve` (:128) writes the reading through `write_budget`.

- `src/run/send.rs` (255-470) — `send` (:306) is the refusal order as code: params, `control-character`
  (:321), `empty-text` (:326), `human-typing` (:329), `turn-running` (:339), the gate's wait, then the second
  read of the wheel and the turn (:357-366). `Ctx::refuse` is the one `send-refused` emitter. The clock is
  `viola_core::Clock`. `append_hook_event` (:216) is where a `turn-ended` line is seen before it is appended
  (:236-238).

- `src/run/wheel.rs` (24-290) — the model: state under one `Mutex` (`Held`), a worker thread fed `Job`s
  (`record_with`, :118), `Recorder::record` (:271) appending the event and updating the snapshot under the
  span `run.wheel_transition` (:262-270, declared, asserted by no test: `grep -rn wheel_transition src` → 1
  hit). `release` (:195-210) refuses a string `from` first, parses `budget`, and answers the constant
  `budget_paused: false`.

- `src/cmd/release.rs` (whole, 40 lines) and `src/cmd/pause.rs` (40-74) — `ReleaseArgs` holds `name` and
  `json` only; `wheel_call` builds params with `from` alone and hands its line writer `(name, holder)`.

- `src/human.rs` (178-232) — `write_released` (:183); `send_hint` (:209) has arms for `human-typing` and six
  `not-delivered` causes, none for `budget-paused`; a unit case `no_hint_names_release` exists (:569 by the

title: 2. The gate: evaluated from `budget.json` at three points

data.head: ### 2. The gate: evaluated from `budget.json` at three points

body:
- Source: `architecture.md:72`. The wrapper evaluates its gate from `budget.json`, read under
  `budget.json.lock`, at start, when a `send` arrives and at each `turn-ended`. It never polls. A crossed
  threshold, a passed `resets_at` or an expired override takes effect at the next of those points, and only then
  is `budget-gate` appended.

- Verified (the arch extract's first constraint; research.md finding 1): the read of `budget.json` is a new
  `viola-state` function beside `write_budget`, under the same lock sibling, through `Read::take(MAX_FRAME)`,
  never writing. An absent, over-cap, unparseable or newer file reads as no reading. Whether the wrapper may
  refuse a driver on that file without a ruling is item 10.

- The wrapper mirrors its budget-pause state, any override included, to the instance snapshot
  (`budget_paused`, `budget_override_until`), where `list` and `ui` will read it (`architecture.md:72`, `:211`,
  `:255`). `budget_override_until` is a new, additive, optional snapshot field.

- The gate declares the span `run.budget_eval` with `trigger` (`start` · `send` · `turn-ended`), `paused` and
  `window` (the obs extract's first constraint). A gate change gets no process-log event of its own: the
  `budget-gate` record is its carrier (the obs extract's fourth constraint).

- [premise-corrected: research.md finding 3 — `viola_core::Clock::now()` is an `Instant`, `viola-core` has no
  chrono, no crate depends on mock_instant] The decision (reading, thresholds, override, the wall-clock instant
  → open, or paused with its window) is a pure function in the root bin that takes the instant as an argument.
  The product passes the wall clock at each of the three points; a unit case passes a literal. The override's
  expiry is a unit case (`test-plan.md:582`, `:845`).

- A window whose `resets_at` has passed does not pause: the reading is of a window that has ended
  (`architecture.md:72`, "the pause lifts when `resets_at` passes").

title: 3. The refusal: `budget-paused` on an automated send only

data.head: ### 3. The refusal: `budget-paused` on an automated send only

body:
- Source: the entry's title; `architecture.md:72`, `:129-142`. An automated `send` is refused `budget-paused`
  with detail `five-hour` or `seven-day`, client exit 11, through the same refusal path as `human-typing`. Human
  keys are never blocked and a running turn finishes.

- Order (`test-plan.md:590`): control-character → empty-text → human-typing → budget-paused → turn-running →
  input-not-ready → no-prompt-submitted; the wrapper returns only the first that applies. The second read after
  the readiness gate's wait names `human-typing` and `turn-running` only: no second budget read (the arch
  extract's third constraint).

- The refused send appends `send-refused` with no cursor and writes one process-log line with the fields
  obs-plan names (`window`, `used_percentage`, `resets_at`, `paused:true`; the schema admits all four,
  research.md finding 6).

- The human-mode refusal prints the struck-box `unable` line and one `hint:` line, the design's text
  (`design-system.md:760`); the hint never contains `release` (`test-plan.md:862`, `:996`).

- Verified (the arch extract's third constraint): `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause` and `hook.dialog` are not
  gated.

- When both windows are over their thresholds, the detail names one: `five-hour` first. No master line orders
  them; the review card lists it.

title: 4. The lift: at the window's reset, or by a per-instance override

data.head: ### 4. The lift: at the window's reset, or by a per-instance override

body:
- Source: the entry's title ("lift at reset or per-instance override", "release --budget payload");
  `architecture.md:72`. The pause lifts when the crossed window's `resets_at` passes, or on
  `viola release --budget`, which goes to one instance's wrapper and lifts the pause for that instance only,
  until the crossed window's `resets_at` passes, so the next over-threshold reading does not re-pause it.
  `release --budget` leaves the wheel where it is; a plain `release` returns the wheel and lifts no pause.

- The override is logged as `budget-gate{paused:false, override_until}` and stands in the snapshot as
  `budget_override_until`; the record's `override_until` is later than its `ts` and equals the snapshot's
  (`test-plan.md:858-860`).

- [premise-corrected: research.md finding 4 — `ReleaseArgs` holds `name` and `json` only] The CLI flag
  `--budget` is built here: the contract lists it (`architecture.md:285`, `:362`) and the verb does not have it.

- The result of `release --budget` is `{budget_paused:false}` beside the wheel (`test-plan.md:853`); its human

  result carries the override's end as `override_until`, so the human line is derivable from it (requirements
  `v1-13`).

- Answered at P4 (`inputs#I3`, question 3; no master line says, research.md finding 9): when no pause stands,

  `{wheel, budget_paused:false}` with no `override_until`, exit 0. Its human line has no words in any master:

  (`architecture.md:72`: "so the next over-threshold reading does not re-pause it"). The review card lists it.

- `release` carrying a string `from` stays refused `-32602` with or without `budget`, before any lift (the
  security extract's fifth constraint; landed, `src/run/wheel.rs:197-200`).

- Source: the entry's title ("unknown with age"); `architecture.md:72`: with figures missing, viola uses the
  newest reading from any wrapped session and shows its age; with no reading at all it records `unknown` and
  does not block.

- Verified (the arch extract; `architecture.md:216`): an `unknown` window, an `unknown` `used_percentage` and an
  absent `budget.json` never pause; `read_at` is the age's source. The surfaces that show the reading and its

_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-10-10-self-healing-state · **Version:** viola-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-10T09:52:19Z
- **Base commit:** `2f1efe3a8962` (HEAD when this plan was written; the preservation guard names it)

- **Shape:** the state library and the writer. The plan covers scope items 1 to 5 as closed at P3. Scope item 6
  and the readers' use of the replay are left out by the cut the scope states; the review card carries it.

A log whose last line was cut short no longer costs the next record. Today every append goes straight after the
fragment, so the new line is glued to it and lost to every reader. After this chunk the next append starts on a
fresh line, the process that healed writes one `state-recovered` line, and every offset handed out before still
names the start of the same line (per architecture §Established Decisions [Database / State Store];
§Occupied Resources → Filesystem; test-plan §6 Chaos suite; obs-plan §6 Additive field catalog).

The reader counts what it steps over under the contract's three names, `unknown_kinds`, `unknown_fields` and
`torn_lines`, so the surfaces that later print them have them (per architecture §Standard Contracts → GUI list
envelope; test-plan §4 What unit tests cover → viola-state). `viola-state` gains a snapshot read that tells an
absent, an unreadable and a newer-`v` snapshot apart, and a replay of the log that recovers the log-derived fields
(per architecture §Standard Contracts → Snapshot envelope). Both are library code here: the next entry, "viola
revive", is the first reader.

The crate gets its own `tests/` suite, owed since the writers landed, in which every event kind round-trips
(per test-plan §5 Cross-module patterns → On-disk). The newer-peer refusal is already landed and tested; nothing
is built for it.

1. **The kind table in `viola-core`.** In `crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs`, beside `EventKind::WAIT_WAKE` and
   `as_str`, add: one constant listing every variant in declaration order (13, `EventKind` @
   `crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs:49-63` at `2f1efe3`); a parse from a kind's kebab name that returns the variant,
   or nothing for any other text; and for each variant the `data` keys architecture's per-kind list gives
   (`.andromeda/architecture.md:290-304`):

   | kind | `data` keys |
   |---|---|
   | `session-start` | `cause`, `agent_session_id` |
   | `prompt-submitted` | `text`, `origin` |
   | `turn-ended` | `last_assistant_message` |
   | `session-end` | none |
   | `activity` | `tool` |
   | `wheel` | `holder`, `cause` |
   | `budget-gate` | `paused`, `window`, `override_until` |
   | `send-issued` | `cursor`, `from` |
   | `send-confirmed` | `cursor`, `confirmed` |
   | `send-refused` | `refusal`, `detail`, `cursor` |
   | `question` | `dialog_id`, `questions` |
   | `permission` | `dialog_id`, `tool`, `input` |
   | `plan` | `dialog_id`, `plan` |

   Unit cases, their names carrying `kind_table`: every variant's name parses back to that variant; a text that
   is no kind's name parses to nothing; the constant equals the literal list of 13; each variant's key list equals
   the literal row above. The expected values are literals in the test, never the constant itself.

2. **The crate's test log capture.** In `crates/viola-state/src/lib.rs` add a `#[cfg(test)]` capture module after
   the pattern of `viola-channel`'s (`crates/viola-channel/src/lib.rs:103-200`): a unit test runs a closure and
   gets back the diagnostics lines it made, as JSON values. `crates/viola-state/Cargo.toml` takes
   `tracing-subscriber` as a dev-dependency (the workspace pin), and `Cargo.lock` moves with it.

3. **The new cases, written first and read red once.** Write the unit cases of steps 4 to 7 and the crate-level
   and root cases of steps 8 to 10 before the product change. Run the unit filter entry and the integration filter
   entry of `## Test Commands` once on that tree and record the red reading in `evidence/red-green.md`. This is
   the one-off remove-the-guard demonstration for each new guard (`inputs#I1`): every new case fails for want of
   the behaviour it guards. Step 11 records the green side.

4. **The reader's three counts** (`crates/viola-state/src/events.rs`, `Skipped` @ `:127` and `next_line` @
   `:203-236`). `Skipped` holds `unknown_kinds`, `unknown_fields` and `torn_lines`. Per read, from zero:
   - an over-long line adds one to `torn_lines`, whether it ends in LF or is the last line of the read;
   - a line ending in LF that is not one JSON object adds one to `torn_lines`;
   - a last line with no LF adds one to `torn_lines` and is not returned;
   - an object whose `kind` is absent, is not a string, or is no kind of step 1 adds one to `unknown_kinds` and
     is not returned;
   - an object of a known kind that carries a top-level key outside `v`, `ts`, `instance`, `kind`, `source`,
     `data`, or whose `data` is an object carrying a key outside that kind's row, adds one to `unknown_fields`,
     once per line, and is returned. A `data` that is not an object adds nothing.

   `read_from`'s signature, `LoggedLine` and the offsets it reports stay as they are, so its two callers
   (`rebuild` @ `src/run/wait.rs:115`, `scan` @ `src/run/wait.rs:197`) are not edited. Unit cases, names carrying
   `three_counts`: one per bullet above, with the count asserted as a whole literal `Skipped`; a log of the 13
   kinds written by `append_event` with each row's keys reads all zero. The in-file cases that pin today's two
   counts or the uncounted tail (`events_read_an_oversize_torn_last_line_is_not_counted` among them) are restated
   to the rules above, and the in-file cases that write a made-up `kind` are moved to a real one.

6. **The classified snapshot read** (`crates/viola-state/src/snapshot.rs`, beside `read_snapshot` @ `:100-110`).
   A new read returns one of four: the snapshot; absent (no file); unreadable (any other I/O failure, or bytes
   that are not a snapshot envelope with `v` 1 and a readable `data`, a `v` of 0 included); unsupported, with the
   `v` it saw, when the envelope's `v` is above 1, whatever its `data` holds. It reads through the same
   `MAX_FRAME` bound. `read_snapshot` keeps its signature and its results and is defined through the new read, so
   the two cannot disagree; its four product callers are not edited. Unit cases, names carrying `snapshot_cause`:
   one per result, the `v` 99 case reading `v_seen` 99 with a `data` the v1 struct could not hold.

7. **The replay** (new `crates/viola-state/src/replay.rs`, exported from `lib.rs`). One pass over
   `read_from(dir, 0)` returns: `wheel`, the `holder` of the last `wheel` line when it is `human` or `driver`;
   `budget_paused`, the `paused` of the last `budget-gate` line when it is a bool; `budget_override_until`, that
   line's `override_until` when it is a string; `agent_session_id`, from the last `session-start` line whose
   value is a string; `links`, empty; and the pass's three counts. A field no line gave is absent, never a
   default. The result reads `dialog_pending` false. The replay writes no file.

   A second function reads the snapshot through step 6 and returns the snapshot, or absent, or the replay with its
   cause. On the replay arm it writes one `state-recovered` line at WARN with no `corr`: `detail`
   `snapshot-replayed` and `file` `snapshot.json` for an unreadable snapshot; `detail` `snapshot-unsupported-v`,
   `file` `snapshot.json` and `v_seen` for a newer one. An absent snapshot writes no line and replays nothing.
   The replay's span is `state.replay` and the read-or-replay function's is `state.snapshot_recover`, both
   `skip_all`, neither with `err` or `ret`. Unit cases, names carrying `replay_recovers`: each field from its last line; a later `session-start`
   with a null id leaves the earlier string id standing; an empty and an absent log give every field absent; the
   two record shapes, each asserted whole; the present and the absent arm write no line.

8. **The crate-level events suite** (new `crates/viola-state/tests/state_events.rs`). On a temp dir, through the
   crate's public writer and reader only:
   - a table of the 13 kinds, each with a literal `data` body built from its row of step 1: after `append_event`
     the line read back by `read_from` has exactly the six keys in the order `v`, `ts`, `instance`, `kind`,
     `source`, `data`, `v` 1, a `ts` of 24 characters ending in `Z`, and the body unchanged; the counts are zero;
   - the counts on a file the writer made and the test then appended raw lines to: an unknown kind, a known kind
     with an extra top-level key, a known kind with an extra `data` key, a line that is not an object, each
     counted as step 4 says, with the known-kind lines still returned;
   - the heal on a file the writer made and the test then shortened with `File::set_len`: the next append starts
     on a fresh line, an offset taken before the shortening still starts the same line, and `torn_lines` reads 1
     before and after.

9. **The crate-level replay suite** (new `crates/viola-state/tests/state_replay.rs`). On a temp dir: the crate's
   writers lay down a snapshot and a log holding a `wheel` to `human`, a `budget-gate` with `paused` true and two
   `session-start` lines with different ids. Then: the classified read returns the snapshot; with the snapshot
   file shortened mid-object the read-or-replay function returns the replay, `wheel` human, `budget_paused` true,
   the second id, `links` empty, `dialog_pending` false; with the envelope's `v` set to 99 it returns the replay
   with `v_seen` 99; in both, `snapshot.json`'s bytes and modification time are the same after the call as before.
   The broken snapshots are made from the writer's own file (shortened, or its `v` rewritten), never typed whole.

10. **The root cases.**
    - New `tests/chaos_torn_append.rs`, one test whose name carries `torn_tail`: boot a `builder` wrapper over the
      fake agent on a `TestHome`, stop it with `stop_keep`; read the log through `viola_state::events::read_from`
      and assert all three counts zero; shorten `events.ndjson` by a few bytes with `File::set_len` so its last
      line has no LF, and note its length L; assert the reader now counts `torn_lines` 1; boot again on the same
      home with `Wrapper::boot`; wait, on the wrapper's role file and under `WITHIN`, for the `state-recovered`
      line. Then assert: the first L bytes are unchanged; byte L is LF; the line starting at L + 1 is the second
      start's `wheel` record; the reader counts `torn_lines` 1 and nothing else; `diagnostics/run-builder.ndjson`
      holds exactly one `state-recovered` line, `detail` `torn-line-healed`, `file` `events.ndjson`, `offset` L,
      level WARN, no `corr`. Stop the wrapper.
    - In `tests/cli_send.rs`, `path2_send_confirms_with_cl1_events`, and in `tests/cli_answer.rs`,
      `path4_dialogs_are_logged_once_woken_and_answered_by_id` and
      `path4_permission_is_logged_once_woken_and_answered_by_id`: at the end, read the instance's whole log through
      `read_from` and assert the three counts are zero and the number of lines returned equals the number the
      test-side reader sees. This pins the key table of step 1 against what the writers of every kind those paths
      log really write.

11. **Green, and the record.** Run the gates of `## Test Commands` in order. Add the green reading of the two
    filter entries to `evidence/red-green.md` beside step 3's red one. For the key-table guard of step 10's second
    bullet, record one more one-off pair there: with one key removed from one kind's row the `path2` case reads
    red, and with it restored, green.
- `crates/viola-state/src/replay.rs` — the replay and the read-or-replay function with its record
- `crates/viola-state/tests/state_events.rs` — the round-trip of every kind, the counts, the heal on a real dir
- `crates/viola-state/tests/state_replay.rs` — the classified read and the replay on a real dir
- `tests/chaos_torn_append.rs` — a stopped wrapper, a shortened log, a second start

- `crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs` — the list of all kinds, the parse, each kind's `data` keys; keep `as_str` and
  `WAIT_WAKE` as they are

- `crates/viola-state/src/events.rs` — the three counts and the heal; `read_from`'s and the three append
  functions' signatures stay
- `crates/viola-state/src/snapshot.rs` — the classified read; `read_snapshot` keeps its signature and results
- `crates/viola-state/src/lib.rs` — the `replay` module and the test capture
- `crates/viola-state/Cargo.toml` — `tracing-subscriber` under `[dev-dependencies]`
- `Cargo.lock` — that edge
- `tests/cli_send.rs` — the zero-count assertion at the end of one path test
- `tests/cli_answer.rs` — the same at the end of two path tests

The gates are the standing lint and unit entries; one unit filter and one integration filter that select what
this chunk adds; a preservation guard; the harness smoke with G2 and G4 over its home; the native `pre-push`; and
the operator's hygiene, push and CI read.

No mutation entry, no workflow dispatch and no witness run is listed, and no entry is a live leg: no `claude`
start is planned (`inputs#I1`). The mutation run is the epoch boundary's.

One point departs from the take-up note's "unit plus smoke" and is on the review card for the operator's word.
The crate-level suite, the chaos file and the two edited path tests are integration-layer binaries (`kind(test)`,
`crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run/nextest.rs:12`), and `run --unit` selects none of them. So the block carries one
`--integration` entry filtered to those five binaries. The whole default selection is not listed; `pre-push` runs
it under coverage before the push.

Step 3's red reading and step 11's green one are a one-shot pair in `evidence/red-green.md`; the two filter
entries guard the same cases on every re-run. Step 11's key-table control removes one key from a product table
and puts it back: it is a one-shot run at implement, both readings in `evidence/red-green.md`, and never an
entry; `binary(cli_send)` in the integration filter entry guards the same property on re-run. The preservation
guard names the base commit, because the operator
pass's pre-CI commit moves HEAD onto the chunk.

body:
- (arch) After an append to a log whose last line had no LF, the file is the prior bytes, one LF, the new line
  and its LF; the file is never shorter than before, and an offset taken before the heal still starts the same
  line. Proven by the `torn_tail` cases of the unit filter entry and by `binary(state_events)` in the integration
  filter entry (per architecture §Occupied Resources → Filesystem; §Established Decisions [Database / State Store])

- (arch) `append_event_at` returns, and hands its builder, the offset its line really starts at, L + 1 after a
  heal and L otherwise (per architecture §Standard Contracts → Event `data` per kind, `send-issued`)

- (obs) The healing process writes exactly one `state-recovered` line at WARN with `detail` `torn-line-healed`,
  `file` `events.ndjson`, `offset` L and no `corr` key, and an append that did not heal writes none. Proven in
  memory by the unit cases and in a real wrapper's role file by `binary(chaos_torn_append)` (per obs-plan §6
  Additive field catalog; §6 Log levels mapping; §3 Log format JSON schema)

- (obs) The read-or-replay function writes one `state-recovered` line for an unreadable snapshot
  (`snapshot-replayed`) and one for a newer one (`snapshot-unsupported-v` with `v_seen`), each with `file`
  `snapshot.json`, and none for a present or an absent snapshot (per obs-plan §4 Edge flows E5)

- (obs) `bash scripts/agent-run.sh schema-check` and `bash scripts/g2-zero-panics.sh` exit 0 over the homes this
  chunk's tests leave: every new line validates and no panic line exists (per obs-plan §9 Gate commands, G4 and G2)

- (tests) The reader's count is `unknown_kinds`, `unknown_fields`, `torn_lines`; an over-long line, a line that
  is not an object and an unterminated last line each count as torn; an unknown kind is counted and not returned;
  a known kind with an unknown top-level or `data` key is counted once and returned (per test-plan §4 What unit
  tests cover → viola-state; architecture §Standard Contracts → GUI list envelope)

- (tests) Every line this binary's own writers append reads zero on all three counts: the 13-kind table in
  `binary(state_events)` and the three path tests in `binary(cli_send)` and `binary(cli_answer)` (per architecture
  §Standard Contracts → Event `data` per kind)

- (tests) In `crates/viola-state/tests/` every one of the 13 event kinds round-trips the six-key line with its
  `ts` shape (per test-plan §5 Cross-module patterns → On-disk)

- (tests) A snapshot that does not parse, and one whose `v` is 99, each lead to a replay that carries `wheel`,
  `budget_paused`, `budget_override_until` and `agent_session_id` from the log, `links` empty and `dialog_pending`
  false; a field no line gave is absent (per test-plan §4 What unit tests cover → viola-state; architecture
  §Standard Contracts → Snapshot envelope)

- (security) The replay writes no file: `snapshot.json`'s bytes and modification time are unchanged by it, and no
  reader of this chunk reads a line or a snapshot outside the `MAX_FRAME` bound (per security-plan §Security
  Anti-Patterns → Universal; §Input Validation, row "Own state files on read")

- (security) No product reader changes what it does with an absent, unreadable or newer snapshot, and nothing
  under `src/` changes: the preservation guard entry exits 0 (per security-plan §Input Validation, row "Own state
  files on read", Integrity)

- (design) No human line is added or changed on any verb: `wait`, `last` and `verify` print exactly what they
  print today, since nothing under `src/` changes (the preservation guard entry exits 0) (per design-system §Surface: cli → Component Patterns; layout-templates §Surface: cli › Output
  structure — `viola wait` / `viola last`)

- (a11y) The heal adds no way for viola to write to the terminal: its only record is the `obs_event!` line, the
  workspace print ban holds in `viola-state` (the clippy entry exits 0), and nothing under `src/` changes (the
  preservation guard entry exits 0). A terminal-side case over a torn log is not built here (per a11y-plan §1 A11y
  Scope Summary → Surface: tui → Notes)

- (tests) `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --unit` and `bash scripts/agent-run.sh pre-push` exit 0 with `"ok":true`,
  and the operator's CI read prints `verdict: green` for the pushed HEAD; the report names the run id it read (per
  test-plan §3 `run`; §10 Coverage thresholds)

- No capability is claimed. `verification-matrix.json#v1-41` is advanced and not proven by this chunk: its
  "counted and shown" has no surface yet and no reader heals by replay yet. P5 writes one dated ledger note.

- Spec anchors the plan rests on: architecture §Established Decisions [Database / State Store], [Validation],
  [Hook Transport]; §Standard Contracts → ndjson event line, Event `data` per kind, Snapshot envelope, Instance
  snapshot, GUI list envelope; §Occupied Resources → Filesystem; §Infrastructure Patterns → Crate dependency
  direction. security-plan §Input Validation (row "Own state files on read"); §Security Anti-Patterns → Universal;
  §Error Handling. test-plan §3 `run`; §4 What unit tests cover → viola-state; §5 Cross-module patterns →
  On-disk; §6 Chaos suite; §7 Seed strategies; §11. obs-plan §3 Log format JSON schema; §4 Edge flows E5; §6
  Additive field catalog; §6 Log levels mapping; §8 Default-deny posture; §9 Gate commands. design-system
  §Surface: cli → Component Patterns. layout-templates §Surface: cli › Output structure. a11y-plan §1.
- External input: `inputs#I1`, the operator's take-up direction.

- Leans, each with its artifact: the heal is the appender's and one byte (test-plan §6 Chaos suite, "the next
  append starts on a fresh line"; the shared write path at `events.rs:257`); `data` keys are counted as well as
  the six top-level keys (architecture's closed per-kind list, `:290-304`); a crate-level case breaks a file the
  crate's writer made and never types one whole (test-plan §7 Seed strategies, the chaos exception; §6 Scenario
  E5 step 2), while the inline unit cases keep the crate's standing literal-bytes form (`snapshot.rs`,
  `read_snapshot_is_none_for_missing_malformed_or_unsupported`); the root case stops its wrapper and shortens the
  log in place of a kill, because the file on disk is the same and a killed instrumented process can leave a short
  coverage profile (test-plan-amendments, 2026-10-07-a-send-ending-in-a-newline-is-confirmed).

- Healing by shortening, replacing or rewriting `events.ndjson` — rejected: "never truncate, rotate or rewrite
  it" (`.claude/rules/events.md`, Cursors and retention); offsets are cursors.
- Healing from a reader — rejected: a reader holds no lock and writes nothing.

- Healing once at the wrapper's start only — rejected: the hook's direct SessionEnd append
  (`append_session_end` @ `src/cmd/hook.rs:494`) runs when the wrapper is gone, and its line would be glued to
  the fragment.

- Moving any of `read_snapshot`'s four product callers to the fallback — not in this chunk: the CLI pre-check and
  the hook's endpoint read stand under founder-dated exceptions, and a change there is a boundary matter (playbook,
  "Boundary widening", verdict escalate).
- Adding `link` or `unlink` to `EventKind` — not here: no writer exists; they land with "Session links".

- A line per read for the counts, a fourth `state-recovered` detail, or a new field on it — rejected: obs-plan's
  catalogue is default-deny and names no process-log carrier for a read's counts.
- An owner record, a remover or a signal handler for `viola verify` — not in this chunk (scope item 6).
- A new env seam to inject the fault — banned (security.md, the two test seams); torn state is made as files.

- Reading a healed log through `tests/support/events.rs` or `tests/support/ndjson.rs` — rejected: their reader
  fails a test on a complete line that is not JSON, which the healed fragment is. The second boot on the torn home
  is `Wrapper::boot`, never `events::boot`.

- A `sleep`, a test-owned timer, a retry, `#[ignore]`, or a bound other than `WITHIN` in the root case; a kill of
  any process the test did not start (the chaos case kills none).

- A mutation run, a workflow dispatch, a witness run or a live `claude` start (`inputs#I1`); reshaping code for
  mutants.
- Any edit under `.andromeda/` to a spec master, and any edit to `tests/support/`.

- The heal's write is one `write_all` of the LF and the line together. The LF ends the fragment; the line is still
  one complete object and its own LF.
- A log with no LF at all (the fragment is the whole file) heals the same way: L is the file's length.
- `try_append_event` with the lock held writes nothing and heals nothing, as today.

- The counts are per read: each `read_from` call starts from zero. A long-lived caller that re-reads a region
  recounts it. A surface that must show a count that never clears keeps its own total; that is the surface's.

- A line of an unknown kind is not returned, so `scan` does not move its cursor past one that is last in the log;
  the next scan steps over it again. It never wakes a `wait`.

- The reader keeps the position of every line it steps over (`LoggedLines` tracks the offset). A later entry that
  prints a skipped line in place can extend the result; nothing here forecloses it.
- No `cfg` branch is added, so `tests/contract_windows_mutation_scope.rs`'s file lists do not move.

- The hook's SessionEnd fallback is the one hook path through the changed write; it gains one one-byte read. No
  other hook path appends directly.

- The root case's home is a `TestHome` under `target/e2e-home`, inside G2, G4 and the secret scan. Its log holds
  one line that is not JSON after the heal; the harness's own `logs` verb prints such a line as a marked record.

- Forecast, to be measured: the root waits counted by the pattern `Instant::now() + WITHIN` under `tests/` stand
  at 22 sites in 16 files (`grep -rnE 'Instant::now\(\) \+ WITHIN' tests`, at `2f1efe3`); the chaos file adds its
  own. Record what the same grep reads after step 10.

- Expected amendments (wrap): architecture §Established Decisions [Database / State Store] — the "as landed" and
  "owed" sentences: the heal is the appender's, the reader counts three names, the replay stands as library code,
  and what is still owed is named by route entry title.

- Expected amendments (wrap): architecture §Infrastructure Patterns → Project directory structure — the
  `viola-state` comment (`replay.rs`, the crate's `tests/`), and the root wait count by its pattern.

- Expected amendments (wrap): architecture §Standard Contracts → Snapshot envelope — as landed: no reader takes
  the fallback yet, and `links` replays empty until the link kinds land.

- Expected amendments (wrap): security-plan §Input Validation — the "Own state files on read" row: the healing
  and its count as landed.

- Expected amendments (wrap): test-plan §4 What unit tests cover → viola-state, §5 Cross-module patterns →
  On-disk and §6 Chaos suite — the cases as landed (a stop and a shortened file in place of a kill; the surface
  readings owed by title); §6 Scenario E5 — owed, with its `wheel:"human"` after a second start set against the
  landed start, which appends `wheel{driver, start}` on every start.

- Expected amendments (wrap): obs-plan §4 Edge flows and §6 Additive field catalog — where `state-recovered` is
  written as landed (the healing append; the read-or-replay function) and its cadence, one line per heal.

- Route proposals, for the wrap's route step on the operator's word (no master, so not an amendment): a new entry
  for the killed-verify leftover dirs, which needs the founder's rule first, carrying the third CARRY and the
  three classes of dir; and CARRYs for the replay's readers and the shown counts on "viola revive", "The board:
  viola list", "Session links", "Budget governor" and "Server verification before any frame", as the scope lists
  them.

**Chunk:** Self-healing state — torn-line healing, snapshot rebuild by log replay, unknown kinds and fields counted
and surfaced, newer-snapshot and newer-peer tolerance (the cut of the P5 review: scope items 1 to 5, `inputs#I2`)
**Date:** 2026-10-10

- **read_from** — 2 product callers: `rebuild` @ `src/run/wait.rs:115`, `scan` @ `src/run/wait.rs:197`. Its
  signature and `LoggedLine` stay as they are, so neither caller changes. Both stop receiving lines of a kind
  this binary does not know; neither used them (`scan` filters to the wake kinds, `rebuild` reads `turn-ended`
  and dialog ids).

- **skipped** (the method) — 1 caller, the test helper `read` @ `crates/viola-state/src/events.rs:473`. No
  product code reads the count, so its field names are free to take the contract's.

- **write_line** — 3 callers, all in `events.rs`: `append_event` @ `:68`, `append_event_at` @ `:89`,
  `try_append_event` @ `:109`. One heal there covers every writer.

- **append_event / append_event_at / try_append_event** — product callers `start_state` @ `src/cmd/run.rs:440`,
  `append_hook_event` @ `src/run/send.rs:246`, `record` @ `src/run/wheel.rs:279`, `register` @
  `src/run/dialog.rs:238`, `record` @ `src/run/send.rs:390`, `issue` @ `src/run/send.rs:399`,
  `append_session_end` @ `src/cmd/hook.rs:494`. No signature changes, so none is edited.

- **read_snapshot** — 4 product callers: `live_endpoint` @ `src/cmd/client.rs:96`, `ask` @ `src/cmd/hook.rs:254`,
  `deliver` @ `src/cmd/hook.rs:469`, `collision_check` @ `src/cmd/run.rs:294`. It stays as it is; the classified
  read is added beside it and none of the four moves to it.

- **end_offset** — product callers in `src/run/send.rs` and `src/run/wait.rs`, and root tests
  (`tests/cli_send.rs`, `tests/cli_wait_last.rs`). Unchanged: it is the file's length, and a reader started there
  on a torn log already skips to the next line start (`read_within`, 153-164).

- **One shared write path** (`crates/viola-state/src/events.rs:257`): every append is `line_bytes` then one
  `write_all` under `events.ndjson.lock`. The heal joins that write.

- **A lib crate's own log capture** (`crates/viola-channel/src/lib.rs:103-200`): a `#[cfg(test)] mod test_capture`
  with `tracing-subscriber` as a dev-dependency; unit tests read the lines an `obs_event!` call made. `viola-state`

  crate-level `tests/` dir outside `viola-e2e` today.

- **A second start on one home** (`tests/cli_wait_last.rs:283`, `last_survives_a_wrapper_restart`): `stop_keep`,
  then a boot on the returned home.

- **The writers' `data` keys, read against architecture's per-kind list** (`.andromeda/architecture.md:290-304`):
  `session-start` `{cause, agent_session_id}`, `prompt-submitted` `{text, origin}`, `turn-ended`
  `{last_assistant_message}`, `activity` `{}` or `{tool}` (`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/hook.rs:156-167`);

  counts are the reader's return value.
