- **Base commit:** `f02d54865815` (HEAD when this plan was written; the preservation guard names it)

viola records which session drives which. A `link` is one line `driver → driven` in the driven instance's own
`events.ndjson`, written by that instance's wrapper, and the link set is whatever replaying those lines gives
(architecture §Established Decisions, [Links]). This chunk adds the two event kinds, the one rule that turns
`link` / `unlink` lines into a set of `{driver, driven, since}` items, the replay's link half, the wrapper's own
copy of the set (restored from the log at every start, mirrored to `snapshot.json`), and the implicit link a
`send` or an `answer` from another instance makes. It also lands the test the budget chunk left owed: under a
closed budget gate `answer`, `wait`, `last` and `pause` behave as under an open one, with a refused `send` in the
same gate as the control (test-plan §6 Path 6; `inputs#I1`, note 3).

The explicit half is `viola link <driver> <driven>` and `viola unlink <driver> <driven>`, served by two channel
methods, with a `link` result that carries what its human line prints (requirement `v1-13`, the `link` half).
That half widens the local trust boundary in three places no ratified gap covers, so it is **held behind step
11**: the founder's own word. Steps 1 to 10 and the operator pass do not wait for it (`inputs#I1`, note 4).

The chunk needs no ledger row, no `viola verify` child, no re-stamp and no live `claude` start, and it plans no
mutation run, witness run or workflow dispatch (`inputs#I1`, notes 1 and 2). Everything runs under the fake agent.

title: Part A — the link set and the implicit link (no boundary is widened)

data.head: ### Part A — the link set and the implicit link (no boundary is widened)

body:
1. **The two kinds** (`crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs`). Add `Link` and `Unlink` to `EventKind`, in `ALL`
   (13 → 15), `as_str` (`link`, `unlink`) and `data_keys` (`driver`, `driven` for both). Neither joins
   `WAIT_WAKE`. Update the inline oracle: `KIND_TABLE` gains the two rows; the case
   `kind_table_a_text_that_is_no_kind_parses_to_nothing` loses `"link"` and `"unlink"` from its list;
   `kind_table_all_is_the_thirteen_kinds_in_declaration_order` is renamed for fifteen.

2. **The link rule and the replay's link half** (`crates/viola-state/src/replay.rs`). Add one public function
   that applies one logged line to a link set (a `Vec<Value>` of `{driver, driven, since}` items) and says
   whether the set changed. It carries no span and writes nothing. Its rule, whole:
   - a `link` line whose `data.driver` and `data.driven` are strings adds the item with `since` = that line's
     `ts`, unless the pair is already in the set, and then it changes nothing (`since` stays the first one);
   - an `unlink` line removes the pair; for a pair that is not in the set it changes nothing;
   - a `link` or `unlink` line whose `driver` or `driven` is not a string changes nothing; every other kind
     changes nothing.
   `replay` calls it for every line of its one pass, so `Replayed.links` holds the set. Nothing else of `replay`
   changes: its span, its three other fields, its skip counts, and the rule that it writes no file. Add inline
   unit cases named `link_rule_*`: one link; a repeated link keeps the first `since`; a link after an unlink
   takes the later `ts`; an unlink of an absent pair; two drivers of one driven; a line with a non-string name.
   A new test helper must not be named `link` (one exists at `replay.rs:455`).

3. **The crate's suites and samples** (`crates/viola-state/src/events.rs`, `tests/state_events.rs`,
   `tests/state_replay.rs`). The two cases that use `link` as a kind no build knows
   (`events.rs:809`, `state_events.rs:173`) take another kind text that no build knows, and keep their counts.
   The every-kind tables (`events.rs:868–900`, `state_events.rs` `every_kind`) gain the two kinds with
   `{driver, driven}` and still read zero on all three counts. `state_replay.rs` gains crate-level cases over a
   log written through `append_event`: the replayed `links` after link, link again, unlink, link; and
   `replayed()` stays the expected state of the existing cases.

4. **The wrapper's link set** (new `src/run/links.rs`, declared in `src/run/mod.rs`). One owner of the set in
   the wrapper process, holding the instance's name, its directory, the shared `Snapshots` and the set under
   one lock. Four operations:
   - **restore**: one pass over `viola_state::events::read_from(instance_dir, 0)` through step 2's function;
     it appends nothing and logs nothing;
   - **current**: the set as it stands, for the first snapshot;
   - **record(driver)**: under the lock, when `driver → own name` is in the set, return its `since` and
     "already linked" with nothing written; otherwise append one `link` line `{driver, driven}` with source
     `wrapper` through `viola_state::events::append_event`, apply step 2's function with that line's own `ts`,
     write the set into the snapshot through `Snapshots::update`, and return that `since` and "new";
   - **remove(driver)**: under the lock, when the pair is not in the set, return "nothing removed" with nothing
     written; otherwise append one `unlink` line the same way, apply the rule, write the snapshot.
   A failed append or snapshot write is an error to the caller; the set in memory is then left as the log has
   it. The module emits no `obs_event!` line and declares no span (obs-plan §4 Edge flows, E3: the trace of a
   link is the channel pair, the product line and the snapshot). Inline unit cases named `links_set_*`: restore
   over a log with link, unlink, link; record twice writes one line and returns the same `since`; remove of an
   absent pair writes nothing; the snapshot on disk holds the set after each change; restore over an absent
   log is empty.

5. **The set at a wrapper's start** (`src/cmd/run.rs`). Build the link set beside the other slots and restore
   it where the start already rebuilds the wait feed from the log (`src/cmd/run.rs:272`), before
   `server.serve` (289). `start_state` (525) puts the restored set into the first snapshot in place of
   `links: Vec::new()` (547). Hand the set to the send slot and the dialog slot through a setter each, the form
   `SendSlot::budget_with` has (`src/run/send.rs:123`). The start appends no line for links and its three start
   records keep their places. `revive` starts through the same function, so a revived wrapper restores its set
   too. Reach, read at HEAD: no `send` can be issued and no `answer` taken before the first snapshot is
   written, because `send` returns `input-not-ready` until the pump attaches the paste (`src/run/send.rs:367`)
   and a dialog needs the child; so no link is recorded before `Snapshots::init`.

6. **The implicit link on a send** (`src/run/send.rs`). In `send`, after the second wheel and running-turn
   reads (374–383) and directly before `ctx.issue` (384): when `from` is a name and is not the wrapper's own
   name, call the set's record. An error answers `-32603` with nothing issued and nothing typed. A `send`
   refused at any earlier point records nothing (`inputs#I2`, answer 1). A slot that was handed no set records
   nothing. Inline unit cases named `send_link_*`: an issued send from `overseer` appends `link` directly before
   its `send-issued`, and that `send-issued` still carries the offset its own line starts at; a second issued
   send adds no `link`; a send refused `human-typing`, one refused `turn-running` and one with `from` equal to
   the wrapper's name add none; a send with no `from` adds none.

7. **The implicit link on an answer** (`src/run/dialog.rs`). In `answer`, once every refusal has passed and
   the response's kind matched the pending dialog (after line 355), and before the answer is taken (367): when
   `from` is a name other than the wrapper's own, call the set's record. An error answers `-32603` and the
   answer is not taken. A refused answer records nothing. Inline unit cases named `answer_link_*`: a taken
   answer from `overseer` appends one `link`; an answer refused `unknown-dialog` and one refused `human-typing`
   append none; a second taken answer adds no second line.

8. **Root cases for Part A** (new `tests/cli_links.rs`; `.config/nextest.toml`). Every case boots `builder`
   from a stamped home over the committed fixtures and stops its wrapper cleanly. Add `binary(cli_links)` to
   the 20 s kill filter line of `.config/nextest.toml:32` (a stamped-home binary). Cases:
   - `links_a_send_from_another_instance_links_once` over `fixtures/fake-scripts/path3.json`: a `viola send`
     under `VIOLA_NAME=overseer` leaves one `link` line with `data` `{"driver":"overseer","driven":"builder"}`
     and source `wrapper` directly before its `send-issued`; the snapshot's `links` is one item whose `since`
     equals that line's `ts`; after the scripted turn ends a second send leaves the count at one;
   - `links_an_answer_from_another_instance_links` over `fixtures/fake-scripts/path4.json`: an answer to an
     unknown dialog id links nothing; the answer to the raised dialog, under `VIOLA_NAME=overseer`, links once;
   - `links_a_refused_send_and_an_own_name_send_record_none`: after `viola pause`, a send from `overseer` is
     refused exit 10 and no `link` line exists; after `viola release`, a send under `VIOLA_NAME=builder` is
     issued and still no `link` line exists;
   - `links_survive_a_wrapper_restart`: link through a send, stop the wrapper keeping its home, boot again; the
     new start's first snapshot holds the same item with the same `since`, and a further send from `overseer`
     appends no `link`;
   - `e5_the_replay_reads_the_link_the_wrapper_wrote` (test-plan §6 Scenario E5, the `link` step):
     `viola_state::replay::replay` over the wrapper's log returns `links` equal to the snapshot's, with all
     three skip counts 0.
   Each case asserts no home-level line carries the canary and every role line passes
   `schemas/diag-line.v1.json`, as `tests/cli_budget.rs` `assert_logs_clean` does.

10. **Readings for the new cases** (`evidence/red-green.md`, written by implement). For steps 2, 4, 6, 7 and 8:
    each new case read red before its product step and green after. For step 9, whose property is an absence:
    one forced-on run, a gate evaluation added to `DialogSlot::answer` in a scratch edit, reads the case red at
    its step 5, and the edit is reverted and read back (`.claude/rules/testing.md`, the 2026-10-10 extension
    on absence cases). The scratch edit is a one-shot at implement and never a gate entry.

11. **Held for the founder's own word: the explicit `link` / `unlink`.** Steps 12 to 15 are not started until
    his word, given after this widening was shown to him as itself, is recorded as an input of this chunk
    (`inputs.py snap --step implement`, a relay named as relayed verbatim). The word must name `viola link` and
    `viola unlink` and say which form he rules:
    - the two methods served by the wrapper, and the two verbs writing their frame after the liveness-only
      pre-check with the snapshot read under no strict-modes check, as a dated gap of their own until the
      Epoch 6 entries "Server verification before any frame" and "Home and code-bearing file integrity"; or
    - another form (the instance check ahead of the snapshot read as `viola revive` takes it, or no explicit
      verbs before Epoch 6), in which case implement stops and the plan is revised.
    An earlier direction, the operator's included, does not stand in for it (`.andromeda/playbook.md`, "Boundary
    widening — what ratifies it"). Without the word, implement completes steps 1 to 10, runs every gate entry
    that does not select Part B, reports steps 12 to 15 as held, and the operator pass (step 16) goes ahead for
    Part A. Nothing else in this plan waits on it.

title: Part B — the explicit link and unlink (after step 11)

data.head: ### Part B — the explicit link and unlink (after step 11)

body:
12. **Two channel methods** (`src/run/links.rs`, `src/cmd/run.rs`). The link set gains `link(call)` and
    `unlink(call)`; `Methods::dispatch_call` (133) routes `link` and `unlink` to them. Both read `driver` and
    `driven` as strings through `ViolaName::try_new`; anything else is `-32602` with `data: null`. A `driven`
    that is not the serving wrapper's own name, and a `driver` equal to `driven`, are `-32602` with
    `data: null` too. Neither method reads `from`. `link` calls record and answers
    `{"ok":{"since":"<the item's since>","already_linked":<bool>}}`; `unlink` calls remove and answers
    `{"ok":{}}` whether or not a pair was removed (`inputs#I2`, answers 2 and 3). A record that cannot land is
    `-32603`. Both answer only after the line and the snapshot are written. The unit case
    `methods_answer_method_not_found_for_every_other_method` (`src/cmd/run.rs:788`) keeps `"anything"` alone.
    New inline cases named `links_set_method_*`: link twice (one line, the same `since`, `already_linked` false
    then true); unlink then link again (a later `since`); unlink of an absent pair (no line, `{}`); each
    bad-name class, a foreign `driven` and `driver` equal to `driven` (`-32602`, no line, the snapshot
    unchanged); a `from` in the params changes nothing.

13. **The three result lines** (`src/human.rs`). One writer each, stdout, plain in every mode, the forms of
    design-system §Surface: cli → Component Patterns, component 4:
    - `link` then four spaces, `<driver> -> <driven>`, two spaces, `since`, one space, the UTC clock time of
      the reply's `since` in whole seconds with `Z`;
    - the same up to the pair, two spaces, `already linked`;
    - `unlink` then two spaces, `<driver> -> <driven>`.
    The time is always the time-only form; a reply `since` that is no RFC 3339 instant prints escaped, as
    `override_end` does (`src/human.rs:192`). Inline cases pin the three lines byte for byte and that none
    holds an ESC or a non-ASCII byte.

14. **The two verbs** (new `src/cmd/link.rs`, `src/cmd/unlink.rs`; `src/cmd/mod.rs`; `src/main.rs`). Each takes
    `<driver>` and `<driven>` through the shared name parser (`super::send::parse_name`) and `--json`. The
    verb's instance is the driven one: `client::start(home, &driven)` files its role log as
    `cli-<driven>.ndjson`, its detail sink is the driven instance's, and its exit-21 line names the driven
    instance. It resolves the endpoint through `client::live_endpoint` (the liveness-only pre-check step 11
    rules on), sends one request with params `{driver, driven}` and no `from`, under a span named `cli.link` /
    `cli.unlink`, and ends: exit 0 with the result line built only from the reply's keys (step 13) or one
    `--json` document `{"v":1,"ok":…}`; exit 20 for a wrapper fault; exit 21 when the driven instance cannot be
    reached. A refusal reply, an `ok` of `link` without a string `since` and a boolean `already_linked`, and
    any other reply are internal errors (exit 1 through the catch site). `Command` gains `Link` and `Unlink`
    with one-line help texts; `src/main.rs` gains two `role_of` cases reading `Role::Cli`. No help group is
    built (Constraints).

16. **Hygiene, push, CI** (the three `leg = 'operator'` entries). Not held by step 11. The pre-CI commit
    carries whatever was built: Part A alone, or both parts.
- `src/run/links.rs` — the wrapper's link set (step 4) and, after step 11, its two methods (step 12)
- `tests/cli_links.rs` — the root cases of steps 8 and 15
- `src/cmd/link.rs` — `viola link` (step 14, after step 11)
- `src/cmd/unlink.rs` — `viola unlink` (step 14, after step 11)
- `tests/channel_links.rs` — the raw-channel name negative (step 15, after step 11)
- `crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs` — step 1
- `crates/viola-state/src/replay.rs` — step 2
- `crates/viola-state/src/events.rs` — step 3 (two inline cases)
- `crates/viola-state/tests/state_events.rs` — step 3
- `crates/viola-state/tests/state_replay.rs` — step 3
- `src/run/mod.rs` — step 4 (the module's declaration)
- `src/cmd/run.rs` — step 5; step 12 after step 11
- `src/run/send.rs` — steps 5 and 6
- `src/run/dialog.rs` — steps 5 and 7
- `.config/nextest.toml` — step 8
- `tests/cli_budget.rs` — step 9
- `src/human.rs` — step 13, after step 11
- `src/cmd/mod.rs` — step 14, after step 11
- `src/main.rs` — step 14, after step 11

The gates are the standing lint and unit entries; one unit filter and one integration filter that select what
Part A adds; one integration entry for Part B's own binary; a preservation guard; the harness smoke with G2 and
G4 over its home; the native `pre-push`; and the operator's hygiene, push and CI read (`leg = 'operator'`, the
`ci.py conclusion` call, `inputs#I1` note 6).

No mutation entry, no witness run and no workflow dispatch is listed (`inputs#I1` note 1). No entry is a live
leg: nothing starts the real `claude`. Step 10's readings are implement's one-shot runs, in
`evidence/red-green.md`, and are never an entry. The operator entries are not held by step 11.

The entry that selects `binary(channel_links)` reads red until step 15 has run, by construction: nextest
refuses a `binary()` that matches no binary. While step 11 holds Part B, that red is the hold and nothing else.
`tests/cli_links.rs` holds Part A's cases from step 8 on, so the Part A entry is green with or without Part B.

The smoke boots an ordinary `viola run` session, so the start goes through the link set's restore and the
first snapshot's `links`; the harness's readiness check still reads its three start records. The preservation
guard names the base commit, because the operator pass's pre-CI commit moves HEAD onto the chunk. It is what
shows that no ledger row, no Claude shape, no schema value, no fixture, no fake-agent option, no harness file
and no dependency moved, that the budget gate the folded case reads is the shipped one, and that no client
verb but the two new ones changed. It lists no file a step edits.

body: Part A (met at this chunk's wrap whether or not step 11's word arrives):

- (arch) `link` and `unlink` are `viola-core` kinds with `data` keys `driver` and `driven`; the link rule and
  the replay's link half are `viola-state` code; the wrapper's set is root-bin code; the chunk adds no crate
  edge, no dependency, no environment variable and no file under the viola home (per architecture §Conventions,
  Naming patterns → Normalised event kinds; §Infrastructure Patterns → Crate dependency direction). Proved by
  `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features fake-agent -- -D warnings` and the preservation guard.

- (arch) One issued `send` under `VIOLA_NAME=overseer` leaves exactly one `link` record
  `{"driver":"overseer","driven":"builder"}` with source `wrapper` in `builder`'s `events.ndjson`, directly
  before its `send-issued`, whose `cursor` is still the offset its own line starts at; a second issued send and
  a taken answer from the same driver add none (per architecture §Established Decisions, [Links]; §Standard
  Contracts, Event `data` per kind). Cases `links_a_send_from_another_instance_links_once`,
  `links_an_answer_from_another_instance_links`, `send_link_*`, `answer_link_*`.

- (arch) A refused `send`, a refused `answer`, a call with no `from` and a call whose `from` is the wrapper's
  own name record no link (per architecture §Established Decisions, [Links]; `inputs#I2`, answer 1). Case
  `links_a_refused_send_and_an_own_name_send_record_none` and the `send_link_*` / `answer_link_*` refusals.

- (arch) The snapshot's `links` holds one item `{driver, driven, since}` per linked pair, `since` equal to the
  `ts` of the pair's `link` line; a wrapper started over a log that holds links writes that set into its first
  snapshot and appends no second `link` for a pair it already holds (per architecture §Standard Contracts,
  Instance snapshot and Snapshot envelope). Case `links_survive_a_wrapper_restart`.

- (tests) The replay over a log the wrapper wrote returns the link the wrapper recorded, equal to the
  snapshot's, with `unknown_kinds`, `unknown_fields` and `torn_lines` all 0; the crate-level suite holds the
  first-`since`, link-after-unlink and repeated-link cases (per test-plan §6 Scenario E5; §4 What unit tests
  cover → viola-state). Cases `e5_the_replay_reads_the_link_the_wrapper_wrote`, `link_rule_*`, the
  `state_replay.rs` link cases.

- (tests) The fifteen kinds round-trip through the crate's writer and reader with zero on all three counts,
  and a line of a kind no build knows is still counted and not returned (per test-plan §5 Cross-module
  patterns → On-disk). `binary(state_events)`.

- (tests) Under one closed gate an automated `send` is refused exit 11 `budget-paused` / `five-hour`, and
  `wait`, `last`, `answer` and `pause` each give the exit code and document they give under an open gate; the
  log holds one `send-refused` record (per test-plan §6 Path 6; architecture §Established Decisions, [Budget
  Governor]; a11y-plan §8 Cognitive Accessibility → Timeout extensions). Case
  `path6_a_closed_gate_leaves_answer_wait_last_and_pause_alone`; its forced-on reading is in
  `evidence/red-green.md`.

- (obs) The implicit link and the start's restore add no process-log line, no `event` value and no span; no
  home-level line of the new cases holds `driver`, `driven` or `since`; every role line passes
  `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` and no panic line exists (per obs-plan §4 Edge flows; §8 Default-deny posture;
  §9 Gate commands). `bash scripts/agent-run.sh schema-check`, `bash scripts/g2-zero-panics.sh`, the root
  cases' own log read.

- (security) No refusal and no permission added by the chunk rests on `from` or on the link set, and a
  `release` carrying a string `from` is still refused (per security-plan §Authentication & Authorization, row
  "Driver-originated `release`"). The preservation guard holds `src/run/wheel.rs` and `src/cmd/release.rs`
  unmoved; `binary(cli_wheel)` runs under `bash scripts/agent-run.sh pre-push`.

- (tests) `bash scripts/agent-run.sh pre-push` is green on the Linux dev host, and the operator's
  `ci.py conclusion` read of the pushed HEAD prints `verdict: green` for all three OSes, the run id named in
  the report (per test-plan §10 Quality Gates & Coverage Targets).
Part B (met only when step 11's word is recorded and steps 12 to 15 are built; otherwise reported as held):

- (security) Steps 12 to 15 are built only behind the founder's recorded word naming `viola link` and
  `viola unlink`; without it no product code serves `link` / `unlink` and no client verb exists (per
  security-plan §Authentication & Authorization, rows "IPC client-side server verification
  (anti-impersonation)" and "`~/.viola/` access control"; §Security Anti-Patterns → Authentication).

- (security) A `link` and an `unlink` frame whose `driver` or `driven` fails `ViolaName::try_new`, names a
  foreign `driven`, or has `driver` equal to `driven` each read `-32602`, append no line and leave the
  snapshot as it was; the verbs refuse a bad name as a usage error before any frame (per security-plan §Input
  Validation, rows "Channel frames (IPC ndjson)" and "CLI arguments / stdin"; test-plan §6 Security control
  negatives). Cases `channel_link_names_are_validated_by_the_wrapper`, `links_set_method_*`.

- (arch) Two `viola link overseer builder --json` calls and one `viola send builder` under
  `VIOLA_NAME=overseer` leave exactly one `link` record; `viola unlink` appends one `unlink` and empties the
  snapshot's `links`; an `unlink` of a pair that is not linked appends nothing (per architecture §Established
  Decisions, [Links]; test-plan §6 Scenario E3; `inputs#I2`, answer 3). Case
  `e3_two_links_and_a_send_leave_one_link_record`.

- (arch) The `link` result is `{"since":…,"already_linked":…}` and every word of the human `link` line is
  built from those two keys; `unlink`'s result is the empty object (per intent F-13, requirement `v1-13`'s
  `link` half; `inputs#I2`, answer 2). Cases `e3_two_links_and_a_send_leave_one_link_record`,
  `link_verbs_print_the_design_lines`.

- (design) `viola link` prints one stdout line of component 4's form for a new pair and the `already linked`
  form for an existing one, `viola unlink` its one line; each is static, ASCII, holds no ESC byte in any mode,
  and nothing goes to stderr on exit 0 (per design-system §Surface: cli → Component Patterns, component 4
  "Wheel, link and gate verbs"; layout-templates §Surface: cli → Output structure — wheel, handoff and dialog
  verbs; a11y-plan §8 Cognitive Accessibility → Plain language). Case `link_verbs_print_the_design_lines` and
  the inline cases of step 13.

- (obs) Each explicit `link` and `unlink` leaves one `channel-request` and one `channel-response` with that
  `method` sharing `(conn, corr)` in the driven wrapper's role file, neither holding a name, a time or a result
  field, and the verb writes `process-start` and `process-exit` to `cli-<driven>.ndjson` (per obs-plan §4 Edge
  flows; §4 Instrumentation per surface). Case `link_verbs_log_the_channel_pair_and_no_names`.

No capability is claimed. `verification-matrix.json#v1-36` ends at the board and the page, and
`verification-matrix.json#v1-13`'s acceptance names the MCP result; this chunk advances both and proves neither
whole.

- Spec anchors the plan rests on (from the extracts): architecture §Established Decisions ([Links], [Budget
  Governor], [API Style], [Module Boundaries]), §Standard Contracts (Channel methods, Instance snapshot,
  Snapshot envelope, Event `data` per kind), §Conventions (Naming patterns, Error handling schema),
  §Infrastructure Patterns → Crate dependency direction; security-plan §Authentication & Authorization (rows
  "IPC client-side server verification (anti-impersonation)", "`~/.viola/` access control", "Driver-originated
  `release`"), §Input Validation (rows "Channel frames (IPC ndjson)", "CLI arguments / stdin", "Own state files
  on read"), §Security Anti-Patterns; test-plan §3 `run`, §4, §5 Cross-module patterns, §6 (Scenario E3,
  Scenario E5, Path 6, Security control negatives), §10; obs-plan §2 Naming conventions, §3 Trace context
  propagation, §4 Edge flows and Instrumentation per surface, §6, §8 Default-deny posture, §9;
  design-system §Surface: cli → Component Patterns (components 2 and 4), Tokens, Navigation Pattern;
  layout-templates §Surface: cli → Output structure — wheel, handoff and dialog verbs, Component — Primary
  content block 2; a11y-plan §1, §4 (P6), §8.

- Research files inspected: `crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs`, `crates/viola-state/src/{events,replay,snapshot}.rs`,
  `crates/viola-state/tests/{state_events,state_replay}.rs`, `crates/viola-channel/src/server.rs`,
  `src/cmd/{run,pause,release,client,mod}.rs`, `src/run/{send,dialog,wheel,snapshot,wait}.rs`, `src/human.rs`,
  `src/main.rs`, `tests/{cli_budget,cli_answer,cli_wheel,cli_wait_last,channel_paste_validation}.rs`,
  `tests/support/{cli,home}.rs`, `.config/nextest.toml`, `schemas/diag-line.v1.json`,
  `.andromeda/playbook.md` (research.md, Files inspected).
- Inputs: `inputs#I1` (the operator's notes at take-up), `inputs#I2` (the operator's three fork answers).

- The start does not call `viola_state::replay::replay` for its links — that function carries the span
  `state.replay`, and a unit case pins the start's span chain; the wrapper's restore is its own span-less pass
  through the shared rule, so `replay` keeps one product caller.

- No half-verification in the two verbs (a partial server check, an instance check of their own) — the Epoch 6
  entries own the verifier, and which form the verbs take is what step 11 rules.
- No link is recorded at a call's arrival — a refused call links nothing (`inputs#I2`, answer 1).

- No new refusal reason or detail, and no new human line or hint — the three bad shapes of step 12 are
  `-32602`, and an `unlink` of an absent pair prints the worded `unlink` line.

- No `from` on a `link` / `unlink` frame, and neither method reads one — architecture's list of methods that
  read `from` holds neither.

- No change to `InstanceSnapshot`'s `links` type — it stays `Vec<Value>`; every construction site already
  writes an empty one and none needs an edit.

- No grouped `viola --help`, no MCP tool, no `viola list` column, no `/api/links`, no page marker — owned by
  "CLI output discipline", "MCP server for drivers", "The board: viola list", "viola ui loopback server" and
  the Epoch 8 entries.

- No date-bearing `since` on the human line — the date form on the `release --budget` line is a planning form
  the founder has not worded, and a new link's `since` is the moment of the call.

- No span named `link.client` — it would add an `<area>` to obs-plan's closed list; `cli.link` and
  `cli.unlink` fit the list as it stands.

- No test hand-writes `snapshot.json`, `budget.json` or a booted wrapper's `events.ndjson`, sleeps to
  synchronise, or kills a process it did not start.

- **Leans taken without a question, each for the review card:** a `driven` that is not the serving wrapper's
  name and a `driver` equal to `driven` are `-32602` with `data: null` (architecture §Standard Contracts,
  Channel methods: the worded answer to a bad parameter), so `viola link builder builder` ends exit 20 with the
  wrapper-fault line; the verb's instance is the driven one (the frame's target, as every landed client verb
  files under its target); a link line's `source` is `wrapper` (the wrapper appends it; the code's `Source`
  holds `wrapper` and `hook`); a `from` equal to the wrapper's own name links nothing ([Links]: "to another

title: Mechanisms the plan rests on (each read at HEAD)

data.head: ## Mechanisms the plan rests on (each read at HEAD)

body:
- **The control reads `budget-paused` whatever the turn state.** `send` evaluates the gate at
  `src/run/send.rs:345–352`, after `human_typing` (338) and before the running-turn check (356). With the
  driver holding the wheel and a five-hour reading of 91 with a reset ahead, the reply is `budget-paused` /
  `five-hour`, exit 11 (`tests/cli_budget.rs:125–127` is the same call).

- **`pause` goes last in the folded case.** After a `pause` the wheel is the human's and `send` returns at
  line 338, never reaching the gate.

- **The four verbs read no gate.** `answer` is `src/run/dialog.rs:318–370`, `wait` and `last` are
  `src/run/wait.rs:135` on, `pause` is `src/run/wheel.rs:188–192`; none holds a gate call (the five call sites
  are listed in scope.md's folded freight).

- **`send-issued` keeps its own offset.** `append_event_at` computes the line's start under the lock
  (`crates/viola-state/src/events.rs:90`), so a `link` line appended before `ctx.issue` moves no cursor rule.

- **The first snapshot is where a start's set must land.** `start_state` writes `links: Vec::new()` at
  `src/cmd/run.rs:547`; a restored set that is not put there is lost until the next change.
- `src/run/links.rs` — the wrapper's link set: restored from the log, changed by record and remove, mirrored to the snapshot
- `src/cmd/link.rs` — the `viola link` client verb
- `src/cmd/unlink.rs` — the `viola unlink` client verb
- `tests/cli_links.rs` — root cases for the implicit link, the restart, E5's link step and the two verbs
- `tests/channel_links.rs` — the raw-channel name-validation negative for the two methods
- `crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs` — the two kinds and their test oracle
- `crates/viola-state/src/replay.rs` — the link rule and the replay's link half
- `crates/viola-state/src/events.rs` — two inline cases that use link as an unknown kind or list every kind
- `crates/viola-state/tests/state_events.rs` — the every-kind round trip and the unknown-kind sample
- `crates/viola-state/tests/state_replay.rs` — the crate-level link cases
- `src/run/mod.rs` — the new module's declaration
- `src/run/send.rs` — the implicit link on an issued send
- `src/run/dialog.rs` — the implicit link on a taken answer
- `src/cmd/run.rs` — the set at start, the first snapshot, the two dispatch arms and their unit cases
- `src/cmd/mod.rs` — the two subcommands and their dispatch
- `src/human.rs` — the three result lines
- `src/main.rs` — two role cases for the new verbs
- `tests/cli_budget.rs` — the folded closed-gate case
- `.config/nextest.toml` — the 20 s kill filter line gains the new stamped-home binary
- Does a `send` or an `answer` the wrapper refuses record the link? → blocks: plan-decision
- What keys does the `link` result carry, and does `unlink` carry any? → blocks: plan-decision
- What does an `unlink` of a pair that is not in the set do (a line, no line, a refusal)? → blocks: plan-decision

**Working entry** (`viola-0.1.0/working-route.md:121`, the head of the markerless tail, in
`### Epoch 4 — Session state & governance`): Session links — driver-to-driven link on first cross-instance send or
answer, explicit link/unlink, log-derived link set with since, link result payload — plus two CARRY blocks (folded
below; completeness check `route.py pins` → the run dir's trail: two `:121` rows, 521 and 737 chars, no
abstention). The entry carries no `BLOCKED-ON`, no `PREREQ` and no `WATCH`: the chunk has no acceptance gate.
**The operator's direction at take-up** (`inputs#I1`, the invocation, verbatim in the snapshot):
- no mutation run, no witness run and no workflow dispatch is planned;

- the folded test is in scope, with a control that fails without it: `answer`, `wait`, `last` and `pause` are
  not gated by a closed budget gate;

- a widening goes on the card as itself, unsettled, and the plan holds only that item, never the whole operator
  pass;
- a cut is proposed at the card if the chunk does not fit one window;
- the CI read is the `ci.py conclusion` call.

**CI read at Setup** (`ci.py conclusion`, one sha: the last flip commit is HEAD): `f02d5486` green, 15 of 15
checks, wall 454 s, run `ci#38094715870`. No red and no `not green` to disposition.

**Premise closure** (P3, at HEAD `f02d54865815`): every `[inferred]` bullet below was read against the extracts
and the code. A closed bullet carries no tag; a corrected one carries `[premise-corrected: …]`. What no master
sentence settles is listed under "Unworded shapes" for the plan's fork round.

1. **Two event kinds.** `link` and `unlink` join `viola_core::EventKind` (`ALL`, `from_name`, `data_keys`), each
   with the `data` keys `{driver, driven}`. The log reader `viola_state::events::read_from` then returns such a
   line where today it counts it under `unknown_kinds`.

2. **The replay's link half.** `viola_state::replay` derives `links` from the `link` / `unlink` lines of
   `events.ndjson`, each item `{driver, driven, since}`. `since` is the time of the first `link` line of the pair
   after any `unlink` of it (architecture §Established Decisions, [Links]).

3. **The implicit link.** A `send` or an `answer` that reaches a wrapper with a string `from` naming another
   instance appends one `link` line to that wrapper's own `events.ndjson`, only when the pair
   `from → this instance` is not already in its link set. A repeated send or answer adds no line. The snapshot's
   `links` is rewritten on each change of the set (architecture §Standard Contracts, Instance snapshot). `answer`
   already carries `from` on the wire (`src/cmd/answer.rs:120`, `src/run/dialog.rs:323`). A `from` equal to the
   wrapper's own name is no link: [Links] words the link as made "to another instance".

4. **Two channel methods.** `link` and `unlink`, params `{driver, driven}`, served by the driven instance's
   wrapper. Both names go through `ViolaName::try_new` on the wrapper as on the client (security-plan §Input
   Validation, row "Channel frames (IPC ndjson)"). An explicit `link` of an existing pair adds no line; `unlink`
   appends an `unlink` line. A `link` / `unlink` is not refused for a driver's `from` (security-plan
   §Authentication & Authorization, row "Driver-originated `release`"); architecture's list of methods that read
   `from` holds neither.

5. **Two CLI verbs.** `viola link <driver> <driven>` and `viola unlink <driver> <driven>`, in the human, plain
   and `--json` modes. The human lines are design-system §Surface: cli → Component Patterns, component 4
   "Wheel, link and gate verbs": the padded verb word, `<driver> -> <driven>` in ASCII, then for `link` the word
   `since` and a UTC clock time in the `HH:MM:SS` form with `Z`, or for an existing pair the words
   `already linked` with no time. Link output is plain at every colour depth.

6. **The link result payload.** The machine result of `link` carries the facts its human line prints: the
   first-linked time, and whether the pair already existed (requirement `v1-13`, the `link` half; intent F-13).
   Architecture's channel contract and [Links] both still read the result as the empty object, so the payload's
   keys are worded by no master: a fork for the plan and an amendment for the wrap. It is additive (no `v`
   bump).

7. **Tests.** The CLI and log half of test-plan §6 Scenario E3; Scenario E5's `link` step (the replay reads a
   link the wrapper wrote); the folded budget case below; the raw-channel `link` / `unlink` name-validation
   negative of test-plan §6 Security control negatives (found by the tests extract; the methods land here, so
   its case does); unit and crate-level cases for the kind table and the replay. E3's `/api/links` and
   Playwright signals are not built here (Boundaries).

8. **The set at a wrapper's start** (found at research). A wrapper that starts over an existing log, a revived
   one included, starts with the link set its log gives, as it already rebuilds the newest turn and the highest
   dialog id from the log before its endpoint serves (`src/cmd/run.rs:272`, `src/run/wait.rs:112`). The first
   snapshot of a start holds that set, never an empty one.

- **CARRY, chunk 2026-10-10-self-healing-state** (the operator's direction at its wrap, that chunk's
  input `I4`). Items 1, 2 and E5's `link` step in item 7 are this block. Coordinates re-verified at take-up:
  `crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs` declares `ALL: [Self; 13]` and a 13-row `KIND_TABLE`, and its case
  `kind_table_a_text_that_is_no_kind_parses_to_nothing` lists `"link"` and `"unlink"` as texts that are no kind
  (that case changes with item 1); `viola_state::replay`'s recovered state holds `links: Vec<Value>`.
  The mechanism claim is re-derived at HEAD: `events.rs:201` reads a line's kind through
  `EventKind::from_name`, `events.rs:261` counts a line it does not know under `unknown_kinds` and steps over
  it, and `replay.rs:57` matches three kinds and leaves `links` at its default.

- **CARRY, chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor** (the operator's answer at its wrap, that chunk's input `I11`,
  question 3; restated at this take-up, `inputs#I1`). Owed here: a root case in `tests/cli_budget.rs` that drives
  `answer`, `wait`, `last` and `pause` under a closed budget gate, the gate fed through `viola hook statusline`,
  no booted pair needed. It carries a control that fails without the property: in the same closed gate an
  automated `send` is refused `budget-paused`, so a gate that never closed cannot pass the case. Coordinates
  re-verified: `tests/cli_budget.rs` holds `e5_the_replay_reads_what_the_wrapper_wrote` and seven `path6_*` cases.
  One coordinate mis-aims: the block says the masters name this entry, and neither sentence does by title.
  Test-plan §6 Path 6 reads "its case is owed to the route", and a11y-plan §8 reads "no case drives one of them
  under a closed gate yet"; "Session links" is named three times in test-plan, all three for the replay and E5.
  Both sentences are the wrap's to amend when the case lands. The mechanism claim is re-derived at HEAD: the
  gate's product call sites are five (`start` at `src/cmd/run.rs:536`, `evaluate` at `src/cmd/run.rs:126` and
  `src/run/send.rs:347`, `lift` at `src/run/wheel.rs:214`, `paused` at `src/run/wheel.rs:222`; a read of each
  call under `src/`, test modules left out), none in `answer`, `wait`, `last` or `pause`, and no case drives
  one of the four under a closed gate.

_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-10-10-statusline-pass-through · **Version:** viola-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-10T16:32Z

A wrapped session records the usage reading its status line carries, and still shows the user's own status
line. `viola run` (and a passed `viola revive`, which starts through the same start) reads the user's statusline
command from one named source, records it in the instance snapshot, writes a per-session settings override that
puts `viola hook statusline` in the status line's place, and passes that override to the child. `viola hook
statusline` writes the `rate_limits` reading to `budget.json`, runs the user's command with the same stdin and
prints its output unchanged (per architecture §Standard Contracts → Hook contract; security-plan §Data
Protection; obs-plan §4 Scenario: Budget governor; test-plan §6 Path 6).

Nothing statusline-shaped exists at HEAD `4d77eac` (research.md finding 1), so the chunk also gives the fake
agent what it needs to rehearse it: the override read, a statusline run fed by a file the test owns, and the
`statusline-echo` mode. The property the fourth CARRY owes lands with the reader.

The chunk is built and proven under the fake agent only. Four things in it are the founder's and are not
settled by this plan (`inputs#I1`, `inputs#I2`, `inputs#I3`): three boundary widenings (W1 the override file
written at every start and passed to the CLI, W2 the user's command run through a shell, W3 the source files
that decide that command) and how the three CLI behaviours it relies on stand without a ledger row (R). Stop
rule S1 holds the whole chunk until his word on them is recorded. The Windows half is cut, provisionally
(`inputs#I3`), and so is the harness flag; each left-out part is named with its owner under Implementation
notes.

- **S1 — the founder's word on W1, W2, W3 and R.** /implement does not start step 1 until an `inputs/` snapshot
  records his word on each of the four: given in this repository's session, or relayed verbatim, after the
  item was shown to him (`inputs#I2`; the playbook's "Boundary widening — what ratifies it"). A master sentence,
  an operator direction and `inputs#I3` are not his word. With any of the four missing, /implement stops at its
  Setup and reports which are owed. His word given at this plan's review is recorded there and lifts S1.
  - W1: `instances/<name>/settings.json` written by `run` at every start and passed to the CLI with `--settings`.
  - W2: the user's statusline command run by `viola hook statusline` through `/bin/sh -c`, the only shell-out.
  - W3: `<viola home>/statusline-source.json`, and for the default home the user's `~/.claude/settings.json`, as
    the inputs that decide that command.
  - R: whether the three behaviours of step 12's table are relied on with no ledger row, and at what price in
    live starts. A word that opens a ledger row in this chunk is a revision of this plan, not a step of it.

- **S2 — no live start, row, verify child or re-stamp.** No step runs a live `claude` start, adds a
  `LedgerRow`, adds or changes a `viola verify` child, records a fixture or re-stamps a home, except step 12
  on the founder's number (`inputs#I1`).

- **S3 — the Windows cut is provisional** (`inputs#I3`). A different word from the founder comes as a revision.
  Until then every step builds the Windows side as written here: no override, no shell-out.

- Add the budget reading both crates share: two windows, `five_hour` and `seven_day`. A window is either the
  word `"unknown"` or `{used_percentage, resets_at}`; `used_percentage` is a JSON number or `"unknown"`;
  `resets_at` is an RFC 3339 UTC string or `"unknown"` (architecture §Standard Contracts, the `/api/sessions`
  envelope's `budget` bullet; §Conventions → Data model conventions, Unparseable external values).

- It holds no timestamp of its own and no Claude name. Its serde form is the one the file and later readers
  use. Unit cases named `budget_reading_…` pin each of the three "unknown" forms as written JSON.

- A new pure module, the one home of every Claude-specific statusline shape. Nothing in it reads a file, a
  clock or the environment. The crate takes the workspace's `chrono` (research.md, the crate fact).

- **The payload reader.** Input: the statusline stdin bytes. A payload that is not one JSON object is the
  crate's `AgentError::Malformed`. An object with no `rate_limits` object yields no reading. An object with one
  yields a reading: per window, an absent or non-object window is `"unknown"`; `used_percentage` is kept when
  it is a finite number from 0 to 100, else `"unknown"`; `resets_at` is taken as a whole number of Unix epoch
  seconds, or as an RFC 3339 string, and written as RFC 3339 UTC with milliseconds, else `"unknown"`
  (research.md finding 4; security-plan §Input Validation, Hook stdin row). Every other key, the documented
  `spend_limit` window included, is ignored. No `deny_unknown_fields` (architecture §Established Decisions
  [Validation]).

- **The settings reader.** Input: a settings file's bytes. It returns the user's command when the document is
  an object whose `statusLine.type` is the string `command` and whose `statusLine.command` is a non-empty
  string holding no NUL; anything else is no command, never an error.

- **The override document.** Input: the pinned binary's forward-slash absolute path. On Unix it returns the
  JSON document whose `statusLine` is `type` `command` and `command` the path, one space, `hook statusline`,
  but only when every character of the path is an ASCII letter, a digit or one of `_ - . / :`; for any other
  path it returns nothing (research.md finding 6). On Windows it returns nothing for every path (S3).

- **The flag and the shell.** The literal `--settings` is defined here and nowhere else in product code. The
  shell a user's command runs through is defined here: on Unix the absolute `/bin/sh` with `-c` and the
  command as ONE argument; on Windows none (S3). No `SHELL`, `COMSPEC` or `PATH` is read (architecture
  §Cross-cutting Patterns, Config management).

- Tests, in this crate: rstest tables named `statusline_reading_…`, `statusline_user_command_…` and
  `statusline_override_…` with one case per sentence above; and the property
  `statusline_prop_resets_at_never_fails`, `cases: 512`: for an arbitrary JSON value in `resets_at` and in
  `used_percentage` the reader returns without panicking, and each field is `"unknown"` or a value that
  round-trips (a number from 0 to 100; a string chrono parses as RFC 3339 in UTC). Build strings outside the
  format macro inside the `proptest!` body. Run the property red once on a stub that returns a wrong value, so
  proptest writes `proptest-regressions/statusline.txt`, and commit that file (test-plan §6 Property suite).

title: Step 3 — the snapshot field (`crates/viola-state/src/snapshot.rs` and the ten other literals)

data.head: ### Step 3 — the snapshot field (`crates/viola-state/src/snapshot.rs` and the ten other literals)

body:
- `InstanceSnapshot` gains `statusline_command`, optional, in the serde form of `cwd`
  (`crates/viola-state/src/snapshot.rs:58-61`): written when present, omitted otherwise, `v` stays 1.

- Add the field at each of the 11 struct literals (research.md, Graph impact: `src/cmd/run.rs:448`,
  `src/cmd/hook.rs:718`, `src/cmd/revive.rs:382`, `src/run/dialog.rs:444`, `src/run/wheel.rs:780`,
  `src/run/snapshot.rs:59`, `crates/viola-state/src/snapshot.rs:165`, `liveness.rs:79`, `replay.rs:175`,
  `strict.rs:724`, `crates/viola-state/tests/state_replay.rs:22`). Ten of them are test literals and take
  `None`; `src/cmd/run.rs:448` is step 6's.

- Unit cases `snapshot_statusline_command_is_written_under_v_1_and_reads_back` and
  `snapshot_statusline_command_reads_as_absent_without_its_key`, after the two `cwd` cases (`:315`, `:335`).
  The replay arm yields none; `state_replay.rs` asserts it beside `cwd`.

- A new module with one writer: given the viola home, a reading and the instant it was read, it replaces
  `<home>/budget.json` with `{"v":1,"five_hour":…,"seven_day":…,"read_at":"<RFC 3339 UTC ms>"}` under an
  exclusive lock on the sibling `budget.json.lock`, through `replace_private` at `FILE_MODE`
  (architecture §Occupied Resources, Viola home files; §Established Decisions [Database / State Store];
  security-plan §Authentication & Authorization, `~/.viola/` access control row). The lock file is opened with
  `open_private_lock`. Last writer wins.
- It builds no reader: the gate's read is the route entry "Budget governor"'s.

- Unit cases named `budget_write_…`: the written bytes are the envelope above with each "unknown" form; a
  second write replaces the first whole; on Unix both files read mode 0600; a write into a missing home
  directory fails and leaves nothing.

- One function decides which file is the statusline source for a start, from the absolute viola home:
  `<home>/statusline-source.json` when that file exists; otherwise, only when the home is the default home
  (`<user home>/.viola`, the path `resolve_home` yields with no `--home`), `<user home>/.claude/settings.json`;
  otherwise none (scope.md item 2; `inputs#I3`). The comparison is on the two absolute paths; `src/cmd/mod.rs`
  exposes the default home so `start` and `resolve_home` share one definition.

- The chosen file is read through `Read::take(MAX_FRAME)` and handed to step 2's settings reader. Absent,
  unreadable, over the cap, not an object, no command: each is "no command". The start is never refused for
  it, prints nothing and logs no line (the design and layouts extracts; obs-plan §6 names no field for it).
- viola opens both files read-only and writes neither.

- Unit cases named `statusline_source_…`: the home file wins; a `--home` home without it reads nothing even
  when a user settings file exists; the default home falls back to the user file. They use temp directories
  and never the developer's home.

- In `start` (`src/cmd/run.rs:205`), after `pin_and_plugin` and before `start_state`: resolve the user's
  command (step 5). `start_state` (`:437`) takes it and writes it into the first snapshot's
  `statusline_command` (`:448`); its two callers are `start` @ `src/cmd/run.rs:274` and the test helper
  `first_snapshot` @ `:962`.

- After `start_state` has created the instance directory and before `child_launch`: ask step 2 for the override
  document for `pinned.path_fwd`. When there is one, write it to `<instance dir>/settings.json` with
  `replace_private` at `FILE_MODE` (the per-instance helper, not the shared one: research.md, the security
  history's note on `replace_private_shared`), on every start, whatever stands there. A failed write fails the
  start the way a failed plugin write does. When there is none (an unsafe pinned path, or Windows), write
  nothing and pass nothing.

- `child_launch` (`src/run/mod.rs:102`) takes the override file's path, optional. With one, the child's
  arguments are `--plugin-dir <dir>`, then `--settings <file>`, then the caller's arguments (a revived start's
  `--resume` words stay after both). Its three callers: `start` @ `src/cmd/run.rs:283` and the unit tests @
  `src/run/mod.rs:178`, `:212`.

- The override is written and passed whether or not the user has a command, so a user with no status line
  still gets readings.

- No new span and no new log line; the span-order test (`src/cmd/run.rs:1028`) keeps its list. It starts in a
  temp home, which by step 5 reads no user file (research.md finding 13).

- Unit cases: `spawn_settings_flag_follows_the_plugin_dir` and `spawn_without_an_override_passes_no_settings_flag`
  in `src/run/mod.rs`; `snapshot_statusline_command_of_a_start_is_the_source_s_command` beside
  `snapshot_cwd_of_a_start_is_the_spawn_directory` in `src/cmd/run.rs`.

- `hook()` (`src/cmd/hook.rs:89`) dispatches the word `statusline`, with no `--capture`, to the new arm before
  `HookEvent::from_arg` (`:91`). `HookEvent` is untouched: the unit test at
  `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/hook.rs:323` still reads `None` for the word (research.md finding 10).

- The arm, in order. Every path exits 0 and writes nothing to stderr.
  1. `instance_of` (`:72`) on `VIOLA_NAME` and `VIOLA_DIR`. No instance: return, nothing written anywhere.
  2. Canonicalise the directory. If that fails, or the result no longer ends `<home>/instances/<name>`:
     return, nothing written. The canonical home and directory are used from here on.
  3. obs init as the other arms do, then the panic seam, then `hook-invoked` with `hook_event` `statusline`,
     `invoked_at` and no `corr`.
  4. `viola_state::strict::check_instance` on the home and the instance directory. A refusal: `hook-decision`
     with detail `strict-modes-failed` and `budget_written` false; nothing is read, run or written.
  5. Read stdin through `take(MAX_FRAME + 1)`. Over the cap: `parse-rejected` (`hook-stdin`, `oversize`) and
     `hook-decision` with detail `oversize-stdin`; nothing more. Step 2's reader says malformed:
     `parse-rejected` (`hook-stdin`, `malformed`) and `hook-decision` with detail `malformed-json`; nothing
     more (security-plan §Input Validation, Hook stdin row: no body on either).
  6. With a reading: step 4's writer, under a span `state.budget_write` whose fields are `five_hour_pct` and
     `seven_day_pct`. `budget_written` is true only when the write returned Ok. A failed write does not stop
     the arm. With no reading nothing is written and the last file stands.
  7. `read_snapshot` on the instance directory. No snapshot, an unreadable or newer one, or no
     `statusline_command`: skip to 9.
  8. The shell-out, where step 2 names a shell (Unix): spawn it directly with the command as one argument,
     stdin a pipe that receives exactly the bytes read at 5, stdout a pipe, stderr discarded, the arm's own
     environment and working directory unchanged. Log `process-start` and `process-exit` with `subject`
     `statusline-shell` at the call site, the exit line carrying `shell_exit_status` and `duration_ms`, under a
     span `statusline.shell_out`; neither line nor span carries the command. Read the child's stdout through
     `take(MAX_FRAME)`. Wait at most `STATUSLINE_DEADLINE`, a named constant of 5 s marked PROVISIONAL beside
     `CONNECT_DEADLINE` (`src/cmd/hook.rs:48`). At the bound: end the child the arm started, print nothing, and
     the decision carries detail `deadline` and `deadline_hit` true. The child exited 0 in time: ONE `write_all`
     of its stdout bytes to a locked stdout handle, no byte added or removed. Any other exit, or a shell that
     could not be started: print nothing.
  9. `hook-decision` with `hook_event` `statusline`, `budget_written` and `duration_ms` (the arm's whole run,
     the wait at 8 included).

- The bound's wait is a function that takes the bound as a value, so a unit case passes a short one; the
  product passes the constant. Unit cases named `statusline_shell_out_…` (Unix): output passed through byte
  for byte, ESC bytes included; a non-zero exit prints nothing; a child that outlives a 50 ms bound is ended
  and reads as the deadline. The child in each is one the test itself starts through `/bin/sh`.
- No `print!`; no second error enum; no `err` or `ret` on a span (obs-plan §11).

- Two argv options, read like the others and never from the environment: `--settings <file>` (the override
  `run` passes) and `--statusline-stdin <file>` (bytes a test owns).

- With both set: after the launch's SessionStart has fired, read the settings file, take `statusLine.command`,
  split it on ASCII whitespace, and when its first word is an absolute path spawn it directly (no shell, no
  `PATH`) with the remaining words as arguments and the stdin file's bytes on stdin. Receipt one line of kind
  `statusline` with `command_absolute`, `ran`, `exit_code`, `stderr_len`, `stdout_hex` and `stdin_hex`, the
  form of the `hook` receipt (`:445-457`). The run holds the same lock a hook run holds, so the agent's exit
  waits for it. Without `--statusline-stdin` nothing is run and nothing is receipted: the agent invents no
  payload (scope.md item 6). Nothing of the run is drawn on the agent's screen.

- A mode chosen by the first argument: `statusline-echo <marker file>`. It reads its stdin to the end, writes
  the fixed bytes `viola-fake-statusline` and a newline to stdout, appends one line holding the hex of the
  stdin it read to the marker file, and exits 0. With `--exit <code>` after the marker path it does the same
  and exits with that code.
- `tests/cli_fake_agent.rs`: one case per option and one for the mode, named `fake_statusline_…`.

- `home.rs`: a helper that plants `<home>/statusline-source.json` holding one command, only in a home viola
  has already created (a stamped home, or after a first boot and stop), and a helper that builds the test
  user command for this OS from the fake agent's path and a marker path under the home's `fake/`. Both paths
  hold only characters step 2's override rule accepts; the helper asserts it.
- `fake.rs`: the reader of the `statusline` receipt line.

title: Step 10 — the arm on the real binary (`tests/hook_statusline.rs`, `Cargo.toml`, `.config/nextest.toml`)

data.head: ### Step 10 — the arm on the real binary (`tests/hook_statusline.rs`, `Cargo.toml`, `.config/nextest.toml`)

body:
- A new root test file, registered as a `[[test]]` with `required-features = ["fake-agent"]`. If its cases boot
  stamped homes, add it to the verify-driven binary list of `.config/nextest.toml`; if they boot unstamped
  homes, leave that file alone and say so in the report. Each case runs the built `viola hook statusline` with
  `VIOLA_NAME` and `VIOLA_DIR` set by `Command::env`, feeds synthetic stdin that embeds the tests' canary, and
  reads the exit code, stdout and stderr apart through `tests/support/cli.rs`.

- Cases (names start `hook_statusline_`; the Unix-only ones are `cfg(unix)` inside one shared body where they
  can be):
  1. `…_passes_the_user_output_through_and_records_the_reading` (Unix): stdin with `five_hour` 91 and an epoch
     `resets_at`; stdout equals the echo's bytes; exit 0; stderr empty; `budget.json` holds 91 and the RFC 3339
     form of that epoch; the marker file's line is the hex of the stdin fed; the role file holds `hook-invoked`,
     the `statusline-shell` pair, then `hook-decision` with `budget_written` true and no `corr`.
  2. `…_without_rate_limits_writes_no_reading_and_still_passes_through` (Unix).
  3. `…_a_failing_command_prints_nothing` (Unix): the echo with `--exit 3`; empty stdout; exit 0; the pair's
     `shell_exit_status` is 3.
  4. `…_without_a_recorded_command_prints_nothing_and_records_the_reading`: every OS; on Windows this is the
     whole behaviour, with a source planted (S3).
  5. `…_a_home_another_user_can_write_runs_nothing` (Unix): the home at 0770; exit 0; empty stdout; the
     marker file and `budget.json` unchanged; detail `strict-modes-failed`. The frame: `check_instance` reads
     the home first (`crates/viola-state/src/strict.rs:39-47`) and `unix_verdict` refuses any group or other
     write bit (`:76-84`, `mode & 0o022`), which 0770 carries. Take its remove-the-guard reading
     once (the check neutralised inside the arm, the case red, the check restored) into `evidence/red-green.md`.
  6. `…_oversize_and_malformed_stdin_write_nothing`: two labelled cases; no `budget.json`; the two details.
  7. `…_outside_a_wrapped_session_writes_nothing`: no `VIOLA_NAME`; no file or directory is created.
  8. `…_changes_neither_the_snapshot_nor_the_stamps`: bytes and mtime of both read before and after.
  9. `…_keeps_the_command_and_the_payload_out_of_the_process_logs`: the echo's marker, the command string and
     the canary appear in no file under `<home>/diagnostics/`.
- No case waits out the 5 s bound (the bound is step 7's unit case).

title: Step 11 — the start on the real binary (`tests/cli_instance_state.rs`, `tests/tui_passthrough.rs`, `tests/hook_fail_open.rs`)

data.head: ### Step 11 — the start on the real binary (`tests/cli_instance_state.rs`, `tests/tui_passthrough.rs`, `tests/hook_fail_open.rs`)

body:
- `tests/cli_instance_state.rs`, beside `run_rewrites_the_plugin_folder_each_start` (`:334`):
  1. `run_rewrites_the_settings_override_each_start` (Unix): boot, stop, read the file; it is step 2's document,
     mode 0600, its command starting with the absolute pinned path under `<home>/bin/`; plant a sentinel; boot
     again; the sentinel is gone and the bytes are the first read's. On Windows the same case asserts that no
     `settings.json` exists after a start.
  2. `run_records_the_statusline_command_of_the_home_s_source`: a planted source; the snapshot's
     `statusline_command` is that command; the source file's bytes and mtime are unchanged after the start.
  3. `run_with_home_reads_no_user_settings`: the child `viola` is given, by `Command::env`, a user home
     directory (in the test's scratch) whose `.claude/settings.json` holds a command, and `--home` names the
     test home: the snapshot holds no `statusline_command`.
  4. `run_in_the_default_home_reads_the_user_settings`: the same scratch user home and no `--home`, so the
     default home is created under the scratch: the snapshot holds the command, and the user file's bytes and
     mtime are unchanged. The frame both cases turn on: `resolve_home` (`src/cmd/mod.rs:159`) takes the user
     home from `std::env::home_dir()`, which reads `HOME` on Unix and `USERPROFILE` on Windows (the standard
     library's documented behaviour; `pre-push` relies on the same read when it launches every child with the
     passwd `HOME`), so the test sets that one variable on the child.
  5. `path6_wrapped_statusline_prints_the_user_output_unchanged` (Unix): a planted source whose command is the
     echo; the fake agent is given `--statusline-stdin`; its `statusline` receipt reads `ran` true, `exit_code`
     0, and a `stdout_hex` equal to the echo's bytes; `budget.json` holds the fed percentage. This is the one
     case that runs the override end to end: the fake agent, the pinned `viola hook statusline`, `/bin/sh`,
     the echo.

- `tests/tui_passthrough.rs`: `passthrough_with_a_statusline_source_adds_no_viola_bytes`: a start over a home
  with a planted source; the outer-PTY stream holds none of `VIOLA_LITERALS` on every OS. The existing
  comparison cases pass no `--statusline-stdin` and stay as they are.
- `tests/hook_fail_open.rs:180`: the `unknown_event` case names `status-line`, a word that is still unknown.

- Extend the fuzz target `fuzz/fuzz_targets/hook_stdin.rs` to hand the same bytes to step 2's payload reader
  (it must not panic), and add the two synthetic seeds `fuzz/corpus/hook_stdin/statusline-epoch` and
  `statusline-absent`. Neither holds a path, a user name or a real reading.

title: Step 12 — the live readings (held: runs only on the founder's number)

data.head: ### Step 12 — the live readings (held: runs only on the founder's number)

body:
- Not run by /implement unless the founder's number of live `claude` starts for this chunk is relayed (S1's R,
  `inputs#I1`). With no number by the wrap the step is reported as owed and nothing else waits on it.

- What each behaviour is, who relies on it first, and what a reading of it takes:

  | behaviour | relied on by | read by |
  |---|---|---|
  | the settings override: a `statusLine` in `--settings` replaces the user's for the session, and the unquoted `<path> hook statusline` string runs | step 6, from the first wrapped start | start 2 |
  | the shell a statusline command runs through on Linux (`/bin/sh -c` is the plan's hypothesis) | step 7 | start 1 |
  | `rate_limits`: its shape, `resets_at` as epoch seconds, when it is absent | recorded here; first relied on by a `send` refusal in "Budget governor" | starts 1 and 2 |

- With a number of three or more, on the headless pty rig of chunk
  2026-10-09-inner-cr-and-crlf-in-a-sent-text (`evidence/live-pty.py`, `live-start.sh`,
  `live-preconditions.md` there), the stamped CLI's install directory first on `PATH` and `claude --version`
  read by path first, in a trusted folder, with `VIOLA_NAME`, `VIOLA_DIR` and `VIOLA_BIN` removed:
  1. an unwrapped session whose user-scope statusline command is a recorder kept in the rig's private
     directory: it files its stdin and its parent process's name. One short prompt, so a response arrives.
     Read: the shell, the payload's key set, `rate_limits` and the type of `resets_at` (start 1);
  2. the same session under `viola run --home <rig home>` with the recorder planted as the home's source.
     Read: the recorder ran with the same payload, `budget.json`, the hook's role lines (start 2);
  3. a wrapped start with no source: the override alone, and what the status line row shows (start 3).

- Record every reading, each wait's length and what it settled on, in `evidence/live-statusline.md`, with the
  rig's private directory named. No reading becomes a ledger row or a fixture, the recorder's files stay out
  of the tree, and no acceptance criterion below rests on this step.
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/statusline.rs` — the payload reader, the settings reader, the override document, the flag, the shell, their unit and property tests
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/proptest-regressions/statusline.txt` — the property's committed seeds
- `crates/viola-state/src/budget.rs` — `budget.json` under its lock, with its unit tests
- `src/cmd/hook/statusline.rs` — the `hook statusline` arm
- `tests/hook_statusline.rs` — the arm on the real binary
- `fuzz/corpus/hook_stdin/statusline-epoch` — a synthetic seed
- `fuzz/corpus/hook_stdin/statusline-absent` — a synthetic seed
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/lib.rs` — the module; no new error enum
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/Cargo.toml` — the workspace's `chrono`
- `Cargo.lock` — the one line that edge adds
- `crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs` — the normalised reading
- `crates/viola-state/src/lib.rs` — the `budget` module
- `crates/viola-state/src/snapshot.rs` — the field and its cases
- `crates/viola-state/src/liveness.rs` — one snapshot literal
- `crates/viola-state/src/replay.rs` — one snapshot literal
- `crates/viola-state/src/strict.rs` — one snapshot literal
- `crates/viola-state/tests/state_replay.rs` — one snapshot literal and the replay assertion
- `src/cmd/mod.rs` — the default home, shared
- `src/cmd/run.rs` — the source read, the first snapshot's field, the override write
- `src/cmd/revive.rs` — one snapshot literal
- `src/cmd/hook.rs` — the dispatch, one snapshot literal, the new constant
- `src/run/mod.rs` — `child_launch`'s override argument
- `src/run/dialog.rs` — one snapshot literal
- `src/run/wheel.rs` — one snapshot literal
- `src/run/snapshot.rs` — one snapshot literal
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs` — two options, the statusline run, the `statusline-echo` mode
- `tests/support/home.rs` — the source and command helpers
- `tests/support/fake.rs` — the `statusline` receipt reader
- `tests/cli_instance_state.rs` — five cases
- `tests/tui_passthrough.rs` — one case
- `tests/hook_fail_open.rs` — one case's word
- `tests/cli_fake_agent.rs` — the option and mode cases
- `fuzz/fuzz_targets/hook_stdin.rs` — the payload reader joins the target
- `Cargo.toml` — the `[[test]]` entry
- `.config/nextest.toml` — only if step 10's cases boot stamped homes

The gates are the standing lint and unit entries; one unit filter and one integration filter that select what
this chunk adds; a preservation guard; the fuzz corpus replay; the harness smoke with G2 and G4 over its home;
the native `pre-push`; and the operator's hygiene, push and CI read (`leg = "operator"`, the `ci.py conclusion`
call, `inputs#I1`).

No mutation entry, no witness run and no workflow dispatch is listed (`inputs#I1`). No entry is a live leg:
step 12 is held, makes its own record in `evidence/live-statusline.md` when it runs, and no entry reads that
record. Step 10's remove-the-guard reading is implement's, in `evidence/red-green.md`, and is never an entry.

The smoke boots an ordinary `viola run` session. Its home is named by `--home`, so it reads no user settings;
on the Linux dev host the start writes the override and passes it to the fake agent, which runs nothing
without `--statusline-stdin`. The preservation guard names the base commit, because the operator pass's pre-CI
commit moves HEAD onto the chunk; it is what shows that no ledger row, schema value, fixture or harness file
moved.
