body:
- (arch) The statusline payload reader, the settings reader, the override document, the `--settings` literal
  and the shell are defined in `viola-agent-claude` and nowhere else in product code; `budget.json` and
  `settings.json` are written through `viola-state`'s replace helper; `viola-agent-claude` gains no
  `viola-state` edge and no crate gains Tokio. Proven by the unit filter entry and by the entry `cargo clippy
  --workspace --all-targets --features fake-agent -- -D warnings` (per architecture §Infrastructure Patterns →
  Crate dependency direction)

- (arch) `viola hook statusline` exits 0 with empty stderr on every path the cases drive, prints the user
  command's stdout byte for byte, and prints nothing when the snapshot is absent or holds no
  `statusline_command`. Proven by cases 1 to 4 of `binary(hook_statusline)` (per architecture §Standard
  Contracts → Hook contract; §Standard Contracts → Snapshot envelope)

- (arch) `budget.json` is written only by `hook statusline`, by replace under `budget.json.lock`, in the home
  derived from `VIOLA_DIR`, as `v` 1 with the per-window reading and `read_at`, and with `"unknown"` for an
  unparseable field and for an omitted window. Proven by the `budget_write` and `statusline_reading` cases of
  the unit filter entry and by case 1 of `binary(hook_statusline)` (per architecture §Occupied Resources, Viola
  home files; §Conventions → Data model conventions)

- (arch) The chunk adds no environment variable, `config.json` key, flag of `viola`, channel method, event kind
  or listener; the snapshot's `v` stays 1 and `statusline_command` is omitted when no command was found; no
  ledger row, hook event or schema value is added. Proven by the `snapshot_statusline_command` cases and by
  the preservation guard entry exiting 0 (per architecture §Cross-cutting Patterns, Config management;
  §Conventions → Interfaces and versioning, Protocol versioning)

- (arch) A start names its source by one rule: the home's `statusline-source.json` when present, the user's
  settings file only for the default home, none otherwise; viola writes neither file. Proven by the
  `statusline_source` unit cases and by cases 2, 3 and 4 of step 11 in `binary(cli_instance_state)` (per
  architecture §Standard Contracts → Hook contract; §Cross-cutting Patterns, Config management)

- (security) `viola hook statusline` started against a home another user can write runs no command, prints
  nothing, changes neither the marker file nor `budget.json`, leaves stderr empty and exits 0. Proven by case 5
  of `binary(hook_statusline)` with its one-shot remove-the-guard reading in `evidence/red-green.md` (per
  security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Data Protection; §Authentication & Authorization, `~/.viola/` access
  control row)

- (security) After a start over an altered `instances/<name>/settings.json` the file holds the freshly rendered
  bytes at mode 0600 and its command begins with the absolute pinned path; `budget.json` reads mode 0600 on
  Unix. Proven by `run_rewrites_the_settings_override_each_start` and the `budget_write` cases (per
  security-plan §Data Protection, At rest, Code-bearing artefacts)

- (security) A statusline stdin of `MAX_FRAME + 1` bytes, and one that is not a JSON object, each end in exit 0
  with empty stderr and no `budget.json`; a malformed `resets_at` is recorded as `"unknown"`. Proven by case 6
  of `binary(hook_statusline)` and the `statusline_reading` cases (per security-plan §Input Validation, Hook
  stdin row)

- (security) The test statusline command, the echo's marker and the canary are found in no file under
  `<home>/diagnostics/` and in no stderr of the run. Proven by case 9 of `binary(hook_statusline)` (per
  security-plan §Bootstrap phases, `logging-redaction-wire`)

- (security) `hook statusline` changes neither `snapshot.json` nor `ledger/stamps.json`. Proven by case 8 of
  `binary(hook_statusline)` (per security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Universal)

- (tests) The entry `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --unit` and the two filter entries are green; the entry
  `bash scripts/agent-run.sh pre-push` is green with coverage at lines 85, functions 95 and regions 80 or above
  and the ignore regex unchanged; no mutation gate applies (per test-plan §3 `run`; §10 Coverage thresholds;
  §10 Mutation gate)

- (tests) With a home whose source names the fake agent's `statusline-echo`, synthetic stdin piped into `viola
  hook statusline` gives stdout equal to the marker byte for byte, exit 0, empty stderr and a `budget.json`
  holding the fed percentage; under a 0770 home it gives exit 0, empty stdout and an unchanged marker file.
  Proven by cases 1 and 5 of `binary(hook_statusline)` (per test-plan §6 Path 6, Verification signal)

- (tests) The statusline `resets_at` property runs at `cases: 512` and its regressions file is committed; a
  malformed `resets_at` reads `"unknown"` in a unit case. Proven by `statusline_prop_resets_at_never_fails` in
  the unit filter entry and by `crates/viola-agent-claude/proptest-regressions/statusline.txt` in the tree (per
  test-plan §6 Property suite; §4 What unit tests cover)

- (tests) The `hook_stdin` fuzz target reaches the statusline reader and its corpus replays green with the two
  new seeds. Proven by the entry `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --fuzz-replay` (per test-plan §2 Test pyramid,
  Property-based)

- (obs) One wrapped statusline invocation leaves, in `hook-<name>.ndjson`, `hook-invoked`, the
  `statusline-shell` `process-start` / `process-exit` pair, then `hook-decision` with `budget_written` and no
  `corr`; without `VIOLA_NAME` it leaves no file and no line. Proven by cases 1 and 7 of
  `binary(hook_statusline)` (per obs-plan §4 Scenario: Budget governor; §4 Edge flows E1)

- (design, layouts) `viola run` with a statusline source present, absent or unreadable prints no line of its
  own; `viola hook statusline` adds no byte to the user's output; `viola --help` gains no verb. Proven by
  `passthrough_with_a_statusline_source_adds_no_viola_bytes`, by case 1 of `binary(hook_statusline)` and by the
  preservation guard over `src/main.rs` (per design-system §Surface: cli → Component Patterns (5);
  layout-templates §Surface: cli · Component — Header / banner)

- (a11y) The existing zero-viola-bytes cases stay green on all three OS legs after the fake agent gains its
  settings read, and the new statusline-bearing start holds none of viola's literals. Proven by
  `binary(tui_passthrough)` in the integration filter entry and by the operator's CI read (per a11y-plan §3
  Keyboard test harness → Tooling)

- (ci) The run the entry `python -X utf8 ~/.claude/skills/andromeda-phase/../andromeda-tools/scripts/ci.py
  conclusion --sha HEAD --wait 1800` reads on the final HEAD is green on all three OSes; the report names its
  run id (per test-plan §9 CI Integration)

- No capability is claimed. `verification-matrix.json#v1-24` is advanced and not proven by this chunk: its
  acceptance names no OS, and with the Windows half cut (S3) a wrapped session's status line is proven unchanged
  only on Linux and macOS, under the fake agent.

- Spec anchors the plan rests on (from the extracts): architecture §Standard Contracts → Hook contract ·
  §Standard Contracts → Instance snapshot · §Standard Contracts → Snapshot envelope · §Occupied Resources (Viola
  home files; Claude Code integration names; Environment variables) · §Established Decisions [CLI Version
  Compatibility] · [Validation] · [Snapshot writer] · [Database / State Store] · [Session Liveness] ·
  §Cross-cutting Patterns (Capability ledger as the single gate; Cross-platform discipline; Config management)
  · §Infrastructure Patterns → Crate dependency direction; security-plan §Authentication & Authorization
  (`~/.viola/` access control row) · §Input Validation (Hook stdin row; CLI arguments / stdin row) · §Data
  Protection (At rest, Code-bearing artefacts) · §Bootstrap phases (`logging-redaction-wire`) · §Security
  Anti-Patterns → Universal, Data Protection, Code Patterns, Logging; test-plan §1 · §3 `boot` · §4 · §5 · §6
  Path 1, Path 6, Property suite · §7 · §10 · §11; obs-plan §4 Scenario: Budget governor · §6 · §8 · §9 · §10;
  design-system §Surface: cli; layout-templates §Surface: cli; a11y-plan §1 · §3 Keyboard test harness.
- Research files inspected: the 23 entries of research.md §Files inspected (count: the section's items).

- The playbook's `verdict: escalate` patterns were read at P4 (`.andromeda/playbook.md:36-38`, `:48-50`): W1, W2
  and W3 are each a "Boundary widening". W3 was asked as the P4 fork; its answer and the Windows answer are
  `inputs#I3`, both provisional by the operator's own notes.

- Leaned without a question: user-scope settings only as the named file (the entry's "named" and
  `viola-0.1.0/intent.md:263`); `resets_at` as epoch seconds or RFC 3339 (the fetched documentation, research.md
  Platform issues consulted); a write only when `rate_limits` is present (research.md finding 5 and the
  schema's existing `budget_written`); the arm canonicalises `VIOLA_DIR` and runs the instance check, so it
  borrows no dated gap (the security extract's first two constraints).

- A `config.json` key naming the source — every existing test that boots a wrapper would read the developer's
  settings, and a home that does not exist before viola creates it cannot hold the key (`inputs#I3`; research.md
  finding 3).

- A third `fake-agent` environment seam for the source — security-plan allows no seam beyond the two without
  its own entry, and the release build would read another source than the tested one.

- Reading project, local or managed settings for the command — "named" is one file; the limit is stated on
  the card.

- An exec-form override (`command` plus `args`) — the fetched documentation names no `args` key for
  `statusLine`; unmeasured.

- Quoting the pinned path in the override — the right quoting differs by shell and the shell is unmeasured;
  an unsafe path gets no override instead.
- A Windows shell chosen from the documentation, or PowerShell alone — research.md finding 7; S3.

- A recorded or invented statusline payload in the fake agent — test-plan §7's "no shape before a recorded
  fixture"; the agent relays a test's file.

- `statusline` as a tenth `HookEvent` — it is not a Claude Code hook event; the perf rows and the dialog
  parser key on that set.

- A new `hook-decision` detail code, a new span name outside the three obs-plan names, or a `process-start`
  field naming the source — each is a schema or catalog amendment the chunk does not need.

- An end-to-end case that waits out `STATUSLINE_DEADLINE` — a test-owned wait on a product bound (test-plan
  §11 Universal); the bound is a unit case with a short value.
- Do not run the user's command, write `budget.json` or read the snapshot before the instance check passes.
- Do not write the override with `replace_private_shared`: the file is one instance's.
- Do not pass the command to the shell as anything but one argument, and never build a shell line from it.
- Do not add a hint, a refusal line or any terminal byte for an absent or unreadable source.

- **The widenings as the card shows them** (each unsettled, `inputs#I1`):
  - W1 — a code-bearing file viola writes into the instance directory at every start and hands to the CLI.
    Controls in this plan: `replace_private` at 0600, rewritten whatever stands there, the pinned absolute
    path, no override for a path a shell could misread.
  - W2 — a user-written string run through `/bin/sh -c`. Controls: one argument, the instance check first, the
    canonicalised directory, a bound, stderr discarded, no line carrying the string. Not controlled: what the
    command does; it runs as the user, as it does without viola.
  - W3 — two files decide that string. Controls: read-only, capped, tolerant; a `--home` home never reads the
    user's file. Not on security-plan's trusted-file list today.

- **What no master states and this plan chose** (the security extract's last binding): the user's command gets
  the arm's environment and working directory unchanged; its stderr is discarded; the bound is 5 s,
  PROVISIONAL; a status line set outside user-scope settings is not seen.

- **Not measured** (research.md, Platform issues consulted — documentation, not the installed build): that a
  `statusLine` in `--settings` replaces the user's; that the unquoted string runs; the shell on Linux and
  macOS; the payload's shape on 2.1.287; how the CLI cancels a script still running, and whether the user's
  command then outlives the arm. A fake-agent green claims none of these.

- **Counts this chunk moves, each with its rule**: the fake agent's argv options, ten → twelve (architecture's
  own list, `architecture.md:356`, is the count's rule), plus one mode word; `InstanceSnapshot` literals stay 11
  (`grep -rn -E 'InstanceSnapshot \{' src crates tests --include=*.rs`: 18 lines, less the type's own
  definition and the six signature lines); the fail-open matrix stays 11 cases (`tests/hook_fail_open.rs:174-184`,
  the `#[case::…]` lines); the `hook_stdin` corpus, ten → twelve seeds (`ls fuzz/corpus/hook_stdin`); root waits
  (`Instant::now() + WITHIN` under `tests/`): predicted to rise by the new file's waits — record what the count
  reads after step 10.

- **Order**: steps 1 to 4 have no consumer until 6 and 7; build 6 and 7 in the same sitting so no function sits
  without an observable effect (testing.md, 2026-09-24). Step 8 before 10 and 11.

- **Pitfalls**: a case that starts `viola` without `--home` must give the child its user home by `Command::env`
  and nothing else of the developer's; a test command built for `/bin/sh` must hold only the override rule's
  safe characters or it is not what the fake agent can split; the arm's stdout is the user's bytes, so nothing
  else of viola's may reach it, a panic line included (the panic hook writes the role file only).

- Expected amendments (wrap): architecture §Standard Contracts → Hook contract — the named source rule, the
  arm's order, the bound, the command's environment, directory and stderr, no output on oversize or malformed
  stdin, the write only with `rate_limits`.

- Expected amendments (wrap): architecture §Occupied Resources — `statusline-source.json`, `settings.json` as
  landed (when written, the unsafe-path case, none on Windows), `budget.json`'s envelope with `v`, `--settings`
  among the flags passed to the child, the fake agent's twelve options and its mode.

- Expected amendments (wrap): architecture §Standard Contracts → Instance snapshot — `statusline_command` as
  landed. §Established Decisions [Session Liveness] — the override's place in the start order. §Cross-cutting
  Patterns (Config management) — the per-home source. §Cross-cutting Patterns (Capability ledger) — only what
  the founder's word R says; no sentence about relied-on shapes is written without it.

- Expected amendments (wrap): architecture §Infrastructure Patterns → Crate dependency direction —
  `viola-agent-claude` names `chrono`.

- Expected amendments (wrap): security-plan §Data Protection (Code-bearing artefacts) and §Authentication &
  Authorization — `settings.json` as landed, the trusted-file list and `statusline-source.json`, the arm's
  check before the read. §Input Validation — the two new readers and `resets_at` as epoch seconds. Each of W1,
  W2 and W3 is written with the founder's word as recorded, or as "Not ratified". The pattern: Boundary
  widening; answered by the founder only.

- Expected amendments (wrap): test-plan §3 → 5-command implementation — `--statusline-echo` owed to "Budget
  governor", its refusal's premise (the source is now named). §6 Path 6 — step 1's open question closed, step
  2's `resets_at` form. §6 Property suite and §7 Fake agent — the property, the two options, the mode, the
  `statusline` receipt. §7 Seed strategies — the source planted in a home viola created.

- Expected amendments (wrap): obs-plan §4 Scenario: Budget governor — the hook half as landed, the details the
  arm uses. §6 `detail` code catalog — `deadline` covers the command's bound.

- Expected amendments (wrap): a11y-plan §3 → Keyboard test harness — the statusline-bearing start. §8 Cognitive
  Accessibility (Timeout extensions) — the command's bound, on whom it falls.

- No amendment is expected in design-system or layout-templates: the chunk adds no start refusal, no hint and
  no `viola verify` row.

- The ledger notes for the two capabilities this chunk advances and does not claim (`v1-24`, `v1-45`) are
  written by phase P5 after the word, not by the wrap.

- **Pitfall, Windows x64**: a case that starts `viola` in a home the test did not boot before (step 11's
  default-home case) seeds the ConPTY companions into that home first, as every other start does
  (`tests/support/home.rs` `seed_conpty`).

**Chunk:** Statusline pass-through — named read-only source, per-home redirect for tests, settings.json rewritten
each start with absolute pinned path, user output unchanged, readings to budget.json
**Date:** 2026-10-10
**Commits:** `58f8720` chore(…): operator pre-CI commit, for the run this chunk's verdict reads · `67ab367`
fix(…): operator fix after CI run 38080061631, the every-OS hook_statusline cases start from a stamped home and
two unix-only helpers are cfg(unix) (basis: `git log --format='%h %s' 4d77eac..HEAD`, the parent of the oldest
pre-CI commit)

- **Files:** 36 changed against `4d77eac` (basis: `gate.py scope`, `changed 36 · listed 35 · recorded 1`).
  - New (7): `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/statusline.rs`,
    `crates/viola-agent-claude/proptest-regressions/statusline.txt`, `crates/viola-state/src/budget.rs`,
    `src/cmd/hook/statusline.rs`, `tests/hook_statusline.rs`, `fuzz/corpus/hook_stdin/statusline-epoch`,
    `fuzz/corpus/hook_stdin/statusline-absent`.
  - Product, modified: `crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs`, `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/lib.rs`,
    `crates/viola-agent-claude/Cargo.toml`, `crates/viola-state/src/{lib,snapshot,replay,liveness,strict}.rs`,
    `src/cmd/{mod,run,hook,revive}.rs`, `src/run/{mod,dialog,wheel,snapshot}.rs`.
  - Test-only, modified: `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs`, `tests/{cli_fake_agent,cli_instance_state,
    tui_passthrough,hook_fail_open}.rs`, `tests/support/{home,fake}.rs`, `crates/viola-state/tests/state_replay.rs`,
    `fuzz/fuzz_targets/hook_stdin.rs`.
  - Build and config: `Cargo.toml` (one `[[test]]` entry), `Cargo.lock` (one line), `fuzz/Cargo.lock` (24
    packages), `.config/nextest.toml` (one binary added to a list).

- **Symbols / APIs:**
  - `viola-core`: `Reading<T>` (a value, or the word `"unknown"`), `UnknownWord`, `BudgetWindow
    {used_percentage: Reading<f64>, resets_at: Reading<String>}`, `BudgetReading {five_hour, seven_day}`. Serde
    both ways. No timestamp of its own, no Claude name.
  - `viola-agent-claude::statusline` (new module, pure: no file, clock or environment read): `reading(stdin) ->
    Result<Option<BudgetReading>, AgentError>` (not one JSON object → `AgentError::Malformed`; no `rate_limits`
    object → `None`), `user_command(settings) -> Option<String>`, `override_document(pinned_bin_fwd) ->
    Option<String>`, `shell_argv(command) -> Option<[&str; 3]>` (`/bin/sh`, `-c`, the command as one argument),
    `SETTINGS_FLAG = "--settings"`, `USER_SETTINGS = [".claude", "settings.json"]`. On Windows
    `override_document` and `shell_argv` return `None` for every input. No new error enum, no new `AgentError`
    variant.
  - `viola-state`: `budget::write_budget(home, &BudgetReading, read_at)` and `budget::BUDGET`;
    `InstanceSnapshot.statusline_command: Option<String>` (omitted when absent, `v` stays 1).
    **`SnapshotRead::Present` and `replay::Recovered::Snapshot` now hold `Box<InstanceSnapshot>`** (clippy
    `large_enum_variant` once the snapshot reached 216 bytes). Remaining callers: `read_snapshot` (unboxes; its

- **Platform issues consulted:** `https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline`, fetched 2026-10-10. The fetched
  page states, and nothing here was measured on the installed build:
  - `statusLine` goes in user settings (`~/.claude/settings.json`) or project settings; its keys are `type`
    (`"command"`), `command`, and optional `padding`, `refreshInterval`, `hideVimModeIndicator`. It documents no
    `args` key. "The `command` field runs in a shell";
  - on Windows the command runs "through Git Bash when Git Bash is installed, or through PowerShell when Git
    Bash is absent", and paths in `command` take forward slashes;
  - `rate_limits.<window>.used_percentage` is a number from 0 to 100 (its example reads `23.5`) and
    `rate_limits.<window>.resets_at` is "Unix epoch seconds" (its example reads `1738425600`). `rate_limits`
    "appears only for claude.ai Pro and Max subscribers ... and only after the first API response in the
    session"; each window may be absent on its own; a window is dropped once its `resets_at` passes; a third
    window `spend_limit` exists behind a gateway;
  - the script runs once at session start (a resume included) and again on a new assistant message and other
    listed triggers, debounced at 300 ms; "If a new update triggers while your script is still running, Claude
    Code cancels the in-flight script"; Claude Code captures the output and sets `COLUMNS` and `LINES` for the

1. **Nothing statusline-shaped is built.** The search in `scope.md` stands (`grep -rn -i -l -E
   'statusline|status_line' src crates plugin fixtures scripts`: two files, both test data).

2. **The diagnostics schema is ahead of the code.** Every line and field obs-plan's scenario names for the hook
   side is already admitted (`diag-line.v1.json:53-58`, `:78-83`, `:129`, `:131`); no schema change is needed

3. **Every test home would read the developer's own settings.** A start that reads `<user home>/.claude/
   settings.json` whenever no redirect is planted would do so in every existing test that boots a wrapper,
   and under `pre-push` (whose children get the passwd `HOME`). A test home does not exist before viola creates

   default home never reads the user's settings.

4. **`resets_at` is documented as epoch seconds, a number.** Test-plan §6 Path 6 step 2 feeds an RFC 3339
   string, and security-plan §Input Validation says it is "parsed with chrono in UTC only". A parser that took
   only a string would record `"unknown"` for every reading the documentation describes.

title: 1. The source: the user's statusline command, named and read-only

data.head: ### 1. The source: the user's statusline command, named and read-only

body:
- Source: the entry's title ("named read-only source"); architecture §Hook contract (`architecture.md:324`): `run`
  resolves the command from the user's effective Claude Code settings at start, in `viola-agent-claude`, and
  records it in the instance snapshot as `statusline_command` (`architecture.md:255`, an optional field).
- The entry states: the source is named and read-only. viola never writes the user's settings file.

- [premise-corrected: research.md, Platform issues consulted and finding 3 — "effective settings" has several
  scopes, and one named location is what the entry asks for] The named source is one file: the user-scope
  settings file `<user home>/.claude/settings.json`, key `statusLine.command` where `statusLine.type` is
  `"command"`. A status line set only in project, local or managed settings is not seen; the review card says
  so. Which home reads it is item 2.

- Verified (`crates/viola-state/src/snapshot.rs:58-61`, the `cwd` field): `statusline_command` is an optional,
  additive snapshot field, omitted on write when no command was found; the snapshot's `v` stays 1.

- Verified (the security and obs extracts; `security-plan.md:431`): the command string is user content. It
  stands in `snapshot.json` and reaches no process-log line, error body or event.

- Verified (research.md, Patterns detected): the parse of the settings bytes is a pure function in
  `viola-agent-claude`; the read of the file is the root bin's, through `Read::take(MAX_FRAME)`. No
  `viola-agent-claude` → `viola-state` edge is added.

- A settings file that is absent, unreadable, over the cap or not an object, or that holds no command, yields
  no command. The start is not refused and prints nothing (the design and layouts extracts: no statusline
  cause stands in the start-refusal list).

- Source: the entry's title ("per-home redirect for tests"); test-plan §6 Path 6 step 1 (`test-plan.md:838`): the
  settings source the harness writes the user's statusline command to is a §12 open question, and until it is
  resolved the pass-through bullets of that path are blocked.

- Verified (architecture §Cross-cutting Patterns, Config management; the security extract): the redirect is no
  environment variable, no flag and no third test seam.

- [premise-corrected: research.md findings 3 and 13 — a redirect a test must plant first cannot protect a home
  that does not exist before viola creates it] The form: a file in the viola home, `<viola home>/
  statusline-source.json`, in the Claude settings shape, is the source whenever it exists. The user's own
  settings file (item 1) is read only by the default home, `<user home>/.viola`. A home named by `--home` that
  holds no such file has no statusline command. So no test home and no `pre-push` child reads the developer's
  settings, with no step in any test.

- This is a new input that decides a command viola runs through a shell, and a new file in the home that
  nothing lists as trusted (the security extract's last binding). The playbook's "Boundary widening" pattern
  names it. The P4 fork took this form as a planning form only (`inputs#I3`): the widening is being shown to the
  founder, and the plan holds it behind its stop rule until his answer is relayed.

- Source: the entry's title ("settings.json rewritten each start with absolute pinned path") and the third
  CARRY (chunk 2026-09-27-instance-state-and-start-order wrote no such file; this entry rewrites it on every
  start through `viola_state::fs::replace_private`, security-plan §Data Protection).

- Re-verified at P1: `replace_private` exists (`crates/viola-state/src/fs.rs:263`); `security-plan.md:275` (under
  `## Data Protection`) says the file is rewritten by `viola run` at every start, 0600, never reused from an
  existing copy, its command the absolute pinned `bin/<version>-<hash>/viola(.exe)` path; no writer exists.

- The file wraps the statusline with `viola hook statusline` and is passed to the child through the
  settings-override mechanism (`architecture.md:367`), which is an unlanded ledger row (item 8).
- Verified (`src/cmd/revive.rs:103`): `viola revive` starts through `run`'s own start, so it writes the file too.

- Verified (research.md finding 8): `viola verify` already starts the real CLI with `--settings` (Runs C and
  D). The flag is the mechanism; that a `statusLine` key in it replaces the user's status line is not measured.

- [premise-corrected: research.md finding 6 — the documented `command` is a shell string and no `args` key is
  documented] The override's command is the pinned forward-slash path followed by `hook statusline`, written
  with no quoting, and only when the path holds nothing a shell would treat specially (ASCII letters, digits,
  `_`, `-`, `.`, `/` and `:`). For any other pinned path `run` writes no override and passes none: the session
  keeps the user's own status line and viola records no reading. The start is not refused.

- The override is written and passed whenever the start reaches the spawn, whether or not the user has a
  statusline command, so readings are recorded for a user with none.

- **Boundary matter, unsettled** (`inputs#I1`): the review card shows this as a widening. The plan does not
  treat the masters' sentences as his ratification.

- Source: the entry's title ("user output unchanged, readings to budget.json"); architecture §Hook contract
  (`architecture.md:324`), §Occupied Resources (`:359`, `:402`), `:173` (it emits no event).

- The entry and the masters state: it reads the statusline JSON on stdin, records the `rate_limits` reading to
  `budget.json`, runs the user's own command with the same stdin, prints that command's stdout unchanged (empty
  when the command fails) and exits 0. It never writes stderr.

- Verified (`security-plan.md:230`, `:556`; `test-plan.md:853`): stdin goes through `Read::take(MAX_FRAME + 1)`,
  and the command never runs from a home or instance directory that fails the strict-modes check.

- Verified (`src/cmd/hook.rs:72-87`; `crates/viola-state/src/snapshot.rs:104-117`): the command is read from the
  snapshot through `VIOLA_DIR`; with no snapshot, an unreadable one, a newer one or one without the field, the
  wrapper prints nothing and exits 0.

- [premise-corrected: research.md finding 10 — `HookEvent` is the closed set of nine hook events] `statusline`
  is not a hook event. The arm is dispatched beside the nine; `HookEvent` and the perf rows are unchanged.

- [premise-corrected: the security extract, first two constraints — the hook's dated gap is worded for the
  `endpoint` read and the `hook.event` frame] The arm borrows no dated gap. Before it reads the snapshot it
  canonicalises `VIOLA_DIR`, requires the result to end `<home>/instances/<name>`, and runs
  `viola_state::strict::check_instance` on that home and instance directory (security-plan §Input Validation,
  CLI arguments row). A failure runs nothing, prints nothing and exits 0 with the landed detail
  `strict-modes-failed`.

- [premise-corrected: research.md finding 11 — no master states a bound] The wait for the user's command has a
  bound, a named constant marked PROVISIONAL. At the bound the arm ends the command it started, prints nothing
  and exits 0 with the landed detail `deadline`. The number is on the review card.

- The user's command gets the stdin bytes the arm read, and the arm's own environment and working directory
  unchanged (what the CLI would have given the user's command itself; the documentation says the CLI sets
  `COLUMNS` and `LINES` there). Its stderr is discarded. No master states these four; the card lists them.

- The arm logs `hook-invoked`, the `statusline-shell` `process-start` / `process-exit` pair and `hook-decision`
  with `budget_written`, as obs-plan §4 Scenario: Budget governor names them; all are in the schema already.

- **Boundary matter, unsettled** (`inputs#I1`): the command is a user-written shell string and the masters run
  it through the shell Claude Code would use (`architecture.md:324`, `:469`; `security-plan.md:34`, `:596`), the
  only shell-out in viola. The review card shows this as a widening. On Unix the shell is `/bin/sh -c`, by its
  absolute path, a hypothesis until item 8's row is measured. The Windows half is item 9.

- Source: the entry's title ("readings to budget.json"); architecture §Occupied Resources (`architecture.md:402`)
  and §Standard Contracts (`:216`, `:183`).

- The masters state: `budget.json` with `budget.json.lock` holds the newest `rate_limits` reading across wrapped
  sessions, timestamped, last-writer-wins, written only by `hook statusline`: per window `{used_percentage,
  resets_at}`, either field `"unknown"` when unparseable, the whole window `"unknown"` when the statusline omits
  it, plus `read_at`.

- Verified (`architecture.md:96`): the statusline JSON is parsed tolerantly; an unparseable value is never an
  error.

- [premise-corrected: research.md finding 4 — the documentation gives `resets_at` as Unix epoch seconds] The
  reader takes `resets_at` as a number of epoch seconds or as an RFC 3339 string, and writes it as RFC 3339
  UTC; anything else is `"unknown"`. `used_percentage` is a number from 0 to 100; anything else is `"unknown"`.

- [premise-corrected: research.md finding 5 — most invocations carry no `rate_limits`] The file is written only
  when the payload holds a `rate_limits` object. Without one nothing is written, the last reading stands, and
  the decision line says `budget_written: false`.
- The file carries `v` (every viola format does) and is replaced through the one helper under its lock.

- This chunk writes the reading. It builds no reader: the gate, the `budget-gate` evaluation, `budget-paused`
  and `release --budget` are the next route entry's ("Budget governor").

- Source: the second CARRY (chunk 2026-09-24-fake-agent-and-test-data-fixtures deferred the fake agent's
  `statusline-echo` mode and its `settings.json` read to this entry; test-plan §7; "no shape before a recorded
  fixture").

- Re-verified at P1: no `statusline-echo` mode exists; `test-plan.md:838` describes it: the user statusline
  command becomes `viola-fake-agent statusline-echo`, which prints a fixed marker and appends to a marker file.

- [premise-corrected: the tests extract and its history — the one payload the fake agent sets without a
  recording stands on an explicit word, which does not cover statusline stdin] The fake agent invents no
  statusline payload. It runs the override's command only when a test hands it the stdin bytes in a file named
  by an argv option, and feeds those bytes unchanged. Synthetic statusline stdin is test input
  (`test-plan.md:97`, `:1060`), never a file under `fixtures/claude/<version>/`.

- Verified as the design (`src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs:421-428`): the fake agent reads the override file named
  by the `--settings` argument `run` passes, takes the statusline command there, and runs it directly, never
  through a shell, and only when its first word is an absolute path. It receipts the run.
- `statusline-echo` takes the marker file's path as an argument (the fake agent reads no environment).

- Source: the fourth CARRY (chunk 2026-09-27-hooks-to-normalised-events landed the hook stdin and
  `prompt-submitted` round-trip properties but not the statusline one).

- Re-verified at P1: `test-plan.md:1034` (§6 Property suite) says the hook stdin parser landed at `cases: 512`
  with `crates/viola-agent-claude/proptest-regressions/hook.txt` committed, and "statusline JSON with arbitrary
  `resets_at` joins with 'Statusline pass-through'".

- This chunk adds that property: `cases: 512`, committed seeds. The `hook_stdin` fuzz target also feeds the
  statusline reader, with two synthetic seeds (security-plan's parser-surface list names `hook statusline`
  inside the hook stdin parser).

body:

- **Marker:** 2026-10-10-viola-revive · **Version:** viola-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-10T12:58Z

`viola revive <name>` restarts a dead instance in the terminal it is typed in. It reads the instance's last
snapshot and its event log, picks the newest logged session id (or the one `--id` names), and runs the ordinary
`run` start order with the child `claude --resume <id>` spawned in the directory the dead wrapper recorded. It
replays no launch spec: the program is resolved again by name, the environment is the current terminal's, and
any other flag is typed after `--`. `--list` prints the logged session chain. Three preflight refusals are
built (`already-live`, `no-session`, `cwd-missing`), behind a strict-modes check on the files revive reads
(scope.md items 1 to 4; architecture §Established Decisions [Session Liveness]; security-plan §Authentication &
Authorization).

To carry this the chunk adds one optional snapshot field (`cwd`), a session-chain reader beside the landed log
replay (revive is the replay's first product reader), two argv options on the fake agent, and a test that kills
a wrapper it started and revives it (scope.md items 2, 3 and 5).

The plan covers the cut scope.md names. The `session-live` refusal is not built: everything it reads is pinned
on the route entry "The board: viola list" (research.md finding 6). Three live readings are one held step that
waits for the founder's number (step 12). Three P4 forks are closed by `inputs#I3`: no ledger row now, the fake
agent sets two payload fields under `--resume`, and the recorded cwd is ratified as the child's spawn directory.

- Add `cwd` to `InstanceSnapshot` as an optional string, omitted on write when absent and read as absent when
  missing, in the form the struct's other optional fields take (`snapshot.rs:40-57`). `SNAPSHOT_V` stays 1.

- Give every struct literal of `InstanceSnapshot` the field. The sites, re-derived by `grep -rn -l
  'InstanceSnapshot {' src crates tests`: `crates/viola-state/src/liveness.rs`, `replay.rs`, `snapshot.rs`,
  `crates/viola-state/tests/state_replay.rs`, `src/cmd/hook.rs`, `src/cmd/run.rs`, `src/run/dialog.rs`,
  `src/run/snapshot.rs`, `src/run/wheel.rs` (9 files).

- Add a public reader beside `replay` that makes one pass over `events.ndjson` through `events::read_from` and
  returns, in log order, one link per `session-start` line whose `data.agent_session_id` is a string: the line's
  `ts`, its `data.cause` (the string as logged, `unknown` when absent or not a string) and the id. It returns
  the pass's `Skipped` counts with the links. It writes nothing and logs nothing.

- In `crates/viola-state/tests/state_replay.rs` add two cases over a log the crate's own writer wrote: the
  chain of a two-session log, and a replay over an unreadable snapshot that yields no `cwd` and leaves
  `snapshot.json` untouched.

- Add a public check beside `check_stamps` that takes the home and the instance directory and runs `check_path`
  on the home, `<home>/instances`, the instance directory, its `snapshot.json` and its `events.ndjson`, each
  that exists, in that order (a folder before what it holds, as `check_stamps` does, `strict.rs:27-39`). A
  missing path is skipped; a path whose metadata cannot be read is `Refused::Unreadable`.

- Unit cases named with the token `strict_instance`: an owner-only tree passes; on Unix an instance directory
  with a group-write bit is `Refused::Writable`, and so is a `snapshot.json` with one (two `cfg(unix)` cases,
  each body a minimal reader over the shared decision); a tree with no instance directory passes.

- The rule this step builds, quoted: "**Strict-modes check:** in every process that reads `snapshot.json`,
  `ledger/stamps.json` or `statusline_command`" (`.andromeda/security-plan.md:211`). None of the seven dated
  gaps of that row names revive (the security extract, Constraints, first item).

- Not read at P3: the Windows reader's verdict on a tree viola itself created on a CI runner. If the check
  refuses a home and instance that `viola run` just made, on any OS, stop and report it as a finding about the
  creating side or the check; do not skip a path, loosen the rule or gate the check to one OS.

- Add, beside `PLUGIN_DIR_FLAG`: the program name `claude`, the flags `--resume` and `--fork-session`, a
  function that says whether a string is a session id (36 characters, hyphens at offsets 8, 13, 18 and 23, an
  ASCII hex digit of either case everywhere else), and a function that builds the resume arguments from an id
  and the fork choice: `--resume`, the id, then `--fork-session` when forking.

- Unit tables with literal oracles, named with the tokens `session_id_shape` and `resume_args`: the committed
  fixtures' id form passes; `s-1`, an empty string, a 35 and a 37 character string, a non-hex letter, a
  misplaced hyphen, a leading or trailing space and an id holding a control character each fail; the arguments

title: Step 6 — `start` takes its launch from its caller (`src/cmd/run.rs`)

data.head: ### Step 6 — `start` takes its launch from its caller (`src/cmd/run.rs`)

body:
- `start` reads the program, the child's arguments and the current directory from `RunArgs` and
  `std::env::current_dir()` today (`run.rs:178-182`). Change it to take them from its caller as one value
  holding four things: the instance name, the program word, the child's arguments, and the child's spawn
  directory. `run` builds that value from its arguments and the current directory, so a `viola run` does what
  it does today.

- The spawn directory is used for `SpawnSpec.cwd` alone. Program resolution and the version gate keep reading
  the starting process's own current directory, as they do today (`run.rs:183`, `:208`). Callers of `start`
  from the code-graph: `run @ src/cmd/run.rs:148` and the span-order test `@ src/cmd/run.rs:937`; both move to
  the new signature.

- `start_state` (`run.rs:406-443`) writes the spawn directory into the first snapshot's `cwd` when it is valid
  UTF-8, and writes no `cwd` otherwise. Nothing else of the first snapshot or of the two start events changes:
  the wheel record stays `wheel{holder:"driver", cause:"start"}` (`run.rs:435`).

- Make `start`, `Started`, `collision_check`, `refused` and `pump_child` reachable from `src/cmd/revive.rs`
  (the `pub(super)` form `refuse_tampered_pin` has, `run.rs:552`).

- A unit case named with the token `snapshot_cwd` beside `run.rs`'s tests: the first snapshot of a start holds
  the spawn directory.

- Arguments: `<name>` through the shared name parser (`run.rs:44-46`); `--id <ID>`, refused by clap as a usage
  error (exit 2) unless step 4's function accepts it; `--fork`; `--list`, which conflicts with `--id`, `--fork`
  and the trailing arguments; and the child's extra arguments after `--`, optional.

- The start arm logs as process `run`: it initialises the log as `run` does (`run.rs:138-143`) and its
  `DetailSink` is `ObsProcess::Run`. `role_of` (`src/main.rs:90-106`) names `revive` beside `run`, with new
  rows in its case table. `--list` initialises no process log.

- The order is decided by one plain function over the four readings, tested by a table named with the token
  `preflight_order`: each refusal alone, each pair in which the earlier one wins, and the pass.

- The stderr pairs, proposed wording (the hint words are the founder's by precedent; the review card shows
  them, and a reworded line changes only these literals and their tests):
  - `strict-modes-failed`: `unable: <name>'s state files can be written by another user` / `hint: viola will
    not read them; make the viola home and its files owner-only`
  - `no-session`, no link: `unable: <name> has no logged session to resume` / `hint: start one: viola run
    <name> -- claude`
  - `no-session`, an `--id` the log does not hold: `unable: <name> has no logged session with that id` /
    `hint: viola revive <name> --list`
  - `cwd-missing`: `unable: <name>'s recorded directory is missing` / `hint: resume it by hand from a directory
    you choose: viola run <name> -- claude --resume <id>, ids from viola revive <name> --list`
  No line holds the recorded directory, a pid, or an id read from the log.

- A passed preflight builds the launch of step 6: program `claude`, arguments step 4's resume arguments then
  the human's, spawn directory the recorded one. It calls `start` and then `pump_child`, as `run` does. The
  start arm calls no `human::` writer after the preflight.

- `--list`: step 3's check, then the chain. Each link whose id passes step 4's check prints one stdout line
  through `human::result`: `<ts>  <cause>  <id>`, two spaces between fields, in log order, the `ts` through
  `human::escape_message`, the cause printed as logged when it is one of `startup`, `clear`, `resume`,
  `compact`, and as `unknown` otherwise. No header, no colour. No such link is the `no-session` pair and exit
  1; a failed check is the `strict-modes-failed` pair and exit 1.
- `src/cmd/mod.rs`: the `Revive` arm with a one-line help text, and its dispatch.
- `src/human.rs` is not edited: `refuse` and `result` carry every line.
- `OuterPty` gains a kill of the child it spawned, through the PTY seam's own kill.

- `home.rs` gains, beside `Wrapper::boot`: a way to put a copy of the fake agent named `claude` (`claude.exe`
  on Windows) into a directory inside the test's own home scratch and to start `viola revive` under an
  `OuterPty` with that directory first on the child's `PATH` (`Command::env` per child, never `set_var`), from
  a given current directory, with the fake agent's own flags after `--` (`--control` on a fresh control file,
  `--receipt`, `--fixtures`, `--cli-version`, `--screens`, `--trusted-root`); a `Wrapper::kill` that kills the
  wrapper this test booted, waits for its exit, then waits for the recorded child to be gone by pid and start
  time and for the endpoint to be unconnectable (`wait_endpoint_gone`); and a boot that starts the first
  wrapper in a given directory (`OuterPty::spawn_in`).
- Every new wait is `Instant::now() + WITHIN` with an exit check, as `wait_ready` is (`home.rs:438-463`).

title: Step 10 — the refusal and list cases (`tests/cli_revive.rs`)

data.head: ### Step 10 — the refusal and list cases (`tests/cli_revive.rs`)

body: Each case owns a stamped home and the fake agent as `claude` on its own `PATH`. Oracles are literals.

- `revive_on_a_live_name_prints_the_run_collision_pair`: over a booted wrapper, exit 1, stderr is the landed
  pair ending `hint: viola list`, stdout empty.

- `revive_of_a_name_never_started_is_no_session`, `revive_with_an_id_the_log_does_not_hold_is_no_session`,
  `revive_with_a_malformed_id_is_a_usage_error` (exit 2).

- `revive_whose_recorded_directory_is_gone_is_cwd_missing`: the first wrapper is booted in a directory the
  test made, whose name holds the tests' canary word, then stopped; the directory is removed; revive exits 1
  with the `cwd-missing` pair, and neither stdout nor stderr holds the directory's name.

- `revive_of_a_snapshot_with_no_cwd_is_cwd_missing`: the stopped wrapper's `snapshot.json` is cut short (the
  chaos tests' sanctioned alteration of a file the product wrote); revive exits 1 with the `cwd-missing` pair,
  and `run-<name>.ndjson` gains exactly one `state-recovered` line with detail `snapshot-replayed`, held to
  `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` inside the case.

- `revive_refuses_state_another_user_could_write` (`cfg(unix)`): the stopped instance's directory gets a
  group-write bit; revive exits 1 with the `strict-modes-failed` pair and starts no child.

- Every refusal case also reads `run-<name>.ndjson`: exactly one new `process-exit` with `subject` `self`,
  `exit_code` 1 and the case's detail, and no `process-start` with `subject` `claude-child` after it.

- `revive_list_prints_the_logged_chain`: over a stopped wrapper, exit 0, one stdout line whose three fields
  are a timestamp, `startup` and the fixture's session id, stderr empty, no ESC byte in either stream.

- `revive_with_fork_reports_the_fork_session`: over a stopped wrapper, `viola revive <name> --fork`; the new
  `session-start` past the pre-revive offset has cause `resume` and the fake agent's compiled fork id.
`revive_after_a_killed_wrapper_resumes_the_logged_session_in_the_recorded_directory`:

- Boot a wrapper in directory A (step 9). Wait for the first life's `session-start` and for the fake agent's
  `hook` receipt line of that SessionStart, so no hook is running. Read the session id from the log.

- Kill the wrapper (step 9's `Wrapper::kill`: its own child, then gone by pid and start time, then the
  endpoint). Take the log's length and a hash of its bytes.

- Run `viola revive <name>` from directory B, a different directory the test made. Wait for its readiness:
  the two new `process-start` lines, the new receipt `start`, the snapshot and a fresh heartbeat.

- Assert, past the taken offset: the first record is `wheel{holder:"driver", cause:"start"}`; exactly one
  `session-start` whose `data.cause` is `resume` and whose `data.agent_session_id` equals the first life's id.
  Assert the bytes before the offset hash as before; the new receipt's `cwd` line is A and not B; the new
  snapshot's `cwd` is A; `viola revive <name> --list` prints two lines, `startup` then `resume`, with one id;
  the outer terminal's bytes of the second life hold neither `unable` nor `hint:`.
- Stop the second life through the drop guard. Both lives sit behind drop guards.

- The mechanism the central assertion rests on, as the equality it needs: the fake agent started with
  `--resume X` reports `session_id` X (step 5), and viola passes `--resume` with the id the first life logged
  (step 7), so the logged id of the second life equals the first's exactly when viola read the id from the log
  and put it into the child's argv. The first life's id is the fixture's; the second life's would be the same
  fixture id even with no `--resume` at all, so the case's discriminating half is `cause` `resume`, which the
  fake agent reports only under `--resume`, and step 10's fork case, where the id differs from every fixture.

- A reading this case makes for the first time: on Linux and macOS, that the wrapper's child is gone after the
  wrapper is killed (research.md finding 8). If the child is still alive at the bound on either, stop and
  report it; do not lengthen the wait, add a kill of the child, or gate the case to Windows.

- The kill and coverage (the operator's word at the P5 review, `inputs#I4`): if killing the instrumented
  wrapper breaks the coverage merge in `bash scripts/agent-run.sh pre-push`, stop and report it. Do not exclude
  the case from coverage: no ignore-regex change, no `cfg` or skip of the case under the coverage run, no
  uninstrumented stand-in for the wrapper.

- One-shot control at implement, both readings in `evidence/red-green.md`: neutralise step 7's resume
  arguments (the launch built without them), show this case red on `cause`, restore, show it green. A second
  one-shot for step 3's guard: skip the check, show `revive_refuses_state_another_user_could_write` red,
  restore.

body:
- (arch) The verb is a module under `src/cmd/`; the `--resume` and `--fork-session` literals, the program name
  and the session-id shape are defined in `viola-agent-claude` and nowhere else in product code; no crate gains
  a dependency: the preservation guard entry exits 0 over `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock` (per architecture
  §Infrastructure Patterns → Project directory structure; §Infrastructure Patterns → Crate dependency direction)

- (arch) A snapshot written with `cwd` carries `v` 1; a snapshot without the key reads as having none; the
  replay arm yields no `cwd` and writes no file. Proven by the `snapshot_cwd` cases of the unit filter entry
  and by `binary(state_replay)` in the integration filter entry (per architecture §Conventions → Protocol
  versioning; §Standard Contracts → Snapshot envelope)

- (arch) After a kill and a revive the instance's `events.ndjson` is longer, every byte before the revive is
  unchanged, and the new `session-start` line reads `cause` `resume` with the first life's `agent_session_id`.
  Proven by `binary(chaos_revive)` (per architecture §Established Decisions [Session Liveness]; §Conventions →
  Naming patterns, Hook → kind map)

- (arch) A `viola run` start is unchanged in what it writes but for the snapshot's `cwd`: the first record of
  every start, a revived one included, is `wheel{holder:"driver", cause:"start"}`, and `viola-core` is
  untouched (the preservation guard entry exits 0). Proven by `binary(chaos_revive)` and by the smoke's `boot`
  entry (per architecture §Established Decisions [Human Takeover / Wheel])

- (security) A revive against an instance directory or a `snapshot.json` another user could write starts no
  child and uses no snapshot value: exit 1, detail `strict-modes-failed`. Proven by the `strict_instance` cases
  and by `revive_refuses_state_another_user_could_write` in `binary(cli_revive)`, with its one-shot
  remove-the-guard reading in `evidence/red-green.md` (per security-plan §Authentication & Authorization,
  `~/.viola/` access control row)

- (security) An `--id` that is not the closed id shape is a usage error (exit 2), and one the instance's own
  log does not hold is refused `no-session` before any spawn; the accepted id reaches the child as one argv
  element of a direct spawn. Proven by the `session_id_shape`, `resume_args` and `preflight_order` cases and
  by `binary(cli_revive)` (per security-plan §Input Validation, Boundary paragraph; §Security Anti-Patterns →
  Code Patterns)

- (security) No refusal line, hint or `--list` row holds the recorded directory or a pid: the `cwd-missing`
  case reads no occurrence of its canary directory name in stdout or stderr (per security-plan §Error
  Handling, External responses; §Bootstrap phases, `logging-redaction-wire`)

- (security) After a revive `snapshot.json` is written by the revived wrapper alone, and the chain read and
  the replay write no file: `binary(state_replay)` holds the replay's untouched-snapshot case, and
  `binary(chaos_revive)` the unchanged log prefix (per security-plan §Input Validation, Own state files on
  read row)

- (obs) Each preflight refusal leaves exactly one `process-exit` line with `subject` `self`, `exit_code` 1 and
  its closed detail (`strict-modes-failed`, `already-live`, `no-session`, `cwd-missing`) in
  `run-<name>.ndjson`, and no `process-start` with `subject` `claude-child` after it. Proven by
  `binary(cli_revive)` (per obs-plan §6 `detail` code catalog; §7 Error classes captured)

- (obs) A revive over a snapshot cut short writes exactly one `state-recovered` line with detail
  `snapshot-replayed` in its role file, valid against `schemas/diag-line.v1.json`. Proven by
  `revive_of_a_snapshot_with_no_cwd_is_cwd_missing` in `binary(cli_revive)` (per obs-plan §4 Edge flows, E5)

- (obs) `bash scripts/g2-zero-panics.sh` and `bash scripts/agent-run.sh schema-check` exit 0 over the homes
  this chunk's tests leave, the killed wrapper's among them (per obs-plan §9 Gate commands, G2 and G4)

- (layouts) `viola revive <name>` on a live name prints the `viola run` collision pair on stderr with
  `hint: viola list` last, exits 1 and prints nothing on stdout (per layout-templates §Surface: cli · Output
  structure — `viola run`)

- (layouts) `no-session` (both forms), `cwd-missing` and `strict-modes-failed` each print one `unable:` line
  and one `hint:` line as the last stderr line, each hint distinct, none naming `viola release` (per
  layout-templates §Surface: cli · Component — Primary content block 2, Hint line)

- (design) `viola revive <name> --list` writes one static line per logged session to stdout, in log order,
  ASCII only, two spaces between fields, with no ESC byte and nothing on stderr; every revive refusal carries
  no ESC byte (per design-system §Surface: cli → Tokens (platform-specific) → Colour decision order; §Surface:
  cli → Tokens (platform-specific) → Width)

- (a11y) A revive that passes its preflight writes no line of its own while the child holds the terminal: the
  outer terminal's bytes of the second life in `binary(chaos_revive)` hold neither `unable` nor `hint:`, and
  the pump is `run`'s own, unchanged. A separate outer-PTY leg for the revived start is not built here (per
  a11y-plan §1 A11y Scope Summary, CLI and terminal entities → `viola run` TUI passthrough)

- (a11y) Each revive refusal ends stderr with one `hint:` line and exits with a typed code inside the closed
  list (1, or 2 for the usage error) (per a11y-plan §8 Cognitive Accessibility, Error recovery → CLI)

- (tests) The kill-and-revive case kills only the wrapper it started, waits for gone-by-pid-and-start-time and
  an unconnectable endpoint, reads past the pre-revive offset, and uses no sleep and no retry; the receipt's
  `cwd` line of the second life equals the first wrapper's directory and differs from the directory revive was
  typed in (per test-plan §6 Chaos suite; §2 Agent-runnable invariants; `inputs#I2`)

- (tests) Without `--resume` the fake agent's payloads are the recorded bytes: `contract_fake_agent_drift`
  stays green inside `bash scripts/agent-run.sh pre-push`, and the `fixtures` path of the preservation guard
  is unmoved (per test-plan §7 Fake agent)

  id it read (per test-plan §3 `run`; §10 Coverage thresholds; §9 Matrix builds)

1. **The id chain does not exist.** `replay` keeps one id (`crates/viola-state/src/replay.rs:63-67`). `--id`'s
   membership check and `--list` need every `session-start` line that carries an id, with its `ts` and `cause`.
   The chunk adds that reader beside `replay`, over the same `read_from` and its three counts.

2. **No recorded resume payload exists.** The committed SessionStart files carry `source` `startup` three times
   and `clear` once (derivation: `grep -o '"source":"[a-z]*"' fixtures/claude/*/SessionStart*.json`), and every
   `session_id` in them is a UUID (a regex check over the four files). The fake agent fires `SessionStart.default`
   at every launch, so a revived fake child reports `startup` with the fixture's fixed id. The E2E's
   `cause:"resume"` with the dead session's id needs either a recorded variant (a live start) or the fake agent
   setting `source` and `session_id` on the recorded default payload under `--resume`, which test-plan §7 does
   not allow as written. A fork for P4.

3. **The fake agent's id is never the dead session's own.** Every start of the fake agent reports the same
   fixture id, so "the same id" is only a real assertion when the E2E revives with `--id` set to an OLDER id of a
   two-entry chain, or when the fake agent echoes the id it was given. The first needs a chain of two (the
   recorded `clear-1` pair under `--framing` gives one: its SessionStart carries a second id).

4. **`/clear` rotates the id, as recorded.** In `fixtures/claude/2.1.287/` the `clear-1` SessionEnd and
   SessionStart carry different `session_id` values, and the default start's id differs from both (a comparison
   of the three files). That is the `/clear` half of the study's P6, recorded by `viola verify` on 2.1.287 and
   read live on 2026-10-08 (architecture's amendment history). The `/compact` half has no reading.

5. **`run`'s start runs no strict-modes check on the home or the snapshot.** The only strict read on the start
   path is the stamps file (`src/run/version_gate.rs:136`); `collision_check` reads `snapshot.json` plainly
   (`src/cmd/run.rs:294`). `viola_state::strict::check_path` exists and is tested per OS. Security-plan requires
   the check at every entry point that reads `snapshot.json`, and none of the seven dated gaps names revive.

6. **Everything `session-live` reads is routed later.** No `claude agents` call exists in `src` or `crates`
   (the query and a search for `agents` outside the harness). The join-field ledger row, its `viola verify`
   probe, the fake agent's stub and the parser's property and fuzz targets are pinned by three CARRYs on the route
   entry "The board: viola list". Security-plan's accepted PATH risk for that call names `list`, `mcp` and `ui`
   only.

7. **The ledger limit does not reach revive.** Architecture's capability-ledger pattern (`:462`) holds one ruled
   limit, the founder's: "a CLI shape no `send` relies on needs no probe", stated for the long-paste frame. The
   amendment history reads it as scoped to `send`. `--resume <id>` reopening the same session with a SessionStart
   of source `resume` is relied on by revive, has no row, and its only reading is the study's carried F5
   (2026-09-25, CLI 2.1.28x). A row needs a `viola verify` probe: a fifth interactive child (the founder's
   ruling), a re-stamp, and every stamped home reads unverified until then. A fork for P4.

8. **The child's death with its wrapper is pinned on Windows only.** `run_child_ends_when_its_wrapper_is_terminated`
   is `#[cfg(windows)]`; the P5 evidence is a Windows reading of 2026-10-03. On Linux and macOS no test and no
   record shows a wrapper's child ending when the wrapper is killed. The kill-and-revive E2E is the first reading
   there, with the fake agent, which exits at stdin EOF.

9. **A kill is set against coverage.** An instrumented child killed during its exit-time profile write leaves a
   short profile (3 of 4 800 loaded runs, test-plan's history), and the last chunk's chaos case chose a stop over
   a kill for that reason. A wrapper killed while it runs writes no profile; the risk is a hook or the fake agent
   in its own exit at the kill. The E2E kills only after the start's hook has ended and the fake agent is idle.

10. **Revive's program is a name, not an argument.** The study's form is `viola revive <name> [-- extra claude
    args]`; the program is resolved by name at revive time. Root tests today pass the fake agent's path as the
    program word, so a revive test needs a `claude` on a test-scoped `PATH` (the harness's own pattern,
    `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/boot.rs:125`). With no launch replay the fake agent's own flags
    (`--control`, `--receipt`, `--fixtures`, `--screens`, `--trusted-root`) reach the revived child only after
    `--`.

11. **The role.** `role_of` would file `revive` under `cli`; the verb becomes the wrapper. The process enum is
    closed at five values. A revive that logs as `run` (`run-<name>.ndjson`, the wrapper's panic rules) needs
    `role_of` to name it beside `run`; `--list` is a short read.

12. **Exit 1 has no `--json` document** (design-system's cli component 2, pending an architecture amendment), and
    `run` takes no `--json`. The route entry "CLI machine contract" owns the machine forms.

title: 2. The recorded cwd: a new snapshot field

data.head: ### 2. The recorded cwd: a new snapshot field

body:
- Source: the first CARRY ("the child cwd the snapshot's recorded `cwd` (study §6 puts that field in this
  scope)").

- Re-verified at P1 and P3: `InstanceSnapshot` (`crates/viola-state/src/snapshot.rs:39-57`) holds `endpoint`,
  `pid`, `started_at`, `pinned_bin`, `cli_verified`, `cli_version`, `wheel`, `budget_paused`, `links`,
  `child_pid`, `pending_dialog`. It holds no `cwd` and no `agent_session_id`.

- Verified (study §2; `src/cmd/run.rs:406-443`): the wrapper writes `cwd` in its first snapshot, from the
  directory its child is spawned in. No event carries it, so the replay cannot rebuild it. It is shown on no
  external surface (no `list`, no `/api/sessions`, no error body, no process-log line) and is used only as the
  child's spawn cwd, never joined with anything.

- Verified (architecture §Conventions, Protocol versioning and Data model conventions; the arch extract): the
  field is optional and additive, omitted on write when absent, and the snapshot's `v` stays 1.

- [premise-corrected: research.md findings 1 and 5 — the entry names no outcome; the nearest closed code is
  `cwd-missing`] A revive with no recorded cwd to use is refused `cwd-missing`, the same as a recorded
  directory that is gone. That covers a snapshot written by a binary older than this chunk, an unreadable or
  newer snapshot (the replay arm yields no `cwd`), and a `cwd` that is not valid UTF-8 and so was never written.

- A widening the wrap amends: security-plan §Input Validation (Child executable resolution row) says the
  child's cwd is the spawner's current directory. The founder ratified the recorded cwd as the child's spawn
  directory live on 2026-10-10, shown to him as a widening (`inputs#I3`, the overseer as relay), with the
  strict-modes check run before the value is used (item 4).

title: 3. The id read: the first reader of the log replay

data.head: ### 3. The id read: the first reader of the log replay

body:
- Source: the third CARRY (chunk 2026-10-10-self-healing-state, citing that chunk's own fourth input
  snapshot): the replay landed as library code with no caller, and this entry is its first reader.

- Re-verified at P1 and P3: `viola_state::snapshot::read_snapshot_classified`
  (`crates/viola-state/src/snapshot.rs:123`) and `viola_state::replay::read_snapshot_or_replay`
  (`crates/viola-state/src/replay.rs:84`) exist, and neither has a caller outside `viola-state` (the code-graph
  query, 65 rows). `read_snapshot` has four product callers (`src/cmd/client.rs:96`, `src/cmd/run.rs:294`,
  `src/cmd/hook.rs:254`, `:469`), as the CARRY says.

- [premise-corrected: research.md finding 1 — `replay` keeps one id and the snapshot arm returns none] The
  CARRY's claim holds as far as it goes: `replay` returns the last `agent_session_id` a `session-start` line
  carried (`replay.rs:63-67`), and `read_snapshot_or_replay` writes one `state-recovered` line on its replay arm
  (`:96-102`). But the snapshot holds no id, so the id comes from the log on every arm, and nothing returns the
  chain. This chunk adds the chain reader beside `replay`, over the same `read_from` and its three counts, and
  revive calls `read_snapshot_or_replay` for the snapshot's side (the `cwd`, and the `state-recovered` line when
  the snapshot is unreadable or newer).

- The four product callers' behaviour on an unreadable or newer snapshot is not this entry's: it is owed to the
  entries the last wrap's CARRYs name ("The board: viola list", "Server verification before any frame").

body:

  "each with an exit code and hint that join Epoch 6's exit-cause catalogue" (the route entry "Exit-cause code

title: The sixteen survivors, site by site

data.head: ## The sixteen survivors, site by site

body: The fifteen of the CARRY, and one more the first dispatch recorded. Each row states what a test must distinguish.

- `strict.rs:30:5` (`check_stamps → Ok(())`) and `:34:23` (the `NotFound` guard → `true`): the shared test
  `check_stamps_of_a_path_that_cannot_be_statted_is_unreadable` (added after the audit) expects
  `Err(Refused::Unreadable)` for a path holding a NUL. Under either mutant the call returns `Ok(())`, so the test
  fails on any host where the stat of that path fails with a kind other than `NotFound`. On Linux both grade
  caught (the cleanup chunk's record). On Windows std refuses a NUL in a path before any system call, with
  `InvalidInput`; that reading is from std's documented behaviour, not from a Windows run.

- `strict.rs:43:5` (`check_path → Ok(())`) and `:163:9` (`win::check → Ok(())`): no Windows test refuses a real
  path. The verified half of the audit's claim. A killing test needs a real folder or file whose DACL grants a
  write right to a foreign SID, checked through `check_stamps` or `check_path`.

- `strict.rs:170:9` (`win::persistent_acls → Some(true)`): on an NTFS path the function returns `Some(true)`, so
  only an input for which it returns `None` separates them: a path whose volume cannot be read. The pure verdict
  for a volume without persistent ACLs is already tested on every OS (`windows_verdict(.., false)`).

- `strict.rs:192:37` (`&` → `|`, `&` → `^`): `flags & PERSISTENT_ACLS != 0`. A hosted runner has no volume with
  the bit clear, so the reader cannot separate them. The decision as a plain function of `flags` can, on every OS
  (the scratch probe's five mutants).

- `strict.rs:207:44` and `fs.rs:161:47` (`|` → `^` between two distinct flag constants): bit-identical values,
  so no test can fail. `testing.md` 2026-09-27 names the remedy: the combined value as one literal, pinned by a
  test against the named flags, as `WRITE_RIGHTS` already is (`strict.rs:69`, pinned at `:314`).

- `fs.rs:186:13` and `:187:13` (`||` → `&&` in `win::dacl_of`): the guard is `call == 0 || present == 0 ||
  dacl.is_null()`. A descriptor with a NULL DACL (`present` set, the pointer null) separates the second mutant.
  The first, `(call == 0 && present == 0) || dacl.is_null()`, differs from the original only where `present` is 0
  and the pointer is not null, which the API never returns for a pointer initialised null: `present == 0`
  repeats what `dacl.is_null()` already reads (`testing.md` 2026-09-24, extended 2026-09-27).

- `fs.rs:18:5` (`restrict → Ok(())`): on a non-Unix build the function's body is `let _ = (path, mode); Ok(())`,
  so the mutant is the function. No test can fail and the run's verdict has no arm for an argued mutant.

- `lib.rs:434:9` (`is_console → true`, `→ false`) and `:436:76` (`!=` → `==`): `host_stdin` (`:355–360`) takes
  viola's `ReadConsoleW` reader on a console stdin and `std::io::stdin()` otherwise. The rig's two `reads` cases
  run with a console stdin and pass under `→ false`, because the bytes they send read the same through either
  reader. What differs: std's console reader ends a read at Ctrl-Z and viola's keeps it
  (`console_input_keeps_every_ctrl_z`, on a scripted source), and `ReadConsoleW` fails on a handle that is not a
  console.

- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/cleanup.rs:106:35` (`+` → `-` on the kill deadline): **graded MISSED on Windows**
  at run 37174673472 (`windows-dispatch.md`, "A shared-body Windows survivor"). Its killing test
  `cleanup_waits_its_deadline_for_a_target_that_outlives_its_kill` is `cfg(target_os = "linux")`: it uses PID 1,
  which a kill cannot end. Read again at P5 on the operator's direction (`inputs#I3`: no test sends a kill at a
  process it does not own):
  - a process the test starts cannot stand in. `ProcessId::of` (`harness/mod.rs:185–195`) returns `None` for a
    zombie, so a killed Unix child reads gone at once; and nothing in user mode holds a terminated Windows
    process in the process table for a time the test controls. A case that only samples the moment between the
    kill and the first poll is a race (`testing.md` 2026-09-27);
  - the expression can be restated so a test on every OS reads it. Measured on cargo-mutants 27.1.0
    (`.andromeda/runs/2026-10-10T02-04-59-phase/list-probe-deadline.rs.txt`, `cargo mutants --list`): the
    deadline as a plain function of an instant gets `+` → `-`, `+` → `*` and a `Default::default()` body. The
    first stays killable by a case asserting the returned instant lies five seconds after the given one; the
    other two do not compile for `Instant`. The remedy is `testing.md` 2026-09-24's (a decision in a plain
    function tested on every OS); that rule's letter names an OS-gated function, and here the OS-gated thing is
    the only killing test.
- **Decisions as plain functions, readers per OS** (`strict.rs:1–5`, `:55`, `:90`): the module's own stated shape.
- **A combined flag as one pinned literal** (`strict.rs:69`, its pin at `:314–329`).

- **A Windows test home under the workspace's `target/e2e-home`** (`strict.rs:377–397`, `fs.rs:485–519`): never
  `%TEMP%`, so the protected DACL is set at creation and the CI scans cover it.

- **The DACL read back, not the SDDL written** (`fs.rs:499–512`): the assertion is over `strict::win::allows`'
  SIDs, masks and flags.
- **A host-keyed arm as a compile-time const** (`scratch.rs:11`, `fs.rs:243`), each pinned by a test of the const.

- **The harness's tool calls go through the `Runner` seam** (`run.rs:34`,
  `dyn FnMut(&mut Command) -> (Option<i32>, String)`), so a test passes a stand-in and never nests a tool.

- **The retired cfg reader** (`cfg_legs.rs` at `d5deb01^`, 410 lines with its tests): syn 2.0.119 and proc-macro2
  1.0.107 with `span-locations`, a visitor collecting the `cfg` attributes covering a line, a three-valued `eval`
  where only a predicate proven false drops a leg. Both crates are still in `Cargo.lock` at those versions, as
  transitive dependencies.

- `testing.md` 2026-09-27: a crate's security property takes a test inside that crate; cargo-mutants runs only
  the mutated package's tests.

- `testing.md` 2026-09-24 (the awaited line; the mutant-reachable wait): a new test's wait detects the watched
  process's exit and stays under the kill line — 10 s for a root or crate test under the `mutants` profile, 30 s
  for `viola-e2e` (`.config/nextest.toml:39–55`).

- `testing.md` 2026-09-28: no body is reshaped to leave cargo-mutants' generated set. The three restatements
  above are of another kind: each removes an operand or a body no test can observe, by a rule the same file names.
- `testing.md` 2026-10-03: an item used only in `cfg(windows)` test code is imported inside that item.

- `testing.md` 2026-09-25: every new guard test carries its remove-the-guard run. For a Windows-gated test that
  run is the dispatch itself: the mutant is the guard neutralised and `caught` is the test red.

- `testing.md` 2026-10-04: no `[[gate]]` entry is a mutation run; a scoring or kill run is a one-off witness with
  its counts in `evidence/`.
- test-plan §4 (the `viola-e2e` exception): the harness's unit cases are a labelled case table in one `#[test]`.
- architecture, Occupied Resources: a harness document carries counts and repo-relative names only.
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run/mutants/host.rs` — the host exclusion and its case table
- `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-10-windows-mutation-grade/evidence/` — the survivor record, the host-excluded record, the Linux witness, the dispatch reading, the operator pass
- `crates/viola-state/src/strict.rs` — the Windows refusal cases, the unreadable-volume case, the bit decision as a plain function, the combined read flags as one pinned literal

- `crates/viola-state/src/fs.rs` — `restrict` as two cfg-gated functions, the combined set flags as one pinned literal, the DACL setter taking its SDDL, `dacl_of`'s repeated operand and its no-DACL case
- `crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs` — the rig's two new child cases
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/cleanup.rs` — the kill deadline as a plain function of an instant, and its case on every OS
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run/mutants.rs` — the exclusion applied before the counts are read, the document's new field
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run.rs` — the caller of `mutants_suite`, if its signature moves
- `crates/viola-e2e/Cargo.toml` — syn and proc-macro2, and the unused-dependency note for proc-macro2
- `Cargo.toml` — the two `[workspace.dependencies]` lines
- `Cargo.lock` — viola-e2e's two dependency lines
- `.github/workflows/windows-mutants.yml` — the `viola` item split in four, a label per item for the job name
- `tests/contract_windows_mutation_scope.rs` — the job names stay distinct

- none — the three plan-decision forks P3 raised were settled by the operator at P4 (`inputs#I2`): the `viola` job
  is split per file; `restrict` becomes two cfg-gated functions; the retired syn reader is revived. The retired
