- **Marker:** 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list · **Version:** viola-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-11T01:34:44Z

Build `viola list` for wrapped sessions: a read model over the home's `instances/`, the machine form
`viola list --json` (`items`, `budget`, `skipped`) and the uncoloured human board (the BAY line, the six
captions, one row per session). The verb reads the disk itself and contacts no wrapper (architecture §Standard
Contracts, Channel methods; GUI list envelope). It is the first surface that shows the reader's three skip
counts, and the second product reader of the snapshot's replay fallback.

This is a cut of the route entry, by the operator's direction (`inputs#I1`): the smallest slice that needs no
word of the founder. It reads no `claude agents --json`, so every row's STATUS is `unknown` and no unwrapped
row is printed; it prints no colour, so the masters' styled terminal form stays unmet; it shows no link. Every
part left out is on the review card with a price and a proposed owner.

A failed strict-modes check refuses the whole board with exit 21 (the operator's answer to the P4 fork,
`inputs#I2`, not a ruling of the founder).

1. **The budget read with its instant** — `crates/viola-state/src/budget.rs`. Give the one checked read a
   second public form that returns the reading together with the stored `read_at` as a
   `viola_core::Reading<String>` (`"unknown"` when the key is absent or no string). `read_budget` keeps its
   signature and its one product caller (`BudgetGate::decide_at` @ `src/run/budget.rs:268`) and becomes a call
   of the new form. The order of the read does not change: `check_path` on the home, on the file, the shared
   lock, the capped read, the tolerant parse, `v` = 1; every failure is no reading and no line. Unit cases
   `budget_stamped_*`: the instant `write_budget` wrote comes back; a file with no `read_at` reads
   `"unknown"`; an absent file is nothing and creates nothing.

2. **The read model** — new `crates/viola-state/src/board.rs`, declared in `crates/viola-state/src/lib.rs`.
   Sync, std only, no Claude shape, no anyhow. Two entry points, so the caller can open its log between them:
   - **the scan and the checks.** Given the absolute home: `check_path` on the home and on `instances/`, each
     that exists; then the entries of `instances/` read with `symlink_metadata`. A directory whose name passes
     `ViolaName::try_new` is an instance; a link is counted as ignored; any other entry is counted as
     malformed. No path is joined from a name that did not parse. Then `check_instance` for every instance, in
     name order. The result is the name-ordered instance list with the two counts, or a refusal that says
     which failed first: the home (the home or `instances/`) or one named instance. Nothing under the home is
     opened for reading or writing by this step.
   - **the read.** Given the scan's result and `now` (a `SystemTime` argument, never read inside): for each
     instance, `read_snapshot_or_replay`, then:
     - a snapshot that reads: `classify(beat_age(dir, now), same_process(&snapshot))`. `Gone` gives no item.
       Otherwise the item holds the name, `wrapped: true`, the liveness word, `status: "unknown"`, the
       snapshot's `wheel`, `budget_paused`, `dialog_pending` (whether `pending_dialog` is set), `cli_version`
       when recorded and `cli_verified`. The pending dialog's kind is kept beside the item for the human row
       and is not a document field.
     - a replay: a beat at most `STALE_AFTER` old gives an item with liveness `live`, `wheel` and
       `budget_paused` only where the log gave one, `dialog_pending: false` and no CLI field. An older or
       absent beat gives no item. It is never `stale`.
     - an absent snapshot gives no item.
     - the skip counts: for a replay, the replay's own `skipped`; otherwise one drained `read_from(dir, 0)`
       pass and its `skipped()`. The board's `skipped` is the field-wise sum over every scanned instance,
       items or not.
     - after the loop, one `parse-rejected` line per nonzero scan count through `obs_event!`: parser
       `state-entry`, detail `symlink-ignored` or `malformed`, with `count` (obs-plan §6, `detail` code
       catalog, Filesystem refusals). No entry name is logged.
   - The item and the counts derive `Serialize` with the contract's snake_case keys in the contract's order;
     an absent optional field is omitted. `endpoint`, `pinned_bin`, `cwd`, `statusline_command`, `pid`,
     `started_at` and `links` are on no type of this module.
   - Unit cases `board_scan_*` and `board_read_*`, each through the writers (`write_snapshot`,
     `touch_heartbeat`, `append_event`), a malformed file made only by altering the writer's bytes: an absent
     home passes with no instance; a widened home and a widened instance directory are refused, the instance
     by name, the first in name order (`cfg(unix)`); a link, a plain file and a name that is no `ViolaName`
     give no instance and the right count; this process's own pid and start time with a fresh beat is `live`;
     the same with `now` six seconds past the beat is `stale`; a wrong start time is omitted; a snapshot cut
     mid-object with a fresh beat is `live` with the logged `wheel` and `budget_paused`, and with an old beat
     is omitted; a `v` above this build's reads the same way; a pending dialog reads `dialog_pending: true`
     with its kind; `skipped` sums two instances' torn tails, one of them gone; the serialised item equals a
     literal, once with every optional field and once with none.

3. **The human text** — `src/human.rs`.
   - `escape_row`: every control character as `\xHH` text, LF and TAB included, DEL and C1 included, nothing
     stripped. It sits beside `escape_message` and does not replace it (its six callers are unchanged).
   - the board's writers, pure functions over the read model's result that take `&mut impl Write`:
     - the BAY line, cells two spaces apart, in the fixed order (layout-templates §Surface: cli / Component —
       Header / banner): `BAY`; `5H <n> %` with ` expired` after it when the window's `resets_at` is known and
       not later than `now`, or `5H unknown`; the same for `7D`; `read <n>m ago`, or `read unknown`;
       `gate open` or `budget-paused`; `skipped a - b - c`. With no reading the line is
       `BAY  5H unknown  7D unknown  read unknown  gate open  skipped 0 - 0 - 0` with the real counts
       (design-system §Color Palette, Domain status colors, `BudgetEnvelope::unknown`).
     - the caption row `NAME`, `LIVE`, `STATUS`, `WHEEL`, `DIALOG`, `CLI`, and one row per item in name order.
       Columns are padded to their widest word with a two-space gutter: LIVE 5, STATUS 7, WHEEL 22, DIALOG 17;
       NAME to the longer of its caption and the longest name on the board; CLI is last and unpadded. No line
       ends in a space.
     - the cells: LIVE `live` / `stale`; STATUS the item's word; WHEEL the holder, or `unknown` when the log
       gave none, followed by ` - budget-paused` when the item's `budget_paused` is true; DIALOG `none`, or
       `DIALOG` and the kind when it is one of `question`, `permission`, `plan`, else `DIALOG unknown`; CLI
       the version through `escape_row`, one space, `verified` or `unverified-cli`, or `unknown` when no
       version is recorded.
     - the empty board: the BAY line, the caption row, then
       `no wrapped sessions  start one: viola run <name> -- claude`.
   - the two refusal pairs through `human::refuse`. The instance pair's text moves from
     `src/cmd/revive.rs` `Refusal::pair` into one function here that `revive` and `list` both call, its words
     unchanged. The home pair is new code with the master's words: `the viola home is not private to you` /
     `the viola home must be readable only by you; viola does not change its permissions` (design-system
     §Surface: cli, Component Patterns 2).
   - Five forms here are worded by no master. They are planning forms, on the review card for the operator's
     confirm, and each is an expected amendment marked as a planning form:
     1. a window's figure prints as a whole number, rounded down (`89.6` prints `89 %`);
     2. the reading's age is whole minutes, rounded down, at every age (`read 0m ago`, `read 75m ago`); a
        `read_at` that does not parse, or lies ahead of `now`, prints `read unknown`;
     3. nonzero skip counts print as bare numbers in the document's key order (`skipped 2 - 0 - 1`);
     4. a `human` holder with a budget pause prints `human - budget-paused`;
     5. the empty board prints the BAY line and the caption row above its one line.
   - Unit cases `escape_row_*`, `bay_line_*` and `board_row_*` against literals: ESC, a C1 byte, DEL, LF and
     TAB each print as hex text and the row stays one line; each BAY form above; the default row; `stale`; the
     `human` holder; both paused composites; each dialog kind and the unknown one; `unverified-cli`; a missing
     version; a 32-character name printed whole with the other columns moved right; rows in name order
     whatever their state; the empty board; no byte outside printable ASCII and LF in any output.

4. **The verb** — new `src/cmd/list.rs`; the `List` variant and its dispatch arm in `src/cmd/mod.rs`
   (`--json` only, beside the global `--home`; the detail sink is the caller's `VIOLA_NAME` when it parses, as
   `verify`'s arm builds it). In order:
   1. the home made absolute (`std::path::absolute`, as `revive`);
   2. step 2's scan and checks. A refusal ends the run here with exit 21 and nothing opened: under `--json`
      one document on stdout, `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":null}`, and no stderr line;
      otherwise the pair for what failed, the hint last, and nothing on stdout. No log is opened and no line
      is written; the home's mode is left as found (`inputs#I2`);
   3. only now, and only when `client::own_name()` is set: `client::start(home, name)`, the `cli` log start
      the other verbs use. With no `VIOLA_NAME` no file is opened or created (obs-plan §3 Log file location);
   4. under one span `cli.list` (`#[instrument(skip_all, name = "cli.list", fields(json))]`): step 2's read
      with `SystemTime::now()`; step 1's stamped read; `budget::read_thresholds(home)`, each rejection logged
      as the wrapper logs it; `paused` as `budget::decide` reads the reading under those thresholds with no
      override at the same instant. `budget` is `{five_hour, seven_day, read_at, paused}`, or the word
      `"unknown"` when there is no reading;
   5. `--json`: one document `{"v":1,"ok":{"items":[…],"budget":…,"skipped":{…}}}` through
      `client::document`. Otherwise step 3's board on stdout as one write;
   6. `run::log_self_exit(0, None)`, exit 0.
   Unit cases `list_document_*`: the envelope equals a literal with a reading and without one; `paused` is
   true for a `five_hour` reading of 91 with a later reset under the default thresholds and false at 89; the
   arguments parse (`list`, `list --json`, a stray argument refused).

5. **The role table** — `src/main.rs`: one `#[case]` row, `list` and `--home <dir> list` read `Role::Cli`.
   `role_of` itself is not edited.

6. **Root cases of the verb** — new `tests/cli_list.rs`, from `stamped_home` and `tests/support/` only, every
   `viola list` run before the home drops, every wrapper stopped cleanly:
   - `path1_list_shows_a_booted_wrapper`: `list --json` exits 0 with exactly one stdout line; the item is the
     booted name, `wrapped:true`, `liveness:"live"`, `status:"unknown"`, `wheel:"driver"`,
     `budget_paused:false`, `dialog_pending:false`, `cli_version:"2.1.287"`, `cli_verified:true`;
     `budget` is `"unknown"`; the three counts are 0. `snapshot.json` and `events.ndjson` are byte-identical
     before and after, and the home holds no `budget.json` and no `budget.json.lock`.
   - `list_human_board_is_the_literal_rows`: the three stdout lines equal literals (the BAY line with no
     reading, the caption row, the row); stderr is empty; neither stream holds an ESC byte or a byte outside
     ASCII, for the human form and for `--json`.
   - `list_after_a_pause_reads_the_human_wheel`: after `viola pause`, the item reads `wheel:"human"` and the
     row's WHEEL cell `human`.
   - `list_of_a_stopped_wrapper_is_an_empty_board`: after a clean stop the item list is empty and the human
     form is the three empty-board lines, exit 0.
   - `list_of_a_home_that_does_not_exist_creates_nothing`: exit 0, the empty board, and the path still absent.
   - `list_logs_its_start_and_exit_only_under_a_name`: with `VIOLA_NAME` set, `cli-<name>.ndjson` gains one
     `process-start` and one `process-exit` with `exit_code` 0, `process` `cli`, each valid against
     `schemas/diag-line.v1.json`; with none, `diagnostics/` holds no `cli-*.ndjson`.
   - `e5_list_reads_a_live_wrapper_through_the_replay`: a booted, idle wrapper's `snapshot.json` cut
     mid-object; `list --json` under a `VIOLA_NAME` shows the item `live`, `wheel:"driver"`,
     `budget_paused:false`, `dialog_pending:false` and no `cli_version` or `cli_verified` key; the caller's
     role file gains exactly one `state-recovered` line with detail `snapshot-replayed`; the cut file's bytes
     are unchanged by the run. A sibling case sets the envelope's `v` to 99 and reads detail
     `snapshot-unsupported-v`.
   - `list_refuses_a_home_another_user_could_write` (`cfg(unix)`): the home at 0770, `VIOLA_NAME` set. Exit 21;
     stdout empty and stderr the home pair, hint last; under `--json` stdout the one exit-21 document and
     stderr empty; no file added under the home, and the home's mode still 0770.
   - `list_refuses_an_instance_another_user_could_write` (`cfg(unix)`): one instance directory at 0770. Exit
     21 and the instance pair naming it; nothing of any instance printed.
   Each new case carries its remove-the-guard reading in `evidence/red-green.md` (testing.md, 2026-09-25): for
   the two refusals the check neutralised and the case red; for the absence cases the behaviour forced on.

7. **The owed readings** — in the files that hold their neighbours:
   - `tests/chaos_torn_append.rs`: in the stopped-wrapper case, after the log is shortened and before the
     restart, `list --json` reads `.ok.skipped.torn_lines` 1 and an empty item list.
   - new `tests/chaos_forward_compat.rs`: a stopped wrapper's product-written log gains two complete lines,
     each appended by the case as one write (`OpenOptions::append`, as `tests/chaos_torn_append.rs` opens the
     log): one of a kind no build knows (not `link` or `unlink`) and one `wheel` line with an extra key.
     `list --json` exits 0 with `unknown_kinds` 1, `unknown_fields` 1 and `torn_lines` 0. That a known-kind
     line with an extra key is still returned stays held below the surface by
     `crates/viola-state/tests/state_events.rs`.
   - `tests/cli_budget.rs`, beside the `path6_` cases and gated as they are:
     `path6_list_shows_the_reading_and_the_pause`. After a `five_hour` reading of 91 and the refused send:
     `.ok.budget.paused` true, `.ok.budget.five_hour.used_percentage` 91, a string `read_at`, the item's
     `budget_paused` true, the row's WHEEL cell `driver - budget-paused` and the BAY line's gate cell
     `budget-paused`. After `release --budget`: the item's `budget_paused` false and `.ok.budget.paused`
     still true.

8. **The kill line** — `.config/nextest.toml`: `cli_list`, and `chaos_forward_compat` if its case starts from
   `stamped_home`, join the `[profile.ci]` 20 s filter line by its own rule (every verify-driven root binary).
   No kill line moves.

9. **The gates and the record** — run the `[[gate]]` block. Write `evidence/red-green.md` (step 6's readings)
   and `evidence/gates.md`. No `evidence/` file holds a home path.
- `crates/viola-state/src/board.rs` — the read model
- `src/cmd/list.rs` — the verb
- `tests/cli_list.rs` — the verb's root cases
- `tests/chaos_forward_compat.rs` — the forward-compat reading
- `crates/viola-state/src/lib.rs` — the module's declaration
- `crates/viola-state/src/budget.rs` — the stamped form of the one checked read
- `src/cmd/mod.rs` — the subcommand and its arm
- `src/cmd/revive.rs` — its state-files pair read from the shared text
- `src/human.rs` — the row-mode escaper, the board's writers, the two pairs
- `src/main.rs` — one `role_of` table row
- `src/run/budget.rs` — only if `decide` or `read_thresholds` is not reachable from the verb as it stands
- `tests/chaos_torn_append.rs` — the `skipped.torn_lines` reading
- `tests/cli_budget.rs` — Path 6's board readings
- `.config/nextest.toml` — the new binaries on the 20 s line

The gates are the standing lint and unit entries; one unit filter and one integration filter that select what
this chunk adds; a preservation guard; the harness smoke with G2 and G4 over its home; the native `pre-push`;
and the operator's hygiene, push and CI read (`leg = 'operator'`, the `ci.py conclusion` call, `inputs#I1`
item 5).

No mutation entry, no witness run and no workflow dispatch is listed (`inputs#I1` item 4). No entry is a live
leg: nothing starts the real `claude`. `run --e2e` is no gate here: its selector is unbuilt. Step 6's
remove-the-guard readings are implement's one-shot runs, recorded in `evidence/red-green.md`, never an entry.

The smoke boots an ordinary `viola run` session, which this chunk does not change; the harness `status`
document's `list` member stays `null` (it is on the review card). `schema-check` on the dev host reads the
booted smoke home and whatever kept homes stand, not the new cases' lines: the cases' own schema read and CI's
G4 step hold those. The preservation guard names its base commit, because the operator pass's pre-CI commit
moves HEAD onto the chunk. It shows that no Claude shape, ledger row, schema value, fixture, plugin file,
fake-agent option, harness file, workflow or dependency moved, and that the readers the board reuses, the
shared client and every landed client verb but `revive` are the shipped ones. It lists no file a step edits.

body:
This chunk claims no capability. `verification-matrix.json#v1-37` needs idle or busy status, the unwrapped
rows and the GUI envelope it must equal; `verification-matrix.json#v1-41` still waits on the five snapshot
readers that read an unreadable snapshot as absent. Both are advanced and not proven, and each takes a dated
ledger note at P5.

- (arch) In a home with no live wrapper `viola list --json` prints exactly one document on stdout, the success
  envelope holding `items`, `budget` and `skipped`, and exits 0; the verb connects to no endpoint
  (`list_of_a_stopped_wrapper_is_an_empty_board`; per architecture §Standard Contracts, Channel methods)

- (arch) A booted wrapper's item reads `wrapped:true`, `liveness:"live"`, `status:"unknown"` and its `wheel`,
  `budget_paused`, `dialog_pending`, `cli_version` and `cli_verified` as the snapshot holds them
  (`path1_list_shows_a_booted_wrapper`; per architecture §Standard Contracts, GUI list envelope)

- (arch) A gone instance is absent from `items`; an instance whose snapshot is unreadable or newer and whose
  beat is fresh is present, `live`, with `dialog_pending:false`, no CLI field, and `wheel` and `budget_paused`
  from the log; with an old beat it is absent, never `stale` (the `board_read_*` cases and
  `e5_list_reads_a_live_wrapper_through_the_replay`; per architecture §Standard Contracts, Snapshot envelope)

- (arch) After a `list` every instance's `snapshot.json` and `events.ndjson` are byte-identical, and a home
  without `budget.json` holds neither it nor its lock sibling (`path1_list_shows_a_booted_wrapper`; per
  architecture §Occupied Resources, Filesystem, the `budget.json` row)

- (security) With the home, or one instance directory, writable by another user, both forms exit 21 and print
  nothing built from any snapshot or log; the home's mode is left as found and no file is opened or added
  under it, with `VIOLA_NAME` set (the two `list_refuses_*` cases, `cfg(unix)`; per security-plan
  §Authentication & Authorization, row "`~/.viola/` access control"; the outcome is `inputs#I2`)

- (security) An `instances/` entry that is a link, is no directory, or whose name is no `ViolaName` gives no
  path join and no item (the `board_scan_*` cases; per security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Input)

- (security) A recorded version text holding ESC, a C1 byte, DEL, LF or TAB reaches the row only as `\xHH`
  text, and the row is one line (the `escape_row_*` and `board_row_*` cases; per security-plan §Bootstrap
  phases, `logging-redaction-wire`)

- (security) No type of the read model holds the snapshot's `endpoint`, `pinned_bin`, `cwd` or
  `statusline_command`, and the serialised item equals its literal (the `board_read_*` literal cases; per
  security-plan §Threat Model Summary, Data classification)

- (layouts) The human form's first line is the BAY line with its cells in the fixed order, two spaces apart;
  the second is the six captions in order; rows follow in name order whatever their state; every value
  starts in its caption's column (`list_human_board_is_the_literal_rows`, the `bay_line_*` and `board_row_*`
  cases; per layout-templates §Surface: cli / Component — Header / banner and Primary content block 1)

- (design) Each state prints as its domain word: `live` / `stale`, `unknown`, `driver` / `human`,
  ` - budget-paused` in WHEEL, `none` / `DIALOG <kind>`, `verified` / `unverified-cli`, `gate open` /
  `budget-paused`, ` expired` after a passed window (the `board_row_*` and `bay_line_*` cases; per
  design-system §Color Palette → Semantic Colors, Domain status colors)

- (a11y) Neither form writes an ESC byte or a byte outside ASCII to either stream, on a board with a session
  and on the empty board (`list_human_board_is_the_literal_rows`,
  `list_of_a_stopped_wrapper_is_an_empty_board`; per a11y-plan §4 ARIA Patterns & Roles, P6)

- (a11y) The caption row is pinned by a literal in a root case, the tree's form of a fixed-string pin
  (`list_human_board_is_the_literal_rows`; per a11y-plan §8 Consistency and predictability)

- (obs) With a valid `VIOLA_NAME` one run leaves one `process-start` and one `process-exit` with `exit_code` 0
  in `cli-<name>.ndjson`; with none it creates no `cli-*.ndjson`
  (`list_logs_its_start_and_exit_only_under_a_name`; per obs-plan §4 Instrumentation per surface)

- (obs) A run under a `VIOLA_NAME` over one unreadable snapshot leaves exactly one `state-recovered` line with
  detail `snapshot-replayed`, and one with `snapshot-unsupported-v` for a newer one
  (`e5_list_reads_a_live_wrapper_through_the_replay` and its sibling; per obs-plan §4 Edge flows, E5)

- (tests) `.ok.skipped.torn_lines` reads 1 after a stopped wrapper's log is shortened mid-line; one
  unknown-kind line and one known-kind line with an extra key read `unknown_kinds` 1 and `unknown_fields` 1
  at exit 0 (`tests/chaos_torn_append.rs`, `tests/chaos_forward_compat.rs`; per test-plan §6 Chaos suite)

- (tests) With a reading over the threshold `.ok.budget.paused` and the item's `budget_paused` read true, the
  row and the BAY line print the pause, and after `release --budget` the item reads false while
  `.ok.budget.paused` stays true (`path6_list_shows_the_reading_and_the_pause`; per test-plan §6 Path 6)

- (tests) `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --unit` and the two filter entries read `"ok":true`, and
  `bash scripts/agent-run.sh pre-push` reads `"ok":true` with its `linux-tests` stage (per test-plan §10
  Quality Gates & Coverage Targets)
- (tests) The preservation guard exits 0 against `995dc55a3d6b`

- (ci) The run `ci.py conclusion` reads for the operator pass's final HEAD is `verdict: green`; the report
  names its run id

- Spec anchors: architecture §Standard Contracts (Channel methods, GUI list envelope, Snapshot envelope,
  Session liveness, CLI `--json` output), §Occupied Resources (Filesystem), §Established Decisions [Budget
  Governor]; security-plan §Authentication & Authorization (row "`~/.viola/` access control"), §Input
  Validation (row "Own state files on read"), §Security Anti-Patterns; design-system §Color Palette (Domain
  status colors), §Surface: cli (Tokens, Component Patterns 1 and 2); layout-templates §Surface: cli (Output

- **check_instance** — 2 product callers, `src/cmd/revive.rs` `trusted` and `src/cmd/hook/statusline.rs` `trusted`. The board is the third.

- **escape_message** — 6 product callers in `src/human.rs` and `src/cmd/revive.rs`. Unchanged; the row mode is a second function beside it.
- **role_of** — `main` and one table test. No product edit.
- **Check before any open** (`src/cmd/revive.rs:102`): the instance check runs on the absolute home before the wrapper log opens, because the open narrows the home.
- **A `cli` verb's log start** (`src/cmd/client.rs:21`): `read_diagnostics_level`, `viola_obs_init(home, Cli, Some(name), level)`, `log_self_start`, then any config rejection.
- **One document, one write** (`src/cmd/client.rs:116`): `--json` output is `format!("{doc}\n")` in one `write_all`.
- **Static rows** (`src/cmd/revive.rs:226`): two-space-separated fields, one `human::result` per row, an escaped field where the text is not viola's own.
- **A reader's unit cases alter the writer's bytes** (`crates/viola-state/src/replay.rs:172`, `budget.rs:99`): write through the writer, then cut or re-version.
- **Human text only in `src/human.rs`**: writers take `&mut impl Write` and are unit-tested against literals (`src/human.rs:11`).
- **No environment seam**: a time-dependent decision takes its instant as an argument (`src/run/budget.rs` `decide`), so the board's read model takes `now`.
- **Root cases start from `stamped_home`** and use `tests/support/` helpers only; a new verify-driven binary is named on the `[profile.ci]` 20 s line.

- **Fixed human strings are pinned by literal asserts**: `trycmd`, `snapbox` and `assert_cmd` are in no manifest (`grep -E "trycmd|snapbox|assert_cmd|predicates" Cargo.toml crates/*/Cargo.toml`: 0 hits), and `tests/cli_verify.rs` is the precedent.

- **No on-disk source of idle or busy.** The snapshot has no such field and a running turn records nothing. The masters source `status` from `claude agents --json` and give `unknown` when that read is missing, failed or not joined, never an error. Every row of this slice reads `unknown`.

- **`skipped` needs a pass over every log.** The counts exist only as the result of a read. A snapshot that reads needs no log, so a board that passed only replayed logs would show a torn tail on a healthy instance as 0. The total is the sum of one whole-log pass per instance directory that passes its check, gone instances included (the torn-append case's wrapper is stopped, so its instance is gone and its log still counts). A replayed instance's pass is the replay's own.

- **`budget` needs two things the reader does not give.** `read_at` (dropped by `read_budget`) and `paused`, which is the gate's crossed rule over thresholds only the wrapper reads today. The equality the criterion needs: for a reading with `five_hour.used_percentage` 91 and a `resets_at` later than now, `decide` under the default thresholds reads paused with window `five-hour` (`src/run/budget.rs`, `gate_decide_five_hour_pauses_at_ninety_and_not_below`).

- **An unreadable or newer snapshot has no pid.** Its liveness rests on the heartbeat alone and is never `stale`: a beat at most 5 s old is `live`, anything else leaves the instance off the board. An absent snapshot gives nothing to show.
- **The heartbeat is outside `check_instance`'s five paths.** Its age is read from a file inside an instance directory the check has passed, which no other user can write into.
- **An absent home passes the check** ("each that exists") and is an empty board.
- **With `VIOLA_NAME` set, a `cli` verb's log start creates a missing home.** That is what `send`, `wait` and the others do today; `list` takes the same start, after its checks.

- **The home's refusal pair is worded and not built.** design-system gives `unable: the viola home is not private to you` with its hint as `run`'s strict-modes refusal; no source file holds the text (`grep -rn "not private to you" src`: 0 hits), because `run` makes no such check yet. `list` is its first writer. The instance pair is built, in `src/cmd/revive.rs` `Refusal::pair`.
- **The built `--help` is clap's ordered list**, not the grouped table the masters draw. Grouping is no part of this slice.

- **E5 on the board is drivable without a restart.** A booted wrapper's `snapshot.json` is cut mid-object while the wrapper idles (bytes the wrapper wrote); `list --json` then takes the replay for that live instance. `run`'s collision check still calls `read_snapshot`, so the scenario's step 3 stays as its As landed note words it.
- **The budget readings are Unix root cases.** `budget.json` is written only by `viola hook statusline`, which runs a command on Unix only.

title: The slice — what this chunk builds

data.head: ## The slice — what this chunk builds

body: `viola list` for wrapped sessions: the read model, the machine form and the uncoloured human rows.

- The verb `viola list` with the global `--home` and with `--json`. It is not a channel method: the calling
  process reads the home's `instances/*/` itself and needs no live wrapper (architecture, the channel methods'
  `list` line).

- The machine form `viola list --json`: one document `{"v":1,"ok":{"items":[…],"budget":…,"skipped":{…}}}` on
  stdout (layout-templates, Output structure — `viola list --json`).
  - each item is `{name, wrapped, liveness, status, wheel?, budget_paused?, dialog_pending, cli_version?,
    cli_verified?}` (architecture, GUI list envelope). Every item of this slice is a wrapped one.
  - `budget` is `{five_hour, seven_day, read_at, paused}` or `"unknown"`.
    [premise-corrected: `viola_state::budget::read_budget` returns the two windows only and drops `read_at`
    (`crates/viola-state/src/budget.rs`, `Stored`), and nothing on the `list` side reads the thresholds
    `paused` is measured against] The slice gives the one checked read a second form that also returns
    `read_at`, and `paused` is the gate's own crossed rule over the thresholds `config.json` gives the wrapper
    (`src/run/budget.rs`). No second reader of `budget.json` is written.
  - `skipped` is `{unknown_kinds, unknown_fields, torn_lines}`: the reader's three counts, shown for the first
    time. The total is the sum of one whole-log pass per instance directory that passes its check, gone
    instances included; a replayed instance's pass is the replay's own (research, "Findings the plan rests
    on").

- The human form `viola list`: the BAY context line, the caption row `NAME LIVE STATUS WHEEL DIALOG CLI`, one
  strip row per wrapped session ordered by name, and the empty-board line (layout-templates, Output structure —
  `viola list`, both forms, and the two cli Components for the BAY line and the strip rows).
  - It prints the uncoloured form on every stream: the same characters the masters give for a piped stream,
    with no SGR. Verified against layout-templates and design-system: that form is lossless in words. The
    masters also require bold NAME, an amber `DIALOG` word and a dim stale row on a colour-capable terminal;
    that requirement stands unmet after this chunk and goes on the review card with the colour layer.
  - Nothing is truncated: the width is treated as unknown, and only unwrapped names are ever clipped
    (design-system, cli Tokens, Width).
  - The row-mode escaper lands with its first consumer here, for the recorded CLI version text: every control
    character as `\xHH` text, LF and TAB included, DEL and C1 included.
    [premise-corrected: the masters name the row mode for fields of `claude agents --json` origin only, and
    word its set without DEL; the landed message mode already escapes DEL (`src/human.rs`, `escape_message`)]
    Applying the row mode to a snapshot field is this slice's own rule and an expected amendment.

- The read model, per instance directory:
  - the instance check (`viola_state::strict::check_instance`) before any snapshot or log value is used and
    before any file under the home is opened, the process log included (opening it narrows the home). What
    `list` does when the home, `instances/` or one instance fails the check is worded by no master. The
    operator's answer to the P4 fork (`inputs#I2`, not a ruling of the founder): the whole board is refused
    with exit 21, nothing read, no log opened, the home's mode left as found; `--json` prints the one worded
    exit-21 document, and the human form the worded pair for what failed.
  - the snapshot through `viola_state::replay::read_snapshot_or_replay`, so a session whose snapshot is
    unreadable or newer still shows `wheel`, `budget_paused` and its liveness.
  - liveness `live` / `stale` from the heartbeat age and the snapshot's pid and start time; a gone instance is
    omitted. For an unreadable or newer snapshot the liveness rests on the heartbeat alone and is never
    `stale`: a fresh beat is `live`, anything else leaves the instance off the board. An absent snapshot gives
    no row.
  - `status`. [premise-corrected: no file on disk says a session is idle or busy; the snapshot has no such
    field and a running turn records nothing (architecture sidecar, 2026-10-04-running-turn-refusal)] The
    masters source it from `claude agents --json` and give `unknown` when that read is missing, failed or not
    joined. Every row of this slice reads `unknown`.
  - `dialog_pending` only from the snapshot's `pending_dialog`; a reader that fell back to replay reports
    `dialog_pending: false` (architecture).
  - the CLI cell from the snapshot's recorded version and `cli_verified`; a missing version prints `unknown`.
    No ledger file is read for it.
  - an instance directory name passes `ViolaName::try_new` before any path join.
  - nothing of the snapshot's `endpoint`, `pinned_bin`, `cwd` or `statusline_command`, and nothing of a
    pending dialog but its kind word, reaches a row, the document, an error or a log line.

- Tests owed with these surfaces (test-plan §6): Scenario E5's `list --json` signal, driven on a live
  wrapper's snapshot cut mid-object and on a sibling set to `v` 99; the Chaos suite's `skipped.torn_lines`
  reading and the forward-compat case's reading, both on `list --json`; Path 6's `list --json` readings
  (`budget` and each item's `budget_paused`) and the board's budget cells, as Unix root cases.

inside it sees the inheritance it sees under `%TEMP%` — the 799 root tests the fail-fast baseline never reached
included — and leaves `check_instance` untouched (security extract; arch §Occupied Resources, the scratch row).

The split is a pure move (arch §Infrastructure Patterns → Project directory structure; design-system and
layout-templates §Surface: cli): no line of output, no refusal order, no span or event, no test name moves; every

   re-creation after the removal goes through `viola_state::fs::create_private_dir` instead of

4. **`src/human.rs` split by phase.** `src/human.rs` stays the module root and keeps the shared writers

title: §2 — the Windows baseline red, closed against run 38215104120

data.head: ### §2 — the Windows baseline red, closed against run 38215104120

body: - Re-read at P3 (`gh run view 38215104120 --log-failed`, shard `viola-run-env`): `FAILED Unmutated baseline in 82s build + 137s test`; `FAIL [0.013s] (422/1224) viola::bin/viola cmd::hook::statusline::tests::statusline_an_instance_viola_laid_down_passes_its_check`, `panicked at src\cmd\hook\statusline.rs:510:9`; `Summary [136.901s] 425/1224 tests run: 424 passed (5 slow), 1 failed, 0 skipped`. The build dir is `D:\a\viola\viola-mutants-scratch\cargo-mutants-viola-2CPhiJ.tmp\`.

- **The baseline stopped at the first failure** (`[profile.mutants]` `fail-fast = { max-fail = 1 }`): 799 of the root package's 1224 tests never ran in the scratch copy. "Only this test fails there" is not established by the run.

- **The mechanism, as an equality.** For the statusline test's inputs: the home `<tempdir>/vhome` and `instances/` are made by plain `create_dir_all`, and `create_private_dir(&instance.dir)` finds nothing missing, so it protects nothing; every folder of the instance tree carries the tempdir's inheritance. Under CI's checkout run, the tempdir is under `%TEMP%` in the profile (the profile's inheritance: user, SYSTEM, Administrators full, Users read-execute — accepted, `strict.rs` `windows_verdict_takes_the_profile_inheritance`). Under the mutants run, `TMP`/`TEMP` point at `D:\a\viola\viola-mutants-scratch\`, which `wipe` re-creates with plain `create_dir_all` on the runner's workspace drive, so the tempdir inherits BUILTIN\Users `0x2`/`0x4` container-inherit (measured, ci#37214281447) and `check_instance` refuses the home `Err(Writable)`. The check behaves as security-plan writes it; what differs is the scratch's DACL against `%TEMP%`'s.

- **The cause-level fix site.** `wipe` (scratch.rs) re-creates the scratch; created through `viola_state::fs::create_private_dir`, the scratch is the topmost created folder outside the profile and takes the protected user + SYSTEM `OICI` DACL, so every tempdir cargo-mutants' tests lay inside it inherits an owner-only DACL, as one under `%TEMP%` does. This restores the property for the whole suite (the 799 unrun included), where fixing the one test would not. The protected scratch grants user + SYSTEM only, `%TEMP%` also Administrators (trusted) and Users read-execute: a subset of trusted grants, so a lay-down `%TEMP%` passes passes here too; a test that asserts a REFUSAL from `%TEMP%`'s Users read-execute ACE would read differently (none found: the Windows refusal cases build their own DACL, `strict.rs` `everyone_may_write`).

- **The witness without a dispatch.** CI's `test (windows-2025)` runs viola-e2e's unit tests (`coverage.rs:25–27`, `--workspace`). A Windows-only scratch.rs test can lay a scratch down through `wipe` under `target/e2e-home` (the runner's workspace drive) and lay the statusline test's tree inside it — accepted by `check_instance` — beside the same tree laid in a plain-created sibling, refused (the measured drive). The refused control is what keeps the accepted reading from passing vacuously. Its named limit: a Windows checkout under the profile reads the control accepted.
- No `viola-state` dependency in viola-e2e today (`crates/viola-e2e/Cargo.toml`); the root `[workspace.dependencies]` names `viola-state` by path (`Cargo.toml:135`).

- Neither file holds `cfg(windows)` / `cfg(unix)` code (`grep -c` reads 0 in each), so neither is a `windows-mutants.yml` `--file` subject and `tests/contract_windows_mutation_scope.rs` is unaffected.

- No code, script, test or workflow pins either file by path (`grep -rn -e 'human\.rs' -e 'run/send\.rs'` over `scripts tests src crates .github .config`: 0 hits); the docs and masters that name them (`.claude/docs/services/viola.md`, the masters' tree entries and test-plan §4's file citations) are the wrap's reconcile.
- nextest overrides key on name regexes (`send_window_`, `verify_window_`) and binaries; a moved test keeps its name, so none moves out of its override.

- `src/run/send.rs` phases (production 1–565): the classification (`Match`, `Confirms`, `classify` 44–73), the in-flight slot (`InFlight`, `Flight`, `SendSlot` and its `claim` / `session_started` / `settle` / `confirm`, `append_hook_event`, `close`, `window_ms`, `Reserved` 74–289), the params (`parse`, `parse_from` 300–325), the send and its context (`Ctx`, `send`, the refusals, `issue`, `confirm`, `unconfirmable`, `log_confirmed`, `budget_paused` 290–565). Tests (566–2415): shared fixtures 636–1023 (`quiet_gate`, `verified_gate`, `poisoned_gate`, `call`, `events`, `kinds`, `prompt`, `feed`, `occupy`, `paused`, `send_refusal_order`, `confirmed_with`, `confirmed_as`) used across the phases' cases, then cases grouped by the match/relabel, the text refusals, the slot, the turn rung, the local command, the gate wait, the budget gate and the link.

- `src/human.rs` phases (production 1–466): the shared writers (`write_refusal`, `refuse`, `write_internal_error`, `internal_error`, `write_result`, `result` 15–45), the send mirror (`MIRROR_WORD`, `mirror_line`, `write_send_open`, `write_read_back`, `write_send_unconfirmable`, `write_send_unable`, `write_wrapper_fault`, `write_unable` 47–113), the two escapers (`escape_message`, `escape_row` 114–141), the board (`instance_state_pair`, `home_state_pair`, `BayBudget`, the cells, `bay_line`, `board_rows`, `write_board`, `EMPTY_BOARD` 142–317), wait and last (318–369), the verb lines (`write_answered`, `write_paused`, `write_released`, `override_end`, `write_budget_lifted`, `write_budget_open` 370–417), the hints (`HUMAN_TYPING_HINT`, `answer_hint`, `send_hint` 418–466).

- `rustup target list --installed` reads `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` and `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`; `rust-toolchain.toml` carries no `targets` key, so the Windows std is host preparation (installed, never by a gate).

title: §1 — the survivors, surveyed (the proposed split moves this section to an entry of its own)

data.head: ### §1 — the survivors, surveyed (the proposed split moves this section to an entry of its own)

body: - `crates/viola-state/src/fs.rs` `replace_private_with` (`:281`, `:285` ×4, `:286`): with `HOST_IS_WINDOWS = cfg!(windows)` false, `retry_replace` is false on Linux, so the loop never retries and each mutant behaves as the original on this host; the retry decision is a const, so the harness never leaves these out (test-plan §3 `run` step 4). A Linux kill needs the decision supplied by the caller (a restatement); otherwise they are reachable only on Windows.

- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run/mutants/scratch.rs` `prepare` (`:48`, `:54`): `HOST_SCRATCH` false returns before both sites on Linux; test-plan §10 already records the pair "not measured here; owed to" a route entry (chunk 2026-10-09-epoch-3-cleanup-ii), and run 38036448183 read them caught on `windows-2025`. §2's edit of `wipe` moves no line of `prepare`; a change to `prepare` would move both coordinates.

- `crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs` `PortablePty::resize` (`:202`): three Linux-compiled tests resize and wait for the child to report `size 120x40` (`lib.rs:1196`, `:1233`, `:1255`, `wait_line` panics after `CHILD_WITHIN` 7 s); why they read the mutant missed is not known (the unit's baseline test phase read 1.7 s, `c-mutation-viola-pty.json`). Measured by hand-applying the mutant, at the survivors' own take-up.

- `src/cmd/verify/typed.rs` (18): `framing_turns`'s two waits (`count(..) > prompts && count(..) > stops`, `> starts || > prompts`), `max_gap`'s window filter, `SharedPty`'s three forwarders (`resize`, `close`, `child_pid` to the inner PTY), `Feed::take`'s `total > MAX_FRAME`, `end_by_ctrl_c`'s two deadline sums, `wait_pump`, `finish`'s deadline sum.

- **Marker:** 2026-10-13-epoch-4-survivors-ii · **Version:** viola-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-13 (P4, HEAD `64d7e5f7f620`)

The Epoch 4 boundary audit left 16 missed mutants in `src/cmd/verify/typed.rs`, `viola verify`'s Run B driver. The
founder's split moved them here from "Epoch 4 survivors": `framing_turns` 5, `<impl Pty for SharedPty>` 5, and
`Run`'s Ctrl-C ending 6 (scope §1). Each is disposed in the form test-plan §10 Mutation gate allows: a
behaviour-preserving restatement whose mutants a nextest case in the root package then kills. The case is shown red
under the hand-applied mutant and green restored. Every site compiles and runs on Linux, so no "not measured here"
record is expected (research.md §Measured facts 6). The reader that confirms each kill is the Epoch 5 boundary audit
(`inputs#I1`).

The restatement is three moves inside `typed.rs`, each putting a survivor's operator into a function its cases call
directly (scope §1, premise-corrected; research.md §Measured facts 3–5):

- the framing waits become two named predicates over the captures dir, and `clock.now() + PROBE_DEADLINE` becomes one
  named deadline;

- `SharedPty` becomes generic over its `Pty`, so a hand-written recording double in the test module reaches its three
  forwarders;

- the Ctrl-C ending and the pump wait become plain functions of a clock and closures. `Run` keeps only calls into
  them.

What `viola verify` types, waits on, records and logs does not change. That covers the four compiled pastes and
their order, the input-box/modal guard, `PROBE_DEADLINE` = 120 s, the Ctrl-C → 500 ms → Ctrl-C → kill ending, the
`MAX_FRAME` cap under `catch_unwind`, and one `verify-pty-probe` pair per run. These rest on founder rulings
(security-plan §Threat Model Summary, Child process spawning vector; architecture §Established Decisions [CLI Version
Compatibility]). `tests/cli_verify.rs` pins them end to end over the fake agent.
No mutation run, witness run or workflow dispatch, and no live `claude` (`inputs#I1`). No test starts any PTY child.
Every hand-applied mutant follows testing.md 2026-09-25 (the remove-the-guard run):
1. Re-read the site, since the rustfmt hook reflows after every write.

2. Apply the mutation's exact text at its restated site, with `rustfmt` on the file in the same call when a script
   writes it.
3. Confirm the edit landed.

4. Run the case through `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --unit --filter 'test(/(^|::)tests::<name>$/)'`
   (verification-harness.md 2026-09-27, the corrected filter) and read it red on its own assertion. A compile error
   or a panic outside the assertion is not a red, except a `-` on an `Instant` that panics at the mutated statement,
   which testing.md 2026-10-13 records as its kill.
5. Restore the file, confirm the restore landed, and read the case green.

Each pair goes into `evidence/survivors.md` as `{audit coordinate} · {mutation} · {restated site} · {test} · red:
{line} · green: {line}`.

2. **The framing waits (5): two predicates and one deadline, in `typed.rs` beside `framing_turns`.**
   a. `added_turn_ended(captures: &Path, prompts: usize, stops: usize) -> bool`: today's `:271` condition verbatim,
      `count_of(captures, UserPromptSubmit) > prompts && count_of(captures, Stop) > stops`. `framing_turns`' first
      `wait_for` closure (`:270-272`) calls it with its `prompts` and `stops`.
   b. `local_command_answered(captures: &Path, starts: usize, prompts: usize) -> bool`: today's `:288` condition
      verbatim, `count_of(captures, SessionStart) > starts || count_of(captures, UserPromptSubmit) > prompts`.
      `framing_turns`' second `wait_for` closure (`:287-289`) calls it.
   c. `probe_until(clock: &dyn Clock) -> Instant`: `clock.now() + PROBE_DEADLINE`. It replaces every
      `clock.now() + PROBE_DEADLINE` in `typed.rs`: `dialog_run` `:147`, `plan_run` `:180`, `framing_turns` `:269`,
      `:286`, and steps 4's two `self.clock.now() + PROBE_DEADLINE` (`:651`, `:671`). That is six sites, from the
      research sweep `grep -n 'clock.now() + PROBE_DEADLINE' src/cmd/verify/typed.rs`. `turn`'s
      `pasted + PROBE_DEADLINE` (`:239`) stays, since its base is not the clock.
   d. Cases, each over a `tempfile` dir of planted empty captures named `<Event>.<k>.json`
      (`ledger::parse_capture_file_name`; the pattern of `captured_reads_only_the_named_event`, `typed.rs:905`):
      - `added_turn_ended_needs_a_new_prompt_and_a_new_stop`, an rstest table:
        - none added, with prompts and stops at 0 → `false`;
        - one `UserPromptSubmit.1.json` and no `Stop` → `false`. This kills `:271:84` `>`→`==` and `>`→`>=` at the
          restated second operand.
        - one `Stop.1.json` and no prompt → `false`;
        - both added → `true`;
        - one prompt and one stop planted with prompts = stops = 1 → `false`. The baseline counts what was already
          there.
      - `local_command_answered_needs_a_new_start_or_a_new_prompt`, an rstest table:
        - none, with starts and prompts at 0 → `false`. This kills `:288:40` `>`→`==` and `>`→`>=` at the restated
          first operand.
        - one `SessionStart.1.json` → `true`;
        - one `UserPromptSubmit.1.json` → `true`;
        - one start planted with starts = 1 → `false`.
      - `probe_until_is_the_probe_deadline_after_now`: a fixed clock at `t` (`t` an `Instant::now()` taken in the
        case) yields `t + Duration::from_secs(120)`. The oracle is the literal 120 s, never the product's const
        (testing.md §What to assert). This kills `:286:29`, `:651:45` and `:671:53` (`+`→`-`), all three now this
        one `+`.
   e. Hand-apply each of the five survivors' mutations at the restated site and read it as the steps above say.

3. **`SharedPty` (5): generic over its `Pty`.** a. Restate `struct SharedPty(Arc>)` (`:385`) as `SharedPty

(Arc>)`, with `lock` on `impl

SharedPty

` and the seven forwarders on `impl Pty for SharedPty

`, each body unchanged. `Run::spawn`'s `SharedPty(shared)` (`:570`) infers `PortablePty`, and nothing else changes. `Run.pty` stays `Arc>`. b. In the test module, a hand-written `Recording` double implements `Pty`: - `resize` stores the size it was given and returns `Ok(())`; - `close` counts its calls; - `child_pid` returns `Some(4242)`; - `reader` and `writer` return `io::empty()` and `io::sink()`; - `try_wait` returns `Ok(None)` and `kill` returns `Ok(())`. No `mockall`: the root package declares none, and viola-pty's `MockPty` exists only in that crate's own test build (research.md §Measured facts 1). Three cases over `SharedPty(Arc::new(Mutex::new(Recording::default())))`: - `shared_pty_resize_reaches_its_pty_with_the_size`: after `resize(Size { cols: 120, rows: 40 })` returns `Ok`, the double holds that size. This kills `:403:9` → `Ok(())`. - `shared_pty_close_reaches_its_pty_once`: after one `close`, the double's count is 1. This kills `:415:9` → `()`. - `shared_pty_child_pid_is_its_ptys`: `child_pid()` is `Some(4242)`. This kills `:419:9` → `None`, `Some(0)` and `Some(1)`. c. Hand-apply each of the five.

4. **`Run`'s ending (6): the decisions as plain functions.**
   a. `ended_by(clock: &dyn Clock, until: Instant, finished: impl Fn() -> bool) -> bool`: `wait_pump`'s loop
      (`:659-665`) verbatim, with `finished()` where `self.pump.is_finished()` stood. `Run::wait_pump` is removed, and
      its three call sites call `ended_by(self.clock.as_ref(), until, || self.pump.is_finished())` (research.md
      §Measured facts 5: a kept one-call `bool` wrapper re-generates `→ true` where no test reaches it).
   b. `ctrl_c_ending(clock: &dyn Clock, mut ctrl_c: impl FnMut(), mut ended: impl FnMut(Instant) -> bool, mut kill:
      impl FnMut())`: today's `end_by_ctrl_c` order verbatim. It calls `ctrl_c()`, then
      `if !ended(clock.now() + CTRL_C_AGAIN) { ctrl_c() }`, then `if !ended(probe_until(clock)) { kill() }`.
      `Run::end_by_ctrl_c(self, keys)` becomes `ctrl_c_ending(…)` then `self.finish()`, with these closures:
      - the key send `let _ = keys.send(CTRL_C.to_vec())`;
      - `|until| ended_by(self.clock.as_ref(), until, || self.pump.is_finished())`;
      - `|| self.kill()`.
   c. `Run::finish`'s `ended` (`:671`) becomes
      `ended_by(self.clock.as_ref(), probe_until(self.clock.as_ref()), || self.pump.is_finished())`. Its status read
      and `obs_event!` stay as they are (obs-plan §4, the `verify` bullet; obs-plan §6, Child / shell spawns).
   d. Cases. The test module gets its own `FixedClock(Instant)` (research.md §Measured facts 8):
      - `ctrl_c_ending_sends_again_only_when_the_first_did_not_end_it`, an rstest table over the scripted `ended`
        readings. Each row records the Ctrl-C sends, the instants `ended` was given, and the kills:
        - `[true, true]` → 1 send, waits `[t + 500 ms, t + 120 s]`, 0 kills;
        - `[false, true]` → 2 sends, the same waits, 0 kills. This row kills `:648:12` (1 send) and `:651:12`
          (1 kill).
        - `[false, false]` → 2 sends, 1 kill;
        - `[true, false]` → 1 send, 1 kill.

        The wait instants kill `:648:45` (`t − 500 ms`) and read `:651:45` again through `probe_until`. Oracles are
        literals (500 ms, 120 s).
      - `ended_by_reads_true_once_finished_and_false_once_the_deadline_passes`, a table over a fixed clock and a
        `finished` closure that counts its calls, true from a given call on:
        - finished from the 2nd call, `until` after `t` → `true`;
        - never finished in 3 calls (true from the 4th, a guard so no mutant can spin), `until == t` → `false`. This
          kills `:659:9` → `true`.
        - finished from the 2nd call, `until == t` → `false`;
        - finished from the 2nd call, `until` before `t` → `false`.

        Each row ends within one `POLL` (5 ms) of real sleep, far below the `mutants` profile's 10 s kill
        (testing.md 2026-09-24).
   e. Hand-apply each of the six. `:651:45` and `:671:53` are the one `+` in `probe_until` (step 2c), so step 2's
      `probe_until` reading is their reading, cited in both rows.

5. **Close the ledger.** Every row's `file_at_head` and `by` are filled. The ledger probe reads it whole against the
   earlier chunk's 16 `owed` rows, and `evidence/survivors.md` carries the red/green pairs. That is 14 distinct
   hand-applications: the 16 audit mutations, where `:286:29`, `:651:45` and `:671:53` share one restated `+`.
- none (the chunk's `evidence/` files are records, not code)

and the test double on the `windows-2025` side, check only. G1 and the lint probes run. `tests/cli_verify.rs` runs
whole: it is the end-to-end witness that Run B is unchanged over the fake agent. It covers the seventeen steps and
the stamp, the six spawn pairs, the trusted run's typed order, the modal guards and no run dir left behind
(`tests/cli_verify.rs:95`, `:398`, `:749`, `:914`, `:972`, `:995`).

push and the CI read (`leg = 'operator'`).

The Epoch 4 boundary audit left 47 missed mutants (scope §1). The founder split the entry at P4 (`inputs#I2`), so
this chunk disposes 31 of them, keeps the 2 `scratch.rs` records as they stand, and owes `typed.rs`'s other 16 to
"Epoch 4 survivors II". That new entry, directly after this one, takes the Run B driver restatement. Each of the 31
takes one of the forms test-plan §10 Mutation gate and §3 `run` step 4 allow, worded for the reader that confirms it,
the Epoch 5 boundary audit (`inputs#I1`). The forms are a nextest test in the package that owns the mutated file,
failing under the hand-applied mutant and passing on the original, or a behaviour-preserving restatement whose
mutants a test then kills.

Two restatements change shape without changing behaviour. `viola_state::fs::replace_private_with` takes its retry
decision from its caller, so the five const-gated `fs.rs` mutants become killable on Linux (research.md §Measured
facts 2; architecture §Established Decisions [Snapshot writer] stays as written). `viola send`'s issue-line decision
becomes a named function of `--json` and the terminal reading, because nextest never runs under a terminal (research.md
§Measured facts 6; layout-templates §Surface: cli · Output structure — `viola send` stays byte-identical). One test-side
fix is likely: `viola-pty`'s resize tests name their report files after the test alone. The audit's two cargo-mutants
jobs shared one `TMPDIR`, which can let one job's run satisfy another's wait (research.md §Measured facts 1,
HYPOTHESIS). Step 2 measures it first.

No mutation run, witness run or workflow dispatch, and no live `claude` (`inputs#I1`). A kill is shown by a
hand-applied mutant in the working tree, reverted after its reading. Every disposal lands in one ledger,
`evidence/survivors.ndjson`, with 47 rows, the 16 owed rows included, which the Epoch 5 boundary audit reads against
its own run.

Every hand-applied mutant follows testing.md 2026-09-25 (the remove-the-guard run): re-read the site, apply the
mutant's exact text at its coordinate (`rustfmt` on the file in the same call when a script writes it), confirm the
edit landed, run the new case and read it red on its own assertion (not a compile error, not a panic outside the
assertion), restore the file, confirm the restore landed, and read the case green. Each pair goes into
`evidence/survivors.md` as `{coordinate} · {mutation} · {test} · red: {line} · green: {line}`. Cases run through
`bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --unit --filter '<expr>'`, the harness's own filter (verification-harness.md
2026-09-27: `test(=tests::name)` or a regex form), never a bare `cargo test`.

1. **The survivor ledger, before any edit.** Write `evidence/survivors.ndjson`: 47 lines, one per row of the audit
   record's `mutation.survivors`
   (`.andromeda/runs/2026-10-12T06-54-29-code-audit/record.json`). Each line is `{"coordinate", "mutation", "file_at_head",
   "form", "by"}`: `coordinate` and `mutation` are the audit's text verbatim, `file_at_head` is where the function sits
   at HEAD, `form` is one of `test` · `restatement` · `not-measured-here` · `owed`, and `by` is the test name, the
   record or the owing entry. The 16 `typed.rs` rows of `framing_turns`, `SharedPty` and `Run::end_by_ctrl_c` /
   `wait_pump` / `finish` are `owed`, `by` "Epoch 4 survivors II". The 2 `scratch.rs` rows are `not-measured-here`,
   `by` naming the test-plan §10 Mutation gate record and run 38036448183. The other 29 rows start with `form` and `by`
   set to the step that disposes them, and each step fills `by` with its test's name. `evidence/survivors.md` holds the
   same rows as a table, plus each kill's red and green reading.

2. **`viola-pty` `<impl Pty for PortablePty>::resize` (`crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs:202:9`, → `Ok(())`): measure,
   then dispose.**
   a. Hand-apply the mutant and run the three resize tests (`spawn_runs_a_raw_child_that_sees_its_size_a_resize_and_its_own_exit_code`,
      `spawn_reports_a_resize_to_a_child_that_reads_no_key`,
      `spawn_delivers_a_key_written_right_after_a_resize_to_a_child_not_yet_reading`) alone, one harness call, no
      other test process running. Record each test's verdict and duration and the child report its failure message
      prints.
   b. **If they read red alone** (the expected reading: no `size 120x40` within `CHILD_WITHIN`), the miss came from
      outside the test. Make `report_paths` (`lib.rs:852`) name both files after the test AND this process
      (`std::process::id()`), so no other process's run can write the file a test waits on. The `Drop` and failure-dump
      behaviour stays as it is. Re-read the three tests red under the mutant and green restored. Record in

   c. **If any reads green alone**, the hypothesis is falsified. Read the child report the test leaves (a passing test

      panicking after the wait in a scratch edit). Record what changed the child's size. Then write a `viola-pty` case

4. **`viola-state` `fs::replace_private_with` (6): the retry decision passed in, then killed.**

      holds today's loop verbatim, with `retry(e.error.raw_os_error())` where `retry_replace(…, HOST_IS_WINDOWS)` stood.

   b. Two cases in `fs.rs`'s tests, each with a target that is an existing non-empty directory, so `persist` fails at
      the same call on every OS (testing.md 2026-09-24):
      - `retry` always true: the pause runs exactly `REPLACE_ATTEMPTS - 1` times, the call returns the error, and the
        directory is untouched. The pause panics past `REPLACE_ATTEMPTS`, as the Windows case at `fs.rs:440-447`

5. **`viola-state` `board.rs` (4).**

6. **`src/run/wheel.rs` (9): rows in the classifier tables, and one recorder case.** Each split-read case feeds two

   - `:427:17` (delete the ESC arm in `Seq::Esc`): `\x1b\x1b[` then `I`. The original carries `Csi` into the second

   - `:458:24` (guard `osc` → `true`): a DCS reply ended by BEL (`\x1bP1$r0m\x07`) is typing; only OSC ends on BEL.
   - `:467:35` (`<`→`<=`): an OSC payload of exactly `BOUND` + 1 bytes ended by BEL is typing; `BOUND` bytes is not.
   - `:516:49` (`==`→`!=` in DA): `\x1b[?c` and `\x1b[>c` (DA with no field) are replies, rows in
     `classifier_terminal_reply_is_not_editing`.
   - `:518:47` (`&&`→`||` in the kitty flags reply): `\x1b[?1;2u` (two fields) is typing, a row in
     `classifier_typing_is_editing`.
   - `Recorder::record` `:297:18` (`&&`→`||`): a recorder whose `events.ndjson` append fails while the snapshot write
     lands. The instance dir holds a directory named `events.ndjson`, and the snapshot is seeded as the module's
     helpers seed it. A `pause` through the wheel then reads `Err(ProtocolError::Internal)`; the mutant reads `Ok`.
   Every new row keeps F-W2's closed list exact: no shape is added to `REPLIES`, and no existing row changes its
   verdict (a11y-plan §3 Keyboard test harness; security-plan §Threat Model Summary, the human-stdin vector).

7. **`src/run/dialog.rs` (2).**
   - `millis` `:144:5` (→ `1`): a case of the function itself: 1 500 ms reads `1500`, and `Duration::MAX` reads
     `u64::MAX`.
   - `DialogSlot::hook_dialog` `:208:42` (`!=`→`==` in the arm retain): PreToolUse for tool A, then PreToolUse for tool
     B, on one slot with the module's fixed clock. Tool A's arm survives tool B's raise, read through A's
     PermissionRequest continuation (equal tool and `tool_input`), which takes A's `dialog_id` and raises nothing new.
     Under the mutant A's arm is gone and the continuation is raised as a new dialog. The case reuses the
     `continuation_*` cases' helpers (`dialog.rs:662-756`).

8. **`src/cmd/hook.rs` `answer` (`:403:27`, `||`→`&&`).** A case with a dialog event (the leading operand false, per
   testing.md 2026-09-24's operator-token rule) and a RELATIVE `answers` path that resolves, from the test process's
   current dir, to a planted answers dir in a tempdir. The path is built from `..` components and the tempdir's
   path, so `answers.is_absolute()` is false. The original prints nothing; the mutant reads the planted answer and
   prints its body. It sits beside `answer_reads_no_relative_answers_dir_and_no_oversize_file` (`hook.rs:1078`),
   whose relative dir does not exist and so cannot tell the two apart.

9. **`src/cmd/send.rs` `Out<'_>::open` (`:119:12`, delete `!`): the decision named, then tested.** Restate the
   condition as a private `fn issue_line_shows(json: bool, terminal: bool) -> bool` (`!json && terminal`), called by
   `open` with `io::stdout().is_terminal()`. A table case covers all four inputs; only `(false, true)` shows. The
   line's text, stream and timing stay as they are (layout-templates §Surface: cli · Output structure — `viola send`,
   the `[  ] open` line on stderr on a TTY only). Hand-apply the mutant on the moved `!`.

10. **`src/run/send/slot.rs` `close` (`:207:5`, → `()`; the audit's `src/run/send.rs:271:5`).** A case in `slot.rs`'s
    tests: after `confirm` returns `None` at its deadline on the fixed test clock, a matching line that lands later is
    not claimed. The flight is `Closed`, so `settle` leaves it unchanged and a second `confirm` returns `None` at once.
    The mutant leaves it `Waiting` and claims the line. The case uses `src/run/send/test_support.rs`'s fixtures.

11. **`src/cmd/verify/typed.rs` (2 of 18).** Only in the test module (`typed.rs:689` on); `framing_turns`, `SharedPty`
    and `Run` are not touched (they are owed, `inputs#I2`).
    - `max_gap` `:304:54` (`&&`→`||`): a case with a chunk after `to` that is not the last output in the window. For
      window `[t, t+100 ms]` and chunks `[t+500 ms]` the gap is `100`; the mutant reads `500`.
    - `Feed::take` `:439:23` (`>`→`>=`): with `total` set to `MAX_FRAME - 1`, a one-byte take reaches exactly
      `MAX_FRAME` and does not poison the screen. A second byte poisons it.

12. **Close the ledger.** Every `test` and `restatement` row's `by` names the test that read red under its mutant.
    The `survivors` probe entry reads the ledger whole, and `evidence/survivors.md` carries the 29 red/green pairs.
- none (the chunk's `evidence/` files are records, not code)
- `crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs` — step 2: `report_paths` per process (branch b), or a new resize case (branch c)
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/statusline.rs` — step 3: the whole-argv assertion
- `crates/viola-state/src/fs.rs` — step 4: `replace_private_retrying` and two cases
- `crates/viola-state/src/board.rs` — step 5: three cases
- `src/run/wheel.rs` — step 6: eight table rows or split-read cases and one recorder case
- `src/run/dialog.rs` — step 7: two cases
- `src/cmd/hook.rs` — step 8: one case
- `src/cmd/send.rs` — step 9: `issue_line_shows` and its case
- `src/run/send/slot.rs` — step 10: one case
- `src/cmd/verify/typed.rs` — step 11: two cases in the test module only

The standing lint and unit entries, and the Windows-target clippy, which reads the `cfg(windows)` half of
`fs.rs`'s cases. G1 and the lint probes run. The survivor ledger is read whole against the audit's record. A guard
keeps `typed.rs`'s edits inside its test module, and a preservation guard covers every other file. `cargo deny`
runs, and so do the harness smoke with G2 and G4 and the native `pre-push`. The operator pass fires hygiene, the push
and the CI read (`leg = 'operator'`).

No mutation entry, no witness run and no workflow dispatch is listed (`inputs#I1`). Each kill is a hand-applied
mutant read inside a step and recorded in `evidence/survivors.md`; the Epoch 5 boundary audit is its reader. No
entry is a live leg: nothing starts the real `claude`. The ledger entry reads `evidence/survivors.ndjson`, which
step 1 writes and step 12 closes, and carries no `artifact`. The guards name their base `c6e130181e51` (HEAD at P4),

- (tests) Each of the 31 disposed survivors has a nextest case in the package that owns its mutated file. The case
  reads red on its own assertion under the hand-applied mutant and green on the restored file, with both readings in
  `evidence/survivors.md`; no survivor is called equivalent or disposed by argument (per test-plan §10 Mutation gate;
  per test-plan §3 `run` step 4, Test scope).

- (tests) The ledger entry reads `last line 1`: `evidence/survivors.ndjson` holds one row for each of the audit's 47
  survivors, keyed on the audit's coordinate and mutation text. 16 are `owed` to "Epoch 4 survivors II" (`inputs#I2`),
  2 are `not-measured-here` (the `scratch.rs` record, test-plan §10), and every row names its disposer (per test-plan
  §10 Mutation gate).

- (tests) No mutation run, witness run or workflow dispatch is made, and no live `claude` starts (`inputs#I1`; per
  test-plan §10 Mutation gate, the epoch-boundary cadence).

- (arch / security) `replace_private_with` keeps its contract: the mode is set before any byte, at most
  `REPLACE_ATTEMPTS` = 100 attempts, and only raw OS error 5 on a Windows host is retried. Its existing cases pass, the
  two new Linux cases read the attempt count and the immediate return, and its two callers are unchanged (the
  preservation guard) (per architecture §Established Decisions [Snapshot writer]; per security-plan §Data Protection,
  the `~/.viola/` access control row).

- (security / layouts) `shell_argv` returns exactly `["/bin/sh", "-c", command]` on Unix and `None` on Windows, and
  remains the only shell-out (per security-plan §Input Validation, the statusline shell-out row).

- (security / obs / layouts) `board::scan` refuses an unstattable home (`ScanRefused::Home`) and returns `Err` for an
  unlistable `instances/`, writing no line in either case. `board::read` sums `unknown_fields` across instances, and
  `list --json`'s `skipped` shape is unchanged (per security-plan §Data Protection, the `list` clause; per obs-plan
  §10 Bounded exemptions, item 7; per layout-templates §Surface: cli · Output structure — `viola list --json`).

- (a11y / security) Every new classifier row keeps F-W2's closed list exact. No row is added to `REPLIES`, the
  existing typing, reply and split tables pass unchanged, and every split-read case asserts both reads' verdicts (per
  a11y-plan §3 Keyboard test harness; per security-plan §Threat Model Summary, the human-stdin vector).

- (layouts) `viola send`'s `[  ] open` issue line prints on stderr only on a TTY without `--json`, and no human
  output line of `send` changes (per layout-templates §Surface: cli · Output structure — `viola send`; per
  layout-templates §Surface: cli · IA notes).

- (tests) `typed.rs` changes only inside its test module (the hunk entry, `last line 0`). `framing_turns`, `SharedPty`
  and `Run` are unchanged and owed (`inputs#I2`).

- (obs) G1 reads no bare `#[instrument]`, and G2 and G4 stay green on the booted home and the kept homes (per obs-plan
  §9 Gate commands).

- (tests) `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --unit` reads `"ok":true`, `pre-push` reads `"ok":true` at stage
  `linux-tests`, and the CI-read entry reads `verdict: green` on HEAD across `windows-2025`, `macos-latest` and
  `ubuntu-latest`. The report names the run id (per test-plan §10 Zero-flakiness budget; per test-plan §10 Coverage
  thresholds).

No verification-matrix capability is claimed. No unclaimed capability's acceptance is this chunk's: of the 37-id pool
read at P4, none names mutation strength or a survivor site. `v1-07` is per-OS coverage, which this chunk does not
move.

- The founder's own answer to the P4 Size fork: split (`inputs#I2`).

  runtime patching) and the scope survey's own words ("unless the caller supplies the decision"). `Out::open` by

- **Pause seam on the replace** (`crates/viola-state/src/fs.rs:268`): `replace_private_with` takes the pause as
  `&mut dyn FnMut()`. The tests count pauses, and on Windows bound them with a panic past the last attempt
  (`fs.rs:440-447`).

- **Pure decision beside a const** (`fs.rs:257` `retry_replace(raw, host_is_windows)`,

- **Child-entry PTY tests** (`crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs:631`, `:895`): the test binary re-runs itself under the PTY
  as `tests::pty_child_entry`, which reports each step to a file; waits are on report lines under

  (testing.md 2026-09-24) — `hook.rs:403`'s `!event.is_dialog() || !answers.is_absolute()`, `wheel.rs:518`.

- **The remove-the-guard run**: each new test is shown red under its hand-applied mutant, then green on the restored
  file, with the site re-read before each edit (the rustfmt hook reflows; testing.md 2026-09-25).
- **I/O errors per OS**: a forced persist failure must fail at the same call on every CI OS (testing.md 2026-09-24).

- **No reshaping for mutants** (testing.md 2026-09-28): never move a body out of cargo-mutants' generated set; a
  restatement keeps every mutant generated and makes it killable.

1. **`PortablePty::resize` (`viola-pty` `lib.rs:202:9`).** The audit's log for this mutant shows viola-pty's own three
   resize tests ran under it and PASSED: `spawn_runs_a_raw_child_that_sees_its_size_a_resize_and_its_own_exit_code`
   5.352 s, `spawn_reports_a_resize_to_a_child_that_reads_no_key` 5.404 s, and
   `spawn_delivers_a_key_written_right_after_a_resize_to_a_child_not_yet_reading` 6.106 s, all marked SLOW past 5 s
   (log lines 177–184; `40 tests run: 40 passed`). Each waits for the child's `size 120x40` report line
   (`lib.rs:1213`, `:1247`, `:1265`). So under a resize that does nothing, the child still reported 120×40 about 5 s
   later. What changed the child's size is NOT measured: the watch reports under `<temp dir>/viola-pty-watch/` are
   gone (the audit scratch's dir is empty). The tests sit in `viola-pty` itself, so the tests-history item that
   places the resize tests in the root package does not hold for these three.
   HYPOTHESIS (read at P4, not measured): a report written by another job. The audit ran cargo-mutants with
   `-j 2` (`.andromeda/runs/2026-10-12T06-54-29-code-audit/mut-driver.py:18`, `JOBS = 2`, passed as `-j` at `:53`)
   and one `TMPDIR` for both jobs (`:59`). The child's report path is `<temp dir>/viola-pty-watch/<test name>.report`,
   keyed by test name only (`crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs:852-866` `report_paths`). The child appends to it
   (`report`, `:618-626`), and `wait_line` takes any matching line in the file (`:951-964`). So the other job running
   the same test on an unmutated `resize` can write `size 120x40` into the file the mutant's test waits on.

2. **`crates/viola-state/src/fs.rs` `replace_private_with` (6).** With `HOST_IS_WINDOWS` false the guard
   `attempts < REPLACE_ATTEMPTS && retry_replace(raw, false)` is false, whatever `attempts` is. So `:281:18`
   (`+=`→`*=`), `:285:20` (guard→`false`) and the three `:285:29` swaps behave as the original on Linux. But
   `:286:21` (`&&`→`||`) does not: on any failed `persist` it reads `attempts < 100 || false`, pauses, and retries 99
   times before returning the error. No Linux test makes `persist` fail, which is why it read missed. A target that
   is an existing non-empty directory fails `persist` on all three OSes.

3. **`scratch.rs` `prepare` (2).** At `dffad3e` and at HEAD, `:47` is `fn prepare`, `:48` its first statement
   `if !HOST_SCRATCH`, and `:54` `if !scratch_allowed(&root, &scratch)`, inside the `HOST_SCRATCH` branch. Both
   mutants are reached only when `HOST_SCRATCH` (`cfg!(windows)`) is true. test-plan §10 already records them "not
   measured here", read caught on `windows-2025` in run 38036448183 (job `mutants (viola-e2e)`).

4. **`typed.rs` `SharedPty` (5).** `typed.rs`'s pump is `pump_with_paste(&mut SharedPty(..), .., Size::DEFAULT,
   &mut || None, ..)` (`typed.rs:569-578`). The pump calls `resize` only when its size closure reports a new size
   (`pump.rs:186-190`), so never here, and never calls `child_pid` (`pump.rs`: `try_wait` `:170`/`:211`, `close`
   `:171`/`:219`, `resize` `:190`, `kill` `:208`). `SharedPty::resize` and `::child_pid` are trait-required
   forwarders no product path calls. `close` is called at the child's exit. `SharedPty` wraps the concrete
   `PortablePty`, and `Run` holds `Arc<Mutex<PortablePty>>`: there is no `Pty` double seam in `typed.rs`.

5. **`typed.rs`, the rest (13).** `max_gap`'s filter (`:304:54`) is a pure function; its test
   (`typed.rs:715`) has no chunk outside the window on BOTH sides that changes the answer. `Feed::take`'s
   `total > MAX_FRAME` (`:439:23`) is tested past the cap only, never at exactly `MAX_FRAME`. `framing_turns`
   (`:271:84` ×2, `:286:29`, `:288:40` ×2) needs a `Run` with a live pump and paste handle. `Run::end_by_ctrl_c`
   (`:648:12`, `:651:12`, `:648:45`, `:651:45`), `::wait_pump` (`:659:9`) and `::finish` (`:671:53`) need a `Run`
   whose pump the test controls. No unit test builds a `Run`; the root tests reach these only through a whole
   `viola verify` against the fake agent, where the fake's speed hides each mutant.

6. **`src/cmd/send.rs` `Out<'_>::open` (`:119:12`).** The condition is `!self.json && io::stdout().is_terminal()`.
   Under nextest stdout is never a terminal, so both the original and the mutant print nothing in every test.

7. **`src/cmd/hook.rs` `answer` (`:403:27`).** `!event.is_dialog() || !answers.is_absolute()`: with the leading
   operand false (a dialog event) and a relative `answers`, the original returns at once. The mutant reads the answer
   file at `answers.join(..)` relative to the process cwd, which no test has planted.

8. **`statusline.rs` `shell_argv` (2).** The crate test checks `shell_argv(command).is_some() == cfg!(unix)`
   (`statusline.rs:385`), which `Some([""; 3])` and `Some(["xyzzy"; 3])` both pass on Unix.

9. **`board.rs` (4), `wheel.rs` (9), `dialog.rs` (2), `slot.rs` `close` (1)** — each reachable on Linux through a unit
   case in its own file; none needs a restatement (sites read; the cases are P4's).
