title: 3. The root package's Windows mutation baseline (CARRY 3, an observation, not this chunk's work)

data.head: ### 3. The root package's Windows mutation baseline (CARRY 3, an observation, not this chunk's work)

body:
- watch: the green reading of `windows-mutants.yml` on the root package (run 38215104120 red at `dffad3e`; its cause
  removed by the Epoch 4 cleanup, witnessed on CI at ci#38375200217) is not measured — it is read at the next
  `windows-mutants.yml` dispatch, the Epoch 5 boundary audit (1/1; since chunk 2026-10-13-epoch-4-cleanup).
  No dispatch inside this chunk (`inputs#I1`).

- No mutation run (`cargo mutants`), witness run or workflow dispatch inside the chunk (`inputs#I1`); a hand-applied
  mutant in the working tree, reverted, is the only mutant this chunk runs.
- No live `claude` start (`inputs#I1`); no new capability-ledger row, no `viola verify` probe change.

- No production behaviour change: a restatement keeps behaviour; a test-only seam stays behind `cfg(test)` or the
  existing test features.

- The "Paste newline ledger row" CARRY on `fs.rs` stays there; this chunk disposes the six `fs.rs` survivors under
  the three forms and names that entry where a record is owed to it.

- Sizing (`inputs#I1`): 47 survivors across 11 files in 5 packages, sized against one window. The founder split it
  at P4 (`inputs#I2`): 31 disposed here plus the 2 `scratch.rs` records; `typed.rs`'s other 16 are owed to "Epoch 4
  survivors II", and no step of this chunk edits `framing_turns`, `SharedPty` or `Run`.

_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-10-13-interrupted-verify-cleanup · **Version:** viola-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-13T18:42Z
- **HEAD at P4:** `d9f01b1b8642` (the base every guard below names).

A `viola verify` stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM now ends its run cleanly. It ends the child it is running with no key,
removes only the dirs that run created, prints one `unable:` / `hint:` pair, logs
`process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail:"interrupted"}` and exits 1. It writes no stamp, no step line and
no `stamped` line. Older, foreign and kill-or-crash leftovers stay by hand. No owner record and no remover of an
earlier run's dirs is built. This is the founder's narrow entry (scope.md §1, CARRY), and the operator answered its
three open forms at P4 (`inputs#I2`).

Ctrl-C and TERM mean Unix `SIGINT` and `SIGTERM`, and Windows `CTRL_C_EVENT` and `CTRL_BREAK_EVENT`. A closed console
window, logoff, shutdown, SIGKILL and a crash keep their default and are the stated exception (`inputs#I2`;
research.md §Measured facts 3). Every wait verify makes already polls a predicate on a short `POLL`. A stop flag read
in the same loops ends a wait within one `POLL`, and the run's existing kill and drop guards then do the rest
(research.md §Measured facts 2, 4). The handler sits on `libc` (Unix) and `windows-sys` (Windows), both already the
root package's. No manifest line and no `Cargo.lock` package changes (research.md §Measured facts 6).

The chunk also moves two CARRY'd literals onto their one homes, both behaviour-preserving (research.md §Measured
facts 7). Verify's default program becomes `viola_agent_claude::PROGRAM`, and Runs C and D's `--settings` becomes
`viola_agent_claude::statusline::SETTINGS_FLAG`. Per architecture §Occupied Resources, security-plan §Data Protection
and §Threat Model Summary, obs-plan §4 / §6, test-plan §5 / §11, design-system and layout-templates §Surface: cli.

1. **The stop, `src/cmd/verify/stop.rs` (new).** One stop flag for the verify process, with:
   - `install`, called once by verify;
   - a read;
   - a set that tests use with no signal.

   The handler only sets the flag (an async-signal-safe store). On Unix it is installed for `SIGINT` and `SIGTERM`
   through `libc`'s `sigaction`.

   On Windows a console control routine is registered through `windows-sys`'s `SetConsoleCtrlHandler`. The routine sets
   the flag and returns TRUE for `CTRL_C_EVENT` and `CTRL_BREAK_EVENT`. For every other event it returns FALSE without
   setting it, so the OS default stands.

   Which events stop is a plain function of the event number, tested on every OS. The `cfg(windows)` routine only
   forwards to it (testing.md 2026-09-24, the `cfg` reader rule). A failed install, such as no console on Windows,
   is ignored: the run goes on as it does today, fail-open.

   Each FFI call sits in its own `unsafe` block, as `src/panic_frames.rs` does. The module carries its inline
   `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` (step 7).

2. **Install before the first child (`src/cmd/verify.rs` `measure`).** `measure` installs the stop as its first act,
   before program resolution, the pin and the version probe (`verify.rs:102`–`:156`). By then `main` has already run
   the panic hook and `restrict_dll_search()` (`src/main.rs:48`, `:52`). Verify is the only verb that installs it. No
   other verb's signal behaviour changes.

3. **The bounded children observe the stop (`src/run/version_gate.rs` `run_bounded`).** `run_bounded` takes one more
   input, the stop. When the stop reads set, it kills the child, reaps it and returns with the outcome "stopped", which
   is told apart from the deadline's kill. `version_gate` (`version_gate.rs:115`) passes an input that never stops, so
   `run`'s gate is byte-for-byte unchanged in behaviour. Verify's `run_logged` (`verify.rs:76`) passes the stop and
   still writes its spawn pair: the `process-exit` of a stopped child carries `duration_ms` and no
   `child_exit_status`.
   - When the version probe or the print probe is stopped, `measure` ends as step 5 says, before `ProbeDir` exists or
     with `ProbeDir` dropped on the return.
   - Impact: `run_bounded` @ `src/cmd/verify.rs:86`, `src/run/version_gate.rs:115`, and its two unit cases `:301`,
     `:321` (research.md §Graph impact).

4. **The interactive runs observe the stop (`src/cmd/verify/typed.rs`).**
   - **The waits.** Every wait a run makes returns as soon as the stop reads set. That covers `wait_for` (`:195`),
     `wait_capture` (`:328`), and the loops in `Run::settle` (`:639`) and `Run::box_wait` (`:655`). The polling those
     four loops share becomes one plain function of a clock, a deadline, the stop and a predicate, unit-tested with the
     stop set and unset.
   - **The Ctrl-C ending.** The stop also ends the two waits of `ctrl_c_ending` (`:543`) early, so a stop during Run
     B's Ctrl-C ending goes straight to its kill.
   - **The pump wait is the exception.** The wait for the pump to end after a kill, `ended_by` inside `Run::finish`
     (`:705`), does NOT observe the stop. A run's dir is never removed while its child may still be writing into it.
   - **Ending a stopped run.** After any wait returns, a run that finds the stop set ends its child with
     `Run::end_by_kill` (no key, `:684`) and drops its dir. `measure` (`:63`) then returns the outcome "stopped" and
     starts no later run.
   - **Normal runs are unchanged.** A run that is not stopped behaves exactly as today: Run B's Ctrl-C ending, every
     deadline, paste, guard and order.
   - **The literal.** The two `--settings` literals (`:132`, `:173`) read `SETTINGS_FLAG`.
   - Impact: `end_by_kill` from `measure` `:77`, `trusted_run` `:111`, `dialog_run` `:159`, `plan_run` `:188`;
     `settle` ×7, `wait_for` ×4, `wait_capture` ×2 (research.md §Graph impact).

5. **The interrupted outcome (`src/cmd/verify.rs`).**
   - **When the stop counts.** `measure` reads the stop:
     - when a bounded child or `typed::measure` reports "stopped";
     - once more after `typed::measure` returns and the probe dir is dropped, before `check_rows` (`:211`).

     Set at either point, `measure` prints no step line, calls neither `update_stamps` nor `record`, and prints the
     pair below through `human::refuse` (`src/human.rs:38`). Once `check_rows` has begun, the run completes as today.
     The stamp write is atomic through `replace_private` (research.md §Measured facts 4).
   - **The pair.** The stderr pair, verbatim (a planning form on the operator's word, the founder's wording owed;
     `inputs#I2`):
     ```
     unable: verify was stopped before it finished
     hint: run viola verify again to stamp this CLI
     ```
   - **Exit and log.** The exit is 1. Under a `VIOLA_NAME`, `verify` (`:67`–`:69`) writes
     `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail:"interrupted"}` through `run::log_self_exit`.
   - **Default program.** The default program (`:105`) reads `viola_agent_claude::PROGRAM`.

6. **The schema (`schemas/diag-line.v1.json`).** `process-exit.detail` gains the member `interrupted`, making it 12
   members (the rule: the enum's members as listed in research.md §Files inspected, plus this one). No other schema
   change.

7. **Unit cases (inline `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`, literal oracles).**
   - `stop.rs`:
     - the event decision on every OS: `0` and `1` stop; `2`, `5` and `6` do not;
     - a `cfg(unix)` case per signal: install, raise `SIGINT` (and in a second case `SIGTERM`) at the test's own
       process, and read the flag set with the process alive (one process-global flag per test; nextest runs each
       test in its own process, testing.md 2026-09-24);
     - a `cfg(windows)` case that calls the routine directly with `CTRL_C_EVENT` and `CTRL_BREAK_EVENT` (TRUE, flag
       set) and with `CTRL_CLOSE_EVENT` (FALSE, flag unset), on CI's `windows-2025` leg (`inputs#I2`, the third
       answer).
   - `typed.rs`:
     - the shared polling function returns at once with the stop set and waits to its predicate or deadline with the
       stop unset (a fixed clock);
     - `ended_by` still waits with the stop set;
     - the existing `ctrl_c_ending` / `ended_by` cases stay green.
   - `version_gate.rs`:
     - with the stop set, `run_bounded` kills and reaps a child the test started (one that runs until killed) and
       reads "stopped";
     - the two existing cases pass the never-stop input unchanged.
- `src/cmd/verify/stop.rs` — the stop flag, its per-OS installation and the event decision, with inline unit cases.

- `src/cmd/verify.rs` — the install, the stopped bounded children, the interrupted outcome and its pair, exit and
  `detail`, the default program through `PROGRAM`; `mod stop;` beside `mod typed;`.

- `src/cmd/verify/typed.rs` — the stop observed by every wait but the pump wait, a stopped run ended by kill, the
  "stopped" outcome, `SETTINGS_FLAG` at two sites, the shared polling function and its cases.

- `src/run/version_gate.rs` — `run_bounded`'s stop input and "stopped" outcome; `version_gate` passes the never-stop
  input; the new unit case.
- `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` — `interrupted` in `process-exit.detail`.
- `tests/cli_verify.rs` — the SIGINT and SIGTERM table.
- `tests/support/verify.rs` — the started, unwaited verify without the turn's Stop.

These are the standing lint and unit entries. The Windows-target clippy reads `stop.rs`'s `cfg(windows)` routine and
its case on the Linux host, check only. G1 and the lint probes run.
Three integration binaries run:
- `cli_verify`: the new stop table, plus every existing verify case, which holds the uninterrupted run byte-identical;
- `cli_version_gate`: `run`'s gate over the changed `run_bounded`;
- `contract_diag_schema`: the schema with the twelfth member.

A literal probe confirms the two moved literals are gone from product code. A preservation guard holds every other
file; it reads no `Cargo.toml` or `Cargo.lock` change. `cargo deny`, the harness smoke with G2 and G4, and the native
`pre-push` run. The operator pass fires hygiene, the push and the CI read (`leg = 'operator'`). The CI read is where
the `cfg(windows)` unit case and the macOS leg are read.

The criteria that name `ledger/stamps.json`, the run's dirs and `cli-<name>.ndjson` are asserted inside the step 8
cases, over each case's own test home, cwd and temp root, which the cases create and read themselves. No entry
produces them as a file a later entry reads, so no entry carries `artifact`.

No mutation entry, no witness run and no workflow dispatch is listed (`inputs#I1`). No entry is a live leg. Nothing
starts the real `claude`: the stop is proven against the fake agent, and the plan holds zero live starts
(`inputs#I1`). The guards name their base `d9f01b1b8642`, HEAD at P4, because the operator pass's pre-CI commit
moves HEAD onto the chunk.

body:
- (security / arch) On Unix, a `viola verify` against the fake agent stopped mid-run by `SIGINT`, and in a second case
  by `SIGTERM`, exits by itself. Afterwards none of that run's dirs remain: its `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>` dir, its
  `<home>/ledger/probes/<pid>/` and its Run A temp dir. The planted foreign `.viola-verify-0` and
  `.viola-verify-0-plan`, `viola-verify-foreign` and `ledger/probes/0/` remain unchanged. Nothing is removed by a
  pattern or a listing (per security-plan §Data Protection, Interactive probe dirs / Probe captures; per architecture
  §Occupied Resources → Filesystem).

- (layouts / design / a11y) The stopped run's stdout is empty: no step line and no `stamped` line. Its stderr is
  exactly the two lines of step 5, plain ASCII with no ESC and no CR. The exit is 1 (per layout-templates §Surface: cli,
  Output structure — `viola verify`; per design-system §Surface: cli → Per-Surface Bans, cli; per a11y-plan §1 Surface:
  cli → Notes; per architecture §Conventions, CLI exit codes; `inputs#I2`).

- (arch / tests) A stopped run writes no `ledger/stamps.json` (per architecture §Established Decisions [CLI Version
  Compatibility]; per test-plan §5 Integration Test Strategy, CLI).

- (obs) Under a `VIOLA_NAME`, the stopped run's `cli-<name>.ndjson` meets three conditions. It closes every spawn pair
  it opened. It ends with `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail:"interrupted"}`. It holds no `panic` line,
  and every line validates against `schemas/diag-line.v1.json`, whose `process-exit.detail` holds `interrupted` (per
  obs-plan §6 Log Coverage, Child / shell spawns and the `detail` code catalog; per obs-plan §9 CI Integration, G2 / G4;
  `inputs#I2`).

- (security) On the stop path no byte is written to a PTY child: every run ends by `Run::kill`. The child is ended and
  reaped before its dir is removed, and the pump wait observes no stop (per security-plan §Threat Model Summary,
  Attack surface: Child process spawning and PATH resolution). The step 7 `typed.rs` cases hold the order.

- (tests) On Windows, the console routine, called directly on `windows-2025`, stops for `CTRL_C_EVENT` and
  `CTRL_BREAK_EVENT` and leaves `CTRL_CLOSE_EVENT` to the OS default. Event delivery to a running verify on Windows is
  not claimed (per test-plan §11 Test Strategy; `inputs#I2`, the third answer).

- (arch / security) The uninterrupted run is unchanged: `binary(cli_verify)` reads `"ok":true` with its seventeen
  steps, stamp, six spawn pairs and no run dir left. `binary(cli_version_gate)` reads `"ok":true` over `run`'s gate.
  The literal probe reads `last line 0`: verify's default program is `PROGRAM` and Runs C and D's flag is
  `SETTINGS_FLAG`, byte-identical (per architecture §Occupied Resources → Claude Code integration names; per
  security-plan §Data Protection, Code-bearing artefacts).

- (arch / security) No dependency, feature, seam or environment variable is added. The preservation guard holds
  `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` and the fake agent, and `cargo deny check` reads green (per architecture §Infrastructure
  Patterns → Crate dependency direction; per security-plan §Dependency Security).

- (tests) `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --unit` reads `"ok":true`, and `pre-push` reads `"ok":true` at stage
  `linux-tests`. The CI-read entry reads `verdict: green` on HEAD across `windows-2025`, `macos-latest` and
  `ubuntu-latest`, and the report names the run id (per test-plan §10 Zero-flakiness budget; per test-plan §10
  Coverage thresholds).
- (tests) No mutation run, witness run, workflow dispatch or live `claude` start is made (`inputs#I1`).

No verification-matrix capability is claimed. Of the 37-id pool read at P4 (`matrix.py show --unclaimed`), none names
an interrupted verify. `v1-40` (CLI output discipline) needs `wait` / `last` / `list` escaping, the `waiting:` line
and `ui`'s launch line, all owned by other entries (its requirement, read with `show --id v1-40`). This matches the
handoff's note that the entry has no `requirements.md` line and no ledger entry.

- Research files inspected: `src/cmd/verify.rs`, `src/cmd/verify/typed.rs`, `src/run/version_gate.rs`,
  `src/main.rs`, `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs`, `tests/cli_verify.rs`, `tests/support/verify.rs`,
  `tests/support/cli.rs`, `Cargo.toml`, `schemas/diag-line.v1.json`, `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/lib.rs`,
  `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/statusline.rs`.

- Graph: `.andromeda/runs/2026-10-13T18-24-05-phase/tree-query-2026-10-13-interrupted-verify-cleanup.json` (one read,
  `db_state fresh`, 79 rows).

- The narrow entry is the founder's (CARRY, relayed as `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-10-self-healing-state/inputs/I4-relay-1.md.txt`). The three
  forms are the operator's answers at P4 (`inputs#I2`). The pair's wording is a planning form with the founder's wording
  owed, as with the board forms.

- Decisive leans:
  - **Every stopped run ends by kill with no key.** The basis is security-plan §Threat Model Summary: no byte goes into
    any dialog, and a modal start is killed with no key. A stop can land while any screen is up, and only a kill types
    nothing. Run B's founder-ruled Ctrl-C ending is its normal end, and it stays unchanged. The stop path is a new end,
    not a change to that ruling.
  - **The handler lives in the root package, verify-local.** It is the only process that installs it. `viola-pty`
    stays agent-agnostic and gains no process-wide disposition. The edge is already the root's (research.md §Measured
    facts 6).
  - **The stop is read once more after the interactive runs, never after `check_rows` begins.** Past that point the
    measurement is complete and the stamp write is atomic.
  - **A second Ctrl-C during the cleanup changes nothing.** The flag is already set. The cleanup's waits are the
    existing kill and pump join, which end at once after a kill (research.md §Measured facts 4). The stop path adds no
    bound.
  - **Sized against one window** (`inputs#I1`): one verb's stop path, about ten wait and ending sites in one file, one
    `run_bounded` input, one schema member, two literal moves, two integration cases and about eight unit cases. No
    split is proposed.

- **A crate such as `ctrlc` or `signal-hook`, or `tokio::signal`.** The existing `libc` / `windows-sys` edges carry the
  handler (research.md §Measured facts 6), and `tokio` is banned in sync crates (architecture §Cross-cutting
  Patterns, Tokio containment).

- **Removing anything by a pattern or a listing.** That rules out a glob of `viola-verify-*`, a `<pid>` scan, an older
  run's dir, another process's dir, an owner record or a SIGKILL / crash recovery (the founder's narrow entry, CARRY).
  The same-pid pre-clean in `ProbeDir::create` / `TrustedDir::create` predates the ruling and stands unchanged
  (research.md §Measured facts 8).
- **Typing Ctrl-C, or any byte, into a PTY child on the stop path** (security-plan §Threat Model Summary).

- **Making the pump wait after a kill (`ended_by` in `Run::finish`) observe the stop.** The dir would then be removed
  under a child that may still write into it.

- **Holding `CTRL_CLOSE_EVENT` (or logoff / shutdown) for cleanup.** The operator chose Ctrl-C and Ctrl-Break only
  (`inputs#I2`). The OS terminates the process about 5 s after a close handler starts.

- **A Windows integration case that delivers `CTRL_BREAK_EVENT` to a running verify.** It is not chosen (`inputs#I2`).
  Whether the runner's test process has a console is unmeasured.
- **A new exit code (130).** Exit 1 is inside architecture's set (`inputs#I2`).

- **A new fake-agent option or test seam to hold verify mid-run.** The existing flags without `--turn-stop` hold Run B
  in its turn wait (research.md §Measured facts 5). A new seam is a boundary widening (security-history
  `2026-09-28-hook-perf-gate`).

- **A `sleep` before the signal, a `kill()` after it, or a signal at a process the test did not start** (testing.md
  2026-10-10; test-plan §10 Coverage thresholds, the short-profile rule).

- **Changing verify's probes, texts, deadlines, order, stamps or ledger rows on an uninterrupted run, or any other
  verb's signal behaviour.**

- Mechanism, stated as the equality the cases need (research.md §Measured facts 4). With the stop set, a wait returns
  within one `POLL`: 5 ms in `typed.rs` (`:38`), 10 ms in `run_bounded` (`version_gate.rs:23`). The kill and the pump
  join then precede the guards' drop on the return. The frames that produce the asserted quantities are the polling
  loops, `Run::kill` (`typed.rs:675`) and the `Drop` impls (`verify.rs:304`, `typed.rs:363`, the `TempDir` at
  `typed.rs:68`).

- On Unix a terminal's Ctrl-C also reaches the `run_bounded` child, which shares verify's process group. The PTY
  children are their own session leaders and see no signal. Verify ends whichever child it is running
  (research.md §Measured facts 3).

- The case waits for the receipt's third `cwd` line and its first `prompt` line, and signals only then. At that point
  the UserPromptSubmit hook has already run and no hook is in flight, so the kill hangs up none (verification-harness.md,
  the fake agent's exit rule).

- A new `Instant::now() + WITHIN` wait in the stop case's receipt watch moves the registered count of root `WITHIN`
  sites, 28 in 20 files (the rule: the pattern `Instant::now() + WITHIN` under `tests/`, test-plan sidecar
  `2026-10-10-budget-governor`). Re-take it with that rule at the wrap; it is not counted here.

- A script that edits a `.rs` file runs `rustfmt` in the same call. Pipeline-tool output is redirected to a file and
  read whole (the handoff's standing rules). Every record time comes from `date -u` in the writing call (`inputs#I1`).

- Expected amendments (wrap):
  - architecture §Occupied Resources → Filesystem: Ctrl-C and TERM (Unix `SIGINT` / `SIGTERM`, Windows Ctrl-C /
    Ctrl-Break) are exit paths that remove the run's dirs. SIGKILL, a crash and a Windows close, logoff or shutdown
    leave them by hand.
  - architecture §Occupied Resources → Claude Code integration names: verify reads `PROGRAM` and `SETTINGS_FLAG`, and
    the clause that owes the move to this entry is retired.
  - architecture §Conventions, CLI exit codes: exit 1 covers an interrupted `verify`.
  - architecture §Infrastructure Patterns → Crate dependency direction: the root's `libc` (`sigaction`) and
    `windows-sys` (`SetConsoleCtrlHandler`) roles.
  - security-plan §Data Protection: Interactive probe dirs and Probe captures removed on a stop, with the stated
    exceptions; the Code-bearing artefacts clause owing the `--settings` move is retired.
  - obs-plan §6, the `detail` code catalog: `interrupted` on `process-exit` for `verify`, 12 schema members by the
    enum's rule, with its Decisions Log entry (the D-35/D-36 template).
  - obs-plan §4 Edge flows: the `verify` bullet's interrupted exit.
  - design-system §Surface: cli → Exit-code phraseology and Component Patterns 5: the interrupted pair, a planning form
    on the operator's word, the founder's wording owed (`inputs#I2`).
  - layout-templates §Surface: cli, Output structure — `viola verify`: the interrupted form beside exit 0 / 1.
  - a11y-plan §1 cli Notes and §8 Error recovery: the pair; the stop path adds no time bound.
  - test-plan §5 Integration Test Strategy, CLI (the `tests/cli_verify.rs` bullet): the stop table. Also the root
    `WITHIN` count, by its rule.
- For the founder's next batch: the pair's wording (`inputs#I2`).

**Date:** 2026-10-13 (wrap run `.andromeda/runs/2026-10-13T20-00-28-wrap/`)
**Commits:** `c22161e chore(2026-10-13-interrupted-verify-cleanup): operator pre-CI commit, for the run this chunk's verdict reads` (since `last_wrap` 2026-10-13T18:18:44Z; base `d9f01b1b8642`)

- **Files:** `src/cmd/verify/stop.rs` (new) · `src/cmd/verify.rs` · `src/cmd/verify/typed.rs` · `src/run/version_gate.rs` ·
  `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` · `tests/cli_verify.rs` · `tests/support/verify.rs` · `.github/workflows/windows-mutants.yml`
  (the out-of-list companion, see Deviations). Basis: `gate.py scope` — `clean — changed 8 · listed 7 · recorded 1`.

- **Symbols / APIs:**
  - **`cmd::verify::stop`** (`src/cmd/verify/stop.rs`, new, 1-119), the root package's one signal / console-control
    handler. Verify is the only verb that installs it; no other verb's signal behaviour changes.
    - `install()` (16-20), `stopped()` (22-25) and `set()` (27-30) over one process-global `AtomicBool`; the handler's
      only act is that store.
    - `stops_on(event)` (32-36), a plain decision: `0` (`CTRL_C_EVENT`) and `1` (`CTRL_BREAK_EVENT`) stop, every
      other event does not.
    - Unix (43-56): `on_signal` is installed for `SIGINT` and `SIGTERM` through `libc::sigaction` with `SA_RESTART`.
    - Windows (58-75): `console_routine`, through `windows-sys` `SetConsoleCtrlHandler`, returns TRUE with the flag
      set for Ctrl-C and Ctrl-Break, and FALSE for every other event (close, logoff, shutdown keep the OS default).
    - A failed install is ignored (fail-open). SIGKILL and a crash keep their default and leave the dirs by hand.
  - **`src/cmd/verify.rs`**:
    - `enum Ended { Exit(u8), Interrupted }` (85-89).
    - `verify` (69-78) prints the pair `unable: verify was stopped before it finished` / `hint: run viola verify again
      to stamp this CLI` through `human::refuse`, logs `run::log_self_exit(1, Some("interrupted"))` under a
      `VIOLA_NAME`, and exits 1.
    - `measure` installs the stop as its first act. It reads the stop at the version probe's end (179-181), at the
      print probe's end (204-206), when `typed::measure` returns `None` (228-230), and once more after the probe dir
      is dropped, before `check_rows` (242-244). After that the run completes as before.
    - The default program reads `viola_agent_claude::PROGRAM`.
    - `run_logged` passes `stop::stopped` to `run_bounded`; the spawn pair is unchanged. A stopped child's
      `process-exit` carries `duration_ms` and no `child_exit_status`.
  - **`src/run/version_gate.rs`**:
    - `run_bounded` gains a sixth input, `stopped: fn() -> bool`, read before the child's exit on every 10 ms poll.
      At the stop it kills and reaps the child (`fn end`, 85-88).
    - `Bounded` gains `stopped: bool`, which tells the stop from the deadline's kill.
    - Two callers remain: verify's `run_logged` and `run`'s `version_gate`. The latter passes `never_stopped`, so
      `run`'s gate is unchanged in behaviour.
  - **`src/cmd/verify/typed.rs`**:
    - `Inputs` gains `stop: fn() -> bool`. `measure` returns `Option<TypedRun>` (`None` = stopped) and runs the four
      runs in one loop with one stop read before each (78-89, `RunStep`); Run A is now `untrusted_run`.
    - One polling function, `poll_until(clock, until, stopped, found)` (217-225), serves `wait_for` (241-249),
      `wait_capture` (both gain a stop input), `Run::settle`, `Run::box_wait`, and the two waits of
      `end_by_ctrl_c`.
    - `ctrl_c_ending` gains `stopped`: with the stop set it sends no Ctrl-C (or no second one) and goes to the kill.
    - `Run::paste_text` (690-693) refuses a paste once the stop is set.
    - The pump wait after a kill, `ended_by` in `Run::finish`, does NOT observe the stop.
    - Runs C and D's `--settings` read `viola_agent_claude::statusline::SETTINGS_FLAG`.
  - **Interfaces:** no IPC method, endpoint, event kind, port, socket or env var is added.

   attached to that console, `viola verify` and its `run_bounded` child; the ConPTY children are attached to their
   pseudo console (`viola-pty`). So in every case verify itself must end the child it is running.

4. **The equality the stop needs**: with a stop flag set while verify is inside any of its waits, the wait returns
   within one `POLL` (5 ms in `typed.rs`, 10 ms in `run_bounded`); the run then ends its child by `Run::kill` (no key)
   and `finish` (pump joined within `PROBE_DEADLINE`, in practice at once after a kill: the child's PTY reaches EOF);
   `measure` returns before `check_rows`, so no step line, no `stamped` line and no `update_stamps` call; the guards drop
   in reverse order on that return. Producing frames: `typed.rs:195`/`:328`/`:559`/`:639`/`:655` (the loops),
   `:675`/`:684` (the kill), `verify.rs:209`–`:214` (drop, then stamp).

5. **A deterministic stop point exists with no new fake-agent option**: with `--screens` and the workspace as trusted
   root but without `--turn-stop`, Run B pastes the probe prompt, the fake agent fires UserPromptSubmit and writes its
   `prompt` receipt (`viola-fake-agent.rs:568`, `:579`) and fires no Stop (`:574`), so verify waits in
   `wait_capture(Stop)` (`typed.rs:242`) for up to `PROBE_DEADLINE` (120 s). A test that waits for the receipt's third
   `cwd` line and its first `prompt` line has an observed event, then signals the pid it started. No hook is in flight
   then (the UserPromptSubmit hook ran before the `prompt` receipt was written), so the kill hangs up no hook mid-exit.

6. **Windows reach**: the root package's `windows-sys` inherits the workspace feature list, which holds
   `Win32_System_Console` (`Cargo.toml:160`, `:232`); `libc` is the root's Unix dependency (`:164`). No manifest line and
   no `Cargo.lock` package is added by a handler on either OS. Architecture's crate-direction text names the root's
   `windows-sys` roles without the console (arch-history `2026-09-28-capability-ledger-and-viola-verify`): a wrap
   amendment, not a code change.

7. **The two literals**: `PROGRAM` and `SETTINGS_FLAG` hold exactly `claude` and `--settings`, each pinned by a literal
   case in its crate, and both are `pub` (`viola_agent_claude::PROGRAM` already read by `src/cmd/revive.rs:10`,
   `SETTINGS_FLAG` by `src/run/mod.rs:18`). Reading them changes no byte of any argv. VERIFIED.

8. **Same-pid pre-clean**: `ProbeDir::create` (`verify.rs:263`) and `TrustedDir::create` (`typed.rs:356`) remove a path
   of this run's own name (`<pid>`) before creating it. That is a leftover of an earlier process that had the same pid,
   removed by name. It predates the founder's narrow ruling (chunk 2026-10-05-real-cli-verify-probes) and this chunk

9. **Log shape**: `process-exit.detail` is closed at 11 values (fact above). An interrupted-run `detail` would be the
   twelfth: a `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` change plus an obs Decisions Log entry at the wrap (obs-history
   `2026-09-29-sideloaded-conpty`, the D-35/D-36 template). `exit_source: "kill-fallback"` is a `run`-PTY field; the
   verify-pty-probe exits already log a killed run as `duration_ms` without `child_exit_status`

- `src/cmd/verify/stop.rs` — the stop flag and its per-OS handler installation for `viola verify` (Unix SIGINT and
  SIGTERM, Windows console control events), with its inline unit cases.

- `src/cmd/verify.rs` — installs the stop before the first child, reads `PROGRAM`, ends an interrupted run before the step lines and the stamp with its exit and line, the stop observed by the bounded children.

title: 1. Ctrl-C and TERM end a verify run cleanly (the entry; CARRY, the founder's word)

data.head: ### 1. Ctrl-C and TERM end a verify run cleanly (the entry; CARRY, the founder's word)

body:
- The founder's narrow entry (CARRY, live in the overseer's dialog 2026-10-10T10:26:30Z, «Узкая запись», relayed as
  `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-10-self-healing-state/inputs/I4-relay-1.md.txt`): `viola verify` handles Ctrl-C and TERM and removes only what it
  created in that run, nothing older and nothing foreign; what a SIGKILL or a crash leaves stays by hand. **No owner
  record and no remover of an earlier run's dirs is built here.**

- On either stop the run ends its PTY child (no key typed into any dialog — security-plan's standing rule for verify's
  children), lets its directory guards remove what this run made, and exits. The order is child ended and reaped
  first, then the removal: a dir is not removed under a live child writing into it (verified, research.md §Measured
  facts 4: every wait is a `POLL` loop a stop flag ends within one `POLL`; the run's `kill` + `finish` precede the
  guards' drop on the return).

- [premise-corrected: research.md §Measured facts 3 — every OS-level reach was read; the Windows event set is not
  settled by any artifact] "Ctrl-C and TERM" per OS: Unix `SIGINT` and `SIGTERM` (a terminal Ctrl-C reaches verify and
  its `run_bounded` child, never a PTY child; a `kill <pid>` reaches verify alone). Windows: `CTRL_C_EVENT` and
  `CTRL_BREAK_EVENT` reach verify and its `run_bounded` child, never a ConPTY child; whether `CTRL_CLOSE_EVENT` also
  counts as TERM is a P4 fork. In every case verify itself ends the child it is running.

- [premise-corrected: research.md §Measured facts 4, 9 — architecture §Conventions, design-system and layout-templates
  hold no form for an interrupted run] An interrupted run writes no stamp and prints no step line and no `stamped`
  line: the stop returns from `measure` before `check_rows` and `update_stamps` (verified, by construction at
  `verify.rs:209`–`:214`). Its exit status (inside the defined set or a new code), its stderr lines and its
  `process-exit` `detail` (none, or a twelfth closed member) are a P4 fork; none is invented here.

- [premise-corrected: research.md §Measured facts 6 — the root's `windows-sys` inherits `Win32_System_Console` from the
  workspace feature list] No new dependency, no manifest line and no `Cargo.lock` package: `libc` (root, Unix) and
  `windows-sys` (root, Windows, the workspace features) carry the handler. Architecture's crate-direction text, which
  names the root's `windows-sys` roles without the console, is a wrap amendment.

- **Marker:** 2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows · **Version:** viola-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-13T22:58Z

The statusline settings override, the `/bin/sh` shell and the statusline payload's `rate_limits` become three probed,
stamped capability-ledger rows (`v1-34`), the cut the founder chose for this entry (`inputs#I1`, fork 1). `rate_limits`
is the one owed shape a shipped refusal rests on: the budget gate refuses a driver's `send` as `budget-paused` on it
(security history 2026-10-13-t06-38-35-wrap). All three are measured from Run B's own session. Run B is started with a
probe `--settings` document. Its `statusLine` command is the pinned `viola` with a new hidden `hook statusline
--capture` arm. That arm files each payload and a closed verdict on the shell that ran the command. This is a boundary
widening of the founder-ratified verify child set, and his own answer to fork 3 (`inputs#I1`). It adds no `claude`
start (research.md §Measured facts 3, 9).

The three rows are relied on only where the status line is wrapped: Unix, where `run` writes the override and `hook
statusline` shells out (`statusline::WRAPPED_HERE`, `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/statusline.rs:21`). So a Unix host
checks, prints and stamps 21 rows, and a Windows host the 18 it checks today. The step counter and the stamp verdict
read the set relied on this OS (per architecture §Established Decisions [CLI Version Compatibility]; per
security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Universal). The fake agent replays the recorded statusline payloads under
`--framing`. One live round on `claude` 2.1.287 records the two variants. One `run --local-live` round reads the
twenty-one rows live. That is ten starts, the founder's cap (`inputs#I1`, fork 4).

The other three shapes leave this entry by his answers. `--resume` and `/compact` go to a new entry directly after this
one, and the `claude agents --json` join row goes onto its consumer, "Unwrapped sessions on the board" (`inputs#I1`,
forks 1 and 2; the review card's `## Beyond the plan`). `v1-34` is not claimed: its harness-prefix and R8
identity-floor rows stay owed with no entry.

1. **The rows and the relied set** (`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs`). Append three members to `LedgerRow`
   after `PasteNewline`, in this order:
   - `StatusLineOverride`: id `statusline-override`, words `a --settings statusLine runs in the status line's place`;
   - `StatusLineShell`: id `statusline-shell`, words `a statusline command runs through /bin/sh`;
   - `StatusLineRateLimits`: id `statusline-rate-limits`, words `the statusline payload carries two whole-number rate_limits windows`.

   `ALL` becomes `[Self; 21]`. Add `LedgerRow::relied_here(self) -> bool`: false for the three on an OS where the status
   line is not wrapped, true otherwise. Read the same cfg as `statusline::WRAPPED_HERE`, exposed as a `pub const` or
   fn of the `statusline` module, never a second `cfg!`. Add `pub fn relied() -> Vec<LedgerRow>`: `ALL` filtered by
   it, in `ALL` order.

   The stamp verdict (`ledger.rs:957`, today `LedgerRow::ALL.iter().all(…)`) reads `relied()`.

   Add a closed `ShellVerdict { BinSh, Other }` with the file words `bin-sh` and `other`. Add `StatusLineCapture
   { bytes: Vec<u8>, shell: ShellVerdict }` and a `statusline: Vec<StatusLineCapture>` field on `Probes`.

2. **The three check arms** (`ledger.rs`, `check`). Each arm reads `probes.statusline`:
   - `StatusLineOverride` passes when at least one capture exists.
   - `StatusLineShell` passes when at least one exists and every capture's `shell` is `BinSh`.
   - `StatusLineRateLimits` passes when some capture's bytes parse as one JSON object whose `rate_limits` holds
     `five_hour` and `seven_day` objects, each with a `used_percentage` that is a JSON integer in 0–100 and a
     `resets_at` that is a JSON non-negative integer. This is the whole-number shape read on 2.1.287 (scope §5). It is
     narrower than `statusline::reading`, which also takes an RFC 3339 string and a fraction: the row stamps what the
     CLI sends, not what the gate tolerates.

   Write three named unit cases per row: `check_statusline_override_`, `check_statusline_shell_`,
   `check_statusline_rate_limits_` prefixes, nine in all. Each row gets: pass on the recorded shape, fail on the broken
   post-condition (a shell `Other` among `BinSh`; a window missing, a fractional percentage, a string `resets_at`;
   there is no third shape for the override row), and fail with no capture. Write them before the arms.

   Add a unit case on `relied()`: twenty-one ids on Unix, eighteen on Windows (`cfg`-split asserts, literals).

3. **The probe document and the file names** (pure). In `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/statusline.rs`, add
   `pub fn probe_document(pinned_bin_fwd: &str, captures_dir_fwd: &str) -> Option<String>`. On a wrapped OS, and only
   when both strings are made only of `is_shell_plain` characters, it returns `{"statusLine":{"type":"command",
   "command":"<pinned> hook statusline --capture <dir> --shell \"$0\""}}`; otherwise `None`. Add `pub const
   SHELL_FLAG: &str = "--shell"` and `pub const BIN_SH: &str = "/bin/sh"`. Unit cases:
   - the command string, byte for byte;
   - `None` for a non-plain pinned path and for a non-plain captures dir;
   - `None` where the status line is not wrapped (through the existing `_on(…, wrapped)` pattern).

   In `ledger.rs`, add `statusline_capture_file_name(k) -> "StatusLine.<k>.json"`, its shell sibling
   `"StatusLine.<k>.shell"`, and their parser, beside `capture_file_name`.

4. **The capture arm** (`src/cmd/hook.rs`). Add to `HookArgs` a hidden `--shell <WORD>` option. When `args.event ==
   statusline::WORD` and `args.capture` is `Some`, take a new arm before the pass-through:
   - The dir must be absolute and an existing directory; else exit 0 with nothing written.
   - stdin is read through `take(MAX_FRAME + 1)`.
   - The payload is filed under the first free `StatusLine.<k>.json` through the same `create_private_new` claim and
     `replace_private` 0600 as `file_from`.
   - The sibling `StatusLine.<k>.shell` holds exactly `bin-sh` when the `--shell` word equals `statusline::BIN_SH`
     byte for byte, else `other`. A missing word is `other`. The word itself is written nowhere.
   - Nothing is printed. Exit 0 on every path. No `VIOLA_*` read, no obs init, no channel, no `budget.json`, no
     snapshot read.

   `--shell` with any other arm changes nothing. `hook statusline` without `--capture` keeps today's pass-through
   unchanged. Cases go in `tests/hook_fail_open.rs`, beside the capture arm's own cases:
   - a payload and `/bin/sh` → the two files at 0600, empty stdout, exit 0;
   - `sh`, an empty word and no word → `other`;
   - a relative or missing dir → nothing filed, exit 0;
   - an over-cap stdin → nothing filed, exit 0;
   - `VIOLA_NAME` set → no role file.

5. **Run B gains the probe settings** (`src/cmd/verify.rs`, `src/cmd/verify/typed.rs`).
   - `ProbeDir::create` makes `typed/statusline/` (0700, `create_private_dir`).
   - When `statusline::probe_document(pinned, fwd(typed/statusline))` is `Some`, write it to `typed/statusline.json`
     (0600, `replace_private`).
   - `typed::Inputs` gains `statusline_settings: Option<&Path>`.
   - `trusted_run` appends `SETTINGS_FLAG` and that path after its `--plugin-dir` pair when it is `Some`, and nothing
     when it is `None` (Windows).

   No other run changes and no new run is added. Runs A, C and D keep their arguments: Runs C and D keep their one
   `--settings`, and Run B has one at most. After the runs, `measure` reads `typed/statusline/` in `k` order with
   `take(MAX_FRAME + 1)` per file into `Probes.statusline`; an unreadable or absent shell file reads `Other`.
   `check_rows` walks `LedgerRow::relied()`, and the step line's `total` is its length (`check_rows @
   src/cmd/verify.rs:390`, `measure @ :246`). The `ProbeDir` drop guard already removes `typed/` whole. Cases:
   - `ProbeDir` makes `typed/statusline/` and, on Unix, `typed/statusline.json` naming the probe command;
   - the step-line case at the relied total.

6. **Recording the variants** (`src/cmd/verify.rs`, `ledger.rs`). Add a pure `statusline_variants(&[StatusLineCapture])
   -> Vec<(String, &[u8])>`:
   - `StatusLine.default-1.json` is the first capture whose payload holds no `rate_limits`;
   - `StatusLine.rate-limits-1.json` is the first that passes the rate-limits arm.

   `named_payloads @ src/cmd/verify.rs:459` adds them to what `record` scrubs, refuses on `unclean` and writes only
   at 0 failing rows, as every variant today. Unit case: the two names from a three-capture list (none, none, with),
   and none from an empty list.

7. **The version gate** (`src/run/version_gate.rs`). The verdict reads `relied()` (step 1). The older-stamp oracle
   (`:299`, `:305`) gains a case: a stamp holding exactly the eighteen pre-chunk ids, all `pass`, reads unverified on
   Unix and verified on Windows (`cfg`-split, literals).

8. **The fake agent** (`src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs`). Under `--framing`, when `--settings <file>` names a settings
   file whose `statusLine.command` is absolute (`statusline_words`, `:337`), fire that command twice:
   - once after the launch SessionStart's hooks, with the bytes of the set's `StatusLine.default-1.json`;
   - once after the first Stop's hooks, with the bytes of `StatusLine.rate-limits-1.json`.

   The command is split on ASCII white space, and the one word exactly `"$0"` (with its two quotes) is handed over as
   `/bin/sh`. That is the launch measured on 2.1.287 (chunk 2026-10-10-statusline-pass-through,
   `evidence/live-statusline.md`, Start 1). It is never run through a shell. Each firing writes a `statusline` receipt
   with `stdin_hex`. A set without the two variants fires nothing, so the rows fail, as a set without framing variants
   must.

   No new option: the `--settings` + `--statusline-stdin` path stays as it is, and the new path needs `--framing`.
   Unit cases: the two firings and their order; the `"$0"` word handed over as `/bin/sh` and any other word unchanged;
   nothing fired without `--framing`, without the variants or for a relative command.

9. **The statusline fixture schema** (`schemas/claude-statusline-fixture.v1.json`, new). A tolerant object schema with
   `session_id` required as a string; `rate_limits`, when present, is an object whose `five_hour` and `seven_day` are
   objects. `tests/contract_fixture_hygiene.rs` validates every `fixtures/claude/*/StatusLine.*.json` against it and
   every other file against `claude-fixture.v1.json`, as today, with the same path, username and email walk. A
   planted `StatusLine` file with no `session_id` reads red.

10. **The pinned readers** (literals, never `LedgerRow::ALL`; testing.md 2026-10-07: list them by the function they
    decide):
    - `tests/cli_verify.rs`: `STEPS_PASS`, `ROW_IDS`, the summaries and the partial-failure shapes at twenty-one on
      Unix and eighteen on Windows. Each partial-failure shape is re-derived from the fake agent's options:
      - a run without `--framing` also fails the three statusline rows on Unix;
      - the dialog-less run reads its four dialog rows failing.
    - `tests/contract_ledger_probes.rs`: `ROW_IDS` and the 2.1.287 summary.
    - `tests/support/home.rs`: the dialog-less summary (`:376`, `:386`).
    - `tests/support/verify.rs`: `framing_set` gains synthetic `StatusLine.default-1.json` / `StatusLine.rate-limits-1.json`
      for the synthetic version.
    - `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run.rs`: `LEDGER_ROWS` and `LIVE_PASS` per OS.
    - `tests/contract_fake_agent_drift.rs`: replays the two variants byte for byte as the `statusline` receipt's
      `stdin_hex`.

11. **The live round** (one record round, 5 starts: print, Runs A–D). The block's probe, record and census entries,
    fired once by `gate.py run --live-legs`; a red is reported, never re-fired. The record entry copies the two
    `StatusLine` variants alone into `fixtures/claude/2.1.287/`; every other committed fixture keeps its bytes.

12. **The live-suite round** (5 starts). `run --local-live` with the 2.1.287 install dir first on `PATH`
    (verification-harness.md 2026-10-10), reading the twenty-one rows from a fresh live home. Fired once; a red is
    reported, never re-fired. The two rounds are the cap of ten (`inputs#I1`, fork 4).
- `schemas/claude-statusline-fixture.v1.json` — the statusline payload fixture schema (step 9)
- `fixtures/claude/2.1.287/StatusLine.default-1.json` — recorded live, copied alone from the record round (step 11)
- `fixtures/claude/2.1.287/StatusLine.rate-limits-1.json` — recorded live, copied alone from the record round (step 11)
- `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows/evidence/` — `live-round.md`

- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs` — the three rows, `relied_here` / `relied`, `ShellVerdict`, `StatusLineCapture`, `Probes.statusline`, the arms, `statusline_variants`, the file names, the verdict at `:957`, the unit cases (`LedgerRow::ALL` read at `check_rows @ src/cmd/verify.rs:390`, `src/run/version_gate.rs:205`)
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/statusline.rs` — `probe_document`, `SHELL_FLAG`, `BIN_SH`, the wrapped-here reading made public, the cases
- `src/cmd/hook.rs` — `HookArgs` `--shell`, the statusline capture arm
- `src/cmd/verify.rs` — `ProbeDir`'s `typed/statusline/` and `statusline.json`, the capture read, `check_rows` over `relied()`, `named_payloads`, the step-line cases
- `src/cmd/verify/typed.rs` — `Inputs.statusline_settings`, `trusted_run`'s one `--settings` (one caller: `measure @ typed.rs:72`)
- `src/run/version_gate.rs` — the verdict over `relied()`, the older-stamp case
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs` — the `--framing` statusline replay and its cases
- `tests/hook_fail_open.rs` — the statusline capture arm's cases

- `tests/cli_verify.rs`, `tests/contract_ledger_probes.rs`, `tests/contract_fixture_hygiene.rs`, `tests/contract_fake_agent_drift.rs`, `tests/support/home.rs`, `tests/support/verify.rs` — literals per OS, the schema split, the replay
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run.rs` — `LEDGER_ROWS` and `LIVE_PASS` per OS

The standing lint and unit entries run first, then the nine row cases by name. The live round follows, fired once by
`gate.py run --live-legs` and never re-run by the wrap (re-verified from `evidence/live-round.md`):
- the non-priming probe;
- the record entry (5 starts: print, Runs A–D);
- the census;
- a second probe;
- the `run --local-live` entry (5 starts);
- a second census.

The record entry regenerates committed fixtures, so it precedes every entry that reads them: the fixture guard, the
integration binaries, the harness smoke and `pre-push`. No entry produces `evidence/live-round.md` and none reads it:
step 13 writes it from the logs, and the record entry's `contains stamped 2.1.287  21 pass  0 fail` and the fixture
guard assert the round on every re-run of the block.

No count-literal probe is listed. The predecessor's "no old count left" probe cannot hold here, because Windows keeps
eighteen by design (step 1). The Linux integration entry reads every Unix literal, and CI's `windows-2025` leg reads
every Windows one. No mutation entry, witness run or workflow dispatch is listed. The guards name their base
`14e62329f808`.

body:
- (arch) `LedgerRow::ALL` holds twenty-one rows, the last three in order `statusline-override`, `statusline-shell`,
  `statusline-rate-limits`. `relied()` holds all twenty-one on Unix and the first eighteen on Windows. The stamp
  verdict reads `relied()`. On Unix, a stamp holding only the eighteen pre-chunk ids, all `pass`, reads unverified;
  on Windows the same stamp reads verified (`bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --unit`) (per architecture §Established
  Decisions [CLI Version Compatibility]).

- (tests) `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --unit --filter 'test(/check_statusline_/)'` reads 9 passed, 0 failed. Each
  row passes on its recorded shape and fails on its broken post-condition (a shell verdict `other`, a fractional
  percentage, a string `resets_at`, a missing window) and with no capture (per test-plan §4 Unit Test Strategy,
  viola-agent-claude).

- (security) Run B carries exactly one `--settings`: the probe document. Its `statusLine` command is the pinned
  absolute `viola` with `hook statusline --capture <dir> --shell "$0"`, written only for shell-plain paths and only
  where the status line is wrapped. No other run's argv changes, no run is added, and no byte is typed into a dialog.
  The widening is the founder's own answer to P4 fork 3 (`inputs#I1`) (per security-plan §Threat Model Summary,
  Attack surface: Child process spawning and PATH resolution).

- (security) The capture arm files each payload raw at 0600 through `take(MAX_FRAME + 1)` and its shell verdict as
  exactly `bin-sh` or `other`; the shell word itself is written nowhere. It prints nothing, exits 0 on every path,
  reads no `VIOLA_*` and opens no role file (`tests/hook_fail_open.rs` in the integration entry) (per security-plan
  §Input Validation, the Hook stdin row).

- (tests) One record round on `claude` 2.1.287 (exactly five starts, fired once) prints
  `stamped 2.1.287  21 pass  0 fail`, and its census finds no probe-dir `claude` left. One `run --local-live` round
  (exactly five starts, fired once) reads `"suite":"local-live","passed":1,"failed":0`, and its census finds none.
  Both are recorded in `evidence/live-round.md` (per test-plan §3 `run`; per test-plan §7 Seed strategies; the
  founder's cap, `inputs#I1`).

- (tests) `fixtures/claude/2.1.287/` gains exactly `StatusLine.default-1.json` and `StatusLine.rate-limits-1.json` and
  no other change (the fixture guard). `contract_ledger_probes` stamps the 2.1.287 set at the relied count with each
  literal row id once. `contract_fake_agent_drift` replays both variants byte for byte. `contract_fixture_hygiene`
  validates them against `schemas/claude-statusline-fixture.v1.json` and walks them for paths, usernames and emails
  (the integration entry) (per test-plan §5 Integration Test Strategy; per test-plan §7 Fixture hygiene).

- (design / layouts / a11y) `viola verify` over a complete set prints one `[NN/MM] <row id> <row words>  pass|fail`
  line per relied row, in `ALL` order, with MM the relied count (21 on this host). It then prints
  `stamped <ver>  <n> pass  <m> fail` with n + m = MM, plain ASCII with no SGR byte, and the interrupted pair stays
  byte-identical (`tests/cli_verify.rs`) (per design-system §Surface: cli §Component Patterns, pattern 5 `verify`; per
  layout-templates §Output structure — `viola verify`; per a11y-plan §4 Critical Paths P6).

- (obs) A verify run still writes six spawn pairs (no run added), every subject in the closed enum and every line
  schema-valid. No line carries the probe command, a statusline payload or a path. The capture arm writes no line
  (`tests/cli_verify.rs`, G4) (per obs-plan §4 Edge flows → `verify` / `plugin install`; per obs-plan §10 SLO
  Invariants, bounded exemption 5).

- (tests) The harness's `LEDGER_ROWS` names twenty-one ids on Unix and eighteen on Windows, and its `LIVE_PASS` unit
  proof reads them (`run --unit`) (per test-plan §3 `run`).

- (security) No new dependency, `cargo deny check` passes, `send` and the statusline pass-through arm are untouched,
  and no file outside the modify set changes (the preservation guard) (per security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns →
  Code Patterns).

- (tests) The pushed HEAD's CI run reads `verdict: green` on all three OSes, the Windows leg at eighteen rows (the
  operator's CI entry).

- Spec anchors: architecture §Established Decisions [CLI Version Compatibility], §Cross-cutting Patterns (Capability
  ledger), §Infrastructure Patterns → Crate dependency direction, §Occupied Resources (Repository); security-plan
  §Threat Model Summary (child spawning), §Security Anti-Patterns → Universal and → Code Patterns, §Input Validation
  (Hook stdin row; Statusline shell-out row), §Data Protection (Repository fixtures; Interactive probe dirs);
  test-plan §3 `run`, §4, §5, §7; obs-plan §4 Edge flows → `verify`, §6, §8, §10; design-system §Surface: cli
  pattern 5; layout-templates §Output structure — `viola verify`; a11y-plan §4 P6, §8.

- Research files inspected: research.md §Files inspected (sixteen reads), plus `src/cmd/hook.rs:30`–`:60`,
  `:367`–`:392`, `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs:80`–`:125`, `:337`, `:476`, `schemas/claude-fixture.v1.json`,
  `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run.rs:354`–`:395` and chunk 2026-10-08-first-live-test-and-self-drive's plan `:509`–`:517`
  at P4.

- Leaned (decisive, per `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/statusline.rs:20`–`:21`: "no Windows reading of the shell
  exists", `WRAPPED_HERE = cfg!(unix)`; per security-plan's statusline override "none on Windows"): the three rows are
  relied on only where the status line is wrapped. Shipping them on Windows would read `fail` there forever and leave
  every Windows home unverified and transport-only. Passing them there would print `pass` for a shape never
  measured. The step counter's MM becomes the relied count, an expected amendment.

- Leaned (decisive, per test-plan §7 Fake agent: "never through a shell"; per the 2.1.287 live reading of the launch,
  chunk 2026-10-10-statusline-pass-through `evidence/live-statusline.md` Start 1: "`/bin/sh`, on all three"): the fake
  agent hands the `"$0"` word over as `/bin/sh` and runs no shell. The live round is what stamps the real CLI's shell.

- Leaned (decisive, per research.md §Measured facts 3 and the founder's fork 3): Run B's probe settings go in a
  0600 file under its own probe dir, `typed/statusline.json`, as `run` passes its override (`--settings <instance
  dir>/settings.json`). The fake agent's `--settings` takes a file path (`src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs:124`).

- Mechanism (check 8): the shell verdict reaches the check through the CLI's own expansion of `"$0"`, read as
  `/bin/sh` on 2.1.287 in two live starts (`evidence/live-statusline.md`, Starts 1 and 2). The arm compares the word
  byte for byte with `statusline::BIN_SH`. `rate_limits` was absent on a session's first payload and present after a
  turn in both readings (research.md §Measured facts 7), and Run B types a turn and four pastes before its Ctrl-C
  (`typed.rs:138`–`:140`).
- A separate statusline run (Run E): rejected by the founder's fork 3 (`inputs#I1`). It would cost a start per round.

- A second `--settings` on Runs C or D: the probe document goes on Run B alone, so which of two flags wins stays
  unmeasured and unrelied (scope §3).
- Capturing the shell word as text: only the closed verdict is filed (the founder's fork-3 preview, `inputs#I1`).

- Routing the statusline capture through `HookEvent` or the `--answers` path: the arm is its own, beside them
  (security history 2026-09-28-capability-ledger-and-viola-verify; research.md §Measured facts 5).

- Running a shell anywhere in viola for the probe, or in the fake agent: `statusline_command` stays the only
  shell-out (security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Code Patterns).

- Writing or reading `~/.claude/settings.json`, `budget.json` or a snapshot in the probe: viola writes nothing under
  `~/.claude` (security-plan §Threat Model Summary).

- A hand-written `StatusLine` fixture, or the whole re-recorded set copied: the fake agent invents no shape before a
  recorded fixture (test-plan §7), and every other committed fixture keeps its bytes (the fixture guard).

- `--resume`, `/compact` and `claude agents --json` rows: moved off this entry by the founder's forks 1 and 2
  (`inputs#I1`).

- Any change to `send`, `typed_text`, `validate_paste_text`, the paste write, the budget gate or `hook statusline`'s
  pass-through: this chunk measures what they rely on and changes nothing about them.

- Raising a nextest kill line if a verify-driven case slows by the two fake-agent statusline firings: measure, then
  remove the slow work (testing.md 2026-09-28).

- A new fake-agent option, env seam or `config.json` key: the replay rides `--framing` (architecture §Cross-cutting
  Patterns, Config management).

- A second live round of either kind, a rehearsal start, or any other `claude` start: the cap is ten (`inputs#I1`). A
  red round is reported, never re-fired.

- The sites of step 10 are research's sweep (research.md §Sweeps): 80 hits of
  `18\]|; 18\]|18 pass|\[&str; 18\]|eighteen|/18\b` in six files, plus the dialog-less summary's three hits of
  `14 pass|4 fail`. Every Unix literal moves to twenty-one, and every Windows literal keeps eighteen under a `cfg`
  split.

- The two fake-agent statusline firings add two short `viola hook` spawns to every stamped-home verify. Read the
  integration entry's durations and record them.

- The live round's homes sit under the tmpfs backing; record where they stand after the rounds. A removal the
  permission layer denies is moved into `target/e2e-home.disk/`, never done another way (the handoff's standing rule).
- Every UTC time written into an evidence record comes from `date -u` in the writing call.

- Expected amendments (wrap): architecture §Occupied Resources (Repository) — the two `StatusLine` variants in the
  2.1.287 set (its file count with its rule); `schemas/claude-statusline-fixture.v1.json`.

- Expected amendments (wrap): security-plan §Threat Model Summary / §Data Protection (the verify child-set bullet)
  and §Input Validation (Hook stdin row) — Run B's probe `--settings` and the `hook statusline --capture --shell` arm.
  The playbook pattern is "Boundary widening the founder answered himself to a P4 fork" (escalate), the founder's own
  answer relayed by the operator (`inputs#I1`). §Security Anti-Patterns → Universal: a non-`null` decision needs
  every relied row.

- Expected amendments (wrap): obs-plan §10 (bounded exemption 5) — the statusline capture is inside the hidden
  capture arm: no obs init, no line.

- Expected amendments (wrap): design-system §Surface: cli pattern 5 — MM is the relied count (21 Unix, 18 Windows),
  and the three rows are named.

- Expected amendments (wrap): layout-templates §Output structure — `viola verify` — the row list, MM with its rule,
  and the worked example at twenty-one.

- `v1-34` is not claimed. Its not-claimed note is written at phase P5 step 4, not by the wrap: three rows land at
  twenty-one, the harness-prefix and R8 rows stay owed with no entry, and `--resume` / `/compact` / `agents --json`
  move.

and the `claude agents --json` row moved off this entry by the founder's forks (`inputs#I1`)

- The CARRY's own marker, kept verbatim: "hypothesis: the send waited for a `prompt-submitted` that a local command

- An owed row with its `viola verify` probe: a `statusLine` given through `--settings <file>` takes the status line's

title: 4. The Unix shell `/bin/sh` (CARRY 4, the same block)

data.head: ### 4. The Unix shell `/bin/sh` (CARRY 4, the same block)

body:

  `/bin/sh`. Read by hand on 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host (same evidence). The recorder that reads which shell ran,
  by three quoted words, is that chunk's `evidence/live-recorder.sh`.
- Not measured: the flag the CLI hands its shell. Windows has no `/bin/sh` arm (the override is not written there).

- The `rate_limits` ledger row and its `viola verify` probe. The wrapper's budget gate refuses an automated `send` as
  `budget-paused` on this shape, outside the ruled limit "a shape no `send` relies on needs no probe". The founder's
  own answer (Epoch 4 boundary batch, 2026-10-13, relayed verbatim by the Viola overseer, «Строку к Paste newline
  ledger row»): the build stays as it is, and the row and its probe join this entry.

- The shape: `rate_limits` with `five_hour` and `seven_day`, each a whole-number `used_percentage` and a whole-number
  `resets_at` read as epoch seconds (read by hand on 2.1.287, chunk 2026-10-10-statusline-pass-through's
  `evidence/live-statusline.md`).

- The CARRY's own marker, kept verbatim: "hypothesis: `rate_limits` arrives from the second payload of a session on,
  not only after the first API response as the fetched documentation says (one live start: present 0.35 s after the
  first payload; cause not known)." Not re-derivable at HEAD (a CLI behaviour; no live start at research): it stays the
  hypothesis it is. What a probe may lean on is narrower and was read twice: absent on a session's first payload,
  present after a turn (research.md §Measured facts 7).

- Not measured: an account without `rate_limits`, the `spend_limit` window, the real `claude` against the gate. A
  drift in `resets_at` opens the gate for that window (fail-open). The masters name this entry (architecture
  §Cross-cutting Patterns, Capability ledger).

title: Gates (not a `BLOCKED-ON`; the founder's own word, asked at P4)

data.head: ## Gates (not a `BLOCKED-ON`; the founder's own word, asked at P4)

body:
- **The verify child set is founder-ratified** (`.claude/rules/security.md`, the bullet on `viola verify`'s four
  interactive PTY children: Run B's five pastes are compiled literals — the probe prompt, a long text, a tag-like
  text, a newline text, `/clear`; Runs C and D answer dialogs only through the hidden `--capture --answers` arm).
  Every shape above that needs a new child shape, a new paste, a resume start, a compaction turn, a statusline child
  or a `claude agents` invocation is a boundary widening needing his own word, asked at P4 with its count. Without it
  no row of that shape lands. Verified, and widened by one finding: `hook statusline --capture` files nothing today,
  so a statusline capture is also a new capture arm (research.md §Measured facts 5).

- **The cap of live `claude` starts** for this chunk is his word too (CARRY 1: "a live-start cap of its own at
  take-up"). No live start beyond the cap he gives is planned.

- A planned step that departs from a founder ruling is never a decisive lean or a card-confirm item: the plan goes up
  to it and holds it behind a stop rule naming what counts as his word (CLAUDE.md Session Learnings).

- Six shapes, each a ledger row with a probe — a resume child, a compaction turn, statusline children, a
  `claude agents --json` start — plus fixtures re-recorded and every stamped home re-stamped, do not fit one window as
  one chunk (verified: research.md §Measured facts 2, 4, 5, 8 — `/compact` adds a product change to `send`'s claim,
  the resume row a sixth child and a new id source, the statusline rows a new capture arm and, for `rate_limits`, a
  new fixture class). Two CARRYs (2, 4) direct this phase to propose a cut. The cut is P4's; moving a row off this
  entry that the founder placed here (CARRY 5, by his own answer; the entry itself, by his fork-3 answer) is his word,
  asked at P4.

- The live-start count is read per part the plan keeps: one `viola verify` round is five starts (print plus Runs A–D),
  six with a resume child; a record round and a re-stamp of the tmpfs `--local-live` home are two rounds when both are
  wanted (verified: research.md §Measured facts 9).

- Every reader that pins the row set by shape moves with each row added, not only the count literals (verified:
  research.md §Sweeps — six files of count literals, the dialog-less summary in `tests/support/home.rs`, the
  older-stamp oracle in `src/run/version_gate.rs`).

title: The cut, as answered at P4 (validation-1: intent-incomplete, amended at P5)

data.head: ## The cut, as answered at P4 (validation-1: intent-incomplete, amended at P5)

body:
- Found at planning, decided by the artifacts (plan.md §Provenance, leaned): the three rows are relied on only where
  the status line is wrapped (Unix, `statusline::WRAPPED_HERE`). A Unix host checks and stamps twenty-one rows, a
  Windows host eighteen, and the step counter's MM is the relied count.

- `v1-34`'s harness-prefix row and its R8 identity-floor row — the founder, 2026-10-07T09:43Z: no entry minted, each
  needs its own ruling. So `v1-34` is not completed by this chunk whatever it lands.

- The `paste-newline` row's Windows reading — owned by a CARRY on "Windows-only live measurements" (`BLOCKED-ON` an
  interactive Windows host).
- No live `claude` start beyond the founder's cap; no change to the verify child set without his word.

- Paste text, `send`'s typed text and its validation are unchanged; this chunk measures and stamps what viola relies
  on, it does not change what it types.

- Behaviour on an unverified CLI build stays transport-only; a row added to `ALL` gates `cli_verified` like the
  eighteen.
- Never a key typed into a dialog of a verify child; viola writes nothing under `~/.claude`.

_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-10-13-paste-newline-ledger-row · **Version:** viola-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-13T21:10Z
- **Base (HEAD at P4):** `19483111dbe9` — every git-reading entry below names it.

An LF typed inside a bracketed paste, which every multi-line `send` relies on (an inner CR or CR LF is typed as one LF
since chunk 2026-10-09-inner-cr-and-crlf-in-a-sent-text), becomes the eighteenth capability-ledger row,
`paste-newline`, probed by `viola verify` and stamped on the live CLI. The row is gated like the seventeen
(architecture §Established Decisions [CLI Version Compatibility]; security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Universal): a
stamp holding only the seventeen older ids reads unverified, so every stamped home is re-stamped by running `verify`,
never by an edit.

The probe is a **fifth Run B paste**, a compiled synthetic text holding one inner LF, pasted after the tag-like text
and before `/clear`, only into a settled input box — the founder's own answer to fork 1 (R-L29, a boundary widening
of the ratified verify child set; `inputs#I2`). Its recorded prompt (`paste-3`) is taken from **one** `viola verify
--record` round on `claude` 2.1.287, named by path: five live starts (print, Runs A–D), the whole of the founder's cap
(fork 2, `inputs#I2`), fired once and never retried. Only the new variant is copied into the stamped set, so CI's
fake agent replays it and the committed 2.1.287 set stamps eighteen rows.

The six other owed shapes the route parked here (`--resume`, `/compact`, the statusline override, `/bin/sh`,
`rate_limits`, the `claude agents --json` join field) move to a new entry placed directly after this one — the
founder's own answer to fork 3 (`inputs#I2`). The chunk also disposes CARRY 2's four timeout-graded mutants in the
project's hand-applied form (no mutation run, witness run or workflow dispatch: `inputs#I1`). No matrix cap is
claimed: `v1-34` still needs the harness-prefix and R8 identity-floor rows (research.md §Measured facts 10).

1. **The compiled text and the row** — `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs`:
   - add `pub const PROBE_NEWLINE_PASTE: &str`, exactly
     `"viola verify probe: this paste holds one line break here\nand the next line ends it. Reply with the single word ok"`
     (synthetic ASCII, one LF, not at either end, no CR, short enough to arrive unwrapped — under the 1 500-byte long
     text that the CLI wraps);
   - `FRAMING_TURNS` grows from 3 to 4 rows in paste order: `paste-1` long, `paste-2` tag-like, **`paste-3` the LF
     text**, `clear-1` the local command; update its doc comment ("Run B's four added pastes") and the array pattern in
     `framing_variants` (`ledger.rs:715`, a 3-element destructuring today) so it names `paste-3` beside `paste-1`,
     `paste-2` and keeps the `clear-1` pair exactly as now;
   - append `LedgerRow::PasteNewline` as the **eighteenth and last** member of `ALL` (rows 1–17 keep their slots and
     numbers); id `paste-newline`; words `an LF inside a paste stays inside the one prompt submitted` (ASCII, one
     line); its `check` arm is `pasted(&probes.trusted, PROBE_NEWLINE_PASTE).is_some()` — the equality on the whole
     text is the post-condition: a CLI that submitted at the LF leaves no capture equal to the whole text.

2. **The row's unit cases** — `ledger.rs` tests, the three-case form of the framing rows (research.md §Patterns):
   `check_paste_newline_passes_on_the_one_prompt_holding_the_lf`,
   `check_paste_newline_fails_when_the_lf_split_the_prompt` (two UserPromptSubmit captures, the first line and the
   second line, and no capture equal to the whole text), `check_paste_newline_fails_without_a_matching_capture`.
   Extend the existing `ledger_rows_are_the_seventeen_measured_behaviours_in_order` (renamed `…_eighteen_…`, its id
   list a test literal), `[true; 17]` at `ledger.rs:1519` → 18, `framing_texts_are_fixed_ascii_each_with_its_stem`
   (the LF text: ASCII, exactly one `\n`, no `\r`, stem `paste-3`), and
   `framing_variants_name_the_two_prompts_and_the_hooks_the_local_command_fired` (now three prompts). Row ids and the
   LF text are literals in the tests, never the product's constants (testing.md §What to assert).

3. **Run B pastes the text** — `src/cmd/verify/typed.rs` `framing_turns` (`:306`): the added-paste list at `:309`
   becomes `[PROBE_LONG_PASTE, PROBE_TAG_PASTE, PROBE_NEWLINE_PASTE]` under the same per-paste guards (`input_box_up`
   on the rows the turn before left, `paste_text` refusing after the stop, `added_turn_ended` then `box_wait`); the
   local command still follows last. Update the doc comments at `:108` and `:301` (four added pastes). Any existing
   `typed.rs` case that pins the paste list or its count (the restated Run B driver of chunk
   2026-10-13-epoch-4-survivors-ii) moves to the four-text list and keeps its kills.

4. **The version gate's older-set oracle** — `src/run/version_gate.rs` `stamps_verdict_needs_the_dialog_rows`
   (`:265`): the seventeen rows all passing now read `(false, None)` ("the seventeen rows of an older stamp"); adding
   `PasteNewline` passing reads `(true, None)`; `PasteNewline` joins the per-row failing loop; the doc comment says
   eighteen.

5. **The test-side fixtures and literals** (no recorded fixture is read yet):
   - `tests/support/verify.rs` `framing_set` (`:78`) gains `("UserPromptSubmit", "paste-3", …)` whose `prompt` is a
     test literal `NEWLINE_PASTE` equal to the text of step 1 (the CLI sends it unchanged, `rule-inner-lf`); its doc
     comments say five variants and four added pastes (`:76`, `:420`);
   - `tests/cli_verify.rs`: `STEPS_PASS` / `ROW_IDS` at eighteen, `[NN/18]`, the new line
     `[18/18] paste-newline an LF inside a paste stays inside the one prompt submitted  pass`, every
     `stamped 2.1.0  17 pass  0 fail` → `18 pass`, the failing-row tables, the stop table's receipt counts (one more
     Run B prompt), and the comment at `:1012`; the no-framing case still fails `local-command-clear` alone (without
     `--framing` the fake agent fires `default` with `prompt` = the typed text, so `paste-newline` passes there —
     research.md §Measured facts 5);
   - `tests/contract_ledger_probes.rs`: `ROW_IDS` at eighteen and `stamped {version}  18 pass  0 fail`;
   - `src/cmd/verify.rs` tests (`:546`–`:569`): the step-line literals at `/18` and the last line
     `[18/18] paste-newline …`;
   - `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run.rs`: `LEDGER_ROWS: [&str; 18]` with `paste-newline`, `LIVE_PASS` at `/18`
     with its eighteenth line and `stamped 2.1.287  18 pass  0 fail`, and its unit cases (`:1001`–`:1005`).

6. **CARRY 2 — the four timeout-graded mutants, by hand-applied mutant** (no cargo-mutants run: `inputs#I1`). For
   each, hand-apply the mutant at its site as of `19483111dbe9`, run the owning package's unit tests under the nextest
   `mutants` profile, read whether a case fails **on an assertion** (its panic line), restore the site and read green:
   - `delete !` at `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs:450` (the `!has("PreToolUse")` operand) and again at `:450` (the
     `!has("PermissionRequest")` operand) in `Agent::replay_dialogs` (`:446`);
   - `delete match arm "--screens"` in `Opts::parse` (`:107`);
   - `ProbeDir::typed` (`src/cmd/verify.rs:318`) replaced by `Default::default()`.
   Where an existing case already reads red by its assertion (e.g. `opts_parse_reads_values_flags_and_ignores_unknown`
   asserts `o.screens` at `:993`), that case is the kill and no case is added. Otherwise add one named case in the
   same file's inline test module: for `replay_dialogs`, a stem whose variant set holds only a PreToolUse and one that
   holds only a PermissionRequest, each still replayed; for `ProbeDir::typed`, the typed path is the `typed` dir inside
   the probe dir and differs from `questions` / `plan`. Re-read the site before each neutralising edit (rustfmt reflows
   on write, testing.md 2026-09-25). Record every reading — the mutant, the case, its red line, the restored green —
   in `evidence/carry2-kills.md`.
7. **Unit gates green** before any live start (fmt, clippy, the unit suite, the named row cases).

8. **The live round — 5 starts, the founder's cap (`inputs#I2`), fired once by `gate.py run --live-legs`:**
   the non-priming probe (the 2.1.287 binary is executable by path), then the record entry: a fresh
   `target/e2e-home/viola-record-<UTC>` dir, home `vhome` (never a component named `home`, testing.md 2026-10-05),
   `env -u VIOLA_NAME -u VIOLA_DIR -u VIOLA_BIN` (testing.md 2026-10-07), from the repo root (a trusted parent),
   `viola verify --record` against `~/.local/share/mise/installs/claude/2.1.287/claude`, then **only**
   `UserPromptSubmit.paste-3.json` copied into `fixtures/claude/2.1.287/`. Then the census: no `claude` with a probe-dir
   cwd left. Record in `evidence/live-round.md`: the UTC start and end (each from `date -u`), the five starts by
   name, the stdout step lines and the `stamped` line, the census, and the recorded `paste-3` prompt's bytes against
   the compiled text.
   **STOP rule:** a red round, a refusal of the recording (an unclean payload names its file and closed code), or a
   `paste-newline` fail on the live CLI is never re-fired — the cap is spent. Stop, record the reading, and report to
   the operator; the founder decides what follows. No further `claude` start of any kind in this chunk.

9. **Integration over the recorded set** — `cli_verify`, `contract_ledger_probes`, `contract_fake_agent_drift`,
   `contract_fixture_hygiene`, `cli_version_gate` (the stamped 2.1.287 set at eighteen rows, the new variant replayed
   byte for byte, scrubbed and schema-valid), then the guards, the literal probe, `cargo deny`, the harness smoke with
   G2 / G4, and `pre-push`.
10. **The operator pass** (not /implement): hygiene, the pre-CI commit, the push, the CI read.
- `fixtures/claude/2.1.287/UserPromptSubmit.paste-3.json` — the live-recorded LF prompt, copied alone from the record round (step 8)
- `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-13-paste-newline-ledger-row/evidence/` — `live-round.md`, `carry2-kills.md`

- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs` — `PROBE_NEWLINE_PASTE`, `FRAMING_TURNS` (2 refs: `framing_stem @ ledger.rs:167`, `framing_variants @ ledger.rs:715`), `LedgerRow::PasteNewline` (`ALL` read at `check_rows @ src/cmd/verify.rs:390` and `src/run/version_gate.rs:205`), its `check` arm (called by `check_step @ src/cmd/verify.rs:400`), the unit cases
- `src/cmd/verify/typed.rs` — `framing_turns` (one caller, `trusted_run @ typed.rs:138`)
- `src/cmd/verify.rs` — step-line test literals; `ProbeDir::typed`'s case if step 6 needs one (`framing_variants` reaches `named_payloads @ verify.rs:459` unchanged)
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs` — step 6's cases only, if needed; no product change (a new stem reaches `Agent::submit @ :557` and `Agent::end_turn @ :598` through `framing_stem`)
- `src/run/version_gate.rs` — the older-set oracle
- `tests/cli_verify.rs`, `tests/contract_ledger_probes.rs`, `tests/support/verify.rs` — literals at eighteen, the synthetic `paste-3`
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run.rs` — `LEDGER_ROWS`, `LIVE_PASS`, their cases

The standing lint and unit entries run first, then the row's three cases by name. The live round follows: one
non-priming probe, the record entry, the census (`leg = 'round'` / `'live'`), fired once by `gate.py run --live-legs`,
never re-run by the wrap (it is re-verified from `evidence/live-round.md`). The record entry regenerates a committed
fixture, so it precedes every entry that reads it: the integration binaries, the fixture guard, the harness smoke and
`pre-push`. The live-start ledger is the record entry's own five sessions (print, Runs A, B, C, D); the probe runs
`test -x` and starts nothing, and verify's own `--version` read is part of its round as in every earlier round.
`evidence/live-round.md` is written by implement's step 8 from the record and census entries' logs (the gate tool's
`logs` dir) and `date -u`; no entry produces it, and no entry reads it — the record entry's own `contains stamped
2.1.287  18 pass  0 fail` and the fixture guard assert the round on every re-run of the block.

Step 6's mutants are hand-applied and reverted, a tree state that exists once, so they are one-shot controls at
implement, not entries (`evidence/carry2-kills.md`); the unit entry holds the same cases on every re-run. No mutation
entry, no witness run and no workflow dispatch is listed (`inputs#I1`; testing.md 2026-10-04). No `run --local-live`
entry: the cap is five (`inputs#I2`), and the tmpfs live home re-stamps itself at its next firing (owed, `## Beyond
the plan` on the review card). The guards name their base `19483111dbe9`.
