body:
- (arch) `LedgerRow::ALL` holds eighteen rows, the eighteenth `paste-newline` (`an LF inside a paste stays inside the
  one prompt submitted`), checked by `pasted(trusted, PROBE_NEWLINE_PASTE)`; a stamp holding only the seventeen older
  ids, all `pass`, reads unverified and the eighteen passing reads verified (`stamps_verdict_needs_the_dialog_rows`,
  in `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --unit`) (per architecture §Established Decisions [CLI Version Compatibility]).

- (security) Run B pastes exactly five compiled texts — the probe prompt, the long text, the tag-like text, the LF
  text, `/clear` — each only into a settled input box and none after the stop; no byte is typed into a dialog. The
  widening is the founder's own answer to P4 fork 1 (R-L29, `inputs#I2`) (per security-plan §Threat Model Summary,
  Attack surface: Child process spawning and PATH resolution).

- (tests) `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --unit --filter 'test(/check_paste_newline_/)'` reads 3 passed, 0 failed:
  the row passes on one prompt holding the LF, fails when the LF split it, fails with no matching capture (per
  test-plan §4 Unit Test Strategy, viola-agent-claude).

- (tests) One live round on `claude` 2.1.287 — exactly five starts, fired once — prints
  `stamped 2.1.287  18 pass  0 fail`, its recorded `paste-3` prompt equals the compiled LF text byte for byte, and the
  census finds no probe-dir `claude` left (`evidence/live-round.md`) (per test-plan §7 Fixture hygiene; the founder's
  cap, `inputs#I2`).

- (tests) `fixtures/claude/2.1.287/` gains `UserPromptSubmit.paste-3.json` and no other change (the fixture guard);
  `contract_ledger_probes` stamps the 2.1.287 set `18 pass  0 fail` with each literal row id once,
  `contract_fake_agent_drift` replays `paste-3` byte for byte, `contract_fixture_hygiene` passes it (the integration
  entry) (per test-plan §5 Integration Test Strategy; per test-plan §7 Fixture hygiene).

- (design / layouts / a11y) `viola verify` over a complete set prints exactly eighteen `[NN/18] <row id> <row words>
  pass|fail` lines in `ALL` order, the last `[18/18] paste-newline …`, then `stamped <ver>  18 pass  0 fail`, plain
  ASCII with no SGR byte; the interrupted pair stays byte-identical (`tests/cli_verify.rs`) (per design-system §Surface:
  cli §Component Patterns, pattern 5 `verify`; per layout-templates §Output structure — `viola verify`; per a11y-plan
  §8 Cognitive Accessibility → Error recovery).

- (obs) A verify run still writes six spawn pairs, every subject in the closed enum, every line schema-valid, no row
  text, prompt or path in any line (`tests/cli_verify.rs`, G4) (per obs-plan §4 Edge flows → `verify` / `plugin
  install`).

- (tests) The harness's `LEDGER_ROWS` names the eighteen ids and its `LIVE_PASS` unit proof reads eighteen (`run
  --unit`) (per test-plan §3 `run`).

- (tests) Each of CARRY 2's four mutants, hand-applied, reads red by a case's assertion (an existing case or a new
  named one) and green restored, recorded in `evidence/carry2-kills.md`; no mutation run (per test-plan §10 Mutation
  gate).

- (security) No new dependency, `cargo deny check` passes, and no file outside the modify set changes (the
  preservation guard) (per security-plan §Dependency Security).
- (tests) The pushed HEAD's CI run reads `verdict: green` on all three OSes (the operator's CI entry).

- Spec anchors: architecture §Established Decisions [CLI Version Compatibility], §Cross-cutting Patterns (Capability
  ledger), §Occupied Resources (Repository); security-plan §Threat Model Summary (child spawning), §Security
  Anti-Patterns → Universal, §Data Protection (Repository fixtures; Interactive probe dirs); test-plan §3 `run`, §4,
  §5, §7, §10; obs-plan §4 Edge flows → `verify`, §6; design-system §Surface: cli pattern 5; layout-templates §Output
  structure — `viola verify`; a11y-plan §1, §8.

- Research files inspected: `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs`, `src/cmd/verify.rs`, `src/cmd/verify/typed.rs`,
  `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs`, `src/run/version_gate.rs`, `tests/support/verify.rs`, `tests/contract_ledger_probes.rs`,
  `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run.rs`, `crates/viola-state/src/fs.rs`, `.config/nextest.toml`.
- Inputs: `inputs#I1` (the operator's take-up direction), `inputs#I2` (the founder's three answers).

- Leaned: the row appended last, not before `local-command-clear` — rows 1–17 keep their slots, and nothing orders
  rows by paste order (`check_rows @ src/cmd/verify.rs:390` walks `ALL`); the text placed third in `FRAMING_TURNS` so
  `/clear` stays the last paste, as `clear_start` (`ledger.rs:687`) searches forward from the tag-like prompt.

- Mechanism (check 8): the LF reaches the fake agent as an LF — `PasteHandle::paste @ crates/viola-pty/src/pump.rs:77`
  writes the text's bytes unchanged inside the bracket, the fake agent's `Input::feed @ src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs:702`
  keeps every in-paste byte as prompt content, and `Agent::submit @ :557` looks the whole text up with `framing_stem`;
  on the live CLI the same equality was measured once (`rule-inner-lf`, chunk 2026-10-09-inner-cr-and-crlf-in-a-sent-text).

- Leaned: CARRY 2 disposed by hand-applied mutants per chunk 2026-10-13-epoch-4-survivors' form, its cargo-mutants
  grading owed to the Epoch 5 boundary audit — `inputs#I1` excludes the witness run the CARRY named.

- A hand-written `paste-3` fixture — the fake agent invents no shape before a recorded fixture (test-plan §7; tests
  history 2026-09-24-fake-agent-and-test-data-fixtures).

- Copying the whole re-recorded 2.1.287 set — every other committed fixture keeps its bytes (the fixture guard; the
  precedent round of chunk 2026-10-06-local-command-and-paste-framing-rows).

- A second live round, a rehearsal session, a `run --local-live` firing, or any other `claude` start — the cap is five
  (`inputs#I2`); a red round is reported, never re-fired.
- Folding the LF into the tag-like text — the founder chose the fifth paste (`inputs#I2`, fork 1).

- Any of the six other shapes (`--resume`, `/compact`, the statusline override, `/bin/sh`, `rate_limits`, `claude
  agents --json`) — moved to the new entry (`inputs#I2`, fork 3).

- Any change to `send`, `typed_text`, `validate_paste_text` or the paste write — this chunk measures what `send`
  types, it changes nothing about it (scope §Boundaries).

- Raising a nextest kill line if a verify-driven case slows by the fifth paste — the timing rule applies (testing.md
  2026-09-28): measure, then remove the slow work.

- A new fake-agent seam or option — the new stem reaches the fake agent through `framing_stem` (research.md §Graph
  impact).

`unconfirmable` at once instead of a false exit 13 `no-prompt-submitted` while the command runs (per architecture

   `resume_run` follows `plan_run`, and the stop check between runs stays as it is (`typed.rs:87`–`:92`). `resume_run`

9. **The literals, per OS** (research.md §Sweeps), each listed by the function it decides:

     Each is predicted to gain one `pass` (Run E needs no framing variant): `17 pass  4 fail` → `18 pass  4 fail` and

    `send-issued` then `send-confirmed{confirmed:false}`, and no `send-refused` or `prompt-submitted`. This is the model
    of `send_window_local_command_is_not_presumed_delivered` (`:674`).

12. **CI sizing re-read.** Run E adds one fake-agent start to every verify-driven test. Read the verify-driven
    binaries' wall under `profile.ci` against their 20 s kill, and the `verify_window_` class, before and after. The
    before-reading is P5's baseline firing of the integration entry on the untouched tree (39.31 s whole; the phase run
    dir's gate trail). The after-reading is the block's firing of the integration entry after step 13's record round,
    never before it: the entry reads the fixture that round lands. A kill moves only under the by-design-floor rule,
    with a planted-hang control both ways (test-plan history 2026-10-07-send-waits-out-the-paste-hint); otherwise
    record the reading and move nothing.

13. **The record round** (live, 6 starts: print, Runs A–E). Fired once by `gate.py run --live-legs`, never retried:
    the record entry below. It copies `SessionStart.resume-1.json` only into `fixtures/claude/2.1.287/`. If the round
    is red, stop and report. A stalled start is first a finding about the tmpfs backing (verification-harness.md
    2026-10-07 extension).

14. **The live-suite round** (live, 6 starts): `run --local-live` re-stamps the tmpfs home at twenty-two rows. That is
    the second half of the founder's cap of twelve (`inputs#I1`, fork 3).
- `fixtures/claude/2.1.287/SessionStart.resume-1.json` — recorded by step 13 (`viola verify --record`), scrubbed.
- `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows/evidence/live-round.md` — step 15.

- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs` — steps 1–3 (graph: `merge_stamp` 11 sites, `relied` 5,
  `framing_variants` 6; research.md §Graph impact).
- `src/run/send/classify.rs` — step 4, unit rows only.
- `src/cmd/verify/typed.rs` — step 5 (`trusted_run @ typed.rs:84`, `measure`'s run list).
- `src/cmd/verify.rs` — step 6 (`ProbeDir`, `Probes`, `named_payloads`; `read_captures` read by step 5 unchanged).
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs` — step 7 (`resume_fields`, 7 sites in the file).
- `src/run/version_gate.rs` — step 8.
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run.rs` — step 9.
- `tests/cli_verify.rs`, `tests/contract_ledger_probes.rs` — step 9.
- `tests/contract_fixture_hygiene.rs`, `tests/contract_fake_agent_drift.rs`, `tests/cli_fake_agent.rs` — step 10.
- `tests/cli_send.rs` — step 11.

- `tests/support/verify.rs` — step 9: a shaped session-id literal for Run E, and `verify_started`'s `after` parameter
  for the new stop case (measured at implement, the outcome's §Deviations).
- `tests/support/home.rs` — step 9: `dialogless_home`'s summary literal (the revision, `inputs#I4`).

The standing lint and unit entries run first, then the five row cases by name. The live round follows, fired once by
`gate.py run --live-legs` and never re-run by the wrap (re-verified from `evidence/live-round.md`):
- the non-priming probe;
- the record entry (6 starts: print, Runs A–E);
- the census;
- a second probe;
- the `run --local-live` entry (6 starts);
- a second census.

The record entry regenerates a committed fixture, so it precedes every entry that reads fixtures: the fixture guard,
the integration binaries, the harness smoke and `pre-push`. No entry produces `evidence/live-round.md` and none reads
it: step 15 writes it from the logs. On every re-run of the block, the record entry's `contains stamped 2.1.287
22 pass  0 fail` and the fixture guard assert the round.

No count-literal probe is listed: Windows keeps nineteen by design (step 9), the Linux integration entry reads every
Unix literal and CI's `windows-2025` leg reads every Windows one. No mutation entry, witness run or workflow dispatch is
listed. The guards name their base `880b056377f4` (HEAD at P4).

- (arch) The `resume-session` check passes only on Run E's first SessionStart of source `resume` whose id equals Run
  B's first SessionStart id. It fails on another source, another id, no capture, or a target off the session-id shape
  (per architecture §Cross-cutting Patterns → Capability ledger as the single gate). Proved by the
  `test(/check_resume_session_/)` entry (5 passed).

- (security) Run E's id reaches the child's argv only through `resume_args` after `is_session_id`, as one argv element
  of a direct spawn under the R8 strip, in a 0700 `-resume` dir its guard removes on pass, fail and stop. No key is
  typed into it (per security-plan §Input Validation, Session id as a child argv value row; §Threat Model Summary, the
  verify child set, widened by the founder's own answer to fork 2, `inputs#I1`). Proved by the integration entry's stop
  table and spawn-pair cases.

  <ver>  22 pass  0 fail` (Unix) / `19 pass  0 fail` (Windows) (per test-plan §5 Integration Test Strategy, CLI); the
  Windows half is read by CI's `windows-2025` leg through the `ci.py conclusion` entry.

- (tests) `SessionStart.resume-1.json` is recorded live (the record entry, `contains stamped 2.1.287  22 pass  0
  fail`), passes the hygiene walk and the schema, and is replayed byte for byte by `contract_fake_agent_drift`. The
  fake agent's `--resume` builds its launch payload on it with the given id (per test-plan §7 Test Data & Fixtures).
  Proved by the fixture guard and the integration entry.

- (obs) An uninterrupted `viola verify` under a `VIOLA_NAME` writes seven spawn pairs (`version-probe`,
  `verify-probe`, five `verify-pty-probe`), each `process-exit` with `child_exit_status` and `duration_ms`, and no row
  text, prompt or path (per obs-plan §4 Span / Trace Coverage, Capability ledger → `verify`). Proved by the integration
  entry.

- (design / layouts / a11y) A driver's `viola send` of `/compact` on a verified CLI exits 0 with the `[  ]
  unconfirmable` line and logs `send-confirmed{confirmed:false}`, with no `send-refused` and no new detail (per
  design-system §Surface: cli, pattern 2 `viola send`; layout-templates §Surface: cli, Signature placement). Proved by
  the integration entry (`binary(cli_send)`).

  operator's host, within the founder's cap of twelve starts (`inputs#I1`, fork 3); `evidence/live-round.md` records
  each start.

  green` on the final HEAD, its run id named in the report.

body: The founder answered the three P4 forks himself, relayed verbatim by the operator (`inputs#I1`):

  here, and the relied set moves 21 → 22 on Unix and 18 → 19 on Windows (one row), not the two-row forecast in
  §Premises.

  Run B's own first SessionStart capture. This is the boundary widening of the verify child set, ratified by him.

- (arch) `e2e-web/`, `scripts/install-node.sh` and `scripts/npm-audit.sh` are gone. After the pre-CI commit
  `git ls-files '*tsconfig.json'` lists nothing, so the ts plane has no input (per architecture §Infrastructure
  Patterns → Project directory structure, Build system).

- (tests) No workflow, pre-push stage, harness verb, script or config runs, installs or checks `node` / `npm` / `npx`
  or the browser suite. The browser-and-Node absence guard reads `exit 1`, `no output` after reading the sites at the
  base (per test-plan §3 `run`, `pre-push`; architecture §Stack and Technologies, Browser e2e row).

- (tests) `gate --require playwright` exits 2 with `"detail":"unknown-suite"`. The `test` job's verdict step and the
  pre-push's `linux-tests` gate both read `gate --require coverage,doctest` (per test-plan §3 `gate`).

- (security) The pre-push launcher still carries exactly `HOME` and `PATH`, its PATH holds no `.local/viola-node`
  element, and its `tools` stage runs no `node`. Each is pinned by `pre_push_every_native_call_carries_only_home_and_path`
  and `pre_push_native_stages_run_tools_then_linux_tests_and_end_the_pass`, with
  `pre_push_native_child_sees_only_home_and_path` still green (per security-plan §Secret Management).

- (security) `cargo deny check` and the sole-root tokio loop pass; `bash scripts/deny-probes.sh` prints
  `deny-probes: 12/12 banned, control clean`; zizmor exits 0 over the three workflows (per security-plan §Dependency
  Security).

- (security) The secret scan keeps every `CLAUDE*` canary, the content canary, the `cookie:` header and the
  non-0600 check. It no longer reports `?t=`, `viola_<port>=` or a `ui/*.url` token, pinned by
  `secret_scan_ignores_the_removed_gui_forms` (per security-plan §Secret Management; `inputs#I1`, fork 1).

- (obs) Both line schemas hold no `ui` process value and none of `http-request` / `liveness-changed` / `sse-opened` /
  `sse-closed`. `diag-line.v1.json` holds no `port`, `last-event-id` or `liveness` def. Both keep top-level
  `unevaluatedProperties: false`. `contract_diag_schema` and G4 read zero failures (per obs-plan §8 Default-deny
  posture, §9 G4).

- (obs) `ObsEvent::ALL` holds the fifteen and `ObsProcess::ALL` the four (`run`, `hook`, `mcp`, `cli`), pinned by
  literal oracles. `src/obs.rs`'s `Targets` names no `viola_ui`. The leftover-vocabulary absence guard reads
  `exit 1`, `no output` (per obs-plan §3 Log format JSON schema, §6 Per-module log levels).

- (obs) In `ci.yml`, G2, G4 and `secret-scan` stay `if: always()`. Every `diag-` / `harness-` / `junit-<os>` upload
  stays gated on `steps.secret-scan.outcome == 'success'`, and `junit-<os>` carries the nextest JUnit alone (per
  obs-plan §9 Step order and conditions).

- (tests) The status document has no `ui` / `api_sessions_equal_list`; the cleanup report has no `port_free` /
  `url_file_removed`; the session record has no `ui` / `cookie_file`. `harness_lifecycle` and the booted smoke read
  green (per test-plan §3 Status endpoint shape, `cleanup`).

- (tests) `.config/nextest.toml` has no `fixed-port` group. `windows-mutants.yml` keeps ten items with
  `contract_windows_mutation_scope` green (per test-plan §5 Setup / teardown lifecycle, §9 CI Integration).

- (a11y) The CLI output-discipline and TUI boundary cases run unchanged inside the gated `coverage` suite on all
  three OSes. None is `#[ignore]`d, and the CI read is green (per a11y-plan §1 CI integration, §4).

- (tests) Every gate above reads green, `pre-push` included, and CI's run on the final HEAD reads `verdict: green`
  (per test-plan §9 CI Integration).
- No capability is claimed: the entry names no matrix id, and v1-08 and v1-23 are `verified` (the ledger notes below).

- Rulings: the founder's of 2026-10-16 (`.andromeda/runs/2026-10-16T14-58-10-wrap/inputs/I1-restructure-cli-only.md.txt`,
  item 3); the overseer's two answers at that wrap (route CARRY 2 and 3); the P4 forks (`inputs#I1`).

  this chunk only narrows, so no fork named one.

`viola list` learns what the disk cannot tell it. It runs `claude agents --json` once, joins the rows to the wrapped
instances, and gives each joined wrapped row STATUS `idle` or `busy`. Every row that joins no wrapped instance prints
as a read-only unwrapped row, under `-- UNWRAPPED - READ-ONLY --` on the human board and as a `wrapped: false` item in
`list --json`. A failed, oversize or malformed read changes nothing that `list` prints today
(architecture §Standard Contracts, Session liveness and the `list` payload; design-system §Surface: cli, pattern 1;
layout-templates §Output structure — `viola list`).

`viola revive` gains its fourth preflight reading, `session-live`. The same read refuses a resume of a session id that
a live `claude` already holds. `--fork` skips the reading, and a failed read fails open (architecture [Session
Liveness]; the founder's answers, `inputs#I1` forks 3 and 4).

The join field becomes the twenty-third capability-ledger row, `agents-join`, relied on every OS. Its `viola verify`
probe is one bounded `claude agents --json` read taken while Run B's session is live (`inputs#I1` fork 1). The fake
agent answers `agents --json` from files beside its own executable, with no env (`inputs#I1` fork 2). The parser takes
a 512-case property and a fuzz target. One recorded `claude agents --json` row is committed under
`fixtures/claude/2.1.287/`. Two live legs are spent: the record round (6 starts) and the P4 / P12 leg (2 starts), the
founder's cap of 8 (`inputs#I1` fork 3).

- **The founder's own answers** (`inputs#I1`, live in the overseer's dialog, 2026-10-16T19:54:09Z, relayed verbatim
  by the operator):
  - (1) The join row is relied, with its probe in Run B. This ratifies a widening of verify's child set.
  - (2) The fake agent's mode comes from files beside its exe, so there is no third env seam.
  - (3) `session-live` is built as a refusal now, with a P4 leg, and this chunk's cap is 8 live starts (6 + 2).
  - (4) The wording is the "open elsewhere / --fork" pair.

- **Narrowed within answer 1 (a lean):** the probe makes ONE read, before Run B's `/clear` paste. That is the one
  added child and the 7 → 8 spawn pairs the fork's text stated. P12 (does `sessionId` follow `/clear`?) is measured in
  the P4 leg instead, with no added start. The fork's preview showed a second read after `/clear`. Taking one is
  narrower than the answer, never wider.

- **Leaned, each settled by an artifact:**
  - **The unwrapped NAME and the `--json` `name` are the row's `sessionId`.** Architecture §Standard Contracts (`list`
    payload) names it "the session identifier", and the design sample is a hex id. design-system §Anti-Patterns
    (cli bans) forbids printing upstream text, and the CLI's `name` is a free-text title (research §Measured).
  - **The join keys are `child_pid` OR `agent_session_id`, per architecture §Standard Contracts (Session liveness).**
    The snapshot gains `agent_session_id` as architecture §Standard Contracts (Instance snapshot) lists it, and the
    wrapper writes it on each `session-start` (research: the field is absent today).
  - **The read takes the version probe's bound and strip** (`VERSION_DEADLINE` 5 s, the R8 strip plan; security-plan
    §Input Validation, Constants and the child rows). It was measured at about 125 ms (research §Measured).
  - **An over-`MAX_FRAME` read logs `detail: "oversize"`.** `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` already admits it for every
    parser, and obs-plan §6's per-parser catalog line follows at the wrap.
  - **The recording is made on 2.1.287**, the stamped set's version, so one stamped set stays the fake's default
    (verification-harness.md 2026-10-10: the stamped version's install dir goes first on `PATH`).
  - **Revive's order is holder → logged session → `session-live` → recorded directory.** The reading needs the id the
    session reading picks. It stands ahead of `cwd-missing`, whose hint names a by-hand resume, which would be a
    second writer.
  - **An empty wrapped rack with unwrapped rows** prints the BAY line, the caption, the founder-ruled empty-board line
    unchanged, then the separator and the rows. No ruled form changes, and the rack follows the wrapped rows as the
    design places it.
  - **No truncation and no colour on the new rows.** Width-known truncation belongs to the styled TTY form, which is
    owed to "CLI output discipline" (layout-templates §Output structure — `viola list` (piped …), its as-built
    paragraph).

- **Playbook check** (`.andromeda/playbook.md`, the `verdict: escalate` patterns): forks 1 and 2 were put as
  "Boundary widening" and answered by the founder himself, the pattern "Boundary widening the founder answered
  himself to a P4 fork". The new `claude agents --json` child of `list` and `revive` is no widening: security-plan
  §Threat Model Summary (child spawning vector) and §Input Validation (Child executable resolution row, "for `run`,
  `revive` and `claude agents`") already state it, owed to this entry.

1. **The agents reading** — new `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/agents.rs`, pure, no I/O. It is re-exported from
   `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/lib.rs`.
   - **The row type.** A tolerant row over the measured keys (`pid`, `sessionId`, `status`, `kind`, `cwd`, `name`,
     `startedAt`). It uses `#[serde(default)]` / `Option<T>`, never `deny_unknown_fields`, and keeps the raw `Value`
     for the recorder (architecture §Established Decisions [Validation]).
   - **`parse(bytes) -> Result<Vec<AgentsRow>, AgentsFailure>`.** It returns `Oversize` above `MAX_FRAME` and
     `Malformed` for anything that is not one JSON array at serde's default depth. An element that is not an object,
     or has no string `sessionId`, is skipped and counted.
   - **The status mapping.** A closed status, idle · busy · unknown, mapped one to one from the measured `status`
     words. Any other value is unknown.
   - **The join predicate.** A row joins a wrapped instance when its `pid` equals that instance's `child_pid`, or its
     `sessionId` equals its `agent_session_id`.
   - **A row's `sessionId` is content.** It is never a `ViolaName` (security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns, Input).
   - **Unit cases:**
     - the measured 7-key row;
     - an extra key, kept and counted as tolerated;
     - a `background` row of the `--all` shape (no `pid`, no `status`): listed with status unknown, joinable only by
       `sessionId`;
     - a row with no `sessionId`, skipped;
     - a non-array document and a non-UTF-8 document;
     - the `MAX_FRAME` boundary (`MAX_FRAME` bytes parse, `MAX_FRAME + 1` is `Oversize`);
     - every measured `status` word and one unknown word.

2. **The property and the fuzz target** (test-plan §6 Property suite; §2 Property-based row).
   - A proptest over arbitrary JSON values, `cases: 512`, in the agents module. `parse` never panics. It returns
     either rows or a closed failure, and every returned row's `sessionId` is a string taken from the input unchanged.
   - Its regressions file is `crates/viola-agent-claude/proptest-regressions/agents.txt`, committed once proptest
     writes it.
   - New `fuzz/fuzz_targets/claude_agents_json.rs` with a `[[bin]]` in `fuzz/Cargo.toml` (the crate already
     path-depends on `viola-agent-claude`) and `fuzz/Cargo.lock` following.
   - A synthetic corpus in `fuzz/corpus/claude_agents_json/`: the measured 7-key shape with invented values, the
     `--all` background shape, an empty array, a non-array, a deep array and a row whose `sessionId` holds control
     characters. The count is stated by `ls fuzz/corpus/claude_agents_json | wc -l`. No recorded content.
   - `.gitattributes` gains `fuzz/corpus/claude_agents_json/** binary` (the `paste_text` precedent,
     `.gitattributes:6`).

3. **The bounded read** — new `src/run/agents.rs`, a module of `src/run/mod.rs`, beside the version gate.
   - It resolves `claude` through `run::resolve_program`, the same rule as `run`'s (a `.cmd` / `.bat` shim to its
     `claude.exe`; any other batch script refused). A refusal or a missing program is a failed read, never an exit
     change.
   - It spawns `claude agents --json` directly under the same `StripPlan` the version gate builds, with stdin null,
     killed and reaped at `VERSION_DEADLINE`.
   - It reads stdout through `take(MAX_FRAME + 1)`. Either `run_bounded`'s drain in `src/run/version_gate.rs` gains
     the over-the-cap flag, keeping its two callers' readings unchanged, or the agents read takes its own drain. A
     non-zero exit is a failed read.
   - It returns the rows, or a closed failure word: `oversize` · `malformed` · `unreadable` (spawn failure, deadline,
     non-zero exit, refused resolution).
   - The callers log the spawn pair at their own sites (obs-plan §6, Boundary-call wrappers):
     - `process-start{subject:"agents-probe"}` and `process-exit{subject:"agents-probe", child_exit_status,
       duration_ms}`, with no row text, id, `cwd` or path;
     - on a parse failure one `parse-rejected{parser:"claude-agents-json", detail, count}` at `warn`;
     - `run_bounded` stays unlogged.
   - No line is written where the caller has no open log (`list` with no `VIOLA_NAME`).

4. **The snapshot's session id.** `crates/viola-state/src/snapshot.rs` `InstanceSnapshot` gains `agent_session_id:
   Option<String>`, additive (`#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`). The wrapper rewrites it
   whenever the hook tap takes a `session-start` whose `agent_session_id` is a string. A `session-start` with no string
   id leaves it as it stands. The tap is `append_hook_event` in `src/run/send/slot.rs`, and the write goes through the
   wrapper's snapshot handle (`src/run/snapshot.rs` `update`), after the line is appended. Unit cases: a `startup`
   then a `clear` start rewrites the field twice, and a start with a null id writes nothing.

5. **The board's read model** (`crates/viola-state/src/board.rs`; it takes no agent-crate type — architecture
   §Infrastructure Patterns → Crate dependency direction).
   - `SessionStatus` gains `Idle` and `Busy` (kebab `idle` / `busy`).
   - `read` also gives each wrapped item's join keys: the snapshot's `child_pid` and `agent_session_id`, and for a
     replayed instance the replay's `agent_session_id` with no pid. They are not serialised.
   - A new constructor builds an unwrapped item: `wrapped: false`, `liveness` `live`, `dialog_pending: false`, and no
     `wheel` / `budget_paused` / `cli_version` / `cli_verified` key (architecture §Standard Contracts, `list` payload).
   - A join takes plain observations: a pid, a session-id string and a status. For each wrapped item it sets the
     joined observation's status. Every observation that joins no item becomes an unwrapped item. Unwrapped items are
     sorted by name and placed after every wrapped item.
   - Liveness is never changed, and a gone instance is never brought back (architecture [Session Liveness]).
   - Unit cases: a pid join; a session-id join; a row matching neither; one row matching two keys of one item (one
     join, no unwrapped row); a stale wrapped item joined keeps `stale`; the unwrapped item serialised to its contract
     literal.

6. **`viola list`** (`src/cmd/list.rs`, `read`).
   - After `board::read`, the read of step 3 runs once. Its rows are mapped to observations: status through step 1's
     closed mapping, the name being the `sessionId`. Then the board is joined.
   - A failed read leaves the board as `board::read` gave it: every status `unknown`, no unwrapped item.
   - The exit and every refusal path are unchanged: the scan's exit 21 before any spawn, and the strict-modes order.
   - The spawn pair and the parse line go to `cli-<name>.ndjson` only under a parsed `VIOLA_NAME`, after the scan
     passed (obs-plan §4, the cli row).
   - `--json` serialises the joined items whole, in board order, as `{v, ok:{items, budget, skipped}}`.

7. **The human board** (`src/human/board.rs`).
   - The STATUS cell prints `idle` · `busy` · `unknown`.
   - Every row's NAME goes through `escape_row`. A wrapped `ViolaName` is unchanged by it.
   - NAME's width is taken over the escaped names of both racks.
   - When at least one unwrapped item exists, after the last wrapped row (or after the empty-board line when the
     wrapped rack is empty) comes one line `-- UNWRAPPED - READ-ONLY --`. Then one row per unwrapped item: NAME, LIVE
     `live`, its STATUS, and `n/a` in WHEEL, DIALOG and CLI, in the fixed widths, with no trailing space.
   - With no unwrapped item, no separator is printed.
   - Still one write, ASCII only, no SGR (design-system §Surface: cli, pattern 1; layout-templates §Output structure —
     `viola list`).
   - Unit cases in the file's `board_row_*` family:
     - the separator and an unwrapped row literal;
     - an unwrapped name holding `\n`, `\t`, ESC and a C1 character printed as `\xHH` on one line;
     - column offsets equal to the caption's;
     - the empty wrapped rack with unwrapped rows;
     - no separator without unwrapped items.

8. **`viola revive`'s `session-live`** (`src/cmd/revive.rs`).
   - **The refusal.** `Refusal::SessionLive`, detail `session-live`. Its pair is the founder's wording (`inputs#I1`,
     fork 4) with the instance's name: `unable: <name>'s session is open in another claude` and `hint: close it there
     first, or start a copy: viola revive <name> --fork`. No pid, directory or id.
   - **Its place in `preflight_order`.** The chain becomes holder → logged session → `session-live` → recorded
     directory. The read runs only when the logged session passed. It is skipped under `--fork`.
   - **What refuses.** It refuses when a row's `sessionId` equals the id about to be resumed. A failed read passes
     (fail open), and the read's spawn pair lands in `run-<name>.ndjson`, as the wrapper log is open by then.
   - **What a refusal writes.** One `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail:"session-live"}`, no child,
     exit 1, and nothing on stdout (design-system §Surface: cli, pattern 2; layout-templates §Output structure —
     `viola revive`).
   - **The unit cases change with the arity.** The two `preflight_order_*` cases follow the new arity, and one case
     shows that a refused `session-live` takes no directory reading.

9. **The schema.** `schemas/diag-line.v1.json`'s `process-exit` `detail` enum gains `session-live`, its 13th member
   (the rule: the enum's members; obs-plan §6, `detail` code catalog). No other schema value moves: `agents-probe`,
   `claude-agents-json`, `oversize` and `malformed` are already members (research).

10. **The ledger row** (`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs`).
    - `LedgerRow::AgentsJoin` is appended last to `ALL` (23).
    - Its id is `agents-join`, and its words are `claude agents --json names the live session by pid and session id`.
    - `relied_on` is true on every OS (`inputs#I1` fork 1, the `resume-session` precedent), so `relied()` reads 23 on
      Unix and 20 on Windows.
    - Its probe field is the raw capture of the one read.
    - **Its check passes when** the capture parses (step 1) and holds exactly one row whose `pid` equals Run B's
      child pid, whose `sessionId` equals the `session_id` of Run B's first SessionStart capture, and whose status is
      idle or busy.
    - **It fails when** that row is missing, the pid or id differs, or the capture is absent or does not parse.
    - Unit cases in the arm's shape: pass on the recorded shape, each broken post-condition, no capture
      (`check_agents_join_*`).
    - A home stamped before this row reads `cli_verified:false` until its next `viola verify` (the 2026-10-13
      precedent).

11. **The probe in Run B** (`src/cmd/verify/typed.rs`, `src/cmd/verify.rs`).
    - **When it reads.** Once Run B's first turn has settled and before the `/clear` paste
      (`PROBE_LOCAL_COMMAND`, `typed.rs:382`), verify runs step 3's read once: the program Run B spawned,
      `agents --json`, cwd the probe dir, the strip plan, `VERSION_DEADLINE`. The capture goes raw to Run B's captures
      dir.
    - **How it is logged.** One `agents-probe` spawn pair in `cli-<name>.ndjson`, so an uninterrupted verify writes 8
      spawn pairs. A Ctrl-C or TERM stop during the read kills and reaps it under the existing stop rules (no further
      spawn, the pair closed).
    - **What `--record` keeps.** The capture is filtered to the probe's own row (the row whose `pid` is Run B's child)
      and passed through the scrub (home → `~`, the user word → `<user>`, refused whole on a `home-path`
      · `absolute-path` · `username` · `email` survivor). It is written as `Agents.recorded-1.json`. No other
      session's row is kept: the read on a host lists every live session, and their titles are user content.
    - **What it adds to verify.** One more `viola verify` child, ratified by the founder (`inputs#I1` fork 1). No live
      start is added.

12. **The fixture class** — new `schemas/claude-agents-fixture.v1.json`: one JSON array of rows holding the measured
    keys with the measured types. `tests/contract_fixture_hygiene.rs` walks `fixtures/claude/*/Agents.*.json` with it
    as its own class (the `StatusLine.` precedent), and the hook walker skips the prefix.

13. **The fake agent** (`src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs`; verification-harness.md §Fake agent; no env, `inputs#I1`
    fork 2).
    - **The `agents` mode word.** A first word `agents` (beside `statusline-echo`) answers `agents --json`. It reads
      `agents-mode` beside its own executable (`std::env::current_exe`'s directory): `recorded` · `oversize` ·
      `malformed`, with an absent file read as `recorded`.
    - **What each mode prints.** `recorded` prints one JSON array: the rows of `agents-rows.json` beside the exe when
      present (a test plants it, or copies the recorded `Agents.recorded-1.json` there), then one row per live entry
      of `sessions/`. `oversize` prints `MAX_FRAME + 1` bytes, and `malformed` prints non-JSON. Each exits 0.
    - **Its live registry.** In interactive mode, once its launch SessionStart fires, the fake writes
      `sessions/<pid>.json` beside its exe: its pid, that SessionStart's `session_id`, `kind` `interactive`, a status
      word (`busy` from a submitted prompt until its Stop, else `idle`), a synthetic `name`, its `cwd` and `startedAt`.
      It rewrites the entry on each status change and removes it at exit.
    - **Concurrent fakes.** An entry whose pid is not alive is left out of the listing, so concurrent tests sharing
      `fake::FAKE` cannot see each other's dead sessions. Liveness is read from the process table and never by a
      signal (no `kill(pid, 0)`), so the listing ends and signals nothing. The fake removes only the entry it wrote
      itself.
    - **Its option count.** No argv option is added: architecture's twelve options stand, and its mode-word list gains
      `agents`.
    - **Unit cases:** each mode's bytes, the registry listing skipping a dead pid, a malformed rows file read as no
      rows.

14. **The tests' `PATH`** (`tests/support/cli.rs`, `tests/support/fake.rs`).
    - **Why.** A root test starts `viola` with the host's environment (`tests/support/cli.rs:3`). On the dev host
      `claude` is on `PATH`, so a test's `viola list` would read the host's live sessions.
    - **The fix.** Every `viola list` and `viola revive` a root test starts runs with `PATH` set (through
      `Command::env`, never `std::env::set_var`) to a test-scoped bin dir. That dir holds either a per-test copy of the
      fake agent as `claude` with its `agents-mode` / `agents-rows.json`, or nothing at all, which makes a failed read.
    - **The helper.** The copy helper lives in `tests/support/fake.rs`, and the runner in `tests/support/cli.rs` takes
      the bin dir.
    - **What it guarantees.** The existing `cli_list` literals hold unchanged under a bin dir with no `claude`, and no
      test reads the host's sessions.

15. **The root tests.**
    - **`tests/cli_list.rs`:**
      - a booted wrapper whose fake is listed by its registry entry reads `idle`, then `busy` while a scripted turn
        holds;
      - a planted rows file prints the separator and its rows;
      - `oversize` and `malformed` each leave every wrapped item `unknown`, with no `wrapped:false` item, the same
        exit and the same stdout as the no-`claude` case;
      - a `send` naming an unwrapped row's name exits 21 (test-plan §6 E1);
      - under a `VIOLA_NAME`, the agents-probe pair and, for `malformed`, one `parse-rejected` line in
        `cli-<name>.ndjson`, schema-valid.
    - **New `tests/cross_list_rows.rs`** (test-plan §6 Non-path suites, `list` row integrity). A planted rows file
      whose session ids hold `\n`, `\t` and one C1 character. `viola list` runs piped, under `NO_COLOR` and
      `TERM=dumb`, and inside the outer PTY. Each run asserts:
      - stdout is exactly BAY + caption + the wrapped rows + the separator + one line per unwrapped item;
      - every row's column offsets equal the caption's;
      - no raw `\n`, `\t` or C1 byte appears inside a NAME cell;
      - `list --json` keeps each original string.
    - **`tests/cli_revive.rs`:**
      - a revive whose logged id is listed by the fake's registry (a second wrapped fake run with that session id, or
        a planted rows file) is refused, with exit 1, the founder's pair, the hint last, one
        `process-exit{detail:"session-live"}` and no child start;
      - the same with `--fork` passes;
      - a `malformed` read passes (fail open).
    - **The contracts.**
      - `tests/cli_verify.rs`: the `[NN/MM]` lines and the summary at 23 (Unix) and 20 (Windows), and the 8 spawn
        pairs.
      - `tests/contract_ledger_probes.rs`: `agents-join` in the relied lists.
      - `tests/contract_fake_agent_drift.rs`: the fake's `recorded` output over a copied `Agents.recorded-1.json` is
        byte-equal to it, and the fake's registry row has the recorded key set and types.
      - `.config/nextest.toml`: the 20 s kill line gains `binary(cross_list_rows)` when that suite boots a stamped
        wrapper.

16. **The record round** (live, 6 starts: print and Runs A–E, `inputs#I1` fork 3). `viola verify --record` against the
    2.1.287 install by path, fired once through the `[[gate]]` block's live round. It is stamped `23 pass  0 fail`,
    and its `Agents.recorded-1.json` is copied into `fixtures/claude/2.1.287/` (so the set reads 33 files, rule
    `ls fixtures/claude/2.1.287 | wc -l`).

17. **The P4 / P12 leg** (live, 2 starts, attended, `inputs#I1` fork 3). It runs on the headless pty rig, copied byte
    for byte from `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-10-viola-revive/evidence/` (`live-pty.py`, `live-ledger.py`,
    `live-drive.py`; `cmp` each).
    - **Setup.** A home stamped at step 16, the 2.1.287 install dir first on `PATH`, and `VIOLA_NAME` / `VIOLA_DIR` /
      `VIOLA_BIN` removed. Read `hyprctl locked` first (the standing rule), though the rig types no desktop key.
    - (a) **Start 1:** `viola run p4a -- claude`. Read its logged `agent_session_id` S1. `viola list` shows `p4a` with
      STATUS `idle`, and the host's other sessions as unwrapped rows: a count, never their ids.
    - (b) **P12:** `viola send p4a` with `/clear` on stdin. Read the new logged id S2, then read the agents row whose
      `pid` is p4a's child. Does its `sessionId` equal S2 (P12 follows) or S1? No start.
    - (c) **Start 2:** `viola run p4b -- claude --resume S2`, a raw CLI resume through `run`'s trailing words, so the
      new refusal cannot stop the measurement. Classify P4 from p4b's logged `session-start` (cause and id) and the
      agents rows carrying S2 (their count):
      - `refused`: p4b's child exits before any `session-start`;
      - `copied`: p4b's id differs from S2;
      - `two writers`: same id, two live rows.
    - (d) **Only on `two writers`:** stop p4a, then `viola revive p4a`. It must be refused `session-live` with the
      founder's pair and start nothing (no start). On any other P4 reading this revive is not typed, because it would
      start a third session.
    - (e) Stop every session through the rig, then the census.
    - **The record.** `evidence/live-p4.md` and the rig's ledger hold counts, codes, causes and equalities only, never
      an id, a title or a text. If P4 reads `refused` or `copied`, the conversion of `session-live` to a warning is
      named as owed to a new route entry (`inputs#I1` fork 3), never done here.

Every master text, and every leaf the cascade re-derives from one (`.claude/docs/`, `.claude/rules/`, `CLAUDE.md`),
goes through the wrap (§Implementation notes). Implement edits none of them.
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/agents.rs` — the row type, the bounded parse, the status mapping, the join predicate, the property
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/proptest-regressions/agents.txt` — the property's committed regressions
- `src/run/agents.rs` — the bounded `claude agents --json` read
- `fuzz/fuzz_targets/claude_agents_json.rs` — the fuzz target
- `fuzz/corpus/claude_agents_json/` — the synthetic seeds
- `schemas/claude-agents-fixture.v1.json` — the recorded agents class's schema
- `fixtures/claude/2.1.287/Agents.recorded-1.json` — the recorded probe row
- `tests/cross_list_rows.rs` — the row-integrity suite
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/lib.rs` — `mod agents`, re-exports
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs` — `AgentsJoin`, its check and probe field
- `crates/viola-state/src/board.rs` — idle / busy, join keys, the unwrapped item, the join (callers: `cmd/list/read` @ `src/cmd/list.rs:86`; `snapshot_item` @ `board.rs:222`)
- `crates/viola-state/src/snapshot.rs` — `agent_session_id`
- `src/run/send/slot.rs` — the snapshot's `agent_session_id` write on a taken `session-start`
- `src/run/mod.rs` — `mod agents`

- `src/run/version_gate.rs` — the drain's over-the-cap flag, if the agents read shares it (`run_bounded` callers: `verify::run_logged` @ `src/cmd/verify.rs:106`, `version_gate` @ `version_gate.rs:136`)
- `src/cmd/list.rs` — the read and the join
- `src/human/board.rs` — STATUS words, the separator, the unwrapped rows, NAME escaped (`board_rows` @ `write_board`, `board.rs:180`; `write_board` @ `src/cmd/list.rs:57`)
- `src/cmd/revive.rs` — `session-live` (`preflight_order` @ `preflight`, `revive.rs:150`)
- `src/cmd/verify.rs` — the probe's spawn pair and capture
- `src/cmd/verify/typed.rs` — the read in Run B before `/clear`
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs` — the `agents` mode and the session registry
- `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` — `session-live`
- `fuzz/Cargo.toml`, `fuzz/Cargo.lock`, `.gitattributes`, `.config/nextest.toml`

- `tests/cli_list.rs`, `tests/cli_revive.rs`, `tests/cli_verify.rs`, `tests/contract_ledger_probes.rs`, `tests/contract_fixture_hygiene.rs`, `tests/contract_fake_agent_drift.rs`, `tests/support/fake.rs`, `tests/support/cli.rs`

The standing lint and unit entries run first, then the new cases by name. Then comes the live record round, fired once
by `gate.py run --live-legs` and never re-run by the wrap: the non-priming probe, the record entry (6 starts), the
census. The record entry regenerates a committed fixture, so it precedes every entry that reads fixtures: the fixture
guard, the integration binaries, the harness smoke and `pre-push`. On every re-run of the block, the record entry's
`contains stamped 2.1.287  23 pass  0 fail` and the fixture guard assert the round.

The P4 / P12 leg (step 17, 2 starts) is an attended rig measurement, not an entry. No entry produces
`evidence/live-p4.md`, and no criterion other than its own record rests on it. No mutation entry, witness run or
workflow dispatch is listed. The guards name their base `92264a7f254c` (HEAD at P4).

body:
- (arch) `verification-matrix.json#v1-37`: with no live wrapper, `viola list` exits 0 and prints the board. Each
  wrapped instance shows:
  - liveness `live` or `stale` (gone omitted);
  - STATUS `idle` or `busy` from the `claude agents --json` row it joins by `child_pid` or `agent_session_id`, else
    `unknown`;
  - the wheel holder with any budget pause;
  - the pending dialog kind;
  - the CLI verdict.

  Every agents row that joins no wrapped instance prints as a read-only row under `-- UNWRAPPED - READ-ONLY --`, with
  `n/a` in WHEEL, DIALOG and CLI and `wrapped: false` in `--json`. A `send` naming one exits 21. Human output is the
  six-column board with its BAY line, every row one line with every control character (`\n` and `\t` included)
  escaped as `\xHH`. `--json` is `{"v":1,"ok":{"items","budget","skipped"}}`. It is proved under the fake agent by
  `binary(cli_list) | binary(cross_list_rows)` on the three CI OSes (the integration entry, the CI entry). The GUI
  envelope clause is out of 0.1.0 by the founder's ruling of 2026-10-16 (v1-37's notes) (per architecture §Standard
  Contracts, `list` payload and Session liveness).

- (arch) An absent, failed, oversize or malformed `claude agents --json` read leaves `viola list`'s exit and stdout
  equal to the no-`claude` case: every wrapped item `unknown`, no `wrapped:false` item, no liveness changed (per
  architecture §Standard Contracts, Session liveness).

- (arch) `LedgerRow::ALL` holds twenty-three rows, the last `agents-join`, relied on every OS. `viola verify` prints
  `[NN/MM]` with `MM` = 23 on Unix and 20 on Windows, and the record round prints `stamped 2.1.287  23 pass  0 fail`
  (per architecture §Established Decisions [CLI Version Compatibility]).

- (security) The agents child is spawned directly from the resolved program under the R8 strip, its stdout read
  through `take(MAX_FRAME + 1)`, killed at 5 s. An unwrapped name is never a `ViolaName`, and every agents-derived
  field printed on the board is `\xHH`-escaped (per security-plan §Input Validation, Child process output row;
  §Bootstrap phases, `logging-redaction-wire`).

- (security) The committed `Agents.recorded-1.json` holds only the probe's own row, passes the `--record` scrub and
  the hygiene walk with no `home-path` · `absolute-path` · `username` · `email` survivor, and `cargo deny
  --manifest-path fuzz/Cargo.toml check advisories sources` reads green (per security-plan §Data Protection,
  Repository fixtures; §Dependency Security).

- (design) `viola revive` on an id live elsewhere prints exactly `unable: <name>'s session is open in another claude`
  then `hint: close it there first, or start a copy: viola revive <name> --fork` on stderr. It exits 1 with an empty
  stdout and starts no child. `--fork` passes the reading, and a failed read passes (per design-system §Surface: cli,
  pattern 2; `inputs#I1` fork 4).

- (layouts) An unwrapped name holding `\n`, `\t`, ESC and a C1 character prints as hex text inside one line. Every
  row's column offsets equal the caption's, no line ends in a space, and no separator prints without an unwrapped
  item (per layout-templates §Component — Primary content block 1: `viola list` strip rows).

- (obs) Each agents read under an open log writes one `agents-probe` spawn pair holding no row text, id, `cwd` or
  path. A malformed read writes one `parse-rejected{parser:"claude-agents-json", detail:"malformed"}` at `warn`. A
  `session-live` refusal writes one `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail:"session-live"}`, and
  `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` admits it (per obs-plan §6 Log Coverage).

- (tests) The parser's property runs at `cases: 512` with its regressions file committed, and the
  `claude_agents_json` target replays green under `run --fuzz-replay` (per test-plan §6 Non-path suites, Property
  suite).

- (tests) Every test-started `viola list` and `viola revive` runs under a test-scoped `PATH`, so no test reads the
  host's sessions (per test-plan §11 Test Anti-Patterns, Test Strategy).

- (live) The record round and the P4 / P12 leg together start at most 8 `claude` sessions, each named in the round's
  log or the rig's ledger (`inputs#I1` fork 3).
- Research: `research.md`, its measured readings, and its graph trace `tree-query-2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board.json`.
- The founder's answers: `inputs#I1`.

- **The CLI's `name` as the unwrapped NAME.** Rejected because it is a free-text title (user content), and the cli
  bans upstream text on the board.
- **A `FAKE_CLAUDE_AGENTS_MODE` env seam.** Rejected by the founder (`inputs#I1` fork 2): the files beside the exe.

- **A second probe read after `/clear`.** Rejected because it is wider than the 7 → 8 spawn pairs the fork stated.
  P12 is measured in the P4 leg.

- **Reading `~/.claude/sessions/`, the CLI's own registry.** Rejected: viola reads and writes nothing under
  `~/.claude`, and the read is the documented subcommand.

- **Gating `list`'s or `revive`'s read on the stamp of the `claude` on `PATH`.** Rejected: architecture makes the
  read an enrichment whose failure is never an error. The stamp gates the wrapped instance's own `cli_verified`.
- **Truncating unwrapped names, or colouring the new rows.** Not this chunk: "CLI output discipline".
- **Converting `session-live` to a warning on a P4 reading.** Not this chunk: a new route entry (`inputs#I1` fork 3).

- **A `boot --agents-mode` flag, and `status` running `viola list`.** Not this chunk: "End-to-end path binary and
  harness legs".

- **The tests' `PATH` comes first** (step 14). Without it the first `viola list` a test starts on the dev host reads
  this host's live sessions, measured at 11 rows at P3.

- **Concurrency in the registry.** Tests share `fake::FAKE`, so its `sessions/` sits beside the shared binary. Each
  fake removes its own entry at exit, and the listing skips dead pids.

- **The verify probe under the fake agent.** The probe's post-condition reads the fake's registry row for Run B's own
  pid. Other tests' live fakes add rows with other pids, which the "exactly one row with this pid" check ignores.

  - architecture §Standard Contracts (Session liveness) — the read is built. The join field is the `agents-join` row,
    and both keys are measured exposed. The "open item" sentence is retired.
  - architecture §Established Decisions [CLI Version Compatibility] — twenty-three rows, relied 23 / 20, verify's
    child set and spawn pairs gain the agents probe (the founder's ratification, `inputs#I1` fork 1).
  - architecture §Occupied Resources — the fake agent's mode words gain `agents`, with its files beside the exe and no
    env. The fixture set's count and the fuzz target list move.
  - security-plan §Threat Model Summary and §Input Validation — the agents spawn is landed for `list` and `revive`. A
    seventh verify spawn kind is ratified (`inputs#I1` fork 1).
  - test-plan §7 Seed strategies — the `FAKE_CLAUDE_AGENTS_MODE` seed row becomes the files beside the exe
    (`inputs#I1` fork 2). Also §6 (the property, the fuzz target, `cross_list_rows`), §5 (the ledger literals).
  - obs-plan §6 — `session-live` in the `process-exit` detail catalog, `oversize` for `claude-agents-json`, and the
    verify spawn-pair count. §1's cause lists.
  - design-system §Surface: cli patterns 1 and 2 — the As-built note's "not built" clauses retired, and the
    `session-live` pair added (the founder's wording, `inputs#I1` fork 4).
  - layout-templates §Output structure — `viola list` and `viola revive` — the unwrapped rack as built, and the sixth
    revive pair.
  - a11y-plan §1, §4 (P6), §8 — the separator and the agents fixture-row case landed. §8 Timeout extensions gains the
    5 s agents-read bound, which falls on no keystroke.

data.head: ## Measured on the Linux dev host (P3, 2026-10-16)

body:
Each reading printed only shapes, never session content (scripts in the session scratchpad: a key/type/closed-value
census, a pid lookup, a `name`-field form census).

- `claude --version` → `2.1.296 (Claude Code)` (mise `latest`). Also installed: `2.1.287` (the stamped set's
  version), `2.1.288`, `2.1.289` (`ls ~/.local/share/mise/installs/claude/`). Both `2.1.296/claude` and
  `2.1.287/claude` are native ELF x86-64 executables (`file -L`).

- `claude agents --json` on 2.1.296: one JSON array of 11 rows (2 911 bytes).
  - Every row's key set is exactly `cwd, kind, name, pid, sessionId, startedAt, status`.
  - Types: `pid` and `startedAt` are integers (`startedAt` 13 digits, epoch ms); the other five are strings.
  - `status` ∈ {`busy`, `idle`}, `kind` ∈ {`interactive`}, and all 11 `sessionId` values are lowercase 8-4-4-4-12
    UUIDs.
  - On 2.1.287 the same census gives the same 7 keys, types and closed values.
  - The study's 2.1.283 field set (`refs/session-memory-options.md` §1 M5) therefore still holds on both builds.

- `claude agents --json --all` adds one `background` row of another shape: `cwd, id, kind, name, sessionId, startedAt,
  state`, with no `pid` and no `status`. viola reads no `--all` (the scope's read is the bare `--json`).

- **Known positive** (this builder session's own `claude`, pid 3231528, the shell's parent): exactly 1 row whose
  `pid` equals it, `status: busy`, `kind: interactive`, read while a turn was running. **Control:** pid 1 → 0 rows.

- The `name` field is a free-text session title, not an id. Across the 11 rows it was 9–35 characters, one row held
  spaces and non-ASCII, and none equalled or prefixed its `sessionId`. It is user content.
- Wall time of one read: 124 / 126 / 127 ms (2.1.296), 115 ms (2.1.287) (`date +%s%N` around each call).

- Not measured here, on purpose:
  - What the R8 strip changes in this output. Listing this session's `CLAUDE*` names would cross the credential
    boundary; that answer is spent, per the 2026-10-07 security sidecar entry.
  - P4 (an interactive `--resume` of a live id).
  - P12 (`sessionId` after `/clear`).
  - Each needs a live start, which is the plan's to ask for.

- `src/cmd/list.rs` (full) — `list` = `board::scan` (strict-modes, before any log) → `client::start` under a name →
  `read` (`board::read`, `read_budget_stamped`, `read_thresholds`) → one `--json` document or `human::write_board`.
  No `claude` resolution and no child spawn today. `document` serialises `board.items` whole.

- `crates/viola-state/src/board.rs` (1–260) — `SessionStatus` has one variant, `Unknown`. `Item` has `wrapped: bool`,
  `status`, optional `wheel` / `budget_paused` / `cli_version` / `cli_verified`, and a non-serialised `dialog_kind`.
  `snapshot_item` and the replayed arm set `wrapped: true, status: Unknown`. `read` takes `(scan, now)` and has no join
  input. It already runs one whole `log_pass` per snapshot-read instance for the skip counts.

- `crates/viola-state/src/snapshot.rs` (30–90) — `InstanceSnapshot` holds `child_pid: Option<u32>` but **no
  `agent_session_id`** (see Graph impact and the closure).

- `src/human/board.rs` (1–240) — `board_rows` pads NAME to `max(4, longest name)` and lays out the five fixed widths
  (`LIVE_WIDTH` 5, `STATUS_WIDTH` 7, `WHEEL_WIDTH` 23, `DIALOG_WIDTH` 17, CLI unpadded). `escape_row` is applied only
  in `cli_cell`. NAME is printed raw, which is safe today because every name is a `ViolaName`. `write_board` makes one
  write of BAY, caption, rows, or `EMPTY_BOARD`.
- `src/human/escape.rs` (`escape_row`, line 20) — escapes every control character, `\n` / `\t` / DEL / C1 included.

- `src/cmd/revive.rs` (40–230) — `Refusal { StrictModes, NoSession, UnknownId, CwdMissing }` with `detail()` / `pair()`.

title: 1. The read: `claude agents --json`, once per `list` (entry; CARRY 1)

data.head: ### 1. The read: `claude agents --json`, once per `list` (entry; CARRY 1)

body: - `viola list` runs `claude agents --json` once and joins its rows to the wrapped instances.

- Measured at P3 on 2.1.296 and on 2.1.287 alike:
  - one JSON array whose rows each hold exactly `cwd, kind, name, pid, sessionId, startedAt, status`;
  - `pid` and `startedAt` (epoch ms) are integers;
  - `status` ∈ {`busy`, `idle`}, `kind` = `interactive`, and every `sessionId` is a lowercase UUID.

  This is the study's 2.1.283 field set unchanged (`refs/session-memory-options.md` §1 M5). `--all` adds a
  `background` row of another shape (no `pid`, no `status`). viola reads the bare `--json`. One read takes about
  125 ms (`research.md` §Measured).

- [premise-corrected: `run_bounded` (`src/run/version_gate.rs:41`) drains stdout through `take(MAX_FRAME)` and keeps
  no over-the-cap flag, so an over-`MAX_FRAME` output reads as a cap-length one] The spawn follows the security
  plan's child rules: a direct spawn of the resolved program (never a `.cmd` / `.bat` shim, never through a shell),
  under the R8 strip, killed at a time bound (`list` "works with no live wrapper" and must not hang on a stuck child).
  Its stdout is read through `take(MAX_FRAME + 1)`, so an over-cap output is told apart and read as a failure.

- The parse is tolerant and closed: an over-`MAX_FRAME`, malformed, absent or failed read leaves every wrapped row
  `unknown` and lists no unwrapped row, and `list` never fails or changes exit on it (architecture §Standard Contracts,
  Session liveness; test-plan §6; a row `name` never becomes a `ViolaName`, test-plan §4).

title: 2. idle/busy STATUS on wrapped rows (entry; CARRY 1)

data.head: ### 2. idle/busy STATUS on wrapped rows (entry; CARRY 1)

body: - A wrapped row's STATUS becomes `idle` or `busy` from the agents row it joins, else `unknown`.

- The mapping is one to one over the measured values (`status` ∈ {`busy`, `idle`}, P3). A value outside them reads
  `unknown`.

- Every agents row that joins no wrapped instance is listed as an unwrapped read-only row: `wrapped: false`,
  `liveness: "live"`, `dialog_pending: false`, no `wheel` / `budget_paused` / `cli_version` / `cli_verified`
  (architecture §Standard Contracts, `list` payload). On the human board it sits under the
  `-- UNWRAPPED - READ-ONLY --` separator, after every wrapped row, with `n/a` in WHEEL, DIALOG and CLI (design-system
  §Surface: cli, pattern 1; layout-templates §Output structure — `viola list`).

- Rows escape every control character through the existing `escape_row` (`src/human/escape.rs:20`), over the call's
  own fields (CARRY 1: "the rows' escape on that call's fields"). As built, NAME is printed raw (`board_rows`) because
  every name is a `ViolaName`. An unwrapped name is not one.

- An unwrapped row is never a valid target (v1-37's requirement; test-plan §6, E1; security-plan §Security
  Anti-Patterns, Input). Its name is not a `ViolaName`.

- [premise-corrected: the CLI's `name` field is a free-text session title (9–35 chars, spaces and non-ASCII
  measured, never equal to `sessionId`), while architecture names the unwrapped `name` "the session identifier" and
  the design sample shows a hex id] Which field fills the unwrapped NAME cell and the `--json` `name` is a P4 fork.
  The design and layout sources fix the rest of the rack: no seventh column, no pid.

title: 4. The join field: a capability-ledger row with its probe (CARRY 5; CARRY 1)

data.head: ### 4. The join field: a capability-ledger row with its probe (CARRY 5; CARRY 1)

body:
- CARRY 5, verbatim in substance: the `claude agents --json` join-field ledger row (child pid or session id) and its
  `viola verify` probe land here. It was moved from "Owed ledger rows" at that chunk's wrap on the founder's own answer
  to its P4 fork 2 («К потребителю»).

- CARRY 1 names the join field as coming "from 'Paste newline ledger row'". Re-verified at P1: that entry and "Owed
  ledger rows" are complete and neither landed the row. `LedgerRow::ALL` holds 22 rows
  (`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs:47`), none of them for `agents --json`. CARRY 5's later move to this entry
  is the standing owner, and the CARRY 1 phrase is a stale coordinate.

- Both candidate fields are exposed (P3: `pid` and `sessionId` on every row). On this host `claude` is a native ELF
  executable, so the PTY's `child_pid` is the `claude` process the agents row names. Known positive: this builder
  session's own pid read exactly one row, `busy`.

- [premise-corrected: `InstanceSnapshot` (`crates/viola-state/src/snapshot.rs:39-69`) has `child_pid` but no
  `agent_session_id`, although architecture §Standard Contracts (Instance snapshot) lists `agent_session_id?` "only to
  join `claude agents --json` rows"; the id is held only in the log (replay) and in the send slot's memory] Whether the
  join keys on `child_pid` alone or also on a snapshot `agent_session_id` the wrapper starts writing is a P4 fork.

- The study's P12 (does `sessionId` follow the new id after `/clear`?) decides whether a session-id join survives a
  `/clear`. The `list` join and the revive preflight both rely on it (`refs/session-memory-options.md` §5, P12). Run
  B already pastes `/clear` (`FRAMING_TURNS`, `ledger.rs:206-211`), so a second probe read after that paste could
  measure P12 inside Run B (`research.md`). Amended at P5 validation-1, intent-incomplete: the founder's answer
  (`inputs#I1` fork 1) stated one added verify child, spawn pairs 7 → 8. The probe therefore reads once, before
  `/clear`, and P12 is measured in the P4 leg with no added start (`plan.md` step 17 (b)).

- The cost frame of the previous ledger-row chunks stands (arch, security, tests history files of this run dir):
  - A new row joining the relied set (`LedgerRow::relied()`, `ledger.rs:149`) leaves every home stamped before it
    `cli_verified:false` until re-stamped.
  - Each new row states on which OS it is relied.
  - A probe that adds a `viola verify` child or a live start is a boundary widening of verify's child set, ruled only
    by the founder's own word, with a live-start cap of its own (the CARRY of "Resume and compact ledger rows", its
    `scope.md` §0; `.andromeda/playbook.md`, "Boundary widening").

  Whether the row is relied (gating `cli_verified`), or only a ledger record exempt under the ruled limit because no
  `send` relies on it, is a P4 fork.

- Deferred to this entry by chunk 2026-09-24-fake-agent-and-test-data-fixtures: the fake agent answers
  `agents --json` with `FAKE_CLAUDE_AGENTS_MODE=recorded|oversize|malformed` (test-plan §7 seed table,
  `.andromeda/test-plan.md:926`), its shape pinned against a recorded `claude agents --json` output.

- [premise-corrected: architecture §Occupied Resources lists the fake agent's interface as argv options with no env,
  and the env seam list is closed at two founder-ratified seams; test-plan §7's env channel contradicts it (P2
  aggregate C)] The mode channel is a P4 fork. Today the fake agent reads no mode env and lets
  `claude agents --json` fall through to interactive mode (`src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs:917-973`).

- The recording lands under `fixtures/claude/<cli-version>/` beside the existing sets. 2.1.287, the stamped set's
  version, is still installed on this host (P3). It passes the `--record` scrub (no home path, absolute path, username
  or email): the rows' `cwd` is an absolute path, so it is rewritten or the recording is refused. It holds no session
  content, and it takes a fixture class and schema of its own (the `StatusLine.` precedent,
  `tests/contract_fixture_hygiene.rs:24-60`).

title: 6. The parser's property and fuzz target (CARRY 3; CARRY 1)

data.head: ### 6. The parser's property and fuzz target (CARRY 3; CARRY 1)

body:
- The `claude agents --json` parser over arbitrary JSON takes a proptest property (`cases: 512`, committed seeds),
  a `fuzz/fuzz_targets/` target and a seeded corpus (test-plan §6 Property suite).
  - The fuzz pipeline today holds `channel_frame`, `hook_stdin`, `paste_text`, `viola_name` and `vt100_feed`.

title: 7. `viola revive` refuses a session id live elsewhere (entry; CARRY 4)

data.head: ### 7. `viola revive` refuses a session id live elsewhere (entry; CARRY 4)

body:
- From chunk 2026-10-10-viola-revive (the founder's answer to its review card, relayed; that chunk's snapshot
  `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-10-viola-revive/inputs/I5-relay-1.md.txt`, point 1): the `session-live` preflight refusal reads `claude agents --json` for a row whose session id is the one
  about to be resumed. Until it lands, viola does not refuse a revive of an id live elsewhere.

- It joins revive's preflight order (`already-live` · `no-session` · `cwd-missing`, `src/cmd/revive.rs`). The
  strict-modes check runs ahead of the preflight and of the wrapper log (since chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor).

- The design and layout rules forbid the pid that the study's wording names (study §3 V2: "refuse `session-live`
  (naming the pid)"). The refusal's `unable:` / `hint:` pair names no pid.

- Two of the study's measurements travel with it (`refs/session-memory-options.md` §5):
  - **P4**: is an interactive `claude --resume <id>` of a live id refused, copied, or two writers on one transcript?
    The answer decides whether `session-live` is a refusal or a warning.
  - **P12**: the `/clear` id follow (§4 above).

- `--fork` (→ `--fork-session`, `resume_args(&id, args.fork)`, `src/cmd/revive.rs:165`) is the study's opt-in escape
  (§3 V2), so a forked revive skips the `session-live` reading.

- A failed or unparseable agents read fails open and revive proceeds as today (architecture §Standard Contracts: the
  read's failure "is never an error"; the human always wins). Whether that is right for a refusal that guards two
  writers on one transcript is a P4 question if P4's measurement reads "two writers".

- The new refusal is a closed `process-exit` detail: the 13th member of `schemas/diag-line.v1.json`'s
  `process-exit.detail`, which is closed at 12. Exit 1, a revive preflight refusal (`.claude/rules/api.md` §CLI).

- `verification-matrix.json#v1-37` is unclaimed. Its notes record the board chunk's advance and what is still owed:
  idle/busy status, the unwrapped rows, and the GUI-envelope equality. The 2026-10-16 note took the GUI-envelope
  clause out of 0.1.0 by the founder's ruling. The CLI half stands unweakened. This chunk is the cap's last named
  owner. Every clause left once the GUI clause is out is built here or already built by the board chunk. Whether the
  concretized acceptance is provable at this chunk's wrap is P5 step 4's.

- [premise-corrected: no `viola-mcp` crate exists (`ls crates/`), so there is no MCP `list` reader to extend] The MCP
  `list` tool is "MCP server for drivers"'s. The colour layer and width-known truncation on `list` are "CLI output
  discipline"'s. `--json` on `viola revive` is "CLI machine contract"'s. The harness's `status` running `viola list`
  (and a `boot --agents-mode` flag with it) is "End-to-end path binary and harness legs"'s.

- Windows readings of `claude agents --json` and of the join row are owed to "Windows-only live measurements", like
  every earlier row's Windows leg. This chunk measures on the Linux dev host.
- No kill of any session: viola never kills a session it did not spawn in this process (study §3, failure-mode table).
- The GUI sessions envelope is 0.2.0's (the founder's ruling, 2026-10-16, on v1-37's notes).
