- **Base:** `f6bcce5ba21a` (HEAD at P4; every git read in the gate block names it)

Close the CLI's machine contract (architecture §Standard Contracts "CLI `--json` output", §Conventions "CLI exit
codes", §Cross-cutting Config management; security-plan §Input Validation CLI row). Seven driver-facing verbs already
print one `--json` document and a typed exit (research §Findings); `viola revive` is the one verb with no machine form
(architecture [CLI Conventions]). This chunk gives it one on both arms, files `revive --list` under the `cli` role log
and so retires obs-plan §10's sixth exemption (CARRY 2). It also lands the documented home resolution order (`--home`,
then the `VIOLA_DIR` grandparent, then the default) with the home canonicalised (CARRY 1; `inputs#I2`), names the
scanned instance on `state-recovered` (CARRY 3), and adds the completeness witness that no flag, `VIOLA_*` variable or
`config.json` key switches off a control. One witness then reads every verb's document and literal exit side by side.

It also removes the cause of the last wrap's red CI, folded on the operator's word (`inputs#I1`, scope §7):
`ci#38994749835` failed `test (ubuntu-latest)` on two `setting_does_not_disable_the_budget_gate` cases, each
`viola verify did not stamp the home … failing rows ["resume-session"]`, on code that built green one run earlier.
That part is measured first, because every `stamped_home` case (20 binaries, research §Sweeps) rests on the stamp.

`run` and `verify` gain no `--json`: `run` is the interactive wrapper, and `verify`'s agent-readable outcome is its
step lines, summary and exit (leaned per architecture [CLI Conventions] and architecture-amendments
`2026-09-28-capability-ledger-and-viola-verify`).

title: Part A — the last wrap's red CI (scope §7), first

data.head: ### Part A — the last wrap's red CI (scope §7), first

body:
1. **Read the recorded run.** Download `ci#38994749835`'s `harness-ubuntu-latest` and `diag-ubuntu-latest` artifacts
   into `target/ci-38994749835/` (`gh run download 38994749835 -n <name> -D target/ci-38994749835/<name>`). Read what
   they keep for the two failing cases. Write `evidence/ci-red.md`: what the artifact holds, and whether it shows which
   of the `resume-session` check's arms failed (no Run E capture, another id, another source:
   `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs` `check_resume_session` cases at ledger.rs:2988-3050).

2. **Force the window on this host.** Add the root case
   `stamped_home_concurrent_verify_runs_each_stamp_the_home` to `tests/cli_verify.rs`. It starts three `viola verify`
   runs against the fake agent from three threads released by one `std::sync::Barrier`. Each run uses its own fresh
   `TestHome` and the same call `stamped_home` makes (`tests/support/verify.rs`). The case asserts that each exits 0
   with the `stamped 2.1.287  <n> pass  0 fail` summary, and on failure prints each run's failing row ids. Hold the
   case to the root tests' kill: three concurrent stamps at about 4.4 s each (research: the CI timings), well under the
   20 s CI kill. Check it against the `mutants` profile's 10 s kill (testing.md 2026-09-24, extended 2026-10-06), and
   record the measured wall in `evidence/ci-red.md`. Run it on the unchanged tree through entry
   `run --integration --filter 'test(/stamped_home_concurrent_/)'` until it reads red, at most 20 firings. Each red's
   failing rows and the Run E captures go in the evidence, read before the next firing overwrites the log
   (verification-harness.md 2026-09-29).

3. **Name the cause, then remove it.** From steps 1-2, name the mechanism in `evidence/ci-red.md` as the equality
   that decides the case: which shared input two simultaneous verify runs read, at which `file:line`. Remove the
   cause at its site, which is one of `src/cmd/verify/typed.rs` (`resume_run`, typed.rs:251), `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs`
   (its resume path or `Registry`, viola-fake-agent.rs:753-795) or `tests/support/home.rs` (`stamped_home`,
   home.rs:347). Never raise a bound, add a retry or serialise the tests (Constraints).
   **STOP rule:** if 20 forced firings and the artifact read give no red and no cause, stop and report for a plan
   revision. Write that reading into `evidence/ci-red.md`. Part A is never shipped blind, and Parts B-E go on only
   after the report is read.

4. **The witness both ways.** After the fix, step 2's case reads green across 20 firings. With the fix reverted in
   place (the remove-the-guard run, testing.md 2026-09-25), the same case reads red on the unchanged tree. Record
   both readings with their failing rows. The acceptance's last half is CI: the push entry's run reads `test
   (ubuntu-latest)` green.

title: Part B — the home: resolution order and canonicalisation (scope §4; `inputs#I2`)

data.head: ### Part B — the home: resolution order and canonicalisation (scope §4; `inputs#I2`)

body:
5. **One `VIOLA_DIR` shape check.** Move `instance_of` (src/cmd/hook.rs:80-97) to `src/cmd/mod.rs` as `pub(super)`,
   unchanged. `hook` keeps calling it, and it is the one validation of `VIOLA_NAME` + `VIOLA_DIR`: a valid
   `ViolaName`, an absolute dir ending `instances/<name>`, the home its grandparent.

6. **`resolve_home` in the documented order** (src/cmd/mod.rs:174). Make it take its inputs as arguments (the
   `--home` value, `VIOLA_NAME`, `VIOLA_DIR`, the user home) so a unit table covers it. The order: `--home` as given,
   else the `instance_of` home when both variables pass the shape check, else `<user home>/.viola`. A `VIOLA_DIR` that
   fails the check is not a home: the order falls through to the default, never refuses. `dispatch`'s ten call sites
   (resolve_home @ src/cmd/mod.rs:80, 93, 105, 110, 115, 120, 126, 135, 140, 145) pass `std::env` values read once.
   `default_home` stays shared with `statusline_source` (src/cmd/run.rs:491), so "only the default home falls back to
   `~/.claude/settings.json`" still keys on `cmd::default_home(user_home)`. A home reached through `VIOLA_DIR` is not
   the default home.

7. **Canonicalise the resolved home once it exists.** One helper in `src/cmd/mod.rs`: when the path exists,
   `std::fs::canonicalize`, then on Windows a `\\?\C:\…` verbatim-disk result is written back in its plain `C:\…`
   form (`std::path::Prefix::VerbatimDisk`; any other verbatim form stays as canonicalised). When the path does not
   exist yet, keep the `std::path::absolute` spelling. Every non-`run` verb calls it in `dispatch`. `run`
   (src/cmd/run.rs:232) calls it right after the home is created and before any read under it, so `endpoint_path`
   (run.rs:463), `VIOLA_DIR` for the child and every log open take the one canonical spelling. `list` against a home
   that does not exist still creates nothing (`list_of_a_home_that_does_not_exist_creates_nothing`).

8. **Tests take the resolved home.** `tests/support/cli.rs` `start` (cli.rs:101-115) and `tests/support/home.rs`
   `boot_with` drop `VIOLA_DIR` and `VIOLA_BIN` beside `VIOLA_NAME` on every child. This host's sessions carry all
   three (research §Sweeps), and a default-home boot passes no `--home`. `tests/support/start.rs` computes
   `endpoint_name` over the canonicalised test home. `tests/cli_instance_state.rs`'s
   `run_in_the_default_home_reads_the_user_settings` (cli_instance_state.rs:408) compares the canonicalised
   `<user home>/.viola`. Re-read every site the `default_of_user` and `endpoint_name(` sweeps name (research §Sweeps)
   before running Part B's gates.
9. **The flag.** Add `--json` to `ReviveArgs` (src/cmd/revive.rs:20), allowed beside `--list` and on the start arm.

10. **Exit-1 documents.** Each refusal is one stdout document `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` with empty
    stderr and exit 1. The code is `Refusal::detail` (revive.rs:59-66): `strict-modes-failed`, `no-session` (both of
    its pairs), `session-live` and `cwd-missing`, plus `already-live` from `run`'s collision check on revive's
    preflight (`collision_check`). Add the writer to `src/cmd/client.rs` beside `fault` / `unreachable`, as one write
    through `document`. Without `--json` every pair stays byte-identical (several are the founder's wording). A refused
    strict-modes check still opens nothing under the home and writes no line on either arm (security-plan
    §Authentication & Authorization; obs-plan §10 exemption 7, untouched).

11. **`--list --json`.** Print one document `{"v":1,"ok":{"sessions":[{"ts":"…","cause":"…","id":"…"}]}}` with the
    rows in log order, carrying the fields `list_rows` builds (revive.rs:248-261: the escaped `ts`, the cause word and
    the session-shaped id), and exit 0. With no row, print the `no-session` document and exit 1. Without `--json` the
    rows stay `<ts>  <cause>  <id>`, byte-identical.

12. **`--list` opens the `cli` role log.** `role_of` (src/main.rs:91-110) files `revive` followed by `--list` (after
    any `--home` pair) under `Role::Cli`, while the start arm stays `Role::Other` and logs as `run`. `revive --list`
    runs its strict-modes check first (revive.rs:229). Only after a passed check, and only under a parsed
    `VIOLA_NAME`, does it open `cli-<name>.ndjson` through `client::start`'s path and write `process-start` …
    `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code, detail}`: `no-session` on its empty-chain exit 1, none on exit 0. A dispatch
    `Err` or panic then reaches the `cli` catch site: one `panic` line plus `process-exit{detail:"internal-error"}`, and
    exactly `error: internal error` (obs-plan §7).

title: Part D — `state-recovered` names the scanned instance (scope §6, CARRY 3)

data.head: ### Part D — `state-recovered` names the scanned instance (scope §6, CARRY 3)

body:
13. **The field.** In `read_snapshot_or_replay` (crates/viola-state/src/replay.rs:150-170), the line gains `scanned`:
    the instance dir's last component when it parses as a `ViolaName`, absent otherwise (null as absence). `instance`
    stays the caller's, set by `obs_event!`. Its callers' signatures are unchanged (board.rs, revive.rs). Add
    `scanned` to `schemas/diag-line.v1.json`'s `state-recovered` row (schema line 82-84) as a string matching the
    `ViolaName` pattern the schema already uses for `instance`. The other `state-recovered` emitter (events.rs, the
    torn-line heal) does not write it.

title: Part E — the completeness witness and the per-verb witness (scope §2, §5)

data.head: ### Part E — the completeness witness and the per-verb witness (scope §2, §5)

body:
14. **`schemas/config.v1.json`.** A tolerant schema (`additionalProperties` allowed): `v` (const 1),
    `diagnostics_level` (`info` | `debug`), `claude_env_keep` (an array of at most 32 strings matching
    `^CLAUDE[A-Z0-9_]*$`), `five_hour` and `seven_day` (integers 0-100). A unit in `src/obs.rs`'s test module pins
    `CONFIG_KEYS` (obs.rs:32-38) equal to the schema's property names as a set.

15. **The completeness case** in `tests/cli_controls_not_disableable.rs`. The literal table holds the global flag
    `--home`, the variables `VIOLA_NAME`, `VIOLA_DIR` and `VIOLA_BIN`, and the five keys. It fails when `viola --help`'s
    options list a long flag the table lacks (`--help` and `--version` excepted, named in the case), or when the schema
    lists a key the table lacks. The table's new rows hold:
    - `VIOLA_DIR` naming a 0770 home's instance dir: `viola list` with no `--home` exits 21 with the
      `instance-unreachable` document. The strict-modes scan still runs on the home the variable chose.
    - `VIOLA_BIN` and `VIOLA_NAME` set to disabling-shaped values: the `send` paste control still refuses a control
      character with exit 13.
    - `diagnostics_level` and `claude_env_keep` given disabling-shaped values (`"off"`, `"debug,trace"`, `[""]`,
      `["*"]`): an identity-floor `CLAUDE*` name is still stripped from the child (`tui_env_strip`'s reading), and the
      budget gate rows stand.

16. **The per-verb witness**, new root file `tests/cli_machine_contract.rs`, integration layer by its stem. For each
    of `send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `list`, `pause`, `release`, `revive`, `revive --list`, one rstest row per
    outcome reached on a stamped home: the literal `--json` document's keys and code, empty stderr, and the literal
    exit (0, 1, 2, 10, 13, 20, 21 as each verb reaches them; 11, 12 and 14 by name in the cases that already pin them,
    cited in the file's doc comment: `tests/cli_budget.rs`, `tests/cli_answer.rs`, `src/cmd/send.rs`
    `exit_of_is_the_closed_table`). Plus three home cases:
    - the resolution order, with `--home` beating `VIOLA_DIR`, `VIOLA_DIR` beating the default, and a malformed
      `VIOLA_DIR` falling to the default;
    - two homes isolated: a wrapper under home A, then `list --json` under home B shows no item, and every state file
      the wrapper wrote is under A's canonical path;
    - a `--home` reached through a symlink canonicalised (`cfg(unix)`): the snapshot's endpoint matches
      `endpoint_name` over the resolved path.

17. **Revive and list cases.** In `tests/cli_revive.rs`, each exit-1 refusal under `--json` (one document, empty
    stderr, exit 1, its code), `--list --json` (rows and the empty case), `--list`'s log pair under a `VIOLA_NAME`, no
    line on a refused check, and the human pairs and rows unchanged. In `tests/cli_list.rs`,
    `e5_list_reads_a_live_wrapper_through_the_replay` asserts `scanned` beside the caller's `instance`.
    `tests/contract_diag_schema.rs` validates a `state-recovered` line with and without `scanned`.
- `tests/cli_machine_contract.rs` — the per-verb `--json` / exit witness and the three home cases (step 16).
- `schemas/config.v1.json` — the tolerant `config.json` schema (step 14).
- `src/cmd/mod.rs` — `instance_of` (moved), `resolve_home` in the documented order, the canonicalising helper (steps 5-7).
- `src/cmd/hook.rs` — calls the moved `instance_of` (step 5).
- `src/cmd/run.rs` — the home canonicalised after creation (step 7).
- `src/cmd/revive.rs` — `--json` on both arms; `--list`'s `cli` log (steps 9-12).
- `src/cmd/client.rs` — the exit-1 error document writer (step 10).
- `src/main.rs` — `role_of`: `revive --list` → `Role::Cli` (step 12).
- `crates/viola-state/src/replay.rs` — `scanned` on `state-recovered` (step 13).
- `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` — the `scanned` field (step 13).
- `src/obs.rs` — test module only: the `CONFIG_KEYS` pin (step 14).
- `tests/cli_controls_not_disableable.rs` — the completeness case and its rows (step 15).
- `tests/cli_revive.rs`, `tests/cli_list.rs`, `tests/contract_diag_schema.rs` — step 17.
- `tests/support/cli.rs`, `tests/support/home.rs`, `tests/support/start.rs`, `tests/cli_instance_state.rs` — step 8.
- `tests/cli_verify.rs` — the concurrent-start witness (step 2).
- One of `src/cmd/verify/typed.rs`, `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs`, `tests/support/home.rs` — the red's cause (step 3; provisional until it is named).

Agent-driven: the harness `run` suites carry the cases; the boot smoke mints one session and reads it back by that
id. There is no live leg against an external process (no `claude` start). The operator pass fires hygiene, the push
and the CI read; the CI read is the acceptance for Part A's last half and for the three-OS legs of Parts B-E.
`evidence/ci-red.md` is a record steps 1-4 write at implement (the artifact read, the forced firings, the named cause,
the reverted-fix reading); no entry produces it and none carries `artifact`. The reverted-fix run of step 4 is a
ONE-SHOT control that mutates source and restores it: implement runs it once, both readings in that file, and the
non-mutating concurrent-start entry (the `stamped_home_concurrent_` filter) guards the property on every re-run.

  read of the final HEAD reads `verdict: green` with `test (ubuntu-latest)` among the checks (`ci.py conclusion --sha
  HEAD --wait 1800`). No bound was raised, no retry added and no test serialised (scope §7, `inputs#I1`).

- (arch) `viola revive --json`'s every exit-1 refusal prints exactly `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` with
  `<code>` one of `strict-modes-failed` · `already-live` · `no-session` · `session-live` · `cwd-missing`, with empty
  stderr and exit 1; `--list --json` prints `{"v":1,"ok":{"sessions":[…]}}` and exits 0; and the human pairs and rows
  are byte-identical without `--json` (per architecture §Standard Contracts CLI `--json` output, `inputs#I2`;
  `tests/cli_revive.rs`).

- (obs) `viola revive <name> --list` under a `VIOLA_NAME`, after a passed instance check, writes one `process-start`
  and one `process-exit` into `diagnostics/cli-<name>.ndjson`; a refused check writes no line and leaves the mode as
  found (per obs-plan §10 exemption 6, retired; security-plan §Authentication & Authorization).

- (obs) `viola list` over a replayed snapshot under a `VIOLA_NAME` writes `state-recovered` with `instance` the
  caller and `scanned` the scanned `ViolaName`, and the line validates against `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` (per
  obs-plan §4 E5; `e5_list_reads_a_live_wrapper_through_the_replay`, `contract_diag_schema`).

- (arch, security) A CLI verb resolves `--home`, else the `VIOLA_DIR` grandparent through the one shape check, else
  `<user home>/.viola`, canonicalised once it exists (plain drive form on Windows); `--home` beats `VIOLA_DIR`, and a
  malformed `VIOLA_DIR` falls to the default (per architecture §Cross-cutting Config management; security-plan §Input
  Validation CLI row; `resolve_home_` units, `tests/cli_machine_contract.rs`).

- (tests) `tests/cli_controls_not_disableable.rs`'s completeness case passes: every long flag `viola --help` lists,
  every `VIOLA_*` variable and every `schemas/config.v1.json` key is a row of the table. The `VIOLA_DIR` row over a
  0770 home reads `list` exit 21, and `CONFIG_KEYS` equals the schema's keys (per test-plan §5 Cross-module patterns
  (CLI)).

- (tests, layouts, design) `tests/cli_machine_contract.rs` reads, for each driver-facing verb and each outcome it
  reaches, one `--json` document of the documented shape with empty stderr and its literal exit from 0, 1, 2, 10-14,

  design-system §Surface: cli → Exit-code phraseology).

- `verification-matrix.json#v1-39` — every driver-facing verb (`send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `list`, `pause`,
  `release`, `revive` with `--list`) has a `--json` form printing one stdout document that mirrors the channel result,

  2026-10-16 ruling (the cap's notes).

- Leaned, not asked: no `--json` for `run` or `verify` (per architecture [CLI Conventions], which names revive as the
  one verb without a machine form). Reading `VIOLA_DIR` in the CLI verbs is not a boundary widening: architecture

- A `--json` for `run` or `verify` — not owed (architecture [CLI Conventions]); `verify`'s stdout is its documented
  agent-readable outcome.

- `{"v":1,"refusal":…}` for revive's exit-1 outcomes — `refusal` is the channel `RefusalReason` set mapped to 10-14,
  and revive's refusals exit 1 (`inputs#I2` chose `error = the code`).

- Refusing on a malformed `VIOLA_DIR` — the variable is wrapper-to-child plumbing; a value that fails the shape check
  is no home, and the order falls through (hook's own reading of it is the same).

- Canonicalising a home that does not exist yet, or writing Windows' `\\?\` verbatim form into plugin-dir, cwd or
  settings arguments — the first fails where `run` and `list` must create or leave nothing; the second is a spelling
  the CLI was never measured on.

- Changing `revive`'s refused-check no-line shape (exemption 7) or any human pair's words — the founder has not ruled
  on the first, and several pairs are his.

- A `scanned` value taken from anything but the instance dir's own last component — no path, no pid (NEVER-log
  floor).

  stamped_home tests` minus `tests/support/home.rs`) rests on the stamp. Part B before C-E, because `run` and the test
  supports must spell one home before the new cases compare paths.

  agent, testing.md §Test data). After step 7 every test home's canonical spelling is under that target, so a case
  compares the resolved home, never `TestHome::path()` (`inputs#I2`, the Overseer's note).

- `role_of`'s new arm must skip a `--home <dir>` / `--home=<dir>` pair before `revive` as it does now, and read
  `--list` anywhere after `revive`. Its unit table (main.rs:338-363) gains `revive --list`, `--home x revive --list`
  and `revive builder` (stays Other).

title: Part B — width-known truncation of unwrapped NAMEs (`inputs#I1` Q2)

data.head: ### Part B — width-known truncation of unwrapped NAMEs (`inputs#I1` Q2)

body:
5. **Units first** in `src/human/board.rs` (`mod tests`, prefix `board_row_width_`). Each expected row is a literal:
   - (a) With no width, nothing is truncated: today's rows are unchanged.
   - (b) With a width, an unwrapped NAME longer than the room left is cut to end in `...`, and its row is exactly the
     width or shorter.
   - (c) A wrapped NAME is never cut, whatever the width. The wrapped row may stay longer than the width.
   - (d) A cut never falls inside a `\xHH` escape. It moves back to before the escape's backslash.
   - (e) A width too small for the `...` form keeps NAME at no less than the caption's 4 columns. An unwrapped NAME is
     then its first character and `...`.
   - (f) An unwrapped NAME that already fits is never cut.

   Read them red against stubs that hold the new parameter and no behaviour (testing.md 2026-09-25, extended
   2026-10-10).

6. In `src/human/board.rs`, `board_rows` and `write_board` take the terminal width as an `Option<usize>` of columns.

   With `Some(w)`, NAME's column width is the largest of:
   - the caption's 4;
   - the longest wrapped escaped NAME;
   - the longest unwrapped escaped NAME, capped at `w` minus the rest of an unwrapped row.

   The rest of an unwrapped row is 65 columns: LIVE 5, STATUS 7, WHEEL 23, DIALOG 17, five 2-space gutters and the
   `n/a` CLI cell. The basis is `src/human/board.rs:98`–`101` and `:136`–`141` at `6d8b662`.

   Every unwrapped NAME longer than that column is cut to the column width minus 3, at a character boundary that is
   not inside an escape, and `...` is appended. The cut acts on the ESCAPED text: `escape_row` runs first, as now at
   `src/human/board.rs:151`.

   With `None`, the rows are byte-identical to today's. The board stays ONE `write_all`.

7. In `src/cmd/list.rs`, in human mode only, pass `viola_pty::host_size().map(|size| usize::from(size.cols))` to
   `write_board`.
   - That reader is a stdout `TIOCGWINSZ` ioctl on Unix and the console buffer on Windows
     (`crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs:466`). It reads no env var.
   - The `--json` path is untouched.
   - A piped stdout reads no size, so a piped board truncates nothing, as layout-templates' piped form requires.

title: Part C — the colour layer (CARRY 2; the reads the founder ratified, `inputs#I2`)

data.head: ### Part C — the colour layer (CARRY 2; the reads the founder ratified, `inputs#I2`)

body:
9. In `src/human/style.rs`, the product (the module declared in `src/human.rs` with its re-exports):
   - **The type.** A closed `Depth` (truecolor · 256 · 16).
   - **The facts.** A `Facts` value: `json`, `passthrough`, `no_color` (whether `NO_COLOR` is present), `term` and
     `colorterm` (their values), `stdout_tty`, and `vt` (`Some(enabled)` on Windows, `None` elsewhere).
   - **The decision.** A pure `decide(&Facts) -> Option<Depth>`: the seven rungs in design-system §Tokens'
     (platform-specific) order, first match wins, then the depth rule.
   - **The tokens.** Per depth, the four SGR tokens of step 8.
   - **The fact reader.** It reads `NO_COLOR`, `TERM` and `COLORTERM` with `std::env::var_os` (the only env reads it
     adds) and stdout's `IsTerminal`. On Windows, and only once rungs 1–6 pass, it makes the VT enable.
     - The enable is `GetConsoleMode` on the stdout handle, then `SetConsoleMode(mode | ENABLE_VIRTUAL_TERMINAL_PROCESSING)`.
       That constant `0x0004` is written as one pinned literal (testing.md 2026-09-27). It is never viola-pty's
       `0x000c` (`crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs:258`).
     - It returns a guard that restores the saved mode when dropped. A failed get or set reads as rung 7: no colour,
       and no mode left changed.
     - The `cfg(windows)` body stays a minimal OS reader: the decision lives in the plain `decide`, tested on every OS
       (testing.md 2026-09-24).
   - **What the facts touch.** They decide only whether and how deep SGR bytes are emitted. They never reach a log
     line, an error or a refusal, and never change escaping, redaction, `validate_paste_text` or any check
     (security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns, Universal; obs-plan §11 Logs).

10. **Board units** in `src/human/board.rs` (prefix `board_row_style_`). Each expected row is a literal byte string:
    - (a) A live wrapped row at each depth: `\x1b[1m` + NAME + `\x1b[0m`, then the padding plain. A pending dialog's
      cell is the attention token + `DIALOG` + `\x1b[0m`, then ` <kind>` plain.
    - (b) A stale row is dim from its first byte to its last. Every span inside it re-opens dim after its reset. NAME
      on it is dim and bold. On a stale row with a pending dialog, only the `DIALOG` word is amber and not dim: the
      kind word and the rest of the row stay dim.
    - (c) An unwrapped row's NAME is bold, and nothing else in the row is styled.
    - (d) The BAY line, the caption row, the empty-board line and the separator carry no SGR.
    - (e) Padding and widths are counted on the plain text, so a styled board shows the same columns as the plain
      one.
    - (f) Under no depth (`None`), every row is byte-identical to today's.
    - (g) An escaped control (`\x1B`, `\x0A`) reads the same at every depth: no raw control byte, and no SGR inside
      an escape.

11. In `src/human/board.rs`, `write_board` takes the style (`Option<Depth>`) beside the width. The spans of step 10
    are applied after layout and truncation, over the escaped cells. The board stays ONE `write_all`.

13. **Test support.**
    - Move `sgr_attributes` from `tests/cli_output_plain.rs` into `tests/support/sgr.rs`, with its self-check case, and
      declare it in `tests/support/mod.rs`. `tests/cli_output_plain.rs` imports it.
    - Move `raise` from `tests/cli_answer.rs:167` into `tests/support/events.rs`. `tests/cli_answer.rs` imports it,
      with no case changed. Shared helpers live only in `tests/support/` (test-plan §2).

14. **The outer-PTY witnesses.** In `tests/cross_list_rows.rs`, each `list` child gets its own env:
    `OuterPty::spawn_without` removes `NO_COLOR`, `COLORTERM` and `TERM`, then sets what the case needs.
    - `cross_list_rows_style_each_span_beside_its_word_on_a_terminal` boots a `path4-permission.json` wrapper and
      raises its permission dialog with `raise`. It runs `list` under a 200-column outer PTY with
      `TERM=xterm-256color`.
      - On Unix, the stream's SGR spans are exactly `\x1b[1m` + `builder` + `\x1b[0m` and `\x1b[38;5;172m` + `DIALOG`
        + `\x1b[0m`, followed by ` permission`. No dim (`2`) appears on a live board, and no other ESC sequence is
        present.
      - It runs again with `COLORTERM=truecolor` (`\x1b[38;2;217;119;6m` before `DIALOG`) and with `TERM=xterm` alone
        (`\x1b[33m`).
      - On `windows-2025`, ConPTY re-renders the stream. The parsed attribute set (`tests/support/sgr.rs`) must hold
        `1` and a foreground colour and must lack `2`. Its exact sequence is copied from the first `windows-2025`
        run's output (testing.md 2026-10-16).
    - `cross_list_rows_print_no_sgr_under_no_color_dumb_piped_or_json` runs over the same booted wrapper with its
      dialog. Each mode reads zero ESC bytes on Unix and an attribute set within `{0}` on Windows:
      - under the outer PTY, `NO_COLOR=1`;
      - under the outer PTY, `NO_COLOR=` (empty);
      - under the outer PTY, `TERM=dumb`;
      - piped, with `TERM=xterm-256color` set, so the non-TTY rung decides;
      - `--json`, with zero ESC bytes.
    - The standing `cross_list_rows_print_escaped_in_the_captions_columns_in_every_mode` keeps its no-ESC reading by
      setting `NO_COLOR=1` on its outer-PTY mode. Its point is that an injected control from a name never reaches the
      terminal raw.
    - The dim span on a real stale row is proven at the unit tier (step 10 (b)), over the writer's own bytes. A stale
      row under the outer PTY needs a heartbeat older than 5 s beside a stopped wrapper. That does not fit the
      `mutants` profile's 10 s kill with the ~4 s stamp (research.md, `.config/nextest.toml:31`–`33`). The
      integration case asserts the dim token's absence on a live board.

15. In `tests/cli_controls_not_disableable.rs`, add three cases to `setting_does_not_disable_the_send_paste_control`:
    `NO_COLOR=1`, `TERM=dumb` and `COLORTERM=truecolor`. No colour variable switches off the paste control (security-plan
    §Security Anti-Patterns, Universal).

16. In `.github/workflows/windows-mutants.yml`, add `src/human/style.rs` to the root-package label its files belong
    with. `tests/contract_windows_mutation_scope.rs` derives the Windows-gated sources and requires each one listed.

title: Part D — the truncation witness and the linear readings still missing

data.head: ### Part D — the truncation witness and the linear readings still missing

body:
18. In `tests/cli_wait_last.rs` `wait_human_lines_are_linear`, add a Unix-only assertion on the outer-PTY stream: no
    ESC byte, and every CR directly followed by LF (no `\r` redraw). The gate is `cfg(unix)`, following
    `cross_list_rows`' precedent, because ConPTY adds its own cursor bytes. Add the same Unix-only CR assertion in
    `tests/cli_output_plain.rs` `help_is_plain_on_a_terminal`, beside its SGR parse.

19. **Re-runs, nothing rebuilt.** Part E's whole `run --integration` and `run --e2e` entries re-run the witnesses
    named in the Goal unchanged, on this host and on the three CI OSes. `run` is rung 2, and `viola run` never calls
    the board writer, so the colour layer adds no byte to the passthrough.

20. Run the `## Test Commands` block in order. Record each red's reading, with its cause, before its fix.
    - Each new guard case gets its remove-the-guard run. Step 1 is red on the current tree. Steps 5, 8 and 10 are red
      on stubs. Steps 14 and 17 are red with `list.rs`'s depth and width forced to `None`. Step 15's cases are absence
      cases: the remove-the-guard run forces the behaviour on (testing.md 2026-09-25, extended 2026-10-10).
    - The Windows legs, VT enable included, are read on the `windows-2025` runner only (test-plan §11 Test Strategy).

- `src/human/style.rs` — the tokens, `Depth`, `Facts`, `decide`, the fact reader with the Windows VT enable and its
  restoring guard, the `colour_` units (steps 8–9)
- `tests/support/sgr.rs` — `sgr_attributes` and its self-check, moved (step 13)
- `src/cmd/mod.rs` — `Cli`: the usage override and the grouped help template, `Options:` kept (step 3)
- `src/human.rs` — `mod style;` and its re-exports (step 9)

- `src/human/board.rs` — `board_rows` / `write_board` take the width and the depth; the unwrapped-NAME cut; the
  spans; the `board_row_width_` and `board_row_style_` units (steps 5–6, 10–11). Callers: `list` @
  `src/cmd/list.rs:60` and six `board_row_*` units (`src/human/board.rs:500`, `:545`, `:591`, `:607`, `:620`,
  `:630`), research.md §Graph impact.
- `src/cmd/list.rs` — the width and the depth in human mode, the VT guard across the write (steps 7, 12)

- `tests/cli_output_plain.rs` — `help_is_the_grouped_verb_table`, `help_lists_only_served_verbs`, the CR assertion, the
  parser imported from support (steps 1, 2, 13, 18)
- `tests/support/mod.rs` — `pub mod sgr;` (step 13)
- `tests/support/events.rs` — `raise`, moved (step 13)
- `tests/cli_answer.rs` — imports `raise` (step 13)

- `tests/cross_list_rows.rs` — the two styled cases, the truncation case, `NO_COLOR` on the standing case's outer-PTY
  mode (steps 14, 17)
- `tests/cli_wait_last.rs` — the no-ESC / CR-before-LF reading (step 18)
- `tests/cli_controls_not_disableable.rs` — the three colour-variable cases (step 15)
- `.github/workflows/windows-mutants.yml` — `src/human/style.rs` listed (step 16)

No live leg runs in this chunk. The boot smoke boots the stamped pair over the fake agent. The Windows VT enable and
the ConPTY span readings are proven on the `windows-2025` runner, read through the operator pass's CI entry.

body:
- (layouts) `viola --help` prints exactly the Usage line `Usage: viola [--home <dir>] <verb> [args]`, a blank line,
  the four rows `board:    list` · `traffic:  send, wait, last, answer` · `wheel:    pause, release` ·
  `setup:    run, revive, verify`, a blank line and the `Options:` section. It carries zero ESC bytes piped under
  `CLICOLOR_FORCE=1` (`help_is_the_grouped_verb_table`; per layout-templates §Output structure — `viola --help`;
  served verbs only by `inputs#I1` Q3, provisional).

- (design) Every verb the table lists answers `viola <verb> --help` with exit 0. The table names no `hook`, `help`,
  `link`, `unlink` or `plugin` (`help_lists_only_served_verbs`; per design-system §Navigation Pattern).

- (tests) `every_flag_variable_and_config_key_is_a_row_of_the_table` and the three `cli_output_plain` plain-output
  cases stay green over the grouped help (per test-plan §5 Cross-module patterns covered, CLI).

- (design) On a terminal whose width leaves an unwrapped row's NAME less room than the name needs, the NAME is cut to
  end in `...` and the row fits the width. A wrapped NAME is never cut, a cut never splits a `\xHH` escape, and a
  piped board and `--json` keep every name whole. Witnessed by the `board_row_width_` units and
  `cross_list_rows_truncate_an_unwrapped_name_only_on_a_terminal_too_narrow_for_it`; per design-system §Surface: cli
  Width, the width read by `viola_pty::host_size()` per `inputs#I1` Q2, provisional.

- (design) The colour decision follows design-system §Tokens (platform-specific): each of the seven rungs alone
  switches colour off, and the depth is truecolor for `COLORTERM` `truecolor` / `24bit`, 256 for a `TERM` holding
  `256color` or a successful Windows VT enable, and 16 otherwise. Each token is its design byte string
  (`colour_decision_each_rung_switches_colour_off`, `colour_decision_picks_the_depth`,
  `colour_tokens_are_the_design_bytes`; per design-system §Tokens (platform-specific)).

- (a11y) Under the outer PTY, `viola list` puts SGR only beside its word: bold on NAME values, the attention token on
  the `DIALOG` word with its kind word plain, and dim only on a stale row (the cocked composition at the unit tier).
  `unable` and `hint:` carry none. Witnessed by the `board_row_style_` units and
  `cross_list_rows_style_each_span_beside_its_word_on_a_terminal`; per a11y-plan §4 ARIA Patterns & Roles, P6.

- (a11y) No SGR is emitted under `NO_COLOR` (an empty value included), `TERM=dumb`, a non-TTY stdout or `--json`
  (`cross_list_rows_print_no_sgr_under_no_color_dumb_piped_or_json`; per a11y-plan §4 ARIA Patterns & Roles, P6).

data.head: # Plan — 2026-10-17-end-to-end-path-binary-and-harness-legs: "End-to-end path binary and harness legs"

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-10-17-end-to-end-path-binary-and-harness-legs · **Version:** viola-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-17T00:40:00Z

The harness and the E2E layer catch up with test-plan §3 and §6 where the product surfaces they drive already exist.
`run --e2e` runs the E2E layer as suite `nextest-e2e`. The integration layer takes its `!binary(…)` exclusion: the
E2E regex already matches 18 root binaries, an exact partition measured on cargo-nextest 0.9.146. `boot` gains
`--statusline-echo` and `--agents-mode`. `status` runs `viola list` and nests its document. Two `path_` binaries
land: Path 1 as one ordered flow over one home on the root chain, and Path 6's harness-session form with step 7's
two-instance leg (per test-plan §3 `boot`, `run`, `status` and Status endpoint shape; §6 Path 1 and Path 6).

The chunk changes no product source. Every leg drives verbs that exist, and a defect a leg finds is a red folded into
this chunk. The legs read machine state from `--json`, and the human board only for its budget cells (per
layout-templates §IA notes; design-system §Surface: cli → Component Patterns, pattern 1 "As built"). Every OS-specific
assertion is `cfg(unix)` with its Windows branch stated (per architecture §Cross-cutting Patterns, Cross-platform
discipline).

- **Fork 1 (`inputs#I1`): Path 1 lives in a root `tests/path1_run_start.rs`.** It runs steps 1–6 as one ordered flow
  over one stamped home on the existing root chain. It does not use a `viola_e2e::fixtures` copy, and the CARRY's
  "viola-e2e" home moves to the root. Answered by the overseer as the founder's delegate on a technical fork:
  PROVISIONAL until the founder's Epoch 5 batch.

- **Fork 2 (`inputs#I1`): `harness_session` keeps the spawned `supervise` process** that the library `boot` starts
  today. That way `cleanup`'s pid + start-time proof stays exact. test-plan §3's "fixture-owned thread" sentence is
  amended at the wrap. Also the overseer's answer, provisional.

- **Leaned `harness_session` is a plain function and drop guard, not an rstest `#[fixture]`**, per
  `.claude/rules/testing.md` §Naming: "`viola-e2e` carries no `[dev-dependencies]`, so its table-driven cases are a
  labelled case table".

- **Leaned a booted instance absent from `list --json` reads `degraded`.** test-plan §3 Status endpoint shape: "`state`
  is `ready` when every booted instance has `liveness:"live"`", and a `gone` item is omitted
  (architecture §Standard Contracts, the `list` payload). `harness_session_with_a_dead_wrapper_reads_degraded` already
  reads it so.

- **Leaned `--statusline-echo` conflicts with `--unstamped`** (clap `conflicts_with`). The home exists only once boot
  step 4's `viola verify` made it (`crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/boot.rs:134-138`), and a home the harness made
  itself would fail the Windows strict-modes check (5-command `boot` step 2). The misuse is the existing usage detail
  `arguments`.

- **Leaned no product file is touched.** research's two lists name no `src/` or product-crate path, and a probe entry
  below asserts it against base `6042af635c3e`.

1. **The two nextest layers** (`crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run/nextest.rs`):
   - `INTEGRATION` becomes `kind(test) & !binary(/^(path|tui|mcp|cross|chaos|contract)_/)`.
   - A new `E2E` constant holds `binary(/^(path|tui|mcp|cross|chaos|contract)_/)`.
   - The stale comment ("arrives with the first E2E binary") is replaced by the measured fact. A regex matching no
     binary is still a parse error on 0.9.146, and the regex matches 18 root binaries at this chunk's start.
   - Unit cases named `e2e_layer_*` pin both strings as literals.

2. **`run --e2e`**:
   - `Selection` gains `e2e: bool`, and `from_flags` sets it under no selector and under `--all`
     (`crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run.rs:56-63`).
   - `test_suites` runs the E2E step after unit and integration as suite `nextest-e2e`, through the one `nextest(…)`
     shape and the same `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`. A `--filter` intersects it as it does the other layers.
   - `--coverage` still replaces all three nextest runs.
   - `RunArgs` in `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-harness.rs` gains `--e2e`.
   - Every full `Selection { … }` literal is updated (research §Graph impact lists the 15 sites; `..` literals need
     nothing).
   - The archive list (`run.rs:167`) is left unchanged (test-plan §3 Output format: `archived` holds the unit,
     integration and coverage JUnit).
   - Unit cases: the default selection and `--all` include `e2e`, a named `--e2e` selects it alone, and a stand-in
     runner sees the E2E expression third and reports `nextest-e2e` (the `run_reports_unit_integration_and_doctest_suites`
     pattern).

3. **`boot --agents-mode`**:
   - A closed `AgentsMode` (`recorded` · `oversize` · `malformed`, kebab serde, default `recorded`) enters
     `BootOptions`.
   - The clap value enum is `--agents-mode` (default `recorded`). An unknown value is a clap error, which reads as usage
     `arguments`.
   - `start` writes `<session dir>/bin/agents-mode` holding the value right after the `claude` copy
     (`boot.rs:123-126`), through `viola_state::fs::replace_private`. No env var is set.
   - The value is recorded in `SuperviseSpec` and `SessionRecord` as `agents_mode`, with `#[serde(default)]` so an
     older record without it still parses (test-plan §3 Session record: no `deny_unknown_fields`).
   - Every `BootOptions` literal (`viola-harness.rs:142`, `boot.rs:756`/`:783`/`:800`, `run/perf.rs:166`,
     `tests/cli.rs:167`, `tests/harness_lifecycle.rs:16`) gains the field.

4. **`boot --statusline-echo`**:
   - `BootOptions.statusline_echo: bool`, with clap `--statusline-echo` `conflicts_with = "unstamped"`.
   - When it is set, after the stamp and before the `supervise.json` write, `start` writes the session home's
     `statusline-source.json`: `{"statusLine":{"type":"command","command":"<bin dir>/viola-fake-agent[.exe]
     statusline-echo <home>/fake/statusline.marker"}}`. Both paths are written with forward slashes.
   - The write goes through `replace_private` (0600), and `<home>/fake/` is made through
     `viola_state::fs::create_private_dir` when absent.
   - A path holding a character outside ASCII letters, digits and `_ - . / :` (the shell-plain rule
     `tests/support/home.rs:300-306` asserts) fails boot with the existing `reason:"build-failed"`.
   - Nothing writes `budget.json` or reads the source: `run` reads it at start (5-command `boot`; security-plan
     §Input Validation, Statusline source row).

5. **`status` runs `viola list`** (`crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/status.rs`):
   - It loads `session.json`, then `supervise.json` (`load_supervise_spec`; `SessionRecord` carries no bin dir).
   - It runs `<bin dir>/viola list --json --home <home>` with `PATH` = `session_path(session_bin)` and `VIOLA_NAME`,
     `VIOLA_DIR` and `VIOLA_BIN` removed. That way no role line is filed under a host bridge's name; this shell carries
     3 `VIOLA_*` variables (`env | grep -c '^VIOLA_'`).
   - stdout is read through `take(MAX_FRAME + 1)` and parsed as one JSON object.
   - A pure function named `status_derives_*` in its cases takes the exit code, the parsed document and the booted
     names, and returns `state`, `ok` and `last_error`:
     - exit 0 with every booted name present as `wrapped:true, liveness:"live"` → `ready`;
     - any booted name `stale` or absent → `degraded`;
     - a non-zero exit → `down` with `last_error:"list-exit-<code>"`;
     - no exit code or no spawn → `down` with `last_error:"list-exit-none"`;
     - an exit 0 whose stdout is no JSON object → `down`, `list:null`, `last_error:"list-exit-0"`.
   - An unwrapped (`wrapped:false`) item is ignored.
   - The document stays `{v, cmd, ok, state, pid:null, uptime_ms:null, last_error, list, instances}`, where `list` is
     the parsed document (the exit-21 error document included) and `instances` keeps the pid + start-time `alive`.
   - The exit is 0 for `ready` and 1 otherwise; an unknown session stays 2.

6. **The CARRY 5 case** (`crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/cleanup.rs:362`): it replaces `fs::create_dir_all(ws.e2e_home())`
   with `ws.ensure_e2e_home()`. Witness: a red-before reading is taken in a scratch workspace whose `target/e2e-home` is
   a dangling link to an absolute, absent target (`create_dir_all` returns `AlreadyExists`), then green after. Both
   readings go in `evidence/carry5-dangling-link.md`.

7. **`harness_session`** (new `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/session.rs`, `pub mod session` in `harness/mod.rs`):
   - It is a guard built from a test name, a label and options (instances, default `overseer` + `builder`;
     `statusline_echo`; `agents_mode`).
   - It boots through the library `boot` with `build: false`, `stamp: true`, `bin_dir_from_exe(current_exe)`, and the
     session id `<test>-<label>-<pid>`.
   - It exposes `home()`, `instance_dir(name)`, `bin_dir()` and `cleanup(self) -> Outcome`. The scenario asserts no
     `false` field in that report.
   - `Drop` runs `cleanup` (keeping homes under `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES=1`), then removes the home parent unless
     `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_FAILED=1` is set and the thread is panicking (the `Booted` contract,
     `tests/harness_lifecycle.rs:60-85`).
   - It never shells out to `agent-run`.

8. **Path 6's harness-session leg** (new `crates/viola-e2e/tests/path6_budget_harness.rs`, one `#[test]`
   `path6_two_instance_release_over_a_harness_session`). Every `viola` verb runs from the session's bin dir with
   `VIOLA_NAME`, `VIOLA_DIR` and `VIOLA_BIN` removed, setting its own only for the statusline feed.
   1. Boot `harness_session` with `statusline_echo: true`. `<home>/statusline-source.json` names `viola-fake-agent
      statusline-echo` and reads mode 0600 on Unix.
   2. Feed `viola hook statusline` as `builder` (`VIOLA_NAME=builder`, `VIOLA_DIR=<instance dir>`, as
      `tests/support/statusline.rs:76-82` does) with `five_hour` 91 and `seven_day` 10, both resets far ahead. It exits
      0 with an empty stderr. On Unix stdout is `viola-fake-statusline\n` and the marker file is non-empty. On Windows
      stdout is empty and no marker is written (no command runs). `budget.json`'s five-hour reading is 91.
   3. `send builder --json` and `send overseer --json` both exit 11 with
      `{"v":1,"refusal":"budget-paused","detail":"five-hour"}`.
   4. `release builder --budget --json` exits 0 with `budget_paused:false` and an `override_until`.
   5. `list --json` reads `.ok.budget.paused` `true`, item `builder` `budget_paused:false` and item `overseer` `true`.
      `builder`'s snapshot `budget_override_until` equals the record's `override_until`. `builder`'s `events.ndjson`
      holds one `budget-gate{paused:false, override_until}` with `override_until` later than its `ts`, and `overseer`'s
      holds none.
   6. A human `list` read shows `overseer`'s WHEEL cell `driver - budget-paused` and `builder`'s without it, with no ESC
      byte.
   7. `send builder --json` exits 0, and `send overseer --json` exits 11 `five-hour`.
   8. `harness::status` reads `ready`, and its `list` items name both instances `live`.
   9. `cleanup()` reports no `false` field.

9. **The status and agents-mode readings** (`crates/viola-e2e/tests/harness_lifecycle.rs`, `crates/viola-e2e/tests/cli.rs`):
   - The lifecycle case's `list.is_null()` becomes the nested document. Each booted name is `wrapped:true,
     liveness:"live"`, and STATUS is `idle` or `busy` under the default `recorded` mode, where the session `claude`
     answers the join.
   - One new lifecycle case boots `builder` with `agents_mode: Malformed`. `<session>/bin/agents-mode` reads `malformed`,
     and `session.json` and `supervise.json` carry `"agents_mode":"malformed"`. `status` reads `ready` with the item
     STATUS `unknown` (a failed read leaves the board as read).
   - The dead-wrapper case keeps `degraded` / exit 1, now from the absent item.
   - `tests/cli.rs`'s `status` case asserts the `list` member over the CLI binary.
   - Unit cases in `viola-harness.rs` named `boot_flags_*`: `--agents-mode` parses, `--statusline-echo` parses, and the
     pair `--statusline-echo --unstamped` is refused.

10. **Path 1 as one flow** (new root `tests/path1_run_start.rs` with `[[test]]` `required-features = ["fake-agent"]` in
    `Cargo.toml`, one rstest `path1_run_start_one_home_in_order(stamped_home)`):
    1. `Wrapper::boot` in the outer PTY. Records 1–3 are `wheel{cause:"start"}`, `budget-gate`, then
       `session-start{source:"hook"}`, and the receipt's `started_at` is later than the `budget-gate` `ts`.
    2. The snapshot holds `pinned_bin`, `pid`, `started_at`, `child_pid` and `endpoint`, and `viola list --json` holds
       item `builder` `{wrapped:true, liveness:"live"}`.
    3. A second `viola run builder --home H` exits 1 with stderr `unable: builder is already live` then
       `hint: viola list`, stdout empty, and `process-exit{detail:"already-live"}`.
    4. A second home H2 (`TestHome::new()`) with `viola_channel::Server::bind` on
       `viola_channel::endpoint_name(builder, H2)` makes `viola run builder --home H2` exit 1 `squatted-name`. The
       squatter is dropped after.
    5. Stop the wrapper (`stop_keep`). Flip one byte of `pinned_bin`, and write a sentinel into
       `instances/builder/plugin/…/hooks.json` and, on Unix, `settings.json`. The start exits 1
       `pinned-hash-mismatch` and starts no child.
    6. Delete the pinned copy and start again. The copy is re-made byte-equal to the built `viola`, `hooks.json` holds
       no sentinel and every hook `command` is the absolute `pinned_bin` path. On Unix `settings.json` is rewritten
       whole at 0600 as the one-key statusline override; on Windows none is written.
    - The start-refusal helpers both files need (`run_refused`, `refused_with`, `child_starts`, `endpoint_of`) move
      from `tests/cli_instance_state.rs` into a new `tests/support/start.rs` (`pub mod start;` in
      `tests/support/mod.rs`), and `cli_instance_state.rs` imports them with its cases unchanged.
    - Its waits use `WITHIN`.

11. **The kill line** (`.config/nextest.toml`): the `[profile.ci]` verify-driven 20 s override gains
    `binary(path1_run_start)` by name (it runs `stamped_home`). `path6_budget_harness` sits under the `viola-e2e`
    package and takes the package's lines.

12. **Gates and evidence** — run the `[[gate]]` block. Record the flow's wall time (step 10) and the leg's (step 8)
    in `evidence/walls.md`, against the `mutants` profile's 10 s root kill and its 30 s `viola-e2e` kill.
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/session.rs` — the `harness_session` guard (step 7)
- `crates/viola-e2e/tests/path6_budget_harness.rs` — Path 6's harness-session leg (step 8)
- `tests/path1_run_start.rs` — Path 1 as one flow (step 10)
- `tests/support/start.rs` — the moved start-refusal helpers (step 10)
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run/nextest.rs` — the two layers (step 1)
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run.rs` — `Selection.e2e`, `from_flags`, `test_suites` (step 2)
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-harness.rs` — `--e2e`, `--agents-mode`, `--statusline-echo`, literals (steps 2–4, 9)
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/boot.rs` — the two boot flags and their records (steps 3–4)
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/mod.rs` — `SessionRecord.agents_mode`, `pub mod session` (steps 3, 7)
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/status.rs` — `status` over `viola list` (step 5)
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/cleanup.rs` — the CARRY 5 case (step 6)
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run/perf.rs` · `run/coverage.rs` · `run/fuzz.rs` · `run/mutants.rs` — the struct literals (steps 2–3)
- `crates/viola-e2e/tests/harness_lifecycle.rs` · `crates/viola-e2e/tests/cli.rs` — literals and readings (step 9)
- `tests/cli_instance_state.rs` · `tests/support/mod.rs` — the moved helpers (step 10)
- `Cargo.toml` — the `[[test]]` table (step 10)
- `.config/nextest.toml` — the kill line (step 11)

The standing lint and unit entries come first, then the new unit cases by name. Next come the integration binaries
this chunk touches, then the E2E layer whole and the two new binaries by name, then the harness smoke with the new
boot flag. The operator pass reads CI for `v1-02` on the three runners. No live leg exists: every case runs against
the fake agent. No mutation entry is listed (testing.md, 2026-10-04): the new `viola-e2e` code is scored at the Epoch 5
boundary audit. The git guard names its base `6042af635c3e` (HEAD at P4). Two records come from implement's one-shot
steps, not from any entry, and no criterion but their own rests on them: `evidence/carry5-dangling-link.md` (step 6's
red-before / green-after pair over a scratch workspace, which mutates nothing in the tree) and `evidence/walls.md`
(step 12's wall times).

    booted instance `wrapped:true, liveness:"live"`.

    runners) and by `crates/viola-e2e/tests/cli.rs` / `harness_lifecycle.rs` under `run --coverage`.

    (the cap's note) (per test-plan §3 5-command implementation; Status endpoint shape).

  layer selects no E2E-prefixed binary: `run --integration --filter 'binary(path1_run_start)'` selects nothing
  (`nextest-exit-4`). Every

- (tests) `boot --statusline-echo` plants `<home>/statusline-source.json` naming `viola-fake-agent statusline-echo`
  (0600 on Unix) before boot step 5. `--agents-mode` writes `<session>/bin/agents-mode` and records `agents_mode` in

- (tests) `status` nests `viola list --json` as `list`. `ready` when every booted instance is live; `degraded` when one
  is stale or absent; `down` with `last_error:"list-exit-<code>"` on a non-zero list. An `oversize` or `malformed`
  agents mode leaves it `ready` (per test-plan §3 Status endpoint shape; security-plan §Input Validation, Child process
  output row).

- (tests) Path 6 step 7 in harness-session form, over `harness_session` with the spawned `supervise`:
  - After `release builder --budget --json`, `.ok.budget.paused` stays `true`, `builder` reads `budget_paused:false`
    and `overseer` `true`.

    snapshot's and later than its `ts`.
  - `send` exits 0 to `builder` and 11 `five-hour` to `overseer`.

    an empty stderr.
  - (per test-plan §6 Path 6; architecture §Established Decisions [Budget Governor])

  exclusion and `--e2e` are buildable now, whatever the new binary: `kind(test) & !binary(…)` reads 27 binaries / 336
  tests, `kind(test)` 45 / 491, an exact partition with no overlap. The re-cut moves those 18 binaries out of
  `nextest-integration` into `nextest-e2e`, the split test-plan §3's regex states.
  `[premise-corrected: 18 root binaries already match the E2E regex (measured on 0.9.146); "no root file matches" and "the exclusion waits for the first binary" are false]`

- CI needs no edit for the E2E step: the test job runs `run --coverage`, whose instrumented run passes no `-E`, so
  every binary (the 18 included) already runs there under `gate --require coverage,doctest`. `gate::SUITES` already
  holds `nextest-e2e` (`crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/gate.rs:14`). The new suite is read locally (`run --e2e`,
  `run --all`, the default selection).
  `[premise-corrected: CI runs run --coverage, not run --all; it picks up the new binaries through coverage, and names no layer]`

- CARRY 3, as it stood: `agent-run boot --statusline-echo` is not built, and neither is the harness-session form of

  `budget_paused`, and the board's cell. The gate never polls, so a snapshot can read `budget_paused: true` after the
  reset until a `send` arrives or a turn ends (architecture [Budget Governor]); the board shows what the snapshot
  holds. The fake agent's `statusline-echo` mode and the root helpers `plant_statusline_source`, `statusline_marker`
  and `statusline_echo_command` (`tests/support/home.rs`) exist, and so does `tests/support/statusline.rs`. test-plan
  §6 Path 6 step 1 and the `boot` key name this entry.

- So (5-command `boot`): `--statusline-echo` runs before boot step 5 and writes the session home's
  `<home>/statusline-source.json` (the Claude settings shape, viola only reads it) naming
  `<bin dir>/viola-fake-agent[.exe] statusline-echo`, appending to `<home>/fake/statusline.marker`. With no
  `--instance` flag the instances stay `overseer` and `builder`.

- On Windows `run` writes no `settings.json` override and the statusline arm runs no command, so the flag writes the
  source on every OS but its marker effect is Unix's; the harness-session Path 6 leg asserts the marker only under

  `shell_argv` return `None` on Windows).

  at step 4 (`crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/boot.rs:134-138`). The plant goes after the stamp and before the
  `supervise.json` write, and under `--unstamped` there is no viola-made home to plant into (research §Files
  inspected, `boot.rs`).

title: 7. The cleanup case over a dangling link (CARRY 5)

data.head: ### 7. The cleanup case over a dangling link (CARRY 5)

body:
- CARRY 5, as it stood: the `viola-e2e` unit case `harness::cleanup::tests::remove_session_home_removes_a_boot_created_parent`
  failed `AlreadyExists` once after a host reboot, because it calls `fs::create_dir_all` on the link `target/e2e-home`
  while the link's tmpfs target is gone and std's `create_dir_all` over a dangling link returns `AlreadyExists` (as
  measured two-sided in a scratch program at chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list; its `report.md`, Decisions &
  corrections); a parallel case's `ensure_e2e_home` re-made the target mid-run and every later firing read green. The
  case, or the harness's home-base preparation it relies on, owes a form that survives a dangling link.

- The fix routes the case through `Workspace::ensure_e2e_home` instead of its bare `fs::create_dir_all(ws.e2e_home())`
  (verified at `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/cleanup.rs:362`). The keeper's own case
  `e2e_home_backing_gone_target_is_made_again_owner_only` (`crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/mod.rs:394`) already proves it
  re-makes a gone link target. The fix's witness is a red-before reading of the case over a dangling link in a
  scratch workspace.

- watch: the `viola::cli_send` case `send_under_the_paste_hint_a_human_key_during_the_gate_wait_wins` red once (exit 0
  where 10 is asserted: the second send delivered where `human-typing` is asserted), green in 3 other local firings,
  in 20 two-sided reruns on that tree and on its parent, and on all three runners of ci#38971772946; cause not known
  (0/3; since chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board; retires: a recurrence, or 3 green runs; placed on the
  entry that next touches the send / gate path by the operator's word at that chunk's wrap invocation). This chunk
  touches the send / gate path only as a caller (Path 6's `send` to both instances), not its code: verified, because
  research's two lists name no `src/` product file.

- No product behaviour changes: the product verbs these legs drive (`run`, `list`, `hook statusline`, `release
  --budget`, `send`) exist, and research's lists name no product source; a defect a new leg finds is a red folded
  into this chunk. (Verified.)

- Not here: the MCP forms of any step (owed to "MCP server for drivers"); Paths 2–5, 7 and E1–E5 as E2E binaries
  (their root cases stand; this entry names Path 1 and Path 6's harness form only); override expiry (§4 unit tier, by
  test-plan §6 Path 6 step 7); the harness-prefix and R8 identity-floor rows of `v1-34` (owed, no entry minted).

- Windows: every new case runs on the three CI runners; a Unix-only assertion is `cfg(unix)` with its Windows
  branch stated, as test-plan §6 already writes them.

- test-plan §3: the `run --e2e` usage-error clause and "`--e2e` selects nothing yet" retire; the integration layer's
  `!binary(…)` form becomes the standing one; `boot`'s "not built" clauses for `--statusline-echo` and `--agents-mode`
