- **Marker:** 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers · **Version:** viola-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-17T11:25Z
- **Base:** `574ad969d6fc` (HEAD at P4: the last wrap's flip, CI green 15/15, `ci#39019099990`)

- **The founder's answers to the four P4 forks** (`inputs#I2`, given live in the overseer's dialog at
  2026-10-17T11:18Z and relayed by the overseer):
  - Q1: an eighth dated gap, and MCP `list` reads agents as CLI `list` does. He ratified this widening.
  - Q2: one live `claude` 2.1.287 start.
  - Q3: gap-list group 2 only.
  - Q4: a new switch entry after the gap entries; this chunk does not claim `v1-33`.

Land viola's fourth interface: the stdio MCP server `viola mcp` (rmcp 3.4, features exactly `server` +
`transport-io`). It gives a wrapped driver session the tools `send · wait · last · answer · list`, each returning
the same result and refusal as its CLI verb's `--json` form, with refusals as code-only `isError` results. It has no
wheel or link tool, re-validates every input server-side, and bounds every call below the client's tool-call
timeout (architecture §Established Decisions [MCP], §Conventions Error handling schema; security-plan §Input
Validation, §Error Handling; test-plan §1, §4, §6).
The server is a thin adapter.

- Its frame tools reach the instance's wrapper through `viola-channel`'s new Tokio client behind the `tokio`
  feature, after the same liveness-only pre-check the CLI verbs make. That is the eighth dated gap the founder
  ratified (`inputs#I2` Q1), closed with the other seven by "Server verification before any frame" and "Home and
  code-bearing file integrity".

- Its `list` tool returns the same board document CLI `list --json` builds, including the one `claude agents
  --json` read (`inputs#I2` Q1).

- The root bin owns the subcommand, the home, the role log and the board. `viola-mcp` owns the runtime, the tools and
  the result mapping. The root bin hands the board in as a provider, so no crate edge points back at the root
  (architecture §Infrastructure Patterns → Crate dependency direction).
The chunk folds its five carried items:
- `viola-channel` stays tokio-ban-checked, through a `cargo tree` form (CARRY 1);
- the rmcp feature assertion lands as a non-vacuous lint step (CARRY 2);
- `role_of` names `mcp` as its own role (CARRY 3);
- the MCP `budget-paused` form is asserted (CARRY 4);
- the switch question is answered: group 2 only, a new entry claims `v1-33` (CARRY 5, `inputs#I2` Q3 and Q4).

One live `claude` 2.1.287 start measures what CI cannot: that a wrapped driver session loads viola's MCP server from
the plugin and gets exactly the five tools (`inputs#I2` Q2).

1. **Workspace pins** (`Cargo.toml` `[workspace.dependencies]`).
   - Add `rmcp = { version = ">=3.4.1, <3.5", default-features = false, features = ["server", "transport-io"] }`
     (security-plan §API Security, §Dependency Security "Pinning"; arch Build system `~3.4`).
   - Add `tokio = "=1.53.1"` (architecture §Stack and Technologies) with the minimal features the server and the
     client need.
   - Add `schemars = "=1.2.2"`.
   - Add the root package's dependency on `viola-mcp`.
   - rmcp 3.4.x is not in the host's cargo cache (research.md §Scope); the first build fetches it from crates.io, and
     `Cargo.lock` records the resolution. It must resolve to `>=3.4.1, <3.5`; 3.5.x is out of range.

2. **The Tokio client** (`crates/viola-channel/Cargo.toml`, `crates/viola-channel/src/tokio_client.rs`,
   `crates/viola-channel/src/lib.rs`).
   - A `tokio` feature enabling `dep:tokio` and `interprocess/tokio`, and `#[cfg(feature = "tokio")] pub mod
     tokio_client`.
   - The client has the sync client's contract: connect to a recorded `endpoint` with the process label for `conn`
     (`mcp-<pid>-<t0>-<n>`), then one `request(method, params)` per call. Every `params` carries `v` and `sender`.
   - The reply is read through `MAX_FRAME`, with the same `ChannelError` classes (`Connect`, `Closed`, `Io`,
     `Oversize`) and the same `channel-request` / `channel-response` lines and `channel.request` span.
   - On Windows it opens with `SECURITY_SQOS_PRESENT | SECURITY_IDENTIFICATION` and `FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED`, never
     interprocess's default connect (security-plan §Authentication & Authorization, IPC client-side row; arch history
     2026-09-25-security-prerequisites).
   - Unit cases under the feature cover the reply shapes, the oversize frame and a closed peer, against
     `viola-channel`'s `test_support` server.
   - The two comments that say the client "lands with viola-mcp" are re-worded to as-built
     (`crates/viola-channel/Cargo.toml:18`, `crates/viola-channel/src/lib.rs:3`).

3. **CARRY 1: `viola-channel`'s own normal graph stays tokio-ban-checked** (`scripts/channel-tokio-free.sh`,
   `scripts/sync-crates.txt`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `scripts/deny-probes.sh`).
   - The script asserts that `cargo tree -p viola-channel -e normal --target all -i tokio` does not match (exit 101,
     `did not match any packages`). Its control is that `--features tokio` does match. It prints one verdict line.
     The form resolves the named package's features alone (measured on cargo with resolver 3 in a scratch workspace,
     research.md Mechanism re-derivations).
   - `viola-channel` leaves `scripts/sync-crates.txt`. The CI step `Tokio ban per sync crate (sole root)` runs the
     script beside its loop.
   - `scripts/deny-probes.sh` proves the form fires: its control matches, and a planted `tokio` edge without the
     feature fails.
   - The other four sync crates keep their `deny-sync.toml` sole-root run.

4. **CARRY 2: the rmcp feature assertion** (`scripts/rmcp-features.sh`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` lint job).
   - The script runs `cargo tree -e features -p viola --edges normal --target all`.
   - It first asserts that rmcp is present (non-vacuous), then that rmcp's features are exactly `server` and
     `transport-io` (test-plan §9 Lint; arch Build system).
   - It is wired into the per-OS `lint` job beside `Lint probes`, and runs beside the `deny.toml` `[[bans.features]]`
     gate.

5. **One liveness pre-check for every client** (`crates/viola-state/src/liveness.rs`, `src/cmd/client.rs`).
   - `live_endpoint(instance_dir)` moves from `src/cmd/client.rs:95-102` into `viola_state::liveness` unchanged:
     snapshot, beat age, `classify`, `same_process`, the recorded `endpoint`. Its unit moves with it.
   - Its root callers (`src/cmd/{send,wait,last,answer,pause}.rs`, `src/cmd/client.rs` per research.md §Graph
     impact) call it there.

6. **The `viola-mcp` crate** (`crates/viola-mcp/Cargo.toml`, `src/lib.rs`, `src/tools.rs`, `src/result.rs`).
   - Edges are exactly those of arch Crate dependency direction (`viola-core`, `viola-channel` with `tokio`,
     `viola-state`, `viola-agent-claude`, rmcp, schemars, tokio), plus the shared serde, serde_json, thiserror and
     tracing pins. It sets `[lints] workspace = true`.
   - It reads no environment variable. The root bin passes in the home, the server's own name and the board provider.
   - **Entry** `viola_mcp::serve(home, own_name, list_provider)` builds the one Tokio runtime and serves the rmcp
     stdio transport until stdin closes. A spawned task's panic is contained at the task boundary (obs-plan §7).
     stdout carries MCP frames only.
   - **Tool list**: exactly `send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `list`. Their descriptions name no `release`, `pause`,
     `link` or `unlink`.
   - **Inputs** are advertised as schemars schemas, but each handler takes its arguments as a JSON object and
     re-validates them itself, so no serde text reaches a result:
     - `target` passes `ViolaName::try_new` before any `instances/<name>` join;
     - `dialog_id` must be a `u64`, and `after` / `timeout_ms` absent or a `u64`;
     - `response` goes through `viola_agent_claude::dialog::Response::parse`;
     - `text` must be a string.
   - **Bad input**: a value failing those checks returns `isError: true`, `structuredContent`
     `{"error":"invalid-params","detail":"<field>"}` (the field a closed word: `target`, `text`, `after`,
     `timeout_ms`, `dialog_id`, `response`), and text `refused: invalid-params`. No frame is written.
   - **`send`**: the text first, in `refusal_of`'s order: `validate_paste_text`, then `typed_text` empty. A refusal is
     `{"refusal":"not-delivered","detail":"control-character"|"empty-text"}` with no frame, and one client-side
     `send-refused` line (obs-plan §6).
   - **`answer`**: `validate_paste_text` on every free-text value of the response, with the same refusal.
   - **Frame tools** (`send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`), the eighth dated gap (`inputs#I2` Q1):
     - `live_endpoint(home/instances/<target>)`; none → `{"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":null}`;
     - one Tokio-client request with `from` set to the server's own name when it has one;
     - `wait` sends `timeout_ms = min(given, WAIT_CAP)`, defaulting to `WAIT_CAP`, with `WAIT_CAP = 50_000` ms.
       It passes `after` through. The wrapper's own deadline ends the call, so no adapter-owned timer exists.
   - **Result mapping** (`src/result.rs`):
     - a channel `ok` → `isError: false`, `structuredContent` the `ok` payload, text its JSON;
     - a refusal → `isError: true`, `structuredContent` `{refusal, detail}`, text `refused: <reason>`;
     - a JSON-RPC fault → `isError: true`, `{"error":"wrapper-fault","detail":{code,message,data}}`;
     - `Connect` / `Closed` / `Io` → `{"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":null}`;
     - any other channel error, a reply of no known shape, or a `wait` / `last` refusal → the crate's one thiserror
       `McpError`, whose fixed message rmcp sends as a JSON-RPC error. This is a fault of the MCP call itself:
       code `-32603`, message `internal error`, data null.

     These are the CLI `--json` documents less `v` (architecture §Conventions, Error handling schema, MCP bullet;
     `src/cmd/client.rs:73-75,140-156`; `src/cmd/send.rs:130-155`).
   - **Obs**: one `#[instrument(skip_all, name = "mcp.tool_call", fields(tool = …))]` span per tool call wraps the
     Tokio client's `channel.request`. Each line goes through `obs_event!` with explicit `corr` / `conn`. No send
     text, response or message reaches a span field or a line; only `text_bytes` is logged (obs-plan §4 viola-mcp
     row, §6, §8).
   - **`list`** calls the provider and returns its document's `ok` member, or the `instance-unreachable` error, as
     the result.

7. **The board as a provider** (`src/cmd/list.rs`).
   - The scan → read → document path becomes one function returning the `list --json` document: `ok` with `items`,
     `budget`, `skipped`, or the `instance-unreachable` refusal.
   - CLI `list` and the `mcp` dispatch both call it. CLI `list`'s output, exit codes and lines are unchanged: its
     cases stay the witness.
   - In the `mcp` process the agents read's `agents-probe` pair and the board's `state-recovered` / `parse-rejected`
     lines land in `mcp.ndjson`. That is new writer territory, recorded under Expected amendments.

8. **`viola mcp`** (`src/cmd/mcp.rs`, `src/cmd/mod.rs`).
   - A clap subcommand `Mcp`, `#[command(hide = true)]` with the doc line "Serve the MCP tools to a Claude Code
     session (run by the plugin, never by a person)". This is the `Hook` precedent at `src/cmd/mod.rs:80-82`. It
     takes no argument but the global `--home`.
   - Order of work:
     1. resolve the home through `resolved_home` (`--home`, then the `instance_of` home from `VIOLA_NAME` /
        `VIOLA_DIR`, then the default);
     2. run the home's strict-modes check before anything under the home is opened. A refusal exits 1 with nothing on
        stdout and no log (security-plan §Authentication & Authorization, the `~/.viola/` access control row naming
        `mcp`; obs-plan §3 init order; the 0770 trap, security history 2026-10-10-budget-governor). A home that does
        not exist yet is created by the log open, as for every role;
     3. obs init as `ObsProcess::Mcp` with the instance `own_name()`, then `process-start{subject:"self"}`;
     4. `viola_mcp::serve(home, own_name, provider)`;
     5. `process-exit` on stdin EOF, exit 0.
   - Its dispatch arm passes a `DetailSink` of process `Mcp` when an instance resolves.

9. **The `mcp` role** (`src/main.rs`).
   - `role_of` returns `Role::Mcp` for a first word `mcp`, after the global `--home <dir>` / `--home=<dir>`, like
     `hook` (CARRY 3; obs-plan §7 Main-thread catch site).
   - `exit_code` maps `Mcp` like `Other`: its own code, or 1 on a failure or panic.
   - `prints_internal_error` stays `Cli`-only, so a failed or panicking `mcp` prints nothing on stdout or stderr.
     The panic hook's line and `process-exit{detail:"internal-error"}` go to `mcp.ndjson` (obs-plan §7).
   - The tables `role_of_skips_the_home_flag_and_its_value` and `exit_code_maps_role_and_outcome` gain the `mcp`
     rows.

10. **The plugin registers the server** (`plugin/.mcp.json`, `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/lib.rs`).
    - `.mcp.json` becomes `{"mcpServers": {"viola": {"command": "@@VIOLA_BIN@@", "args": ["mcp"]}}}`: server name
      `viola` (arch §Occupied Resources), the absolute pinned path substituted at every start, never a PATH lookup.
    - `run` already rewrites the plugin every start, so `run` itself does not change.
    - The pin test at `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/lib.rs:606` asserts the rendered document: the pinned path, no
      `@@` token. The comment at `:153-154` becomes as-built.

12. **Tests, integration tier** (`crates/viola-mcp/tests/handlers.rs`).
    - Handler tests against a `viola-channel` test wrapper, with no stdio: each frame tool's channel reply maps to its
      result, a schema-violating call writes no frame (the test wrapper's frame count is 0), and `send` carries `from`
      when a name is given.
    - The binary name does not match the E2E regex `^(path[0-9]*|tui|mcp|cross|chaos|contract)_`, so it reports as
      integration (test-plan §3 `run`).

13. **Tests, E2E tier** (`crates/viola-e2e/Cargo.toml`, `crates/viola-e2e/tests/mcp_tools.rs`).
    - An rmcp 3.4 client (`client` + `transport-child-process`) spawns `<bin dir>/viola mcp --home <home>` with no
      `VIOLA_*` variables, over instances booted through `harness_session` on the fake agent (test-plan §6 drivers per
      surface). Each case is keyed on cursors and event offsets, never a sleep (test-plan §11).
    - `tools_list_is_exactly_the_five_tools`.
    - Path 2: `send` reads back. `structured_content` equals the CLI's `send --json` `ok` for the same instance's next
      send (the keys `submitted_at` and `cursor` present, `confirmed` absent).
    - Path 3:
      - `last` equals CLI `last --json`'s `ok`;
      - a `wait` with the send's cursor as `after` wakes on `turn-ended` with the CLI's cursor, never on `activity`;
      - a `wait` with `timeout_ms` 500 and no event returns `{"timed_out": true}`;
      - a `wait` on a stopped instance returns `{"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":null}`.
    - Path 4: `answer` of a pending question by its id returns `isError: false`. A second answer of the same id is
      `{"refusal":"not-delivered","detail":"unknown-dialog"}`.
    - Path 5: after CLI `viola pause`, `send` is `isError: true` with text `refused: human-typing`, and neither the
      text nor `structured_content` holds `release`.
    - Path 6 (CARRY 4): with a `budget.json` over the five-hour threshold, seeded only through `viola hook statusline`
      (boot `--statusline-echo`), `send` is `{"refusal":"budget-paused","detail":"five-hour"}`. It has no cursor, and
      no `release` appears in its text or body.
    - Path 7: on an unstamped home, `answer` with a non-null decision is `refused: unverified-cli`.
    - `list` equals `list --json`'s `ok` over the same home under the same test-scoped `PATH` (the fake agent's
      `agents`), unwrapped rows included.
    - Schema violations: the four test-plan §1 inputs each return `invalid-params` or the `control-character` pair, and
      the target wrapper's `events.ndjson` grows by no `send-issued`.
    - Every `isError` body and text holds no absolute home path and no `Caused by` (test-plan §6 Error sanitization).
    - If the binary starts from a stamped home, `binary(mcp_tools)` joins the 20 s kill line in `.config/nextest.toml`
      (tests history 2026-10-17-end-to-end-path-binary-and-harness-legs).

14. **Tests, the CLI surface stays as pinned** (`tests/cli_output_plain.rs`, `tests/contract_lints.rs`).
    - `viola --help` stays byte-equal to the `HELP` literal: `mcp` is hidden. `help_lists_only_served_verbs` asserts
      that `mcp` does not appear in `viola --help`.
    - `contract_lints` covers `viola-mcp` as a member that inherits the workspace lints.

15. **The live leg** (one live `claude` start, attended, `inputs#I2` Q2). It runs on the headless pty rig, copied byte
    for byte from `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board/evidence/` (`live-pty.py`,
    `live-ledger.py`, `live-drive.py`; `cmp` each).
    - **Setup.**
      - Read `hyprctl locked` first (the standing rule), though the rig types no desktop key.
      - A fresh home `target/e2e-home/viola-live-mcp-<UTC stamp>/vhome`, unstamped: no `viola verify` run, so no
        further live start.
      - The rig's environment: the 2.1.287 install dir first on `PATH` (verification-harness.md 2026-10-10), and
        `VIOLA_NAME` / `VIOLA_DIR` / `VIOLA_BIN` removed.
      - The build: `target/debug/viola` of this chunk's tree.
    - **(a)** Start `viola --home <vhome> run builder -- <the fake agent's path>`. This is not a `claude` start.
    - **(b)** The one start: `viola --home <vhome> run driver -- claude --model haiku --allowedTools
      mcp__plugin_viola_viola`. `--model haiku` follows the rig's last starts
      (`viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board/evidence/live-p4.md:43`). The server-level allow
      is for the plugin `viola` and its server `viola` (`plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` `"name": "viola"`). If that name does not match, the call raises a permission dialog, which the rig never
      answers: the `permission` event's tool name is then the reading.
    - **(c)** One `viola send driver` with a fixed prompt from a file. It asks the session to call the viola `list`
      tool, then the viola `wait` tool for `builder` with no `timeout_ms`, then reply with one fixed word. Then `viola
      wait driver` for the turn's end.
    - **(d) Readings, codes and counts only:**
      - `mcp.ndjson`'s `process-start{subject:"self"}` with `instance` `driver`;
      - its `channel-request` / `channel-response` pair with `method` `wait` and the response's `outcome`
        `timed-out`;
      - the wait's duration between 50 and 60 s;
      - the turn's end;
      - `viola last driver`'s word equal to the fixed word;
      - whether any `permission` event was raised.
    - **(e)** Stop both sessions through the rig, then the census.
    - **The record.** `evidence/live-mcp.md` and the rig ledger, with no prompt or assistant text, id or path.
16. **Matrix and route records** are P5's and the wrap's, never implement's.

Every master text, and every leaf the cascade re-derives from one (`.claude/docs/`, `.claude/rules/`, `CLAUDE.md`),
goes through the wrap (§Implementation notes). Implement edits none of them.
- `crates/viola-mcp/Cargo.toml` — the sixth product crate's manifest (step 6)
- `crates/viola-mcp/src/lib.rs` — `serve`, the runtime, the rmcp service, `McpError`, `WAIT_CAP` (step 6)
- `crates/viola-mcp/src/tools.rs` — the five handlers and their re-validation (step 6)
- `crates/viola-mcp/src/result.rs` — channel reply → `CallToolResult` (step 6)
- `crates/viola-mcp/tests/handlers.rs` — the adapter-level integration tests (step 12)
- `crates/viola-channel/src/tokio_client.rs` — the Tokio client (step 2)
- `src/cmd/mcp.rs` — the hidden subcommand (step 8)
- `crates/viola-e2e/tests/mcp_tools.rs` — the stdio E2E (step 13)
- `scripts/channel-tokio-free.sh` — CARRY 1's form (step 3)
- `scripts/rmcp-features.sh` — CARRY 2's assertion (step 4)

- `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers/evidence/` — the rig copies, its ledger, `live-mcp.md`
  (step 15)
- `Cargo.toml` — the three pins and the root's `viola-mcp` dependency (step 1)
- `Cargo.lock` — the resolution (step 1)
- `crates/viola-channel/Cargo.toml` — the `tokio` feature (step 2)
- `crates/viola-channel/src/lib.rs` — the feature-gated module (step 2)
- `crates/viola-state/src/liveness.rs` — `live_endpoint` (step 5)
- `src/cmd/client.rs` — `live_endpoint` moved out (step 5)
- `src/cmd/list.rs` — the board document as a provider (step 7)
- `src/cmd/mod.rs` — the hidden `Mcp` subcommand and arm (step 8)
- `src/main.rs` — `Role::Mcp` (step 9)
- `plugin/.mcp.json` — the `viola` server (step 10)
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/lib.rs` — the pin test and the comment (step 10)
- `crates/viola-e2e/Cargo.toml` — the rmcp client and tokio (step 13)
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — the rmcp lint step and `viola-channel`'s tree form (steps 3, 4)
- `scripts/sync-crates.txt` — `viola-channel` removed (step 3)
- `scripts/deny-probes.sh` — the tree form proven live (step 3)
- `tests/contract_lints.rs` — `viola-mcp` in the member set (step 14)
- `tests/cli_output_plain.rs` — `mcp` absent from `--help` (step 14)
- `.config/nextest.toml` — the kill line, conditional (step 13)
Graph impact (research.md §Graph impact, rust plane, 0-indexed lines +1):
- `role_of` @ `src/main.rs:53` (`main`) and its table @ `src/main.rs:354`;
- `live_endpoint` callers @ `src/cmd/{send,wait,last,answer,pause}.rs`;
- `read_here` @ `src/cmd/list.rs:104` and `src/cmd/revive.rs:166` (revive unchanged);
- `plugin_files` @ `src/cmd/run.rs:405` (unchanged) and its two tests in `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/lib.rs`.

The standing lint, deny and unit entries run first. The two new scripts follow, then the new cases by name, then each
layer whole. Then the booted smoke, the pre-push gate and the operator's CI entries. The live leg (step 15, one start)
is an attended rig measurement, not an entry. No entry produces `evidence/live-mcp.md`, and only its own criterion
rests on it. No mutation entry, witness run or workflow dispatch is listed.

The two scripts of steps 3 and 4 are instruments this chunk builds, and their verdict lines are their own. Before
either script's first graded use, implement runs its known-verdict controls once and records the readings in
`chunks/2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers/evidence/instrument-controls.md`:

- `channel-tokio-free.sh`: a must-pass input (the tree as built), and a must-fail input (a scratch clone with a
  normal `tokio` edge planted in `viola-channel` outside the feature).

- `rmcp-features.sh`: a must-pass input (the tree as built), and two must-fail inputs (a scratch clone with an extra
  rmcp feature, and one with rmcp absent, which must read the vacuity guard red).

body:
- (arch) `crates/viola-mcp` exists with exactly the edges of architecture §Infrastructure Patterns → Crate dependency
  direction (plus the shared serde / serde_json / thiserror / tracing pins).
  - `tokio` reaches no other product member's normal graph.
  - `viola-mcp` is not in `scripts/sync-crates.txt`.
  - `bash scripts/channel-tokio-free.sh` and the remaining sole-root loop are green, and `bash scripts/deny-probes.sh`
    proves the tree form fires (per architecture §Established Decisions [Concurrency / Backend Framework]; CARRY 1).

- (tests) `bash scripts/rmcp-features.sh` is green and wired into CI's lint job: rmcp is present and resolves to exactly
  `server` + `transport-io` (per test-plan §9 CI Integration, Lint; CARRY 2).

- (obs) `role_of` classifies `viola mcp` and `viola --home <dir> mcp` as `Role::Mcp`. A failing `mcp` exits 1 and
  prints no `error: internal error`. Its lines are in `<home>/diagnostics/mcp.ndjson` with `process:"mcp"` (per
  obs-plan §7 Main-thread catch site, §3 Logging stack; CARRY 3).

- (security) Every MCP tool input is re-validated server-side whatever the schema advertises.
  - A non-`ViolaName` `target`, a non-`u64` `dialog_id`, an open-string `behavior` and a control character in `text`
    each return a code-only `isError`, and no `send-issued` is logged.
  - An empty or LF-only `text` returns `not-delivered` / `empty-text` (per security-plan §Input Validation).

- (arch, tests) Each tool's success and refusal equal its CLI `--json` counterpart for the same channel result, with
  `isError` and the `refused: <reason>` text. This is `crates/viola-e2e/tests/mcp_tools.rs` over Paths 2–7 and
  `list` (per architecture §Conventions Error handling schema; test-plan §6 Cross-surface parity).

- (security) No refusal or fault body or text holds an absolute path, a `Caused by` or upstream text (per
  security-plan §Error Handling).

- (layouts, a11y) `viola --help` stays byte-equal to the `HELP` literal, and `mcp` appears in no served-verb row (per
  layout-templates §Output structure — `viola --help`; a11y-plan §8 Plain language).

- (arch) The written `plugin/<version>-<hash>/.mcp.json` registers server `viola` with the absolute pinned path and
  `["mcp"]` (per architecture §Established Decisions [Deployment / Distribution]).

- (arch, a11y) `wait`'s `timeout_ms` is clamped to 50 000 ms, defaulting to it, so the wrapper's deadline ends every
  `wait` below the client's tool-call timeout (per architecture §Established Decisions [MCP]; a11y-plan §8 Timeout
  extensions, a driver-only bound).

- (manual, live) `evidence/live-mcp.md` records the one live `claude` 2.1.287 start (`inputs#I2` Q2).
  - A wrapped driver session's `viola mcp` process started, `instance` `driver`.
  - Its `wait` call with no `timeout_ms` went out as one `wait` frame answered `timed-out` between 50 and 60 s, and the
    turn ended with the fixed word.
  - Whether a permission dialog was raised is recorded, and the live start count is 1.
- (tests) Every gate entry of `## Test Commands` green, and CI green on the operator pass's final HEAD.

- `verification-matrix.json#v1-38` — The MCP server for drivers (P5 claim, its concretized acceptance on the review
  card).

- **Research files inspected:** research.md §Files inspected (`src/cmd/{mod,client,send,wait,last,answer,list}.rs`,
  `src/main.rs`, `src/run/agents.rs`, `src/run/wait.rs`, `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/{lib,dialog}.rs`,
  `crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs`, `crates/viola-channel/Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.toml`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`,
  `deny.toml`, `src/obs.rs`, `schemas/diag-line.v1.json`, the two arch key files, `crates/viola-e2e/Cargo.toml`, the
  gap list and the board chunk's inputs).

- **Decisive leans:**
  - Leaned to the Tokio client behind `viola-channel[tokio]`, per architecture §Established Decisions [Module
    Boundaries] (`.andromeda/architecture.md:95`), the Crate dependency direction key (`viola-mcp` →
    `viola-channel[tokio]`) and obs-plan §4 ("wrapping the `viola-channel` Tokio client"), over test-plan §5's
    sentence "using the sync channel client inside the handler under test" (`.andromeda/test-plan.md:601`), which the
    wrap re-words.
  - Leaned to `viola mcp` hidden from `--help`, per the `Hook` precedent ("run by the plugin, never by a person",
    `src/cmd/mod.rs:80-81`) and layout-templates §Output structure — `viola --help` (served verbs only).
  - Leaned to the start-time home strict-modes check with exit 1, per security-plan §Authentication & Authorization
    (the `~/.viola/` row names `mcp`) and the 0770 trap. The frame tools' per-call pre-check stays liveness-only, the
    eighth gap (`inputs#I2` Q1).
  - Leaned to `{"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":null}` with `detail`, per architecture §Conventions (MCP
    bullet: "as in CLI `--json`"), over test-plan §6 Path 3's shape without `detail`.

- **Escalate patterns read:** `.andromeda/playbook.md`. The boundary fork matches "Boundary widening", and the
  founder's own answer covers it (`inputs#I2` Q1).

- `spawn_blocking` around the sync client — rejected: architecture requires `viola-channel[tokio]` three times; a
  blocking pool would leave the arch edge unbuilt and CARRY 1 moot only by deviating.

- rmcp's typed `Parameters<T>` deserialisation as the validator — rejected: a serde failure would answer a JSON-RPC
  error carrying serde text (a field path and value), breaking the code-only rule (security-plan §Error Handling).
  Handlers take the raw object and validate it themselves.

- Reading `VIOLA_NAME` / `VIOLA_DIR` inside `viola-mcp` — rejected: the root bin already reads them
  (`resolved_home`, `own_name`); a second reader would add a `VIOLA_*` literal to the controls table for nothing.

- A copy of `live_endpoint` inside `viola-mcp` — rejected: two copies of the liveness pre-check drift; it moves to
  `viola-state` once.

- An adapter-owned `wait` timer — rejected: forwarding `timeout_ms = min(given, 50 000)` lets the wrapper's deadline
  end the call (`src/run/wait.rs:161`), so no second clock exists to test or to drift.

- A `wait` result carrying a resume cursor on timeout — not added: a wire change to the channel `wait` contract that
  the CLI does not have. A driver resumes with the `after` it passed (CLI parity).

- `cargo deny --exclude viola-mcp` or a `wrappers` allowlist for CARRY 1 — rejected: arch Build system rules both out
  (the `--exclude` false fail is measured).
- Any `pause`, `release`, `link`, `unlink` or screen tool — out: CLI-only or unbuilt (architecture [MCP]).

- A second live start (a refusing `viola mcp` at the CLI's start) — not made: the founder capped the chunk at one
  (`inputs#I2` Q2). Whether a registered server that exits 1 blocks the CLI's start stays unmeasured, and the
  start-time refusal keeps the spec's exit 1.

- **Order.** Steps 1–5 build without `viola-mcp` and leave every standing gate green. Step 6 is the crate. Steps 7–10
  wire it. Steps 11–14 are its tests. Step 15 comes last, on the finished tree.

- **The live leg is attended.**
  - It runs after every local gate is green, once, and is never retried on red.
  - Its `--allowedTools` value is the one assumption it rests on (the plugin server's tool-name prefix). A permission
    dialog is the falsifier and is recorded, not answered.
  - It answers no dialog, types no key into the session, and makes no `viola verify` run.

- **`wait`'s 50 000 ms cap.** It sits below the smallest client-side default read in the 2.1.287 bundle (`_r=60000`)
  and above `send`'s 18.5 s bound (arch [Delivery Confirmation]; arch history 2026-10-07-send-waits-out-the-paste-hint).
  The stdio tool-call default itself is a hypothesis (research.md §Scope: `So=1e8` among five `So=` assignments), and
  the live leg's default `wait` reading is its only measurement here.

- **New lines in `mcp.ndjson`.** The board's `agents-probe` pair, `state-recovered`, `parse-rejected` and the
  `config-json` rejections land there when the `list` tool runs (obs history 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board,
  2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list). The fields are already in the catalogue; the writer is new.

- **Expected amendments (wrap):**
  - security-plan §Authentication & Authorization / §Security Anti-Patterns → Authentication: the eighth dated gap.
    MCP `send` / `wait` / `last` / `answer` frames go after the liveness-only pre-check, borrowing none of the seven,
    until "Server verification before any frame" and "Home and code-bearing file integrity". Pattern "Boundary
    widening the founder answered himself to a P4 fork"; answered by the founder, relayed by the overseer
    (`inputs#I2` Q1).
  - security-plan §Input Validation, Child process output: "`mcp` spawns none (its `list` is not built)" becomes
    "`mcp`'s `list` makes the one read". Same pattern, same answer (`inputs#I2` Q1).
  - architecture §Established Decisions [MCP]:
    - the `wait` default and cap of 50 000 ms closes the open item;
    - `invalid-params` with a closed field `detail` for a schema violation;
    - an internal handler fault is the JSON-RPC `-32603` `internal error`, data null;
    - `mcp`'s `list` is built.
  - architecture §Conventions (Error handling schema, MCP bullet): `invalid-params` beside `instance-unreachable` /
    `wrapper-fault`.
  - architecture §Standard Contracts: "`mcp`'s `list` is not built" becomes built.
  - architecture §Infrastructure Patterns → Build system: `viola-channel` is covered by the `cargo tree` form, not
    "through the sync roots that depend on it" (`[premise-corrected]`, scope.md CARRY 1). The rmcp release-graph check
    has landed.
  - architecture §Infrastructure Patterns → Crate dependency direction: `viola-mcp` as landed, and `viola-state`'s
    `live_endpoint`.
  - architecture §Infrastructure Patterns → CI/CD approach: the lint job's `rmcp-features.sh`, and the supply-chain
    step's channel form.
  - obs-plan §6 Boundary-call wrappers: `mcp` writes the `agents-probe` pair. obs-plan §3 Logging stack: the board's
    lines in `mcp.ndjson`. obs-plan §1: the stale "stderr when `VIOLA_DIR` is unset" (kept current).
  - test-plan §5 MCP: the Tokio client, not "the sync channel client". §6 Path 3: the MCP error shape with
    `detail:null`. §9 Lint and Supply-chain: the two scripts.
  - design-system §Surface: cli · Platform-Specific Notes, and layout-templates §Output structure — `viola --help`:
    `mcp` is a hidden plugin-run verb.
  - a11y-plan §8 Timeout extensions: the `wait` cap as a driver-only bound.

- **Refusals as code-only MCP error results.** Each is an `isError` result that carries a closed code and a fixed

body: - **`viola plugin install` for an unwrapped driver, and `v1-42`** belong to "Optional plugin install".
- **Explicit `viola link` / `unlink`** belong to "Explicit session links". This chunk adds no link control.

- **Server identity before a frame** belongs to "Server verification before any frame" (Epoch 6), unless the
  founder's answer to the boundary fork puts it here.
- **The exit-cause matrix** belongs to "Exit-cause code catalogue".

- **The cross-surface sanitised-error capability `v1-47`** belongs to "Sanitised error surfaces". This chunk holds
  its own tools' errors to the code-only rule.

- **`/compact`'s post-condition row** belongs to "Compact post-condition ledger row". A `send` of `/compact` stays
  `unconfirmable`.
- **No frontend** (deferred to 0.2.0).

- Proving the five tools inside a wrapped driver session against the real CLI needs at least one live `claude`
  start. Verified at P3: the fake agent reads only `hooks/hooks.json` and never loads `.mcp.json`
  (`.claude/rules/verification-harness.md`, Fake agent). CI proves the server through an rmcp stdio client.

- On the dev host the bare `claude` is 2.1.296, newer than the 2.1.287 stamp. A live rig puts
  `~/.local/share/mise/installs/claude/2.1.287/` first on `PATH` (harness rule 2026-10-10).

- How many live starts this chunk may make, and whether it makes any, is a P4 fork and the founder's own word
  (`inputs#I1`).

- **`v1-38` "The MCP server for drivers"** (integration). Its requirement names exactly this entry's surface. It is
  the claim candidate.
- **`v1-42`** is out: "Optional plugin install".
- **`v1-33`** (manual) waits on the founder's answer to the switch fork.

- `574ad969d6fc` (the last wrap's flip, which is HEAD): **green**, checks 15/15, `ci#39019099990` attempt 2,
  wall-clock 1151 s.
- No red to disposition.

- **Marker:** 2026-10-17-optional-plugin-install · **Version:** viola-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-17T17:58Z
- **Base:** `9afbff44442c` (HEAD at P4: the last wrap's flip, CI green 15/15, `ci#39043417231`)

- **The founder's own answers to the four P4 forks** (`inputs#I2`, live in the overseer's dialog at
  2026-10-17T17:50Z, relayed verbatim by the Viola overseer):
  - Q1 «Записать + напечатать»: the verb writes the marketplace and prints the CLI's two commands; viola spawns no
    `claude` child and writes nothing under `~/.claude`.
  - Q2 «Один live-раунд»: the precedence is measured once and recorded as a fact; no 24th `LedgerRow`.
  - Q3 «Local scope в стенде»: the round's four `claude plugin` commands run at `--scope local` from a rig dir under
    `target/`, are removed after, and the residual is measured. He ratified this widening.
  - Q4 «Два старта»: two live `claude` 2.1.287 starts; a red is recorded and never re-fired.

Serve `viola plugin install`, the one two-word verb (layout-templates §Component — Primary navigation). It writes an
MCP-only Claude Code plugin in a local marketplace under `<viola home>/marketplace/`, the directory only this verb
writes (architecture §Occupied Resources → Filesystem).

- The plugin carries `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and `.mcp.json` and no hooks of any kind. A wrapped session that also
  has it installed therefore never runs two hook processes for one event (architecture §Established Decisions
  [Plugin Scope]).

- Its `.mcp.json` registers the server `viola` with the absolute path of the exe that ran the verb, never a PATH lookup
  (security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Universal, the exec-form clause).

- The verb prints the CLI's own two commands for the human to run. viola spawns no `claude` child and writes nothing
  under `~/.claude` (`inputs#I2` Q1).

It takes the CLI contract of every verb (architecture §Established Decisions [CLI Conventions], §Standard Contracts
CLI `--json` output):
- human text by default, `--json` for agents, codes only, no path in a document;

- a home strict-modes check before any write and before its log, as `viola list` does (security-plan §Authentication
  & Authorization; security history 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list);
- the `cli.plugin_install` span and, under `VIOLA_NAME`, the `cli` self pair (obs-plan §4 `verify` / `plugin install`).

`viola --help`'s `setup:` row gains `plugin install`, and the `HELP` literal and the served-verbs case move with it
(the CARRY of chunk 2026-10-17-cli-output-discipline; layout-templates §Output structure — `viola --help`).
One live round on claude 2.1.287 measures what CI cannot (`inputs#I2` Q2–Q4, test-plan §11):

- which `viola` MCP server a wrapped session holding both the `--plugin-dir` plugin and the installed one starts and
  answers with;

- whether a registered `viola mcp` that exits 1 blocks the CLI's start (the CARRY of chunk
  2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers).

Both readings are recorded as facts in `evidence/` and written into the masters by the wrap. No ledger row is added
(`inputs#I2` Q2).

1. **The marketplace renderer** (`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/marketplace.rs`, `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/lib.rs`).
   - A pure module beside `plugin_files` (Claude-specific shapes live only in `viola-agent-claude`, architecture
     §Infrastructure Patterns → Crate dependency direction): `pub mod marketplace;` in `lib.rs`.
   - One function takes the exe path and the home path, each already in forward slashes, and returns the three
     `(relative path, contents)` pairs of the tree. Each document is built through `serde_json` and is never a string
     template. The embedded `render` is a raw replace with no JSON escaping (`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/lib.rs:180-184`,
     scope.md's premise correction).
   - The shape is the one 2.1.287's own `claude plugin validate --strict` passed at P3 (research.md §Patterns
     detected):
     - `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`: `{"name":"viola","owner":{"name":"viola"},"description":…,"plugins":[{"name":"viola","source":"./viola","description":…,"author":{"name":"viola"}}]}`;
     - `viola/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`: `{"name":"viola","version":<CARGO_PKG_VERSION>,"description":…,"author":{"name":"viola"}}`;
     - `viola/.mcp.json`: `{"mcpServers":{"viola":{"command":<exe>,"args":["--home",<home>,"mcp"]}}}`.
   - The two descriptions are fixed ASCII sentences naming MCP tools for an unwrapped driver, and neither names
     hooks. The wrapped plugin's own `plugin.json` description names hooks, so it is not copied.
   - Nothing in the three documents holds the word `hooks` as a key or value.

2. **The verb** (`src/cmd/plugin.rs`, `src/cmd/mod.rs`).
   - **Clap shape.**
     - `Command::Plugin` has the doc line "Write viola's MCP-only plugin for an unwrapped driver".
     - It takes one required sub-verb, `Install`, which takes `[--json]` and nothing else under the global `--home`.
     - `viola plugin` alone is a clap usage error (exit 2). There is no other sub-verb (layout-templates §IA notes).
   - **`HELP_TEMPLATE`** (`src/cmd/mod.rs:34`): `setup:    run, revive, verify, plugin install`. No other row changes.
   - **Order of work**, `list`'s order (`src/cmd/list.rs:38-51`):
     1. Resolve the home through `resolved_home` (`src/cmd/mod.rs:239`): `--home`, then the `instance_of` home, then
        the default, canonicalised by `canonical_home`.
     2. Run `viola_state::strict::check_path` on the home and on each of `marketplace/`, `marketplace/.claude-plugin/`,
        `marketplace/viola/` and `marketplace/viola/.claude-plugin/` that exists. This comes before anything under the
        home is created, written or opened.
        - A refusal exits 21 with the home left as found and no log opened.
        - Human mode prints `human::home_state_pair` (`src/human/board.rs:25`).
        - `--json` prints exactly `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":null}` through
          `client::refused_document` (`src/cmd/client.rs:101-110`), with stderr empty.
        - This is `list`'s refusal and code (tests history 2026-10-10-viola-revive: strict-modes is CLI 21 for every
          verb but `run` / `mcp` / `revive`).
     3. Under a parsed `VIOLA_NAME` only, `client::start` opens `cli-<name>.ndjson` and writes
        `process-start{subject:"self"}`.
     4. Write the tree:
        - every directory through `viola_state::fs::create_private_dir` (`crates/viola-state/src/fs.rs:35`): the home
          when absent, then `marketplace/`, `marketplace/.claude-plugin/`, `marketplace/viola/` and
          `marketplace/viola/.claude-plugin/`;
        - each of the three files through `viola_state::fs::replace_private` (`crates/viola-state/src/fs.rs:263`), 0600
          with its mode set before any byte.
        - A re-run rewrites the three files whole and reuses none (security-plan §Data Protection, Code-bearing
          artefacts).
        - Entries in the tree other than the five directories and three files are left as found.
     5. `run::log_self_exit(0, None)`, then the result.
   - **The exe path** is `std::env::current_exe()`, canonicalised to the plain drive form on Windows, as
     `canonical_home` spells a home (`src/cmd/mod.rs:273-281`, `plain_drive` at `:281`). It is written in forward slashes, as `pin_exe` spells
     `path_fwd`. That is "the absolute path of the exe that ran `plugin install`" (architecture [Plugin Scope]). The
     home argument is the resolved canonical home, also in forward slashes. Both are absolute by construction.
   - **The result.**
     - `--json` prints `{"v":1,"ok":{"marketplace":"viola","plugin":"viola@viola"}}` (one stdout write, stderr empty).
       It holds no path, because CLI `--json` output is codes only (security-plan §Error Handling).
     - Human mode prints these lines on stdout (`src/human/verbs.rs`, re-exported from `src/human.rs`):

       ```
       viola@viola  written  <marketplace dir>
       run these to add it to Claude Code:
         claude plugin marketplace add <marketplace dir>
         claude plugin install viola@viola
       ```

       - This is a **planning form**; the founder's wording is owed (design history 2026-10-10-budget-governor).
       - `<marketplace dir>` is the canonical home's own spelling joined with `marketplace`.
       - On Unix it is printed bare when every character is an ASCII letter, a digit or one of `_ - . / :`, and
         otherwise in single quotes with each `'` written `'\''`.
       - On Windows it is printed bare unless it holds a space, and then in double quotes.
       - The output is ASCII only, carries no SGR, and is written once, never redrawn (design-system §Surface: cli →
         Colour decision order, Width).
       - The printed path is the command `inputs#I2` Q1 answered: the question showed `claude plugin marketplace add
         <dir>`.
   - **Faults.** A failed write, a `current_exe` that cannot be read, or a home that cannot be created is an internal
     error. It reaches the `cli` catch site: exit 1, exactly `error: internal error`, and under `VIOLA_NAME`
     `process-exit{detail:"internal-error"}` (obs-plan §7).
   - **Obs.**
     - `#[instrument(skip_all, name = "cli.plugin_install")]`, with no field holding a path (obs-plan §2, §8).
     - No new event, field, `subject` or `detail` value: `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` is unchanged (research.md
       §Files inspected: the subject enum read).

3. **The role** (`src/main.rs`).
   - `role_of` already files `plugin` as `Role::Cli` (`src/main.rs:94-119`; research.md §Graph impact).
   - Its unit table (`src/main.rs:364`) gains a `plugin install` row and a `--home <dir> plugin install` row as
     witnesses. The function is unchanged.

4. **Unit tier** (`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/marketplace.rs` `#[cfg(test)]`).
   - `marketplace_files_are_the_validated_shape`: the three relative paths and each document, parsed, equal to the
     shape of step 1, with the version equal to `env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")`.
   - `marketplace_mcp_json_escapes_the_paths`: an exe and a home holding `"`, `\` and a space round-trip through a
     `serde_json` parse to the same `command` and `args`.
   - `marketplace_files_hold_no_hooks`: no rendered document holds a `hooks` key at any depth, and none holds the text
     `hooks`.

5. **Integration tier** (`tests/cli_plugin_install.rs`).
   - Every case uses a fresh `TestHome` under `target/e2e-home`, through `tests/support/cli.rs`'s runner, with
     `VIOLA_*` dropped (test-plan §5 Setup / teardown).
   - The `.mcp.json` oracle is the canonical path of the exe the test ran (the cargo-built `viola`) and the
     `resolved(home)` spelling, in forward slashes (test-plan §5, home resolution).
   - The cases:
     - `plugin_install_writes_the_mcp_only_marketplace`: exit 0. The tree holds exactly the five directories and
       three files. `.mcp.json`'s `command` is that absolute exe path, never a bare word, and its `args` are
       `["--home", <home>, "mcp"]`. No path under the tree has a component `hooks` or a name `hooks.json`.
     - `plugin_install_writes_owner_only_modes` (`cfg(unix)`): under `sh -c 'umask 000; exec viola …'` every
       directory reads 0700 and every file 0600 (test-plan §6, Security control negatives).
     - `plugin_install_rerun_rewrites_the_same_tree`: a second run exits 0 and leaves byte-identical files with the same
       modes.
     - `plugin_install_json_prints_the_ok_document`: stdout is exactly
       `{"v":1,"ok":{"marketplace":"viola","plugin":"viola@viola"}}\n`, stderr empty, and no absolute path appears on
       either stream (test-plan §6, Error sanitization).
     - `plugin_install_prints_the_two_commands`: the human stdout equals the planning form of step 2 for the test's
       home (pinned by literal, a11y-plan §8 Plain language), and stderr is empty.
     - `plugin_install_refuses_a_widened_home` (`cfg(unix)`): a home set to 0770 after a first install.
       - Human mode exits 21 with the `home_state_pair` lines and `hint:` last on stderr.
       - `--json` exits 21 with exactly `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":null}`, stderr empty.
       - Either way the home still reads 0770, `marketplace/` is unchanged, and no `diagnostics/` file is created or
         grown.
     - `plugin_install_logs_the_self_pair_under_a_name`:
       - with `VIOLA_NAME` set to a valid name, `cli-<name>.ndjson` holds one `process-start{subject:"self"}` and one
         `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:0}`;
       - with no name, no `diagnostics/` file is created (obs-plan §4 `verify` / `plugin install`).
     - `plugin_install_writes_no_escape_byte`: no `\x1b` and no non-ASCII byte on either stream, piped, under
       `NO_COLOR` and under `TERM=dumb`, in human and `--json` mode (a11y-plan §6; design-system §Surface: cli).
     - `plugin_alone_is_a_usage_error`: `viola plugin` exits 2.
   - The binary starts no stamped home and spawns no `claude`, so it joins no kill line in `.config/nextest.toml`.

6. **The CLI surface pins** (`tests/cli_output_plain.rs`).
   - The `HELP` literal's `setup:` row (`tests/cli_output_plain.rs:62`) becomes
     `"setup:    run, revive, verify, plugin install\n"`.
   - `help_lists_only_served_verbs` (`tests/cli_output_plain.rs:79-123`) is reshaped for the two-word verb:
     - The served list holds verb paths. `plugin install` is fired as `plugin install --help` and must exit 0, and its
       usage must read `viola plugin install`: the program word, then both verb words.
     - The table words are read from the group rows alone, the rows after the usage line and before `Options:`. A
       two-word entry is then one word, `plugin install`, and the `!word.contains(' ')` filter, which only dropped the
       usage line, goes.
     - The unserved list keeps `plugin` as a bare entry, so a lone `plugin` in the table still fails. `hook`, `mcp`,
       `help`, `link` and `unlink` stay listed.
   - `help_is_the_grouped_verb_table` is otherwise unchanged.

7. **The live round** (attended; the founder's cap of two starts and four `claude plugin` commands, `inputs#I2`
   Q2–Q4). It runs last, on the finished tree, after every local gate is green, once.
   - **The rig.** `live-pty.py` and `live-ledger.py`, copied byte for byte from
     `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers/evidence/` (`cmp` exit 0 on each).
   - **The environment.**
     - The rig declares 8 names and no `CLAUDE*` / `VIOLA*` name (`live-pty.py`'s `declared_env`).
     - `~/.local/share/mise/installs/claude/2.1.287` goes first on `PATH`, and every `claude` command names the
       2.1.287 binary by absolute path. `claude --version` is read by path before each start
       (verification-harness.md 2026-10-10).
     - Read `hyprctl locked` before each start (the standing rule), though the rig types no desktop key.
   - **The dirs.**
     - The rig dir `target/plugin-live-<UTC stamp>/` holds `proj/`, the cwd of every `claude` command and both starts,
       and `priv/`, the rig's private dir.
     - The homes go under `target/e2e-home/viola-live-plugin-<UTC stamp>/`: `ihome/` (the install), `whome/` (the
       wrapped start) and `lhome/` (unused unless a reading needs a clean home).
     - Every home is fresh and unstamped, and no `viola verify` is run.
   - **Before.**
     - Write a listing of `~/.claude/plugins/` (relative path, size and sha256 per file) to `priv/`.
     - Record the sha256 of `~/.claude/settings.json`.
     - Record that `.claude/settings.local.json` at the repository root is absent: it is absent at P4, and
       `.gitignore:10` ignores it.
   - **(a) The install.**
     - `target/debug/viola --home <ihome> plugin install --json` must print the `ok` document.
     - Then, from `proj/`: `claude plugin marketplace add <ihome>/marketplace --scope local --json`, then
       `claude plugin install viola@viola --scope local --json`. These are the first two of the founder's four commands
       (`inputs#I2` Q3), and neither is a session start.
     - **Guard, read right after the first command:** `proj/.claude/settings.local.json` exists, the repository root's
       `.claude/settings.local.json` is still absent, and `~/.claude/settings.json`'s sha256 is unchanged.
     - If any of the three fails, stop: run the two removal commands of (d) at once, make no start, record it as a
       finding, and bring it to the founder.
   - **(b) Start 1, the precedence reading.**
     - Write the ledger row first: `start` n 1, cap 2, authority `inputs#I2` Q4.
     - From `proj/`, under `live-pty.py`: `target/debug/viola --home <whome> run driver -- <claude 2.1.287> --model
       haiku --allowedTools mcp__plugin_viola_viola`.
     - Then one `viola --home <whome> send driver --file <prompt> --json` and `viola --home <whome> wait driver`. The
       prompt is one fixed file in `priv/`: call the viola `list` tool once, then reply with one fixed word.
     - The stop is the stop file, then the census.
     - **Readings, codes and counts only:**
       - the count of `process-start{subject:"self"}` in `<whome>/diagnostics/mcp.ndjson` and in
         `<ihome>/diagnostics/mcp.ndjson`, each with its `instance`: which server or servers started;
       - which home's `mcp.ndjson` gains the `list` tool's `agents-probe` pair: which server answered;
       - the count of `session-start` events in `<whome>/instances/driver/events.ndjson` (one hook process per event);
       - whether any `permission` event was raised;
       - the turn's end, and whether `viola last driver` equals the fixed word;
       - the CLI's own MCP logs under `~/.cache/claude-cli-nodejs/` for the `viola` server, read and never copied:
         how many connections it made, and each one's outcome.
   - **(c) Start 2, the exit-1 reading.**
     - **Control:** `chmod 0770 <ihome>`. Then `target/debug/viola --home <ihome> mcp </dev/null` must exit 1 with
       stdout and stderr empty and no `<ihome>/diagnostics/mcp.ndjson` growth: the shape under test (obs-plan §10
       exemption 7).
     - Write the ledger row: `start` n 2, cap 2, authority `inputs#I2` Q4.
     - From `proj/`, under `live-pty.py`: `<claude 2.1.287> --model haiku`, unwrapped. Only the installed plugin
       registers `viola`, and no key is typed.
     - 20 s after the start, make one bounded `claude agents --json` read by path (killed at 5 s, stdout to `priv/`),
       the read `viola list` makes. Record only whether a row's `pid` equals the start's `child_pid` (from
       `live-pty.py`'s status file) and that row's `status`. Then the stop file, then the census.
     - **Readings:**
       - the row and its `status`: `idle` means the start did not block; no row, or not `idle`, is recorded as it reads;
       - the CLI's MCP log for the `viola` server: its failure outcome, read, not copied;
       - `<ihome>`'s mode still 0770, and `<ihome>/diagnostics/mcp.ndjson` not grown.
     - Then `chmod 0700 <ihome>`.
     - **If start 2 blocks the CLI's start**, that is a finding against "NEVER let a security refusal block the
       human" (security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Universal). It is recorded, and the fix is brought to the
       founder before any code changes.
   - **(d) The removal**, from `proj/`: `claude plugin uninstall viola@viola --scope local --json`, then
     `claude plugin marketplace remove viola --scope local --json`. These are the last two of the four commands.
   - **After.**
     - Write a second listing of `~/.claude/plugins/` to `priv/`.
     - In the record, keep only the diff: added, removed and changed relative paths under `~/.claude/plugins/`, with
       sizes.
     - Re-read `~/.claude/settings.json`'s sha256, the repository root's `.claude/settings.local.json` absence, and
       what `proj/.claude/settings.local.json` holds after the removal (its keys only).
     - Whatever stays is the measured residual (`inputs#I2` Q3). Other live sessions run on this host, so a change
       outside the paths the four commands name is recorded as unattributed.
   - **The record.**
     - `evidence/live-round.md` and `evidence/live-sessions.ndjson` (the start ledger) are written with no prompt or
       assistant text, no session id, and no path content beyond the rig's and the residual's relative paths.
     - The rig and home dirs stay on disk for the founder's desk (the standing removal rule).
     - The two starts are the whole cap. A red on either is recorded and never re-fired (`inputs#I2` Q4). Neither
       `claude plugin validate` nor any `claude` command other than the four and the one agents read is run.
8. **Matrix and route records** are P5's and the wrap's, never implement's.

Every master text, and every leaf the cascade re-derives from one (`.claude/docs/`, `.claude/rules/`, `CLAUDE.md`),
goes through the wrap (§Implementation notes). Implement edits none of them.

- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/marketplace.rs`: the pure renderer of the marketplace tree and its unit cases
  (steps 1, 4).
- `src/cmd/plugin.rs`: the `plugin install` verb (step 2).
- `tests/cli_plugin_install.rs`: the verb's root cases (step 5).

- `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-17-optional-plugin-install/evidence/`: the rig copies, the start ledger and
  `live-round.md` (step 7).

- `src/cmd/mod.rs`: the `Plugin` / `Install` subcommand, its dispatch arm, and the `setup:` row of `HELP_TEMPLATE`
  (step 2).
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/lib.rs`: `pub mod marketplace;` (step 1).
- `src/human/verbs.rs`: the install's result lines (step 2).
- `src/human.rs`: their re-export (step 2).
- `src/main.rs`: the `plugin install` rows of `role_of`'s unit table (step 3).
- `tests/cli_output_plain.rs`: the `HELP` literal and the reshaped `help_lists_only_served_verbs` (step 6).
Graph impact (research.md §Graph impact, rust plane, 0-indexed lines +1):

- `plugin_files` @ `src/cmd/run.rs:405` and its two tests @ `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/lib.rs:589` / `:620`:
  unchanged, since the installed plugin is a second renderer.
- `role_of` @ `src/main.rs:53` (`main`) and its table @ `src/main.rs:364`: a witness row only.
- `refused_document` (5 callers: `list` ×2, `revive`, `run`, `tests/cli_revive.rs`): reused, unchanged.

- `relied` @ `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs:1207` and `src/cmd/verify.rs:457`, and `write_plugin` (5 callers
  in `src/cmd/verify.rs` and `tests/cli_fake_agent.rs`): untouched, since no ledger row is added (`inputs#I2` Q2).

The standing lint, deny and unit entries run first, then the new cases by name, then each layer whole. The booted
smoke, the pre-push gate and the operator's CI entries follow.

The live round (step 7, two starts) is an attended rig measurement, not an entry. No entry produces
`evidence/live-round.md`, and only its own criterion rests on it. No mutation entry, witness run or workflow dispatch
is listed.

title: CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target/wincheck cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features fake-agent --target x86_64-pc-windows

body:
- (arch, security) `viola plugin install` writes exactly the tree below under `<home>/marketplace/`, and a re-run
  rewrites it byte for byte (`plugin_install_writes_the_mcp_only_marketplace`,
  `plugin_install_rerun_rewrites_the_same_tree`; per architecture §Established Decisions [Plugin Scope]; security-plan
  §Security Anti-Patterns → Universal).
  - `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, `viola/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and `viola/.mcp.json`.
  - The `.mcp.json` registers server `viola` with `command` the canonical absolute path of the exe that ran the verb,
    in forward slashes, and `args` `["--home", <home>, "mcp"]`.
  - No hooks file, directory or key is anywhere in the tree.

- (security) On Unix, under `umask 000`, every directory reads 0700 and every file 0600
  (`plugin_install_writes_owner_only_modes`; per security-plan §Authentication & Authorization, `~/.viola/` access
  control).

- (security, obs) A home widened to 0770 is refused before anything is written or logged, with the home left as found
  (`plugin_install_refuses_a_widened_home`; per security-plan §Authentication & Authorization; obs-plan §10 exemption 7).
  - The exit is 21.
  - Human mode prints the `home_state_pair` with `hint:` last on stderr.
  - `--json` prints exactly `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":null}`, with stderr empty.

- (arch, security) `--json` success prints exactly `{"v":1,"ok":{"marketplace":"viola","plugin":"viola@viola"}}`. No
  `--json` document or refusal line holds an absolute path (`plugin_install_json_prints_the_ok_document`; per
  architecture §Standard Contracts CLI `--json` output; security-plan §Error Handling).

- (design, layouts, a11y) The human result is the step 2 planning form, pinned by literal, with the CLI's two
  commands. Neither stream carries an ESC or non-ASCII byte, piped, under `NO_COLOR` or under `TERM=dumb`
  (`plugin_install_prints_the_two_commands`, `plugin_install_writes_no_escape_byte`; per design-system §Surface: cli;
  a11y-plan §6, §8; `inputs#I2` Q1).

- (obs) Under a valid `VIOLA_NAME`, one `process-start{subject:"self"}` and one `process-exit{subject:"self",
  exit_code:0}` land in `cli-<name>.ndjson`. With no name, no `diagnostics/` file is created
  (`plugin_install_logs_the_self_pair_under_a_name`; per obs-plan §4 `verify` / `plugin install`).

- (layouts, design, a11y, tests) `viola --help` prints `setup:    run, revive, verify, plugin install`, pinned by the
  `HELP` literal. `help_lists_only_served_verbs` passes with `plugin install --help` exiting 0, and no bare `plugin`,
  `hook`, `mcp`, `help`, `link` or `unlink` appears in the table (per layout-templates §Output structure —
  `viola --help`; test-plan §5 Cross-module patterns (CLI)).

- (manual, live) `evidence/live-round.md` records the round on claude 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host, within the
  founder's cap: two starts and the four `claude plugin` commands at `--scope local` (`inputs#I2` Q2–Q4).
  - Which `viola` MCP server or servers a wrapped session holding both plugins started, and which answered its `list`
    call, read from the two homes' `mcp.ndjson`.
  - Its one `session-start` event.
  - Whether a registered `viola mcp` that exits 1 left an unwrapped start reaching `idle`.
  - The residual under `~/.claude/plugins/` after the removal, as a diff.
  - The live start count, at most 2.
- (tests) Every gate entry of `## Test Commands` green, and CI green on the operator pass's final HEAD.

- `verification-matrix.json#v1-42` — Optional plugin install for unwrapped drivers (P5 claim, its concretized
  acceptance on the review card).

- **Research files inspected:** research.md §Files inspected (`src/cmd/{mod,run,list,client}.rs`, `src/main.rs`,
  `src/human.rs`, `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/{lib,ledger}.rs`, `plugin/.mcp.json`, `plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`,
  `tests/cli_output_plain.rs`, `schemas/diag-line.v1.json`, claude 2.1.287's plugin help pages and a scratch
  marketplace it validated).

- **External inputs:** `inputs#I1` (the operator's invocation: forks raised as dialogs, a widening and the start cap
  the founder's own word); `inputs#I2` (the founder's answers, Q1–Q4).

- **Decisive leans:**
  - Leaned to the canonical `std::env::current_exe()` as the `command`, per architecture §Established Decisions
    [Plugin Scope] ("the absolute path of the exe that ran `plugin install`"). The verb pins nothing: the pinned
    `bin/<version>-<hash>/` copy belongs to `run`'s start, and the per-frame `v` + sender version is the stated
    safety net for an install not bound to a pinned copy (architecture [Deployment / Distribution]).
  - Leaned to `args` `["--home", <home>, "mcp"]` over `["mcp"]`, per architecture §Occupied Resources (`mcp` "takes no
    argument but the global `--home`") and security history 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers: an unwrapped driver's
    server carries no `VIOLA_*` and would land on the default home, not the home the install was made for. `--home` is
    the first, ratified step of home resolution, so the installed server never rests on the NOT-ratified `VIOLA_DIR`
    step. The two homes also make the precedence readable (research.md §Patterns detected).
  - Leaned to the strict-modes check before the write and the log, with exit 21 and `instance-unreachable`, per
    `viola list`'s landed shape (`src/cmd/list.rs:38-51`) and tests history 2026-10-10-viola-revive.
  - Leaned to a `--json` `ok` document with no path, per security-plan §Error Handling (CLI `--json` output carries
    no absolute path).
  - Leaned to `marketplace/` staying off the strict-modes trusted-file list: viola never reads the tree back, and
    adding a file to the list is the founder's ruling (security history 2026-10-10-budget-governor).

- **Escalate patterns read:** `.andromeda/playbook.md`. The Q3 fork matches "Boundary widening", and the founder's
  own answer covers it (`inputs#I2` Q3). Q1's chosen option moves no boundary. Q2 departs from architecture's
  "is a capability-ledger row" and is his own answer (`inputs#I2` Q2).

- A `claude plugin marketplace add` / `install` child spawned by the verb: rejected by the founder (`inputs#I2` Q1).
  viola writes nothing under `~/.claude`.

- A 24th `LedgerRow` (`plugin-precedence`) with a verify Run F: rejected by the founder (`inputs#I2` Q2). No verify,
  ledger, fake-agent, fixture or harness-literal file changes, and every stamped home keeps its `cli_verified`.

- Reusing the embedded `@@VIOLA_BIN@@` template for the installed `.mcp.json`: rejected, because a raw replace
  breaks on a `"` or `\` in an arbitrary exe or home path (`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/lib.rs:180-184`).

- `args` `["mcp"]` alone: rejected, because an unwrapped driver's server would resolve the default home or the
  unratified `VIOLA_DIR` step instead of the install's home (Decisive leans).
- Any path in the `--json` document: rejected (security-plan §Error Handling).

- `claude plugin validate` in the round: not run. It is not among the four commands the founder's Q3 answer named,
  and whether it writes under `~/.claude` is unmeasured (research.md §Patterns detected). The shape it passed at P3 is
  pinned by `marketplace_files_are_the_validated_shape`.

- Removing an unknown entry found in `marketplace/`: not done. The tree's integrity against a same-user writer
  belongs to the route entry "Home and code-bearing file integrity".
- An uninstall or list sub-verb: out of scope (layout-templates §IA notes: no further sub-verb).
- A third live start, or a re-fire of a red one: not made (`inputs#I2` Q4).

- Any `claude` command beyond the four `claude plugin` commands, the `--version` reads and start 2's one agents read:
  not made.
- **Order.** Steps 1–3 build the verb, steps 4–6 are its tests, and step 7 comes last, on the finished tree, once.

- **The round's stop rules.**
  - The guard after the first `claude plugin` command stops the round with no start if the local scope did not land
    in `proj/.claude/`.
  - A trust dialog or any modal at a start is a red reading: the rig types no key.
  - A blocking start 2 is a finding for the founder before any code change.

- **The `--plugin-dir` server's home in start 1** comes through `VIOLA_DIR`, the wrapper's own plumbing. The installed
  server's home is `<ihome>` through `--home`, so the two `mcp.ndjson` files separate the readings.

- **Expected amendments (wrap):**
  - architecture §Established Decisions [Plugin Scope]: "is a capability-ledger row" becomes the measured reading
    (which server or servers start, which answers), on 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host, with no ledger row by the ruled
    limit "a shape no send relies on needs no probe". Its Windows leg is owed on "Windows-only live measurements".
    Also the `command` as the canonical `current_exe` and the `args` `["--home", <home>, "mcp"]`, built through
    `serde_json`. The founder's own answer, relayed verbatim by the Viola overseer (`inputs#I2` Q2).
  - architecture §Established Decisions [CLI Version Compatibility]: the owed "Plugin precedence" row leaves the
    owed-row list, as a measured fact, not a row (`inputs#I2` Q2).
  - architecture §Established Decisions [Deployment / Distribution]: "Whether a registered `viola mcp` that exits 1
    blocks the CLI's start is unmeasured" becomes the measured reading.
  - architecture §Occupied Resources:
    - Binary, subcommands and exit codes: `plugin install` takes `[--json]` and exits 0 / 1 / 2 / 21;
    - Filesystem: `marketplace/`'s five directories and three files;
    - `diagnostics/`'s producers gain `plugin install`.
  - architecture §Standard Contracts CLI `--json` output: the install's `ok` document and its `instance-unreachable`
    refusal.
  - security-plan §Data Protection: "viola writes nothing under `~/.claude`" kept, and `viola plugin install` writes only
    `<home>/marketplace/`, spawning no `claude` (`inputs#I2` Q1). The chunk's round and its measured residual under
    `~/.claude/plugins/`: pattern "Boundary widening the founder answered himself to a P4 fork", answered by the
    founder, relayed verbatim by the Viola overseer (`inputs#I2` Q3).
  - security-plan §Authentication & Authorization:
    - `plugin install` joins the strict-modes entry points (`check_path` before its write and its log);
    - `marketplace/` is not on the trusted-file list, because viola never reads it;
    - the installed `command` gets no re-hash, because only the pinned copy is re-hashed.
  - security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Universal: the exec-form clause names the installed `.mcp.json` as built.
  - obs-plan §4 `verify` / `plugin install`: as built.
  - obs-plan §10 exemption 7: gains the install's refused check, which writes no line. This is the plan's lean, not
    ruled by the founder.
  - obs-plan §3 / §11: the `refuse` caller census, re-derived by `grep -rcE 'human::refuse\(' src`.
  - test-plan §5 Cross-module patterns (CLI): `help_lists_only_served_verbs` reshaped for the two-word verb, and
    `tests/cli_plugin_install.rs`.
  - design-system §Surface: cli:
    - Navigation Pattern: `plugin install` served in the `setup:` row (the served-verbs-only rule stays the Viola
      overseer's PROVISIONAL answer);
    - Component Patterns 4: the install's result lines as a planning form, the founder's wording owed;
    - Exit-code phraseology: its exit-21 pair.
  - layout-templates §Output structure — `viola --help`: as built. A new Output structure — `viola plugin install`,
    and the catch-site verb list gains `plugin install`.
  - a11y-plan §1 critical path 6, §4 cli landmarks row, §8 Plain language: "owned by" becomes "built" for the
    `setup:` row's `plugin install`.

**Chunk:** viola plugin install: an MCP-only local-marketplace plugin for unwrapped drivers, absolute-path command, no hooks; MCP-server precedence as a ledger row
**Date:** 2026-10-18
**Commits:** `43c6410 chore(2026-10-17-optional-plugin-install): operator pre-CI commit, for the run this chunk's verdict reads` (basis `9afbff44`, its parent; `git log --format='%h %s' 9afbff44..HEAD`)

- **Files:** new `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/marketplace.rs`, `src/cmd/plugin.rs`, `tests/cli_plugin_install.rs`; modified `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/lib.rs`, `src/cmd/mod.rs`, `src/human.rs`, `src/human/verbs.rs`, `src/main.rs`, `tests/cli_output_plain.rs`, `.github/workflows/windows-mutants.yml` (`git diff --stat 9afbff44 -- src crates tests .github`: 10 files, 794 insertions, 13 deletions). Evidence: `chunks/2026-10-17-optional-plugin-install/evidence/` (`live-pty.py` and `live-ledger.py`, byte-equal copies; `live-pty-trust.py`, new; `live-sessions.ndjson`, `live-round.md`, `guard-controls.md`, `operator-pass.md`).

- **Symbols / APIs:**
  - **`viola plugin install [--json]`**, a new CLI verb (`src/cmd/plugin.rs`, 177 lines, new). `PluginArgs` (23-27) holds one required sub-verb `PluginVerb::Install` (29-33) taking `InstallArgs { json }` (35-40) under the global `--home`. `viola plugin` alone is a clap usage error (exit 2). clap also serves its own `viola plugin help [install]` sub-verb, as the top level serves `viola help`; no other sub-verb exists.
  - **The verb's order** (`install`, 48-76):
    1. `std::path::absolute(home)` of the `resolved_home` home.
    2. `tree_passes` (78-87): `viola_state::strict::check_path` on each of the home, `marketplace/`, `marketplace/.claude-plugin/`, `marketplace/viola/`, `marketplace/viola/.claude-plugin/` that exists (`tree_dirs`, 89-100). A dir not there passes; one that cannot be read fails. This runs before anything under the home is created, written or opened.
    3. A refusal is exit 21, with nothing created and no log opened. Human mode prints `human::home_state_pair` through `human::refuse` (stdout empty). `--json` prints exactly `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":null}` through `client::refused_document` (stderr empty).
    4. Under a parsed `VIOLA_NAME` only, `client::start` opens `cli-<name>.ndjson` and writes `process-start{subject:"self"}`.
    5. `write_tree` (102-118, `#[instrument(skip_all, name = "cli.plugin_install")]`, the span opened after the log): the exe is `canonical_home(&std::env::current_exe()?)`; each of the four tree dirs is made by `create_private_dir`, the home created when absent; the home is then **re-canonicalised** (it exists now, `run`'s pattern at `src/cmd/run.rs:232-234`); the three files are written by `replace_private` at 0600, each rewritten whole on a re-run; any other entry in the tree is left as found.
    6. `--json` prints `{"v":1,"ok":{"marketplace":"viola","plugin":"viola@viola"}}` (one write; no path). Human mode prints `human::write_plugin_installed` with `human::command_word(<canonical home>/marketplace)`.
    7. `run::log_self_exit(0, None)`.
    - A failed `current_exe`, dir creation or file write reaches the `cli` catch site: exit 1, `error: internal error`.
  - **`viola_agent_claude::marketplace`** (new pure module, `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/marketplace.rs`, 155 lines; `pub mod marketplace;` at `lib.rs:8`): `pub const NAME = "viola"`, `pub const PLUGIN_REF = "viola@viola"`, and `pub fn marketplace_files(exe_fwd, home_fwd) -> [(&'static str, String); 3]` (22-53), each document built by `serde_json::json!` and written pretty with a trailing LF (`document`, 55-57):
    - `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`: `{"name":"viola","owner":{"name":"viola"},"description":<fixed>,"plugins":[{"name":"viola","source":"./viola","description":<fixed>,"author":{"name":"viola"}}]}`;
    - `viola/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`: `{"name":"viola","version":CARGO_PKG_VERSION,"description":<fixed>,"author":{"name":"viola"}}`;
    - `viola/.mcp.json`: `{"mcpServers":{"viola":{"command":<exe, forward slashes>,"args":["--home",<home, forward slashes>,"mcp"]}}}`.
    - The descriptions are fixed ASCII (17-20) and name no hooks. No document, path or key holds `hooks`.

- **The CLI's install surface, measured on 2.1.287** (`claude plugin marketplace add --help` / `plugin install --help`): a local marketplace is added by `claude plugin marketplace add <path>` (a URL, path or GitHub repo) and its plugin installed by `claude plugin install <plugin>@<marketplace>`; both take `--scope user|project|local` (default `user`) and `--json`; removal is `claude plugin uninstall <plugin> [--scope]` and `claude plugin marketplace remove <name> [--scope]`. Every one of them writes a Claude Code settings scope, so only the human or a `claude` child viola spawns can perform them (P4 fork Q1).

- **The manifest shape, measured** (`claude plugin validate --strict --json`, 2.1.287): `<root>/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` `{"name","owner":{"name"},"description","plugins":[{"name","source":"./<dir>","description","author":{"name"}}]}` beside `<root>/<dir>/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` `{"name","version","description","author":{"name"}}` and `<root>/<dir>/.mcp.json` passes `--strict` with exit 0 on both the marketplace and the plugin; without `description` and `author` it reads `errors: []` and two warnings, exit 1 under `--strict` only. - **A session-only plugin load** (`claude --help`, 2.1.287): `--plugin-dir <path>` loads a plugin "for this session only", repeatable; `--setting-sources user,project,local` chooses which settings scopes load. Whether a `--plugin-dir` plugin and an installed plugin of the same name both load is not stated by the help and is the live measurement this chunk owes.

- **Which `viola mcp` answered is readable without a new capture arm** (`src/cmd/mcp.rs`, architecture §Plugin Scope, obs-plan §3 Log file location): `viola mcp` always writes `<home>/diagnostics/mcp.ndjson` (D-09), so two registrations naming two different homes (`--home A` in the installed `.mcp.json`; the wrapped session's own home through `VIOLA_DIR`) tell which server started by whose `mcp.ndjson` gains a `process-start` — the equality the precedence measurement needs, one start per reading.
