body:
- (arch) `LedgerRow::ALL` holds twenty-four rows, the twenty-fourth `local-command-compact` (`/compact keeps the session
  id and submits no prompt`), relied on every OS; a stamp holding only the twenty-three older ids, all `pass`, reads
  unverified and the twenty-four passing reads verified (`stamps_verdict_needs_the_dialog_rows`, in `bash
  scripts/agent-run.sh run --unit`) (per architecture §Standard Contracts → Ledger stamps envelope; per architecture
  §Established Decisions [CLI Version Compatibility]).

- (arch) On a verified CLI a `send` of `/compact` is confirmed only by a `session-start` of cause `compact` whose
  `agent_session_id` equals the id the slot remembered before it; that line precedes `send-confirmed {cursor}` and no
  `prompt-submitted` claims it; another cause, another id, no id or nothing remembered claims nothing; on an unverified
  CLI it stays `unconfirmable` at once with no window (`send_local_command_compact_*`, `send_compact_*` in the unit and
  integration entries) (per architecture §Established Decisions [Delivery Confirmation]).

- (arch / a11y) `COMPACT_CONFIRM_WINDOW` is a compiled 40 s in `viola_agent_claude::screen`, read only for the compact
  post-condition; `CONFIRM_WINDOW_FALLBACK` stays 10 s for every other send; a compact send's window expires at its own
  bound as `not-delivered` / `no-prompt-submitted` with the cursor, proved clock-driven at the unit tier; the send's
  worst case, 8.5 s + paste + 40 s, sits under the MCP tool-call timeout read at 50 012 ms (per architecture
  §Established Decisions [Delivery Confirmation]; per a11y-plan §8 Timeout extensions).

- (security) Run B pastes exactly six compiled texts — the probe prompt, the long, tag-like and newline texts,
  `/compact`, `/clear` — each only into a settled input box and none after the stop; no byte is typed into a dialog;
  verify still makes six starts and eight spawn pairs. The widening is the founder's own answer to P4 fork 1
  (`inputs#I3`) (per security-plan §Threat Model Summary, Attack surface: Child process spawning and PATH resolution).

- (tests) `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --unit --filter 'test(/check_local_command_compact_|send_local_command_compact_|send_compact_confirm_window_/)'`
  reads `"ok":true`: the row passes on the recorded shape, fails on each broken post-condition and
  with no capture; the claim, the non-claims and the window expiry hold (per test-plan §4 Unit Test Strategy; per
  test-plan §11 Universal).

- (tests) One live round on `claude` 2.1.287 — six starts, at most one re-run after a red, never beyond twelve —
  prints `stamped 2.1.287  24 pass  0 fail`; its recorded `compact-1` SessionStart has source `compact` and Run B's
  first id; the census finds no probe-dir `claude` left; the transcript delta is recorded (`evidence/live-round.md`)
  (per test-plan §7 Fixture hygiene; the founder's cap, `inputs#I3`).

- (tests) `fixtures/claude/2.1.287/` gains `SessionStart.compact-1.json` and no other change (the fixture guard);
  `contract_ledger_probes` stamps the 2.1.287 set `24 pass  0 fail` with each literal row id once,
  `contract_fake_agent_drift` replays `compact-1` byte for byte, `contract_fixture_hygiene` passes it (the integration
  entry) (per test-plan §5 Integration Test Strategy; per test-plan §7 Fixture hygiene).

- (design / layouts / a11y) `viola verify` over a complete set prints exactly twenty-four `[NN/24] <row id> <row
  words>  pass|fail` lines on Unix (twenty-one on Windows) in `ALL` order, the last `[24/24] local-command-compact …`,
  then `stamped <ver>  24 pass  0 fail`, plain ASCII with no SGR byte; a human-mode `viola send` of `/compact` on a
  stamped home prints `[RB] read back` with its cursor on stdout, exit 0, and on an unstamped home the
  `[  ] unconfirmable … local command, no measured post-condition` line (`tests/cli_verify.rs`, `tests/cli_send.rs`)
  (per design-system §Surface: cli · Component Patterns 2 and 5; per layout-templates §Surface: cli, Signature
  placement item 2; per layout-templates §Output structure — `viola verify`).

- (obs) A compact send's `run.confirm_window` span carries `window_ms` 40 000; a verify run still writes eight spawn
  pairs, every subject in the closed enum, every line schema-valid, no session id, prompt or path in any line
  (`tests/cli_verify.rs`, G4) (per obs-plan §4 Scenario: Confirmed `send` (CL-1); per obs-plan §4 Edge flows →
  `verify` / `plugin install`).

- (tests) The harness's `LEDGER_ROWS` names the twenty-four (unix) / twenty-one (windows) ids and its `LIVE_PASS` unit
  proof reads them (`run --unit`) (per test-plan §3 `run`).

- (security) No new dependency, `cargo deny check` passes, and no file outside the modify set changes (the
  preservation guard) (per security-plan §Dependency Security).
- (tests) The pushed HEAD's CI run reads `verdict: green` on all three OSes (the operator's CI entry).

- Research files inspected: `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs`, `screen.rs`, `hook.rs`, `src/run/send/slot.rs`,
  `classify.rs`, `src/cmd/verify/typed.rs`, `src/cmd/verify.rs`, `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs`, `src/human/mirror.rs`,
  `src/run/version_gate.rs`, `tests/cli_send.rs`, `tests/cli_verify.rs`, `tests/contract_ledger_probes.rs`,
  `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run.rs`, the revive and plugin-install evidence records.

- Inputs: `inputs#I1` (the operator's take-up direction), `inputs#I2` (the forks as asked, held overnight),
  `inputs#I3` (the founder's own four answers).

- Leaned: the window 40 s, PROVISIONAL, per architecture §Established Decisions [Delivery Confirmation] ("On the MCP

1. **The equality the post-condition needs** — "a `send` of `/compact` on a verified CLI is claimed by the next `session-start` whose `cause` is `compact` and whose `agent_session_id` equals the id the slot remembered before that line". The normalised line carries both fields: `compact` is a closed cause (`hook.rs:106`) and `agent_session_id` the payload's `session_id`. The live line has them: on 2.1.287 the SessionStart after `/compact` had `source` `compact` and the first id (`live-revive.md:87`, `:101`, `:103`). The frame that decides it is `session_started` (`slot.rs:103`–`:119`); today it overwrites the remembered id first, so the same-id arm must read the prior value before the overwrite. With nothing remembered, no line can equal it: the send is not claimed and waits out its window (never presumed, architecture §Established Decisions [Delivery Confirmation]).

2. **The window** — the one measured compaction took 18.8 s from the send's issue to its SessionStart (14:49:11.194 → 14:49:29.973, `live-revive.md:99`–`:101`), on a session of two short turns (`:147`: "`/compact` on a long session" not measured). Nothing in the tree measures a longer session's compaction (sweep: no other compaction reading under `viola-0.1.0/chunks/*/evidence/`). The ceiling: `GATE_MAX_WAIT` 8.5 s + paste + window must stay under the MCP client's tool-call timeout, which on 2.1.287 is only known to exceed 50 s (a `wait` answered at 50 012 ms, `architecture.md:58`). A window of 40 s gives 48.5 s plus an 8-byte paste, under the 50.012 s reading; 41.5 s is the arithmetic edge.

3. **A compaction inside Run B leaves the other rows' checks true** — `clear_start` searches source `clear` only and `local_command_cleared` compares with Run B's first id, which the compaction keeps (`ledger.rs:807`–`:828`); `framing_variants` takes clear's SessionEnd at `at - 1`, still clear's own when the compact SessionStart precedes it, unless the CLI fires a SessionEnd for `/compact` (unmeasured: the revive reading lists only the `session-start`). Run E resumes Run B's first id, which would then be a compacted session; a resume after a compaction was measured once on 2.1.287 (`live-revive.md`, start 3 resumed the same id after start 2's `/compact`).

4. **The fake agent's replay needs the session id set** — a recorded `SessionStart.compact-1.json` carries the recorded Run B's id, while the fake agent's launch SessionStart carries the set's `default` id (or a resumed one, `viola-fake-agent.rs:438`), so a byte-unchanged replay cannot satisfy the same-id claim; the `--resume` precedent sets `session_id` on a recorded variant and the drift contract stays byte-equal when given the variant's own id (`contract_fake_agent_drift.rs:417`–`:428`).

5. **The no-screen verify case is not lengthened** — `verify_window_without_screens_fails_every_interactive_row` (42.98 s against the mutants profile's 45 s kill, handoff) never reaches `framing_turns`: without screens Run B's input box is never up (`typed.rs:144`), so an added paste adds no wait there. body:
- (arch) `DIALOG_HOLD_DEFAULT` (60 s), `DIALOG_HOLD_MIN` (60 s) and `DIALOG_HOLD_MAX` (3600 s) are the hold's only
  homes. `DIALOG_DEADLINE` is gone from every Rust source (the count entry reads 0). The rendered dialog `timeout`
  (3615) outlasts `DIALOG_HOLD_MAX` by at least 10 s, and the hook's bound is `DIALOG_HOLD_MAX + 5 s` (per
  architecture §Established Decisions [Hook Contract]).

- (arch, security) `config.json`'s `dialog_hold_s` is read once at the wrapper's start, through `take(MAX_FRAME)` and
  `v` = 1. A whole number from 60 to 3600 is the hold. Every other value (0, 59, 3601, -1, 600.5, "600", null, true)
  gives 60 and exactly one `parse-rejected{parser:"config-json", detail:"malformed"}`. No value makes the hold
  unbounded or zero, no env var or flag sets it, and the key is a row of `tests/cli_controls_not_disableable.rs`
  (per security-plan §Input Validation, Configuration values row; §Security Anti-Patterns → Universal;
  architecture §Cross-cutting Patterns, Config management).

- (arch, obs) An expired hold appends exactly one `dialog-expired` line with `source` `wrapper` and `data` keys
  exactly `dialog_id` and `dialog_kind`, with no question, plan or tool text. It wakes a parked `wait` (CLI, and the
  `mcp` `wait` through the same document), and the wrapper writes one `dialog-answered` with `deadline_hit` true under
  `corr` = the `dialog_id` (per architecture §Standard Contracts, ndjson event line and `wait`; obs-plan §4 Scenario:
  Dialog → `answer`).

- (arch, security) At expiry the reply stays `null`: the CLI's own menu is the human's, the hook exits 0 with an
  empty stdout, and a late `answer` is refused `not-delivered` / `unknown-dialog`, exit 13 (per architecture
  [Hook Contract]; security-plan §Error Handling; `inputs#I2` Q2).

- (tests) `EventKind::ALL` holds sixteen kinds and `WAIT_WAKE` six. `state_events.rs` round-trips the sixteen with
  zero on all three counts, and `wait_each_wake_kind_wakes` wakes on `dialog-expired` (per test-plan §5 Cross-module
  patterns, On-disk; §4).

- (design, layouts, a11y) `viola wait` woken by `dialog-expired` prints one line,
  `dialog-expired  <name>  dialog <id>  cursor <n>`, ASCII, with no SGR, written once. During a held dialog of any
  length `wait` prints nothing but its one `waiting:` line (per design-system §Surface: cli §Component Patterns 3;
  layout-templates §Output structure — `viola wait` / `viola last`; a11y-plan §4 P6).

- (a11y) The hold falls on the driver only: any human key still hands the held dialog back at once whatever the
  hold, and nothing in the hold or its key adds a human-facing time limit (per a11y-plan §8 Cognitive Accessibility
  → Timeout extensions; §1 tui boundary).

- (tests) The gate block is green: fmt, clippy (the PREREQ closed), G1, lint probes, the unit, integration and E2E
  layers, the named cases, the guards, the booted smoke, G2, G4 and `pre-push`. CI is green on the operator pass's
  final HEAD (per test-plan §3 `run`; §10 Build failure conditions).

- (security, obs) No file under `evidence/` holds a `CLAUDE*` value, an absolute path, prompt, question or assistant
  text, a session id or a `detail-*.ndjson` line (per security-plan §Secret Management; obs-plan §8).

- No matrix capability is claimed. `v1-21` stays pooled with a P5 note: the dialog deadline's homes move and the cap
  still needs every MCP call bounded.

- **Research files inspected:** research.md §Files inspected (`crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs`, `src/run/dialog.rs`,
  `src/cmd/hook.rs`, `plugin/hooks/hooks.json`, `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/lib.rs`, `src/cmd/run.rs`,
  `src/run/budget.rs`, `src/obs.rs`, `schemas/config.v1.json`, `src/run/wait.rs`, `src/run/send/slot.rs`,
  `crates/viola-channel/src/server.rs`, `src/cmd/wait.rs`, `src/human/wait.rs`, `src/run/wheel.rs`,
  `crates/viola-state/tests/state_events.rs`, `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs`).

- **External inputs:** `inputs#I1` (the operator's direction: the founder-owned forks as one dialog); `inputs#I2`
  (the founder's own answers: Q1 «Ключ, по умолчанию 60», widening ratified; Q2 «Отдать человеку»; Q3 «Verify + 1
  старт, 11 мин», a red never re-fired).

- **Decisive leans:**
  - Leaned to compiling the hook's bound and the `hooks.json` timeout at the ceiling, never rendered per start, per
    research (the wrapper replies at its own deadline, `src/run/dialog.rs:281`; `replace_private_shared`'s identity
    premise, `src/cmd/run.rs:403-409`).
  - Leaned to `dialog-expired` taking the dialog form of the `wait` line: it carries `dialog_id`, per layout-templates
    §Output structure — `viola wait` / `viola last` (a dialog-carrying kind prints `dialog <id>`). The kind word and
    the form are planning forms, the founder's wording owed (design-system history 2026-10-10-budget-governor
    precedent).
  - Leaned to reusing `dialog-answered` with `deadline_hit` true at expiry, with no new obs `event` value, per obs-plan
    §4 (its `dialog-answered` already names `deadline_hit`).
  - Leaned to keeping `unknown-dialog` for a late answer, per architecture §Conventions (the closed detail set) and
    design-system cli pattern 2 (its line and hint stay).
  - Leaned to the trusted rig B `proj/` for the wrapped start: the one trusted `proj/` outside the work tree on disk
    (research.md Live-round facts). The handoff's standing rule puts a live rig's `proj/` outside the work tree, and
    `inputs#I2` Q3 allows no key into any dialog.
  - Leaned to no matrix claim: `v1-21`'s requirement still needs "every MCP call completes below the client's
    tool-call timeout", and no step measures it (`matrix.py show --id v1-21`).

- **Escalate patterns read:** `.andromeda/playbook.md`. Q1's chosen key is a "Boundary widening" his own answer
  ratified (`inputs#I2` Q1). Q2 chose the non-widening option. Q3 is his own cap.
- A viola-built deny, or any decision, at expiry: rejected by the founder (`inputs#I2` Q2).

- A `hooks.json` timeout rendered per start from the configured hold: rejected. It breaks
  `replace_private_shared`'s identical-bytes premise for `plugin/<key>/` (security-plan §Data Protection), and the
  ceiling already suffices (research).

- An env var, a flag or a `VIOLA_*` variable for the hold, or any value meaning "forever" or "off": banned
  (security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Universal).

- A test seam shortening the hold, or an E2E case waiting out a real hold: not added. A seam needs a Decisions Log
  entry, and test-plan §11 keeps clock cases at the unit tier.

- A ledger row or `viola verify` probe for the CLI honouring a long hook timeout: not made (`inputs#I2` Q3, the ruled
  limit).

- A `dialog-expired` record on a human hand-back: not written. A hand-back is the human taking the dialog, not an
  expiry.
- A new obs `event` value or a new refusal detail word: none (the leans above).

- A key typed into any dialog in the live round, a fresh `proj/` that would show the trust dialog, a second wrapped
  start, or a re-fire after a red: not made (`inputs#I2` Q3).

- **Order.**
  - Steps 1-2 come first; the compiler then names every exhaustive match on `EventKind` that needs the new arm.
  - Then steps 3-11, then the gate block, then the live round (steps 12-13) on the finished tree.

- **Stop rules.** A red verify makes no start. A red start is recorded and never re-made. A stalled start on the
  tmpfs backing is reported, never re-run for a green (verification-harness.md 2026-09-29 Ext. 2026-10-07).

- **The WATCH** (`send_budget_paused…` case_4, scope §Folded freight) is an observation: no criterion, task or gate.
  Its count moves only on a plain `cargo test` run of that case, and this chunk runs nextest only, so it stands 0/3.

- **Expected amendments (wrap).** One per master section:
  - **architecture §Established Decisions [Hook Contract].** The dialog hold becomes `config.json`'s
    `dialog_hold_s` (60–3600, default `DIALOG_HOLD_DEFAULT` 60 s, PROVISIONAL). The hook's bound is
    `DIALOG_HOLD_MAX + 5 s` and the dialog `timeout` 3615, so viola still ends every wait. At expiry the reply is
    `null` and one `dialog-expired` line is written.
    - Pattern "Boundary widening the founder answered himself to a P4 fork": his own answer Q1, relayed verbatim by
      the operator (`inputs#I2`).
  - **architecture §Occupied Resources (Filesystem: `config.json`, the plugin's `hooks.json`).** The key, and the
    `timeout` 75 → 3615.
  - **architecture §Conventions (Normalised event kinds) and §Standard Contracts (Event `data` per kind; `wait`).**
    `dialog-expired` `{dialog_id, dialog_kind}`, `source: wrapper`. It is the first wrapper-appended kind that wakes
    `wait`, which is now six kinds; the sentence that every wrapper-appended record is log-only is amended to except
    it.
  - **architecture §Cross-cutting Patterns, Config management.** The new key, under the same pattern and answer.
  - **security-plan §Input Validation (Configuration values row; Hook stdin row: the bound 3605 s).** Under the same
    pattern and answer (`inputs#I2` Q1).
  - **obs-plan §4 Scenario: Dialog → `answer`.**
    - At expiry the wrapper writes `dialog-answered{deadline_hit:true}` with no `from`.
    - The hook, handed `null`, writes `hook-decision{decision_emitted:false, deadline_hit:false}`. Its own
      `deadline_hit:true` stays its backstop when the wrapper is unreachable past `DIALOG_HOLD_MAX + 5 s`.
    - `deadline_ms` reports the configured hold.
    - The `wait` scenario's `woken_kind` / `outcome` gain `dialog-expired`, §6 catalogs the product kind, and §1's
      copy moves with §4.
  - **test-plan §5 Cross-module patterns** (On-disk: sixteen kinds, rule `EventKind::ALL`'s length; CLI: the controls
    table at ten rows, rule `SETTINGS`) **and §4** (the wake set at six).
  - **design-system §Surface: cli §Component Patterns 3 and layout-templates §Output structure — `viola wait` /
    `viola last`.** `dialog-expired` takes the dialog form, as a planning form with the founder's wording owed.
  - **a11y-plan §8 Cognitive Accessibility → Timeout extensions.** The hold falls on the driver only (default 60 s,
    configurable 60–3600 s, PROVISIONAL), at expiry the dialog is left to the human with one `dialog-expired` record,
    and a late `answer` gets `unknown-dialog` (exit 13).
  - **architecture §Established Decisions [Hook Contract] (the live reading).** On claude 2.1.287 on the Linux dev
    host a dialog hook held about 660 s returned the driver's decision into the CLI (`evidence/live-round.md`). The
    3600 s ceiling stays PROVISIONAL and the Windows leg is owed to "Windows-only live measurements".

**Chunk:** a longer or configurable dialog hold and a record of an expired hold (gap-list group 2)

**Working entry (title, verbatim):** Dialog hold for the driver — a longer or configurable dialog hold and a record of
an expired hold (gap-list group 2)
**Epoch:** Epoch 5 — Driver surface · **version:** viola-0.1.0

- A dialog the wrapper holds for a driver's answer can be held long enough for a driver that relays the dialog to a
  person and back: the hold is longer than today's compiled `DIALOG_DEADLINE` (60 s, "PROVISIONAL, unmeasured",
  `crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs:16-19`), or configurable, or both (the entry: "a longer or configurable dialog hold").

- An expired hold leaves a record: today the hold's end at the deadline writes no event line, `wait` reports
  nothing, and a late `answer` is refused `unknown-dialog` (gap-list item 28,
  `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-08-first-live-test-and-self-drive/evidence/gap-list.md`). The entry: "a record of an
  expired hold".

- The record is a normalised event line in `events.ndjson` (a new kind beside `question` / `permission` / `plan`,
  carrying `dialog_id` and the dialog kind, no upstream text), so `wait` (CLI and the `mcp` `wait` tool) wakes on it
  and a driver learns the dialog is gone; the event catalog (obs-plan), the closed kind set (`viola-core`), the
  event-line contract (architecture §Standard Contracts) and the human `wait` line (`src/human/wait.rs`,
  `src/cmd/wait.rs`) each take it. (Closed at P3: a wrapper line reaches `wait` through `WaitFeed::appending`,
  `src/run/send/slot.rs:228`, and wakes it only when its kind is in `EventKind::WAIT_WAKE`, `src/run/wait.rs:200-206`;
  the logged `outcome` derives from the same set, `crates/viola-channel/src/server.rs:417`.)

- [premise-corrected: the wrapper replies `null` at its own deadline, 5 s before the hook's bound
  (`src/run/dialog.rs:281`, `src/cmd/hook.rs:64-70`), so the hook bound and `hooks.json` need only outlast the LONGEST
  hold] The hook side follows the hold's ceiling, not each start's hold: each dialog hook's `hooks.json` `timeout`
  (75 s today, `plugin/hooks/hooks.json:10,13`) must outlast the longest hold by at least 10 s (architecture [Hook
  Contract]; `hooks_json_dialog_timeouts_outlast_the_dialog_deadline`, `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/lib.rs:617-641`),
  and the hook's own bound (`DIALOG_DEADLINE + REPLY_GRACE`, `src/cmd/hook.rs:64-70`) moves with it. A configurable
  hold therefore leaves the rendered `timeout` a compiled literal and `plugin/<key>/` byte-identical across starts
  (`replace_private_shared`, `src/cmd/run.rs:403-409`).

- That the CLI honours a dialog hook `timeout` far past 75 s (the prototype held 3500 s, gap-list item 27, guide
  L55-56; a prototype hold of 58 min is recorded in
  `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers/inputs/I2-relay-2.md.txt`) is a CLI behaviour viola has not
  measured on 2.1.287 — under the project's rule a capability-ledger row with a `viola verify` probe, or a measured
  live reading, or a ruled limit. (Closed at P3: no ledger row names it, `LedgerRow::ALL` is 24,
  `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs:49`; the hold engages only on a stamped CLI with the wheel `driver`,
  `src/run/dialog.rs:199-202`, and no standing home holds a stamp of the 24-row set, so a live reading needs its own
  `viola verify` first.)

- The reply at expiry is a product question: today `null` (the CLI's own menu, left to the human,
  `src/run/dialog.rs:273-306`); the prototype denied with a fixed message and the driver answered later as a prompt
  (gap-list item 28). A viola-built deny at expiry would be viola deciding a dialog no one answered. (Closed at P3.)

- At HEAD an expired hold leaves no line saying so: the wrapper writes no `dialog-answered` at expiry
  (`ObsEvent::DialogAnswered` only in `answer`, `src/run/dialog.rs:372-381`), and the hook, handed a `null` reply,
  writes `hook-decision` with `deadline_hit:false` (`src/cmd/hook.rs:305-336`) — obs-plan §4's Dialog → `answer`
  scenario names `dialog-answered{…deadline_hit…}` and a `hook-decision{deadline_hit:true}` at the deadline. Closed at
  P3 (read at HEAD): the chunk writes `dialog-answered` with `deadline_hit:true` at expiry; the hook's
  `deadline_hit:true` stays its own backstop's (the wrapper unreachable), and obs-plan's sentence is amended to say so.

- The human always wins: a human key during a held dialog still hands it back at once (`hand_back`,
  `src/run/dialog.rs`), however long the hold.
- No config key, env var or flag may disable a control; a hold setting is bounded (a closed range), never "forever".

- Not in this chunk: gap-list groups 3 (screen read), 4 (`allow <n>`) and 5 (the start line and scripts, outside this
  repository); the switch itself and `v1-33` (owned by "Overseer switch to viola").

- CARRY (minted at the 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers wrap from its P5 review card's row 1, approved by the

- **Marker:** 2026-10-19-newer-claude-cli-rows · **Version:** viola-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-19T23:36Z
- **Base:** HEAD at P4, `50e2f76167ee` (every guard below names it).

- **Gated criterion's block (verbatim):** the founder's own word on the live-start cap and on Fork 2
  (`.andromeda/runs/2026-10-19T23-10-05-phase/founder-forks.md`). Planned this way on the overseer's PROVISIONAL
  delegate direction (`inputs#I4`), not on his answer.

claude 2.1.302 read `stamped 2.1.302  20 pass  4 fail` in the overseer's verify
(`chunks/2026-10-19-overseer-switch-to-viola/inputs/I20-verify-2.1.302-20261019.out.txt`). P3 re-measured the four
red rows from the CLI's own records (`inputs#I3`): they are one stop.

- After Run B's long paste, verify's `box_wait` waited its full 120 s for the input-box literal `"for agents"` and
  never saw it. So the tag-like, newline, `/compact` and `/clear` pastes were never typed.

- `tag-escaping` and `paste-newline` find no capture. `local-command-clear` and `local-command-compact` are anchored
  on those two captures (`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs:817-849`).

- The 2.1.302 bundle draws that footer hint only until `agentsHintExpired`, a 10 s value over the session's attached
  clients. 2.1.296 draws it always (`inputs#I3` R4).

- The same literal decides `run`'s pre-send readiness gate on a verified CLI (`src/run/gate.rs:508`). So the remedy is
  a product reliance, per architecture §Established Decisions [CLI Version Compatibility] and the scope's way (b):
  the input-box literal set gains the literal 2.1.302's resting input box keeps, measured live, and the 2.1.302
  shapes are recorded so CI's fake agent replays them.
Planned to complete now, with no live start:
- a fake-agent reproduction of the stop, where verify reads the same four rows red plus the `input-box-signature` row;

- that row also reads the screen Run B settles on after the long paste's turn, so it names the cause instead of
  passing by timing;

- the macOS readiness flake of `b6ddc198` (`inputs#I1` item 1). Its two wrappers stalled inside `run.start` before
  the version gate (`inputs#I3` R5). It is measured, then fixed at its measured cause.

The gated criterion is the founder's: the live screen measurement (Fork 2), the literal it yields, the 2.1.302 record
round and `--local-live` (Fork 1's cap). The live round and its fixtures follow architecture §Occupied Resources →
Repository and test-plan §3 `run` / §7.

1. **`TypedRun` keeps the long turn's screen.**
   - In `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs` add `long_turn: Option<Vec<String>>` to `TypedRun`
     (`ledger.rs:605`).
   - In `src/cmd/verify/typed.rs` `framing_turns` (`typed.rs:388`), set it to the rows `run.box_wait(stopped)` settles
     on after the FIRST added text (the long paste's) turn, or none when that wait fails or the turn never ended.
   - Thread it through `measure` / `trusted_run`'s `typed` the way `turn` is (`typed.rs:343-364`).
   - It is never written to `measured` (architecture §Standard Contracts → Ledger stamps envelope: `run` reads no
     number from the stamp, and no row text enters the stamp).

2. **The `input-box-signature` row reads it.**
   - `check(InputBoxSignature)` (`ledger.rs:1007-1009`) becomes `input_box_ready(ready) && input_box_ready(turn) &&
     input_box_ready(long_turn)`.
   - Its words stay `a trusted start shows a compiled input-box literal and no modal` (layout-templates §Output
     structure — `viola verify`: row ids, order and words unchanged).
   - Unit cases beside `check_input_box_signature_needs_both_screens_without_a_modal` (`ledger.rs:2425`), each name
     holding `long_turn`:
     - a `long_turn` holding the literal passes;
     - a `long_turn` holding a modal row fails;
     - a `long_turn` of `None` fails.
   - Every other `input-box-signature` case gets a `long_turn` holding the input-box row. Each case is a literal
     table (test-plan §4).

3. **The fake agent's `--long-turn-screen <phase>`.** In `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs`, with `--framing` and
   `--turn-stop`, `end_turn` (`viola-fake-agent.rs:723`) draws `Screen.<phase>` of the set after the long paste's turn
   in place of `Screen.turn`, as `--tag-turn-screen` does after the tag-like turn (`viola-fake-agent.rs:733`).
   - It is a test-only option, `cfg(feature = "fake-agent")` like every fake-agent mode.
   - Its parse cases are named for `long_turn_screen`, beside the `tag_turn_screen` ones (`viola-fake-agent.rs:1268`,
     `:1305`).
   - Its side effect comes after the turn's Stop, as the paste-hint hold does (verification-harness.md 2026-10-14).

4. **The reproduction case.** In `tests/cli_verify.rs` add `verify_pastes_nothing_more_once_the_long_turn_screen_shows_a_modal`
   beside `verify_pastes_no_local_command_once_the_tag_turn_screen_shows_a_modal` (`tests/cli_verify.rs:1442`), on the
   same `write_spine_set` / `write_screen` helpers. The screen after the long turn holds a modal literal beside the
   input box, so Run B's settle ends at once on a compiled literal and nothing waits out the 120 s. It asserts:
   - exit 1 and the summary: predicted `stamped 2.1.0  19 pass  5 fail` on Unix and `16 pass  5 fail` on Windows, the
     literal copied from the first run (testing.md 2026-10-16);
   - the five red rows exactly `input-box-signature`, `tag-escaping`, `local-command-clear`, `paste-newline`,
     `local-command-compact`, read from the stamp;
   - every other relied row `pass`;
   - the receipt's typed list exactly the probe prompt and the long paste;
   - `probes_left == 0`.

   Its red-before reading is taken with steps 1–3 built and step 2's `check` arm not yet extended. It must read
   `20 pass  4 fail` on Unix, the overseer's 2.1.302 verdict reproduced, its four red rows the set in
   `chunks/2026-10-19-overseer-switch-to-viola/inputs/I20-verify-2.1.302-20261019.out.txt`. That reading goes to `evidence/reproduction.md`.

5. **The moved literals.** Every `cli_verify` per-OS summary or row assertion that the long turn's screen changes moves
   deliberately, copied from the first run, never imported (test-plan §11).
   - Candidates: the no-framing and no-turn-stop summaries (`tests/cli_verify.rs:1375-1377`, and the case whose
     `input-box-signature` already reads `fail`, around `tests/cli_verify.rs:1420`).
   - A case whose run never reaches the long turn reads `input-box-signature` `fail` already and does not move.
   - The `--tag-turn-screen` case (`21 pass  3 fail`) is unchanged: its long turn draws the input box.

6. **The macOS readiness flake — measure first** (testing.md 2026-09-28: measure the phases on the runner that failed
   before changing the work; never raise a bound).
   - (a) The stalled wrapper's state in the watch report: in `tests/support/home.rs` `wait_ready` (`home.rs:615`), at
     the deadline and before the panic, append to the report the wrapper's own last `run-<name>.ndjson` event name. On
     macOS also append `/usr/bin/sample <pid> 1`'s call graph, its stack lines only; on Linux `/proc/<pid>/wchan` and
     `/proc/<pid>/stat`'s state field. It never signals the process (testing.md 2026-10-10) and adds nothing to a
     passing boot.
   - (b) The phase gap from recorded runs. From the `diag-macos-latest` artifacts of the operator pass's CI runs
     (the pre-CI commit's run and each fix run), and of ci#39321117796 both attempts, read every
     `run-*.ndjson`'s gap from `process-start{subject:"self"}` to `process-start{subject:"version-probe"}`. Record
     the distribution per run and every gap over 1 s in `evidence/macos-run-start.md`. The scratch reader lives in
     the chunk folder, never in `scripts/`.
   - (c) From (a) or (b), name the stalled phase of `run.start` (`src/cmd/run.rs:216-251`): `resolve_program`,
     `collision_check`, `pin_and_plugin` (`crates/viola-state/src/pin.rs:71-92`), `statusline_command` or
     `plan_strip`.

7. **The macOS readiness flake — fix at the measured cause.**
   - Change the named phase (or the test-side boot, if the reading puts the wait there) to remove the slow or blocking
     work. Keep `WITHIN`, every kill line, `retries = 0` and the test-thread count unchanged (test-plan §10; test-plan
     §11 bans serialisation and retries).
   - Its witness reinstates the cause and reads red, then the fix reads green, both recorded in
     `evidence/macos-run-start.md` (testing.md 2026-09-25, the remove-the-guard run). Where the cause is a slow phase,
     force it with a test-only hold that the fixed code no longer reaches (testing.md 2026-09-27); a new env seam
     needs a Decisions Log entry, so prefer a hold inside the test's own process.
   - If neither (a) nor (b) locates the phase on the runs the pass produces, step 7 does not run. The flake's
     acceptance reads unmet and the report names that: a red stays open until its cause is known (CLAUDE.md
     Tier 1).

body:
8. **The 2.1.302 footer reading** (Fork 2 option 1, `inputs#I4`'s fork text as corrected at P4: a
   `.viola-footer-<pid>/` cwd under the repo root).
   - `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-19-newer-claude-cli-rows/footer-reading.sh` first runs `cargo build -q` (a live rig
     rebuilds `target/debug/viola` first, handoff standing rule), then runs `target/debug/viola --home
     <tmpfs>/vhome run m302 -- <the 2.1.302 claude by path>` in a detached `tmux` session (80×24, that cwd), with
     `VIOLA_NAME` / `VIOLA_DIR` / `VIOLA_BIN` removed (testing.md 2026-10-07). No key is typed.
   - At ~2 s it runs one `viola --home <that home> list`, with the 2.1.302 install dir first on `PATH` so its
     `claude agents --json` reaches that CLI (verification-harness.md 2026-10-10).
   - At ~15 s and ~25 s it takes `tmux capture-pane -p`'s last three rows, scrubbed of the home and user word, into
     `evidence/footer-2.1.302.md`, with `date -u` beside each. Then `tmux kill-session` and the cwd removed, by a
     `trap` on every exit (neither `.viola-footer-*` nor `.viola-verify-*` is gitignored: `git check-ignore` exits 1).
   - It prints `footer-reading: written` last.
   - It counts as start 1 of the cap. It is the round's entry `bash viola-0.1.0/chunks/…/footer-reading.sh`, fired
     alone through `gate.py run … --live-legs --entry {n} --void {n}:block cleared — {his word}`.

9. **The literal.** From `evidence/footer-2.1.302.md`, choose the shortest text the 2.1.302 resting input box keeps
   at both readings that is not on any modal row.
   - Add it to `SIGNATURES.input_box` beside `"for agents"` (`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/screen.rs:39`), compiled,
     never built from screen text (security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Code Patterns).
   - Unit cases named for `resting_footer`:
     - `holds_any` reads each measured 2.1.302 row `true`, the 2.1.287 recorded row
       `"  ⏸ manual mode on · ← for agents"` still `true`, and each modal literal row unchanged;
     - a quiet verified screen whose only input-box row is the measured resting row reads `Ready`, its gate step
       `Done(Ready)` (`screen.rs:282` pattern).
   - Whether `viola list` expired the hint goes into `evidence/footer-2.1.302.md` (`send`'s exposure).

10. **The 2.1.302 record round** (6 starts): `viola verify --home <tmpfs>/vhome --record <out> -- <2.1.302 claude>`,
    then `fixtures/claude/2.1.302/` copied whole from `<out>/2.1.302/`. It must read
    `stamped 2.1.302  24 pass  0 fail`; `--record` writes only at 0 fail (architecture §Occupied Resources →
    Repository). One re-run after a red stays inside the cap Fork 1 option 1 holds, and never a third.

11. **The 2.1.302 set in CI.**
    - `tests/contract_ledger_probes.rs` lists `2.1.302` on the stamped list (each set on exactly one list, test-plan
      §5).
    - `contract_fake_agent_drift` and the `claude_fixtures` hygiene walk pick it up by their run-time walks (test-plan
      §6, §7).
    - The fake agent's default version stays 2.1.287 (`DEFAULT_CLI_VERSION`; leaned per test-plan history, chunk
      2026-10-04-dialog-answers-by-dialog-id: moving it is a deliberate decision this chunk does not need).

12. **`--local-live` on 2.1.302** (6 starts): `PATH` with the 2.1.302 install dir first, so the run stamps
    `target/e2e-home/viola-live-<pid>/home` at 2.1.302 and never `~/.viola` (test-plan §3 `run`).

13. **Fork 1 option 2 only:** a 2.1.296 verify (6 starts) into a fresh `--home`, reading `24 pass  0 fail`. Under
    option 3, steps 12–13 do not run. Fired only if his answer names that option.

- `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-19-newer-claude-cli-rows/footer-reading.sh` — step 8's reading (gated); the version

  where step 6 names it

The lint and unit entries run first, then the new cases by name, the integration and E2E binaries, the guards, the
harness smoke and `pre-push`.

**The gated live round** sits in one contiguous span (gate-contract §Live round: no non-leg entry inside it). Its
entries:
- the non-priming probe;
- the transcript count;
- the footer reading;
- a census;
- the record round;
- a census;
- the count again;
- `--local-live`;
- its census;
- the option-2 verify and its census.

Every round entry carries `defer = "gated: …"` and fires only through `--void {n}:block cleared — {his word}`. Step 8
fires alone (`--entry`) before step 9's code change, step 10 after it, step 12 after step 11. Starts per firing: the
footer reading 1, the record round 6, `--local-live` 6, the option-2 verify 6. The probe and counts start nothing.

The round is never re-run by the wrap; it is re-verified from `evidence/live-round.md`, which implement writes from
the round entries' logs and `date -u`. No entry produces that file and no entry reads it. The record entry's own
`contains stamped 2.1.302  24 pass  0 fail`, the fixture guard and the integration binaries assert the round on every
re-run of the block.

Steps 6(b) and 7's macOS readings come from CI artifacts the operator pass produces: `evidence/macos-run-start.md` is

- **The four failures are one stop, measured, not four** (`inputs#I3` R1, R2):
  - On 2.1.302, Run B's transcript holds two user turns only (the probe prompt and the long paste). The long paste's
    turn ended 18:18:53.356Z.
  - Run C's project dir appeared 18:20:55Z, ~122 s later. That gap is `box_wait`'s 120 s `PROBE_DEADLINE` running out
    on the screen after the long paste's turn (`typed.rs:402`).
  - So the tag-like, newline, `/compact` and `/clear` pastes were never typed. `tag-escaping` and `paste-newline` find
    no capture. `local-command-clear` and `local-command-compact` cannot pass by construction, being anchored on those
    two captures (`ledger.rs:817-849`).

  - The overseer's stamp agrees: 2.1.302's `compact_latency_ms` is null, while 2.1.296 reads 3648 (`inputs#I3` R3).

- **The cause in the CLI, read from the shipped bundle (not from a live screen)** (`inputs#I3` R4):
  - 2.1.296 draws the footer hint `" for agents"` unconditionally.
  - 2.1.302 draws it only while `restingHintExpired` is false. That flag is the app state's `agentsHintExpired`, set
    by `xxe()` from a 10 s value (`sIo=1e4`) over `Fc() != null`. `Fc` is
    `surfaceCapabilities.attacherCaps()`, which is set by an incoming `{type:"attacher-caps"}` message.
  - The literal `SIGNATURES.input_box` names is therefore not a stable input-box signature on 2.1.302. Unmeasured:
    - what makes `attacherCaps` non-null in Run B (its one `claude agents --json` read is the nearest candidate);
    - which of the bundle's twelve `Hr` definitions `xxe` calls, so whether the 10 s counts from the attach or from
      the start.

- **The same literal gates `send`**: `run`'s readiness gate reads `SIGNATURES` on a verified CLI (`src/run/gate.rs:508`).
  A 2.1.302 home stamped verified with today's literal set would refuse a `send` `input-not-ready` once the hint is gone
  (`src/run/send.rs:666`'s case is that path). The fix is a product reliance (scope's way (b)), not a probe fix alone.

- **`input-box-signature` passed on 2.1.302 by timing**: `check(InputBoxSignature)` reads the `ready` and `turn`
  screens only (`ledger.rs:1006-1008`). Both settle well inside 10 s (`ready_settle_ms` 1058, `turn_settle_ms` 317,
  `inputs#I3` R3). So the row cannot see a literal that disappears later.

- **Marker:** 2026-10-19-overseer-switch-to-viola · **Version:** viola-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-19T10:45Z

The viola overseer stops driving its builder (`viola-builder`, this repository's session) through the prototype
and drives it through this repository's `viola`. The switch is the v1-33 proof on the Linux dev host. With the
product binary and claude 2.1.296 stamped in `~/.viola`, the overseer sends a pipeline skill, waits for the turn,
reads the final text, answers a review dialog and clears between skills. A key the founder types in the session
terminal then takes the wheel, and his own `viola release` returns it.
The founder answered the four P4 forks himself (`inputs#I14`):
- **Start cap:** the builder keeps claude 2.1.296, with a live-start cap of 8.
- **Switch:** mid-implement.
- **Takeover:** he types the key and runs the release himself, later. No agent-typed key, so no widening.
- **New gaps:** both are built, the background tasks as a count only.
So the chunk ships three things:

- A small additive event-data change: each question option's `description` and `preview`, and a Stop's background
  task count on `turn-ended`, for the two gaps research found beyond the 2026-10-08 gap list (scope §Gaps found at P3).
- One verify and the switch, made at a turn end in the middle of implement.
- The recorded proof.

The takeover waits for the founder at his keyboard. It is this chunk's gated criterion (§Acceptance Criteria), so
the chunk can wrap `gated` and finish it later.

The overseer's scripts live outside this repository. They change as the overseer's own steps O1–O7 (§Overseer
steps), never as files of this repository (`inputs#I1`). This repository gains no subcommand, channel method, MCP
tool, env var or config key (per architecture §Established Decisions → [Scope Boundary]).

title: Part A — the two gaps (under the prototype, before the switch)

data.head: ### Part A — the two gaps (under the prototype, before the switch)

body:
1. **Option detail on the question event.** In `question_data` (`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/dialog.rs:138-155`;
   callers `dialog/classify` @ `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/dialog.rs:102`, `dialog/tool_data` @ `:129`, from the
   P3 graph query), each question object gains one key, `option_details`.
   - It is an array parallel to `options`, in the same order: one `{"description": <string|null>,
     "preview": <string|null>}` per option, read from that option's `description` and `preview`.
   - A key that is absent, or not a string, reads `null` and never refuses the dialog. The `label` rule
     (`DialogMalformed`) is unchanged.
   - `options`, `question`, `header` and `multi_select` keep their shapes. Decision bodies keep being built from the
     stored raw `input`.
   - Unit cases in that module:
     - `question_option_details_carry_description_and_preview`
     - `question_option_details_are_null_when_absent_or_not_a_string`
   - The existing data pin at `dialog.rs:523-529` is updated to the new shape, as are the `multi_select` pins in
     `src/run/dialog.rs`.

2. **Background task count on `turn-ended`.** In `normalise` (`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/hook.rs:116-162`, the
   `HookEvent::Stop` arm at `:162`; caller `cmd/hook/handle` @ `src/cmd/hook.rs:164`), a Stop's data gains
   `background_tasks`.
   - The value is the length of the payload's `background_tasks` array as a whole number, or `null` when the key is
     absent or not an array. A non-array value takes the same tolerant type-mismatch path the module already takes for
     a non-string `last_assistant_message` (`hook.rs:443-449`).
   - No element of the array is read or carried: no task text, id or description (the founder's "count only",
     `inputs#I14`).
   - Unit cases in that module:
     - `turn_ended_background_tasks_counts_the_array`
     - `turn_ended_background_tasks_is_null_when_absent_or_not_an_array`

3. **The kind's data keys.** `EventKind::TurnEnded`'s data keys (`crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs:119`) become
   `["last_assistant_message", "background_tasks"]`. The contract pin `kind_table_data_keys_are_the_contract_rows`
   (`crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs:636-638`) is updated with it. Readers then count no unknown key on a new line
   (`crates/viola-state/src/events.rs:214`).

4. **Reader cases.** In `crates/viola-state/tests/state_events.rs`, a `turn-ended` line carrying `background_tasks`
   and a `question` line carrying `option_details` are read with zero unknown-key skips.

5. **End to end under the fake agent.** In `tests/hook_events.rs`, two cases:
   - A recorded Stop (`fixtures/claude/2.1.287/Stop.default.json`) reaches `events.ndjson` as `turn-ended` with
     `background_tasks` equal to that fixture's array length.
   - A recorded AskUserQuestion (`fixtures/claude/2.1.287/PreToolUse.ask-user-question.json`) reaches it as a
     `question` whose `option_details` equal the fixture's per-option `description` / `preview`.
   - Each expected value is read from the fixture file, never typed into the test. The fake agent is unchanged: it
     already replays both fixtures byte for byte (`contract_fake_agent_drift`).

6. **Gates.** Every entry of §Test Commands up to and including `pre-push` reads green. The WATCH case
   (`send_budget_paused_is_refused_with_the_window_word_and_no_cursor` case_4) is an observation only. Every
   nextest run of it in this chunk is recorded in the report as `k/3`, with no retry and no `#[ignore]`
   (per test-plan §10).

title: Part B — the stamp and the switch point (the builder, still under the prototype)

data.head: ### Part B — the stamp and the switch point (the builder, still under the prototype)

body:
7. **The driving binary.**
   - `cargo build --release --bin viola` (the `build` entry) produces `target/release/viola` from the finished
     Part A tree.
   - `evidence/switch-round.md` opens with its sha256, the time, and the live-start ledger: cap 8 (`inputs#I14`),
     0 spent.
   - The overseer later copies that file out of the work tree (step O1), so the builder's own rebuilds never move the
     binary that drives it (scope §Facts, the last bullet).

8. **The verify of claude 2.1.296 (live starts 1–6 of 8).**
   - Before the run, record `claude --version` read by path as `2.1.296` (verification-harness.md 2026-10-10).
   - Then one `target/release/viola verify` with no `--home`, so its home is the default `~/.viola`, run from the
     repository root, a folder the user trusts.
   - Each start is ledgered with its clock time before it is made.
   - The printed last line must be `stamped 2.1.296  24 pass  0 fail` (layout-templates verify wireframe,
     `MM` 24 on Unix).
   - Then record `stat -c %a ~/.viola`, expected to read `700`: the product's log open narrowed it (`src/obs.rs:43-46`).
     `sessions/` and `archive/` are still listed (the prototype's folders, untouched).
   - **A failed relied row halts the chunk for the founder's word.** No fallback start (`inputs#I14` Q1).
   - The verify's CLI residual under `~/.claude` is counted in the evidence (per security-plan §Data Protection),
     never removed.

9. **The switch point.**
   - The builder writes the hand-off line into `evidence/switch-round.md`: the binary's sha256, the stamp line, and
     the prototype session id read from `~/.viola/sessions/viola-builder/session_id`.
   - It ends its turn naming the switch: "switch point reached; run O1–O6".
   - Nothing further runs under the prototype.

title: Overseer steps (outside this repository: the viola overseer's own, named here, never files of this repo)

data.head: ### Overseer steps (outside this repository: the viola overseer's own, named here, never files of this repo)

body:
These are the overseer's work in its own folders (`inputs#I1`). The builder neither edits nor runs them. Each one
is reported to the builder after the switch, as a line in the re-entry send, and the builder records it.

- **O1.** Copy `target/release/viola` to `~/.local/viola-product/bin/viola` (0700), and check its sha256 against
  step 7's. Every overseer call names this absolute path. The prototype stays first on the host's `PATH` for the
  other overseers (scope §Facts).

- **O2.** Write `~/.viola/config.json` at 0600 as `{"v":1,"dialog_hold_s":3600}` (per `schemas/config.v1.json`),
  before the switched start. The hold is read once at the wrapper's start (history 2026-10-19-dialog-hold-for-the-driver).

- **O3.** The viola-builder start line. `vb.sh` / `vbr.sh` (`inputs#I2`, `inputs#I3`) and `vstart.sh`
  (`inputs#I7`) gain a product form for viola-builder only:
  - `<O1 path> run viola-builder -- claude --effort high -n viola-builder [--resume <id>]` in its own terminal
    window, with the same Hyprland placement.
  - Dropped from that form: `--plugin-dir` (run writes its own plugin), `--dialog-timeout` (O2 sets the hold), and
    the session-folder archive (the product never deletes).
  - The already-running check reads the product's `list --json`.
  - `pulse-builder`, `conductor-builder`, `escher-builder` and `andromeda-worker` keep their prototype launch
    byte-for-byte: `vstart.sh` is shared (`inputs#I10`–`I13`).
  - The prototype forms of `vb.sh` / `vbr.sh` are kept beside the new ones as the fallback.

- **O4.** `up.sh`'s viola-overseer row (`inputs#I8`) raises viola-builder through `<O1 path> revive viola-builder`
  after a reboot, where it used `vb.sh --continue`. `revive` resumes the newest logged id
  (history 2026-10-10-viola-revive).

- **O5.** The wait scripts.
  - `waitm.sh` (`inputs#I4`) calls the O1 path: `wait viola-builder --after <cursor> --json`, with `last`.
  - It reads the product's kinds (`turn-ended`, `question`, `permission`, `plan`, `session-end`, `dialog-expired`,
    `timed out`) in place of the prototype's first-line words.
  - It prints each option's `preview` from the question event's `option_details` (Part A step 1), not from a
    `dialogs/<id>.json`.
  - `waitlong.sh` (`inputs#I5`) reads STATUS `idle` / `busy` from `list --json`. It reads the background-task count
    from the `turn-ended` line in `~/.viola/instances/viola-builder/events.ndjson` (Part A step 2), not from a Stop
    payload.
  - `scr.sh` (`inputs#I6`) has no product counterpart (gap-list group 3, unbuilt by the founder's Q3 of 2026-10-17)
    and is not used for viola-builder.

- **O6.** End the prototype-wrapped builder at its switch-point turn end.
  - The prototype's processes for viola-builder are confirmed gone, and no live `claude` holds its session id:
    the product `list` shows no unwrapped row for it. Two writers on one transcript is a measured hazard
    (history 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board).
  - Then start it with O3's form and `--resume <the step 9 id>`: **live start 7 of 8**.
  - `revive` cannot take this first start, because no product log holds the id yet (scope §Facts).

- **O7.** `driving-guide.md` (`inputs#I9`) is re-written for the product. It covers:
  - `send` text from stdin or `--file`.
  - `answer <name> <dialog_id>` with one JSON document on stdin.
  - `release` as the founder's verb, never the overseer's.
  - Any key of the founder's, Esc included, takes the wheel until his `release`.
  - The cap rule: live start 8 is the one spare `revive`. A start past 8 waits for the founder's word.

title: Part C — the proof (the builder, under the product)

data.head: ### Part C — the proof (the builder, under the product)

body:
10. **The re-entry is the skill send.** The overseer sends `/andromeda-implement` through `send` (O1 path, text on
    stdin), and implement re-enters at this step. The builder records `evidence/switch-readings.ndjson` lines (one
    JSON object per act: `act`, the clock time, cursors, kinds, exit codes, durations, never any text) for:
    - `switched` — the start records `wheel{holder:"driver",cause:"start"}`, `budget-gate`, `session-start`;
      `snapshot.json`'s `cli_version` `2.1.296` and `cli_verified` true; the O1–O6 reports. It also records that every
      exec-form `command` in `~/.viola/plugin/<version>-<hash>/hooks/hooks.json` and `.mcp.json` and in
      `~/.viola/instances/viola-builder/settings.json` is an absolute path (a count of `command` values and of absolute
      ones, never the paths themselves).
    - `verify-stamped` — step 8's stamp line, sha256 and mode reading.
    - `skill-sent` — the `send-issued` / `send-confirmed{confirmed:true}` pair of this send, by cursor.

11. **The review dialog.**
    - The builder raises the switch-record review as one question dialog (AskUserQuestion: "Is the switch record
      complete? approve / revise"). Its two options carry a `description` and a `preview` of the record, which
      Part A step 1 now carries.
    - The overseer answers it with `answer viola-builder <id>`, a non-`null` decision.
    - The builder records `review-answered`: the `question` event with `option_details` present, then
      `dialog-answered` with `from` and its `duration_ms`.
    - A late answer is a natural hold reading, never a contrived one. If `duration_ms` is 3000 s or more, it is the
      CARRY's near-ceiling reading (scope §Folded freight). Otherwise the CARRY stays owed (§Beyond the plan, on the
      card).

12. **The clear between skills.**
    - The builder ends its turn asking for a clear.
    - The overseer `wait`s (woken by `turn-ended`), reads `last` (exit 0), sends `/clear` (read back by
      `session-start{cause:"clear"}` with a new `agent_session_id`), and sends `/andromeda-implement` again.
    - Implement re-enters here and records three acts, from the home's `events.ndjson` and
      `diagnostics/run-viola-builder.ndjson` (`channel-request` / `channel-response` method `wait`, `last`):
      - `turn-waited` — the `turn-ended` cursor and its `background_tasks` count.
      - `final-read`.
      - `clear-confirmed`.

13. **The record.**
    - `evidence/switch-round.md` gains the act table, the live-start ledger (expected 7 of 8 spent), the counted
      CLI residual, and the count of `event:"panic"` lines in `~/.viola/diagnostics/*.ndjson` (expected 0, read by
      hand; per obs-plan §10).
    - The §Test Commands evidence readers read green, except the gated one.
    - Implement reports. The operator pass, its push, the CI read and the wrap all run under the product, driven
      by the overseer.

title: Part D — the gated takeover (the founder at his keyboard; this chunk's LAST attended step)

data.head: ### Part D — the gated takeover (the founder at his keyboard; this chunk's LAST attended step)

body:
14. **The takeover.**
    - At a builder turn end the overseer names, the founder presses one key in the viola-builder terminal window
      himself. That writes `wheel{holder:"human",cause:"human-input"}`.
    - The overseer's next `send` must exit 10 `human-typing`, with no `send-issued`.
    - The founder runs `~/.local/viola-product/bin/viola release viola-builder` in his own terminal. His shell carries
      no `VIOLA_NAME`, and `viola` on his `PATH` is the prototype, so he uses the full path. It prints
      `viola-builder  wheel driver  you have control` and writes `wheel{holder:"driver",cause:"release"}`.
    - The builder records `takeover` with the three cursors and the exit code.
    - **If he is back before the wrap**, the gated entry runs through `--void <n>:block cleared — evidence/switch-readings.ndjson takeover line`.
    - **If he is not**, the wrap flips this record `gated` and pins nothing else. When he is at his keyboard, the
      overseer runs `/andromeda-implement` (its gated mode), which runs this step alone, then
      `/andromeda-wrap-session` flips it `complete`. Every other act stands verified meanwhile.
    - No agent ever types this key (`inputs#I14` Q3).
- `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-19-overseer-switch-to-viola/evidence/switch-round.md` — the binary, the verify, the switch, the act table, the live-start ledger and residual (steps 7–9, 13, 14)
- `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-19-overseer-switch-to-viola/evidence/switch-readings.ndjson` — one line per act (steps 10–12, 14)
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/dialog.rs` — `option_details` in `question_data`, two unit cases, the data pin (step 1)
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/hook.rs` — `background_tasks` count on the Stop arm, two unit cases (step 2)
- `crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs` — `TurnEnded` data keys and its contract pin (step 3)
- `crates/viola-state/tests/state_events.rs` — the two known-key reader cases (step 4)
- `tests/hook_events.rs` — the two fixture-driven end-to-end cases (step 5)
- `src/run/dialog.rs` — its question-data unit pins (step 1)

The standing lint entries run first. Next come the unit layer and then the new cases by name, then the integration
and E2E layers. A preservation guard guards the modify list, against base `f23586fbda77` (HEAD at P4). The release
build the switch runs on comes next, then the booted smoke, G2, G4 and `pre-push`, then the operator pass. The three
evidence readers come last.

The live acts (steps 8, 10–12, 14) are not entries. Their starts are the founder's cap (`inputs#I14`), which a
light-gate re-run must never spend, and the overseer drives them. The readers carry no `artifact`: steps 7–14 produce
the evidence files, and the wrap re-verifies them from `evidence/`. The takeover reader is the gated criterion's
entry, with `defer = "gated: …"`. No mutation entry is listed (test-plan §10: the epoch-boundary audit).

body:
- (arch) A `question` event's data carries, for each question, `option_details` parallel to `options`, each
  `{description, preview}` a string or `null`. A missing or non-string value never refuses the dialog
  (per architecture §Standard Contracts; held by the new filter entry and `binary(hook_events)`).

- (tests) The WATCH case reads green on every run made in this chunk, with no retry or `#[ignore]` (per test-plan §10
  Quality Gates & Coverage Targets, Zero-flakiness budget).

- (security) The live verify prints `stamped 2.1.296  24 pass  0 fail` in `~/.viola`. The switched builder's
  `snapshot.json` reads `cli_verified` true, and the review dialog is answered with a non-`null` decision only on that
  stamp (per security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Universal).

- (security) Every exec-form `command` in the switched builder's `plugin/<version>-<hash>/hooks.json` and
  `.mcp.json` and in `instances/viola-builder/settings.json` is an absolute path, as read in step 10
  (per security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Universal).

- (obs) The record cites kinds, cursors, exit codes and durations only: no prompt, skill or dialog text,
  `last_assistant_message` or `detail-*.ndjson` content anywhere under the chunk folder. The live home's home-level
  role files hold zero `event:"panic"` lines (per obs-plan §8 PII Scrubbing; per obs-plan §10 SLO Invariants).

- (layouts) The overseer's `wait` ends in a product result line or its `--json` document. The `/clear` reads back
  on its new-session post-condition, and every human line form of `send · wait · last · answer · list · release`
  stays byte-identical, the new data reaching `--json` and the MCP results only
  (per layout-templates §Surface: cli · IA notes).

- (a11y) The zero-viola-bytes passthrough property stays held by its existing outer-PTY cases, inside the
  `run --integration` and `run --e2e` entries. The live builder's terminal is not read, because no screen read is built
  or used (per a11y-plan §1 Entity: `viola run` TUI passthrough; per a11y-plan §11 Universal).

- `verification-matrix.json#v1-33` — on the Linux dev host, with the product binary (`target/release/viola` of this
  chunk's tree, its sha256 recorded) and claude 2.1.296 stamped 24/24 in `~/.viola`, the viola overseer drives
  viola-builder through the product's CLI. It sends a pipeline skill (`send-confirmed{confirmed:true}`), waits for the
  turn (a `wait` woken by `turn-ended`), reads the final text (`last`, exit 0), answers a review dialog (a
  `dialog-answered` with `from`), and clears between skills (`/clear` read back by `session-start{cause:"clear"}` with
  a new id): the seven ungated acts of the first reader entry. A key the founder types in the session terminal takes
  the wheel (`wheel{holder:"human",cause:"human-input"}`, the next send exit 10), and his `viola release` returns it —
  **gated: the founder at his keyboard in the viola-builder terminal for his own key and his own viola release (he is
  away from the builders' terminals at the take-up, inputs#I14)**, proved by the takeover reader entry. Afterwards the
  overseer drives viola-builder through the product (O3–O5 reported in `evidence/switch-round.md`).

- Spec anchors: architecture §Established Decisions → [Scope Boundary], [CLI Version Compatibility], [Human Takeover / Wheel], [Session Liveness]; architecture §Standard Contracts; architecture §Cross-cutting Patterns → Config management; security-plan §Authentication & Authorization; security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Universal; security-plan §Data Protection; test-plan §3 `run`, §6, §10, §11; obs-plan §4 Scenarios (Confirmed `send`, Dialog → `answer`, Human takes the wheel), §8, §10; layout-templates §Surface: cli · IA notes and Output structure; design-system §Surface: cli Component Patterns 2–4; a11y-plan §1, §4 P4, §8 Timeout extensions.

- Research files inspected: `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/dialog.rs`, `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/hook.rs`, `crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs`, `crates/viola-state/src/events.rs`, `src/run/dialog.rs`, `src/cmd/run.rs`, `src/obs.rs`, `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/lib.rs`, `fixtures/claude/2.1.287/`.

- External inputs: `inputs#I1` (the operator's direction), `inputs#I2`–`I9` (the overseer's scripts and guide as at the take-up), `inputs#I10`–`I13` (the launchers sharing `vstart.sh`), `inputs#I14` (the founder's four answers).

- Leaned decisions:
  - **Home: the default `~/.viola`.** Leaned per research: only the default home reads the founder's
    `~/.claude/settings.json` status line. A product start narrows it to 0700 and takes nothing from the prototype's
    same-user processes (`src/obs.rs:43-46`).
  - **Overseer drives by the CLI, not MCP.** Leaned per research: MCP would need the overseer's own session restarted
    with the plugin, a `claude` start outside the cap (history 2026-10-17-optional-plugin-install).
  - **`option_details` as a parallel array.** Leaned per layout-templates §Surface: cli · IA notes ("new fields go
    into `--json` first"): `options` keeps its `[label]` shape for every existing reader.

- Changing `options` from `[label]` to `[{label, description, preview}]` — rejected. It breaks every existing reader
  of the question data (`multi_select` sweep: 3 files, `research.md` §Sweeps); `option_details` is additive.

- Carrying the `background_tasks` array or any element of it — rejected. It is the founder's "count only"
  (`inputs#I14` Q4), and it keeps task descriptions (upstream text) off the event.

- An agent typing the takeover key, or the overseer running `viola release` — rejected (`inputs#I14` Q3; a
  driver-facing release is banned, architecture §Established Decisions → [MCP]).

- A fallback verify of 2.1.287 on a failed 2.1.296 row — rejected by `inputs#I14` Q1. A failed row halts for the
  founder's word.

- Starting the switched builder by `viola revive` — not possible for the first start: no product log holds the id.
  O6 uses `run … -- claude --resume <id>`.
- Editing any overseer script or doc from this session — forbidden (`inputs#I1`); O1–O7 are the overseer's.
- A contrived long hold to read the 3600 s ceiling — rejected. Only a hold that arises naturally (step 11) is read.

- Live-start ledger (cap 8, `inputs#I14`): 6 for the verify (history 2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows: "A
  verify is six `claude` starts"), 1 for O6's switched start, 1 spare for one `revive` after a crash. `claude --version`
  and `claude agents --json` reads are not starts. A ninth start waits for the founder's word.

- Fallback: a product defect after the switch that stops the driving (a wrapper fault, a refusal loop) is fixed in
  this chunk, because a red met during a chunk folds into it. The overseer first restarts the builder under its kept
  prototype scripts, and that restart spends no product start but is ledgered. The second switch is the spare start.

- The builder's switched child inherits the overseer's environment. The R8 strip removes `CLAUDE*` values (history
  2026-09-25-pty-wrapper-on-windows), and step 10 records the `process-start{claude-child}` stripped names, names only.

- The overseer's `send`, `wait`, `last` and `answer` write their frames under the dated liveness-only gaps (fourth to
  sixth). This chunk adds no frame, method or process (per security-plan §Authentication & Authorization).

- Expected amendments (wrap):
  - architecture §Standard Contracts — the `question` data's `option_details` and the `turn-ended` data's
    `background_tasks` (count). The option text crossing into `events.ndjson`, `wait --json` and the MCP `wait` is a
    "Boundary widening" (playbook) answered by the founder himself to P4 fork Q4 (`inputs#I14`), so the wrap halts
    once as the answer card.
  - security-plan §Input Validation / §Data Protection — the same widening, the same answer.
  - obs-plan §4 Scenario: `wait` / `last` event-driven readback — the two additive keys.
  - test-plan §6 Paths 3–4 — the new cases by name. test-plan §6 also gets the switch's live readings stated as a
    local measurement, not a suite.
  - a11y-plan §3 Keyboard test harness — the takeover reading on the product, once step 14 is read.

- v1-33's dated note (the switch record, the stamp, the gated part) rides its claim at P5 step 4 (`--note-file`),
  never a wrap ledger note: the cap is planned, not verified.

**Chunk:** Overseer switch to viola — the overseer drives its builder through the product viola instead of the prototype; v1-33 proven live
**Date:** 2026-10-19
**Commits:** `aa965127 chore(2026-10-19-overseer-switch-to-viola): operator pre-CI commit, for the run this chunk's verdict reads` (the one commit since `last_wrap` 2026-10-19T09:56:16Z; `git log --format='%h %s' f23586fb..HEAD`)

- **Files:** six source/test files (research's Files to modify, all six; `gate.py scope`: `clean — changed 6 · listed 6 · recorded 0`):
  - `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/dialog.rs`
  - `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/hook.rs`
  - `crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs`
  - `crates/viola-state/tests/state_events.rs`
  - `tests/hook_events.rs`
  - `src/run/dialog.rs`

  The chunk folder (`plan.md`, `research.md`, `scope.md`, `evidence/{switch-round.md, switch-readings.ndjson, profraw-red.md, operator-pass.md}`, `inputs/` I1–I20) and `viola-0.1.0/verification-matrix.json` (v1-33) are bookkeeping. No master, key file, leaf or fixture was edited.

- **Symbols / APIs:**
  - **`question` event data** (`viola_agent_claude::dialog::question_data`, private; `dialog.rs` 151-156 per the listing below):
    - Each question gains `option_details`: one `{description, preview}` per option, parallel to `options`. Each field is the option's string or `null`.
    - A missing or non-string value gives `null` and never refuses the dialog.
    - `options` keeps its `[label]` shape.
    - The data reaches every consumer of the question data: `events.ndjson`'s `question` line, `hook.dialog`'s frame, CLI `wait --json` and the MCP `wait` result. Human `wait` lines are unchanged.
    - The doc comment at `dialog.rs:119-120` states the new shape.
  - **`turn-ended` event data** (`viola_agent_claude::hook::data_of`, Stop arm; `hook.rs` 170-173):
    - It gains `background_tasks`: the Stop payload's `background_tasks` array length, or `null` when the key is absent, `null` or not an array.
    - No element is read or carried: `Known.background_tasks` is `Option<Vec<serde::de::IgnoredAny>>` (`hook.rs` 104-105).
    - A non-array value writes a drift entry `{"path":"background_tasks","expected":"array"}` (`hook.rs` 147-152). Before this chunk every drift entry's `expected` was `string`, and the doc comment of `Known` (`hook.rs:92`) is reworded.
  - **`viola_core::EventKind::TurnEnded` data keys** (`lib.rs:119`): `["last_assistant_message", "background_tasks"]`. The `KIND_TABLE` pin follows at `lib.rs:550`.
  - No IPC method, CLI verb, flag, env var, port, socket or exit code changed. No function signature changed, so every caller is unchanged.
- **Crates / modules:** changed `viola-agent-claude` (`dialog`, `hook`) and `viola-core` (`EventKind` data keys); added none, removed none.
- **Dependencies:** none (`Cargo.toml` / `Cargo.lock` untouched; `serde::de::IgnoredAny` is in serde already pinned).

- **Schema / config:**
  - Two additive data keys on product event lines: `question.data.questions[].option_details` and `turn-ended.data.background_tasks`. There is no `v` bump; readers skip unknown fields.
  - `background_tasks` is a count only, by the founder's "count only" (`inputs#I14` Q4), and no task text crosses.
  - `option_details` carries the CLI's option `description` / `preview` text into `events.ndjson`, `wait --json` and the MCP `wait`. That is upstream text crossing a boundary: the "Boundary widening" (playbook) the founder answered himself at P4 fork Q4 (`inputs#I14`). The plan expects ONE halt on it at this wrap, as the answer card.
  - No config key changed. The overseer's home `~/.viola/config.json` carries `dialog_hold_s` 3600 (O2, the overseer's, outside this repo).
- **Spec-master edits:** none.
- **Retired:** none.

- **Counts / qualifiers moved:**
  - **`turn-ended`'s data keys, `{last_assistant_message}` → `{last_assistant_message, background_tasks}`.** Pattern `turnended` (`turn-ended`): 36 standing.
    - `architecture.md:255` (`- \`turn-ended\`: \`{last_assistant_message}\` (string or \`null\`)`): **stale**.
    - `architecture.md:230`: an example `hook.event` frame whose `data` holds only `last_assistant_message`. A Stop's frame now carries `background_tasks` too: **stale example**.
    - The other 34 are true claims sharing the token (the wake set, budget triggers, turn running/ended, CLI line forms): no-change.
    - Pattern `bgtasks`: control unfired over the masters at aa965127 (0 sites; the refusal line `control: bgtasks … never fired over the seven masters' pre-pass text (aa965127)`).

data.head: ## Facts measured at the take-up that the plan must meet (closed at P3)

body:
- `viola` first on the host's PATH is the prototype (`which -a viola`: `…/viola-lab/prototype/target/debug/viola`).
  The other overseers keep using it, so the switched overseer names the product by absolute path. (Verified.)

- The installed `claude` is 2.1.296 (`claude --version`; 2.1.287, 2.1.288, 2.1.289 also installed under mise), and
  every product ledger stamp so far is on 2.1.287. On a CLI version with no `viola verify` stamp in the builder's home,
  `cli_verified` is false. Then a non-`null` dialog decision is refused `unverified-cli`, and a send is confirmed
  after the fact only. `[premise-corrected: it is worse than "answers refused" — on an unverified CLI every dialog is
  answered null AT ONCE, never held, so the builder's own dialogs (its founder forks, its review card) fall to the CLI's
  menu in its terminal; src/run/dialog.rs:436, src/cmd/run.rs:869-886]`. `run` takes an absolute program path as
  given (`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/lib.rs:510`), so a builder can run a pinned CLI install.

- `~/.viola` (the product's default home) is the prototype's state root, mode 0755, holding `sessions/` and `archive/`
  for five builders. The product's strict-modes check refuses a home that is not 0700, and a product start narrows an
  existing home to 0700 (`src/obs.rs:43-46`, verified). The prototype's processes run as the same user, so the
  narrowing takes nothing from them. Only the default home reads the user's status line (`~/.claude/settings.json`
  holds a `command` status line); a separate `--home` reads none until `statusline-source.json` is planted. (Verified.)

- The builder that implements this chunk is the session being switched. The switch restarts it under the product
  wrapper, so the moment of the switch decides which of this chunk's own pipeline steps (implement, wrap) run under
  the product. Its first product start is `viola run viola-builder -- claude --resume <id>`, the id from the
  prototype's `~/.viola/sessions/viola-builder/session_id`. `viola revive` only resumes an id a product instance log
  holds (history 2026-10-10-viola-revive), so it serves the restarts after the first. (Verified.)

- The product binary that drives the builder must not be the `target/debug/viola` the builder rebuilds while it works.
  `run` pins a hashed copy under `bin/<version>-<hash>/` for the hooks, but the wrapper process and the overseer's CLI
  calls run the path they were started from (history 2026-09-27-instance-state-and-start-order). (Verified.)

data.head: ## Gaps found at P3 beyond the 2026-10-08 gap list

body:
The founder's Q3 answer named groups from the 2026-10-08 list. These two were not on it; both stop a part of the
overseer's procedure as `inputs#I4`, `inputs#I5` and `inputs#I9` hold it.

- **Option detail.** A `question` event carries each option's `label` only. `question_data` drops `description`
  and `preview` (`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/dialog.rs:138-155`), although the CLI sends both (recorded in
  `fixtures/claude/2.1.287/PreToolUse.ask-user-question.json`). `waitm.sh` prints each option's `preview` from the
  prototype's `dialogs/<id>.json`, and the overseer relays a builder's founder fork with its options' arguments. On
  the product it would relay bare labels.

- **Background tasks at a turn end.** `turn-ended` carries `last_assistant_message` only (`hook.rs:162`;
  `EventKind::TurnEnded` data keys, `crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs:119`). The Stop payload's `background_tasks` is
  dropped (recorded in `fixtures/claude/2.1.287/Stop.default.json`). `waitlong.sh` returns on a turn end whose Stop
  `background_tasks` is empty: the builder then waits for its driver (V103, V105 in `inputs#I9`). On the product it
  cannot tell a progress turn end from one that waits for the driver.
Whether these are built in this chunk or the overseer adapts is a P4 fork.

  away from the builders' terminals at the take-up, so the takeover reading (v1-33's "a key typed in the session
  terminal takes the wheel") cannot be taken now. Every other act proceeds; the takeover is the chunk's last attended
  step and its gated criterion.
