title: Item (5) — the sizes (pure moves, behaviour unchanged)

data.head: ### Item (5) — the sizes (pure moves, behaviour unchanged)

body:
2. **Before any move, record the baseline.** Write each touched package's `cargo nextest list --features fake-agent
   --message-format oneline` output for `viola`, `viola-agent-claude`, `viola-state`, `viola-e2e` and `viola-mcp`, plus the
   tokei code-line count of each file this item touches, to `evidence/sizes-before.md`. These are the before readings
   step 5 compares against.

3. **Move `ledger.rs`'s test module out.** Its body goes, whole, to the new file `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger/tests.rs`,
   and `ledger.rs` keeps only `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;` in its place.
   - Every test keeps its name. The module path stays `ledger::tests::…`.
   - In the same move, fold the relied-count assert at `ledger.rs:1606-1609` (one `#[cfg(unix)]` statement and one
     `#[cfg(windows)]` statement) into a single statement whose expected count comes from a `cfg!(unix)` expression
     (24 on Unix, 21 elsewhere). Without this, `tests/contract_windows_mutation_scope.rs:59-66` reads the moved file whole
     as product code, sees a Windows gate, and fails because no matrix line holds the file (research.md §Conventions).
   - `ledger.rs` itself still stands at about 1214 code lines (tokei at HEAD). That is expected: the move takes it off
     `sizes.file_max`, but not off `sizes.over_800` (scope.md §Item (5)).

4. **Split `src/cmd/verify/typed.rs` and `src/human/board.rs` by concern.** Each becomes a module root plus child files
   under `src/cmd/verify/typed/` and `src/human/board/`.
   - The root re-exports what its callers use, so every caller keeps its path: `src/human.rs:16` keeps `BayBudget`,
     `home_state_pair`, `instance_state_pair` and `write_board`, and `src/cmd/verify.rs` keeps `typed::measure`,
     `typed::RunDirs` and `typed::Inputs`.
   - Each child keeps its own inline `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` at its bottom, holding the cases of the concern it took
     (test-plan §4).
   - Every case keeps its name: the `bay_line_*`, `board_row_*`, `escape_row_*` and `instance_and_home_state_pairs_*` units
     named by a11y-plan §4 and §8, and `typed.rs`'s Epoch 4 kills (`added_turn_ended`, `local_command_answered`,
     `probe_until`, `SharedPty`, `ctrl_c_ending`, `ended_by`).
   - The concern seams research read:
     - typed: the runs and their args; the framing turns and the waits; the PTY plumbing (`KeyPipe`, `SharedPty`, `Feed`,
       `Sink`); `Run`.
     - board: the refusal pairs; the BAY line; the cells and spans; the rows and the writer.
   - Every new file stands under 800 tokei code lines, its tests included. If one does not, split it at the next seam.
   - No styled byte moves out of `src/human/style.rs`. No `#[allow(clippy::print_stdout)]` lands on a module root; it may
     stay only on a site that writes (obs-plan §11 Logs). No `obs_event!` site, `#[instrument(skip_all, fields(..))]` or
     `human::refuse(` call changes in number.

5. **Read back after the moves.**
   - Each package's test listing equals step 2's, except for the module segment a moved case gains.
   - Write the tokei counts to `evidence/sizes-after.md`.
   - Count, before and after, the verify spawn-pair `obs_event!` sites (`grep -rn 'obs_event!' src/cmd/verify`, read by
     subject) and the `human::refuse(` calls (`grep -rhoE 'human::refuse\(' src | wc -l`; 14 at HEAD). Write both counts to
     `evidence/sizes-after.md`.

6. **Close the `serde` reading.**
   - Drop `serde.workspace = true` from `crates/viola-mcp/Cargo.toml` and run `cargo check -p viola-mcp --all-targets`.
   - Green: the edge goes, `Cargo.lock` follows, and `cargo machete crates/viola-mcp` reads clean. The removal departs
     from architecture §Infrastructure Patterns → Crate dependency direction, which lists the edge, so it goes to the wrap
     as an expected amendment.
   - Red: the edge stays. The failing reading (the error code and the derive that needs it, no path) goes to
     `evidence/serde.md`, and the machete gate's red is recorded as unmet. No machete `ignored` entry is written
     (§Constraints).

title: Item (4) — the 16 survivors, each killed in its own package

data.head: ### Item (4) — the 16 survivors, each killed in its own package

body: For every row below, implement does four things:
- writes the case first;

- applies the mutant by hand, over a scratch clone of HEAD (`--project-root {clone}`) where the classifier refuses the
  in-tree edit;
- reads the case red by its own panic line under `test(/(^|::)tests::<name>(::|$)/)`;

- reverts, reads it green, and records both readings in `evidence/survivors.ndjson`, one line per survivor
  (`{n, site, mutation, case, red, green, kind}`, where `kind` is `killed` or `restated`, as in chunk
  2026-10-13-epoch-4-survivors's ledger).
The site lines are as read at HEAD 844de976 (scope.md §Item (4)).

7. **#1 `LedgerRow::relied_here` → `true`** (`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs:142`).
   - Restate: `relied()` filters on `relied_on(WRAPPED_HERE)` directly, and `relied_here` goes. Its only caller is
     `relied()` (`ledger.rs:157`, the graph query; a name grep finds no other), so the site no longer exists.
   - The decision it wrapped, `relied_on(row, wrapped)`, is already reached on both arguments by `ledger.rs:1593`'s case.
   - The witness is `relied_on` → `true` applied by hand: that case reads red.
   - `kind: restated`.

8. **#2, #3 `statusline::probe_document` → `Some("xyzzy")` / `Some(String::new())`** (`statusline.rs:117`).
   - New case `statusline_probe_document_on_a_wrapped_host_is_the_capture_command_document`.
   - On a `cfg!(unix)` host the document equals the literal JSON text, with
     `"<pinned> hook statusline --capture <dir> --shell \"$0\""` as its command. The oracle is a literal, never
     `probe_on`'s output.
   - Elsewhere the document is `None`.
   - Each mutant reads red.

9. **#15, #16 `liveness::live_endpoint` → `None` / `!=` → `==`** (`liveness.rs:74`, `:76`).
   - New case `live_endpoint_of_a_live_instance_is_its_endpoint_and_of_a_stale_one_none`.
   - Write a snapshot through `write_snapshot` with this process's pid, `own_start(pid)` and an `endpoint`, then touch the
     heartbeat through `touch_heartbeat`. That reads `Some(endpoint)`.
   - The same snapshot with no heartbeat reads `None`.
   - Nothing is hand-written (test-plan §11 Test Data). The kill sits in `viola-state`'s own unit tests, sync, with no new
     dependency (architecture §Cross-cutting Patterns → Tokio containment).

10. **#4, #5 `scratch::prepare` → `Ok(None)` / `delete !`** (`crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run/mutants/scratch.rs:47`, `:48`).
    - Restate as `prepare(root, host: bool)`. `mutate()` (`mutants.rs:223`, its only caller) passes `HOST_SCRATCH`, so the
      behaviour is unchanged on every host.
    - New case `prepare_on_the_scratch_host_empties_the_scratch_and_off_it_is_none`, on every OS, with the root inside its
      own tempdir so the scratch is the tempdir's `viola-mutants-scratch` child:
      - `prepare(root, true)` creates and then empties it (bytes reported) through `create_private_dir`;
      - `prepare(root, false)` leaves it alone and reads `None`.
    - `prepare_empties_the_scratch_and_reports_what_it_held` keeps its name and passes `HOST_SCRATCH`.
    - The guard `scratch_allowed` is untouched, and no path reaches a document (obs-plan §8, the scratch never printed).
    - Both mutants read red on Linux.

11. **#6–#9 `HarnessSession::drop`** (`crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/session.rs:110-124`).
    - Restate the flag read as the plain `flag_set(Result<String, VarError>) -> bool`, true for exactly `Ok("1")`. Restate
      the drop's two decisions as the plain `drop_steps(cleaned, keep) -> (cleanup, remove)`, with `cleanup = !cleaned` and
      `remove = !keep`. `Drop` calls both.
    - New labelled-table cases (viola-e2e takes no rstest): `flag_set_is_exactly_one` (`Ok("1")`, `Ok("0")`, `Ok("")`,
      `Ok("true")`, and an `Err` value) kills #8 at its new site.
    - `drop_steps_clean_an_uncleaned_session_and_remove_an_unkept_home` (all four input pairs) kills #6 and #9 at their new
      sites.
    - `dropped_session_removes_its_home_unless_kept` builds a `HarnessSession` in the module's own tests: `cleaned: true`,
      and a home two levels inside a fresh tempdir. It drops the session and asserts the parent is gone exactly when
      `keep_home` over the two flags read through `flag_set` is false. That kills #7, the body replaced by `()`.
    - The case reads the flags and never sets them (no `std::env::set_var`).
    - #7's red is read under `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES=0` / `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_FAILED=0`, the environment the audit's mutation run
      gives each test (verification-harness.md, `run --mutants`). Under CI's `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES=1` the case reads green
      by its own expectation.

12. **#10, #11 `read_list` `+` → `*` / `-`** (`crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/status.rs:71`).
    - Restate the capped read and parse as the plain `capped_document(impl Read) -> Option<Value>`, called by `read_list`,
      keeping `take(MAX_FRAME + 1)` and `within = len <= MAX_FRAME`.
    - New labelled-table case `capped_document_takes_a_document_of_exactly_the_bound_and_refuses_one_byte_more`:
      - a JSON object of exactly `MAX_FRAME` bytes reads `Some`, which kills `-`;
      - the same object plus one trailing `\n` (`MAX_FRAME + 1` bytes) reads `None`, which kills `*`.

13. **#13, #14 `get_info` → `Default` / `list_tools` → `Ok(Default)`** (`crates/viola-mcp/src/tools.rs:195`, `:200`).
    - New case `served_initialize_advertises_tools_and_tools_list_carries_the_five` in `tools.rs`'s tests.
    - Serve a `Server` over a `tokio::io::duplex` pair on a current-thread runtime built in the test (rmcp `server` brings
      `transport-async-rw`; no new tokio feature). Write raw JSON-RPC lines:
      - an `initialize` request, whose response must carry `capabilities.tools` and `serverInfo.name == "viola"`;
      - `notifications/initialized`;
      - `tools/list`, whose result must carry 5 tools, `ttlMs` 0 and `cacheScope` `private`.
    - The oracles are literals.

14. **#12 `serve` → `Ok(())`** (`crates/viola-mcp/src/lib.rs:61`).
    - New case `serve_on_a_closed_stdin_is_the_initialize_error`. It re-runs the test binary
      (`std::env::current_exe()`, `--exact <module>::tests::serve_child_entry`) with stdin null and a test-module env
      marker on the child alone. This is the `viola-pty` `sideload_child_entry` / `PTY_SIDELOAD_TEST_CASE` precedent:
      `Command::env`, never `set_var`.
    - The child entry returns at once without the marker. With it, the child calls `serve(...)` and exits with a code that
      names the result.
    - The parent asserts the code for `Err(ServeError::Initialize)`.

title: Item (7) — the recorded live `tools/list` exchange (the founder's one start, inputs#I2)

data.head: ### Item (7) — the recorded live `tools/list` exchange (the founder's one start, inputs#I2)

body:
15. **The tap.** Add the new `[[bin]]` `viola-mcp-tap`, `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-mcp-tap.rs`, test-only and in
    `viola-e2e` alone.
    - Its record form: `viola-mcp-tap record <capture file> <viola exe> <args…>`. It spawns `<viola exe> <args…>` directly
      (no shell, no PATH lookup) and copies stdin to the child and the child's stdout back, line for line, each line
      bounded by `take(MAX_FRAME)`. It appends each line, tagged with its direction, to the capture file, created 0600
      through `OpenOptionsExt::mode`. It exits with the child.
    - Its fixture form: `viola-mcp-tap fixture <capture file> <out file>`. It builds the class document, runs
      `viola_agent_claude::ledger::scrub` (home → `~`, user word → `<user>`) and the same closed-code refusal `--record`
      applies (`home-path` · `absolute-path` · `username` · `email`, naming the file and the code, never the content), and
      writes the document only when clean.
    - The class document holds three things: the client's `initialize` request, its `notifications/initialized`, and its
      `tools/list` request, verbatim and in order; the server's two results; and a `v`.
    - `viola-e2e` gains a `viola-agent-claude` edge for the scrub (a test-only crate's edge).

16. **The class.** Add `schemas/claude-mcp-fixture.v1.json`.
    - `tests/contract_fixture_hygiene.rs` walks `fixtures/claude/*/Mcp.*.json` against it, at run time and red on an empty
      walk, with planted cases: a home path, a user word, an email-shaped token, and a schema violation.
    - Read `tests/contract_fake_agent_drift.rs` and `tests/contract_ledger_probes.rs` against a set that now holds an `Mcp.`
      file, and keep both passing. An edit to the drift contract is listed. `contract_ledger_probes` is read only.
    - Before the recording is committed, read its keys for identity-bearing values the scrub does not rewrite
      (`clientInfo`, a host or account word; testing.md 2026-10-14).

17. **The replay case.** Add `crates/viola-e2e/tests/mcp_recorded_exchange.rs`; its `mcp_` prefix puts it in the E2E layer.
    - Case `mcp_recorded_exchange_replays_the_client_frames_and_keeps_the_accepted_result_shape`. For every walked `Mcp.`
      fixture it starts a `viola mcp` child the test owns, by the `mcp_tools.rs` form: a `harness_session`, unstamped,
      `VIOLA_*` removed, stdin and stdout piped. It writes the recorded client frames verbatim, reads the two responses
      through `take(MAX_FRAME)`, closes stdin and waits for the exit.
    - Viola's `tools/list` result must hold every key path of the recorded result with the same JSON type, and the same
      tool names in the same order.
    - Its labelled table plants two negatives: viola's own result with `ttlMs` removed, and with `cacheScope` removed. The
      comparator must report each as missing, so the check cannot pass vacuously.
    - If its wall needs `mcp_tools`'s class, `binary(mcp_recorded_exchange)` joins that kill line in `.config/nextest.toml`.

18. **The live round (one start; inputs#I2). Nothing live runs before steps 15–17 are green against a planted capture.**
    - **Setup.**
      - Read `hyprctl locked` first (the standing rule), though the round types no desktop key.
      - The rig: `live-ledger.py` copied byte for byte from
        `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers/evidence/` (`cmp` exit 0). The start is ledgered before it
        runs (`start` n 1, cap 1, authority `inputs#I2`).
      - A fresh, unstamped home `target/e2e-home/viola-live-tap-<UTC stamp>/vhome`, and a project dir outside the work
        tree (the 2026-10-18-plugin-precedence-live-readings rig).
      - `~/.local/share/mise/installs/claude/2.1.302` first on `PATH`, and `claude --version` read by path:
        `2.1.302 (Claude Code)` (verification-harness.md 2026-10-10).
      - The rig's environment: the 2026-10-17 declared-names set, with no `CLAUDE*` and no `VIOLA*` name.
      - The build: `target/debug/viola` and `target/debug/viola-mcp-tap` of this chunk's tree.
      - An `--mcp-config` file in the rig's private dir (0600) naming one server, `viola`, with `command` set to the tap's
        absolute path and `args` set to `record <capture> <abs viola> --home <vhome> mcp`.
    - **The one start.** `claude -p --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config <that file> '<a fixed synthetic prompt: reply with the
      single word ok>'`, from the rig dir, a direct spawn. The prompt's sha256 prefix is recorded, never its text in a
      committed file.
    - **After.**
      - Read the capture's direction-tagged line count and its methods (`initialize`, `notifications/initialized`,
        `tools/list`).
      - Run the tap's fixture form to `fixtures/claude/2.1.302/Mcp.tools-list-1.json`.
      - Run step 16's hygiene and step 17's replay over it.
      - Write `evidence/live-tap.md`: the times, the codes and counts, the prompt hash, the ledger rows and the build's
        sha256 prefixes. No prompt text, assistant text, session id or path content goes in it.
    - **If the start does not yield a recording** (no `tools/list` in the capture, a scrub refusal, a tap fault): stop, and
      record exactly what was read. A second start needs the founder's new word (inputs#I2: the cap is 1).

19. **Close the run.** Run the gate block below. Write `evidence/survivors.ndjson`, `evidence/sizes-*.md`,
    `evidence/serde.md` and `evidence/live-tap.md`. Clean the scratch clones made under the session scratchpad.
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger/tests.rs` — `ledger.rs`'s test module, moved whole, its relied-count assert one `cfg!(unix)` expression
- `src/cmd/verify/typed/` — the children of `typed.rs` by concern, each under 800 code lines with its own tests
- `src/human/board/` — the children of `board.rs` by concern, each under 800 code lines with its own tests
- `crates/viola-e2e/tests/mcp_recorded_exchange.rs` — the replay case over a `viola mcp` child
- `schemas/claude-mcp-fixture.v1.json` — the `Mcp.` class schema
- `fixtures/claude/2.1.302/Mcp.tools-list-1.json` — the recorded exchange
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-mcp-tap.rs` — the recording tap and its fixture form
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs` — `relied()` reads `relied_on(WRAPPED_HERE)`, `relied_here` goes, and `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;`
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/statusline.rs` — the `probe_document` document case
- `crates/viola-state/src/liveness.rs` — the live / stale `live_endpoint` case
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run/mutants/scratch.rs` — `prepare(root, host)` and its every-OS case
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run/mutants.rs` — `mutate()` passes `HOST_SCRATCH` (`prepare` @ `mutants.rs:223`, its only caller)
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/session.rs` — `flag_set`, `drop_steps` and the three cases
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/status.rs` — `capped_document` and its case (`read_list` @ `status.rs:87,213`)
- `crates/viola-mcp/src/lib.rs` — the `serve` re-exec case and its child entry
- `crates/viola-mcp/src/tools.rs` — the served-duplex case
- `crates/viola-mcp/Cargo.toml` — the `serde` edge measured and dropped, or kept with its reading
- `Cargo.lock` — follows the manifests
- `src/cmd/verify/typed.rs` — the module root and its re-exports
- `src/human/board.rs` — the module root and its re-exports
- `crates/viola-e2e/Cargo.toml` — the `viola-mcp-tap` `[[bin]]` and the `viola-agent-claude` edge
- `tests/contract_fixture_hygiene.rs` — the `Mcp.` class walk and its planted cases
- `tests/contract_fake_agent_drift.rs` — read against a set holding an `Mcp.` file and kept passing
- `.config/nextest.toml` — `binary(mcp_recorded_exchange)` beside `mcp_tools`, only if its wall needs it
The block runs in this order:
1. the `/tmp` reading;
3. the unit tier;
4. the new cases by name;
5. the size and census reads;
6. the changed root binaries;
7. the E2E binaries;
8. the deny and machete reads;
9. the preservation guard;
10. the harness smoke, G2 / G4 and `pre-push`;
11. the operator trio last.

**No live leg entry.** The one live start is step 18, attended and ledgered, and it is never re-run by a reader. Its
record is `evidence/live-tap.md`. The replay entry reads the fixture the start produced, so before step 18 that entry is
red by construction (no `Mcp.` file to walk).
**Evidence no entry produces:**
- the hand-applied mutant readings (steps 7–14), which go to `evidence/survivors.ndjson`;
- the before and after listings and counts (steps 2, 5), which go to `evidence/sizes-*.md`;
- the `serde` check (step 6), which goes to `evidence/serde.md`;
- the live round (step 18), which goes to `evidence/live-tap.md`.
No mutation entry (testing.md 2026-10-04; inputs#I1, item 1).

- (tests) All 16 survivors of `.andromeda/runs/2026-10-19T21-08-30-code-audit/proposals.md` §Informational end killed or
  restated in `evidence/survivors.ndjson`, one line each. A `killed` line names a case in the package that owns the mutated
  file, red under the hand-applied mutant by its own panic line and green reverted. A `restated` line names the gone site and
  the case that kills the decision it wrapped. None ends "equivalent" or "recorded", and none rests on a `cargo mutants` run
  (per test-plan §3 `run` step 4 "Test scope"; test-plan.md:1095; inputs#I1 item 1). The nine new cases pass: the
  `cargo nextest run --workspace --features fake-agent -E` entry naming them reads `9 tests run: 9 passed`.

- (arch) Each `viola-mcp` and `viola-state` kill sits in its own crate's tests. No manifest gains an edge to `viola-e2e`,
  and the sync crates' tokio ban holds: `cargo deny check` exits 0 (per architecture §Infrastructure Patterns → Crate
  dependency direction).

- (tests) The moves keep every test name. Each touched package's listing after the moves equals its listing before,
  except for the module segment a moved case gains and the nine added cases (`evidence/sizes-before.md` against
  `evidence/sizes-after.md`; per test-plan §4).

- (arch) After the splits, `bash scripts/orphans-check.sh --probe && bash scripts/orphans-check.sh` exits 0, every caller
  compiles against its unchanged path, and `binary(contract_windows_mutation_scope)` passes inside the E2E entry (per
  architecture §Infrastructure Patterns → Project directory structure / CI/CD approach).

- (tests) The size reads hold. The `tokei --files -o json …` entry reads `last line 0`: no file of the two splits stands
  over 800 code lines. The `grep -c -E '^mod tests \{' crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs` entry reads `last line 0`
  (per the code audit's M1/M2; test-plan §10).

- (design / layouts / a11y) The board and verify output is byte-identical after the moves:
  `binary(cli_list)`, `binary(cli_verify)`, `binary(cli_output_plain)` and `binary(cli_plugin_install)` pass in the
  integration entry, and `binary(cross_list_rows)` in the E2E entry, with no literal edited. Every named board unit (`bay_line_*`, `board_row_*`,
  `escape_row_shows_every_control_character_as_hex_text`, `board_row_cli_cell`,
  `instance_and_home_state_pairs_are_the_fixed_texts`) exists under its own name (per design-system §Surface: cli §Tokens;
  layout-templates §Surface: cli; a11y-plan §4).

- (obs) G1 exits 1 with no output, and `bash scripts/lint-probes.sh` exits 0 over the moved files. The refuse census reads
  `last line 14`. The verify spawn-pair `obs_event!` sites are equal in number before and after, as `evidence/sizes-after.md`
  records (per obs-plan §9 Gate commands G1; §6 Log Coverage).

- (security) `cargo machete crates/viola-mcp` exits 0 with no `ignored` entry in any manifest. If step 6's check is red, this
  criterion is recorded unmet, with `evidence/serde.md` (per security-plan §Dependency Security).

- (security) `bash scripts/rmcp-features.sh` exits 0. `viola-e2e`'s rmcp stays `client` without `transport-child-process`
  (per security-plan §API Security).

- (tests / security) `fixtures/claude/2.1.302/Mcp.tools-list-1.json` exists, made by the one live start of step 18 and no
  other (inputs#I2), with its ledger row in `evidence/live-tap.md`. It passes `binary(contract_fixture_hygiene)`, whose
  planted home-path, user, email and schema cases each read red. It holds no `CLAUDE*` value, no home prefix, no `/home/`,

  test-plan §7 Fixture hygiene).

  the recorded client frames yields a `tools/list` result holding the recorded result's key paths with their types and the

  'equivalent'"), and the second is owed to no leg, since `ledger.rs` holds no `windows-mutants.yml` line. Both are
  restated instead.

- A machete `ignored` entry for `serde` — rejected as a gate-silencing form (security-plan §Dependency Security; security
  extract). The edge goes, or it stays with its reading.

- A kill for #12–#14 left to `crates/viola-e2e/tests/mcp_tools.rs` — rejected, because the audit's package run never
  executes another package's tests (test-plan §3 `run` step 4).

- `std::env::set_var` in any case — banned (edition 2024; testing.md Determinism). Flags are read, or passed to a plain
  function.

- Moving `ledger.rs`'s tests while keeping the `#[cfg(windows)]` statement — rejected, because the Windows scope contract
  would read `ledger/tests.rs` as Windows-gated product code (`tests/contract_windows_mutation_scope.rs:59-66`).

- A tap behind a shell, a PATH lookup or a listener — banned (security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns). The `--mcp-config`
  `command` is the tap's absolute path, and the tap spawns the absolute `viola` directly.
- A second live start without the founder's new word — rejected (inputs#I2: the cap is 1).

- A replay compared byte for byte with the recording — rejected: every tool-description edit would then need a new live
  start. Key and type shape guards the class the CLI rejects.

- Splitting `ledger/tests.rs` itself into row families — not taken. M1 names one `ledger/tests.rs`, and the audit's
  `file_max` then reads the larger of it and `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs`, below 3732 either way.

- **Order** (inputs#I2): (5), then (4), then (7). The kills for #1–#3 land after the `ledger.rs` move, so their cases go
  in `ledger/tests.rs` and `statusline.rs`'s module.

- **The survivors' coordinates** are as re-read at HEAD 844de976 (scope.md §Item (4)). Before each hand-applied mutant,
  re-Read the site and confirm the edit landed (testing.md 2026-09-25 ext.: the rustfmt hook reflows after every write).

- **The hand-mutant filter** is `test(/(^|::)tests::<name>(::|$)/)`. A red counts only with the case's own panic line
  (verification-harness.md 2026-09-27).

- **#7's reading** needs the audit's environment: run its red with `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES=0 AGENT_RUN_KEEP_FAILED=0` on that
  one command (`Command::env`-style prefix on the nextest call), never exported into the session.

- **The capped-document case** builds a `MAX_FRAME`-byte (16 MiB) object in memory, which must run under the `mutants`
  profile's 10 s kill. Record its wall in `evidence/survivors.ndjson`.

- **The serve re-exec case** waits on the child with a bound below the 10 s kill, through `try_wait` (testing.md
  2026-09-24 ext.).

- **Item (7) staging**: steps 15–17 are built and green against a planted, synthetic capture before step 18 fires. Only
  the replay entry stays red until the recording lands.

body:
- **relied_here** — 1 caller, `LedgerRow::relied()` at `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs:157`. A name grep over the
  tree finds the same two lines and nothing else. Inlining it as `relied_on(WRAPPED_HERE)` touches no other file.

- **prepare** (`scratch::prepare`) — 1 production caller, `mutate()` at `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run/mutants.rs:223`,
  plus 3 calls in its own test (`scratch.rs:163,172,179`). A `host: bool` parameter threads through those two files only.

- **live_endpoint** — 12 production calls across `src/cmd/{send,wait,last,answer,pause}.rs` and `crates/viola-mcp/src/tools.rs`,
  and 1 test call. Its signature does not change: the kill is a new case in `liveness.rs`'s own tests.

- **read_list** — 2 calls, `status()` (`status.rs:87`) and the test `status_derives_down_with_no_session_bin_to_run`
  (`status.rs:213`). A capped-parse helper split out of it changes no caller.

- **probe_document** — 2 calls, `ProbeDir::create` (`src/cmd/verify.rs:320`) and the one test (`statusline.rs:445`).
  Unchanged.

- **serve** (`viola_mcp::serve`) — 1 caller, `src/cmd/mcp.rs:35`. Every other `serve` row is `viola_channel`'s
  `Server::serve`, a different symbol. Unchanged.

- **get_info / list_tools** — 0 rows. These are trait methods rmcp calls at run time, and zero callers is no leaf evidence
  (cookbook §Reading the result). A grep over `crates/viola-mcp/` finds only their definitions.

- **Const-gated decision passed in by the caller** (test-plan.md:1095, `viola_state::fs`'s retry decision at chunk
  2026-10-13-epoch-4-survivors): a site that a const makes unreachable on Linux becomes reachable when the caller passes the
  const, with no behaviour change. This fits `prepare` (`HOST_SCRATCH`) and `relied_here` (`WRAPPED_HERE`).

- **Pure decision split out of an I/O body** (`ctrl_c_ending`, `ended_by`, `probe_until` in `typed.rs` at chunk
  2026-10-13-epoch-4-survivors-ii): the decision becomes a plain function with its own case table. This fits `Drop`'s flag
  read and `read_list`'s capped parse.

- **Module root plus children by concern** (`src/run/send.rs` + `src/run/send/*`, `src/human.rs` + `src/human/*`): the root
  keeps the public items and `pub(crate) use` re-exports them, so every caller keeps its path. Each child keeps its own
  inline `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` at its bottom (test-plan §4).

- **Recorded fixture class with its own schema** (`Agents.recorded-1.json` + `schemas/claude-agents-fixture.v1.json`,
  chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board): scrubbed before the write, refused whole when unclean, hygiene-walked
  with planted cases, and compared by key-and-type shape (`fake_agent_agents_replay_matches_every_recorded_agents_set`).

- **Test names**: `<subject>_<condition>_<expected>`. viola-e2e takes labelled case tables in one `#[test]` (no rstest), and
  viola-state and viola-agent-claude take rstest `#[case]` (test-plan §4; `.claude/rules/testing.md` Naming).

- **No env write in a test**: `std::env::set_var` is banned (edition 2024). A flag read is tested as a pure function of the
  read's result, never by setting the variable (`.claude/rules/testing.md` Determinism).

- **Hand-applied mutant**: each kill is read red with the mutant applied, by its own case's panic line under the
  `test(/(^|::)tests::name(::|$)/)` filter, and green once the mutant is reverted. Where the classifier refuses the in-tree
  edit, the mutant goes on a scratch clone of HEAD (`--project-root {clone}`) (`.claude/rules/testing.md` 2026-09-25 ext.
  2026-10-20; `.claude/rules/verification-harness.md` 2026-09-27).

  (protocol 2026-07-28) dropped every tool; only the one live start could see it".

  2026-10-19-newer-claude-cli-rows: "a subprocess start of the user's CLI whose output reaches the repository is a

  chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board] A recorded exchange committed as a fixture passes the NEVER-log floor

  rmcp's client does not.

   `send_under_the_paste_hint_a_human_key_during_the_gate_wait_wins` by name). `tests/contract_lints.rs` gains one

    other `Wrapper::kill` callers, until one reproduces a refused `viola hook` profile. Each refused one is attributed by
    the counter method of that evidence file. The counts, runs and workers are written with their basis. Before each
    census run, one line tells the operator that it starts and for how long, as the script's own chunk did
    (`viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-a-send-ending-in-a-newline-is-confirmed/evidence/profraw-red-green.md`).
    (c) If the refused profile is a `viola hook` cut off by its terminal's hangup (research's hypothesis): the fake
    agent's `run_hook` (`src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs:631`) spawns each hook in a process group of its own on Unix
    (`std::os::unix::process::CommandExt::process_group(&mut cmd, 0)`, the `hold_inherited_stdout` precedent at
    `:1018`), and the same census reads 0 refused over the same runs.
    (d) If (b) reproduces nothing, or the attribution names another killer: no fix is applied. The reading, the cases
    tried and the counts stand in the evidence as the item's finding, and the WATCH stands open. A fix for another
    killer is a change of the same kind, recorded in `scope-record.md` before it is made.

11. **(9) The keepers read the backing's headroom first.** In `tests/support/home.rs` `prepare_home_base`'s link
    branch (the dev host's tmpfs backing, `:119–137`) and the same branch of `Workspace::ensure_e2e_home`
    (`crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/mod.rs`), after the existing checks, read the target's free bytes with
    `libc::statvfs` (`f_bavail × f_frsize`) behind `#[cfg(unix)]`. Refuse below a compiled floor with a fixed message
    holding the two counts and no path (`e2e-home backing: {free} MiB free, below the {floor} MiB floor`). The decision
    is a plain function of the two numbers, tested on every OS (testing.md 2026-09-24). Root tests take its cases in
    `tests/cli_instance_state.rs` beside the backing cases; viola-e2e takes its own in `harness/mod.rs`'s test module.
    A plain-directory base (every CI runner) reads no headroom and is unchanged. `crates/viola-e2e/Cargo.toml` gains
    `libc.workspace = true` under `[target.'cfg(unix)'.dependencies]`, with `Cargo.lock`'s edge. The floor is one named
    constant per keeper, equal in both. It is set at implement from a fresh `statvfs` reading against the recorded
    EDQUOT reading (about 8 G free by `df`, 24 G used of 32 G,
    `.andromeda/runs/2026-10-19T19-16-36-wrap/relay-3.md`) and the run's footprint (32 test threads × a 101 163 992 B
    pinned `viola`, research §Mechanisms (9)), with that basis written beside the constant and in
    `evidence/headroom.md`. No env var, flag or config key sets it. Remove-the-guard: the comparison neutralised, the
    below-floor unit case reads red, restored green.

12. **(10) The web leftovers in the rule and doc files.**
    - `.claude/rules/frontend.md`: `paths:` drops `crates/viola-ui/assets/**` and keeps `src/cmd/**`. The
      `## Web-spa (deferred to 0.2.0)` section goes, and its one line is already the file's opening sentence.
    - `.claude/rules/a11y.md`: `paths:` names the terminal surfaces its body governs in place of the five web paths.
      These are `src/human.rs`, `src/human/**`, `src/run/wheel.rs`, `tests/cli_output_plain.rs`,
      `tests/cross_list_rows.rs` and `tests/tui_*.rs` (`ls tests/ | grep -E '^(tui_|cli_output|cross_list)'`;
      `ls src/human/`). Its `## The frontend (deferred to 0.2.0)` section keeps only that one deferral sentence.
    - `.claude/rules/api.md`: `paths:` drops `crates/viola-ui/src/**`.
    - `.claude/rules/testing.md`: `paths:` drops `e2e-web/tests/**`.
    - `.claude/docs/services/viola-ui.md` is removed (`git rm`). If the permission layer refuses the removal, it is not
      done another way. The refusal is recorded and the removal is the founder's at the desk (host-linux.md 2026-10-07,
      extended 2026-10-16).
    - No `## Session Additions` text moves.

    The master bodies and `CLAUDE.md`'s `GENERATED:setup:deeper-topics` pointer are the wrap's (`## Implementation
    notes`).

13. **The report's inputs.** `evidence/operator-pass.md` is the operator pass's record. Implement's own record is
    every evidence file above, written before the report.

- `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-20-epoch-5-cleanup/evidence/` — `baseline.md`, `kill-lines.md`, `viola-pty-leak.md`,
  `windows-baselines.md`, `profraw-cause.md`, `headroom.md`, `operator-pass.md`
- `.config/nextest.toml` — the paste-hint override; `verify_window_`'s `mutants` kill at 60 s (steps 3, 4)
- `tests/contract_lints.rs` — the paste-hint override's pin (step 3)
- `tests/contract_fake_agent_drift.rs` — concurrent set walks, assertions unchanged (step 2)
- `tests/contract_ledger_probes.rs` — concurrent stamped-set walk (step 2)
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run/mutants/scratch.rs` — the made plain control (step 6)
- `crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs` — the unconditional guard kill and the per-test child copy (step 7)
- `tests/support/home.rs` — `dialogless_home` derived (step 9); the headroom read (step 11)
- `tests/cli_instance_state.rs` — the headroom decision's cases (step 11)
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/mod.rs` — the headroom read and its cases (step 11)
- `crates/viola-e2e/Cargo.toml` — `libc` under `cfg(unix)` (step 11)
- `Cargo.lock` — the `viola-e2e` → `libc` edge (step 11)
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs` — the hook spawn's process group, only under step 10(c) (step 10)
- `scripts/profraw-census.sh` — the integration-case subject form (step 10)

- `.claude/rules/frontend.md`, `.claude/rules/a11y.md`, `.claude/rules/api.md`, `.claude/rules/testing.md` —
  `paths:` and the stub sections (step 12)
- `.claude/docs/services/viola-ui.md` — removed (step 12)

The block runs in this order: the `/tmp` reading, then the lints (the Windows-target clippy because steps 6 and 7 edit
`cfg(windows)` and Windows-sensitive test code), the unit tier, the changed binaries by name, the root baseline under
`mutants`, the guard, the harness smoke, G2 / G4 and `pre-push`. The operator trio comes last. No live leg: nothing in
the chunk starts a real `claude`.
**Evidence no entry produces:**

- the planted-hang pairs and the remove-the-guard readings (steps 3, 4, 7, 11) are one-off readings over scratch
  clones, written to `evidence/` by implement;
- the item (8) census (step 10) is a dev-host script run whose counts go to `evidence/profraw-cause.md`;
- the Windows readings of step 8 are recorded runs read by id.
No entry reads those files. No mutation entry (test-plan §10: the epoch-boundary audit; testing.md 2026-10-04).

**`pre-push` read red at P5's baseline** on the WATCH's own class: every test passed and the coverage merge refused one
truncated `viola` profile (`.andromeda/runs/2026-10-20T07-58-07-phase/p5-prepush-red.md`). That red is item (8)'s
subject, which this chunk builds. At implement and at the light gate, a `pre-push` red of exactly that shape (every
test passed, the merge refusing a truncated `viola` profile) is read through step 10's finding, never as a pass:
- after a named and fixed cause, it is this chunk's red, its fix owed;
- after a recorded no-reproduction, it stands with the finding as the item's open red.
Any other `pre-push` red is the chunk's red as written.

title: Mechanisms, each the equality the plan needs

data.head: ## Mechanisms, each the equality the plan needs

body:
- **(1) the replay walks:** each case's wall is the sum of one `viola verify` per recorded set; run concurrently it is
  the slowest set's, its assertions unchanged. Verified for the summing half: the walks are sequential loops
  (`## Sweeps`); the concurrent wall is implement's measurement.

- **(1) the paste-hint pair:** each waits the product's gate (`GATE_MAX_WAIT` 8.5 s) by design — the by-design floor
  class `send_window_` already holds (`.config/nextest.toml`, the `send_window_` comment).

- **(2):** the case waits the gate's maximum four times plus Run E by design (42.9–43.7 s on three OSes, `## The CI and
  dispatch readings`); the class's `mutants` kill sits 1.3–2.1 s above it, under the 60 s it has under `ci`.

- **(3a):** under cargo-mutants the tree is copied into the scratch, laid down owner-only; the case's `target/e2e-home`
  is then inside it, so its plain control inherits owner-only and reads `Ok(())`. In CI's checkout it inherits the
  workspace drive's `BUILTIN\Users` write grant and reads `Err(Writable)` (0.019 s green). The equality the fix needs:
  a plain control that reads `Err(Writable)` whatever its parent's DACL. [hypothesis: the copy location is read from
  `mutants.rs:255–262`'s `TMP` / `TEMP`; the reading inside the copy is the next boundary's]

- **(3c):** a `try_wait` mutant that reports the child gone makes the guard skip its kill (`:834–836`); the child is
  the test binary itself (`:901`, `:1295`), which then stays running, and on Windows a running image cannot be
  replaced, so every later mutant's link of that test binary fails — `unviable`. The equality the fix needs: no
  mutant can leave the build's own test binary running. [hypothesis: the lock is read from the log's shape, not from
  a recorded link error — the job log names no error line]

- **(3b):** no local mechanism: CI's windows-2025 leg reads 5.502 s under `ci`, the dispatch's baseline 10 s under
  `mutants`; the difference is not measured, and measuring it is a dispatch.

- **(8):** see scope item (8) — research's hypothesis, a hangup reaching an in-flight hook; the census script reads one
  fixed unit test, not a kill-shaped case.

- **(9):** `statvfs` reads the filesystem (14 134 MiB free now); the per-user quota is unreadable from the session

- **Marker:** 2026-10-25-windows-endpoint-admission · **Version:** viola-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-25T23:41:19Z
- **Base:** HEAD `b6740d59d839f5c094d92af56e0b3ebfc7260466` (the commit the chunk starts from)
- **Forks:** the four P4 forks answered by the founder live (`inputs#I5`, re-asked on the operator's word `inputs#I4`)

Bring security-plan §Authentication & Authorization's "IPC access control (Windows)" clause from "partly landed" to
asserted on the `windows-2025` CI leg, for what chunk 2026-09-27-wrapper-channel left unasserted. The protected DACL's
text read-back, both-ends non-inheritance, the first-pipe-instance property (a second `Server::bind` of a live name is
`BindTaken`) and the `squatted-name` start refusal are already asserted and stay as they are (scope.md, closed at P3).
Two controls get their first witness, each with a control that proves the witness can fire:

- **the DACL's effect:** an open of the bound listener under the anonymous token is denied, while the same anonymous
  open of a test-owned pipe carrying the default descriptor succeeds (fork (c), `inputs#I5`), which amends test-plan §1's
  untestable zone at the wrap.

No product file changes: viola's listener already takes interprocess 2.4.4's defaults whole (research.md, Patterns).
The listener tests are Windows-only and are verified only on CI's `test (windows-2025)` leg (test-plan §11: a Linux run
proves no Windows branch).

The folded CARRY (the budget send case_4) is closed at its root cause (fork 3, `inputs#I5`). tracing-core 0.1.36 caches
a callsite's interest as `never` when the callsite is first registered, while at most one dispatcher is registered, on
a thread with no subscriber; the one scoped capture then loses its own thread's line (research.md, P4 additions). The
fix is one shared root-bin test helper that keeps a second, always-interested dispatcher registered for the process,
routed through every scoped capture of the root bin, and a witness case that reproduces the loss without it. The three
other plain `cargo test --bin viola` reds are recorded with their known cause and get no owner: plain `cargo test` is not
a supported runner, nextest is the gate (fork 4, `inputs#I5`).

1. **The `/tmp` reading.** Fire the `df -h /tmp` entry before any stamped-home gate (the standing rule, `inputs#I1`
   item 5) and keep its line in `evidence/`.

2. **The capture witness, first, red.** In `src/main.rs`'s `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`, add
   `scoped_capture_sees_a_line_whose_callsite_another_thread_registered_first`. Inside one scoped capture on the test
   thread, it spawns a thread that emits one line at a fixed `obs_event!` site (a private helper fn holding the single
   call site) and joins it. Then it emits the same site on the test thread, and asserts the capture holds exactly that
   one line. The emitting thread installs no subscriber, and the case installs no global default. Write it first
   against a bare `tracing::subscriber::with_default`. Under nextest's process-per-test it must read RED: the capture is
   then the only registered dispatcher, so the off-thread first hit caches `never`. Record that red reading in
   `evidence/capture-witness.md` (the remove-the-guard run, testing.md 2026-09-25) before step 3.

3. **The helper.** In `src/main.rs`'s `#[cfg(test)] pub(crate) mod test_support`, add
   `pub(crate) fn with_scoped_default<S, R>(subscriber: S, f: impl FnOnce() -> R) -> R`. It first registers, once per
   process, a pinned always-interested dispatcher: a `Dispatch` over `tracing_subscriber::registry()` with no layer and
   no filter, held for the process in a `std::sync::OnceLock<tracing::Dispatch>`, and never set as the global default.
   Then it returns `tracing::subscriber::with_default(subscriber, f)`. Its doc comment states the mechanism in one
   sentence and cites testing.md 2026-09-27. Move the witness of step 2 onto the helper and record it GREEN in the same
   evidence file.

4. **Every scoped capture of the root bin through the helper.** Replace each `tracing::subscriber::with_default(` call
   with `crate::test_support::with_scoped_default(`, with no other change to the capture. There are 9 sites
   (`grep -rn 'subscriber::with_default' src` at `b6740d59`): `src/cmd/hook/statusline.rs:375`,
   `src/cmd/run.rs:772`, `src/cmd/run.rs:909`, `src/run/gate.rs:465`, `src/run/budget.rs:859`,
   `src/run/send/test_support.rs:421` (`capture_lines`, case_4's capture), `src/run/dialog.rs:902`,
   `src/run/dialog.rs:1270` and `src/obs.rs:624`. Leave `src/run/gate.rs:429`'s `set_global_default` as it is.
   Afterwards the census entry reads exactly 1 site in `src/`, the helper's own.

5. **The pipe-type read-back's dependency.** In the root `Cargo.toml`, add a `[target.'cfg(windows)'.dev-dependencies]`
   table holding `windows-sys = { workspace = true, features = ["Wdk_Storage_FileSystem"] }`. Leave the workspace pin
   and every normal dependency table untouched. Under `resolver = "3"` a dev-dependency's feature reaches no release
   build.

6. **(a) Remote clients rejected — `tests/security_negatives_channel.rs`.**
   - Add `security_negative_viola_listener_rejects_remote_clients`. It binds `viola_channel::Server::bind` on
     `\\.\pipe\viola-test-chan-<pid>-remote`, opens it with `CreateFileW` (`FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES`), reads
     `NtQueryInformationFile(…, FilePipeLocalInformation)`, and asserts `NamedPipeType & FILE_PIPE_REJECT_REMOTE_CLIENTS != 0`.
   - Add two controls on test-owned `CreateNamedPipeW` pipes:
     - `security_negative_control_accept_remote_pipe_reads_the_bit_clear`: `PIPE_ACCEPT_REMOTE_CLIENTS` reads the bit clear.
     - `security_negative_control_reject_remote_pipe_reads_the_bit_set`: `PIPE_REJECT_REMOTE_CLIENTS` reads the bit set.
   - Each name is unique per test and the expected bit is a literal, never a product constant (test-plan §11).

7. **(c) The DACL's effect — the same file.**
   - Add `security_negative_viola_listener_denies_an_anonymous_open`. On a spawned thread of its own, it binds the
     listener on `\\.\pipe\viola-test-chan-<pid>-anon`, calls `ImpersonateAnonymousToken(GetCurrentThread())`, then
     `CreateFileW(GENERIC_READ)` on the pipe. It asserts the open fails with `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` (the literal 5), then
     `RevertToSelf`.
   - Add the control `security_negative_control_default_pipe_admits_an_anonymous_read`: the same anonymous open
     succeeds on a test-owned `CreateNamedPipeW` pipe whose security attributes are null, so it carries the default
     descriptor, which «grant[s] read access to … the anonymous account» (Microsoft Learn `CreateNamedPipeA`, research.md).
   - The impersonation never leaves its thread, and the thread reverts before it ends.

8. **The case_4 reading under both runners.** Fire the plain `cargo test --bin viola` entry. It must show case_4 `ok` and
   the step-2 witness `ok`. The run's own result line still reads `FAILED` on the three known-cause reds of fork 4,
   which are recorded and not fixed. Copy the run's failing-test list into `evidence/plain-run.md`.

9. **The remaining gates**, in the block's order. On Windows the first-instance, DACL text and non-inheritance cases
   stand unchanged and need no edit (scope.md). Report the two Windows witnesses and their controls from the
   `test (windows-2025)` JUnit.
- none
- `tests/security_negatives_channel.rs` — five new `#[cfg(windows)]` cases (steps 6, 7)
- `Cargo.toml` — the root Windows dev-dependency feature (step 5)
- `src/main.rs` — `test_support::with_scoped_default` and the witness case (steps 2, 3)
- `src/run/send/test_support.rs` — `capture_lines` through the helper (step 4)
- `src/run/dialog.rs` — two captures through the helper (step 4)
- `src/run/budget.rs` — one capture through the helper (step 4)
- `src/run/gate.rs` — one capture through the helper; the global install untouched (step 4)
- `src/obs.rs` — one capture through the helper (step 4)
- `src/cmd/run.rs` — two captures through the helper (step 4)
- `src/cmd/hook/statusline.rs` — one capture through the helper (step 4)
The block runs in this order:
1. the `/tmp` reading;

2. the lints. The Windows-target clippy is in because the chunk adds `cfg(windows)` test code the dev host does not
   build;
3. the unit tier, then the capture witness by name, then the census;
4. the plain `cargo test` reading;
5. the deny families and the tokio-free tree;
6. the preservation guard;
7. the harness smoke, G2 and G4, then `pre-push`;
8. the operator entries last.

**No live leg.** The chunk drives no external process, and its Windows witnesses run inside CI's `test (windows-2025)`
instrumented nextest run. **No mutation entry**: mutation runs at the epoch boundary only (test-plan §10, `(sampler)`
test-strategy.md:28).
**Two reds are expected and are not this chunk's:**

- **CI's `supply-chain` job** is red on RUSTSEC-2026-0386 (`tokio 1.53.1`). It is owned by the new route entry

body:
- (security) On `test (windows-2025)` the bound viola listener's pipe type reads `FILE_PIPE_REJECT_REMOTE_CLIENTS` set
  (`security_negative_viola_listener_rejects_remote_clients`). Its two controls read the bit clear on an
  accept-remote pipe and set on a reject-remote pipe. If the controls cannot tell the two apart on that runner, the
  claim is owed to "Windows-only live measurements" and the report says so (per security-plan §Authentication &
  Authorization, IPC access control (Windows); `inputs#I5` fork (a)).

- (security) On `test (windows-2025)` an anonymous-token open of the bound viola listener fails with
  `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` (`security_negative_viola_listener_denies_an_anonymous_open`), while the same anonymous open of a
  default-descriptor pipe succeeds (`security_negative_control_default_pipe_admits_an_anonymous_read`). If the control
  fails on that runner, the DACL's effect is owed to "Windows-only live measurements" (per security-plan
  §Authentication & Authorization; `inputs#I5` fork (c)).

- (security) The DACL text read-back, both-ends non-inheritance, the first-instance `BindTaken` cases and the
  `squatted-name` start refusal stay green and unedited on all three legs (per security-plan §Authentication &
  Authorization; scope.md premise closure).

- (tests) The capture witness `scoped_capture_sees_a_line_whose_callsite_another_thread_registered_first` reads red on
  a bare `with_default` and green on `with_scoped_default`, both readings in `evidence/capture-witness.md`
  (testing.md 2026-09-25; per test-plan §10 Zero-flakiness budget: the flake fixed at its root cause).

- (tests) `cargo nextest run --workspace --features fake-agent -E 'test(/(^|::)tests::scoped_capture_sees_a_line_whose_callsite_another_thread_registered_first$/)'`
  reads `1 test run: 1 passed` (per test-plan §4 Unit Test Strategy).

- (tests) Under `cargo test --bin viola`, case_4 and the witness each read `ok`. The three other reds of that runner are
  recorded in `evidence/plain-run.md` with their known cause and no owner (`inputs#I5` fork 4; per test-plan §4
  Framework: nextest is the executor).

- (tests) `grep -rn 'subscriber::with_default' src | wc -l` reads `1`: every scoped capture of the root bin goes
  through the helper (per test-plan §11: no mutable state shared across parallel tests is relied on to deliver a line).

- (tests) `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --unit` reads `"ok":true`, and `pre-push` reads `"ok":true` at `linux-tests`
  (per test-plan §9).

- (arch) `cargo deny check bans licenses sources` and `bash scripts/channel-tokio-free.sh` read green. The added
  `Wdk_Storage_FileSystem` feature sits on a root Windows dev-dependency only, and no ignore is added (per architecture
  §Infrastructure Patterns → Crate dependency direction; per security-plan §Dependency Security).

- (obs) The witness's line and every capture's lines go through `obs_event!`. G2 reads zero panics and G4 reads every
  line conformant over the booted and kept homes (per obs-plan §9 CI Integration).

- (design · layouts · a11y) No human output line, refusal text or SGR byte changes: no product file is edited (per
  design-system §Surface: cli; layout-templates §Output structure — `viola run`; a11y-plan §8).

- (CI) `ci.py conclusion --sha HEAD --name 'test (windows-2025)'` reads `verdict: green` on the pushed chunk, its run id
  named in the report. The full row is recorded, its only red `supply-chain` (per test-plan §9 Matrix builds).

- Research files inspected: `crates/viola-channel/src/server.rs`, `crates/viola-channel/src/server/win.rs`,
  `crates/viola-channel/src/test_support.rs`, `crates/viola-channel/src/lib.rs`, `crates/viola-channel/Cargo.toml`,
  `Cargo.toml`, `tests/security_negatives_channel.rs`, `tests/channel_sqos_open.rs`, `tests/path1_run_start.rs`,
  `tests/cli_instance_state.rs`, `src/run/send/budget.rs`, `src/run/send/test_support.rs`, `src/run/gate.rs`,
  `src/main.rs`, interprocess 2.4.4's listener options, tracing-core 0.1.36's callsite and dispatcher.

- External inputs: `inputs#I1` (directive), `inputs#I2` (the supply-chain red's owner), `inputs#I3` (invocation),
  `inputs#I4` (the re-ask), `inputs#I5` (the founder's four answers).

- A `\\localhost\pipe\…` open as the remote-client witness — test-plan §11 «NEVER use real network calls in tests»
  (`.andromeda/test-plan.md:942`); the founder chose the read-back (`inputs#I5`).

- A second `set_global_default` as the capture fix — the binary's one global install is `src/run/gate.rs:429` («the one
  global-subscriber test of its process»), and a second would panic its `expect`.
- Closing case_4 on three green plain runs — the founder chose the root cause (`inputs#I5`).

- Fixing the three plain-run reds, or minting an owner for them — the founder ruled plain `cargo test` an unsupported
  runner (`inputs#I5`).

- Any product edit to `crates/viola-channel` or `src/cmd/run.rs` — the listener already holds every property
  (research.md); a product change would widen the chunk with nothing to fix.
- Single-threading, a retry, `#[ignore]` or a sleep for the capture — test-plan §11, §10.

- Changing `viola-state`'s and `viola-channel`'s own scoped captures (`crates/viola-state/src/lib.rs:87`,
  `crates/viola-channel/src/test_support.rs:184`, `crates/viola-channel/src/lib.rs:199`) — other test binaries, never
  observed red; the CARRY names the root bin. Recorded below as the same class.

- The witness's determinism holds only in its own process (nextest). Under plain `cargo test`, other tests' dispatchers
  make the unfixed reading racy, so its red reading is taken under nextest (step 2).

- The pinned dispatcher has no layer and no filter, so it receives the events of no thread (events go to the current
  thread's default) and contributes `Interest::always()` to every rebuild. It never touches the global default, so
  `src/run/gate.rs:429` keeps its install.

- The anonymous impersonation is thread-scoped. The case runs it on a spawned thread that reverts before returning, so
  no other test's thread is affected.

- Curation candidate (wrap's, not a master amendment): `.claude/rules/testing.md` 2026-09-27 — the same fact also
  loses an ON-thread line whose callsite another, subscriber-less thread registered first.

- Ledger: `matrix#v1-44` notes — its requirement spans every OS, client-side server verification and the macOS gap,
  owned by "Server verification before any frame", "Unix endpoint and home hardening" and "Linux and macOS parity", so
  this chunk claims it on no part (P5 step 4 writes the note).
- Same class, not changed here: the three crate-level scoped captures named under Constraints.

title: P4 additions (read after the founder's answers, `inputs#I5`)

data.head: ## P4 additions (read after the founder's answers, `inputs#I5`)

body:
- **The case_4 mechanism, re-derived at the pinned versions** (tracing 0.1.44, tracing-core 0.1.36 per `Cargo.lock`):
  `NoSubscriber::register_callsite` returns `Interest::never()` (`tracing-core-0.1.36/src/subscriber.rs:676`); with no
  global default and no scoped dispatcher on a thread, `get_default` hands that thread `NONE`
  (`dispatcher.rs:383-386, 446-449`); while at most one dispatcher is registered (`has_just_one`, set by
  `register_dispatch` as `len <= 1`, `callsite.rs:551-557`) a callsite's first registration reads only the registering
  thread's own default (`Rebuilder::JustOne` → `get_default`, `callsite.rs:544-547, 562-567`), so a callsite first hit
  on a subscriber-less thread caches `INTEREST_NEVER` (`callsite.rs:308-341`); the event macro then skips it on every
  thread (`tracing-0.1.44/src/macros.rs:36`), the one scoped capture's own thread included, until the next
  `register_dispatch` rebuilds the cache (`callsite.rs:484-488`). The equality the fix needs: with a second
  always-interested dispatcher kept registered for the process, `has_just_one` is false whenever a scoped capture is
  live, so a first registration on any thread takes the `Read` path over every live dispatcher and the capture's own
  `registry().with(..)` (no filter: `Interest::always()`) makes the callsite's interest non-never.

- **The same fact is already recorded twice in the repo**, each time for a line emitted OFF the test thread:
  `crates/viola-channel/src/lib.rs:186-188` (`capture_global`) and `.claude/rules/testing.md:64` (2026-09-27). Case_4's
  line is on the test thread; its loss is the callsite's first registration on another, subscriber-less thread.

- **The root bin's scoped captures** (`grep -rn 'subscriber::with_default' src`, 9 sites in 7 files):
  `src/cmd/hook/statusline.rs:375` · `src/cmd/run.rs:772` · `src/cmd/run.rs:909` · `src/run/gate.rs:465` ·
  `src/run/budget.rs:859` · `src/run/send/test_support.rs:421` · `src/run/dialog.rs:902` · `src/run/dialog.rs:1270` ·
  `src/obs.rs:624`. The one global install of the binary is `src/run/gate.rs:429` («the one global-subscriber test of its
  process»), so the fix cannot be a second global default.

- **The pipe-type read-back** is in windows-sys 0.61.2 under `Wdk_Storage_FileSystem`: `NtQueryInformationFile`
  (`src/Windows/Wdk/Storage/FileSystem/mod.rs:671`, `windows_link` to ntdll), `FILE_PIPE_LOCAL_INFORMATION` (2341, its
  `NamedPipeType`), `FilePipeLocalInformation` = 24 (3210), `FILE_PIPE_REJECT_REMOTE_CLIENTS` = 2 (2372); `windows-link`
  is already in `Cargo.lock` (`grep -c '^name = "windows-link"'`: 1). `ImpersonateAnonymousToken` is in `Win32_Security`
  (`src/Windows/Win32/Security/mod.rs:103`), already in the workspace pin. Whether NPFS reports the reject bit through
  `NamedPipeType` is unmeasured: the controls decide it on CI.

- **`pre-push` runs no `cargo deny`** (`crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/pre_push.rs:3`: `tools → linux-tests`), so the
  advisory red reaches only `cargo deny check`'s advisories family and CI's `supply-chain` job.

- **The harness `run`'s first step runs through nextest** (`crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run.rs:238-271`:
  `nextest-unit`, `nextest-integration`, `nextest-e2e`), so test-plan's «the workspace unit and integration tests
  (`cargo test`)» (`.andromeda/test-plan-detail/test-scope-summary.md:80`) names libtest executed by nextest, as §4 states.
- none — the four P4 forks were answered by the founder live (`inputs#I5`)

**Working entry (viola-0.1.0/working-route.md, Epoch 6 — Security hardening):** Windows endpoint admission — pipe
access for the owning user and SYSTEM only, remote pipe clients rejected, squatted name blocks start (per
security-plan §Authentication).

**Invocation:** the operator's (`inputs#I3`), with the overseer's directive for this phase (`inputs#I1`): forced
sample at P2, every transcript and the run dir kept, a hard cascade failure stops the phase.

another process already holds refuses `viola run` at start, and holds non-inheritable handles. The entry is scoped to

- **Marker:** 2026-10-26-explicit-session-links · **Version:** viola-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-26T14:45Z

- **The founder's word:** «Сначала instance check (Рекомендую)» — his own answer to this chunk's P4 fork, live by
  dialog, relayed verbatim (`inputs#I3`): the wrapper serves `link` / `unlink`, and `viola link` / `viola unlink`
  run the instance check before any log or snapshot read, as `viola revive` does, then the liveness pre-check and the
  server check. This is the boundary widening's ratification for the two verbs; no dated gap is taken.

The wrapper serves the two channel methods `link` and `unlink` over its existing `LinkSet`, and the two verbs
`viola link <driver> <driven>` and `viola unlink <driver> <driven>` reach the driven instance's wrapper with them
(architecture §Established Decisions [Links], §Standard Contracts Channel methods). `link` records the pair once and
answers `{since, already_linked}`; `unlink` removes it, appending the first product `unlink` line, and answers the
empty object; an `unlink` of an absent pair appends nothing (the operator's answers,
`chunks/2026-10-10-session-links/inputs/I2-relay-2.md.txt`).

The verbs take the form the founder named (`inputs#I3`): `viola_state::strict::check_instance` on the home and the
driven instance's tree before any log opens and before any snapshot value is read (security-plan §Authentication &
Authorization, `~/.viola/` access control; the order of `src/cmd/revive.rs:116-121`), then the liveness-only
pre-check and the server check through `cmd::client::connect` like every other CLI frame verb (security-plan
§Authentication & Authorization, IPC client-side server verification). A refused check exits 21 with no log and no
line; a server that is not the recorded wrapper gets no frame and exits 21. `viola --help` gains its
`handoff:  link, unlink` row, and the three result lines print in design-system §Surface: cli pattern 4's forms.

No ledger row, no `viola verify` child, no re-stamp, no live `claude` start and no MCP tool: a link is recorded from
viola's own parameters, and `link` / `unlink` stay CLI-only (architecture [MCP]).

1. **The two method handlers** (`src/run/links.rs`). The link set gains `link(params)` and `unlink(params)`, each
   returning the channel result or a `ProtocolError`. Each reads `params.driver` and `params.driven` as strings
   through `ViolaName::try_new`; a missing, non-string or invalid name is `ProtocolError::InvalidParams` (`-32602`,
   `data: null`). Then a `driven` that is not the set's own `name` is `-32602`, then a `driver` equal to `driven`
   is `-32602`. Neither method reads `from`: a `from` in the params, of any shape, changes nothing. `link` calls
   `record(driver)` and answers `{"ok":{"since":<since>,"already_linked":<bool>}}`; `unlink` calls
   `remove(driver)` and answers `{"ok":{}}` whether or not a pair was removed. A `record` / `remove` error is
   `ProtocolError::Internal` (`-32603`). Each answers only after the line and the snapshot write have been made
   (`change`, `src/run/links.rs:98-104`, unchanged). `remove` loses `#[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]`
   and its "not served yet" doc sentence; the module doc names the two methods. Neither method opens a span or
   writes a process-log line (obs-plan §4 Edge flows E3). Inline cases (keeps tests S2), named `links_set_method_*`:
   link twice (one line, the same `since`, `already_linked` false then true); unlink then link (a later `since`);
   unlink of an absent pair (no line, `{}`); each bad-name class (`../x`, `BUILDER`, `a/b`, `""`, 33 characters, a
   number, absent) on each param, a foreign `driven`, `driver` equal to `driven` (each `-32602`, no line, the
   snapshot's `links` unchanged); a `from` in the params, valid or not, changes nothing; a failing append is
   `-32603` with the set unchanged.

2. **The wrapper routes them** (`src/cmd/run.rs`). `Methods` (71-79) gains the `LinkSet`; `start` hands it the
   restored set (after `links.restore()`, 287, as it already hands it to `send` and `dialogs`); `dispatch_call`
   (134-145) routes `"link"` and `"unlink"` to it; the `Methods` doc comment (68-70) names the nine served methods.
   The unit helper `methods()` (778-810) builds a `LinkSet` over its instance dir. The case
   `methods_answer_method_not_found_for_every_other_method` (821-830) keeps `"anything"` alone and calls
   `dispatch_call`; a new case `methods_route_link_and_unlink_to_the_link_set` sends a valid `link` then `unlink`
   through `dispatch_call` and reads one `link` and one `unlink` line.

3. **The three result lines** (`src/human/verbs.rs`, re-exported from `src/human.rs`). One writer each, one
   `write_all` to the given `Write`, plain in every mode (design-system §Surface: cli pattern 4; keeps design S1–S3):
   - `link    <driver> -> <driven>  since <time>` (the word padded to `unlink`'s width, two-space gutters);
   - `link    <driver> -> <driven>  already linked`;
   - `unlink  <driver> -> <driven>`.
   `<time>` is the reply's `since` as its UTC clock time in whole seconds with `Z` (`%H:%M:%SZ`, always the time-only
   form: the wireframe shows no date, leaned per layout-templates §Output structure — wheel, handoff and dialog
   verbs); a `since` that is no RFC 3339 instant (the restore's `"unknown"`) prints through `escape_message`, as
   `override_end` does (28-39). Inline cases pin each line byte for byte and that none holds an ESC or a non-ASCII
   byte, a non-instant `since` included.

4. **The two verbs** (new `src/cmd/link.rs`, `src/cmd/unlink.rs`). `link.rs` holds the shared call, as
   `src/cmd/pause.rs:49-86`'s `wheel_call` serves `release`; `unlink.rs` is its thin second verb. Each verb takes
   `<driver>` and `<driven>` through `super::send::parse_name` and `--json`. The verb's instance is the driven one.
   In order:
   1. the absolute home and `<home>/instances/<driven>`; `check_instance(home, instance_dir)` — refused: under
      `--json` the document `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":null}` on stdout with stderr empty,
      else `human::instance_state_pair(driven)` through `human::refuse`; exit 21; nothing under the home opened,
      no role file, no line (the shape of `src/cmd/list.rs:100-108` and `revive`'s, with exit 21 as every CLI verb
      but `run` / `mcp` / `revive` maps a strict-modes refusal, test-plan §5 On-disk);
   2. `client::start(home, &driven)` (the `cli` role file and `process-start`);
   3. `live_endpoint` — none: exit 21 through `client::unreachable` and `client::unable_unreachable(driven, …)`;
   4. params `{driver, driven}` plus `from` from `client::own_name()` when set;
   5. one request through `client::connect` under `#[instrument(skip_all, name = "cli.link")]` /
      `name = "cli.unlink"` (obs-plan §2 span naming: `cli.<verb>`; keeps obs S2);
   6. the reply through `client::answer_of`: an `ok` of `link` with a string `since` and a boolean
      `already_linked`, or an `ok` of `unlink` that is an object, prints the step-3 line built from the verb's own
      parsed names and the reply's keys, or under `--json` `{"v":1,"ok":<ok>}`, then `run::log_self_exit(0, None)`,
      exit 0; `Fault` → `client::fault`, exit 20; unreachable (`Dead`, `ServerUnverified`) → exit 21 with the cause's
      hint; a `Refused` or an `ok` of another shape → an internal error (exit 1 through the `main` catch site).
   Each module's test module, gated `#[cfg(test)]` + `#[cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))]` (testing.md 2026-10-26),
   holds `request_refuses_an_unverified_server_inside_its_dispatch_span` through `client::refused_inside`; `link.rs`
   also holds the reply-shape table (`#[case]` rows: each accepted and refused `ok` shape, a refusal, a fault).

5. **The subcommands and the help row** (`src/cmd/mod.rs`). `mod link; mod unlink;`; `Command` gains `Link` and
   `Unlink` with one-line help texts ("Link a driver to the driven instance: its wrapper records the pair",
   "Remove a driver's link to the driven instance"); their `dispatch` arms resolve the home through `resolved_home`
   and take `cli_sink(&home, &args.driven)`; `HELP_TEMPLATE` gains `handoff:  link, unlink` between `wheel:` and
   `setup:` (layout-templates §Output structure — `viola --help`). `role_of` (`src/main.rs:94-119`) reads both
   words as `Role::Cli` already: no change.

6. **The unserved-method examples move** (`tests/channel_endpoint.rs:217-250`). The case
   `channel_wrapper_logs_each_call_with_corr_and_conn` uses `link` and a raw `unlink` frame as its unserved
   method; both become `anything`, its `-32601` assertions and joins unchanged.

7. **The help pins** (`tests/cli_output_plain.rs:56-136`). The `HELP` literal gains the `handoff:  link, unlink`
   row; `help_lists_only_served_verbs`'s served list gains `"link"`, `"unlink"` after `"release"` and its forbidden
   list drops them.

8. **The server-identity negative and its control** (`tests/security_negatives_server_identity.rs`). The impostor
   `Dispatch` answers `link` / `unlink`; `verb()` gains `["link", "overseer", "builder"]` and
   `["unlink", "overseer", "builder"]`; the mismatch table gains four rows (both verbs, both modes) and the control
   table two (keeps tests S8's impostor exception, security S3).

9. **E3 and the verbs' root cases** (`tests/cli_links.rs`; each from `stamped_home`, keeps tests S3, S6, S8, S9):
   - `e3_two_links_and_a_send_leave_one_link_record` (test-plan §6 Scenario E3 steps 1 to 3): two
     `viola link overseer builder --json` read exit 0 with `already_linked` false then true and one `since`; a
     `viola send builder` under `VIOLA_NAME=overseer` adds no `link`; the log holds exactly one
     `link{driver:"overseer",driven:"builder"}` record; `viola unlink overseer builder --json` reads
     `{"v":1,"ok":{}}` and appends one `unlink` record the wrapper wrote; the snapshot's `links` is empty; a second
     unlink appends nothing; a further link has a later `since` and `already_linked` false;
   - `link_verbs_print_the_design_lines`: the three human lines on stdout, the time matched by shape
     (`HH:MM:SSZ`), stderr empty, no ESC byte;
   - `link_verbs_against_a_stopped_instance_exit_21`: both verbs, human (`unable  builder  instance-unreachable`,
     the not-running hint last) and `--json` (the `instance-unreachable` document, stderr empty);
   - `link_verbs_log_the_channel_pair_and_no_names`: `run-builder.ndjson` holds one `channel-request` and one
     `channel-response` per call with that `method` and a shared `(conn, corr)`; neither holds `overseer`, `since`
     or `already_linked`; `cli-builder.ndjson` holds the verb's `process-start` and `process-exit` exit 0;
   - `link_verbs_refuse_a_widened_instance_before_any_log` (`#[cfg(unix)]`, the order trap of
     test-plan §6 Exit-cause matrix): with `instances/builder` set 0770 while the wrapper runs, both verbs in both
     modes exit 21 with the instance-state pair (human) or the `instance-unreachable` document (`--json`, stderr
     empty), `cli-builder.ndjson` gains no line, the directory reads 0770 after, and the wrapper received no frame
     (`run-builder.ndjson` gains no `channel-request`);
   - `links_an_unlink_survives_a_wrapper_restart`: link, unlink, stop, boot again over the same home: the first
     snapshot's `links` is empty and no line is appended (the restore over a product-written `unlink`).
   The driver is not booted: its name is self-reported (`from` / `driver`), the wrapper never contacts it, and the
   landed step-2 cases boot `builder` alone (`tests/cli_links.rs:103-141`) — leaned per that precedent; test-plan
   §6 E3's "Boot `overseer` and `builder`" is an Expected amendment below.

10. **The raw-channel name negative** (new `tests/channel_links.rs`, test-plan §6 Security control negatives,
    keeps tests S1, S4): over `booted_wrapper`, frames written straight to the endpoint for `link` and for
    `unlink` with `driver` or `driven` set to `../x`, `BUILDER`, `a/b`, `""`, a 33-character name and a number each
    read `-32602`; so do a foreign `driven` and `driver` equal to `driven`; no `link` / `unlink` record is appended
    and the snapshot's `links` stays empty; the control, a valid `link` frame, reads `ok` and appends one line.
    `channel_link_names_are_validated_by_the_wrapper`, one rstest table.
11. **The kill line** (`.config/nextest.toml:24`). `binary(channel_links)` joins the stamped-home named list.
12. **The operator pass**: the three `leg = 'operator'` entries (hygiene, push, CI).
- `src/cmd/link.rs` — `viola link` and the call both verbs share; its unit cases
- `src/cmd/unlink.rs` — `viola unlink`; its unit case
- `tests/channel_links.rs` — the raw-channel `link` / `unlink` name negative
- `src/run/links.rs` — the two method handlers; `remove`'s allow ends (step 1)
- `src/cmd/run.rs` — `Methods` holds the set; `dispatch_call` routes the two methods (step 2)
- `src/cmd/mod.rs` — the modules, `Command` variants, dispatch arms, the help row (step 5)
- `src/human/verbs.rs` — the three result-line writers (step 3)
- `src/human.rs` — their re-export (step 3)
- `tests/channel_endpoint.rs` — the unserved-method examples become `anything` (step 6)
- `tests/cli_output_plain.rs` — the `HELP` literal and the served list (step 7)
- `tests/security_negatives_server_identity.rs` — the two verbs in both tables (step 8)
- `tests/cli_links.rs` — E3 and the verbs' cases (step 9)
- `.config/nextest.toml` — `binary(channel_links)` on the kill line (step 11)

The block runs in this order: the `/tmp` reading (the stamped-home cases follow); the lints (the Windows-target
clippy is in because steps 4 and 9 add `cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))` / `cfg(unix)` test code, and the orphans
check because two modules are added); the unit tier; the five binaries this chunk adds to or edits, by name; the
supply-chain read; the preservation guard; the harness smoke, G2 and G4; the hook perf rows (the wrapper's dispatch
gains two arms); `pre-push`; the operator entries last.

**No live leg.** The chunk drives no external process; its Windows witnesses run in CI's `test (windows-2025)` run,
its Linux ones there and on this host. **No mutation entry**: mutation runs at the epoch boundary only (test-plan §10
Mutation gate). **macOS:** the two verbs' captured-span cases and the server-identity rows compile out on
`macos-latest`; the verbs' other cases run there.
