body:
- (arch) A served `link` of a pair not in the set appends exactly one `link{driver, driven}` line with
  `source: wrapper` and answers `{"since": <that line's ts>, "already_linked": false}`; a second `link` of the pair
  appends nothing and answers the same `since` with `already_linked: true`; `unlink` of a held pair appends one
  `unlink` line, of an absent pair nothing, each answering `{}`; the snapshot's `links` follows each line, and a
  wrapper restarted over the log restores the set the log ends on (per architecture §Established Decisions [Links];
  §Standard Contracts Instance snapshot) — `links_set_method_*`, `e3_two_links_and_a_send_leave_one_link_record`,
  `links_an_unlink_survives_a_wrapper_restart`, run by `cargo nextest run --workspace --features fake-agent -E 'binary(cli_links)'`.

- (security) A raw `link` or `unlink` frame whose `driver` or `driven` is `../x`, `BUILDER`, `a/b`, `""`, a
  33-character name or a number, whose `driven` is not the serving wrapper's name, or whose `driver` equals `driven`
  is answered `-32602` with `data: null`, and no `link` / `unlink` line is appended (per security-plan §Input
  Validation, channel frames) — `channel_link_names_are_validated_by_the_wrapper`.

- (security) On Linux and Windows, `viola link` and `viola unlink` against an endpoint served by a process other
  than the one `snapshot.json` records write no frame and exit 21: `--json` exactly
  `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":null}` with stderr empty, human the
  `unable  builder  instance-unreachable` line with the server-verify hint last; against the recorded wrapper each
  delivers one frame (per security-plan §Authentication & Authorization, IPC client-side server verification) —
  the two tables of `tests/security_negatives_server_identity.rs`.

- (security) With the driven instance's directory group-writable (Unix), both verbs refuse before any log opens and
  before any snapshot value is used: exit 21, the instance-state pair or the `instance-unreachable` document, no
  line in `cli-builder.ndjson`, no frame to the wrapper, the directory's mode as found (per security-plan
  §Authentication & Authorization, `~/.viola/` access control; `inputs#I3`) —
  `link_verbs_refuse_a_widened_instance_before_any_log`.

- (obs) Each verb's server-check refusal falls inside its `cli.link` / `cli.unlink` span with no frame written
  (per obs-plan §4 Span / Trace Coverage) — `request_refuses_an_unverified_server_inside_its_dispatch_span` in
  `src/cmd/link.rs` and `src/cmd/unlink.rs`; each call leaves one `channel-request` / `channel-response` pair with
  its `method` on the wrapper, joined by `(conn, corr)`, holding no driver name, `since` or `already_linked` (per
  obs-plan §6 Log Coverage, Boundary-call wrappers) — `link_verbs_log_the_channel_pair_and_no_names`.

- (design) `viola link` prints exactly `link    overseer -> builder  since HH:MM:SSZ` for a new pair and
  `link    overseer -> builder  already linked` for a held one, and `viola unlink` prints `unlink  overseer -> builder`,
  each one plain ASCII stdout line with stderr empty and no ESC byte; under `--json` each prints `{"v":1,"ok":…}`
  carrying the same facts (per design-system §Surface: cli Component Patterns 4) — the step-3 inline cases and
  `link_verbs_print_the_design_lines`.

- (design) A stopped driven instance makes both verbs exit 21 with the not-running hint last, or the
  `instance-unreachable` document under `--json` (per design-system §Surface: cli Exit-code phraseology) —
  `link_verbs_against_a_stopped_instance_exit_21`.

- (layouts) `viola --help` prints `handoff:  link, unlink` between `wheel:` and `setup:`, and every listed verb
  answers its own `--help` (per layout-templates §Output structure — `viola --help`) — `help_is_the_grouped_verb_table`,
  `help_lists_only_served_verbs`.

- (tests) The unserved-method example of `channel_wrapper_logs_each_call_with_corr_and_conn` still reads `-32601`
  (per test-plan §5 Cross-module patterns — Wrapper channel).

- (tests) `bash scripts/agent-run.sh pre-push` reads `"ok":true` at stage `linux-tests`, and CI on the operator's
  push reads `verdict: green` (per test-plan §9).

- No verification-matrix capability is claimed by this chunk (P5 step 4): `v1-13` and `v1-36` each name a surface no
  chunk can build under the masters as they stand (Implementation notes).

- Spec anchors: architecture §Established Decisions [Links], [MCP], [CLI Conventions], §Standard Contracts (Channel
  methods, Instance snapshot, Session liveness, Event data), §Conventions (CLI exit codes); security-plan
  §Authentication & Authorization (IPC client-side server verification; `~/.viola/` access control), §Input
  Validation (channel frames; CLI arguments), §Security Anti-Patterns (Universal: a new channel method's Decisions
  Log entry); design-system §Surface: cli (Component Patterns 4, Exit-code phraseology, Navigation Pattern);
  layout-templates §Output structure — `viola --help`, — wheel, handoff and dialog verbs; test-plan §6 Scenario E3,
  Security control negatives, §5 Wrapper channel and CLI; obs-plan §2 span naming, §4 Edge flows E3 and the cli
  server check, §6 Log Coverage, §10 bounded exemptions; a11y-plan §8 Error recovery, §4 the `--help` labels.

- `(sampler)` items carried: the snapshot rewrite through `Snapshots` (established-decisions.md:142), the `send`
  link ordering left intact (standard-contracts.md:53), Tokio-free sync crates (dependency-security.md:14), G2's one
  exemption (dependency-security.md:42), the 1.96 MSRV leg (ci-integration.md:43), the perf rows
  (quality-gates-coverage-targets.md:26), the restore appending nothing (span-trace-coverage.md:39), the board's
  caption order unchanged (cognitive-accessibility.md:45).

- Research files inspected: `src/run/links.rs`, `src/cmd/run.rs`, `src/cmd/client.rs`, `src/cmd/pause.rs`,
  `src/cmd/send.rs`, `src/cmd/revive.rs`, `src/cmd/list.rs`, `src/cmd/mod.rs`, `src/main.rs`, `src/human.rs`,
  `src/human/verbs.rs`, `src/human/hints.rs`, `src/human/board/pairs.rs`, `crates/viola-state/src/strict.rs`,
  `tests/channel_endpoint.rs`, `tests/cli_output_plain.rs`, `tests/security_negatives_server_identity.rs`,
  `tests/cli_links.rs`, `.config/nextest.toml`.

- Code-graph impact (research.md): `LinkSet::remove` 0 product callers (its own tests @ `src/run/links.rs:302`,
  `:307`, `:317`) → 2 (the `unlink` method); `check_instance` 3 product callers → 4 (`src/cmd/link.rs`, shared by
  both verbs); `live_endpoint` 7 → 8; `cmd::client::connect` 6 → 8.

- A client-side refusal of `driver` equal to `driven` — rejected: the wrapper re-runs every check and answers it
  `-32602` (the operator's answer, `chunks/2026-10-10-session-links/inputs/I2-relay-2.md.txt`); the verb maps it to
  exit 20 like any wrapper fault.

- An MCP `link` / `unlink` tool — rejected: architecture [MCP] keeps both CLI-only, and the recorded `Mcp.` exchange
  holds the five tools.

  this chunk; the second CARRY's re-parse rule binds the first surface that shows one.

  (`chunks/2026-10-10-session-links/inputs/I2-relay-2.md.txt`).

- A trycmd case for the result lines — rejected: no manifest holds trycmd and no `tests/cmd/` exists (measured at

- The check before the log is the measured trap: opening a role file narrows an existing home to 0700, so a check

  `started_at` without the strict-modes check.

  writing their frame after the liveness-only pre-check with the snapshot read under no strict-modes check, as a dated
  gap of their own until the Epoch 6 entries "Server verification before any frame" and "Home and code-bearing file
  integrity""; "the instance check ahead of the snapshot read as `viola revive` takes it"; "no explicit verbs before
  Epoch 6".

- **Marker:** 2026-10-26-home-and-code-bearing-file-integrity · **Version:** viola-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-26T18:16Z

Every process that reads or opens anything under the viola home first refuses a home, instance tree, code-bearing
folder or diagnostics file another user could write (or read, where content lives), and does it before the first open,
because opening a role file narrows an existing home to 0700 and a check made after it passes a 0770 home (CARRY 14,
re-derived at src/obs.rs:43–45, 76–78). The check lands at the six CLI frame verbs, `viola hook`'s nine events, `viola
mcp`'s frame tools, `viola verify`, `viola run` (and `revive`'s start) and the diagnostics opens, closing the eight dated
strict-modes gaps the founder ratified until this entry (per security-plan §Authentication & Authorization, `~/.viola/`
access control; the detail authentication-authorization.md:25–39). The master's read rule lands with it: Unix `mode &
0o077` on the home and `instances/<name>/`, and on Windows a read grant to another SID on the home, `instances/<name>/`,
its `diagnostics/` and `events.ndjson` (authentication-authorization.md:38, :40) — neither is in code today
(strict.rs:76–84 refuses `0o022`, `windows_verdict` write rights only).

By the founder's own answers (`inputs#I3`): the four snapshot readers (hook `connect`, hook statusline `serve`, `run`'s
`collision_check`, `viola_state::liveness::live_endpoint`) move onto `read_snapshot_or_replay`, each after the new check
(his ratification of that boundary widening; test-plan §6 E5 steps 1–3); a refused check at every new entry point writes
no line, as `link` / `unlink`; the six frame verbs print `link`'s instance pair; and CARRYs 11 and 16 (build
reproducibility, the `pin_exe` race) leave this chunk for a new entry «Pinned copy race and reproducible builds» right
after this one (the P5 card's Beyond-the-plan row). The Windows proofs (the widened instance tree, the seeded home's
DACL, the `RUNNER_TEMP` negative, the `conpty/` leg) run on CI's `test (windows-2025)` leg (per test-plan §9; §11 «NEVER
treat a Linux-only local run as proof for Windows»).

1. **The read rule and the tree checks in `viola_state::strict`** (`crates/viola-state/src/strict.rs`). Keep
   `check_path` (the write rule) as is for files and code-bearing folders. Add a read-rule check for the content-bearing
   directories: Unix refuses `mode & 0o077 != 0` beside the owner test (a pure `unix_read_verdict(mode, uid, euid)` beside
   `unix_verdict`); Windows refuses, on top of the write rule, any allow ACE granting `FILE_READ_DATA` (0x1), `GENERIC_READ`
   (0x8000_0000) or `GENERIC_ALL` to a SID `trusted_sid` rejects, inherit-only ACEs included (a pure `windows_read_verdict`
   beside `windows_verdict`, its mask a pinned `READ_RIGHTS` literal as `WRITE_RIGHTS` is). `check_instance` applies the
   read rule to the home, `instances/<name>/`, `instances/<name>/diagnostics/` (each that exists) and, on Windows,
   `events.ndjson`; the write rule to `instances/`, `snapshot.json` and Unix `events.ndjson`, in the order they nest. Add
   `check_home_tree(home, name: Option<&ViolaName>, key: Option<&str>)`: the home (read rule), `instances/` and
   `instances/<name>/` (read rule, `check_instance`'s set) when a name is given, `ledger/`, `bin/`, `plugin/`, and, with a
   key, `bin/<key>/`, the pinned `viola(.exe)`, `plugin/<key>/` and its `hooks/` and `.claude-plugin/` (write rule), each
   that exists; it returns which side refused (`HomeLevel` · `InstanceLevel`) so a caller picks its pair. Add
   `check_diagnostics(path)`: refuse a symlink (`symlink_metadata`), then the read rule on a directory and the write rule +
   Unix `0o077` on a file. Unit cases (keeps tests S1, S3, S6): the pure verdict tables on every OS (`0o040`, `0o004` refused
   on a dir; a Windows read ACE and an inherit-only `GENERIC_ALL` read ACE refused; `CREATOR OWNER` passes), the
   `check_home_tree` and `check_diagnostics` refusals on Unix (each widened path in turn, a symlinked role file), and
   `#[cfg(windows)]` cases on CI's leg: an instance tree a sibling of which is granted Users write through `icacls`
   (its exit asserted, the `wipe_scratch_takes_an_instance_tree_the_check_accepts_where_a_plain_dir_does_not` form)
   refused `Writable`, the `create_private_dir` tree passing, and a `diagnostics/` granted Users read refused. `#[cfg(test)]`
   first, the OS gate second (testing.md 2026-10-26).

2. **`update_stamps` checks before it reads** (`crates/viola-state/src/stamps.rs`): inside its lock, `check_stamps(home)`
   before the capped read; a refusal is a new `StampsError` variant with a fixed message and writes nothing. The
   `take(MAX_FRAME + 1)` bound and over-cap-as-absent stay. Unit: a world-writable `ledger/` refuses with the file
   unchanged (Unix).

3. **The frame verbs' shared check** (`src/cmd/client.rs`): `refuse_untrusted(home, name, json) -> Option<u8>` runs
   `check_instance` on `std::path::absolute(home)` and `instances/<name>` and, on a refusal, prints `client::refused_document
   ("instance-unreachable")` under `--json` or `human::refuse` of `human::instance_state_pair(name)`, returning 21; it opens
   nothing under the home. `link_call` (src/cmd/link.rs:98) moves onto it unchanged in behaviour. `send` (after its text
   read, before `client::start`, send.rs:190), `wait` (wait.rs:43), `last` (last.rs:30), `answer` (answer.rs:94), `pause`
   (pause.rs:32) and `release` (release.rs:35) call it first. Its refusal writes no line (the founder's answer, `inputs#I3`).
   The client's exit-13 text refusals now follow it. Update the module doc of `client.rs` (the dated gap retired).

4. **`viola hook`'s nine events** (`src/cmd/hook.rs`, `src/cmd/hook/statusline.rs`): move `canonical` and `trusted` from
   statusline.rs into hook.rs, used by both arms; on the event and dialog paths take `instance_of(…).and_then(canonical)
   .filter(trusted)` before `read_diagnostics_level` and `viola_obs_init` (hook.rs:101–104): a refused instance returns
   `ExitCode::SUCCESS` at once with no `config.json` read, no role file, no stdin read, no line, no frame and no SessionEnd
   append. The two `--capture` arms stay ahead of it, unchanged. The `FAKE_AGENT_HOOK_PANIC` seam keeps its place after
   `viola_obs_init`. Retire the `connect` doc's dated-gap sentence.

5. **The readers onto the replay** (`inputs#I3`, the founder's ratification): `live_endpoint`
   (crates/viola-state/src/liveness.rs:89) reads `replay::read_snapshot_or_replay`: `Snapshot` as today; `Replayed`,
   `Absent` or an error → `None` (a replayed snapshot has no `endpoint`, `pid` or `started_at`, so no frame is written on it;
   architecture §Standard Contracts, Snapshot envelope). Hook `connect` (hook.rs:203): `Replayed` or `Absent` →
   `NotSent::Unreachable` (fail open, `channel-unreachable`, SessionEnd's direct append as today). Statusline `serve`
   (statusline.rs:141): a replayed snapshot has no `statusline_command`, so nothing is run or printed. `collision_check`
   (src/cmd/run.rs:378): `Replayed` → liveness from the beat alone, `beat_age ≤ STALE_AFTER` → `already-live`, else free;
   an error or `Absent` → free, as an unreadable snapshot reads today. Each replay writes its one `state-recovered` line
   into the role file already open (obs-plan §4 E5). Unit cases per reader: a snapshot cut short and one of `v` 99, made
   from the writer's own bytes (testing.md Test data).

6. **`viola mcp`'s frame tools** (`crates/viola-mcp/src/tools.rs` `frame`, :323): `check_instance(&ctx.home,
   &instance_dir)` before `live_endpoint`; a refusal returns `result::unreachable()` (no frame, no line; inside
   `mcp.tool_call`).

7. **`viola verify`** (`src/cmd/verify.rs` `verify`, :57): before its `cli` log, `check_home_tree(home, None, None)` (the
   home, `ledger/`, `bin/`, `plugin/`); a refusal prints `human::home_state_pair()` through `human::refuse` and exits 1,

8. **`viola run` and `revive`'s start** (`src/cmd/run.rs` `run`, :163; `src/cmd/revive.rs` `trusted`, :134): before
   `open_wrapper_log`, read the exe's bytes once, take their key (`pin::content_key`) and run `check_home_tree(home,
   Some(name), Some(&key))`; `HomeLevel` → `human::home_state_pair()`, `InstanceLevel` → `human::instance_state_pair(name)`,
   each through `human::refuse`, exit 1, no log opened, no line, no child (revive under `--json` keeps its
   `strict-modes-failed` document). `pin_exe` takes the bytes already read. The canonicalisation after the log stays.

9. **The diagnostics opens** (`src/obs.rs` `open_role_file`, :70; `write_detail`, :310): `check_diagnostics` on the
   existing `diagnostics/` dir and the role or detail file before `ensure_private_dir` narrows anything; a refusal is
   returned as an `io::Error` exactly as a failed open is today (the writer ends at `std::io::sink`, a detail line is
   dropped; obs-plan §3 OTel SDK init).

10. **The ConPTY companions' owner/DACL leg** (Windows x64; `crates/viola-state/src/pin.rs` `pin_companions`, :154):
    `check_path` on `conpty/` and on each companion that exists, before the held open; a refusal is a new `PinError`
    variant that `run`'s `sideload_outcome` (src/cmd/run.rs:460) maps to the outcome `strict-modes-failed`: the child runs
    on the inbox ConPTY with `sideload_fallback` `strict-modes-failed`, never a refusal, byte or exit change (architecture
    §Established Decisions [PTY]). Add the word to `schemas/diag-line.v1.json`'s `sideload_fallback` enum.

11. **The seeded home** (`tests/support/home.rs` `seed_conpty`, :272): make the home with
    `viola_state::fs::create_private_dir(home)` (the product's creation: the protected DACL outside the profile) before
    `bin/<key>/conpty/`, and the seed dir `target/conpty-seed/<key>/` with `create_private_dir` too, so a hard-linked
    companion carries an owner-only DACL and passes step 10. On `windows-2025` record once, in `evidence/`, the canonical
    SDDL of a plain `create_dir_all` home under `target/e2e-home` and that `check_instance` refuses it `Writable` (CARRY 13's
    owed reading; the answer recorded: such a home is one the product must refuse).

12. **The Windows `check_instance` proof and the hook rows**: `tests/hook_fail_open.rs` gains a widened-instance row in
    both matrices (Unix `chmod 0770` on `instances/<name>`; Windows `icacls … /grant *S-1-5-32-545:(OI)(CI)(W)`, its exit
    asserted): exit 0, empty streams, under the 1.0 s `Instant` bound, no frame at the wrapper, no line added to
    `hook-<name>.ndjson`, the mode or ACL read back as found. `tests/hook_statusline.rs` gains the Windows form of the
    widened-instance case (no command run, no line). The impostor rows stay on homes that pass the check.

13. **`tests/security_negatives_strict_modes.rs`** (new; keeps tests S2, S3, S7): (a) each of `send`, `wait`, `last`,
    `answer`, `pause`, `release` against a widened instance in both modes beside a control against the same live wrapper
    unwidened: exit 21, the instance pair with `hint:` last and stdout empty, or exactly
    `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":null}` with stderr empty, no line added to `cli-<name>.ndjson`, no frame
    at the wrapper (`events.ndjson`'s length unchanged), the mode or ACL as found, no digit run in any output (the
    `digit_runs` form); all three OSes. (b) Single writers: record `ledger/stamps.json` and `snapshot.json` bytes, stop the
    wrapper (`Wrapper::stop`), run every other writer-capable entry point (each `hook <event>` including `hook statusline`,
    `list`, `wait` / `last` / `send`, the MCP tools through `viola mcp`), and read both files byte-identical. (c)
    `#[cfg(unix)]` umask-independent modes: `sh -c 'umask 000; exec viola run …'`, every home file 0600, dir 0700, the pinned
    `viola` 0700. (d) `#[cfg(windows)]` a not-yet-existing `--home` under `target/e2e-home` gets the protected DACL read back
    as exactly the user and SYSTEM (canonical SDDL); a pre-existing dir there granted Users read refuses `viola run` with
    exit 1 and the home pair.

14. **`run`, `verify` and the sideload cases**: `tests/run_cli.rs` — a 0770 home, a widened `instances/<name>`, a widened
    `bin/` and a pinned copy made group-writable each refuse `viola run` exit 1 with its pair, no `run-<name>.ndjson`
    line, the mode as found (Windows by `icacls`). `tests/cli_verify.rs` — a widened `ledger/` refuses `verify` exit 1, the
    home pair, no step line, `stamps.json` unchanged. `tests/conpty_sideload.rs` — a companion granted Users write leaves
    the child on `conhost.exe` with `sideload_fallback` `strict-modes-failed` and exit unchanged.

15. **MCP and the controls table**: `crates/viola-mcp/tests/handlers.rs` — the four frame tools against a widened
    instance return `instance-unreachable`, `detail: null`, no frame, no line. `tests/cli_controls_not_disableable.rs` — a
    case `setting_does_not_disable_the_home_check` runs `viola send` against a 0770 home under each `SETTINGS` row and reads
    exit 21 (`cfg(unix)`); the `--home` row names it (CARRY 4).

16. **E5 steps 1–3** (`tests/chaos_snapshot_replay.rs`, new): a wrapper driven through `link`, `pause` and a budget
    pause, stopped; its `snapshot.json` cut short (sibling case: envelope `v:99`, from the writer's own bytes); once the
    heartbeat is older than `STALE_AFTER` (the beat file's age read, never a sleep), `viola run builder` again: exit not 1,
    one `state-recovered` line (`snapshot-replayed` / `snapshot-unsupported-v`) in `run-builder.ndjson`, the new first
    snapshot's `links` equal to the logged ones; and a start while the beat is fresh refuses `already-live`. The two
    signals set against what landed are restated (step 17).

17. **Retire the dated-gap comments** at every site this chunk closes (client.rs module doc, liveness.rs, hook.rs
    `connect`), and record the Expected amendments below in `report.md`.
- `tests/security_negatives_strict_modes.rs` — step 13
- `tests/chaos_snapshot_replay.rs` — step 16
- `crates/viola-state/src/strict.rs` — step 1 · `crates/viola-state/src/stamps.rs` — step 2 · `crates/viola-state/src/liveness.rs` — step 5 · `crates/viola-state/src/pin.rs` — step 10
- `crates/viola-mcp/src/tools.rs` — step 6 · `crates/viola-mcp/tests/handlers.rs` — step 15
- `src/cmd/client.rs`, `src/cmd/link.rs`, `src/cmd/send.rs`, `src/cmd/wait.rs`, `src/cmd/last.rs`, `src/cmd/answer.rs`, `src/cmd/pause.rs`, `src/cmd/release.rs` — step 3
- `src/cmd/hook.rs`, `src/cmd/hook/statusline.rs` — steps 4, 5 · `src/cmd/run.rs`, `src/cmd/revive.rs` — steps 5, 8, 10 · `src/cmd/verify.rs` — step 7 · `src/obs.rs` — step 9
- `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` — step 10

- `tests/support/home.rs` — step 11 · `tests/hook_fail_open.rs`, `tests/hook_statusline.rs` — step 12 · `tests/run_cli.rs`, `tests/cli_verify.rs`, `tests/conpty_sideload.rs` — step 14 · `tests/cli_controls_not_disableable.rs` — step 15

Graph impact (research.md §Graph impact): `client::start` keeps its 10 callers, the six frame verbs gaining the check
ahead of it (send.rs:190, wait.rs:43, last.rs:30, answer.rs:94, pause.rs:32, release.rs:35); `live_endpoint` @
liveness.rs:89 keeps its 7 callers (answer.rs:119, last.rs:38, link.rs:113, pause.rs:64, send.rs:218, wait.rs:51,
viola-mcp tools.rs:335) and its signature; `read_snapshot`'s 3 product callers under `src/` (hook.rs:204,
statusline.rs:142, run.rs:383) move to the replay; `update_stamps` has 1 product caller (verify.rs:264); `viola_obs_init`
has 6 (client.rs:22, hook.rs:104, statusline.rs:60, mcp.rs:27, run.rs:184, verify.rs:65), each now behind a check.

The block runs in this order: the `/tmp` reading (the stamped-home cases follow); the lints (the Windows-target clippy
is in because steps 1, 10–14 add `cfg(windows)` code); the unit tier; the binaries this chunk adds or edits, by name;
the supply-chain read; the preservation guard; the harness smoke, G2 and G4; the hook perf rows (every hook now runs the
instance check); `pre-push`; the operator entries last.

**No live leg.** The chunk drives no external process; its Windows witnesses run in CI's `test (windows-2025)` run, its
Unix ones there and on this host. **No mutation entry**: mutation runs at the epoch boundary only (test-plan §10 Mutation
gate). **No orphans entry**: no module is added. **macOS:** the strict-modes cases run there (they need no peer pid);
only the server-identity rows compile out.

  mode or ACL left as found, on all three OSes — `binary(security_negatives_strict_modes)` (per security-plan
  §Authentication & Authorization; the founder's pair, `inputs#I3`).

  1.0 s bound, write no frame and no line and append no SessionEnd; the capture arms are unchanged —
  `binary(hook_fail_open) | binary(hook_statusline)` (per security-plan §Error Handling).

body:
**Working entry (viola-0.1.0/working-route.md, Epoch 6 — Security hardening):** Home and code-bearing file integrity —
owner-only home, DACL check before any diagnostics file, pinned-binary re-hash, per-start plugin rewrite, single
stamp/snapshot writers.

**Invocation:** the operator's `/andromeda-phase Proceed.`, with the overseer's directive for this phase (`inputs#I1`):
forced sample at P2 (`detail.py sample --side phase --force`), the two-draw classify's first live run, every subagent
and Workflow transcript and the run dir kept, a hard cascade failure (or agents writing nothing, or doing the
orchestrator's work) stops the phase with no re-spawn around it; the founder's own forks — the readers' move onto the
log replay (fork CARRY 7/8) is his to rule at P4 as a live dialog, and any boundary widening halts for his live word;
standing: no epoch boundary inside Epoch 6, `df -h /tmp` read before a stamped-home gate.

security.md §Local trust boundary's home rules made whole at every entry point, and the end of the dated strict-modes
exceptions the founder ratified "until the Epoch 6 entry 'Home and code-bearing file integrity'".

- **Owner-only home.** Every directory under the home created 0700 and every file 0600 explicitly on Unix; on Windows
  a protected owner + SYSTEM DACL. The working entry states it; what already stands (`viola_state::fs::create_private_dir`,
  `replace_private`, the Windows DACL at creation for a home outside `%USERPROFILE%`) is P3's to read.

- **DACL check before any diagnostics file** (working entry): the Windows owner + DACL read before
  `instances/<name>/diagnostics/detail-*.ndjson` (and any role file) is opened. Verified at P3: `open_role_file`
  (obs.rs:70) and `write_detail` (obs.rs:310) open with no check on either OS and narrow an existing dir first on Unix;
  the Windows proof of `check_instance` (CARRY 12) and the seeded-home question (CARRY 13) are its witnesses.

- **Pinned-binary re-hash** (working entry): `bin/<version>-<hash>/viola` re-hashed (truncated SHA-256) before reuse;

- **Marker:** 2026-10-26-server-verification-before-any-frame · **Version:** viola-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-26T08:11Z

Every viola client that writes a frame to a wrapper's endpoint verifies, before its first frame, that the process
serving the endpoint is the wrapper `snapshot.json` records: the connected stream's server pid equals the snapshot's
`pid`, and that pid's OS start time equals its `started_at` (security-plan §Authentication & Authorization, IPC
client-side server verification row; §Security Anti-Patterns › Authentication). The clients are the six CLI frame verbs
(`send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`), `viola hook`'s two (`hook.event` on every event, `hook.dialog`
on `pre-tool-use` / `permission-request`) and `viola mcp`'s four frame tools (`send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`) — every
product connect site (research.md Sweeps).

On a mismatch, or a check that cannot be made, no frame is written: a CLI verb exits 21 with the
`{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":null}` document or its `unable  instance-unreachable` line and the
server-verification hint; an MCP tool returns its `instance-unreachable` `isError` result; `viola hook` fails open —
exit 0, nothing on stdout or stderr (architecture §Conventions exit codes / MCP; §Established Decisions [Hook
Contract]). The process log names the cause: `process-exit{exit_code:21, detail:"server-verify-failed"}` and
`hook-decision{detail:"server-verify-failed"}`, both already members of `schemas/diag-line.v1.json`'s closed enums
(obs-plan §6 Log Coverage, Founder Direction 4).

This closes the server-identity half of the first and the fourth to eighth dated gaps on Linux and Windows. Their
strict-modes half stays with "Home and code-bearing file integrity", and macOS — whose peer credentials carry no pid —
stays on the recorded gap, its euid and socket-directory checks owned by "Unix endpoint and home hardening". Every
snapshot reader keeps `read_snapshot` (the fork's option 1, `inputs#I3`, PROVISIONAL until the founder's own word).

1. **The server pid on the sync client** (`crates/viola-channel/src/client.rs`). `Client` gains one read of the
   connected stream's peer credentials, `peer_creds().pid()` (interprocess 2.4.4 `traits::StreamCommon`): on Linux the
   socket's `SO_PEERCRED` pid, on Windows `GetNamedPipeServerProcessId` on the SQOS-adopted client end, on macOS none.
   It writes nothing to the stream and logs nothing. The Windows open stays `open_handle`'s SQOS + overlapped
   `CreateFileW` adopted by `Stream::try_from`, never a default connect. Unit cases in the module's tests: a `Client`
   connected to a `Server` the test serves reads the test process's own pid, `#[cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))]`; on
   macOS it reads none, `#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]` (keeps arch S2, S3; tests S2).

2. **The same read on the Tokio client** (`crates/viola-channel/src/tokio_client.rs`): `TokioClient` gains the same
   read off its stream, behind the `tokio` feature as the whole file is; no new tokio feature and no new dependency.
   Unit cases mirror step 1's two.

3. **The verification decision and the pre-check's identity** (`crates/viola-state/src/liveness.rs`).
   - `live_endpoint` returns, beside the endpoint, the recorded `pid` and `started_at` it already read from the same
     snapshot in its one `read_snapshot` call (no second read, the file not held open past the read: architecture
     §Established Decisions [Snapshot writer], the Windows `persist` retry).
   - A pure decision takes the recorded `pid`, the recorded `started_at`, the observed server pid (`Option<u32>`), the
     observed pid's start time in whole seconds (`Option<u64>`) and whether the platform reports a peer pid at all, and
     returns a closed verdict: the server matches · it does not (another pid, or the same pid with another start time)
     · it cannot be checked (`started_at` not RFC 3339, no observed pid on a platform that reports one, the observed
     process gone). On a platform with no peer pid (macOS) it returns "matches" with no comparison — the recorded gap,
     never a refusal. The platform fact is the decision's argument, not a `cfg!` inside it, so every row runs on the
     Linux host.
   - One function joins them: the observed pid's start time read through `process_start_time` (sysinfo, a zombie
     none), the decision applied. Unit cases: an rstest `#[case::label]` table over the decision's rows (keeps tests
     S2, S7), plus one case over the joined function with the test process as the recorded and the observed server.

4. **The exit-21 outcome names its cause** (`src/cmd/client.rs`). `unreachable` takes a closed cause in place of the
   bare `during`: the existing one (`instance-dead` + `during` `connect` | `call`) and the server check

15. **Expected amendments recorded** — the wrap applies them (Implementation notes); no step edits a master.
- `tests/security_negatives_server_identity.rs` — the CLI verbs' impostor negatives and their control (step 13)
- `crates/viola-channel/src/client.rs` — the connected stream's server pid (step 1)
- `crates/viola-channel/src/tokio_client.rs` — the same on the Tokio client (step 2)
- `crates/viola-state/src/liveness.rs` — the recorded identity from `live_endpoint`, the decision, the joined check (step 3)
- `src/cmd/client.rs` — the exit-21 cause (step 4)
- `src/human/hints.rs` — the server-verification hint (step 5)
- `src/cmd/send.rs` — step 6 (`deliver`, `request`, `Out::unreachable`)
- `src/cmd/wait.rs`, `src/cmd/last.rs` — step 7
- `src/cmd/answer.rs` — step 8
- `src/cmd/pause.rs`, `src/cmd/release.rs` — step 9
- `src/cmd/hook.rs` — step 10 (`deliver`, `ask`, `handle`, `handle_dialog`, `dialog_decided`, the `served` fixture)
- `crates/viola-mcp/src/tools.rs` — step 11 (`frame`)
- `crates/viola-mcp/tests/handlers.rs` — step 12
- `tests/hook_fail_open.rs` — step 14

Graph impact (research.md, the code-graph query): `live_endpoint` @ `src/cmd/send.rs:219`, `src/cmd/wait.rs:49`,
`src/cmd/last.rs:36`, `src/cmd/answer.rs:116`, `src/cmd/pause.rs:60`, `crates/viola-mcp/src/tools.rs:330` (6 product
callers; the 3 test callers in `liveness.rs` move with the signature); `connect_by` @ `src/cmd/hook.rs:249`, `:497`;
`read_snapshot` under `src/` @ `src/cmd/hook.rs:246`, `:494` (kept, the check after them), `statusline.rs:142`,
`run.rs:379` (no change: no frame, no connection).

The block runs in this order: the `/tmp` reading; the lints (the Windows-target clippy is in because steps 1, 13 and
14 add `cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))` / `cfg(target_os = "macos")` code and the Windows pipe path compiles a different
stream type the dev host does not build); the unit tier; the three new or widened binaries by name (each red on the
untouched tree); the deny families and the tokio-free tree; the preservation guard; the harness smoke, G2 and G4; the
hook perf rows (the hook path gains the check inside every timed sample); `pre-push`; the operator entries last.

**No live leg.** The chunk drives no external process; its Windows witnesses run inside CI's `test (windows-2025)`
instrumented nextest run, its Linux ones there and on this host. **No mutation entry**: mutation runs at the epoch
boundary only (test-plan §10 Mutation gate, (sampler) quality-gates-coverage-targets.md:15; test-strategy.md:29).
**macOS:** steps 13 and 14 compile out on `macos-latest`; the step-1 macOS unit case (no peer pid) runs there.

body:
- (security) On Linux and Windows, with an endpoint served by a process other than the one `snapshot.json` records,
  `viola send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause` and `release` each write no frame and exit 21 with exactly
  `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":null}` on stdout under `--json` (stderr empty), and in human mode
  stdout empty with `the process on <name>'s endpoint is not its recorded wrapper; it was not contacted` as the last
  stderr line — `binary(security_negatives_server_identity)` (per security-plan §Authentication & Authorization, IPC
  client-side server verification row; design-system §Surface: cli, Exit-code phraseology).

- (security) The same verbs against a snapshot recording the serving process reach it, one frame each — the control
  rows of the same binary (per security-plan §Authentication & Authorization).

- (obs) Each refused verb writes one `process-exit{exit_code:21, detail:"server-verify-failed", during:"connect"}` at
  WARN into `cli-<name>.ndjson` and no `channel-request`, with no pid, start time, path or endpoint in any line (per
  obs-plan §6 Log Coverage, detail `log-details`; obs-plan §8 PII Scrubbing).

- (security) `viola hook stop`, `hook pre-tool-use` and `hook permission-request` facing the impostor exit 0 with empty
  stdout and stderr within `< 1.0 s`, write no frame, and write `hook-decision` with `detail:"server-verify-failed"` —
  `binary(hook_fail_open)` (per security-plan §Error Handling, the `hook` row; obs-plan §6 `hook-decision` fail-open
  codes).

- (arch) A SessionEnd whose server check fails takes the direct append, as an unreachable one does — the hook unit
  case of step 10 (per architecture §Standard Contracts, `hook.event`; §Established Decisions [Hook Transport]).

- (security) `viola mcp`'s `send`, `wait`, `last` and `answer` facing the impostor return `isError` with
  `{"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":null}` and text `refused: instance-unreachable`, no frame — `binary(handlers)`
  (per security-plan §Error Handling, MCP `isError`; test-plan §5 Wrapper channel).

- (tests) The decision table covers the match, another pid, another start time, an unparseable `started_at`, no
  observed pid where one is reported, the observed process gone, and the no-peer-pid platform passing with no
  comparison — `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --unit` (per test-plan §4 unit-test-strategy, the peer-credential
  decision with injected values).

- (tests) `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --perf` reads every hook row `max < SPINE_DEADLINE` and zero panics with the
  check in the timed path (per test-plan §10 Performance budgets; obs-plan §10).

- (arch) No sync crate gains tokio: `bash scripts/channel-tokio-free.sh` green and `cargo deny check` green (per
  architecture §Established Decisions [Module Boundaries]).

- (tests) The CI run of the final HEAD reads `verdict: green`, its Windows, Linux and macOS test legs and perf jobs
  included (per test-plan §9 Matrix builds).
- No verification-matrix capability is claimed (P5 step 4 records why for `v1-44` and `v1-41`).

- Spec anchors: security-plan §Authentication & Authorization (IPC client-side server verification row, `~/.viola/`

title: Scope — Server verification before any frame (2026-10-26-server-verification-before-any-frame)

data.head: # Scope — Server verification before any frame (2026-10-26-server-verification-before-any-frame)

body:
**Working entry (viola-0.1.0/working-route.md, Epoch 6 — Security hardening):** Server verification before any frame —
clients match the recorded wrapper pid and start time; CLI/MCP report unreachable, hooks fail open on mismatch.

**Invocation:** the operator's (`inputs#I2`), with the overseer's directive for this phase (`inputs#I1`): forced sample
at P2, every transcript and the run dir kept, a hard cascade failure stops the phase, a boundary widening held for the
founder's live word (he is asleep; a widening fork is held as such and never answered from a recorded direction).

security.md §Local trust boundary's clause "Before the FIRST frame of any method (including `hook.event`), verify the
server: pid (+ sysinfo start time) against a `snapshot.json` that passed strict-modes in the same process (macOS: euid +
dir only, recorded gap)", built in every client that writes a frame to a wrapper's endpoint, and with it the end of
the dated exceptions the founder ratified "until the Epoch 6 entries".

- The clients, every one of them (verified at P3: the product `Client::connect` / `connect_by` / `TokioClient::connect`
  sites, research.md Sweeps): CLI `viola send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `release` (`release` through
  `pause::wheel_call`); `viola hook`'s `hook.event` (every event, `deliver`) and `hook.dialog` (`pre-tool-use` ·
  `permission-request`, `ask`); `viola mcp`'s `send` / `wait` / `last` / `answer` tools (`frame`, Tokio client). No
  other product process writes a frame: `run`'s collision check reads the snapshot and opens no connection, `list` reads
  the disk, `revive` and `verify` hold no client.

- The check, before the first frame: the connected server's process id and its start time match the `pid` and
  `started_at` the instance's `snapshot.json` records. [premise-corrected: the server pid is the connected stream's
  `peer_creds().pid()` on both clients — Linux `SO_PEERCRED`, Windows `GetNamedPipeServerProcessId` on the
  SQOS-adopted client end (interprocess 2.4.4 source, research.md; not run on Windows here, CI's windows-2025 leg is its
  witness) — and the start time `viola_state::liveness::process_start_time` (sysinfo); macOS's `peer_creds()` gives
  no pid, and the euid and the socket-directory checks macOS's verification rests on are "Unix endpoint and home
  hardening"'s (its own freight: "the directory verification … and the peer euid check stay this entry's"), so this
  chunk's pid + start-time check is Linux and Windows, macOS keeping the recorded gap.]

- The dated exceptions this chunk acts on: the first (`hook.event`, Decisions Log `2026-09-28`), the fourth (`send`),
  fifth (`wait` / `last`), sixth (`answer` and `hook.dialog`), seventh (`pause` / `release`) and eighth (`viola mcp`'s
  frame tools); their text in security-plan is amended at the wrap (a master amendment, not a phase edit). Whether
  each closes WHOLE here or only its server-identity half — every one also names a strict-modes half that "Home and
  code-bearing file integrity" carries — is the boundary question below, settled at P4.

- "Home and code-bearing file integrity" (the entry after "Explicit session links") carries the strict-modes half for the
  same verbs: `send`, `wait` / `last`, `answer`, `pause` / `release`, the MCP frame tools and the hook client's
  snapshot read each get a strict-modes check there (verified: its line's CARRYs name each verb, "this entry adds
  `send` to the strict-modes entry points", and the hook client's "runs the strict-modes check … before that read").
  security.md's clause requires the snapshot the verification reads to have "passed strict-modes in the same process",
  so verification here either takes the strict-modes check with it or stands on a snapshot read without one until that
  entry — P4's to lean on that freight.

- "Explicit session links" sits between the two and stays held (the founder's «Не делать до Эпохи 6»); nothing here
  serves `link` / `unlink`.

- Windows pipe admission (the listener DACL, remote rejection, first-instance) landed with
  2026-10-25-windows-endpoint-admission; the client's SQOS open already stands. Unix socket hardening is "Unix endpoint
  and home hardening".

- No boundary is widened. A widening found on the way — a client that would write a frame on a new basis, a reader
  added off the trusted-file list — halts for the founder's live word (`inputs#I1` item 5).

title: Folded freight (working-route.md, the entry's own line — nine CARRYs)

data.head: ## Folded freight (working-route.md, the entry's own line — nine CARRYs)

body:
1. CARRY (chunk 2026-09-27-hooks-to-normalised-events, operator ruling at its P4 fork 2; the gap ratified by the founder,
   live, 2026-09-28, Decisions Log `2026-09-28`): `viola hook` sends `hook.event` to the endpoint `snapshot.json`
   records with no server verification; this entry adds it to the hook client, with its fail-open-on-mismatch case
   (exit 0, nothing on stdout or stderr), closing that dated exception. → "What it builds", hook client.

2. CARRY (chunk 2026-09-29-verify-stamped-test-homes-and-harness): on Windows a `viola hook` fired within milliseconds
   of the wrapper's exit reached the exiting wrapper's own pipe and wrote its `hook.event` (measured at
   ci#36532038635, 25 ms after the wrapper's exit line; "why the pipe outlives the observed exit is not established");
   the notification reads as delivered, so `SessionEnd`'s direct-append fallback is skipped in that window — a product
   consequence no entry owned; tests now wait for the endpoint to be gone (test-plan §3 `run` step 2). This entry owns
   that consequence (verified: the CARRY sits on this line). What P3 established: the exiting wrapper IS the recorded
   process, so a pid + start-time check that passes there is the right verdict, and the check is not built to close the
   window; whether sysinfo still lists a terminated Windows process whose pipe handle is open is unmeasured (research.md
   Open questions) — P4 names the window as unclosed or plans its measurement. The CARRY's mechanism text, kept
   verbatim: "why the pipe outlives the observed exit is not established" [inferred: not re-derived — a Windows-only
   timing this host cannot reach; it stays the CARRY's statement, never this chunk's].

3. CARRY (chunk 2026-10-04-confirmed-send-with-cl-1-records; the founder's ruling, live, 2026-10-04, the fourth dated
   gap): CLI `viola send` writes its `send` frame after a liveness-only pre-check (snapshot pid + start time alive,
   heartbeat live, `endpoint` present), no server identity check — removed here (security-plan IPC client-side server
   verification row; §Anti-Patterns Authentication).

4. CARRY (chunk 2026-10-04-wait-and-last; the fifth dated gap): `viola wait` / `viola last`, the same pre-check —
   removed here with `send`'s.

   after the same pre-check, and `viola hook pre-tool-use|permission-request` writing `hook.dialog` after only its
   payload shape check — removed here with `send`'s.

6. CARRY (chunk 2026-10-04-the-wheel; the founder's ruling F-W1, the seventh dated gap): `viola pause` / `viola release`
   after the same pre-check — removed here with `send`'s.

7. CARRY (chunk 2026-10-10-self-healing-state, the operator's direction at its wrap,
   `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-10-self-healing-state/inputs/I4-relay-1.md.txt`): what a client's pre-check does with an
   unreadable or newer `snapshot.json` is undecided and unchanged — `read_snapshot` reads either as absent, so
   `live_endpoint` finds no endpoint and the verb exits 21; the classified read and the log replay stand as library
   code no client calls. "A client that connected on a replayed endpoint and a heartbeat alone would change the dated
   pre-check's outcome: a boundary matter, the founder's to rule before this entry plans it." → **held**: this chunk
   keeps today's outcome (unreadable or newer reads as absent, exit 21 / fail open) unless the founder's own live word
   rules otherwise; the plan goes up to it behind a stop rule and the fork is raised at P4 as his, never leaned.

8. CARRY (chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list, the review card the founder approved,
   `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list/inputs/I3-relay-3.md.txt` and
   `…/inputs/I8-board-card-owners.md.txt`): the board landed its half of the self-healing carry; the five other
   snapshot readers (`src/cmd/client.rs`, `run`'s collision check, `src/cmd/hook.rs` twice,
   `src/cmd/hook/statusline.rs`) still call `read_snapshot` and take no replay, which keeps
   `verification-matrix.json#v1-41` open and E5's steps 1–3 unbuilt. [premise-corrected: `src/cmd/client.rs` holds no
   `read_snapshot(` call at HEAD (`grep -c`, 0) — the CLI verbs' snapshot read moved to
   `viola_state::liveness::live_endpoint` (`crates/viola-state/src/liveness.rs:75`) at chunk
   2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers; under `src/` four product callers remain (`hook.rs:246`, `hook.rs:494`,
   `statusline.rs:142`, `run.rs:379`), research.md Sweeps.] Those readers' move to the classified read is owed here
   and is bound to item 7's hold — moving a client to the replay is the change item 7 names.

9. CARRY (chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers, its P5 card's row 4,
   `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers/inputs/I3-relay-3.md.txt`; the founder's own answer to its P4
   fork Q1, `…/inputs/I2-relay-2.md.txt`): the eighth dated gap — `viola mcp`'s `send` / `wait` / `last` / `answer`

title: CI since the last wrap (Setup 5a, `ci-no-marker.json` in the run dir)

data.head: ## CI since the last wrap (Setup 5a, `ci-no-marker.json` in the run dir)

body: Every sha from the last wrap's flip (`6bdfdda8`) through HEAD (`6bdfdda8`), newest first:

- `6bdfdda8` in progress · 15/15 checks · ci#40283761039 in_progress, its oldest open check `test (windows-2025)` at
  185 s — **CI 6bdfdda8: verdict not yet available**, never read as green; no wall-clock yet. The pre-CI commit under it
  (`948f7f01`) read green at ci#40278510123 (the handoff).

_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-10-26-tokio-rustsec-2026-0386-lock-bump · **Version:** viola-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-26T05:58Z
- **Starts from:** HEAD `b1249fb1a87bed38d167637c2d45e19508db5c3f` (the 2026-10-25-windows-endpoint-admission wrap)
- **Mode:** an ordinary chunk, no forced sample at P2 (`inputs#I1`); the cascade drew `sample: no`

Move the workspace's tokio from 1.53.1 to 1.53.3, the first release RUSTSEC-2026-0386 lists as patched on the 1.53 line
(`inputs#I2`), so `cargo deny check`'s advisories family stops failing and CI's `supply-chain` job reads green again.
The bump closes the CARRY this entry holds: since the 2026-10-20 wrap every CI run has failed `supply-chain` alone, last
at ci#40257114709 on `b1249fb1` (per security-plan §Dependency Security, the `deps-supply-chain` group naming this
entry as owner).

The change is two files and no source. The workspace pins tokio exactly (`Cargo.toml:242`, `=1.53.1`), so the pin moves
with the lock, keeping the `=` form and `default-features = false` (per architecture §Infrastructure Patterns → Build
system; security-plan §Dependency Security, Pinning). Research measured the whole move in a scratch worktree of HEAD:
the lock changes only the `tokio` entry's `version` and `checksum`, and every supply-chain step, the lint gate and the
sync-crate tokio bans pass on it (research.md, Patterns detected). RUSTSEC-2017-0008 stays the only advisory ignore,
and no policy file changes (per security-plan §Dependency Security, `deny.toml` additions).

Tokio stays where it is built today: `viola-mcp` (`rt`), `viola-channel`'s optional `tokio` feature (`io-util`, dev
`rt`) and the test-only `viola-e2e` (`rt` + `process`) (per architecture §Established Decisions → [Concurrency /
Backend Framework] KEYSTONE and [Module Boundaries]). The 1.53.2 and 1.53.3 fixes that touch code viola runs
(`DuplexStream` wakers, `current_thread` paused time, the Windows child-handle wait, the blocking-pool mutex,
`inputs#I4`) are witnessed by the Tokio-bearing suites: `crates/viola-mcp/tests/handlers.rs`,
`crates/viola-e2e/tests/mcp_tools.rs` and the `viola-channel` `tokio_client` units. They run on Linux in `pre-push`'s
coverage run and on every OS in CI's `test` row (per test-plan §5, §6, §9).

1. **Move the pin.** In `Cargo.toml` `[workspace.dependencies]`, change line 242 from
   `tokio = { version = "=1.53.1", default-features = false }` to
   `tokio = { version = "=1.53.3", default-features = false }`. Keep the comment on lines 240–241 as it stands. No crate
   manifest changes: the three consumers take `workspace = true` with their own features (research.md, Files
   inspected).

2. **Move the lock through cargo.** Run `cargo update -p tokio --precise 1.53.3` once, from the project root. The
   expected result, measured at P3 (research.md, Patterns detected): exit 0, one `Updating tokio v1.53.1 -> v1.53.3`
   line, and a `Cargo.lock` diff that is the `tokio` entry's `version` and `checksum` lines and nothing else. Never
   edit `Cargo.lock` by hand. Never run a broad `cargo update` (§Constraints).

3. **Read the delta before the gates.** Gate entries 6–8 (`## Test Commands`, the pin, the lock version, and the
   lock-delta count of 4) must read green before any later entry is fired. A lock diff with more than the four lines
   means cargo moved something else: stop and record it. It is outside this plan's write set (the guard entry reads it
   too).

4. **Fire the block** in order (`gate.py run --plan … `). The `/tmp` reading comes first, before the stamped-home entries
   (the smoke session, `pre-push`), per the standing word (`inputs#I1`). No source change is expected anywhere. If clippy
   or a suite turns red on the new tokio, its cause is fixed inside this chunk (tests standing S3, zero flakiness). Any
   such fix enters the write set as a recorded deviation and is never silenced with an `#[allow]` (§Constraints).

5. **Operator pass** (`.claude/rules/ci.md` §The operator pass): `pre-push` again, the hygiene entry, the pre-CI commit
   `chore(2026-10-26-tokio-rustsec-2026-0386-lock-bump): operator pre-CI commit, for the run this chunk's verdict reads`,
   the guarded push, then the full-row CI read. This is the first CI run since 2026-10-20 on which `supply-chain` gets
   past its first step. Its four later steps (`Fuzz lockfile audit`, `Tokio ban per sync crate (sole root)`,
   `Ban probes`, `Workflow lint (zizmor)`) are read on CI here for the first time since then (scope.md, CI since the
   last wrap). A red among them is this chunk's to fix with a fix commit on top.
- none
- `Cargo.toml` — line 242, the `[workspace.dependencies]` tokio pin `=1.53.1` → `=1.53.3` (step 1)
- `Cargo.lock` — the `tokio` entry's `version` and `checksum`, written by `cargo update -p tokio --precise 1.53.3` (step 2)

No live leg runs in this chunk. The smoke session (boot, status, cleanup) is the project's standing boot check; the
`viola run` path it boots holds no tokio, and it stays in for parity with the last chunk's block. The CI full-row read
asserts green: once the lock has moved, every check of the row, `supply-chain` included, is this chunk's to read
green. The diff is not OS-conditional (no `cfg` site changes). tokio's own Windows and macOS paths (`windows-sys`, the
1.53.2 Windows child-handle fix, `inputs#I4`) are witnessed by CI's `test (windows-2025)` and `test (macos-latest)` legs
in the full row.

body:
- (security) `verification-matrix.json#v1-46` — every external reader is size-capped, depth-limited and closed-typed,
  names are validated before any path join, the paste rule holds client-side and authoritatively in the wrapper, and
  a terminal-parser panic degrades to `input-not-ready` without harming passthrough, its resume-cursor clause out of
  scope per its notes (the founder's ruling of 2026-10-16), proved by `tests/contract_bounded_readers.rs` green under
  `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --e2e --filter 'binary(contract_bounded_readers)'`, with every boundary row's
  named witness green in the gate block (per security-plan §Input Validation; test-plan §11 Unit)

- (security) A `viola mcp` stdin line of more than `MAX_FRAME` bytes, its `\n` counted, passes no byte to rmcp and
  ends the session after the lines before it are answered: exit 0, stderr empty, stdout only the earlier frames, one
  `parse-rejected{parser:"mcp-stdin", detail:"oversize", count:1}` in `mcp.ndjson` holding no byte of the line
  (`mcp_tools_a_line_past_max_frame_ends_the_session_with_one_line`; the step-2 child case) (per security-plan §Input
  Validation, Constants; obs-plan §8 PII Scrubbing)

- (security) A line of exactly `MAX_FRAME` bytes with its `\n`, and of `MAX_FRAME − 1`, passes whole; one of
  `MAX_FRAME + 1` is cut, across any split of reads (the `stdin::tests` cases) (per architecture §Standard Contracts,
  Wrapper channel frames)

- (security) `replace_private_shared` reads at most `bytes.len() + 1` bytes of its target and its outcome is the
  whole-file compare's for an equal, a longer, a shorter and a different target
  (`replace_private_shared_reads_no_more_than_one_byte_past_the_bytes` and the two existing cases) (per security-plan
  §Input Validation, Constants)

- (security) `deny.toml` bans serde_json's `unbounded_depth`, `cargo deny check` reads clean, and
  `bash scripts/deny-probes.sh` ends `deny-probes: 14/14 banned, control clean` (per security-plan §Security
  Anti-Patterns › Input; §Dependencies)

- (security) The census reads every product reader call bounded in its own statement or named in `EXCEPTIONS`, and
  its self-check reads an unbounded planted read as a hit (`product_readers_are_each_bounded_or_named`,

title: Scope — Bounded inputs at every boundary

data.head: # Scope — Bounded inputs at every boundary

body:
**Marker:** `2026-10-27-bounded-inputs-at-every-boundary` · **Version:** viola-0.1.0 · **Epoch:** Epoch 6 — Security hardening
**Working entry (verbatim title + hint):** Bounded inputs at every boundary — size caps, depth limits, closed types,
names validated before path joins, paste rule client and wrapper side

Every input that crosses into a `viola` process from outside it is bounded and validated where it enters: a reader of
an external byte stream or file is size-capped before it buffers, a JSON parse runs at serde_json's default depth, a
decision read from outside is a closed type, a name reaches no path join unvalidated, and the paste rule holds on the
client side and authoritatively in the wrapper. The chunk makes that property hold at every boundary and proves it,
so that the boundary set is one a reader can enumerate and check, not a set of separate chunks' local claims.

- **Size caps** — every external reader (stdin of `hook` and `mcp`, channel frames on both sides, the child's PTY
  output into the vt100 feed, `claude agents --json` and `claude --version` output, the `--file` / stdin text of
  `send`, every file read under the home or the user's `~/.claude` — `config.json`, `snapshot.json`,
  `events.ndjson`, `budget.json`, `ledger/stamps.json`, `statusline-source.json`, `settings.json` — and the status
  line command's stdout) reads through `Read::take(MAX_FRAME)` (or the documented `MAX_FRAME + 1` over-size form)
  before it buffers; a reader found without one is bounded. [premise-corrected: the product census (research.md
  §Sweeps) reads 24 of these sites through `take(…)` already; two readers have no bound — `viola mcp`'s stdin,
  read by rmcp 3.4.1's `AsyncRwTransport::receive` with an unbounded `read_until` (`inputs#I2`), and
  `replace_private_shared`'s whole-file compare read of a plugin file or ConPTY companion under the home
  (`crates/viola-state/src/fs.rs:354`) — and the chunk bounds both; the process's own executable
  (`checked_exe`, `pin_exe`) is read whole and is no external input]

- **Depth limits** — every serde_json parse of external bytes runs at the default recursion limit; no
  `unbounded_depth` anywhere in the product graph. [verified: 0 hits for `unbounded_depth` or
  `disable_recursion_limit` in any manifest or product source; `Cargo.lock` records no features, so no gate holds
  the absence today — the chunk adds the `deny.toml` feature ban and its probe]

- **Closed types** — every decision read from an external input (a hook event kind, a dialog decision, a channel
  method and its params, an MCP tool argument, a config value, a `claude agents --json` row's status) is a closed
  enum or a validated newtype, an unknown value refused or skipped and counted as its format's rule says, never
  passed through as a free string into a decision. [verified: the closed shapes stand as landed — `HookEvent`,
  `DialogKind`, the per-kind `response` enums, `dialog_id` `u64`, the channel params checks, the MCP handlers'
  raw-argument re-validation, `Percent` / `DialogHold`, `AgentsFailure` (the security and arch extracts; the
  history files' landings); the chunk names each in its enumeration and changes none]

- **Names before path joins** — every name that reaches a path join (`instances/<name>`, a `VIOLA_NAME`, a CLI
  positional, a channel or MCP `name` / `driver` / `driven`, a revive `--id`, a pinned key) passes
  `ViolaName::try_new` (or its own closed-shape validator) first. [verified: every product join of
  `instances/<name>` takes a `ViolaName` (research.md §Sweeps); the session id passes `is_session_id`, the pinned
  key comes from `pin_key`, the hook's `VIOLA_DIR` from `instance_of`]

- **Paste rule both sides** — `validate_paste_text` runs in the client before any frame (CLI `send`, MCP `send`) and
  authoritatively in the wrapper before the first wheel read; the refusal is `not-delivered` / `control-character`
  (and `empty-text` for an empty typed text), never a strip. [verified: `validate_paste_text` has six product
  callers — CLI `send`, CLI `answer`, MCP `send`, MCP `answer` and the wrapper's `send` and `answer` (code-graph,
  research.md §Graph impact); landed at chunk 2026-10-04-confirmed-send-with-cl-1-records]

- **Terminal-parser panic** — a panic in the vt100 screen model degrades readiness to `input-not-ready` without
  harming passthrough of the child's bytes to the human's terminal. [verified, one half unwitnessed:

  `tests/chaos_feed_panic.rs` witnesses the degrade and a key reaching the child, but asserts nothing about the
  child's output reaching the outer terminal after the panic — the chunk adds that half]

  of external readers named, each with its cap, depth and type rule, so a new reader without a bound is visible.

  and `scan_patterns.rs` are the source-walking precedents, neither about readers)]

data.head: # Plan — 2026-10-27-pinned-copy-race-and-reproducible-builds: "Pinned copy race and reproducible builds"

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-10-27-pinned-copy-race-and-reproducible-builds · **Version:** viola-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-27T01:51:52Z
- **Base:** HEAD `99977116182bae621cdbe494d0f09e46e94e29f1` (the last wrap's commit) · run dir `.andromeda/runs/2026-10-27T00-24-41-phase/`

Close the `pin_exe` first-start race on a fresh home: the absent copy of `bin/<key>/viola(.exe)` is placed once, already
closed, and never replaced under a concurrent first start, so no agent's hook spawn of the pinned path can fail while
another start's write of it is in flight. Research re-derived the folded hypothesis on both halves: viola's
`replace_private_retrying` renames through `NamedTempFile::persist` while it still holds the temp file's write handle
(`crates/viola-state/src/fs.rs:288–303`), and an exec racing that window fails `ETXTBSY` on the Linux dev host
(scratch control: 4059 of 16283 open-handle execs failed, 0 of 13066 with the handle closed first; research.md,
Mechanism re-derivation). The fix lands in `viola_state` (a sibling placement helper in `fs.rs`, used by `pin_bytes`'s
absent-copy arm), never at a call site, keeps hash-before-reuse whole and the start order unchanged (per architecture
§Established Decisions [Snapshot writer] + security-plan §Data Protection, code-bearing artefacts).

Measure whether a rebuild of one tree can read as another binary: two clean release builds of one tree, through
`scripts/release-check.sh`'s build, compared by file and by every section, with two controls; a difference is recorded
as not explained unless its cause is measured, and acting on it is the founder's (the CARRY; verification-harness.md
2026-10-09).

Close the two reds of `ci#40425866096` on `99977116`, the operator having asked both be given a basis and an owner
(`inputs#I2`): Path 1's timeout (owned here — it drives `pin_bytes`'s re-hash and absent-copy arm; its cause a
two-thirds use of its 20 s kill line under a runner-wide slow tail, not the race: research.md, CI reds) by measured
phases and removed slow work, never a raised bound; and the Windows plain-home oracle at `strict.rs:778` (folded here
on the operator's word, `inputs#I4`, delegate overseer1, PROVISIONAL) by reading the inherited write grant by its
right, not one SID.

2. **The fake agent reads its spawn's error.** In `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs` `run_receipted`, a spawn of an
   absolute `command` that fails records the error's raw OS code as `spawn_os_error` (an integer) beside `ran:false`;
   a spawn that succeeds is unchanged, and so is the non-absolute arm. Keeps tests S1, S9 (test-plan §7 fake agent
   receipt kinds; `fake_agent_*` drift replays unaffected — the field appears only on a failed spawn).

3. **The product race read red at the base, with its errno.** Write `evidence/repro-unstamped.py` (runs from the root
   `.`; scratch through `mktemp -d` with a `trap`; spawns `viola-harness` from `target/harness/debug` directly, no
   shell, never a piped `boot`, verification-harness.md 2026-09-25) and run it on the tree as step 2 left it (the pin
   unchanged): 4 rounds × 6 concurrent `boot --unstamped` sessions of the default two-instance pair, each fake agent
   given `--receipt`, each session cleaned up; then the same rounds with `--instance builder` alone (the control).
   Record per input: sessions, failed boots and their closed reasons, each failed instance's SessionStart `hook`
   receipt (`ran`, `spawn_os_error`), in `evidence/race-before.md`. Stop rule S1: the two-instance input reads 0 failed
   of 24 → record "not reproduced on this rig" with the backing reading, claim no product red, and continue: step 5's
   forced window is the two-sided proof either way.

4. **The no-clobber placement.** In `crates/viola-state/src/fs.rs` add `place_private_new(path, bytes, mode) ->
   Result<Placed, StateError>` with `enum Placed { Written, Present }`: a temp file beside `path`
   (`NamedTempFile::new_in(parent)`), its mode set (`restrict`) before any byte, the bytes written and `sync_all`ed,
   the handle CLOSED (`into_temp_path`), then `TempPath::persist_noclobber(path)`; a name already present
   (`AlreadyExists`) is `Ok(Placed::Present)` with the target untouched and the temp path removed; any other failure an
   error with the target as it was. The body is `place_private_new_with(path, bytes, mode, placed: &mut dyn FnMut(&Path))`,
   private, which calls `placed(path)` right after a `Written` placement and before it returns (the forced-window hook;
   `place_private_new` passes a no-op). No retry: a no-clobber placement has no reader-refusal loop. Doc comment: the
   pinned copy's absent-copy write; `replace_private` and `replace_private_shared` keep every other replaced file.
   Keeps arch S7, security S3–S4 (no new error variant — `StateError` as is).

5. **Its unit cases** (inline `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in `fs.rs`; keeps tests S1, S4, S5):
   - `place_private_new_places_the_bytes_once_at_the_mode_and_leaves_no_temp` — `Written`, the bytes read back, Unix
     mode 0700 for `DIR_MODE` and 0600 for `FILE_MODE`, the parent directory listing holding the target alone;
   - `place_private_new_over_a_present_name_is_present_and_leaves_it` — a target already holding other bytes:
     `Present`, the target byte-identical, no temp left;
   - `place_private_new_under_a_missing_dir_fails` — the error, nothing created;
   - `place_private_new_placed_copy_execs_at_once` (`cfg(unix)`; the forced window, testing.md 2026-09-27): the bytes
     of a host executable (`true` from `/usr/bin` or `/bin`, read whole), placed at 0700 through `place_private_new_with`
     whose hook spawns the placed path directly and records the spawn's result; asserts the spawn ran (exit 0, no
     error). Remove-the-guard run (testing.md 2026-09-25): neutralise the guard inside `place_private_new_with` — the
     placement made with the write handle still open (`NamedTempFile::persist_noclobber`, the handle dropped after the
     hook) — read the case red with its panic line naming the spawn error (`ETXTBSY`, raw 26, on the Linux dev host),
     restore, read it green; both readings in `evidence/red-green.md`. macOS gives no `ETXTBSY` (no red leg there —
     stated in the case's doc comment); the case's green leg runs on `ubuntu-latest` and `macos-latest`.
   - `place_private_new_placed_copy_runs_at_once` (`cfg(windows)`): the same with the bytes of
     `%SystemRoot%\System32\whoami.exe`, stdout and stderr null; green on `windows-2025` only, its red leg unmeasured
     (no Windows host; stated in its doc comment).

6. **`pin_bytes` through it.** In `crates/viola-state/src/pin.rs` the `NotFound` arm calls a new private
   `place_absent(path, bytes, hash) -> Result<(), PinError>`: `place_private_new(path, bytes, DIR_MODE)` → `Written` is
   `Ok`; `Present` (a concurrent start placed it first) → `file_key(path)` re-hashes it — equal → `Ok`, different →
   `PinError::HashMismatch`, the file left as found. `pin_exe` delegates unchanged; `pin_companions` unchanged. The
   module doc names the no-clobber placement. Unit cases (inline): `place_absent_over_a_copy_another_start_placed`, a
   labelled rstest table that calls `place_absent` on a path already holding (a) the same bytes → `Ok`, the file
   byte-identical, and (b) other bytes → `HashMismatch`, the file byte-identical; and `place_absent_on_a_free_path_writes_the_copy`
   → `Ok`, the bytes at the path, 0700 on Unix. The four existing `pin_exe_*` cases stay green. Keeps tests S5,
   security S3.

7. **Path 7 back to two instances.** In `crates/viola-e2e/tests/mcp_tools.rs` `mcp_tools_path7_unverified_cli_answer`
   boots `SessionOptions { unstamped: true, ..SessionOptions::default() }` (the default `overseer` + `builder` pair),
   the two-line race comment removed: the harness `boot`'s per-instance readiness (`start_records`, `<name>:events`) is
   then the regression check that two first starts on a fresh home both land their `session-start`, on all three CI
   OSes. `mcp_recorded_exchange.rs` keeps `builder` alone (no race reason). Keeps tests S3, S4, S8.

8. **The product race read clean, two-sided.** Run step 3's script again on the tree as steps 4–7 left it, both
   inputs, same rounds; record in `evidence/race-after.md` beside step 3's table. The verdict is the pair: two-instance
   failures before (with their errno) → 0 of 24 after, the single-instance control 0 of 24 on both sides.

9. **Measurement B: two clean release builds of one tree.** Write `evidence/repro-builds.sh` (runs from the root `.`;
   scratch through `mktemp -d` outside the tree with a `trap`) and run it once on the tree as step 8 left it: twice,
   `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<scratch>/target bash scripts/release-check.sh` (last line `release-check: viola only`) into a
   `<scratch>/target` the script itself makes empty before each build (made by `mkdir`, the first build's removed by
   the script before the second — the one path it removes is one it made; `target/release-check/` is never cleaned or
   touched), the built `<scratch>/target/release/viola` copied to `<scratch>/build-1` / `build-2` after each, both
   builds at the one same target path so the comparison varies nothing but the build; then for the two copies: sha256
   and size; `readelf -S` section lists; every
   section's sha256 through `objcopy -O binary --only-section=<name>` (every section `readelf -S` names, the six loaded
   sections of the CARRY among them), `readelf -n`'s build-id note, and a count of differing `strings` lines; two
   controls through the same script (a copy against itself: 0 unequal; a copy against another host program: all
   unequal). Record in `evidence/reproducible-builds.md` with times and the toolchain; a difference is recorded by
   section and note, its cause "not explained" unless measured. No product or build change rests on it: acting on it is
   the founder's (Expected amendments below; the handoff carries it). Keeps arch S3 (the scratch outside the tree, no
   new registered path), S6.

10. **Red 1: Path 1's phases measured, then its slow work removed.** Measure Path 1's per-step wall times on the dev
    host: five firings of `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --e2e --filter 'binary(path1_run_start)'` with a temporary
    per-step timing record the test appends to a file outside its home (each step's start and end through
    `std::time::Instant`, a measurement only, never a wait or verdict), and the JUnit time of each firing; record in
    `evidence/path1-phases.md` beside the CI readings (13.468 s green `ci#40403389629`, 20.089 s red `ci#40425866096`,
    the red's last line at step 5, research.md). Name the step(s) whose work dominates. Remove that slow work inside
    `tests/path1_run_start.rs` without changing what Path 1 asserts (test-plan §6 Path 1 steps 1–6; the tamper still one
    flipped byte and an exit-1 `pinned-hash-mismatch`, step 6 still the re-copy equal to the built `viola`), its kill
    line unchanged (`.config/nextest.toml` untouched, testing.md 2026-09-28); remove the timing record; take the same
    five readings after. Stop rule S2: the phases name no step whose work can be removed without changing Path 1's
    asserted contract (the cost lies in the `stamped_home` verify or a product start alone) → stop, record the readings,
    and report to the operator with them; no bound moves and no step is cut on this plan's word.

11. **Red 2: the plain-home oracle by its right.** In `crates/viola-state/src/strict.rs`
    `strict_instance_refuses_a_plain_home_made_before_viola_and_names_the_entry`, the second assertion reads that some
    inherited, untrusted ACE of the plain home carries a write right (`ace.mask & WRITE_RIGHTS != 0`, inherited, not
    `trusted_sid`), whichever SID holds it, the failure message still printing every ACE; and add its control in the same
    case: the same filter over a home `instance_tree()` makes (the protected DACL) reads empty, so the oracle cannot pass
    vacuously. The doc comment names both runner readings (Users write on `ci#40403389629`'s host, Authenticated Users
    on `ci#40425866096`'s, image `windows-2025-vs2026` 20261021.278.1). Green on `windows-2025` only (a `cfg(windows)`
    module); its red-before is `ci#40425866096` itself. Keeps tests S8.

12. **Re-read the unchanged rules and run the block.** Fire the whole `[[gate]]` block (below); the operator pass
    fires the operator entries. The OS-sensitive cases and their witnesses are named in the `ci.py` entry's note.

- `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-27-pinned-copy-race-and-reproducible-builds/evidence/` — `preconditions.md`, `repro-unstamped.py`, `race-before.md`, `race-after.md`, `red-green.md`, `repro-builds.sh`, `reproducible-builds.md`, `path1-phases.md` and the operator entries' records
- `crates/viola-state/src/fs.rs` — `place_private_new` / `place_private_new_with` / `Placed`, and their unit cases (steps 4–5)
- `crates/viola-state/src/pin.rs` — `pin_bytes`'s absent-copy arm through the placement; the `Present` arm's re-hash; its unit cases (step 6)
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs` — `spawn_os_error` on a failed hook spawn's receipt (step 2)
- `crates/viola-e2e/tests/mcp_tools.rs` — Path 7 on the default pair, the race comment removed (step 7)
- `tests/path1_run_start.rs` — the slow work its measured phases name removed (step 10, under stop rule S2)
- `crates/viola-state/src/strict.rs` — the plain-home oracle by its right, with its control (step 11)

Graph impact (research.md §Graph impact): `pin_bytes` has two callers, `pin_exe` @ `crates/viola-state/src/pin.rs:79`
and `pin_and_plugin` @ `src/cmd/run.rs:451`; `pin_exe`'s product caller is `measure` @ `src/cmd/verify.rs:171`; no
signature changes, so neither call site changes. `replace_private_shared` keeps its two other product callers
(`pin_and_plugin` @ `src/cmd/run.rs:463`, the plugin files; `pin_companions` @ `crates/viola-state/src/pin.rs:187`).

The gates /implement runs. Steps 3, 8, 9 and 10's readings are attended measurements outside this block (their
records in `evidence/`, read by the report, not re-run by the wrap). Live leg: none — no real `claude` is started.
The harness smoke boots one unstamped `builder` session as the boot path's smoke.
