# Founder forks — chunk 2026-10-19-newer-claude-cli-rows, phase P4 (away form)

Written 2026-10-19 by `/andromeda-phase` P4 while the founder is away (`inputs#I2`). The step stops here, and no
`plan.md` is written until his answer arrives. Live `claude` starts are his cap, given per chunk (`inputs#I1` item 2),
and no live start runs before his word.

## What P3 found (the context for both forks)

- **The four 2.1.302 failures are one stop, not four.** Run B's 2.1.302 transcript holds only the probe prompt and
  the long paste (`inputs#I3` R1). After the long paste's turn, verify's `box_wait` waited its full 120 s for the
  input-box literal and never saw it (`src/cmd/verify/typed.rs:402`). So the tag-like, newline, `/compact` and
  `/clear` pastes were never typed.
  - `tag-escaping` and `paste-newline` find no capture.
  - `local-command-clear` and `local-command-compact` cannot pass without those two captures, because they are
    anchored on them.
  - On 2.1.296 the same sequence ran its five added pastes, long paste to `/clear`, in 16 s (`inputs#I3` R2).
- **The cause, read from the CLI bundle and not yet from a live screen.** The input-box literal is `"for agents"`,
  the footer hint (`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/screen.rs:39`). 2.1.296 always draws it. 2.1.302 hides it once
  `agentsHintExpired` is set: a 10 s value tied to the session's attached clients (`inputs#I3` R4). What attaches in
  Run B is unmeasured. The nearest candidate is Run B's own `claude agents --json` read.
- **It reaches the product.** `run`'s pre-send readiness gate waits for the same literal on a verified CLI
  (`src/run/gate.rs:508`). A 2.1.302 stamped verified with today's literal would refuse a driver's `send`
  `input-not-ready` once the hint is gone. The fix is a measured literal the 2.1.302 resting input box keeps, added
  to the compiled set beside `"for agents"`, and recorded so CI's fake agent replays it.
- **Planned to complete now, with no live start:**
  - the fake agent reproduces the 2.1.302 resting footer, and a `cli_verify` case reads exactly the overseer's
    `stamped …  20 pass  4 fail` with the same four rows red;
  - the `input-box-signature` row also reads a screen past the hint's expiry, so it can no longer pass by timing;
  - a `send` gate case covers that screen;
  - the macOS readiness flake is measured and fixed. The two failing wrappers stalled inside `run.start` before the
    version gate (`inputs#I3` R5). Its phase is measured on `macos-latest` by timing-only pushes before any change.

## Fork 1 — the live round's start cap (his cap)

Each `viola verify` is six starts (Runs A–E plus the print probe). Every round runs under a `target/e2e-home/…` home
and never stamps `~/.viola` (test-plan §3 `run --local-live`). The overseer's own home and his pin to 2.1.296 are his
to move after the wrap. PATH `claude` is 2.1.302; the rig puts that install first and reads `claude --version` by
path before its first start.

1. **19 starts: one screen measurement (1), one record round, one `--local-live`, one re-run held for a red (Recommended)**
   - 1 — the 2.1.302 screen measurement of Fork 2 (option 1).
   - 6 — `viola verify --home <tmpfs home> --record` on 2.1.302 after the literal is added. It stamps 24/0 and
     writes `fixtures/claude/2.1.302/`, which CI then replays.
   - 6 — `scripts/agent-run.sh run --local-live` on 2.1.302: the harness's own verdict, `local-live` passed 1.
   - 6 — held, spent only if the record round reads red: one re-run after a fix, as the compact chunk's cap allowed.

   Why it wins: one start measures the cause before any code changes, one round produces the fixtures CI needs, and
   the harness witnesses it. 2.1.296 needs no live re-run: its bundle draws the hint unconditionally (`inputs#I3` R4)
   and its 24/24 stamp stands in the overseer's home. The trade-off: no live reading on 2.1.296 after the change.
2. **25 starts: option 1 plus a 2.1.296 no-regress verify (6)** — the version the overseer drives on today, read live
   against the changed literal set. It costs six more starts for a version whose footer the bundle already shows
   unchanged.
3. **7 starts: the measurement (1) and the record round (6) only** — no `--local-live` witness and no re-run held.
   The record round's own `stamped 2.1.302  24 pass  0 fail` is the only live verdict, and any red halts the chunk
   for a new word.

## Fork 2 — how the 2.1.302 resting input box is measured (a boundary: "Boundary widening", `.andromeda/playbook.md`)

The literal must be measured on the installed CLI. verify keeps only signature rows, and none of today's literals is
on the 2.1.302 screen once the hint is gone. A scratch read outside `viola verify` needs his fresh ruling: the
security history records the 2026-10-07 scratch answers as spent (`.andromeda/security-plan-amendments.md`, chunk
2026-10-07-live-rows-and-paste-shapes-on-the-dev-host).

1. **One scratch measurement start, footer rows only (Recommended)**
   - One `viola run` start of 2.1.302 under a tmpfs `--home`, its cwd a scratch dir outside the work tree, behind an
     outer PTY (80×24). No key is typed, and the start is killed at the end.
   - At ~2 s, one `viola list` against that home, its `claude agents --json` read being the suspected attach.
   - At ~15 s and ~25 s, the bottom three screen rows written to the chunk's `evidence/`. Only those footer rows are
     written, scrubbed of the home and user word, and never the CLI's text above them.
   - It counts as start 1 of Fork 1.

   Why it wins: it measures both the literal to add and whether a driver's `viola list` alone expires the hint in a
   product session (the exposure of `send`), for one start. The trade-off: one new crossing, footer rows of the live
   CLI screen into `evidence/`, which the wrap escalates as a boundary widening with his answer cited.
2. **No scratch read: take the literal from the bundle's render code** — no new crossing. The record round's
   `input-box-signature` row validates the guess. A wrong guess costs a six-start re-run, and whether `viola list`
   expires the hint stays unmeasured.

## The overseer's delegate direction, while he is away (2026-10-19T23:31:00Z) — PROVISIONAL, not his answer

- **Neither fork is answered.** The live-start cap and the Fork 2 crossing are his alone, and both are HELD for his own
  word (a boundary widening is never settled by a delegate). His answer, when it comes, goes under "His answer" below.
- **To keep the work moving meanwhile:** write `plan.md` with the live round (Fork 1) and the screen measurement
  (Fork 2) as the chunk's GATED CRITERION. Its block is "the founder's own word on the live-start cap and on Fork 2
  (`.andromeda/runs/2026-10-19T23-10-05-phase/founder-forks.md`)". Every item that needs no live start is planned to
  complete now: the fake agent's 2.1.302 resting footer, the `cli_verify` 20/4 case, the `input-box-signature` reading
  past the hint's expiry, the `send` gate case, and the macOS readiness flake. A cap whose acceptance rests on the live
  round is claimed gated. Implement runs the non-live work tonight. If his word has not come by the wrap, the wrap takes
  the gated arm, and his word then runs the gated part.
- **Authority:** the Viola overseer as the founder's delegate. PROVISIONAL, for his morning batch.

# The macOS readiness flake — phase measurement (plan steps 6–7)

Written by /implement (run dir `.andromeda/runs/2026-10-19T23-48-08-implement/`). The operator pass's CI runs append
below.

## 6(a) — the stall report, installed

`tests/support/home.rs` `Wrapper::wait_ready`: at the `WITHIN` deadline, just before the `wrapper <name> not ready`
panic, `note_stall` adds these lines to the watch report:
- `stall last event <event>`: the wrapper's own last `run-<name>.ndjson` event, or `none`;
- `stall pid <pid>`: the `viola` whose arguments hold the boot's fake-agent control file, found through one sysinfo
  read. When none is found the line reads `stall pid unknown`;
- on macOS, `stall sample` and then `stack <line>` for each line of `/usr/bin/sample <pid> 1 -mayDie`'s
  `Call graph:` section, at most 120 lines. The file goes under the temp dir's `viola-root-watch/`. `sample` gets 4 s
  and is killed past that (`stall sample timed out`). It is a child the test started, and it reads the task without
  signalling it;
- on Linux, `stall wchan <wchan> state <state field of /proc/<pid>/stat>`.

The report adds nothing to a passing boot: `note_stall` runs only once the deadline has passed. Nothing signals the
wrapper. `WITHIN`, the kill lines, `retries` and the thread count are unchanged.

## 6(b) — the gap from `process-start{self}` to `process-start{version-probe}`, from recorded runs

**Source:** ci#39321117796 (sha `b6ddc19856e55fd9d4083db4400a8196f24f6488`), its diagnostics artifacts, downloaded
2026-10-19 ~23:53Z:
- `diag-macos-latest` attempt 1, artifact 12219784289 (20:47:16Z);
- `diag-macos-latest` attempt 2, artifact 12221562534 (21:00:54Z);
- for the two-sided read, `diag-ubuntu-latest` 12220487228 and `diag-windows-2025` 12220391778.

- `cross_list_rows_print_escaped_in_the_captions_columns_in_every_mode`: started 20:44:50.770Z, 16.835 s.

Both watch reports read in full `starts w0 c0 r0 snapshot false beat false` / `starts w1 c0 r0 snapshot false beat
false`. So each wrapper's `process-start{self}` was seen, and no `claude-child` start ever followed it.

**Reader:** `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-19-newer-claude-cli-rows/macos-run-start.py`, run with `python3 -I`, one
`<label>=<dir>` per extracted artifact. Its output, verbatim, except that only the rows with a gap over 1 s and the
two `none` stalls are kept. The other `no version-probe` rows all end `last event process-exit`: those are starts the
tests refuse on purpose.

title: footer-reading.sh
body:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Plan step 8 of chunk 2026-10-19-newer-claude-cli-rows: the 2.1.302 footer reading, one live start
# (the founder's Fork 2 option 1, inputs#I6). Only the pane's bottom three rows are written, scrubbed.
set -euo pipefail

root="$(pwd -P)"
cdir="$HOME/.local/share/mise/installs/claude/2.1.302"
claude="$cdir/claude"
viola="$root/target/debug/viola"
evidence="$root/viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-19-newer-claude-cli-rows/evidence/footer-2.1.302.md"
session=vf302
user="$(id -un)"
cwd="$root/.viola-footer-$$"
base="$root/target/e2e-home/viola-footer-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
home="$base/vhome"
started=0

cleanup() {
    if [ "$started" = 1 ]; then
        tmux kill-session -t "$session" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
    for i in $(seq 1 50); do
        left=""
        for p in $(pgrep -x claude || true); do
            [ "$(readlink "/proc/$p/cwd" 2>/dev/null || true)" = "$cwd" ] && left="$left $p"
        done
        [ -z "$left" ] && break
        if [ "$i" = 30 ]; then kill $left 2>/dev/null || true; fi
        sleep 0.1
    done
    case "$cwd" in
        "$root"/.viola-footer-*) rm -rf -- "$cwd" ;;
    esac
}
trap cleanup EXIT

scrub() {
    local s="$1" p
    for p in "$(realpath -m "$home")" "$home" "$(realpath -m "$base")" "$base" "$cwd" "$root"; do
        s="${s//"$p"/<scrubbed>}"
    done
    s="${s//"$HOME"/\~}"
    s="${s//"$user"/<user>}"
    printf '%s\n' "$s"
}

footer() {
    local label="$1" at rows hint
    at="$(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
    rows="$(tmux capture-pane -p -t "$session" -S 21 -E 23)"
    hint=no
    case "$rows" in *"for agents"*) hint=yes ;; esac
    {
        printf '\n## %s — %s\n\n```text\n' "$label" "$at"
        while IFS= read -r line; do scrub "$line"; done <<<"$rows"
        printf '```\n\n`for agents` on these rows: %s\n' "$hint"
    } >>"$evidence"
}

cargo build -q
version="$("$claude" --version)"
case "$version" in
    2.1.302*) ;;
    *) echo "footer-reading: wrong claude version" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac

mkdir -m 0700 "$cwd"
mkdir -p "$base"
chmod 0700 "$base"

t0="$(date +%s)"
start_at="$(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
tmux new-session -d -s "$session" -x 80 -y 24 -c "$cwd" \
    env -u VIOLA_NAME -u VIOLA_DIR -u VIOLA_BIN PATH="$cdir:$PATH" "$viola" --home "$home" run m302 -- "$claude"
started=1

sleep 2
list_at="$(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
list_rc=0
list_out="$(env -u VIOLA_NAME -u VIOLA_DIR -u VIOLA_BIN PATH="$cdir:$PATH" "$viola" --home "$home" list --json 2>/dev/null)" || list_rc=$?
list_row="$(printf '%s' "$list_out" | python3 -c '
import json, sys
try:
    items = json.load(sys.stdin)["ok"]["items"]
except Exception:
    print("unreadable")
    sys.exit(0)
rows = [i for i in items if i.get("name") == "m302"]
print(" · ".join("{}={}".format(k, rows[0].get(k)) for k in ("wrapped", "liveness", "status")) if rows else "no m302 row")
')"

{
    printf '# Footer reading — claude 2.1.302 (plan step 8)\n\n'
    printf 'Written by `footer-reading.sh`. One `viola run` start of `%s` under a tmpfs `--home`, its cwd a fresh\n' "$version"
    printf '`.viola-footer-<pid>/` under the repository root, in a detached tmux pane 80×24, with no key typed\n'
    printf "(the founder's Fork 2 option 1, \`inputs#I6\`). Only the pane's bottom three rows are kept, scrubbed of the\n"
    printf 'home and the user word.\n\n'
    printf -- '- Start: %s.\n' "$start_at"
    printf -- '- `viola list --json` at ~2 s: %s · exit %s · the m302 row: %s.\n' "$list_at" "$list_rc" "$list_row"
} >"$evidence"

until_s() {
    local wait=$(($1 - ($(date +%s) - t0)))
    [ "$wait" -gt 0 ] && sleep "$wait"
    return 0
}

until_s 15
footer "~15 s"
until_s 25
footer "~25 s"

tmux kill-session -t "$session"
started=0
printf '\n- Killed: %s, with no key typed.\n' "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" >>"$evidence"
echo "footer-reading: written"

N=${1:-viola-builder}; skipped=0; i=0
# One waiter per builder: a newer waitm replaces an older one (duplicates were found 2026-09-25).
PIDF="$HOME/dev/projects/additional/viola-overseer/.waitm-$N.pid"
old=$(cat "$PIDF" 2>/dev/null)
if [ -n "$old" ] && [ "$old" != "$$" ] && kill -0 "$old" 2>/dev/null; then
  for c in $(ps -ef | awk -v p="$old" '$3==p{print $2}'); do kill "$c" 2>/dev/null; done; kill "$old" 2>/dev/null
  echo "[waitm: replaced older waiter pid $old]"
fi
echo $$ > "$PIDF"
while [ $i -lt 60 ]; do
  i=$((i+1))
  out=$("$V" wait "$N" --timeout 3000)
  first=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | head -1)
  body=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed '1d')
  if [ "$first" = "turn-end" ] && [ ${#body} -lt 300 ] \
     && ! printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q -E '\?|▸|[Cc]omplete|[Rr]eady|[Hh]alt|[Ee]rror|[Ff]ail|wheel'; then
    skipped=$((skipped+1)); last="$body"; continue
  fi
  # a longer turn end that only announces background work, with no question and no prompt marker
  if [ "$first" = "turn-end" ] && printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q -E '⟲|running in the background|is running\.|[Ss]till waiting on|[Ww]aiting on (the )?(last|arch|security|tests|obs|a11y|design|layouts)|detectors? (are|is) back' \
     && ! printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q -E '\?|▸|[Hh]alt|[Ee]rror|[Ff]ail|wheel'; then
    skipped=$((skipped+1)); last="$body"; continue
  fi
  echo "[skipped $skipped progress turns; last: $(printf '%s' "$last" | head -1)]"
  echo "[host] $(free -g | awk '/^Mem:/{print "mem_free=" $7 "G"}') $(df -h --output=avail $HOME/dev | tail -1 | tr -d ' ' | sed 's/^/dev_free=/')"
  printf '%s\n' "$out"
  # A dialog's preceding text is not in the builder's transcript while it is pending (the jsonl flushes only
  # after the answer), so the screen travels with the dialog.
  # An option's `preview` (a route wording, a diff) is not in `viola wait`'s print: read it from the dialog's file.
  case "$first" in question*)
    did=$(printf '%s' "$first" | sed -n 's/.*(dialog \([^)]*\)).*/\1/p')
    [ -n "$did" ] && python3 -c '
import json,sys
try: j=json.load(open(sys.argv[1],encoding="utf-8"))
except Exception as x: sys.exit(0)
for q in j.get("tool_input",{}).get("questions",[]):
    for o in q.get("options",[]):
        if o.get("preview"): print("[preview · "+o.get("label","")+"]\n"+o["preview"])
' "$HOME/.viola/sessions/$N/dialogs/$did.json" ;;
  esac
  case "$first" in question*|plan*)
    echo "[screen before the dialog]"; sh $HOME/dev/projects/additional/viola-overseer/scr.sh "$N" 60000 4000; echo ;;
  esac
  exit 0
done
echo "[waitm: 60 progress turns skipped, returning; last: $last]"

title: I5-waitlong.sh.txt
body:
#!/bin/sh
# Wait through an HOURS-LONG builder run (a mutation tier, a workflow dispatch): waitm.sh returns at once on a builder
# that idles at a turn end waiting for its own background run, and on every long progress turn (V93). This loop waits
# for the builder to LEAVE idle, then runs waitm.sh, and returns on a dialog, a hold, an exit, or a turn end at which
# the builder has no background task of its own (it then waits for the driver); a turn end with tasks still running
# is printed as one progress line and the loop goes on.
#   sh waitlong.sh [name]      run it in the background with timeout 7200000 (the harness's maximum); restart it when it
#                              ends without a report (the heartbeat does that).
V=$HOME/dev/projects/additional/viola-lab/prototype/target/debug/viola
N=${1:-viola-builder}; D=$HOME/dev/projects/additional/viola-overseer; O="$D/.waitlong-$N.out"
# The ts_ms of the newest Stop event: a wake turn shorter than one poll (a task notification answered in seconds)
# leaves idle and returns between two status reads, so a new Stop also ends the wait (2026-10-13: an implement's
# last turn at 09:36:50Z was missed for 70 minutes).
last_stop() {
  python3 - "$HOME/.viola/sessions/$N/events.ndjson" <<'PY'
import json, sys
t = '0'
try:
    for line in reversed(open(sys.argv[1], encoding='utf-8').read().splitlines()[-400:]):
        try:
            e = json.loads(line)
        except ValueError:
            continue
        if (e.get('data') or {}).get('hook_event_name') == 'Stop':
            t = str(e.get('ts_ms', 0))
            break
except OSError:
    pass
print(t)
PY
}
while :; do
  S0=$(last_stop)
  until [ "$("$V" list | awk -v n="$N" '$1==n{print $3}')" != "idle" ] || [ "$(last_stop)" != "$S0" ]; do sleep 60; done
  echo "[builder left idle at $(date -u +%FT%TZ)]"
  sh "$D/waitm.sh" "$N" > "$O" 2>&1
  # A turn end with NO background task of the builder's own is one that waits for the driver: return on it, whatever
  # its words (V103, V105: a word list passed over a review card for 21 minutes and a finished wrap for 10). The
  # Stop event carries the count; a dialog, a hold or an exit returns as before.
  BG=$(python3 - "$HOME/.viola/sessions/$N/events.ndjson" <<'PY'
import json, sys
p = sys.argv[1]
n = 'unread'
try:
    for line in reversed(open(p, encoding='utf-8').read().splitlines()[-400:]):
        try:
            d = (json.loads(line).get('data') or {})
        except ValueError:
            continue
        if d.get('hook_event_name') == 'Stop':
            n = str(len(d.get('background_tasks') or []))
            break
except OSError:
    pass
print(n)
PY
)
  if [ "$BG" = "0" ] || [ "$BG" = "unread" ] || head -c 3000 "$O" | grep -q -E '^question|^plan|^permission|^exited|^held'; then
    echo "[background tasks at the last Stop: $BG]"; cat "$O"; exit 0
  fi
  echo "[progress turn at $(date -u +%FT%TZ), $BG background task(s): $(sed -n '4p' "$O" | cut -c1-200)]"
  sleep 30
done

title: I9-driving-guide.md.txt
body:
# Driving the builder with the viola prototype

How this overseer operates a builder session through the viola prototype. It is written for the next window
after a `/clear` or a compact. Conventions only: where the work stands lives in `.claude/session-handoff.md`.

## The pieces

- **Binary:** `~/dev/projects/additional/viola-lab/prototype/target/debug/viola` (Linux since 2026-10-03). It is not on PATH:
  set `V=$HOME/dev/projects/additional/viola-lab/prototype/target/debug/viola`.
- **Plugin:** `~/dev/projects/additional/viola-lab/prototype/plugin`, passed with `--plugin-dir`.
- **State:** `~/.viola/sessions/<name>/`. Since 2026-10-04 (V53), `vstart.sh` moves a dead session's folder to `~/.viola/archive/{name}-{UTC}/` before a relaunch, because `viola run` deletes it (`run.rs:37`). Old event history lives there. It holds `events.ndjson` (every hook event and viola action),
  `status`, `wheel` (present while the human holds it), `dialogs/`, `sent/`, `out.raw` (the raw terminal).
- **The builder session:** named `viola-builder`, cwd `~/dev/projects/viola`, started by the founder.
- **Screen check:** `sh scr.sh [name] [bytes]` in this folder prints the ANSI-stripped tail of `out.raw`.
  Use it to catch CLI-native modals the hooks never report.

## Starting a builder

The overseer cannot launch it itself: the permission classifier denies spawning a new Claude session
("Create Unsafe Agents"). The founder runs one short line:

    ~/dev/projects/additional/viola-overseer/vb.sh

`vb.sh` wraps andromedaV3's `docs/tools/vstart.sh`: it opens a new terminal window titled viola-builder running
`viola run viola-builder … -- claude …` in `~/dev/projects/viola` (`--dry-run` prints the command; `vbr.sh <id>` resumes).
A first launch in a folder shows Claude's CLI trust menu, which no hook sees: the founder answers it once, by hand. Hand the founder only short lines: a long path wraps in the
terminal and breaks. Check with `$V list` that the state is `idle` and the wheel is `viola`.

## The loop

1. **Before sending,** run `$V list` (state `idle`, wheel `viola`). After any surprise, check `sh scr.sh`
   too: an idle status does not prove the input box is ready.
2. **Send:** `$V send viola-builder '<text>'`. (On the old Windows host, Git Bash needed `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` before a `/skill` text; Linux does not.)
3. **Wait:** `$V wait viola-builder --timeout 3000` with `run_in_background: true`. The harness wakes you
   when it exits. Read its output file. The first line names what happened: `turn-end` (the final text
   follows), `question`, `permission`, `plan`, `exited` or `timeout`.
4. **Answer:** a plain-text prompt at a turn end gets a `send`. A multi-question dialog takes ALL its answers in ONE call, in order:
   `$V answer viola-builder 'Label 1' --note '…' 'Label 2' --note '…'`. Separate calls are refused (`1 answer(s) given`). A dialog gets `$V answer viola-builder
   <label|text> [--note …]`, `allow` / `allow <n>` / `deny <msg>`, or `approve` / `revise <what>`.
5. **After a send,** confirm delivery: the last lines of `events.ndjson` must show a `UserPromptSubmit`
   with your text. `viola:typed` alone proves nothing.
6. **Background-research turns** end with "research is running". Just `wait` again. The harness
   re-wakes the builder when its agent returns.
7. **Long autonomous stretches** (iteration loops, research): run `sh waitm.sh viola-builder` in the
   background instead of a bare `wait`. It skips short progress-only turn ends and returns on a dialog, a
   question, a long turn end, or completion. It prints how many turns it skipped.

## Waiter lifetime (Linux host, 2026-10-04)

The harness stops a background `waitm.sh` at its background time limit (killed after ~10–30 min, measured twice). A long run therefore needs the 30-min heartbeat to restart the waiter. Measured 2026-10-04 ~15:10Z: the stop is the background Bash call's own `timeout`, which defaults to 1 800 000 ms (30 min). Start the waiter with `timeout: 7200000` (2 h, the maximum) so a long implement keeps its waiter. Nothing is lost: the builder's events stay in `events.ndjson`, and `$V wait` reads the current state.

## Clears and dialogs (2026-10-04, from overseer1)

- **Clear through the shared tool:** `bash ~/dev/projects/additional/andromedaV3/andromeda-overseer/docs/worker/clear-worker.sh viola-builder --then '<skill line>'`. It proves the clear took, then sends, in one call. Never chain a send after a clear with `;` (PC16).
- **Since ~01:58Z on 2026-10-04 (PC20 binary), an unanswered dialog is HELD, not dropped to the CLI menu.** After 3500 s viola denies it with "No answer from the driver … end your turn and wait"; the event is `viola:dialog-held` and `viola wait` reports `held`. Send the answer afterwards as a plain PROMPT; a late `viola answer` is refused. The old binary is at `viola-lab/backups/viola-pre-PC20-f058e74e.bin`. First hold, measured 2026-10-04 13:16Z (2.1.287): the PreToolUse(AskUserQuestion) hold was followed by a PermissionRequest for the same tool, which viola also denied with the hold message. The builder ended its turn cleanly ("paused before P4 on one fork that needs the founder's live answer"), and the answer, sent as a plain prompt, resumed it. A founder AskUserQuestion on the overseer side can outlast the 58-min hold.
- (Superseded by the line above for the held case.) **Dialog fallback is 3500 s now** (the session's `config.json`; vstart.sh for new starts). A dialog held past the CLI's 3600 s hook cap degrades to the CLI menu. Never answer a degraded menu by digits (PC20: an answer landed inverted). Hold a founder question with free text.

## Known pitfalls, measured 2026-09-23 (CLI 2.1.280)

- **CLI-native modals bypass every hook.** "Teach auto mode about your environment?" appeared after a
  Stop, the status read `idle`, and a `send` answered the modal (it picked Yes and opened
  `/auto-mode-setup`). viola can only paste + Enter, and Enter would press the modal's default. Ask the
  founder to press Esc in the builder window. Esc alone does not take the wheel.
- **Harness-injected prompts** (`<agent-message from=…`, `<task-notification>`) fire `UserPromptSubmit`.
  Fixed in the prototype: they log `viola:harness-prompt` and never take the wheel.
- **The CLI wraps a long paste in `<pasted_content id=…>`** (981 bytes wrapped, 749 not), and escapes
  tag-like text a user typed (`<pasted_content` arrives as `<\pasted_content`). Both are normalized in the
  prototype. The model still treats wrapped text as the user's own (measured).
- **Local commands** (`/remote-control`, and probably `/clear`) fire no `UserPromptSubmit`. The send's
  record stays in `sent/`, so delete it (`rm ~/.viola/sessions/<name>/sent/*.txt`) once the command has
  visibly taken effect (check with `scr.sh`).
- **At a dialog, the builder's transcript lags** (measured 2026-09-24, CLI 2.1.280): the text printed just
  before an `AskUserQuestion` is not in `~/.claude/projects/-home-turbolet-dev-projects-viola/<session>.jsonl` (Windows-era key then) while the
  dialog is pending. It appeared only after the dialog was answered, which cost one "Edit first" round. Never
  conclude "not shown" from the jsonl. `waitm.sh` returning on a `question` or `plan` prints the screen's last
  4000 chars after the dialog (`[screen before the dialog]`); by hand, `sh scr.sh viola-builder 60000 4000`.
  Otherwise ask with a note that carries a question, not a claim.
- **Other overseers run `waitm.sh` too** (pc-overseer, for pulse-builder and conductor-builder, measured 2026-09-29). Never count `waitm.sh` processes, and never kill one by count: this instance killed pc-overseer's waiter that way at 07:29. Check your own waiter with `kill -0 "$(cat .waitm-viola-builder.pid)"`, and read `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` before killing anything.
- **Tag-like text in a send** (measured 2026-09-27 23:48): the CLI escapes a typed `<pasted_content` as
  `<\pasted_content` and `</pasted_content` as `<\/pasted_content`. Until the 2026-09-28 prototype fix (un-escape
  before strip), such a send took the wheel as `human`. The builder also read the escaped form as the CLI's own
  wrapper, so describe tags in words, or point to a file that holds them.
- **If the wheel reads `human` unexpectedly:** find the prompt that moved it with
  `grep '"viola:wheel"' events.ndjson`. If the founder did not type it, it is a prototype defect: fix it,
  then `$V release viola-builder`. Never release while the founder is actually typing.

## Rebuilding the prototype under a running session

On Linux a running binary can be replaced in place (cargo writes a new inode), so `cargo build` and `cargo test`. The wrapper keeps the old binary. New hook processes pick up the new
one through PATH. If the e2e tests fail instantly with "path not found", the cached test binaries predate
a move: `touch tests/e2e.rs examples/*.rs` and test again. Baseline: 5 unit tests + 7 e2e tests, all green.

## Answering policy

- **Answer from the brief** (`~/dev/projects/viola/refs/viola-brief.md`): its DECIDED items, its
  PROPOSED items, and anything that follows from an answer already given. Accept a recommendation only after
  checking it against the brief and the prior answers.
- **Bring the founder** (AskUserQuestion, recommended-first) anything the brief does not settle and that
  is theirs: scope, trajectory, naming, anything irreversible (brief Appendix A). The builder waits:
  dialogs hold for 1200 s, and plain-text prompts hold indefinitely.
- **Fold measured facts into the answers:** what the prototype and today's session proved, marked as
  measured, with the date and the CLI version.
- **Provenance:** answers typed by this overseer are "overseer (founder-delegated)". A founder ruling is
  recorded as the founder's. Arch's dialogue log already carries this for the arch run.
- **Keep sends short where possible.** Over roughly 800 bytes the CLI wraps the paste. That is harmless
  now, but short sends are easier to verify.

## Between pipeline skills (founder-ruled 2026-09-23)

When a greenfield skill finishes (its master is in `.andromeda/`, its `project.yaml` key is added, and the
next-skill footer is printed), verify those artifacts, then send `/clear`, then the next skill:
arch → security → design → tests → obs → a11y → route → setup-project. Never clear in the middle of a
skill. After `/clear`, confirm that the builder answers and that `SessionStart` shows `source: clear` in
the events. That is also the first live measurement of the /clear post-condition.

## The chunk loop's clear points (founder-ruled 2026-09-27, calibrate as data comes in)

A chunk runs as: new-session → phase → **/clear** → new-session → implement (with the operator pass and the CI read) → wrap.
Before sending the wrap, read the builder's context (`ctx NN%` in `sh scr.sh viola-builder 4000`):

- **≤ 60 %:** send the wrap whole, with the note "the 85 % and 90 % context alarms are expected: finish the wrap; stop only
  at 95 %".
- **> 60 %:** send the wrap with "run P1 only, then stop" (since overseer1's `33f0f8e`, V112: the letter's two-window form carries the candidates in P1's Decisions & corrections; order no separate resume file); then /clear →
  new-session → `/andromeda-wrap-session resume in <run dir>`.

Measured on 2026-09-27 over 20 builder sessions (`python3 ctxskills.py ~/.claude/projects/-home-turbolet-dev-projects-viola`; the Windows-era readings were under the old key):
phase ends at ~37 %; implement ends at ~50 % on Epoch 1 chunks and 60–74 % on Epoch 2's larger ones; a warm wrap costs
~22 % on average (max 29 %), and ~34 % on a chunk with ~45 amendments. After every wrap, add its start and end to the
calibration log below.

Calibration log (wrap start → end, warm unless marked):
- 2026-09-27 epoch-2-cleanup: wrap start 58 % → whole, finished without a pause.
- 2026-09-27 browser-verdict-reachability: wrap start 39 % → whole, no pause.
- 2026-09-27 wrapper-channel: implement 9.2 → 90.1 % (81 %: four operator-pass fix loops, two host memory kills); wrap start 90 % → P1 only, then /clear.

- 2026-10-13 epoch-4-survivors-ii: implement (16 hand kills, one file, CI green first time) → 27.6 %; wrap start 27.6 % → whole, 1 amendment, 2 rejected, no halt, 17 minutes.
- 2026-10-13 interrupted-verify-cleanup: implement (a plan-defect fork, a macOS runner never acquired, one job re-run) → 41.8 %; wrap start 41.8 % → whole, 27 amendments over seven masters, 13 leaf comparers, two non-decision dialogs while it waited on its agents (V122), no halt → about 69 % at P2's start; 30 minutes.
- 2026-10-13 paste-newline-ledger-row: implement (one live round of 5 starts, CI green first time) → 42.2 %; wrap start 42.2 % → whole, 38 amendments over five masters, one answer card (the overseer's delegate confirm), a route insertion, no pause; 27 minutes.

- The implement send always ends with the operator pass, or the builder stops at "Next: the operator pass" and waits (V62): `/andromeda-implement <marker>. <live-session line>. Run the operator pass with the ci.py conclusion read (leg=operator) as usual.`
- At every phase P5, the operator CI read must be the T14 tool call (`ci.py conclusion --sha HEAD --wait S`, leg=operator), never a copied jq/poller.
  Cross-check with `sh ciwatch.sh <run-id>`, which exits on the first failed job.
- Send directives as ONE line. Any send with newlines arrives wrapped in `<pasted_content>`, whatever its size (measured at
  609 B on 2026-09-27), and the builder treats a wrapped block as relayed text rather than the operator's own words. It
  refused to act on one that claimed a founder ratification, and asked for a confirmation typed outside the paste. A
  single line of 663 B arrived unwrapped. A skill starts only when its `/command` is the first text of an UNWRAPPED
  prompt; a wrapped command does not fire, and the model may not start the skill for it. So a skill send is one line:
  `/andromeda-… <directive on the same line>` (740 B arrived fine; a single line of 808 B arrived WRAPPED, 2026-09-27
  23:16). Keep a skill send under 740 B, and put what does not fit into a FILE the line names (a relay in this folder, as `d94-route-adaptation.md` was). Never a second send after the skill has started: it lands while the builder reads `busy`, viola waits 120 s and exits 1 ("busy, not at a turn boundary"), and the directive is not in the builder's context when the skill begins (measured by escher-overseer 2026-10-07, its ES17, relayed by overseer1).

## A gate red where no assertion failed on a value (a stall, a timeout, a kill)

Read the host's own record BEFORE any re-run (overseer1's standing host record, founder-ruled 2026-10-07, running since 2026-10-07T11:35:05Z and started by `up.sh` at every host start):

    python3 ~/dev/projects/additional/andromedaV3/andromeda-overseer/docs/tools/hostwatch.py read --trail <gate trail> --for viola

or `read --last 15`, or `read --from <UTC> --to <UTC>`; `status` says whether it runs. One verdict: CONTENDED (8 s or more with tasks stalled on IO for half the interval), QUIET or NO RECORD; with `--for viola`, Viola's own link is not counted. It records and prevents nothing. The test homes are on tmpfs since 2026-10-07 (`target/e2e-home` is a link), so what remains exposed on the shared volume is cargo's own `target/` and the coverage profiles. A QUIET stalled-start red is a finding about the backing: stop and report, never re-run for green.

## Live `claude` sessions and long runs (2026-10-09 → 2026-10-10)

- **A live session runs HEADLESS, on a plain pty the chunk's rig opens itself** (`evidence/live-pty.py` of chunk `2026-10-09-epoch-3-cleanup`; five starts over two chunks, none stalled, no stop rule fired), rehearsed under the fake agent first with no live start. The nested compositor of 2026-10-08 is NOT repeated: its one start ended the desktop shell on a locked desktop. A reading that needs a typed key or a window is the founder's to grant. At P5, send a plan back that copies the compositor rig.
- **Every live start is inside the founder's cap for THAT chunk** (a number he gives in a dialog; it does not carry to the next chunk), ledgered before it is made with the clock's time. The stamped 2.1.287 home lives on tmpfs (`target/e2e-home/viola-live-4043089/home`): after a reboot a re-stamp costs five starts.
- **An hours-long builder run** (a mutation run, a workflow dispatch): the builder idles at a turn end waiting for its own background run, so `waitm.sh` returns at once. Use `sh waitlong.sh viola-builder` in the background (timeout 7200000): it waits for the builder to leave idle and returns on a dialog, or on a turn end where the Stop event's `background_tasks` is empty (the builder then waits for the driver; V103, V105: a word list over the turn end's text missed a review card and a finished wrap). Use it for a phase and a wrap too: both idle at turn ends while their own agents run. Tell the builder in the implement line to journal each run in its run dir before the wait — the CLI compacts an idle session after about 55 minutes.
- **At P5, beside the profile's checklist:** a preservation guard lists no file a step edits (it cost one revision round on 2026-10-09) · a step that asks a rebuilt file's hash to equal an earlier build's cannot hold once a comment changes (compare loaded sections) · no test sends a kill at a process it does not own · a plan that fires a mutation run or a workflow dispatch is the founder's (the profile's mutation direction).
- **An empty dialog while the builder waits on its own agents** (V122, OPEN since 2026-10-16; an instrument slot after G3): answer it in free text, the text «continue; the agents' notification is the wake» through `viola answer viola-builder`, never by a label.
- **A founder dialog holds THIS session** (measured 2026-10-09: 75 minutes, while overseer1 waited for a seam answer): before raising one, answer every pending message and say in the report what will wait behind it.

## Our own window

Read only the final artifacts a skill promotes (founder-ruled 2026-09-23). Run-dir drafts, iteration
snapshots and changelog lines stay unread, and the turn-end text is enough to follow progress.

At every skill boundary, before the builder's `/clear`, update `.claude/session-handoff.md`: where the
chain stands, decisions taken, findings not yet in the brief, and whether the builder is running. The
`ctx-alarm` hook fires at 85/90/95 %. At 85 %, finish the step, write the handoff, and tell the founder.
The `/clear` of this window is the founder's.

# Relay 2 — the P4 founder dialog and its answers (verbatim)

Raised at P4 as one dialog of four questions, per the operator's take-up direction (`inputs#I1`). It came back
answered in the session, each answer carrying a note naming it as the founder's own word given live in the
overseer's dialog.

## Q1 — Start cap
Question: Live claude start cap and CLI version for the switched builder. The installed claude is 2.1.296, but
every viola stamp is on 2.1.287. On an unstamped CLI the product answers every dialog null at once and refuses
`answer`, so the overseer could not answer the builder's dialogs. Which version, and how many live starts may this
chunk make?
Options: 1. 2.1.296, cap 8 (Recommended) · 2. Pin 2.1.287, cap 8 · 3. 296, then 287 fallback, cap 14.
Answer: "2.1.296, cap 8 (Recommended)" — notes: The founder's own word, live in the overseer's dialog: «2.1.296, лимит 8».

## Q2 — Switch at
Question: When in this chunk does the overseer switch the builder (this session) from the prototype to the
product? The switch ends the prototype-wrapped builder and restarts it with
`viola run viola-builder -- claude --resume <id>`. The pipeline that follows is the v1-33 proof: a skill sent, the
wait, the final text read, a review answered and /clear between skills.
Options: 1. Mid-implement (Recommended) · 2. Before implement · 3. Before the wrap.
Answer: "Mid-implement (Recommended)" — notes: The founder's own word: «В середине implement».

## Q3 — Takeover (playbook pattern "Boundary widening")
Question: The takeover proof needs a key typed in the session terminal to take the wheel. An agent typing that key
into the LIVE builder window goes beyond your 2026-10-08 ruling, which covered a nested compositor only. That makes
it a boundary widening (playbook: "Boundary widening"). After the key, only a human `viola release` gives the wheel
back; a driver's release is refused by design. How is the key typed?
Options: 1. Agent key, you release (Recommended) · 2. Throwaway instance · 3. You type it yourself.
Answer: "Founder types it himself, later" — notes: The founder's own words: «Я на работе и у меня нет ремота для
билдеров, только для оверсиров» — he cannot type a key or run viola release in the builder's terminal today. No agent
key (no widening). Plan the takeover reading as the chunk's LAST attended step, his own key and his own viola release
when he is at his keyboard; everything else proceeds now; say in the plan how the chunk carries that step if he is
not back before the wrap.

## Q4 — New gaps (playbook pattern "Boundary widening")
Question: Research found two gaps the 2026-10-08 gap list did not name. (1) A question event keeps only option
labels: the product drops each option's description and preview, which the overseer relays to you with your forks.
(2) turn-ended drops Stop's background_tasks, which waitlong.sh uses to tell a progress turn end from one that waits
for the driver. Carrying option text into events.ndjson and drivers' `wait --json` and MCP results is a boundary
widening (a validated surface admits more upstream content). What happens with these gaps?
Options: 1. Build both, count only (Recommended) · 2. Dialog detail only · 3. Neither; overseer adapts · 4. Gap entry first.
Answer: "Build both, count only (Recommended)" — notes: The founder's own word: «Строить оба» — option description
and preview in the question event, background_tasks as a count only; widening ratified by him.

Authority: the founder's own answers to four P4 forks, given live in the overseer's dialog and relayed into this
session (relayed by the overseer). Q4 ratifies the option-text widening as his own answer to a P4 fork. Q3 takes no
widening: no agent-typed key.

# Step 11: the keepers' headroom floor, and its basis

## The readings the floor is set from

- **Fresh `statvfs` reading** (before the floor was written, 2026-10-20T09:04:01Z): the e2e-home link's target
  (an owner-only directory on the `/tmp` tmpfs) reads `f_bavail` 3 562 765 × `f_frsize` 4 096 = 14 593 085 440 B = **13 917 MiB free**, of
  32 097 MiB. `df -h /tmp` at the same time: `tmpfs 32G 18G 14G 57%`.
- **The recorded EDQUOT reading** (`.andromeda/runs/2026-10-19T19-16-36-wrap/relay-3.md`): the switch wrap's light gate
  struck EDQUOT on the tmpfs's per-user quota with `$TMPDIR` at 24 G used of 32 G, about **8 G free by `df`**, a run's
  test homes in place. 13 G used after the founder's cleanup.
- **The run's footprint** (research §Mechanisms (9)): every test home pins a copy of the debug `viola`, 101 163 992 B
  (96.5 MiB). 32 test threads on this host means up to 32 × 101 163 992 B = 3 237 247 744 B (3 087 MiB) at once.
- **The quota itself is unreadable** from the session's shell (`quotactl_fd` → EPERM, research). `statvfs` reads the
  filesystem, so its free bytes stand in for the quota: the same user writes almost all of `/tmp` (other live sessions'
  task output), so the filesystem's free bytes fall as the user's usage rises.

## The floor

- `HEADROOM_FLOOR_MIB = 9 * 1024` (9 216 MiB, 9 GiB), one named constant in each keeper, equal in both:
  `tests/support/home.rs` (`prepare_home_base`'s link branch) and `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/mod.rs`
  (`Workspace::ensure_e2e_home`'s link branch).
- **Why 9 GiB.** The EDQUOT reading already holds a run's homes, so the line to stay above is about 8 GiB free *with*
  the run in place. A home made while the backing reads below 9 GiB is refused. That leaves one GiB, about ten pinned
  `viola` copies in flight, above the recorded EDQUOT point.
- **Why not the whole footprint on top (8 GiB + 3.1 GiB).** Each check reads the backing with the run's own live homes
  already in it. Today's start, 13 917 MiB less a full run's 3 087 MiB, reads about 10 830 MiB mid-run. A floor of
  about 11.1 GiB (11 366 MiB) would refuse the run's own later homes at today's headroom, though the run then still
  stands about 2.6 GiB (10 830 − 8 192 MiB) above the EDQUOT point.
- The refusal is a fixed message with the two counts and no path: `e2e-home backing: {free} MiB free, below the
  {floor} MiB floor` (root: a panic, as the keeper's other checks; harness: `io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput`, which
  `boot` reports as its closed `build-failed`).
- A plain-directory base (every CI runner) reads no headroom. No env var, flag or config key reads or sets the floor.
- The decision `headroom_refusal(free, floor_mib)` is a plain function tested on every OS:
  `home_base_headroom_below_the_floor_is_refused_with_both_counts`,
  `home_base_headroom_at_or_above_the_floor_passes`, `home_base_headroom_floor_is_nine_gib`
  (`tests/cli_instance_state.rs`); `e2e_home_headroom_refuses_below_the_floor_and_passes_at_or_above_it` and the
  Unix reader's `e2e_home_headroom_reads_a_real_filesystem` (`crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/mod.rs`).

## Remove-the-guard (scratch clone `clone-h`: HEAD `d35644a58909aec12c4898e5a066bcfca5a8ebd2` + the chunk's diff)

The comparison was neutralised in both keepers, `(free_mib < floor_mib)` → `(free_mib < floor_mib && false)`
(`$TMPDIR/{scratchpad}/neutralise_headroom.py`).
Then `cargo nextest run -E 'test(/headroom/)'` was run over each package (`…/scratchpad/headroom_guard.sh`):

| package | neutralised | restored (the files re-applied from the diff, 0 neutralised lines) |
|---|---|---|
| `viola` | `3 tests run: 2 passed, 1 failed` — `home_base_headroom_below_the_floor_is_refused_with_both_counts` panicked at `tests/cli_instance_state.rs:598:5`, `left: None`, `right: Some("e2e-home backing: 9215 MiB free, below the 9216 MiB floor")` | `3 tests run: 3 passed` |
| `viola-e2e` | `2 tests run: 1 passed, 1 failed` — `e2e_home_headroom_refuses_below_the_floor_and_passes_at_or_above_it` panicked at `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/mod.rs:406:13`, `one byte short`, `left: None` | `2 tests run: 2 passed` |

body:
# Item (8): who cuts the `viola` profile short (plan step 10)

Each reading below was written before the next step was taken.

## (a) The census's second form

`scripts/profraw-census.sh --case <binary stem> <test name> <runs> <workers> [<name>]` runs one integration case of the
instrumented build `run --coverage` leaves (`target/llvm-cov-target/debug/deps/<stem>-<hash>`, the newest that lists
the test), `<runs>` times over `<workers>` loops. Each run's profiles are named as the coverage run names them
(`r<i>-%p-%<nproc>m.profraw`, so the binary signature is in the name) and each is offered alone to the toolchain's
`llvm-profdata merge --sparse -o /dev/null`. A refused file is kept under `refused/` and printed with its signature and
its size beside the largest size its signature reached in the census. Verdict: exit 0 only when every run passed and no
profile was refused. The first form (the fixed unit test) is unchanged. A dev-host script: no CI, `pre-push` or harness
hook.

## (b) The red side

### P5's own file, read first

- `viola-3929550-11199965415080257827_14.profraw`, 90 112 B, kept in this session's scratchpad `profraw-p5/` (sha256
  `9de3dda876dfb2327536c43fcbf96378c47a3d87f7ae0aae6fe7423f4f2fee61`, the same as P5's copy).
- Its version-10 header: 1 455 data records from byte 160 to 93 280, then the counters from 93 280 to 120 656. The file
  ends at 90 112 B = 22 whole 4 KiB pages, inside the data records (1 405 of 1 455 whole). No counter survives, so the
  counter method (session-learnings, 2026-10-04) cannot name its writer.
- Both truncated files on record end on a page boundary: this one, and the switch chunk's 118 784 B (29 pages).

### The census over the kill-shaped case

- Case: `chaos_wait_vanish chaos_wait_parked_wrapper_killed_exits_21`, the switch chunk's closest candidate. It boots
  an unstamped wrapper, parks a `viola wait` on it, then sends the wrapper `SIGKILL`.
- Build: the instrumented tree P5's `pre-push` left at HEAD `d35644a58909`, the untouched tree
  (`target/llvm-cov-target/debug/viola`, 104 194 856 B, written 2026-10-20T08:48:33Z).
- Call: `bash scripts/profraw-census.sh --case chaos_wait_vanish chaos_wait_parked_wrapper_killed_exits_21 200 8
  e5c-chaos-wait-1`. `df -h /tmp` before: `tmpfs 32G 18G 14G 57%`.
- Result: `runs 200 · passed 200 · profiles 726 · refused 17`. Basis: 200 runs over 8 concurrent loops, every run's
  profiles offered to `llvm-profdata merge` one by one. All 17 refused files carry the `viola` binary's signature
  `11199965415080257827`, against a whole size of 146 344 B:

| size (B) | files | where the cut falls | writer (counter method) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 145 232 | 6 | names section (every counter whole) | `viola hook`: `main` → `cmd::dispatch` → `cmd::hook::{hook, handle, decided, deliver, spine_deadline}` → `viola_channel::client::Client::notify`, and the `viola_agent_claude::hook` normaliser (`HookEvent::{from_arg, kind, as_str, is_dialog}`, `data_of`, `normalise`, `known_fields`); 70 nonzero functions, all named |
| 118 784 | 1 | counters | `viola hook`: the same chain to `Client::notify`; 49 nonzero functions, all named |
| 94 208 | 2 | the first counter page | only `obs::viola_obs_init` and the role-file open: any `viola` role |
| 90 112 | 6 | data records | not named: no counter survives |
| 4 096 | 2 | data records | not named |

- The census dir `target/profraw-census/e5c-chaos-wait-1/` keeps the 17 files under `refused/`. The attribution was
  read by a scratchpad copy of the switch chunk's script with a guard for a cut inside the data records
  (`$TMPDIR/{scratchpad}/profraw_name2.py`).
  The complete sibling was a 146 344 B profile of the same signature from P5's coverage run.
- Reading: every refused file that keeps its counters (7 of 17) is a `viola hook` that had already delivered its event
  and was cut off in its exit-time profile write. No refused file names the wrapper (`cmd::run`). The case kills the
  wrapper, whose PTY then closes, and the fake agent is that terminal's session leader. Its hooks run in its own
  process group, the terminal's foreground group (`src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs` `run_receipted`). The hangup reaches
  them there, while the fake agent's stdout holder already leaves that group for exactly this signal
  (`hold_inherited_stdout`). The writer matches the research hypothesis. The hangup as the killer is inferred, not yet
  read: (c) tests it by taking the hooks out of that group.
- The other `Wrapper::kill` callers were not run: the first case reproduced the class.

## (c) The hooks out of the foreground group: the same census

- Change: `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs` `run_receipted` spawns each command (every hook, and the status line command
  that shares the function) with `std::os::unix::process::CommandExt::process_group(&mut cmd, 0)` on Unix, as
  `hold_inherited_stdout` already does. Nothing else changed in the fake agent.
- Build: `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --coverage` on the chunk's tree, `"ok":true`, suite `coverage` 2 980 passed 0
  failed, its merge refusing nothing. `target/llvm-cov-target/debug/viola-fake-agent` written 2026-10-20T09:10:01Z,
  after the edit (09:09:36Z).
- Call: `bash scripts/profraw-census.sh --case chaos_wait_vanish chaos_wait_parked_wrapper_killed_exits_21 200 8
  e5c-chaos-wait-2`, the host otherwise idle as for (b). `df -h /tmp` before: `tmpfs 32G 19G 14G 59%`.
- Result: **`runs 200 · passed 200 · profiles 800 · refused 0`**, exit 0.

| census | runs | passed | profiles | per run | refused |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| (b) HEAD's build | 200 | 200 | 726 | 3.63 | 17 |
| (c) the process-group build | 200 | 200 | 800 | 4 exactly | 0 |

- The profile count moved too. Before, 74 processes of 200 runs left no profile at all: killed before their exit-time
  write began. After, every run leaves the same four. Over the same runs, the hangup was the killer of every cut-short
  and missing profile this case makes.

## The finding

- **The killer is named:** the terminal hangup that follows a test killing the wrapper. The wrapper's PTY closes, and
  the fake agent, that terminal's session leader, runs its hooks in its own process group, the terminal's foreground
  group. A `viola hook` the hangup reaches after `Client::notify`, in its exit-time profile write, leaves a page-cut
  profile that `llvm-profdata merge` refuses ("file header is corrupt"), or none.
- **The fix is the fake agent's** (test-only, behind `fake-agent`): its commands leave the foreground group. No product
  code changed.
- Basis and limits: one kill-shaped case, 200 runs per side, 8 workers, this host. P5's own file (90 112 B) is not
  attributable by counters. Its size and page-cut shape match six of the reproduced files exactly, which is a match,
  not a reading of its writer. The WATCH's class is now explained. The `pre-push` runs of this chunk read it from here
  on (plan §Test Commands: after a named and fixed cause, a red of that shape is this chunk's red).

# Step 7: the viola-pty test guard under the caught `try_wait` mutant

## What was changed in the tree

- The guard `impl Drop for Child` in `crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs`'s test module now calls `self.pty.kill()`
  unconditionally, its error ignored. Before, it killed only when `try_wait()` read `Ok(None)`.
- Both PTY children the tests spawn from the test binary (`spawn_child_entry`, `close_hangs_up_a_live_child`) now run
  a per-test copy of it in the case's own `tempfile` dir (`copied_test_binary`). The `std::process::Command` child of
  the piped-stdin case is unchanged.

## The remove-the-guard reading (Linux dev host, 2026-10-20)

- Two scratch clones of HEAD `d35644a58909aec12c4898e5a066bcfca5a8ebd2` in this session's scratchpad. In each, the
  product `PortablePty::try_wait` was hand-replaced by `Ok(Some(1))` (the caught mutant before the dispatch's unviables,
  its log line 441), by `$TMPDIR/{scratchpad}/plant_try_wait.py`.
  - `clone-pty-old`: the old guard (HEAD), target dir `target/e5c-pty-old`.
  - `clone-pty-new`: the chunk's diff applied first, target dir `target/e5c-pty-new`.
  - Both build the test binary `viola_pty-77dd4bdbf6cc1891`. The census keys on that name, so it holds a child run
    from the target dir and one run from a tempdir copy alike.
- The readings, in order (`gate.py census`, trail `.andromeda/runs/2026-10-20T08-57-19-implement/gate-2026-10-20-epoch-5-cleanup.json`):

| # | reading | result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | census before either run (`--args` both target dirs) | `census: none running` |
| 2 | old guard: `cargo nextest run --package viola-pty --no-fail-fast` | `40 tests run: 35 passed, 5 failed` (the mutant caught) |
| 3 | census `--args viola_pty-77dd4bdbf6cc1891` | `census: none running` |
| 4 | new guard: the same run | `40 tests run: 35 passed, 5 failed` |
| 5 | census `--args viola_pty-77dd4bdbf6cc1891` | `census: none running` |

- No row was found, so no process was signalled.

## What the reading shows, and what it does not

- **The plan's expected reading (leaked children on the old guard) does not hold on Linux.** On Unix, dropping the
  `PortablePty` closes the master, and the kernel hangs up the child's terminal. The child dies whether or not the
  guard kills it: the module's own `close_hangs_up_a_live_child` pins exactly that. So on this host the old and new
  guards leave the same nothing, and the reading cannot tell them apart.
- The leak the step closes is the Windows mechanism research names, still a hypothesis: a running image there cannot
  be replaced, and the dispatch's `mutants (viola-pty)` turned every later mutant `unviable` right after the
  `try_wait` mutants were caught. That needs a Windows host. It is owed to the next boundary's Windows leg
  (`unviable` ≤ `caught` in `mutants (viola-pty)`), as the plan already places it.
- Acceptance «shows leaked children … on the old guard and none on the new one» is therefore not met as written, by a
  measured host fact. This is raised in the outcome as a premise disproof for the wrap, not worked around.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The one writer of the start ledger (plan.md steps 1, 2, 13 and 15).

It appends one row to `live-sessions.ndjson`: the row is read from a JSON file, parsed and re-serialised, so a
mangled row fails here and never lands, and `written_at` is the UTC time read from the clock at the write, never a
time typed by hand. A `start` row is written before its start is made.

  live-ledger.py <ledger> <row file>

Run from the repository root.
"""
import datetime
import json
import sys


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) != 3:
        sys.exit(__doc__)
    ledger, row_file = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
    with open(row_file, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        row = json.load(f)
    if not isinstance(row, dict) or not isinstance(row.get("kind"), str):
        sys.exit("a row is an object with a kind")
    row["written_at"] = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
    line = json.dumps(row, sort_keys=False)
    with open(ledger, "a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(line + "\n")
    print(line)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

title: evidence/live-tap.py
body:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The live round's rig (plan.md step 18): one print-mode `claude` start whose one MCP server is
`viola-mcp-tap` in front of `viola mcp`.

  live-tap.py setup            make the rig; print its stamp
  live-tap.py start <stamp> <form>   one start (ledgered before it, by live-ledger.py); form 1 ran
                                     start 1, form 2 is the stdin form a second start would take
  live-tap.py read <stamp>     the capture's codes and counts

Run from the repository root. Every child is a direct spawn under a declared environment of eight
names (no `CLAUDE*`, no `VIOLA*`), the stamped CLI's install dir first on `PATH`. Nothing it prints
holds a path, the prompt, an assistant text or a session id: codes, counts, times and hash prefixes.
"""
import datetime
import hashlib
import json
import os
import pathlib
import subprocess
import sys

CLI_VERSION = "2.1.302"
PROMPT = "reply with the single word ok"
START_BOUND_S = 300


def home():
    return pathlib.Path(os.path.expanduser("~"))


def cli_dir():
    return home() / ".local/share/mise/installs/claude" / CLI_VERSION


def declared_env():
    keep = {k: os.environ[k] for k in ("HOME", "LANG", "LOGNAME", "SHELL", "USER", "XDG_RUNTIME_DIR")
            if k in os.environ}
    keep["PATH"] = f"{cli_dir()}:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin"
    keep["TERM"] = "xterm-256color"
    return keep


def dirs(stamp):
    root = pathlib.Path.cwd()
    base = root / "target/e2e-home" / f"viola-live-tap-{stamp}"
    priv = root / "target" / f"mcp-live-tap-{stamp}" / "priv"
    return root, base, priv


def now():
    return datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ")[:-4] + "Z"


def sha8(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(pathlib.Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:16]


def setup():
    stamp = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ")
    root, base, priv = dirs(stamp)
    for d in (base, base / "proj", priv):
        d.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True, exist_ok=False)
        os.chmod(d, 0o700)
    env = declared_env()
    git = subprocess.run(["/usr/bin/git", "init", "-q"], cwd=base / "proj", env=env)
    top = subprocess.run(["/usr/bin/git", "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"], cwd=base / "proj",
                         env=env, capture_output=True, text=True)
    own_top = pathlib.Path(top.stdout.strip()).resolve() == (base / "proj").resolve()
    outside = not (base / "proj").resolve().is_relative_to(root.resolve())
    memory = [str(p.relative_to(p.anchor)) for a in [(base / "proj").resolve(), *(base / "proj").resolve().parents]
              for p in (a / "CLAUDE.md", a / ".claude/CLAUDE.md", a / "CLAUDE.local.md") if p.exists()]
    config = {"mcpServers": {"viola": {
        "type": "stdio",
        "command": str(root / "target/debug/viola-mcp-tap"),
        "args": ["record", str(priv / "capture.ndjson"), str(root / "target/debug/viola"),
                 "--home", str(base / "vhome"), "mcp"],
        "env": {},
    }}}
    fd = os.open(priv / "mcp.json", os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL, 0o600)
    with os.fdopen(fd, "w") as f:
        json.dump(config, f)
    version = subprocess.run([str(cli_dir() / "claude"), "--version"], env=env, capture_output=True,
                             text=True, timeout=60)
    print(json.dumps({
        "stamp": stamp, "git_init": git.returncode, "toplevel_is_proj": own_top,
        "proj_outside_work_tree": outside, "ancestor_memory_files": len(memory),
        "home_exists": (base / "vhome").exists(), "mcp_json_mode": oct(os.stat(priv / "mcp.json").st_mode & 0o777),
        "cli_version": version.stdout.strip(), "env_names": sorted(env),
        "viola_sha": sha8(root / "target/debug/viola"), "tap_sha": sha8(root / "target/debug/viola-mcp-tap"),
        "prompt_sha": hashlib.sha256(PROMPT.encode()).hexdigest()[:16],
    }))


def start(stamp, form):
    """`form` 1 is start 1's argv (the prompt after `--mcp-config`, which 2.1.302 reads as
    variadic `<configs...>`); `form` 2 gives the prompt on stdin and nothing after the config."""
    root, base, priv = dirs(stamp)
    env = declared_env()
    argv = [str(cli_dir() / "claude"), "-p", "--strict-mcp-config", "--mcp-config", str(priv / "mcp.json")]
    stdin = subprocess.DEVNULL
    if form == "1":
        argv.append(PROMPT)
    began = now()
    try:
        done = subprocess.run(argv, cwd=base / "proj", env=env,
                              input=PROMPT.encode() if form == "2" else None,
                              stdin=None if form == "2" else stdin,
                              capture_output=True, timeout=START_BOUND_S)
        code, timed_out = done.returncode, False
        out, err = done.stdout, done.stderr
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as e:
        code, timed_out, out, err = None, True, e.stdout or b"", e.stderr or b""
    ended = now()
    fd = os.open(priv / f"stderr-{form}.txt", os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL, 0o600)
    with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as f:
        f.write(err)
    reply = out.decode("utf-8", "replace").strip()
    print(json.dumps({"form": form, "began": began, "ended": ended, "exit": code, "timed_out": timed_out,
                      "stdout_bytes": len(out), "stderr_bytes": len(err),
                      "stderr_sha": hashlib.sha256(err).hexdigest()[:16],
                      "reply_is_the_word": reply.lower().rstrip(".") == "ok"}))


def read(stamp):
    _, base, priv = dirs(stamp)
    cap = priv / "capture.ndjson"
    lines = cap.read_text().splitlines() if cap.exists() else []
    rows = [json.loads(l) for l in lines]
    seq = []
    for r in rows:
        try:
            frame = json.loads(r["line"])
        except (ValueError, KeyError):
            seq.append((r.get("dir"), "unparsed"))
            continue
        word = frame.get("method") or ("response" if "result" in frame else "error" if "error" in frame else "?")
        seq.append((r.get("dir"), word))
    print(json.dumps({
        "capture_exists": cap.exists(),
        "capture_mode": oct(cap.stat().st_mode & 0o777) if cap.exists() else None,
        "lines": len(lines),
        "by_dir": {d: sum(1 for x, _ in seq if x == d) for d in ("client", "server")},
        "sequence": seq,
        "mcp_log_lines": len((base / "vhome/diagnostics/mcp.ndjson").read_text().splitlines())
        if (base / "vhome/diagnostics/mcp.ndjson").exists() else 0,
    }))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    verb = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else ""
    if verb == "setup":
        setup()
    elif verb == "start" and len(sys.argv) == 4 and sys.argv[3] in ("1", "2"):
        start(sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3])
    elif verb == "read" and len(sys.argv) == 3:
        read(sys.argv[2])
    else:
        sys.exit(__doc__)

The founder is AWAY (the overseer's directive, `inputs#I1` item 5: «He is asleep now, so a widening fork is held as
such and never answered from a recorded direction»). Per gate-contract.md §Scope *Whose word*, his forks take the away
form: written here, the step stopped. A delegate's answer is PROVISIONAL until his own word, and a fork on a boundary
widening is answered by its most conservative option. P4 resumes on the answer appended below.

## Fork 1 — what a verified client does with an unreadable or newer `snapshot.json` (CARRY 7), and whether the snapshot readers move to the replay (CARRY 8)

**The freight, as the working entry holds it.**
- CARRY 7 (chunk 2026-10-10-self-healing-state, the operator's direction at its wrap,
  `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-10-self-healing-state/inputs/I4-relay-1.md.txt`): «what a client's pre-check does with an
  unreadable or newer `snapshot.json` is undecided and unchanged. `read_snapshot` reads either as absent, so
  `live_endpoint` finds no endpoint and the verb exits 21; the classified read and the log replay stand as library code
  that no client calls. A client that connected on a replayed endpoint and a heartbeat alone would change the dated
  pre-check's outcome: a boundary matter, the founder's to rule before this entry plans it.»
- CARRY 8 (chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list, the review card the founder approved): the other snapshot readers
  «still call `read_snapshot` and take no replay, which keeps `verification-matrix.json#v1-41` open and E5's steps 1–3
  unbuilt». P3 corrected the list at HEAD: `src/cmd/client.rs` holds no call any more; the CLI verbs' read is
  `viola_state::liveness::live_endpoint`, and under `src/` four product readers remain (`hook.rs` ×2, `statusline.rs`,
  `run.rs`'s collision check) — `chunks/2026-10-26-server-verification-before-any-frame/research.md` Sweeps.

**What P3 established that bears on it.** A replayed snapshot carries no `endpoint`, `pid` or `started_at`
(architecture §Standard Contracts, Snapshot envelope). The server verification this chunk builds compares the connected
server with the snapshot's own `pid` and `started_at`, so a client holding a replayed snapshot has nothing to verify
against: under this chunk it can never write a frame on a replayed or rebuilt endpoint, whichever option is taken.

**Options, in order:**

1. **Keep today's outcome (Recommended — the most conservative option).** Every reader keeps `read_snapshot`: an
   unreadable or newer snapshot reads as absent, so the CLI verbs exit 21 (`instance-dead`, the not-running hint), the
   MCP tools return `instance-unreachable`, the hook fails open — exactly as today. No client takes the classified read
   or the replay, and none writes a `state-recovered` line. CARRY 8's reader move (`v1-41`, test-plan §6 E5 steps 1–3)
   is NOT built here: it leaves this entry on the P5 card's `## Beyond the plan` as a re-pin, held for your own word
   (its destination proposed on the card). Why it wins: it changes nothing across the boundary, and the replay's two
   product readers (`viola revive`, `viola list`) stay its only ones, as your board ruling left them. Its cost: `v1-41`
   stays open past this chunk.
2. **Move the four readers and `live_endpoint` onto `read_snapshot_or_replay` now.** A replayed snapshot then reaches
   each client as a snapshot with no endpoint and no identity, so every client still reports unreachable or fails open
   (no frame is possible without a recorded `pid` / `started_at`), but each such read writes one
   `state-recovered{snapshot-replayed|snapshot-unsupported-v}` line into the client's role file (`cli-<name>`, `hook-<name>`,
   `mcp`), and `run`'s collision check would classify a replayed instance by its heartbeat alone (live or gone, never
   stale). It closes CARRY 8 and lets `v1-41` be claimed with E5's steps 1–3 built here. Its cost: a new log crossing
   in three client roles and a changed collision outcome on a replayed snapshot — a boundary matter by CARRY 7's own
   words, which only your live word ratifies.

**What counts as his word:** the founder's own answer naming option 1 or 2 (or another form), given live or relayed
verbatim. A delegate's answer is provisional and, the fork touching a boundary, may only be option 1.

## Leans P4 takes without a question (each settled by an artifact; shown so the answer covers the whole picture)
- The strict-modes half of the dated gaps stays with "Home and code-bearing file integrity": that entry's own freight
  names every verb of this chunk («this entry adds `send` to the strict-modes entry points …»). This chunk closes the
  server-identity half only; the gaps' strict-modes half stays dated until that entry.
- macOS: `peer_creds()` gives no pid there, and the euid and socket-directory checks macOS's verification rests on are
  "Unix endpoint and home hardening"'s by its own freight («the directory verification … and the peer euid check stay
  this entry's»). This chunk's pid + start-time check is Linux and Windows; macOS keeps the recorded gap.
- CARRY 2 (a hook reaching an exiting wrapper's own Windows pipe): the exiting wrapper IS the recorded process, so a
  passing check is the right verdict there and the check is not built to close the window; it is named unclosed, and
  its re-pin rides the P5 card.

## Answer
_(appended here when it arrives, then snapped with `--message-file`, `--kind relay` and an `--origin` naming who
answered and when)_

The answer, verbatim, in the session's message of 2026-10-26 (authority: delegate the Viola overseer, 2026-10-26, 08:08Z —

title: evidence/fake-agent-exit-hangup.md
body:
# The fake agent's exit out of the hangup's reach (the wrap's P7.1 red, folded: inputs#I13, inputs#I14)

## The mechanism, read in source
- portable-pty 0.8.1 makes the PTY child its session's leader with the terminal as its controlling tty
  (`unix.rs:220` `setsid()`, `:234` `ioctl(0, TIOCSCTTY, 0)`), so the fake agent under `viola run` is that leader.
- A hangup of that terminal (the master closed: a killed wrapper) signals the session leader with SIGHUP and SIGCONT
  (Linux `tty_signal_session_leader`); portable-pty's own `Child::kill` on Unix is SIGHUP first, then SIGKILL after a
  200 ms grace (`lib.rs:333-361`), which the wrapper's `kill_and_reap` and every `Pty::kill` reach.
- The Epoch 5 fix moved the agent's hooks and status line out of the foreground group (`process_group(0)`,
  `chunks/2026-10-20-epoch-5-cleanup/evidence/profraw-cause.md`). The agent itself cannot move: `setpgid` refuses a
  session leader (POSIX `EPERM`). So the change takes its EXIT out of the hangup's reach instead: from its exit's first
  step (`\x03`, or stdin's end) it sets SIGHUP to `SIG_IGN` (`src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs` `ignore_hangup`, called at
  both of `read_stdin`'s exits, before `close_hooks`). A hangup that lands mid its exit-time coverage write no longer
  cuts the profile; one that lands before the exit begins still ends it as before (no profile at all, which the merge
  does not refuse). The `--exit-no-eof` holder, spawned after it, inherits the disposition; it is outside the group
  already. No product code changed; the fake agent is behind `fake-agent`, never in a release build.

## The test and its red-before-green (`tests/cli_fake_agent.rs`, Linux only)
`fake_agent_exit_outlives_a_hangup_that_lands_while_it_exits`: a scripted Stop whose hook is the agent's own
`statusline-echo` (the marker shows the hook ran), held open by the existing capped `--stop-receipt-hold-ms 1000`
(testing.md 2026-09-27: force the window open with a test-only hold); `\x03` starts the exit, which waits the hold out in
`close_hooks`; the test waits for `/proc/<pid>/status` `SigIgn` bit 0 (SIGHUP) while the agent runs, checks the Stop
hook's receipt line is still unwritten (the hangup lands inside the exit), sends SIGHUP to the child it spawned, and
asserts exit code 0 with no signal and the one `Stop:true` hook line written after the hold.

| reading | tree | command | result |
|---|---|---|---|

body:
# The operator's check — the must-trace paths keep their spans and events on the new refusal paths

The operator's ask at invocation: obs-plan's rule that the six must-trace paths (obs-plan §4, detail
`.andromeda/obs-plan-detail/span-trace-coverage.md`) never skip their spans or events — confirm the new pre-frame refusal
paths keep both, and record what is found.

## The six paths, and which the chunk reaches

| Scenario (obs-plan §4) | New refusal on it? | Root span kept | Lines on the refusal |
|---|---|---|---|
| `viola run` start sequence | no — `run` writes no frame and holds no client (`run.collision_check` reads the snapshot only) | unchanged | unchanged |
| Confirmed `send` (CL-1) | CLI `send`, MCP `send`, and the spine hooks' `hook.event` | `send.client` · `mcp.tool_call` · `hook.handle` | CLI: `process-exit{exit_code:21, detail:"server-verify-failed", during:"connect"}` at WARN; hook: `hook-invoked` then `hook-decision{detail:"server-verify-failed"}` at WARN; MCP: none (as its unreachable path today, the plan's Constraints) |
| `wait` / `last` readback | CLI `wait` / `last`, MCP `wait` / `last` | `wait.block` · `last.client` · `mcp.tool_call` | CLI: the same `process-exit` |
| Dialog → `answer` | the dialog hook's `hook.dialog`; CLI and MCP `answer` | `hook.handle` · `answer.client` · `mcp.tool_call` | hook: `hook-invoked{corr:null}` and `hook-decision{corr:null, decision_emitted:false, detail:"server-verify-failed"}` at WARN; CLI: the same `process-exit` |
| Wheel (`pause` / `release`) | CLI `pause` / `release` | `pause.client` · `release.client` | CLI: the same `process-exit` |
| Budget governor | no — `hook statusline` writes no frame | unchanged | unchanged |

On every refused path no `channel.request` span opens and no `channel-request` line is written: the check runs before
the first frame, so there is no request to trace. That is the scenario's own rule for a call that never reached the
channel (the client-side `send-refused` precedent), not a skipped span.

## The witnesses — measured, not inferred

- **Spans, in process** (spans are not serialised to the role files — `with_current_span(false)`, `with_span_list(false)` —
  so a captured layer is the only reader): `request_refuses_an_unverified_server_inside_its_dispatch_span` in each of
  `src/cmd/{send,wait,last,answer,pause,release}.rs` (shared check `cmd::client::refused_inside::assert_refused_inside`)
  reads exactly `["span <verb span>"]` — the dispatch span opened, nothing else: no `channel.request` span, no line —
  and no frame at the server; `cmd::hook::tests::hook_refuses_an_unverified_server_inside_hook_handle` reads, in order,
  `span hook.handle` · `event "hook-invoked" in hook.handle` · `event "hook-decision" in none` (the event path's decision
  is written by the caller after `handle` returns, as on every fail-open path before this chunk) · `span hook.handle` ·
  `event "hook-invoked" in hook.handle` · `event "hook-decision" in hook.handle` (the dialog path). Each is red with the
  check removed (`red-before-green.md`, second reading: 7 run, 7 failed).
- **Lines, on disk** (the role files a real process wrote): `tests/security_negatives_server_identity.rs` reads one
  `process-exit{level:"WARN", subject:"self", exit_code:21, detail:"server-verify-failed", during:"connect"}` and no
  `channel-request` in `cli-builder.ndjson` for each of the six verbs in both modes, and no recorded pid, home path or
  endpoint in any output; `tests/hook_fail_open.rs`'s three impostor rows read `hook-invoked` then `hook-decision` at
  WARN with `detail:"server-verify-failed"`, both lines schema-valid against `schemas/diag-line.v1.json`.
- **MCP:** `frame` runs inside `call`, the `#[instrument(name = "mcp.tool_call")]` future (`crates/viola-mcp/src/tools.rs`),
  so the span holds by construction; the start-time read runs on `spawn_blocking` and writes no line. No span capture was
  added in `viola-mcp` (it carries no `tracing-subscriber` dev-dependency, and adding one is outside the plan's lists);
  `handlers_frame_tools_write_no_frame_to_a_server_that_is_not_the_recorded_wrapper` witnesses the result and the absent
  frame.

## Finding

The new refusal paths keep their scenario's root span and write their scenario's outcome line. One text in obs-plan §4
no longer holds and is the wrap's to amend (named in the plan's expected amendments): the `wait` / `last` scenario's
«`strict-modes-failed` / `server-verify-failed` cannot occur on `wait` / `last` until client-side server verification
lands» — `server-verify-failed` now occurs there on Linux and Windows. No span was skipped and no event dropped.
