body:
# 1.53.3 (October 13th, 2026)

### Added

- io: add `AsyncFd::register` and `AsyncFd::register_with_interest` ([#8587])

### Changed

- io: deprecate `AsyncFd::{new, with_interest, try_new, try_with_interest}` ([#8587])

### Fixed

- io: wake and drop `DuplexStream` wakers outside the lock ([#8618])
- macros: avoid `unreachable_code` in `join!` and `try_join!` for `Infallible` ([#8518])
- runtime: fix paused time auto-advancing when I/O wakes a task on `current_thread` ([#8595])
- sync: wake waiters outside the lock when closing a semaphore ([#8529])
- test: fix several flaky tests ([#8196], [#8427], [#8609])

### Fixed (unstable)

- rt: keep `io_uring` op alive when submission fails after push ([#8185])

[#8185]: https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio/pull/8185

# 1.53.2 (October 3rd, 2026)

### Fixed

- fs: handle integer overflow in buffered relative seek ([#8574])
- io: revert "always cleanup `AsyncFd` registration list on deregister" ([#8540])
- process: unregister Windows wait before closing child handle ([#8564])
- rt: drop blocking pool mutex before shutting down rejected task ([#8562])
- sync: fix mpsc index wraparound in block reclamation ([#8546])
- sync: forget mpsc `Permit` before sending value ([#8560])
- sync: validate `MAX_PERMITS` in `Semaphore::acquire` ([#8548])
- sync: wake broadcast `Sender::closed` outside mutex ([#8558])
- task: drop replaced waker outside lock in `JoinSet` ([#8554])
- time: drop timer lock before dropping waker in `clear_entry` ([#8552])
- time: expire timers directly on shutdown without rotating wheel ([#8570])

### Fixed (unstable)

- fs: clamp `io_uring` read length to `u32::MAX` ([#8572])
- rt: ignore `current_thread` task dumps from other runtimes ([#8544])
- rt: preserve `io_uring` context if a completion waker panics ([#8566])
- sync: fix semaphore use-after-free and permit leak on tracing panic ([#8542])
- taskdump: restore deferred leaf wakes during capture ([#8445])
- time: drop stored waker when cancelling alt timer entry ([#8550])

[#8445]: https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio/pull/8445
[#8572]: https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio/pull/8572

# 1.53.1 (July 20th, 2026)

### Fixed

- signal: restore MSRV by removing `OnceLock::wait` from the Windows handler ([#8300])

### Fixed (unstable)

- time: fix alt timer cancellation and insertion race ([#8252])

### Documented

- runtime: remove dead link definition in Runtime::block_on ([#8301])

[#8252]: https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio/pull/8252
[#8300]: https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio/pull/8300
[#8301]: https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio/pull/8301

# 1.53.0 (July 17th, 2026)

### Added

- fs: implement `From<OwnedFd>` and `From<OwnedHandle>` for `File` ([#8266])
- metrics: add task schedule latency metric ([#7986])
- net: add `SocketAddr` methods to Unix sockets ([#8144])

### Changed

- io: add `#[inline]` to IO trait impls for in-memory types ([#8242])
- net: implement UCred::pid on FreeBSD ([#8086])
- net: support Nuttx target os ([#8259])
- signal: refactor global variables on Windows ([#8231])
- sync: `mpsc::{Receiver,UnboundedReceiver}` now drops waker on drop, even if there are still senders ([#8095])
- taskdump: support taskdumps on s390x ([#8192])
- time: add `#[track_caller]` to `timeout_at()` ([#8077])
- time: consolidate mutex locks on spurious poll ([#8124])
- time: defer waker clone on spurious poll ([#8107])
- time: move lazy-registration state into `Sleep` ([#8132])
- tracing: remove unnecessary span clone ([#8126])

### Fixed

- io: do not treat zero-length reads as EOF in `Chain` ([#8251])
- net: use getpeereid for QNX peer credentials ([#8270])
- runtime: avoid illegal state in `FastRand` ([#8078])
- sync: wake mpsc receiver when a queued `reserve[_many]` returns permits ([#8260])
- taskdump: skip double wake on `Trace::capture`/`Trace::trace_with` ([#8043])
- time: avoid stack overflow in runtime constructor ([#8093])
- time (alt timer): ensure timers stay in the same runtime after `.reset()` ([#8169])

### IO uring (unstable)

- fs: use io-uring for `fs::try_exists` ([#8080])
- fs: use io-uring for renaming files ([#7800])
- rt: flush io-uring CQE in case of CQE overflow ([#8277])

### Documented

- docs: clarify cancel safety wording ([#8181])
- fs: clarify `create_dir_all` succeeds if path exists ([#8149])
- io: add warning about stdout reordering with multiple handles ([#8276])
- net: document pipe `try_read*`/`try_write*` readiness behavior ([#8032])
- runtime: document interaction with fork() ([#8202])
- sync: clarify broadcast lagging semantics ([#8239])
- sync: document memory ordering guarantees for Semaphore ([#8119])
- task: explain why `yield_now` defers its waker ([#8254])
- time: add panic docs to `timeout_at()` ([#8077])
- time: fix reversed poll order in timeout doc ([#8214])

### Fixed

* sync: fix underflow in mpsc channel `len()` ([#8062])
* sync: notify receivers in mpsc `OwnedPermit::release()` method ([#8075])
* sync: require that an `RwLock` has `max_readers != 0` ([#8076])
* sync: return `Empty` from `try_recv()` when mpsc is closed with outstanding permits ([#8074])

# 1.52.2 (May 4th, 2026)

This release reverts the LIFO slot stealing change introduced in 1.51.0
([#7431]), due to [its performance impact][#8065]. ([#8100])

# 1.52.1 (April 16th, 2026)

## Fixed

- runtime: revert [#7757] to fix [a regression][#8056] that causes `spawn_blocking` to hang ([#8057])

# 1.52.0 (April 14th, 2026)

## Added

- io: `AioSource::register_borrowed` for I/O safety support ([#7992])
- net: add `try_io` function to `unix::pipe` sender and receiver types ([#8030])

## Added (unstable)

- runtime: `Builder::enable_eager_driver_handoff` setting enable eager hand off of the I/O and time drivers before polling tasks ([#8010])
- taskdump: add `trace_with()` for customized task dumps ([#8025])
- taskdump: allow `impl FnMut()` in `trace_with` instead of just `fn()` ([#8040])
- fs: support `io_uring` in `AsyncRead` for `File` ([#7907])

## Changed

- runtime: improve `spawn_blocking` scalability with sharded queue ([#7757])
- runtime: use `compare_exchange_weak()` in worker queue ([#8028])

## Fixed

- runtime: overflow second half of tasks when local queue is filled instead of first half ([#8029])

## Documented

- docs: fix typo in `oneshot::Sender::send` docs ([#8026])
- docs: hide #[tokio::main] attribute in the docs of `sync::watch` ([#8035])
- net: add docs on `ConnectionRefused` errors with UDP sockets ([#7870])

# 1.49.0 (January 3rd, 2026)

### Added

* net: add support for `TCLASS` option on IPv6 ([#7781])
* runtime: stabilize `runtime::id::Id` ([#7125])
* task: implement `Extend` for `JoinSet` ([#7195])
* task: stabilize the `LocalSet::id()` ([#7776])

### Changed

* net: deprecate `{TcpStream,TcpSocket}::set_linger` ([#7752])

### Fixed

* macros: fix the hygiene issue of `join!` and `try_join!` ([#7766])
* runtime: revert "replace manual vtable definitions with Wake" ([#7699])
* sync: return `TryRecvError::Disconnected` from `Receiver::try_recv` after `Receiver::close` ([#7686])
* task: remove unnecessary trait bounds on the `Debug` implementation ([#7720])

### Unstable

* fs: handle `EINTR` in `fs::write` for io-uring ([#7786])
* fs: support io-uring with `tokio::fs::read` ([#7696])
* runtime: disable io-uring on `EPERM` ([#7724])
* time: add alternative timer for better multicore scalability ([#7467])

### Documented

* docs: fix a typos in `bounded.rs` and `park.rs` ([#7817])
* io: add `SyncIoBridge` cross-references to `copy` and `copy_buf` ([#7798])
* io: doc that `AsyncWrite` does not inherit from `std::io::Write` ([#7705])
* metrics: clarify that `num_alive_tasks` is not strongly consistent ([#7614])
* net: clarify the cancellation safety of the `TcpStream::peek` ([#7305])
* net: clarify the drop behavior of `unix::OwnedWriteHalf` ([#7742])
* net: clarify the platform-dependent backlog in `TcpSocket` docs ([#7738])
* runtime: mention `LocalRuntime` in `new_current_thread` docs ([#7820])

reporting the issue).

# 1.21.0 (September 2, 2022)

This release is the first release of Tokio to intentionally support WASM. The
`sync,macros,io-util,rt,time` features are stabilized on WASM. Additionally the
wasm32-wasi target is given unstable support for the `net` feature.

### Added

- net: add `device` and `bind_device` methods to TCP/UDP sockets ([#4882])
- net: add `tos` and `set_tos` methods to TCP and UDP sockets ([#4877])
- net: add security flags to named pipe `ServerOptions` ([#4845])
- signal: add more windows signal handlers ([#4924])
- sync: add `mpsc::Sender::max_capacity` method ([#4904])
- sync: implement Weak version of `mpsc::Sender` ([#4595])
- task: add `LocalSet::enter` ([#4765])
- task: stabilize `JoinSet` and `AbortHandle` ([#4920])
- tokio: add `track_caller` to public APIs ([#4805], [#4848], [#4852])
- wasm: initial support for `wasm32-wasi` target ([#4716])

### Fixed

- miri: improve miri compatibility by avoiding temporary references in `linked_list::Link` impls ([#4841])
- signal: don't register write interest on signal pipe ([#4898])
- sync: add `#[must_use]` to lock guards ([#4886])
- sync: fix hang when calling `recv` on closed and reopened broadcast channel ([#4867])
- task: propagate attributes on task-locals ([#4837])

### Changed

- fs: change panic to error in `File::start_seek` ([#4897])
- io: reduce syscalls in `poll_read` ([#4840])
- process: use blocking threadpool for child stdio I/O ([#4824])
- signal: make `SignalKind` methods const ([#4956])

### Internal changes

- rt: extract `basic_scheduler::Config` ([#4935])
- rt: move I/O driver into `runtime` module ([#4942])
- rt: rename internal scheduler types ([#4945])

### Documented

- chore: fix typos and grammar ([#4858], [#4894], [#4928])
- io: fix typo in `AsyncSeekExt::rewind` docs ([#4893])
- net: add documentation to `try_read()` for zero-length buffers ([#4937])
- runtime: remove incorrect panic section for `Builder::worker_threads` ([#4849])
- sync: doc of `watch::Sender::send` improved ([#4959])
- task: add cancel safety docs to `JoinHandle` ([#4901])
- task: expand on cancellation of `spawn_blocking` ([#4811])
- time: clarify that the first tick of `Interval::tick` happens immediately ([#4951])

### Unstable

- rt: add unstable option to disable the LIFO slot ([#4936])
- task: fix incorrect signature in `Builder::spawn_on` ([#4953])
- task: make `task::Builder::spawn*` methods fallible ([#4823])

# 1.18.0 (April 27, 2022)

`tokio::sync`. In addition, it adds new unstable APIs to `tokio::task` (`Id`s
for uniquely identifying a task, and `AbortHandle` for remotely cancelling a

### Fixed

- blocking: add missing `#[track_caller]` for `spawn_blocking` ([#4616])
- macros: fix `select` macro to process 64 branches ([#4519])
- net: fix `try_io` methods not calling Mio's `try_io` internally ([#4582])

### Added

- net: add `UdpSocket::peer_addr` ([#4611])
- net: add `try_read_buf` method for named pipes ([#4626])
- signal: add `SignalKind` `Hash`/`Eq` impls and `c_int` conversion ([#4540])
- signal: add support for signals up to `SIGRTMAX` ([#4555])
- sync: add `watch::Sender::send_modify` method ([#4310])
- sync: add `broadcast::Receiver::len` method ([#4542])
- sync: add `watch::Receiver::same_channel` method ([#4581])
- sync: implement `Clone` for `RecvError` types ([#4560])

### Changed

- update `mio` to 0.8.1 ([#4582])
- macros: rename `tokio::select!`'s internal `util` module ([#4543])
- runtime: use `Vec::with_capacity` when building runtime ([#4553])

### Documented

- improve docs for `tokio_unstable` ([#4524])
- runtime: include more documentation for thread_pool/worker ([#4511])
- runtime: update `Handle::current`'s docs to mention `EnterGuard` ([#4567])
- time: clarify platform specific timer resolution ([#4474])
- signal: document that `Signal::recv` is cancel-safe ([#4634])
- sync: `UnboundedReceiver` close docs ([#4548])

### Unstable

The following changes only apply when building with `--cfg tokio_unstable`:

- task: add `task::Id` type ([#4630])
- task: add `AbortHandle` type for cancelling tasks in a `JoinSet` ([#4530],
  [#4640])
- task: fix missing `doc(cfg(...))` attributes for `JoinSet` ([#4531])
- task: fix broken link in `AbortHandle` RustDoc ([#4545])
- metrics: add initial IO driver metrics ([#4507])

# 1.17.0 (February 16, 2022)

This release updates the minimum supported Rust version (MSRV) to 1.49, the
`mio` dependency to v0.8, and the (optional) `parking_lot` dependency to v0.12.
Additionally, it contains several bug fixes, as well as internal refactoring and
performance improvements.

### Fixed

- time: prevent panicking in `sleep` with large durations ([#4495])
- time: eliminate potential panics in `Instant` arithmetic on platforms where
  `Instant::now` is not monotonic ([#4461])
- io: fix `DuplexStream` not participating in cooperative yielding ([#4478])
- rt: fix potential double panic when dropping a `JoinHandle` ([#4430])

### Changed

- update minimum supported Rust version to 1.49 ([#4457])
- update `parking_lot` dependency to v0.12.0 ([#4459])
- update `mio` dependency to v0.8 ([#4449])
- rt: remove an unnecessary lock in the blocking pool ([#4436])
- rt: remove an unnecessary enum in the basic scheduler ([#4462])
- time: use bit manipulation instead of modulo to improve performance ([#4480])
- net: use `std::future::Ready` instead of our own `Ready` future ([#4271])
- replace deprecated `atomic::spin_loop_hint` with `hint::spin_loop` ([#4491])
- fix miri failures in intrusive linked lists ([#4397])

### Documented

- io: add an example for `tokio::process::ChildStdin` ([#4479])

### Unstable

The following changes only apply when building with `--cfg tokio_unstable`:

- task: fix missing location information in `tracing` spans generated by
  `spawn_local` ([#4483])
- task: add `JoinSet` for managing sets of tasks ([#4335])
- metrics: fix compilation error on MIPS ([#4475])
- metrics: fix compilation error on arm32v7 ([#4453])

# 1.16.0 (January 27, 2022)

Fixes a soundness bug in `io::Take` ([#4428]). The unsoundness is exposed when
leaking memory in the given `AsyncRead` implementation and then overwriting the
supplied buffer:

```rust
impl AsyncRead for Buggy {
    fn poll_read(
        self: Pin<&mut Self>,
        cx: &mut Context<'_>,
        buf: &mut ReadBuf<'_>
    ) -> Poll<Result<()>> {
      let new_buf = vec![0; 5].leak();
      *buf = ReadBuf::new(new_buf);
      buf.put_slice(b"hello");
      Poll::Ready(Ok(()))
    }
}
```

Also, this release includes improvements to the multi-threaded scheduler that
can increase throughput by up to 20% in some cases ([#4383]).

### Fixed

- io: **soundness** don't expose uninitialized memory when using `io::Take` in edge case ([#4428])
- fs: ensure `File::write` results in a `write` syscall when the runtime shuts down ([#4316])
- process: drop pipe after child exits in `wait_with_output` ([#4315])
- rt: improve error message when spawning a thread fails ([#4398])
- rt: reduce false-positive thread wakups in the multi-threaded scheduler ([#4383])
- sync: don't inherit `Send` from `parking_lot::*Guard` ([#4359])

### Added

- net: `TcpSocket::linger()` and `set_linger()` ([#4324])
- net: impl `UnwindSafe` for socket types ([#4384])
- rt: impl `UnwindSafe` for `JoinHandle` ([#4418])
- sync: `watch::Receiver::has_changed()` ([#4342])
- sync: `oneshot::Receiver::blocking_recv()` ([#4334])
- sync: `RwLock` blocking operations ([#4425])

### Unstable

The following changes only apply when building with `--cfg tokio_unstable`

- rt: **breaking change** overhaul runtime metrics API ([#4373])

# 1.0.1 (December 25, 2020)

This release fixes a soundness hole caused by the combination of `RwLockWriteGuard::map`
and `RwLockWriteGuard::downgrade` by removing the `map` function. This is a breaking
change, but breaking changes are allowed under our semver policy when they are required
to fix a soundness hole. (See [this RFC][semver] for more.)

Note that we have chosen not to do a deprecation cycle or similar because Tokio 1.0.0 was
released two days ago, and therefore the impact should be minimal.

Due to the soundness hole, we have also yanked Tokio version 1.0.0.

### Removed

- sync: remove `RwLockWriteGuard::map` and `RwLockWriteGuard::try_map` ([#3345])

### Fixed

- docs: remove stream feature from docs ([#3335])

# 0.3.0 (October 15, 2020)

This represents a 1.0 beta release. APIs are polished and future-proofed. APIs
not included for 1.0 stabilization have been removed.

Biggest changes are:

- I/O driver internal rewrite. The windows implementation includes significant
  changes.
- Runtime API is polished, especially with how it interacts with feature flag
  combinations.
- Feature flags are simplified
  - `rt-core` and `rt-util` are combined to `rt`
  - `rt-threaded` is renamed to `rt-multi-thread` to match builder API
  - `tcp`, `udp`, `uds`, `dns` are combined to `net`.
  - `parking_lot` is included with `full`

### Changes

- meta: Minimum supported Rust version is now 1.45.
- io: `AsyncRead` trait now takes `ReadBuf` in order to safely handle reading
  into uninitialized memory ([#2758]).
- io: Internal I/O driver storage is now able to compact ([#2757]).
- rt: `Runtime::block_on` now takes `&self` ([#2782]).
- sync: `watch` reworked to decouple receiving a change notification from
  receiving the value ([#2814], [#2806]).
- sync: `Notify::notify` is renamed to `notify_one` ([#2822]).
- process: `Child::kill` is now an `async fn` that cleans zombies ([#2823]).
- sync: use `const fn` constructors as possible ([#2833], [#2790])
- signal: reduce cross-thread notification ([#2835]).
- net: tcp,udp,uds types support operations with `&self` ([#2828], [#2919], [#2934]).
- sync: blocking `mpsc` channel supports `send` with `&self` ([#2861]).
- time: rename `delay_for` and `delay_until` to `sleep` and `sleep_until` ([#2826]).
- io: upgrade to `mio` 0.7 ([#2893]).
- io: `AsyncSeek` trait is tweaked ([#2885]).
- fs: `File` operations take `&self` ([#2930]).
- rt: runtime API, and `#[tokio::main]` macro polish ([#2876])
- rt: `Runtime::enter` uses an RAII guard instead of a closure ([#2954]).
- net: the `from_std` function on all sockets no longer sets socket into non-blocking mode ([#2893])

### Added

- sync: `map` function to lock guards ([#2445]).
- sync: `blocking_recv` and `blocking_send` fns to `mpsc` for use outside of Tokio ([#2685]).
- rt: `Builder::thread_name_fn` for configuring thread names ([#1921]).
- fs: impl `FromRawFd` and `FromRawHandle` for `File` ([#2792]).
- process: `Child::wait` and `Child::try_wait` ([#2796]).
- rt: support configuring thread keep-alive duration ([#2809]).
- rt: `task::JoinHandle::abort` forcibly cancels a spawned task ([#2474]).
- sync: `RwLock` write guard to read guard downgrading ([#2733]).
- net: add `poll_*` functions that take `&self` to all net types ([#2845])
- sync: `get_mut()` for `Mutex`, `RwLock` ([#2856]).
- sync: `mpsc::Sender::closed()` waits for `Receiver` half to close ([#2840]).
- sync: `mpsc::Sender::is_closed()` returns true if `Receiver` half is closed ([#2726]).
- stream: `iter` and `iter_mut` to `StreamMap` ([#2890]).
- net: implement `AsRawSocket` on windows ([#2911]).
- net: `TcpSocket` creates a socket without binding or listening ([#2920]).

### Removed

- io: vectored ops are removed from `AsyncRead`, `AsyncWrite` traits ([#2882]).
- io: `mio` is removed from the public API. `PollEvented` and` Registration` are
  removed ([#2893]).
- io: remove `bytes` from public API. `Buf` and `BufMut` implementation are
  removed ([#2908]).
- time: `DelayQueue` is moved to `tokio-util` ([#2897]).

### Fixed

- io: `stdout` and `stderr` buffering on windows ([#2734]).

# 0.2.0 (November 26, 2019)

A major breaking change. Most implementation and APIs have changed one way or
another. This changelog entry contains a highlight

### Changed

- APIs are updated to use `async / await`.
- most `tokio-*` crates are collapsed into this crate.
- Scheduler is rewritten.
- `tokio::spawn` returns a `JoinHandle`.
- A single I/O / timer is used per runtime.
- I/O driver uses a concurrent slab for allocating state.
- components are made available via feature flag.
- Use `bytes` 0.5
- `tokio::codec` is moved to `tokio-util`.

### Removed

- Standalone `timer` and `net` drivers are removed, use `Runtime` instead
- `current_thread` runtime is removed, use `tokio::runtime::Runtime` with
  `basic_scheduler` instead.

title: evidence/repro-builds.sh
body:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Measurement B (plan step 9): two clean release builds of one tree, compared by file and by section.
# Run from the repository root:  bash viola-0.1.0/chunks/<marker>/evidence/repro-builds.sh
# Both builds go through scripts/release-check.sh into one same target path the script makes empty
# (by mkdir) before each build; the one path it removes is that one, which it made. Then the two copies
# are compared, and two controls run through the same comparison: a copy against itself (0 unequal)
# and a copy against another host program (all unequal).
set -euo pipefail

scratch=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/viola-repro-XXXXXX")
trap 'rm -rf -- "$scratch"' EXIT
target="$scratch/target"

echo "toolchain: $(rustc --version) · $(cargo --version) · $(objcopy --version | head -n 1) · $(readelf --version | head -n 1)"
echo "tree: HEAD $(git rev-parse HEAD) · uncommitted $(git status --porcelain | wc -l)"

for i in 1 2; do
  mkdir "$target"
  start=$(date -u +%FT%TZ)
  verdict=$(CARGO_TARGET_DIR="$target" bash scripts/release-check.sh 2>"$scratch/build-$i.err" | tail -n 1)
  echo "build $i: $start .. $(date -u +%FT%TZ) · $verdict"
  if [ "$verdict" != "release-check: viola only" ]; then
    echo "build $i: FAILED — stderr tail:"
    tail -n 20 "$scratch/build-$i.err"
    exit 1
  fi
  cp "$target/release/viola" "$scratch/build-$i"
  rm -rf -- "$target"
done

# One line per section: its name and type (the NULL entry left out).
sections() {
  readelf -S -W "$1" | awk '/^ *\[ *[0-9]+\]/ { sub(/^ *\[ *[0-9]+\] */, ""); split($0, f, " "); if (f[1] != "NULL") print f[1], f[2] }'
}

# A section's bytes hashed whole, loaded or not: `--only-section` with `-O binary` writes loaded
# sections only and `--dump-section` refuses `.symtab` / `.strtab`, so every section is read from the
# file at its offset and size as `readelf -S` gives them; a NOBITS section holds no bytes and reads as
# its size. A name the file lacks reads `absent`.
section_sha() {
  local row type off size
  row=$(readelf -S -W "$1" | awk -v n="$2" '/^ *\[ *[0-9]+\]/ { sub(/^ *\[ *[0-9]+\] */, ""); if ($1 == n) { print $2, $4, $5; exit } }')
  if [ -z "$row" ]; then
    echo "absent"
    return
  fi
  read -r type off size <<< "$row"
  if [ "$type" = "NOBITS" ]; then
    echo "nobits-size-$size"
  else
    dd if="$1" bs=65536 iflag=skip_bytes,count_bytes skip=$((16#$off)) count=$((16#$size)) status=none | sha256sum | cut -c1-16
  fi
}

compare() {
  local label=$1 a=$2 b=$3 unequal=0 total=0 name ha hb
  echo "== $label"
  echo "file: a sha256 $(sha256sum "$a" | cut -c1-16) size $(stat -c %s "$a") · b sha256 $(sha256sum "$b" | cut -c1-16) size $(stat -c %s "$b")"
  echo "build-id: a $(readelf -n "$a" | awk '/Build ID/ {print $3}') · b $(readelf -n "$b" | awk '/Build ID/ {print $3}')"
  while IFS= read -r name; do
    total=$((total + 1))
    ha=$(section_sha "$a" "$name")
    hb=$(section_sha "$b" "$name")
    if [ "$ha" = "$hb" ] && [ "$ha" != "absent" ]; then
      echo "section $name: equal $ha"
    else
      unequal=$((unequal + 1))
      echo "section $name: UNEQUAL a $ha b $hb"
    fi
  done < <( { sections "$a"; sections "$b"; } | awk '!seen[$1]++ { print $1 }')
  echo "sections: $total named · $unequal unequal"
  echo "strings: $(diff <(strings -a "$a") <(strings -a "$b") | grep -c '^[<>]' || true) differing lines"
}

compare "build-1 vs build-2" "$scratch/build-1" "$scratch/build-2"
echo "the differing strings lines, build-1 (<) against build-2 (>), each cut at 120 bytes:"
diff <(strings -a "$scratch/build-1") <(strings -a "$scratch/build-2") | grep '^[<>]' | cut -c1-120 || true
compare "control: build-1 vs itself" "$scratch/build-1" "$scratch/build-1"
other=/usr/bin/true
[ -f "$other" ] || other=/bin/true
compare "control: build-1 vs $other" "$scratch/build-1" "$other"

title: evidence/repro-unstamped.py
body:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The unstamped first-start race, read through the harness (plan step 3 / step 8).

Run from the repository root:  python3 viola-0.1.0/chunks/<marker>/evidence/repro-unstamped.py <label>

Rounds of 6 concurrent `viola-harness boot --unstamped` sessions, spawned directly from
`target/harness/debug` (no shell, never a piped boot: each boot's stdout goes to a file), each fake
agent given `--receipt`, each session cleaned up through the harness. Two inputs: the default
`overseer` + `builder` pair, then `builder` alone (the control). Every child has a kill deadline,
and every session this script booted is cleaned up on any exit, an interrupt included.
"""

import json
import os
import shutil
import signal
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time

ROUNDS = 4
SESSIONS = 6
BUILD_DEADLINE_S = 900
BOOT_DEADLINE_S = 120
CLEANUP_DEADLINE_S = 60

ROOT = os.getcwd()
HARNESS = os.path.join(ROOT, "target", "harness", "debug", "viola-harness")
INPUTS = [("pair", ["overseer", "builder"]), ("builder-alone", ["builder"])]

scratch = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="viola-race-")
booted = []


def bounded(argv, deadline, stdout, env=None):
    """Runs argv with stdout to a file and a kill deadline; returns (exit code or None, seconds)."""
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    p = subprocess.Popen(argv, cwd=ROOT, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=stdout,
                         stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, env=env, start_new_session=True)
    try:
        code = p.wait(timeout=deadline)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        os.killpg(p.pid, signal.SIGTERM)
        try:
            p.wait(timeout=5)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            os.killpg(p.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
            p.wait()
        code = None
    return code, round(time.monotonic() - t0, 2)


def cleanup(session):
    with open(os.path.join(scratch, f"cleanup-{session}.json"), "wb") as out:
        code, _ = bounded([HARNESS, "cleanup", "--session", session], CLEANUP_DEADLINE_S, out)
    with open(os.path.join(scratch, f"cleanup-{session}.json"), "rb") as f:
        text = f.read().decode(errors="replace").strip()
    try:
        doc = json.loads(text)
    except ValueError:
        doc = {"unparsed": True}
    return code, doc


def teardown():
    for s in list(booted):
        cleanup(s)
        booted.remove(s)
    shutil.rmtree(scratch, ignore_errors=True)


def on_signal(signum, _frame):
    teardown()
    sys.exit(128 + signum)


signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, on_signal)
signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, on_signal)


def receipts(path):
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return []
    rows = []
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        for line in f.read().decode(errors="replace").splitlines():
            try:
                rows.append(json.loads(line))
            except ValueError:
                pass
    return [r for r in rows if r.get("kind") == "hook" and r.get("event") == "SessionStart"]


def one_round(label, names, rnd):
    procs = []
    for n in range(1, SESSIONS + 1):
        session = f"race-{label}-r{rnd}-s{n}-{os.getpid()}"
        args = [HARNESS, "boot", "--session", session, "--unstamped"]
        for name in names:
            receipt = os.path.join(scratch, f"{session}-{name}.ndjson")
            args += ["--instance", f"{name}:--receipt {receipt}"]
        out = open(os.path.join(scratch, f"boot-{session}.json"), "wb")
        p = subprocess.Popen(args, cwd=ROOT, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=out,
                             stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, start_new_session=True)
        booted.append(session)
        procs.append((session, p, out, time.monotonic()))
    results = []
    for session, p, out, t0 in procs:
        left = max(1.0, BOOT_DEADLINE_S - (time.monotonic() - t0))
        try:
            code = p.wait(timeout=left)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            os.killpg(p.pid, signal.SIGTERM)
            try:
                p.wait(timeout=5)
            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                os.killpg(p.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
                p.wait()
            code = None
        out.close()
        with open(os.path.join(scratch, f"boot-{session}.json"), "rb") as f:
            text = f.read().decode(errors="replace").strip()
        try:
            doc = json.loads(text.splitlines()[-1]) if text else {}
        except ValueError:
            doc = {"unparsed": True}
        hooks = {}
        for name in names:
            hooks[name] = [
                {"ran": r.get("ran"), "exit_code": r.get("exit_code"),
                 "spawn_os_error": r.get("spawn_os_error")}
                for r in receipts(os.path.join(scratch, f"{session}-{name}.ndjson"))
            ]
        results.append({"session": session, "exit": code, "ok": doc.get("ok"),
                        "reason": doc.get("reason"), "instance": doc.get("instance"),
                        "missing": doc.get("missing"), "session_start_hooks": hooks})
    for r in results:
        ccode, cdoc = cleanup(r["session"])
        booted.remove(r["session"])
        r["cleanup"] = {"exit": ccode, "ok": cdoc.get("ok"),
                        "processes_gone": cdoc.get("processes_gone"),
                        "endpoint_gone": cdoc.get("endpoint_gone")}
    return results


def main():
    label = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "run"
    env = dict(os.environ, CARGO_TARGET_DIR="target/harness")
    with open(os.path.join(scratch, "build.log"), "wb") as out:
        code, secs = bounded(["cargo", "build", "--workspace", "--features", "viola/fake-agent"],
                             BUILD_DEADLINE_S, out, env)
    print(json.dumps({"build_exit": code, "build_s": secs}))
    if code != 0:
        return 1
    for input_label, names in INPUTS:
        sessions = failed = 0
        for rnd in range(1, ROUNDS + 1):
            t0 = time.monotonic()
            for r in one_round(input_label, names, rnd):
                sessions += 1
                if r["ok"] is not True:
                    failed += 1
                r["round"] = rnd
                print(json.dumps({"label": label, "input": input_label, **r}))
            print(json.dumps({"label": label, "input": input_label, "round": rnd,
                              "round_s": round(time.monotonic() - t0, 2)}))
        print(json.dumps({"label": label, "input": input_label, "sessions": sessions,
                          "failed": failed}))
    return 0


try:
    rc = main()
finally:
    teardown()
sys.exit(rc)

body:
# Measurement B: clean release builds of one tree, compared by file and by section (plan step 9)

Read 2026-10-27 on the Linux dev host, run dir `.andromeda/runs/2026-10-27T02-08-46-implement/`. Script:
`viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-27-pinned-copy-race-and-reproducible-builds/evidence/repro-builds.sh`, run from the root
under a 3600 s `timeout`. Each build is `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<scratch>/target bash scripts/release-check.sh` into a
`<scratch>/target` the script makes by `mkdir` before the build and removes after copying `release/viola` out, so
both builds of a firing use one same, empty target path; `<scratch>` is a `mktemp -d` under `/tmp`, removed by the
script's trap. No `RUSTC_WRAPPER`, `RUSTFLAGS`, `CARGO_BUILD_*` or cargo config file is set on the host (read before
the reading); 32 cores, so a cold release build takes 16–18 s.

Toolchain: `rustc 1.98.1 (48a229cea 2026-09-01)` · `cargo 1.98.1 (797e8a9bc 2026-08-05)` · `GNU objcopy (GNU
Binutils) 2.47` · `GNU readelf (GNU Binutils) 2.47`. Tree: HEAD `99977116182b` plus this chunk's uncommitted edits
(12 rows at the first firing; 13 at the third, the extra row `tests/path1_run_start.rs`'s temporary timing record,
a test file outside `--bin viola`).

## The reading (third firing, the script as it stands)

Builds: 1 at 02:20:25Z..02:20:43Z, 2 at 02:20:43Z..02:21:01Z, each `release-check: viola only`.

| | build 1 | build 2 |
|---|---|---|
| file sha256 (16 hex) | `57bce92d92ca5a2a` | `ff63f38e9700f432` |
| size | 8 179 264 B | 8 179 272 B |
| build-id note | `ce0631a6794b6f97502f3cac1bb919d246a9fe8c` | `bc18839736028f6e6cd1ac24cb0e236bb0b39af8` |

Sections (every section `readelf -S -W` names, each hashed from the file at its offset and size; NOBITS read as its
size): **34 named, 3 unequal** — `.note.gnu.build-id` (`6a892d51…` / `f8ebd7a6…`), `.symtab` (`93644dda…` /
`52a3073e…`), `.strtab` (`3784ad1f…` / `fb529271…`). Equal, among the 31: `.text` `60c6ea8b…`, `.rodata`
`05f4b5fc…`, `.data` `79665d0a…`, `.data.rel.ro` `fc414e05…`, `.eh_frame` `94b2d544…`, `.gcc_except_table`
`1b286c82…` (the CARRY's six loaded sections), and every other loaded section, `.comment` and `.shstrtab`.

`strings -a`: 6 differing lines — three local symbols whose `.llvm.<number>` suffix differs:
`anon.15867591b078eac10c8c2c5140586b7a.{9,56,57}.llvm.2173237286001873254` in build 1 against
`….llvm.13381032314865616282` in build 2 (each line cut at 120 bytes by the script).

Controls, through the same comparison:
- build 1 against itself: 34 named, **0 unequal**, 0 differing strings lines.
- build 1 against `/usr/bin/true` (another host program, 43 320 B): 38 named, **35 unequal**, 76 473 differing strings
  lines. Three sections hash equal there: `.interp`, `.note.ABI-tag` and `.fini` — both are dynamically linked
  glibc x86-64 executables (one interpreter path, one ABI note, one `.fini` stub); the plan's "all unequal" reads 35
  of 38, recorded as measured.

## The three firings

| firing | builds | build 1 | build 2 | the comparison's defects |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (02:17:16Z..02:17:49Z) | cold, one target path | `57bce92d…` | `ff63f38e…` | the `true` control resolved to the shell builtin (no file compared); `-O binary --only-section` writes loaded sections only, so `.comment` / `.symtab` / `.shstrtab` / `.strtab` hashed as empty |
| 2 (02:18:51Z..02:19:24Z) | cold, one target path | `ff63f38e…` | `ff63f38e…` | stopped at `.symtab` (`objcopy --dump-section` refuses it), exit 1; the file pair equal |
| 3 (02:20:25Z..02:21:01Z) | cold, one target path | `57bce92d…` | `ff63f38e…` | none — the reading above |

Six cold builds of one tree gave two files, `57bce92d…` (3 times) and `ff63f38e…` (3 times), in no fixed order
(A/B, B/B, A/B). Wherever the two met (firings 1 and 3) they differed in exactly the build-id note and 8 bytes of
symbol data (`.symtab` / `.strtab`); every loaded section was equal.

## What it means for the pin, and what is not explained

The pin key is a truncated SHA-256 of the whole file (`viola_state::pin::pin_key`), so two clean builds of one tree
can key two `bin/<key>/` and `plugin/<key>/` folders while loading the same code. **Not explained:** why the
`.llvm.<number>` suffix of those three local symbols differs from one cold build to the next (and, with it, the
build-id the linker hashes over the file). No cause was measured, and none is recorded. No product or build change
rests on this reading: acting on it (a profile key, a linker flag, a key over loaded sections) is the founder's.

# Operator pass — 2026-10-31-sanitised-error-surfaces

Run by the session on the operator's word (the /andromeda-implement invocation of 2026-10-31: "Run the operator pass with the ci.py conclusion read (leg=operator) as usual; its first push carries the three records-door commits."). Base: HEAD `7bf5c32add0e` before the pre-CI commit. `origin/build/viola-0.1.0` read `5273ab8c68e8`, so the first push also carries `8ebed5bc`, `2cedb584` and `7bf5c32a`.

## Entry 22 re-run — `bash scripts/agent-run.sh pre-push` (the uncommitted tree)

### First re-run: red, 2026-10-31T09:19:30Z to about 09:21:20Z
`3347 tests run: 3345 passed (22 slow), 2 failed`. The failures are `viola::cli_verify verify_stopped_during_the_resume_run_removes_its_dir_and_exits_1` `case_1_sigint` (7.535 s) and `case_2_sigterm` (7.188 s), each `timed out waiting for Run E's start` at the 7 s `WITHIN` of `tests/support/fake.rs`'s `wait_for`, its watch report showing the receipt still growing.

Host record for that window: `CONTENDED for viola - 20 s stalled on IO: 09:20:14Z..09:20:34Z 20 s (rule: >= 8 s with io some >= 50%); build tools alive in them: escher 20 s, viola 20 s`, load peak 90.7, 22 slow tests against 5 in the green firing before it.

Reading: the red is the host's contention, not this chunk's change. What holds it: the same tree read green on this case in the gate block's second firing and in the re-run below; five rounds alone read green at about 4.3 s, four of them under `QUIET` and one under `CONTENDED`; and this chunk's only edit on the case's path is the `AgentError` rename in `src/cmd/verify.rs`, ahead of any run. What is not measured: the nextest log carries no wall clock per test, so the two cases' position inside the 20 s window is inferred from their place in the run (391 and 400 of 3347), not read. The case's 4.3 s against its 7 s wait leaves a thin margin on a contended host; this pass changes nothing there, and no bound moves.

### Second re-run: green, 2026-10-31T09:23:34Z to 09:25:12Z
Exit 0. `{"v":1,"cmd":"pre-push","ok":true,"stage":"linux-tests","linux":{"run":{"ok":true,"suites":[{"suite":"coverage","passed":3347,"failed":0,"skipped":0,"failures":[]},{"suite":"doctest","passed":0,"failed":0,"skipped":0,"failures":[]}]},"gate":{"ok":true,"breaches":[]}}}`

Host record: `QUIET for viola - 5 s stalled on IO`.

## Entry 24 — `python -X utf8 {tools_dir}/gate.py run --plan … --operator 24` (no run dir), read 2026-10-31T09:26:06Z
